An \emph{implicit atlas of dimension $d=\operatorname{vdim}_AX$} on $X$ is an index set $A$ along with the following data: \begin{rlist} \item(Covering groups) A finite group $\Gamma_\alpha$ for all $\alpha\in A$ (let $\Gamma_I:=\prod_{\alpha\in I}\Gamma_\alpha$). \item(Obstruction spaces) A finitely generated $\mathbb R[\Gamma_\alpha]$-module $E_\alpha$ for all $\alpha\in A$ (let $E_I:=\bigoplus_{\alpha\in I}E_\alpha$). \item(Thickenings) A Hausdorff $\Gamma_I$-space $X_I$ for all finite $I\subseteq A$, and a homeomorphism $X\to X_\varnothing$. \item(Kuranishi maps) A $\Gamma_\alpha$-equivariant function $s_\alpha:X_I\to E_\alpha$ for all $\alpha\in I\subseteq A$ (for $I\subseteq J$, let $s_I:X_J\to E_I$ denote $\bigoplus_{\alpha\in I}s_\alpha$). \item(Footprints) A $\Gamma_I$-invariant open set $U_{IJ}\subseteq X_I$ for all $I\subseteq J\subseteq A$. \item(Footprint maps) A $\Gamma_J$-equivariant function $\psi_{IJ}:(s_{J\setminus I}|X_J)^{-1}(0)\to U_{IJ}$ for all $I\subseteq J\subseteq A$. \item(Regular locus) A $\Gamma_I$-invariant subset $X_I^\mathrm{reg}\subseteq X_I$ for all $I\subseteq A$. \end{rlist} which must satisfy the following ``compatibility axioms'': \begin{rlist} \item$\psi_{IJ}\psi_{JK}=\psi_{IK}$ and $\psi_{II}=\operatorname{id}$. \item$s_I\psi_{IJ}=s_I$. \item$U_{IJ_1}\cap U_{IJ_2}=U_{I,J_1\cup J_2}$ and $U_{II}=X_I$. \item$\psi_{IJ}^{-1}(U_{IK})=U_{JK}\cap(s_{J\setminus I}|X_J)^{-1}(0)$.\footnote{Added in proof: Abouzaid recently pointed out that this axiom is superfluous; it is implied by the other axioms.} \item(Homeomorphism axiom) $\psi_{IJ}$ induces a homeomorphism $(s_{J\setminus I}|X_J)^{-1}(0)/\Gamma_{J\setminus I}\to U_{IJ}$. \setcounter{rcountsave}{\value{rcounti}} \end{rlist} and the following ``transversality axioms'': \begin{rlist} \setcounter{rcounti}{\value{rcountsave}} \item$\psi_{IJ}^{-1}(X_I^\mathrm{reg})\subseteq X_J^\mathrm{reg}$. \item$\Gamma_{J\setminus I}$ acts freely on $\psi_{IJ}^{-1}(X_I^\mathrm{reg})$. \item(Openness axiom) $X_I^\mathrm{reg}\subseteq X_I$ is open. \item(Submersion axiom) The map $s_{J\setminus I}:X_J\to E_{J\setminus I}$ is locally modeled on the projection $\mathbb R^{d+\dim E_I}\times\mathbb R^{\dim E_{J\setminus I}}\to\mathbb R^{\dim E_{J\setminus I}}$ over $\psi_{IJ}^{-1}(X_I^\mathrm{reg})\subseteq X_J$. \item(Covering axiom) $X_\varnothing=\bigcup_{I\subseteq A}\psi_{\varnothing I}((s_I|X_I^\mathrm{reg})^{-1}(0))$. \end{rlist}
nodes.statement_short: An implicit atlas on a compact Hausdorff space $X$: covering groups, obstruction spaces, thickenings $X_I$, Kuranishi maps, footprints and footprint maps, and regular loci, subject to compatibility and transversality (openness, submersion, covering) axioms.
nodes.genus: an index set $A$ along with the following data
differentia: A finite group $\Gamma_\alpha$ for all $\alpha\in A$
A finitely generated $\mathbb R[\Gamma_\alpha]$-module $E_\alpha$ for all $\alpha\in A$
A Hausdorff $\Gamma_I$-space $X_I$ for all finite $I\subseteq A$, and a homeomorphism $X\to X_\varnothing$.
$\psi_{IJ}$ induces a homeomorphism $(s_{J\setminus I}|X_J)^{-1}(0)/\Gamma_{J\setminus I}\to U_{IJ}$.
nodes.label: implicitatlasdefinition

nodes.name: Weakening of the implicit atlas axioms
nodes.statement: The VFC machinery in this paper would go through admitting a slight weakening of the axioms of an implicit atlas. For example, we only ever use the fact that the openness and submersion axioms hold in a neighborhood of $(s_I|X_I)^{-1}(0)$. We will not make this precise here, however, since the constructions of implicit atlases we know of would not be made any easier by such a weakening of the axioms.
nodes.statement_short: The VFC machinery only uses the openness and submersion axioms near $(s_I|X_I)^{-1}(0)$, so the axioms could be slightly weakened.

nodes.name: Smooth implicit atlas
nodes.statement: A \emph{smooth structure} on an implicit atlas consists of a smooth structure on each $X_I^\mathrm{reg}$ such that: \begin{rlist} \item$\Gamma_I$ acts smoothly on $X_I^\mathrm{reg}$. \item$s_I$ is smooth over $X_I^\mathrm{reg}$. \item$s_{J\setminus I}:X_J\to E_{J\setminus I}$ is a smooth submersion over $\psi_{IJ}^{-1}(X_I^\mathrm{reg})$. \item$\psi_{IJ}$ is a local diffeomorphism over $\psi_{IJ}^{-1}(X_I^\mathrm{reg})$. \end{rlist}
nodes.statement_short: A smooth implicit atlas: smooth structures on the regular loci making group actions, Kuranishi maps smooth and footprint maps local diffeomorphisms.
differentia: $\Gamma_I$ acts smoothly on $X_I^\mathrm{reg}$.
$s_I$ is smooth over $X_I^\mathrm{reg}$.
nodes.label: smoothIAdef

nodes.name: Smooth structure not needed for VFC machinery
nodes.statement: The VFC machinery in this paper applies to implicit atlases (without a smooth structure), though the notion of a smooth implicit atlas may be useful for other applications of implicit atlases.

nodes.name: Using finite $I\to A$ instead of finite $I\subseteq A$
nodes.statement: An implicit atlas consists of data parameterized by the \emph{category of finite subsets of $A$} (objects: finite subsets, morphisms: inclusions). A direct modification of the definition allows one to instead use the \emph{category of finite sets over $A$} (objects: finite sets $I\to A$, morphisms: injective maps $I\hookrightarrow J$ compatible with the maps to $A$). In fact, all constructions of implicit atlases we know of yield implicit atlases in this generalized sense. We won't need this generalization in this paper, but let us point out some reasons why it may be useful to keep in mind. With the definition as it stands now (using finite subsets of $A$), we can ``pull back'' an implicit atlas along any \emph{injection} $B\hookrightarrow A$. If we instead use finite sets over $A$, then we can pull back an implicit atlas along any \emph{map} $B\to A$ (in fact, we can pull back along any \emph{coproduct preserving functor} from finite sets over $B$ to finite sets over $A$, which amounts to the specification of a finite set $I_\beta\to A$ for all $\beta\in B$). Also, in the category of finite subsets of $A$ we can only take the disjoint union of subsets which are already disjoint; however in the category of finite sets over $A$ there exist arbitrary abstract finite disjoint unions. This allows some extra (though currently unneeded) flexibility in certain constructions, since we do not need to ensure certain sets are disjoint or that certain maps are injective. Using the category of sets over $A$ is also the natural perspective to take if we wanted to allow $A$ to be a groupoid instead of a set (then an object is a finite set $I$ along with a collection of objects $\{\alpha_i\}_{i\in I}$ of $A$, and a morphism $(I,\{\alpha_i\}_{i\in I})\to(J,\{\alpha_j\}_{j\in J})$ is an injection $j:I\hookrightarrow J$ along with isomorphisms $\alpha_i\xrightarrow\sim\alpha_{j(i)}$ in $A$).
nodes.statement_short: Implicit atlases can be indexed by the category of finite sets over $A$ instead of finite subsets, allowing pullback along arbitrary maps and groupoid index sets.
nodes.label: bettertouseovercategory

nodes.name: Implicit atlas with boundary
nodes.statement: Let $X$ be a compact Hausdorff space together with a closed subset denoted $\partial X\subseteq X$. An \emph{implicit atlas of dimension $d$ with boundary} on $X$ consists of the same data as an implicit atlas, except that in addition we specify a $\Gamma_I$-invariant closed subset $\partial X_I\subseteq X_I$ for all $I\subseteq A$, such that $\partial X_\varnothing=\partial X$. We add the following ``compatibility axiom'': \begin{rlist} \item$\psi_{IJ}^{-1}(\partial X_I)=(s_{J\setminus I}|\partial X_J)^{-1}(0)$. \setcounter{rcountsave}{\value{rcounti}} \end{rlist} and we modify one ``transversality axiom'': \begin{rlist} \setcounter{rcounti}{\value{rcountsave}} \item(Submersion axiom) We allow an additional local model $\mathbb R_{\geq 0}\times\mathbb R^{d+\dim E_I-1}\times\mathbb R^{\dim E_{J\setminus I}}\to\mathbb R^{\dim E_{J\setminus I}}$, and $\partial X_J^\mathrm{reg}\subseteq X_J^\mathrm{reg}$ must correspond to the boundary of the local model. \end{rlist}
nodes.statement_short: An implicit atlas with closed boundary subsets $\partial X_I$ compatible with footprint maps, with a half-space local model allowed in the submersion axiom.
nodes.definiendum: implicit atlas of dimension $d$ with boundary
nodes.genus: the same data as an implicit atlas
differentia: a $\Gamma_I$-invariant closed subset $\partial X_I\subseteq X_I$ for all $I\subseteq A$, such that $\partial X_\varnothing=\partial X$
nodes.label: IAwboundary

nodes.name: Implicit atlas as special case of implicit atlas with boundary
nodes.statement: Just as a manifold is a special case of a manifold with boundary, an implicit atlas is a special case of an implicit atlas with boundary (namely where $\partial X_I=\varnothing$ for all $I$).

nodes.name: Restriction of implicit atlas to boundary
nodes.statement: Let $X$ be a space with implicit atlas $A$ of dimension $d$ with boundary. Then this induces an implicit atlas $A$ (the same index set) of dimension $d-1$ on $\partial X$, simply by setting $(\partial X)_I:=\partial X_I$ and restricting the rest of the data to these subspaces.
nodes.statement_short: An implicit atlas of dimension $d$ with boundary on $X$ restricts to an implicit atlas of dimension $d-1$ on $\partial X$.

nodes.name: Ground ring convention ($\#\Gamma_\alpha$ invertible in $R$)
nodes.statement: In this section, we work over a fixed ground ring $R$, and everything takes place in the category of $R$-modules. We restrict to implicit atlases $A$ for which $\#\Gamma_\alpha$ is invertible in $R$ for all $\alpha\in A$.
nodes.statement_short: Work over a fixed ground ring $R$ and only with implicit atlases whose covering group orders are invertible in $R$.

nodes.name: Overview of the VFC package
nodes.statement: For any space $X$ equipped with a \emph{finite} \emph{locally orientable} implicit atlas $A$ of dimension $d$ with boundary, we define \emph{virtual cochain complexes} $C^\bullet_\mathrm{vir}(X;A)$ and $C^\bullet_\mathrm{vir}(X\operatorname{rel}\partial;A)$. We construct canonical isomorphisms: \begin{align} H^\bullet_\mathrm{vir}(X;A)&\xrightarrow\sim\check H^\bullet(X;\mathfrak o_X)\\ H^\bullet_\mathrm{vir}(X\operatorname{rel}\partial;A)&\xrightarrow\sim\check H^\bullet(X;\mathfrak o_{X\operatorname{rel}\partial}) \end{align} ($H^\bullet_\mathrm{vir}$ denotes the cohomology of $C^\bullet_\mathrm{vir}$) for certain \emph{virtual orientation sheaves} $\mathfrak o_X$ and $\mathfrak o_{X\operatorname{rel}\partial}$ on $X$. There is a canonical map: \begin{equation} C^{d+\bullet}_\mathrm{vir}(X\operatorname{rel}\partial;A)\xrightarrow{s_\ast}C_{\dim E_A-\bullet}(E_A,E_A\setminus 0;\mathfrak o_{E_A}^\vee)^{\Gamma_A} \end{equation} which can be thought of as the (chain level) \emph{virtual fundamental cycle}. To study the virtual cochain complexes (in particular, to construct the isomorphisms \eqref{HXiso}--\eqref{HXreliso}), we define complexes of $\mathcal K$-presheaves on $X$: \begin{align} K&\mapsto C^\bullet_\mathrm{vir}(K;A)\\ K&\mapsto C^\bullet_\mathrm{vir}(K\operatorname{rel}\partial;A) \end{align} whose global sections are the virtual cochain complexes.\footnote{Note that this is a certain abuse of notation, as $A$ is not an implicit atlas on $K\subsetneqq X$.}\footnote{Note that the map $s_\ast$ \eqref{sastintrotvfcsec} is global; it does not exist on $C^\bullet_\mathrm{vir}(K\operatorname{rel}\partial;A)$ for $K\subsetneqq X$ or on any $C^\bullet_\mathrm{vir}(K;A)$.} We show that they are pure homotopy $\mathcal K$-sheaves, and that there are canonical isomorphisms of sheaves on $X$: \begin{align} H^0_\mathrm{vir}(-;A)&=\mathfrak o_X\\ H^0_\mathrm{vir}(-\operatorname{rel}\partial;A)&=\mathfrak o_{X\operatorname{rel}\partial} \end{align} The isomorphisms \eqref{HXiso}--\eqref{HXreliso} then follow from Proposition \ref{cechcohomologypurehomotopysheaf}.
nodes.statement_short: Overview: virtual cochain complexes $C^\bullet_\mathrm{vir}$ with canonical isomorphisms to \v Cech cohomology of the virtual orientation sheaf, a chain-level virtual fundamental cycle $s_\ast$, and pure homotopy $\mathcal K$-sheaf structure.

nodes.name: Virtual cohomology $H^\bullet_\mathrm{vir}$
nodes.statement: We construct canonical isomorphisms: \begin{align} H^\bullet_\mathrm{vir}(X;A)&\xrightarrow\sim\check H^\bullet(X;\mathfrak o_X)\\ H^\bullet_\mathrm{vir}(X\operatorname{rel}\partial;A)&\xrightarrow\sim\check H^\bullet(X;\mathfrak o_{X\operatorname{rel}\partial}) \end{align} ($H^\bullet_\mathrm{vir}$ denotes the cohomology of $C^\bullet_\mathrm{vir}$) for certain \emph{virtual orientation sheaves} $\mathfrak o_X$ and $\mathfrak o_{X\operatorname{rel}\partial}$ on $X$.

nodes.name: Isomorphisms $H^\bullet_\mathrm{vir}=\check H^\bullet(X;\mathfrak o_X)$ (preview)
nodes.statement: H^\bullet_\mathrm{vir}(X;A)&\xrightarrow\sim\check H^\bullet(X;\mathfrak o_X)\\ H^\bullet_\mathrm{vir}(X\operatorname{rel}\partial;A)&\xrightarrow\sim\check H^\bullet(X;\mathfrak o_{X\operatorname{rel}\partial})
nodes.label: HXiso

nodes.name: Chain level virtual fundamental cycle $s_\ast$ (preview)
nodes.statement: C^{d+\bullet}_\mathrm{vir}(X\operatorname{rel}\partial;A)\xrightarrow{s_\ast}C_{\dim E_A-\bullet}(E_A,E_A\setminus 0;\mathfrak o_{E_A}^\vee)^{\Gamma_A}
nodes.label: sastintrotvfcsec

nodes.name: $\mathcal K$-presheaves of virtual cochains (preview)
nodes.statement: K&\mapsto C^\bullet_\mathrm{vir}(K;A)\\ K&\mapsto C^\bullet_\mathrm{vir}(K\operatorname{rel}\partial;A)

nodes.name: $H^0_\mathrm{vir}$ equals virtual orientation sheaf (preview)
nodes.statement: H^0_\mathrm{vir}(-;A)&=\mathfrak o_X\\ H^0_\mathrm{vir}(-\operatorname{rel}\partial;A)&=\mathfrak o_{X\operatorname{rel}\partial}

nodes.name: Orientation module of a vector space
nodes.statement: Let $E$ be a finite-dimensional vector space over $\mathbb R$. We let $\mathfrak o_E$ denote the orientation module of $E$, namely $H_{\dim E}(E,E\setminus 0)$ (a free $R$-module of rank $1$).\footnote{According to the previous definition, we should really call this $(\mathfrak o_E)_0$ (the stalk at $0\in E$ of the orientation sheaf of $E$ considered as a manifold), though we do not anticipate this abuse causing any particular confusion.}

nodes.name: Locally orientable implicit atlas
nodes.statement: Let $X$ be a space with implicit atlas $A$ with boundary. We say that $A$ is \emph{locally orientable}\footnote{This is analogous to the notion of an orbifold being locally orientable.} iff for every $I\subseteq A$ and every $x\in(s_I|X_I^\mathrm{reg})^{-1}(0)$, the stabilizer $(\Gamma_I)_x$ acts trivially on $(\mathfrak o_{X_I^\mathrm{reg}})_x\otimes\mathfrak o_{E_I}^\vee$ (this action is always by a sign $(\Gamma_I)_x\to\{\pm 1\}$). This notion is independent of the ring $R$ (due to our restriction that $\#\Gamma_\alpha$ be invertible in $R$).
nodes.statement_short: An implicit atlas is locally orientable if all stabilizers act trivially on the orientation lines $\mathfrak o_{X_I^\mathrm{reg}}\otimes\mathfrak o_{E_I}^\vee$ at zeros.
differentia: for every $I\subseteq A$ and every $x\in(s_I|X_I^\mathrm{reg})^{-1}(0)$, the stabilizer $(\Gamma_I)_x$ acts trivially on $(\mathfrak o_{X_I^\mathrm{reg}})_x\otimes\mathfrak o_{E_I}^\vee$
nodes.label: IAlocalorient

nodes.name: Virtual orientation sheaf
nodes.statement: Let $X$ be a space with locally orientable implicit atlas $A$ with boundary. Then there exists a sheaf $\mathfrak o_{X,A}$ on $X$ equipped with $\Gamma_I$-equivariant isomorphisms $\psi_{\varnothing I}^\ast\mathfrak o_{X,A}\xrightarrow\sim\mathfrak o_{X_I^\mathrm{reg}}\otimes\mathfrak o_{E_I}^\vee$ over $(s_I|X_I^\mathrm{reg})^{-1}(0)$ for every $I\subseteq A$, which are compatible with the maps $\psi_{IJ}$. We call $\mathfrak o_{X,A}$ the \emph{virtual orientation sheaf} of $X$ (it is unique up to unique isomorphism); it is locally isomorphic to the constant sheaf $\underline R$. We write $\mathfrak o_X$ for $\mathfrak o_{X,A}$ when the atlas is clear from context. We let $\mathfrak o_{X\operatorname{rel}\partial}:=j_!j^\ast\mathfrak o_X$ where $j:X\setminus\partial X\hookrightarrow X$.
nodes.statement_short: The virtual orientation sheaf $\mathfrak o_X$: the locally constant sheaf on $X$ pulling back to $\mathfrak o_{X_I^\mathrm{reg}}\otimes\mathfrak o_{E_I}^\vee$ on each chart; and $\mathfrak o_{X\operatorname{rel}\partial}:=j_!j^\ast\mathfrak o_X$.
nodes.label: IAorientationsheaf

nodes.name: Deformation to the normal cone
nodes.statement: Let $X$ be a space with finite implicit atlas $A$ with boundary. For $I\subseteq J\subseteq A$, we define: \begin{equation*} X_{I,J,A}:=\left\{(e,t,x)\in E_A\times\mathbb R_{\geq 0}^A\times X_J^\mathrm{reg}\;\middle|\;\begin{matrix}t_\alpha=0\text{ for }\alpha\in A\setminus I\hfill\cr s_\alpha(x)=t_\alpha e_\alpha\text{ for }\alpha\in J\hfill\cr\psi_{\{\alpha\in A:t_\alpha>0\},J}(x)\in X_{\{\alpha\in A:t_\alpha>0\}}^\mathrm{reg}\hfill\end{matrix}\right\} \end{equation*} The condition $\psi_{\{\alpha\in A:t_\alpha>0\},J}(x)\in X_{\{\alpha\in A:t_\alpha>0\}}^\mathrm{reg}$ ensures that we only deform to the normal cone of those zero sets $s_{J\setminus I'}^{-1}(0)$ which are cut out transversally ($I'\subseteq I$). Clearly $(\partial X)_{I,J,A}\subseteq X_{I,J,A}$ is the subset where $x\in\partial X_J^\mathrm{reg}$ (the former being with respect to the restriction of $A$ to $\partial X$). There are compatible maps: \begin{equation} X_{I,J,A}\times E_{A'\setminus A}\to X_{I',J',A'}\text{ for }I\subseteq I'\subseteq J'\subseteq J\subseteq A\subseteq A' \end{equation} given by $t_{A'\setminus A}=0$ and $x\mapsto\psi_{J',J}(x)$. For $K\subseteq X$, we let $X_{I,J,A}^K\subseteq X_{I,J,A}$ denote the subspace where $e=0$ and $x\in\psi_{\varnothing J}^{-1}(K)$. Note that $\Gamma_A$ acts on $X_{I,J,A}$ (acting on $X_J^\mathrm{reg}$ via the projection $\Gamma_A\to\Gamma_J$ and on $E_A$).
nodes.section: 4.2 Virtual cochain complexes \texorpdfstring{$C^\bullet_\mathrm{vir}(X;A)$}{C\_vir(X;A)} and \texorpdfstring{$C^\bullet_\mathrm{vir}(X\operatorname{rel}\partial;A)$}{C\_vir(X rel d;A)}
nodes.statement_short: Defines the spaces $X_{I,J,A}\subseteq E_A\times\mathbb R_{\geq0}^A\times X_J^\mathrm{reg}$ (deformation to the normal cone), their compatible maps and subspaces $X^K_{I,J,A}$.

nodes.name: Compatible maps between deformations to the normal cone
nodes.statement: X_{I,J,A}\times E_{A'\setminus A}\to X_{I',J',A'}\text{ for }I\subseteq I'\subseteq J'\subseteq J\subseteq A\subseteq A'
nodes.section: 4.2 Virtual cochain complexes \texorpdfstring{$C^\bullet_\mathrm{vir}(X;A)$}{C\_vir(X;A)} and \texorpdfstring{$C^\bullet_\mathrm{vir}(X\operatorname{rel}\partial;A)$}{C\_vir(X rel d;A)}
nodes.label: pushforward

nodes.name: Chains and cochains
nodes.statement: We use $C_\bullet(X)$ (resp.\ $C^\bullet(X)$) to denote singular simplicial chains (resp.\ cochains) on a space $X$, and we use $C_\bullet(X,Y)$ to denote the cokernel of $C_\bullet(Y)\hookrightarrow C_\bullet(X)$ for $Y\subseteq X$ (``relative chains''). Let us also recall the ``Eilenberg--Zilber map'' $C_\bullet(X)\otimes C_\bullet(Y)\to C_\bullet(X\times Y)$ for spaces $X$ and $Y$, corresponding to the standard subdivision of $\Delta^n\times\Delta^m$ into $\binom{n+m}n$ copies of $\Delta^{n+m}$. The Eilenberg--Zilber map is associative (in the sense that it gives rise to a unique map $C_\bullet(X)\otimes C_\bullet(Y)\otimes C_\bullet(Z)\to C_\bullet(X\times Y\times Z)$) and commutative (in the sense that the following diagram commutes: \begin{equation} \begin{CD} C_\bullet(X)\otimes C_\bullet(Y)@>>>C_\bullet(X\times Y)\cr @VVV@VVV\cr C_\bullet(Y)\otimes C_\bullet(X)@>>>C_\bullet(Y\times X) \end{CD} \end{equation} for all $X$ and $Y$). We should point out that this commutativity fails for some other common models of singular chains, for example singular cubical chains (modulo degeneracies).
nodes.section: 4.2 Virtual cochain complexes \texorpdfstring{$C^\bullet_\mathrm{vir}(X;A)$}{C\_vir(X;A)} and \texorpdfstring{$C^\bullet_\mathrm{vir}(X\operatorname{rel}\partial;A)$}{C\_vir(X rel d;A)}
nodes.statement_short: Fixes singular simplicial (co)chains and recalls the associative, commutative Eilenberg--Zilber map.
nodes.label: chainfixing

nodes.name: Commutativity of the Eilenberg--Zilber map
nodes.statement: \begin{CD} C_\bullet(X)\otimes C_\bullet(Y)@>>>C_\bullet(X\times Y)\cr @VVV@VVV\cr C_\bullet(Y)\otimes C_\bullet(X)@>>>C_\bullet(Y\times X) \end{CD}
nodes.section: 4.2 Virtual cochain complexes \texorpdfstring{$C^\bullet_\mathrm{vir}(X;A)$}{C\_vir(X;A)} and \texorpdfstring{$C^\bullet_\mathrm{vir}(X\operatorname{rel}\partial;A)$}{C\_vir(X rel d;A)}
nodes.label: chainproductcommutes

nodes.name: Independence of chain model
nodes.statement: The particular choice of \emph{singular simplicial} chains is not particularly important. The virtual fundamental classes, etc.\ resulting from our theory should be unchanged by using any other model of singular chains. This independence would follow immediately (and all issues about finding chain models with good chain level functoriality properties would go away) if we setup the VFC package using $\infty$-categories.
nodes.section: 4.2 Virtual cochain complexes \texorpdfstring{$C^\bullet_\mathrm{vir}(X;A)$}{C\_vir(X;A)} and \texorpdfstring{$C^\bullet_\mathrm{vir}(X\operatorname{rel}\partial;A)$}{C\_vir(X rel d;A)}
nodes.label: independenceofchainmodel

nodes.name: Fundamental cycles of vector spaces
nodes.statement: Let $I$ be a finite subset of an implicit atlas $A$. We define: \begin{equation} C_\bullet(E;I):=C_{\dim E_I+\bullet}(E_I,E_I\setminus 0;\mathfrak o_{E_I}^\vee)^{\Gamma_I} \end{equation} There is a canonical isomorphism $H_\bullet(E;I)=R$ (concentrated in degree zero), and we denote the canonical generator by $[E_I]\in H_\bullet(E;I)$.
nodes.section: 4.2 Virtual cochain complexes \texorpdfstring{$C^\bullet_\mathrm{vir}(X;A)$}{C\_vir(X;A)} and \texorpdfstring{$C^\bullet_\mathrm{vir}(X\operatorname{rel}\partial;A)$}{C\_vir(X rel d;A)}
nodes.statement_short: Defines $C_\bullet(E;I)$ as invariant relative chains of $(E_I,E_I\setminus0)$ with fundamental class $[E_I]$.

nodes.name: Definition of $C_\bullet(E;I)$
nodes.statement: C_\bullet(E;I):=C_{\dim E_I+\bullet}(E_I,E_I\setminus 0;\mathfrak o_{E_I}^\vee)^{\Gamma_I}
nodes.section: 4.2 Virtual cochain complexes \texorpdfstring{$C^\bullet_\mathrm{vir}(X;A)$}{C\_vir(X;A)} and \texorpdfstring{$C^\bullet_\mathrm{vir}(X\operatorname{rel}\partial;A)$}{C\_vir(X rel d;A)}

nodes.name: Partial virtual cochain complexes
nodes.statement: Let $X$ be a space with finite implicit atlas $A$ of dimension $d$ with boundary. For any compact $K\subseteq X$, we define: \begin{align} C^\bullet_\mathrm{vir}(K\operatorname{rel}\partial;A)_{IJ}&:=C_{d+\dim E_A-\bullet}(X_{I,J,A},X_{I,J,A}\setminus X_{I,J,A}^K;\mathfrak o_{E_A}^\vee)^{\Gamma_A}\\ C^\bullet_\mathrm{vir}(K;A)_{IJ}&:=\left[\begin{matrix}C_{d+\dim E_A-1-\bullet}((\partial X)_{I,J,A},(\partial X)_{I,J,A}\setminus(\partial X)_{I,J,A}^{K\cap\partial X};\mathfrak o_{E_A}^\vee)^{\Gamma_A}\hfill\cr\downarrow\cr C_{d+\dim E_A-\bullet}(X_{I,J,A},X_{I,J,A}\setminus X_{I,J,A}^K;\mathfrak o_{E_A}^\vee)^{\Gamma_A}\hfill\end{matrix}\right] \end{align} It is clear that $K\mapsto C^\bullet_\mathrm{vir}(K;A)_{IJ}$ and $K\mapsto C^\bullet_\mathrm{vir}(K\operatorname{rel}\partial;A)_{IJ}$ are both complexes of $\mathcal K$-presheaves on $X$. There are canonical maps: \begin{align} C^\bullet_\mathrm{vir}(K\operatorname{rel}\partial;A)_{IJ}&\to C^\bullet_\mathrm{vir}(K;A)_{IJ}\\ C^{d+\bullet}_\mathrm{vir}(X\operatorname{rel}\partial;A)_{IJ}&\xrightarrow{s_\ast}C_{-\bullet}(E;A)\\ \hspace{1.5in}C^\bullet_\mathrm{vir}(-;A)_{IJ}&\to C^\bullet_\mathrm{vir}(-;A)_{I',J'}\text{ for }I\subseteq I'\subseteq J'\subseteq J \end{align} (\eqref{Ethompushforward} is induced by the projection $X_{I,J,A}\to E_A$, and \eqref{Epushforward1} is induced by \eqref{pushforward} with $A=A'$). These are compatible with each other in that certain obvious diagrams commute.
nodes.section: 4.2 Virtual cochain complexes \texorpdfstring{$C^\bullet_\mathrm{vir}(X;A)$}{C\_vir(X;A)} and \texorpdfstring{$C^\bullet_\mathrm{vir}(X\operatorname{rel}\partial;A)$}{C\_vir(X rel d;A)}
nodes.statement_short: Defines partial virtual cochain complexes as invariant relative chains of $X_{I,J,A}$ (relative to boundary or as a cone), with pullback, Thom pushforward and structure maps.
nodes.label: CSTcomplexdef

nodes.name: Definition of partial virtual cochain complexes
nodes.statement: C^\bullet_\mathrm{vir}(K\operatorname{rel}\partial;A)_{IJ}&:=C_{d+\dim E_A-\bullet}(X_{I,J,A},X_{I,J,A}\setminus X_{I,J,A}^K;\mathfrak o_{E_A}^\vee)^{\Gamma_A}\\ C^\bullet_\mathrm{vir}(K;A)_{IJ}&:=\left[\begin{matrix}C_{d+\dim E_A-1-\bullet}((\partial X)_{I,J,A},(\partial X)_{I,J,A}\setminus(\partial X)_{I,J,A}^{K\cap\partial X};\mathfrak o_{E_A}^\vee)^{\Gamma_A}\hfill\cr\downarrow\cr C_{d+\dim E_A-\bullet}(X_{I,J,A},X_{I,J,A}\setminus X_{I,J,A}^K;\mathfrak o_{E_A}^\vee)^{\Gamma_A}\hfill\end{matrix}\right]
nodes.section: 4.2 Virtual cochain complexes \texorpdfstring{$C^\bullet_\mathrm{vir}(X;A)$}{C\_vir(X;A)} and \texorpdfstring{$C^\bullet_\mathrm{vir}(X\operatorname{rel}\partial;A)$}{C\_vir(X rel d;A)}
nodes.label: CcomplexcriticaldefI

nodes.name: Canonical maps of partial virtual cochain complexes
nodes.statement: C^\bullet_\mathrm{vir}(K\operatorname{rel}\partial;A)_{IJ}&\to C^\bullet_\mathrm{vir}(K;A)_{IJ}\\ C^{d+\bullet}_\mathrm{vir}(X\operatorname{rel}\partial;A)_{IJ}&\xrightarrow{s_\ast}C_{-\bullet}(E;A)\\ \hspace{1.5in}C^\bullet_\mathrm{vir}(-;A)_{IJ}&\to C^\bullet_\mathrm{vir}(-;A)_{I',J'}\text{ for }I\subseteq I'\subseteq J'\subseteq J
nodes.section: 4.2 Virtual cochain complexes \texorpdfstring{$C^\bullet_\mathrm{vir}(X;A)$}{C\_vir(X;A)} and \texorpdfstring{$C^\bullet_\mathrm{vir}(X\operatorname{rel}\partial;A)$}{C\_vir(X rel d;A)}
nodes.label: Erelpartialpullback

nodes.name: Virtual cochain complexes
nodes.statement: Let $X$ be a space with finite implicit atlas $A$ of dimension $d$ with boundary. For any compact $K\subseteq X$, we define: \begin{align} C^\bullet_\mathrm{vir}(K;A)&:=\operatornamewithlimits{hocolim}_{I\subseteq J\subseteq A}C^\bullet_\mathrm{vir}(K;A)_{IJ}\\ C^\bullet_\mathrm{vir}(K\operatorname{rel}\partial;A)&:=\operatornamewithlimits{hocolim}_{I\subseteq J\subseteq A}C^\bullet_\mathrm{vir}(K\operatorname{rel}\partial;A)_{IJ} \end{align} where $\operatornamewithlimits{hocolim}_{I\subseteq J\subseteq A}$ is the homotopy colimit (Definition \ref{homotopycolimit}) over $2^A$ with structure maps given by $(\#\Gamma_{J\setminus J'})^{-1}$ times \eqref{Epushforward1}. It is clear that $K\mapsto C^\bullet_\mathrm{vir}(K;A)$ and $K\mapsto C^\bullet_\mathrm{vir}(K\operatorname{rel}\partial;A)$ are both complexes of $\mathcal K$-presheaves on $X$. There are canonical maps: \begin{align} C^\bullet_\mathrm{vir}(K\operatorname{rel}\partial;A)&\to C^\bullet_\mathrm{vir}(K;A)\\ C^{d+\bullet}_\mathrm{vir}(X\operatorname{rel}\partial;A)&\xrightarrow{s_\ast}C_{-\bullet}(E;A) \end{align} (induced by \eqref{Erelpartialpullback}--\eqref{Ethompushforward}). More precisely, \eqref{Fpushforward} is given by \eqref{Ethompushforward} on the $p=0$ part of the $\operatornamewithlimits{hocolim}$ and is zero on the rest.
nodes.section: 4.2 Virtual cochain complexes \texorpdfstring{$C^\bullet_\mathrm{vir}(X;A)$}{C\_vir(X;A)} and \texorpdfstring{$C^\bullet_\mathrm{vir}(X\operatorname{rel}\partial;A)$}{C\_vir(X rel d;A)}
nodes.statement_short: Defines virtual cochain complexes as homotopy colimits over $I\subseteq J\subseteq A$ of the partial complexes, with maps rel boundary and the pushforward $s_\ast$.
nodes.label: Ccomplexdef

nodes.name: Virtual cochain complexes as homotopy colimits
nodes.statement: C^\bullet_\mathrm{vir}(K;A)&:=\operatornamewithlimits{hocolim}_{I\subseteq J\subseteq A}C^\bullet_\mathrm{vir}(K;A)_{IJ}\\ C^\bullet_\mathrm{vir}(K\operatorname{rel}\partial;A)&:=\operatornamewithlimits{hocolim}_{I\subseteq J\subseteq A}C^\bullet_\mathrm{vir}(K\operatorname{rel}\partial;A)_{IJ}
nodes.section: 4.2 Virtual cochain complexes \texorpdfstring{$C^\bullet_\mathrm{vir}(X;A)$}{C\_vir(X;A)} and \texorpdfstring{$C^\bullet_\mathrm{vir}(X\operatorname{rel}\partial;A)$}{C\_vir(X rel d;A)}
nodes.label: CvirdefI

nodes.name: Canonical maps $s_\ast$ and rel-boundary pullback
nodes.statement: C^\bullet_\mathrm{vir}(K\operatorname{rel}\partial;A)&\to C^\bullet_\mathrm{vir}(K;A)\\ C^{d+\bullet}_\mathrm{vir}(X\operatorname{rel}\partial;A)&\xrightarrow{s_\ast}C_{-\bullet}(E;A)
nodes.section: 4.2 Virtual cochain complexes \texorpdfstring{$C^\bullet_\mathrm{vir}(X;A)$}{C\_vir(X;A)} and \texorpdfstring{$C^\bullet_\mathrm{vir}(X\operatorname{rel}\partial;A)$}{C\_vir(X rel d;A)}
nodes.label: Frelpartialpullback

nodes.name: Maps $C^\bullet_\mathrm{vir}(-;A)\to C^\bullet_\mathrm{vir}(-;A')$
nodes.statement: Let $X$ be a space with finite implicit atlases $A\subseteq A'$ with boundary. There are canonical maps: \begin{equation} C^\bullet_\mathrm{vir}(-;A)_{IJ}\otimes C_{-\bullet}(E;A'\setminus A)\to C^\bullet_\mathrm{vir}(-;A')_{I',J'}\text{ for }I\subseteq I'\subseteq J'\subseteq J\subseteq A\subseteq A' \end{equation} induced by \eqref{pushforward} (of which \eqref{Epushforward1} is a special case). These are compatible with each other, and thus extend to the homotopy colimit over $I\subseteq J\subseteq A$. Hence we get canonical maps: \begin{equation} C^\bullet_\mathrm{vir}(-;A)\otimes C_{-\bullet}(E;A'\setminus A)\to C^\bullet_\mathrm{vir}(-;A') \end{equation} which are compatible with \eqref{Frelpartialpullback}--\eqref{Fpushforward}.
nodes.section: 4.2 Virtual cochain complexes \texorpdfstring{$C^\bullet_\mathrm{vir}(X;A)$}{C\_vir(X;A)} and \texorpdfstring{$C^\bullet_\mathrm{vir}(X\operatorname{rel}\partial;A)$}{C\_vir(X rel d;A)}
nodes.statement_short: For finite atlases $A\subseteq A'$, constructs canonical maps $C^\bullet_\mathrm{vir}(-;A)\otimes C_{-\bullet}(E;A'\setminus A)\to C^\bullet_\mathrm{vir}(-;A')$.

nodes.name: Maps of partial virtual cochain complexes for $A\subseteq A'$
nodes.statement: C^\bullet_\mathrm{vir}(-;A)_{IJ}\otimes C_{-\bullet}(E;A'\setminus A)\to C^\bullet_\mathrm{vir}(-;A')_{I',J'}\text{ for }I\subseteq I'\subseteq J'\subseteq J\subseteq A\subseteq A'
nodes.section: 4.2 Virtual cochain complexes \texorpdfstring{$C^\bullet_\mathrm{vir}(X;A)$}{C\_vir(X;A)} and \texorpdfstring{$C^\bullet_\mathrm{vir}(X\operatorname{rel}\partial;A)$}{C\_vir(X rel d;A)}
nodes.label: Epushforward1more

nodes.name: Map $C^\bullet_\mathrm{vir}(-;A)\otimes C_{-\bullet}(E;A'\setminus A)\to C^\bullet_\mathrm{vir}(-;A')$
nodes.statement: C^\bullet_\mathrm{vir}(-;A)\otimes C_{-\bullet}(E;A'\setminus A)\to C^\bullet_\mathrm{vir}(-;A')
nodes.section: 4.2 Virtual cochain complexes \texorpdfstring{$C^\bullet_\mathrm{vir}(X;A)$}{C\_vir(X;A)} and \texorpdfstring{$C^\bullet_\mathrm{vir}(X\operatorname{rel}\partial;A)$}{C\_vir(X rel d;A)}
nodes.label: Fpushforward1

nodes.name: Virtual cochain complexes are free and compatible with base change
nodes.statement: Note that all of the complexes defined here are free $R$-modules (this follows from our assumption that $\#\Gamma_\alpha$ be invertible in $R$) and that everything in sight is compatible with base change $\otimes_RS$ for ring homomorphisms $R\to S$.
assumptions: our assumption that $\#\Gamma_\alpha$ be invertible in $R$
conclusions: all of the complexes defined here are free $R$-modules
everything in sight is compatible with base change $\otimes_RS$ for ring homomorphisms $R\to S$
nodes.section: 4.2 Virtual cochain complexes \texorpdfstring{$C^\bullet_\mathrm{vir}(X;A)$}{C\_vir(X;A)} and \texorpdfstring{$C^\bullet_\mathrm{vir}(X\operatorname{rel}\partial;A)$}{C\_vir(X rel d;A)}

nodes.name: Partial virtual cochain complexes are pure homotopy $\mathcal K$-sheaves
nodes.statement: Let $X$ be a space with finite locally orientable implicit atlas $A$ with boundary. Then $C^\bullet_\mathrm{vir}(-;A)_{IJ}$ and $C^\bullet_\mathrm{vir}(-\operatorname{rel}\partial;A)_{IJ}$ are pure homotopy $\mathcal K$-sheaves on $X$. Furthermore, there are canonical isomorphisms of sheaves on $X$: \begin{align} H^0_\mathrm{vir}(-;A)_{IJ}&=j_!j^\ast\mathfrak o_X\\ H^0_\mathrm{vir}(-\operatorname{rel}\partial;A)_{IJ}&=j_!j^\ast\mathfrak o_{X\operatorname{rel}\partial} \end{align} where $j:V_I\cap V_J\hookrightarrow X$ for $V_I:=\psi_{\varnothing I}((s_I|X_I^\mathrm{reg})^{-1}(0))\subseteq X$ (an open subset).
nodes.statement_short: The partial virtual cochain complexes are pure homotopy $\mathcal K$-sheaves whose $H^0$ is $j_!j^\ast\mathfrak o_X$ for $j:V_I\cap V_J\hookrightarrow X$.
assumptions: Let $X$ be a space with finite locally orientable implicit atlas $A$ with boundary.
conclusions: $C^\bullet_\mathrm{vir}(-;A)_{IJ}$ and $C^\bullet_\mathrm{vir}(-\operatorname{rel}\partial;A)_{IJ}$ are pure homotopy $\mathcal K$-sheaves on $X$
nodes.label: CSTpure

nodes.name: $H^0$ of partial virtual cochain complexes
nodes.statement: H^0_\mathrm{vir}(-;A)_{IJ}&=j_!j^\ast\mathfrak o_X\\ H^0_\mathrm{vir}(-\operatorname{rel}\partial;A)_{IJ}&=j_!j^\ast\mathfrak o_{X\operatorname{rel}\partial}
nodes.label: EisoI

nodes.name: Proof
nodes.statement: Applying Lemmas \ref{singularchainshomotopyKsheaf} and \ref{associatedgradedhomotopysheaf}, we see that $C^\bullet_\mathrm{vir}(-;A)_{IJ}$ and $C^\bullet_\mathrm{vir}(-\operatorname{rel}\partial;A)_{IJ}$ are both homotopy $\mathcal K$-sheaves. Now let us calculate $H^\bullet_\mathrm{vir}(K;A)_{IJ}$ and $H^\bullet_\mathrm{vir}(K\operatorname{rel}\partial;A)_{IJ}$. It follows from the submersion axiom that $X_{I,J,A}$ is a topological manifold of dimension $\operatorname{vdim}_AX+\dim E_A+\#I$ with boundary (not necessarily second countable or paracompact).\footnote{In fact, it carries a natural structure of a manifold with corners, which for the present purpose is mostly irrelevant.} The boundary $\partial(X_{I,J,A})$ is a (not necessarily disjoint) union of two pieces, namely the locus where $x\in\partial X_J^\mathrm{reg}$ (which is precisely $(\partial X)_{I,J,A}$) and the locus where $t_\alpha=0$ for some $\alpha\in I$. It is easy to see that the first piece $(\partial X)_{I,J,A}\subseteq\partial(X_{I,J,A})$ is a closed tamely embedded codimension zero submanifold with boundary. Hence we may apply Poincar\'e--Lefschetz duality in the form of Lemma \ref{poincareduality} to see that: \begin{align} H^\bullet_\mathrm{vir}(K\operatorname{rel}\partial;A)_{IJ}&=\check H_c^{\bullet+\#I}(\psi_{\varnothing J}^{-1}(K\cap V_I\cap V_J)\times\mathbb R_{>0}^I,\mathfrak o_\mathbb R^{\otimes I}\otimes\mathfrak o_{E_J}^\vee\otimes\mathfrak o_{X_J^\mathrm{reg}\operatorname{rel}\partial})^{\Gamma_A}\\ H^\bullet_\mathrm{vir}(K;A)_{IJ}&=\check H_c^{\bullet+\#I}(\psi_{\varnothing J}^{-1}(K\cap V_I\cap V_J)\times\mathbb R_{>0}^I,\mathfrak o_\mathbb R^{\otimes I}\otimes\mathfrak o_{E_J}^\vee\otimes\mathfrak o_{X_J^\mathrm{reg}})^{\Gamma_A} \end{align} (the orientation sheaf of $X_{I,J,A}$ is given by $\mathfrak o_{X_J^\mathrm{reg}}\otimes\mathfrak o_{E_A}\otimes\mathfrak o_{E_J}^\vee\otimes\mathfrak o_\mathbb R^{\otimes I}$). Now we apply the K\"unneth formula to conclude that: \begin{align} H^\bullet_\mathrm{vir}(K\operatorname{rel}\partial;A)_{IJ}&=\check H^\bullet_c(\psi_{\varnothing J}^{-1}(K\cap V_I\cap V_J),\mathfrak o_{E_J}^\vee\otimes\mathfrak o_{X_J^\mathrm{reg}\operatorname{rel}\partial})^{\Gamma_A}\\ H^\bullet_\mathrm{vir}(K;A)_{IJ}&=\check H^\bullet_c(\psi_{\varnothing J}^{-1}(K\cap V_I\cap V_J),\mathfrak o_{E_J}^\vee\otimes\mathfrak o_{X_J^\mathrm{reg}})^{\Gamma_A} \end{align} Since $X$ is locally orientable, we have $\mathfrak o_{X_J^\mathrm{reg}}\otimes\mathfrak o_{E_J}^\vee=\psi_{\varnothing J}^\ast\mathfrak o_X$, so we can write: \begin{align} H^\bullet_\mathrm{vir}(K\operatorname{rel}\partial;A)_{IJ}&=\check H^\bullet_c(\psi_{\varnothing J}^{-1}(K\cap V_I\cap V_J),\psi_{\varnothing J}^\ast\mathfrak o_{X\operatorname{rel}\partial})^{\Gamma_A}\\ H^\bullet_\mathrm{vir}(K;A)_{IJ}&=\check H^\bullet_c(\psi_{\varnothing J}^{-1}(K\cap V_I\cap V_J),\psi_{\varnothing J}^\ast\mathfrak o_X)^{\Gamma_A} \end{align} Now $\Gamma_A$ acts through the projection $\Gamma_A\to\Gamma_J$, and $\psi_{\varnothing J}:\psi_{\varnothing J}^{-1}(K\cap V_I\cap V_J)\to K\cap V_I\cap V_J$ is exactly the quotient by $\Gamma_J$. Hence by Lemma \ref{cechcohomologyfinitequotient} we get isomorphisms: \begin{align} H^\bullet_\mathrm{vir}(K\operatorname{rel}\partial;A)_{IJ}&=\check H^\bullet_c(K\cap V_I\cap V_J,\mathfrak o_{X\operatorname{rel}\partial})\\ H^\bullet_\mathrm{vir}(K;A)_{IJ}&=\check H^\bullet_c(K\cap V_I\cap V_J,\mathfrak o_X) \end{align} Now use Lemma \ref{cptcechembeddingproperty} to write this as: \begin{align} H^\bullet_\mathrm{vir}(K\operatorname{rel}\partial;A)_{IJ}&=\check H^\bullet(K,j_!j^\ast\mathfrak o_{X\operatorname{rel}\partial})\\ H^\bullet_\mathrm{vir}(K;A)_{IJ}&=\check H^\bullet(K,j_!j^\ast\mathfrak o_X) \end{align} Thus $C^\bullet_\mathrm{vir}(-;A)_{IJ}$ and $C^\bullet_\mathrm{vir}(-\operatorname{rel}\partial;A)_{IJ}$ are both pure, and we manifestly have the desired isomorphisms \eqref{EisoI}--\eqref{EisoII}.
nodes.statement_short: Homotopy sheaf property from general lemmas; then compute cohomology via Poincar\'e--Lefschetz duality on the manifold $X_{I,J,A}$, K\"unneth, local orientability and finite quotients.

nodes.name: Poincar\'e--Lefschetz duality for $X_{I,J,A}$
nodes.statement: H^\bullet_\mathrm{vir}(K\operatorname{rel}\partial;A)_{IJ}&=\check H_c^{\bullet+\#I}(\psi_{\varnothing J}^{-1}(K\cap V_I\cap V_J)\times\mathbb R_{>0}^I,\mathfrak o_\mathbb R^{\otimes I}\otimes\mathfrak o_{E_J}^\vee\otimes\mathfrak o_{X_J^\mathrm{reg}\operatorname{rel}\partial})^{\Gamma_A}\\ H^\bullet_\mathrm{vir}(K;A)_{IJ}&=\check H_c^{\bullet+\#I}(\psi_{\varnothing J}^{-1}(K\cap V_I\cap V_J)\times\mathbb R_{>0}^I,\mathfrak o_\mathbb R^{\otimes I}\otimes\mathfrak o_{E_J}^\vee\otimes\mathfrak o_{X_J^\mathrm{reg}})^{\Gamma_A}

nodes.name: K\"unneth reduction
nodes.statement: H^\bullet_\mathrm{vir}(K\operatorname{rel}\partial;A)_{IJ}&=\check H^\bullet_c(\psi_{\varnothing J}^{-1}(K\cap V_I\cap V_J),\mathfrak o_{E_J}^\vee\otimes\mathfrak o_{X_J^\mathrm{reg}\operatorname{rel}\partial})^{\Gamma_A}\\ H^\bullet_\mathrm{vir}(K;A)_{IJ}&=\check H^\bullet_c(\psi_{\varnothing J}^{-1}(K\cap V_I\cap V_J),\mathfrak o_{E_J}^\vee\otimes\mathfrak o_{X_J^\mathrm{reg}})^{\Gamma_A}

nodes.name: Rewriting via local orientability
nodes.statement: H^\bullet_\mathrm{vir}(K\operatorname{rel}\partial;A)_{IJ}&=\check H^\bullet_c(\psi_{\varnothing J}^{-1}(K\cap V_I\cap V_J),\psi_{\varnothing J}^\ast\mathfrak o_{X\operatorname{rel}\partial})^{\Gamma_A}\\ H^\bullet_\mathrm{vir}(K;A)_{IJ}&=\check H^\bullet_c(\psi_{\varnothing J}^{-1}(K\cap V_I\cap V_J),\psi_{\varnothing J}^\ast\mathfrak o_X)^{\Gamma_A}

nodes.name: Quotient by $\Gamma_J$
nodes.statement: H^\bullet_\mathrm{vir}(K\operatorname{rel}\partial;A)_{IJ}&=\check H^\bullet_c(K\cap V_I\cap V_J,\mathfrak o_{X\operatorname{rel}\partial})\\ H^\bullet_\mathrm{vir}(K;A)_{IJ}&=\check H^\bullet_c(K\cap V_I\cap V_J,\mathfrak o_X)

nodes.name: Partial virtual cohomology as \v Cech cohomology of $j_!j^\ast\mathfrak o_X$
nodes.statement: H^\bullet_\mathrm{vir}(K\operatorname{rel}\partial;A)_{IJ}&=\check H^\bullet(K,j_!j^\ast\mathfrak o_{X\operatorname{rel}\partial})\\ H^\bullet_\mathrm{vir}(K;A)_{IJ}&=\check H^\bullet(K,j_!j^\ast\mathfrak o_X)

nodes.name: Local description of isomorphisms $H^0_\mathrm{vir}(-;A)_{II}=j_!j^\ast\mathfrak o_X$
nodes.statement: Let $X$ be a space with finite locally orientable implicit atlas $A$ of dimension $d$ with boundary. Consider the following maps of complexes of $\mathcal K$-presheaves on $X$: \begin{align} C^\bullet_\mathrm{vir}(K;A)_{II}&\leftarrow\left[\begin{matrix}C_{d+\dim E_A-1-\bullet}(E_{A\setminus I}\times\partial X_I^\mathrm{reg},E_{A\setminus I}\times(\partial X_I^\mathrm{reg}\setminus\psi_{\varnothing I}^{-1}(K));\mathfrak o_{E_A}^\vee)^{\Gamma_A}\hfill\cr\downarrow\cr C_{d+\dim E_A-\bullet}(E_{A\setminus I}\times X_I^\mathrm{reg},E_{A\setminus I}\times(X_I^\mathrm{reg}\setminus\psi_{\varnothing I}^{-1}(K));\mathfrak o_{E_A}^\vee)^{\Gamma_A}\hfill\end{matrix}\right]\\ C^\bullet_\mathrm{vir}(K\operatorname{rel}\partial;A)_{II}&\leftarrow C_{d+\dim E_A-\bullet}(E_{A\setminus I}\times X_I^\mathrm{reg},E_{A\setminus I}\times(X_I^\mathrm{reg}\setminus\psi_{\varnothing I}^{-1}(K));\mathfrak o_{E_A}^\vee)^{\Gamma_A} \end{align} (induced by the corresponding maps on spaces). These maps are quasi-isomorphisms, and the isomorphisms \eqref{EisoI}--\eqref{EisoII} from Lemma \ref{CSTpure} coincide with the Poincar\'e duality isomorphisms for the complexes on the right above.
nodes.statement_short: The $(I,I)$ partial virtual cochain complexes are quasi-isomorphic to relative chains on $E_{A\setminus I}\times X_I^\mathrm{reg}$, under which the isomorphisms are Poincar\'e duality.
assumptions: Let $X$ be a space with finite locally orientable implicit atlas $A$ of dimension $d$ with boundary.
conclusions: These maps are quasi-isomorphisms, and the isomorphisms \eqref{EisoI}--\eqref{EisoII} from Lemma \ref{CSTpure} coincide with the Poincar\'e duality isomorphisms for the complexes on the right above.

nodes.name: Virtual cochain complexes are pure homotopy $\mathcal K$-sheaves
nodes.statement: Let $X$ be a space with finite locally orientable implicit atlas $A$ with boundary. Then $C^\bullet_\mathrm{vir}(-;A)$ and $C^\bullet_\mathrm{vir}(-\operatorname{rel}\partial;A)$ are pure homotopy $\mathcal K$-sheaves on $X$. Furthermore, there are canonical isomorphisms of sheaves on $X$: \begin{align} H^0_\mathrm{vir}(-;A)&=\mathfrak o_X\\ H^0_\mathrm{vir}(-\operatorname{rel}\partial;A)&=\mathfrak o_{X\operatorname{rel}\partial} \end{align}

assumptions: Let $X$ be a space with finite locally orientable implicit atlas $A$ with boundary.
conclusions: $C^\bullet_\mathrm{vir}(-;A)$ and $C^\bullet_\mathrm{vir}(-\operatorname{rel}\partial;A)$ are pure homotopy $\mathcal K$-sheaves on $X$

nodes.name: Proof
nodes.statement: This is a special case of Lemma \ref{gluingcechsimple}; we just need to make sure all of the hypotheses are satisfied. The open cover in question is $V_I:=\psi_{\varnothing I}((s_I|X_I^\mathrm{reg})^{-1}(0))$; it follows from the axioms of an implicit atlas that $V_I\cap V_K\subseteq V_J$ for $I\subseteq J\subseteq K$ and $V_I\cap V_{I'}\subseteq V_{I\cup I'}$ for all $I,I'$. Now we just need to check that the system of isomorphisms from Lemma \ref{CSTpure} are compatible with the maps of the homotopy diagram. These being maps of sheaves, it suffices to check compatibility locally (on stalks) and thus is a straightforward calculation (this is where the extra normalization factor of $(\#\Gamma_{J\setminus J'})^{-1}$ in Definition \ref{Ccomplexdef} is important).
nodes.statement_short: Special case of the gluing lemma for homotopy colimits of pure homotopy $\mathcal K$-sheaves; verify the cover hypotheses and stalkwise compatibility of the isomorphisms.

nodes.name: Calculation of $H^\bullet_\mathrm{vir}$
nodes.statement: Let $X$ be a space with finite locally orientable implicit atlas $A$ with boundary. Then there are canonical isomorphisms: \begin{align} H^\bullet_\mathrm{vir}(X;A)&=\check H^\bullet(X;\mathfrak o_X)\\ H^\bullet_\mathrm{vir}(X\operatorname{rel}\partial;A)&=\check H^\bullet(X;\mathfrak o_{X\operatorname{rel}\partial}) \end{align}
nodes.statement_short: Virtual cohomology is canonically isomorphic to \v Cech cohomology of $X$ with coefficients in the virtual orientation sheaf (also rel boundary).
assumptions: Let $X$ be a space with finite locally orientable implicit atlas $A$ with boundary.
conclusions: H^\bullet_\mathrm{vir}(X;A)&=\check H^\bullet(X;\mathfrak o_X)

nodes.name: Long exact sequence of virtual cochain complexes of $(X,\partial X)$
nodes.statement: It follows from the definition that $C^\bullet_\mathrm{vir}(K;A)_{IJ}$ is the mapping cone of the obvious map $C^{\bullet-1}_\mathrm{vir}(K\cap\partial X;A)_{IJ}\to C^\bullet_\mathrm{vir}(K\operatorname{rel}\partial;A)_{IJ}$. Since homotopy colimit commutes with the formation of mapping cones, we see that the same is true dropping the $_{IJ}$ subscript. Hence there are natural maps: \begin{equation} \cdots\to C^{\bullet-1}_\mathrm{vir}(K\cap\partial X;A)\to C^\bullet_\mathrm{vir}(K\operatorname{rel}\partial;A)\to C^\bullet_\mathrm{vir}(K;A)\to\cdots \end{equation} and they induce a long exact sequence on cohomology.
nodes.statement_short: $C^\bullet_\mathrm{vir}(K;A)$ is the mapping cone of $C^{\bullet-1}_\mathrm{vir}(K\cap\partial X;A)\to C^\bullet_\mathrm{vir}(K\operatorname{rel}\partial;A)$, giving a long exact sequence.
conclusions: $C^\bullet_\mathrm{vir}(K;A)_{IJ}$ is the mapping cone of the obvious map $C^{\bullet-1}_\mathrm{vir}(K\cap\partial X;A)_{IJ}\to C^\bullet_\mathrm{vir}(K\operatorname{rel}\partial;A)_{IJ}$

This induces a long exact sequence on \v Cech cohomology (Lemma \ref{cechles}). Note that $\check H^\bullet(X;i_\ast\mathfrak o_{\partial X})=\check H^\bullet(\partial X;\mathfrak o_{\partial X})$ (Lemma \ref{finitemap}).

nodes.name: Orientation conventions at the boundary
nodes.statement: To be slightly pedantic about orientations, it would be more precise to say that $C^\bullet_\mathrm{vir}(-;A)=[C^\bullet_\mathrm{vir}(-\cap\partial X;A)\otimes\mathfrak o_\mathbb R\to C^\bullet_\mathrm{vir}(-\operatorname{rel}\partial;A)]$, where we identify $\mathfrak o_\mathbb R$ canonically with the orientation line of the normal bundle of $\partial X_I^\mathrm{reg}\subseteq X_I^\mathrm{reg}$. Also, note that we should either say that the last map in \eqref{sesofO} is odd or that it is really $\mathfrak o_X\to i_\ast\mathfrak o_{\partial X}\otimes\mathfrak o_\mathbb R$ (and is even).

nodes.name: Proof
nodes.statement: By the definition of the vertical identifications, the commutativity of the first two squares of \eqref{compatibilityoflesdiagram} reduces to the commutativity of the diagram of sheaves: \begin{equation} \begin{tikzcd} H^0_\mathrm{vir}(-\operatorname{rel}\partial;A)\ar{r}{\eqref{sesofF}}\ar[equal]{d}{\text{Prop \ref{Cpure}}}&H^0_\mathrm{vir}(-;A)\ar{r}{\eqref{sesofF}}\ar[equal]{d}{\text{Prop \ref{Cpure}}}&H^0_\mathrm{vir}(-;A)\ar[equal]{d}{\text{Prop \ref{Cpure}}}\\ \mathfrak o_{X\operatorname{rel}\partial}\ar{r}{\eqref{sesofO}}&\mathfrak o_X\ar{r}{\eqref{sesofO}}&i_\ast\mathfrak o_{\partial X} \end{tikzcd} \end{equation} It suffices to check commutativity on stalks, and to do this, we can work with the complexes on the right in Lemma \ref{localdescofISO}, for which the commutativity is clear. In fact, the commutativity of the last square of \eqref{compatibilityoflesdiagram} is also a consequence of the commutativity of \eqref{sheafcommutativity}. To see this, consider the following diagram: \begin{equation*} \begin{tikzcd}[column sep = small] H^\bullet_\mathrm{vir}(\partial X;A)\ar[equal]{d}{\text{Prop \ref{cechcohomologypurehomotopysheaf}}}&\ar{l}[swap]{\sim}H^\bullet[C^{\bullet+1}_\mathrm{vir}(X\operatorname{rel}\partial;A)\to C^\bullet_\mathrm{vir}(X;A)]\ar{r}\ar[equal]{d}{\text{Prop \ref{cechcohomologypurehomotopysheaf}}}&H^{\bullet+1}_\mathrm{vir}(X\operatorname{rel}\partial;A)\ar[equal]{d}{\text{Prop \ref{cechcohomologypurehomotopysheaf}}}\\ \check H^\bullet(\partial X;H^0_\mathrm{vir}(-;A))\ar{d}{\sim}&\ar{l}[swap]{\sim}\check H^\bullet(X;[H^0_\mathrm{vir}(-\operatorname{rel}\partial;A)[1]\to H^0_\mathrm{vir}(-;A)])\ar{r}\ar{d}{\sim}&\check H^{\bullet+1}(X,H^0_\mathrm{vir}(-\operatorname{rel}\partial;A))\ar{d}{\sim}\\ \check H^\bullet(\partial X;\mathfrak o_{\partial X})&\ar{l}[swap]{\sim}\check H^\bullet(X;[\mathfrak o_{X\operatorname{rel}\partial}[1]\to\mathfrak o_X])\ar{r}&\check H^{\bullet+1}(X,\mathfrak o_{X\operatorname{rel}\partial}) \end{tikzcd} \end{equation*} The middle vertical arrow is defined because of the commutativity of the left square in \eqref{sheafcommutativity}. The top left horizontal arrow is a quasi-isomorphism, and thus every left horizontal arrow is a quasi-isomorphism. The bottom left square is commutative because of the commutativity of the right square in \eqref{sheafcommutativity}; the other squares are trivially commutative. Reversing the left horizontal arrows, we see that the outermost square commutes, and this is exactly the last square in \eqref{compatibilityoflesdiagram}.

nodes.statement_short: Reduce the first two squares to a commutative diagram of sheaves checked on stalks via local models; deduce the connecting-map square from it by a diagram chase with mapping cones.

nodes.name: Fiber product formula for virtual fundamental classes
nodes.statement: For example, one would very much like to prove the expected formula for $[X\times_MY]^\mathrm{vir}$ in terms of $[X]^\mathrm{vir}$ and $[Y]^\mathrm{vir}$ (given some natural ``fiber product implicit atlas'' on $X\times_MY$, where $X,Y$ are spaces with implicit atlases and $M$ is a manifold).
nodes.statement_short: Prove the expected formula for $[X\times_MY]^\mathrm{vir}$ in terms of $[X]^\mathrm{vir}$ and $[Y]^\mathrm{vir}$ for a fiber product implicit atlas.

nodes.name: Ground ring convention ($\#\Gamma_\alpha$ invertible in $R$)
nodes.statement: In this section, we work over a fixed ground ring $R$, and everything takes place in the category of $R$-modules. We restrict to implicit atlases $A$ for which $\#\Gamma_\alpha$ is invertible in $R$ for all $\alpha\in A$.
nodes.statement_short: Work over a fixed ground ring $R$ and only with implicit atlases whose covering group orders are invertible in $R$.

nodes.name: Comparison of homology theories
nodes.statement: There are (at least) three natural ``homology groups'' which one can assign to a compact Hausdorff space $X$: \begin{rlist} \item\emph{Dual of \v Cech cohomology} $\check H^\bullet(X)^\vee$ ($^\vee$ denotes dual, i.e.\ $\operatorname{Hom}(-,R)$). \item\emph{\v Cech homology} $\check H_\bullet(X)$ (the inverse limit of the homology of nerves of finite covers). \item\emph{Steenrod--Sitnikov homology} $\overline H_\bullet(X)$ (the homology of the homotopy/derived inverse limit of nerves of finite covers; see \S\ref{steenrodhomologysec}). \end{rlist} These are successively more refined, in the sense that there are natural maps: \begin{equation} \overline H_\bullet(X)\to\check H_\bullet(X)\to\check H^\bullet(X)^\vee \end{equation} If $X$ is homeomorphic to a finite CW-complex, then there are natural isomorphisms: \begin{equation} \overline H_\bullet(X)=H_\bullet(X)\qquad\check H_\bullet(X)=H_\bullet(X)\qquad\check H^\bullet(X)^\vee=H^\bullet(X)^\vee \end{equation} It follows that a virtual fundamental class in any of these groups can be used for all the applications we are aware of. On the other hand, there are some potential advantages to working with the more refined homology groups: \begin{rlist} \item$\overline H_\bullet$ and $\check H_\bullet$ retain torsion information. \item$\overline H_\bullet$ and $\check H_\bullet$ have a natural ``extension of scalars'' map for any map of rings $R\to S$. \item$\overline H_\bullet$ has the expected long exact sequence for pairs of spaces. \end{rlist}
nodes.statement_short: Dual \v Cech cohomology, \v Cech homology and Steenrod--Sitnikov homology of compact spaces: successively more refined, agreeing for finite CW complexes.
nodes.label: alsogetsteenrod

nodes.name: Maps between Steenrod, \v Cech homology and dual \v Cech cohomology
nodes.statement: \overline H_\bullet(X)\to\check H_\bullet(X)\to\check H^\bullet(X)^\vee

nodes.name: Agreement with singular theories for finite CW complexes
nodes.statement: \overline H_\bullet(X)=H_\bullet(X)\qquad\check H_\bullet(X)=H_\bullet(X)\qquad\check H^\bullet(X)^\vee=H^\bullet(X)^\vee

nodes.name: Virtual fundamental class
nodes.statement: Let $X$ be a space with locally orientable implicit atlas $A$ of dimension $d$ with boundary. Let $B\subseteq A$ be a finite subatlas (which exists by compactness). We consider the composite: \begin{equation} \check H^{d+\bullet}(X;\mathfrak o_{X\operatorname{rel}\partial})\overset{\text{Thm \ref{Fsheaffundamentaliso}}}=H^{d+\bullet}_\mathrm{vir}(X\operatorname{rel}\partial;B)\xrightarrow{\eqref{Fpushforward}}H_{-\bullet}(E;B)\xrightarrow{[E_B]\mapsto 1}R \end{equation} We thus get a map $\check H^d(X;\mathfrak o_{X\operatorname{rel}\partial})\to R$. Now suppose $B\subseteq B'$ are two finite subatlases. Then the following diagram commutes (it suffices to check commutativity on stalks, and to do this, we can work with the complexes on the right in Lemma \ref{localdescofISO}, for which the commutativity is clear): \begin{equation} \begin{tikzcd} \mathfrak o_{X\operatorname{rel}\partial}\ar[equal]{r}{\text{Thm \ref{Fsheaffundamentaliso}}}\ar[equal]{d}&H^0_\mathrm{vir}(-\operatorname{rel}\partial;B)\ar{d}{\times[E_{B'\setminus B}]}[swap]{\eqref{Fpushforward1}}\\ \mathfrak o_{X\operatorname{rel}\partial}\ar[equal]{r}{\text{Thm \ref{Fsheaffundamentaliso}}}&H^0_\mathrm{vir}(-\operatorname{rel}\partial;B') \end{tikzcd} \end{equation} Hence the following diagram commutes (the first square following from \eqref{sheafcommforFC}, the rest being clear): \begin{equation} \begin{tikzcd} \check H^{d+\bullet}(X;\mathfrak o_{X\operatorname{rel}\partial})\ar[equal]{r}{\text{Thm \ref{Fsheaffundamentaliso}}}\ar[equal]{d}&H^{d+\bullet}_\mathrm{vir}(X\operatorname{rel}\partial;B)\ar{r}{\eqref{Fpushforward}}\ar{d}{\times[E_{B'\setminus B}]}[swap]{\eqref{Fpushforward1}}&H_{-\bullet}(E;B)\ar{r}{[E_B]\mapsto 1}\ar{d}{\times[E_{B'\setminus B}]}&R\ar[equal]{d}\\ \check H^{d+\bullet}(X;\mathfrak o_{X\operatorname{rel}\partial})\ar[equal]{r}{\text{Thm \ref{Fsheaffundamentaliso}}}&H^{d+\bullet}_\mathrm{vir}(X\operatorname{rel}\partial;B')\ar{r}{\eqref{Fpushforward}}&H_{-\bullet}(E;B')\ar{r}{[E_{B'}]\mapsto 1}&R \end{tikzcd} \end{equation} This shows that the maps $\check H^d(X;\mathfrak o_{X\operatorname{rel}\partial})\to R$ induced by $B$ and $B'$ coincide. Since any two $B_1,B_2\subseteq A$ are contained in a third $B_1\cup B_2\subseteq A$, we see that the resulting element: \begin{equation} [X]^\mathrm{vir}_A\in\check H^d(X;\mathfrak o_{X\operatorname{rel}\partial})^\vee \end{equation} is independent of $B$. We write $[X]^\mathrm{vir}$ for $[X]_A^\mathrm{vir}$ when the atlas is clear from context.
nodes.statement_short: $[X]^\mathrm{vir}$ is the functional on $\check H^d(X;\mathfrak o_{X\operatorname{rel}\partial})$ obtained from $s_\ast$ on a finite subatlas via $H_\mathrm{vir}=\check H$; independent of the subatlas.

Let $A'$ be obtained from $A$ by using instead some open subsets $U_{IJ}'\subseteq U_{IJ}$, $X_I'\subseteq X_I$, $X_I^{\mathrm{reg}\prime}\subseteq X_I^\mathrm{reg}$, and restricting $\psi_{IJ}$, $s_I$ to these subsets, so that $A'$ is also an implicit atlas.
