nodes.name: Proof
nodes.statement: We may assume that $A$ is finite. Certainly there is a map $C^\bullet_\mathrm{vir}(X\operatorname{rel}\partial;A')\to C^\bullet_\mathrm{vir}(X\operatorname{rel}\partial;A)$ which respects the map \eqref{Fpushforward}. Hence it suffices to show that the following diagram commutes: \begin{equation} \begin{tikzcd} H^\bullet_\mathrm{vir}(X\operatorname{rel}\partial;A')\ar{d}\ar[equal]{r}{\text{Thm \ref{Fsheaffundamentaliso}}}&\check H^\bullet(X;\mathfrak o_{X\operatorname{rel}\partial})\ar[equal]{d}\\ H^\bullet_\mathrm{vir}(X\operatorname{rel}\partial;A)\ar[equal]{r}{\text{Thm \ref{Fsheaffundamentaliso}}}&\check H^\bullet(X;\mathfrak o_{X\operatorname{rel}\partial}) \end{tikzcd} \end{equation} where the left vertical arrow is induced by the obvious pushforward on chains. By definition of the isomorphisms above, it suffices to check commutativity of the corresponding diagram of sheaves with $\bullet=0$. This can be checked locally, where it is clear.
nodes.statement_short: Pushforward of chains respects $s_\ast$; reduce to commutativity of a diagram of sheaves in degree 0, checked locally.

nodes.name: Shrinking compatibility diagram
nodes.statement: \begin{tikzcd} H^\bullet_\mathrm{vir}(X\operatorname{rel}\partial;A')\ar{d}\ar[equal]{r}{\text{Thm \ref{Fsheaffundamentaliso}}}&\check H^\bullet(X;\mathfrak o_{X\operatorname{rel}\partial})\ar[equal]{d}\\ H^\bullet_\mathrm{vir}(X\operatorname{rel}\partial;A)\ar[equal]{r}{\text{Thm \ref{Fsheaffundamentaliso}}}&\check H^\bullet(X;\mathfrak o_{X\operatorname{rel}\partial}) \end{tikzcd}

nodes.name: $[X\sqcup Y]^\mathrm{vir}=[X]^\mathrm{vir}\oplus[Y]^\mathrm{vir}$
nodes.statement: Let $X$ and $Y$ be spaces equipped with locally orientable implicit atlases with boundary, on the same index set $A$ and of the same virtual dimension. Let us also denote by $A$ the resulting implicit atlas on $X\sqcup Y$ (let $(X\sqcup Y)_I:=X_I\sqcup Y_I$). Then $A$ on $X\sqcup Y$ is locally orientable with $\mathfrak o_{X\sqcup Y}=(i_X)_\ast\mathfrak o_X\oplus(i_Y)_\ast\mathfrak o_Y$, and $[X\sqcup Y]^\mathrm{vir}=[X]^\mathrm{vir}\oplus[Y]^\mathrm{vir}\in\check H^\bullet(X\sqcup Y;\mathfrak o_{X\sqcup Y\operatorname{rel}\partial})^\vee=\check H^\bullet(X;\mathfrak o_{X\operatorname{rel}\partial})^\vee\oplus\check H^\bullet(Y;\mathfrak o_{Y\operatorname{rel}\partial})^\vee$.
nodes.statement_short: The virtual fundamental class is additive under disjoint union.
assumptions: Let $X$ and $Y$ be spaces equipped with locally orientable implicit atlases with boundary, on the same index set $A$ and of the same virtual dimension.
conclusions: $A$ on $X\sqcup Y$ is locally orientable with $\mathfrak o_{X\sqcup Y}=(i_X)_\ast\mathfrak o_X\oplus(i_Y)_\ast\mathfrak o_Y$
nodes.label: disjointunionfc

nodes.name: Proof
nodes.statement: We may assume that $A$ is finite. There is a natural isomorphism: \begin{equation} C^\bullet_\mathrm{vir}(X\sqcup Y\operatorname{rel}\partial;A)=C^\bullet_\mathrm{vir}(X\operatorname{rel}\partial;A)\oplus C^\bullet_\mathrm{vir}(Y\operatorname{rel}\partial;A) \end{equation} compatible with the map to $C_{-\bullet}(E;A)$. Thus it suffices to show that the following square of isomorphisms commutes: \begin{equation} \begin{tikzcd} H^\bullet_\mathrm{vir}(X\sqcup Y\operatorname{rel}\partial;A)\ar[equal]{d}\ar[equal]{r}{\text{Thm \ref{Fsheaffundamentaliso}}}&\check H^\bullet(X\sqcup Y;\mathfrak o_{X\sqcup Y\operatorname{rel}\partial})\ar[equal]{d}\\ H^\bullet_\mathrm{vir}(X\operatorname{rel}\partial;A)\oplus H^\bullet_\mathrm{vir}(Y\operatorname{rel}\partial;A)\ar[equal]{r}{\text{Thm \ref{Fsheaffundamentaliso}}}&\check H^\bullet(X;\mathfrak o_{X\operatorname{rel}\partial})\oplus\check H^\bullet(Y;\mathfrak o_{Y\operatorname{rel}\partial}) \end{tikzcd} \end{equation} By definition of the horizontal maps, it suffices to check the commutativity of the corresponding diagram of sheaves on $X\sqcup Y$, which is clear.
nodes.statement_short: Virtual cochain complexes split over a disjoint union compatibly with $s_\ast$; reduce to a square of sheaves on $X\sqcup Y$.

nodes.name: Splitting of virtual cochains over disjoint union
nodes.statement: C^\bullet_\mathrm{vir}(X\sqcup Y\operatorname{rel}\partial;A)=C^\bullet_\mathrm{vir}(X\operatorname{rel}\partial;A)\oplus C^\bullet_\mathrm{vir}(Y\operatorname{rel}\partial;A)

nodes.name: Disjoint union compatibility square
nodes.statement: \begin{tikzcd} H^\bullet_\mathrm{vir}(X\sqcup Y\operatorname{rel}\partial;A)\ar[equal]{d}\ar[equal]{r}{\text{Thm \ref{Fsheaffundamentaliso}}}&\check H^\bullet(X\sqcup Y;\mathfrak o_{X\sqcup Y\operatorname{rel}\partial})\ar[equal]{d}\\ H^\bullet_\mathrm{vir}(X\operatorname{rel}\partial;A)\oplus H^\bullet_\mathrm{vir}(Y\operatorname{rel}\partial;A)\ar[equal]{r}{\text{Thm \ref{Fsheaffundamentaliso}}}&\check H^\bullet(X;\mathfrak o_{X\operatorname{rel}\partial})\oplus\check H^\bullet(Y;\mathfrak o_{Y\operatorname{rel}\partial}) \end{tikzcd}

nodes.name: $\partial[X]^\mathrm{vir}=[\partial X]^\mathrm{vir}$
nodes.statement: Let $X$ be a space with locally orientable implicit atlas $A$ with boundary. Then the dual connecting homomorphism $\delta^\vee:\check H^\bullet(X;\mathfrak o_{X\operatorname{rel}\partial})^\vee\to\check H^{\bullet-1}(\partial X;\mathfrak o_{\partial X})^\vee$ sends $[X]^\mathrm{vir}$ to $[\partial X]^\mathrm{vir}$.
nodes.statement_short: The boundary of the virtual fundamental class is the virtual fundamental class of the boundary.
assumptions: Let $X$ be a space with locally orientable implicit atlas $A$ with boundary.
conclusions: the dual connecting homomorphism $\delta^\vee:\check H^\bullet(X;\mathfrak o_{X\operatorname{rel}\partial})^\vee\to\check H^{\bullet-1}(\partial X;\mathfrak o_{\partial X})^\vee$ sends $[X]^\mathrm{vir}$ to $[\partial X]^\mathrm{vir}$
nodes.label: boundaryfundamentalclass

nodes.name: Proof
nodes.statement: We may assume that $A$ is finite. The map $C^\bullet_\mathrm{vir}(\partial X;A)\to C^{\bullet+1}_\mathrm{vir}(X\operatorname{rel}\partial;A)$ in \eqref{sesofF} commutes with the maps from both of these groups to $C_{d-\bullet}(E;A)$. Hence the result follows from the commutativity of the last square in Proposition \ref{compatibilityoflongexactsequence}.
nodes.statement_short: The connecting map of virtual cochains commutes with $s_\ast$; apply the compatibility of long exact sequences.

nodes.name: $(\partial X\to X)_\ast[\partial X]^\mathrm{vir}=0$
nodes.statement: Let $X$ be a space with locally orientable implicit atlas with boundary. Then the pushforward map $\check H^\bullet_\mathrm{vir}(\partial X;\mathfrak o_{\partial X})^\vee\to\check H^\bullet(X;\mathfrak o_X)^\vee$ annihilates $[\partial X]^\mathrm{vir}$.
nodes.statement_short: The virtual class of the boundary pushes forward to zero (cobordism invariance).
assumptions: Let $X$ be a space with locally orientable implicit atlas with boundary.
conclusions: the pushforward map $\check H^\bullet_\mathrm{vir}(\partial X;\mathfrak o_{\partial X})^\vee\to\check H^\bullet(X;\mathfrak o_X)^\vee$ annihilates $[\partial X]^\mathrm{vir}$
nodes.label: cobordismworks

nodes.name: Proof
nodes.statement: The composition $\check H^{\bullet+1}(X;\mathfrak o_{X\operatorname{rel}\partial})^\vee\to\check H^\bullet(\partial X;\mathfrak o_{\partial X})^\vee\to\check H^\bullet(X;\mathfrak o_X)^\vee$ is zero, and $[\partial X]^\mathrm{vir}$ is in the image of the first map by Lemma \ref{boundaryfundamentalclass}.
nodes.statement_short: Exactness of the dual long exact sequence and Lemma 5.2.7.

nodes.name: If $X=X^\mathrm{reg}$ then $[X]^\mathrm{vir}=[X]$
nodes.statement: Let $X$ be a space with locally orientable implicit atlas $A$ with boundary. If $X^\mathrm{reg}=X$ (so in particular, $X$ is a compact topological manifold with boundary of dimension $d=\operatorname{vdim}_AX$), then $[X]^\mathrm{vir}_A$ is the usual fundamental class of $X$.
nodes.statement_short: When $X$ is everywhere regular (a compact manifold), the virtual class is the usual fundamental class.
assumptions: Let $X$ be a space with locally orientable implicit atlas $A$ with boundary.
$X^\mathrm{reg}=X$
conclusions: $[X]^\mathrm{vir}_A$ is the usual fundamental class of $X$
nodes.label: fclasstransverse

nodes.name: Proof
nodes.statement: We may replace $A$ with the finite subatlas $\varnothing\subseteq A$. Now in this case, we have: \begin{equation} C^\bullet_\mathrm{vir}(K\operatorname{rel}\partial;\varnothing)=C^\bullet_\mathrm{vir}(K\operatorname{rel}\partial;\varnothing)_{\varnothing\varnothing}=C_{d-\bullet}(X_{\varnothing,\varnothing,\varnothing},X_{\varnothing,\varnothing,\varnothing}\setminus X_{\varnothing,\varnothing,\varnothing}^K)=C_{d-\bullet}(X,X\setminus K) \end{equation} It follows that the identification $\check H^\bullet(X;\mathfrak o_{X\operatorname{rel}\partial})=H^\bullet_\mathrm{vir}(X\operatorname{rel}\partial;\varnothing)=H_{d-\bullet}(X)$ is simply the usual Poincar\'e duality isomorphism, and the map $H_{-\bullet}(X)\to H_{-\bullet}(E;\varnothing)\to R$ is the usual augmentation on $H_0$. Hence the composition $\check H^\bullet(X;\mathfrak o_{X\operatorname{rel}\partial})\to R$ is pairing against the usual fundamental class of $X$.
nodes.statement_short: Use the empty subatlas: virtual cochains become $C_{d-\bullet}(X,X\setminus K)$ and the identification is ordinary Poincar\'e duality.

nodes.name: Virtual cochains for the empty subatlas
nodes.statement: C^\bullet_\mathrm{vir}(K\operatorname{rel}\partial;\varnothing)=C^\bullet_\mathrm{vir}(K\operatorname{rel}\partial;\varnothing)_{\varnothing\varnothing}=C_{d-\bullet}(X_{\varnothing,\varnothing,\varnothing},X_{\varnothing,\varnothing,\varnothing}\setminus X_{\varnothing,\varnothing,\varnothing}^K)=C_{d-\bullet}(X,X\setminus K)

nodes.name: Calculating $[X]^\mathrm{vir}$ using perturbation
nodes.statement: The properties from this section can be used to calculate the virtual fundamental class in the following sense. Let us suppose we are given an ``explicit'' implicit atlas $A$ on a space $X$. We may always (for convenience) replace $A$ by a subatlas and/or shrink the charts of $A$ and the virtual fundamental class is preserved (Lemmas \ref{sameassubatlas} and \ref{openreduction}). Now suppose we can extend $A$ to an implicit atlas with boundary on a space $Y$ with $\partial Y=X\cup X'$ where $X'=(X')^\mathrm{reg}$ (if $A$ is a smooth implicit atlas, then such an extension is obtained if one can ``coherently perturb'' the Kuranishi maps $s_\alpha$ so they become transverse to zero). Then $X'$ is a closed smooth manifold, and $[X']^\mathrm{vir}=[X']$ is the naive fundamental class (Lemma \ref{fclasstransverse}). Now $Y$ is a cobordism between $X$ and $X'$, so we have $[X]^\mathrm{vir}=[X']$ as homology classes in $Y$ (Lemmas \ref{disjointunionfc} and \ref{cobordismworks}). This allows us to understand the pushforward of $[X]^\mathrm{vir}$ under any map $f:X\to Z$ which extends continuously to $Y$. We do not claim such perturbations always exist; an affirmative answer is provided in very similar, though not identical, contexts by Fukaya--Ono \cite{fukayaono}, Fukaya--Oh--Ohta--Ono \cite{FOOOII,foootechnicaldetails} and McDuff--Wehrheim \cite{mcduffwehrheim}.
nodes.statement_short: If $A$ extends to a cobordism $Y$ to a transversally cut out $X'$ (e.g.\ by perturbing Kuranishi maps), then $[X]^\mathrm{vir}=[X']$ in $Y$.
nodes.label: perturbationcalc

nodes.name: Implicit atlas on the zero set of a smooth section
nodes.statement: Let $B$ be a smooth manifold with boundary, let $p:E\to B$ be a smooth vector bundle, and let $s:B\to E$ be a smooth section with $s^{-1}(0)$ compact. We define an implicit atlas of dimension $\dim B-\dim E$ with boundary on $X:=s^{-1}(0)$ as follows. The index set $A$ consists of all triples $(V_\alpha,E_\alpha,\lambda_\alpha)$ (called \emph{thickening datums}) where: \begin{rlist} \item$V_\alpha\subseteq B$ is an open subset. \item$E_\alpha$ is a finite-dimensional vector space. \item$\lambda_\alpha:E_\alpha\times V_\alpha\to p^{-1}(V_\alpha)$ is a smooth homomorphism of vector bundles. \end{rlist} The thickened spaces are defined as follows: \begin{equation} X_I:=\Bigl\{(x,\{e_\alpha\}_{\alpha\in I})\in\bigcap_{\alpha\in I}V_\alpha\times\bigoplus_{\alpha\in I}E_\alpha\Bigm|s(x)+\sum_{\alpha\in I}\lambda_\alpha(x,e_\alpha)=0\Bigr\} \end{equation} The Kuranishi map $s_\alpha:X_I\to E_\alpha$ is the obvious projection map, the footprint $U_{IJ}$ is the locus where $x\in V_\alpha$ for all $\alpha\in J$, and the footprint maps $\psi_{IJ}:(s_{J\setminus I}|X_J)^{-1}(0)\to U_{IJ}$ are the obvious forgetful maps. The compatibility axioms are an easy exercise. The regular locus $X_I^\mathrm{reg}\subseteq X_I$ is the locus where $X_I$ is ``cut out transversally''; more precisely, $(x,\{e_\alpha\}_{\alpha\in I})\in X_I$ is in $X_I^\mathrm{reg}$ iff the following map is surjective: \begin{equation} \Bigl(ds+\sum_{\alpha\in I}d\lambda_\alpha(\cdot,e_\alpha)\Bigr)\oplus\bigoplus_{\alpha\in I}\lambda_\alpha(x,\cdot):T_xB\oplus\bigoplus_{\alpha\in I}E_\alpha\to E_x \end{equation} The transversality axioms are an easy exercise. Thus $A$ is indeed an implicit atlas on $X$. Since everything here is in the smooth category, $A$ is in fact a smooth implicit atlas.
nodes.statement_short: For a section $s$ of a vector bundle over $B$, the thickening datums $(V_\alpha,E_\alpha,\lambda_\alpha)$ give a smooth implicit atlas on $s^{-1}(0)$ with $X_I$ the zero set of $s+\sum\lambda_\alpha$.
nodes.label: IAonvectorbundlezeroset

nodes.name: Thickened spaces for zero set of section
nodes.statement: X_I:=\Bigl\{(x,\{e_\alpha\}_{\alpha\in I})\in\bigcap_{\alpha\in I}V_\alpha\times\bigoplus_{\alpha\in I}E_\alpha\Bigm|s(x)+\sum_{\alpha\in I}\lambda_\alpha(x,e_\alpha)=0\Bigr\}

nodes.name: Transversality map defining the regular locus
nodes.statement: \Bigl(ds+\sum_{\alpha\in I}d\lambda_\alpha(\cdot,e_\alpha)\Bigr)\oplus\bigoplus_{\alpha\in I}\lambda_\alpha(x,\cdot):T_xB\oplus\bigoplus_{\alpha\in I}E_\alpha\to E_x

nodes.name: Euler class
nodes.statement: Let $B$ be a space equipped with a vector bundle $p:E\to B$ of rank $k$. This induces a canonical locally constant sheaf $\mathfrak o_E$ on $B$ whose stalk at $b\in B$ is $\mathfrak o_{E_b}$. Let $\tau_E\in H^k(E,E\setminus 0;p^\ast\mathfrak o_E)$ denote the Thom class of $E$ (characterized uniquely by the property that its restriction to any local trivialization $\mathbb R^n\times U\to U$ is the pullback of the tautological class in $H^n(\mathbb R^n,\mathbb R^n\setminus 0;\mathfrak o_{\mathbb R^n})$). The \emph{Euler class} $e(E)\in H^k(B;\mathfrak o_E)$ is $s^\ast\tau_E$ where $s:B\to E$ is any section. Any two sections are homotopic, so $e(E)$ is well-defined. For any section $s:B\to E$ with $s^{-1}(0)$ compact, the \emph{Euler class with compact support} $e_c(E,s)\in H^k_c(B;\mathfrak o_E)$ is $s^\ast\tau_E$. If $s_0$ and $s_1$ are homotopic through a section $\tilde s:B\times[0,1]\to E$ with compact support, then $e_c(E,s_0)=e_c(E,s_1)$. The natural map $H^k_c(B;\mathfrak o_E)\to H^k(B;\mathfrak o_E)$ sends the Euler class with compact support to the Euler class.
nodes.statement_short: Thom class of a vector bundle, Euler class $e(E)=s^\ast\tau_E$, and Euler class with compact support $e_c(E,s)$ for sections with compact zero set.

nodes.name: Compactly supported Euler class of a trivial bundle
nodes.statement: The Euler class with compact support can be nonzero even for the trivial vector bundle.

nodes.name: Virtual fundamental class of zero set is the Euler class
nodes.statement: Let $B$ be a smooth manifold, let $p:E\to B$ be a smooth vector bundle, and let $s:B\to E$ be a smooth section with $s^{-1}(0)$ compact. Consider the implicit atlas $A$ on $X:=s^{-1}(0)$ from Definition \ref{IAonvectorbundlezeroset}. Then there is a canonical isomorphism of sheaves $\mathfrak o_X=\mathfrak o_B\otimes\mathfrak o_E^\vee$ on $X$ (in particular, $A$ is locally orientable), and the image of $[X]^\mathrm{vir}$ in $H^{\dim B-\dim E}(B;\mathfrak o_B\otimes\mathfrak o_E^\vee)^\vee$ equals $e_c(E,s)\cap[B]$.
nodes.statement_short: For the natural implicit atlas on the zero set of a section, the virtual class maps to $e_c(E,s)\cap[B]$.
assumptions: Let $B$ be a smooth manifold, let $p:E\to B$ be a smooth vector bundle, and let $s:B\to E$ be a smooth section with $s^{-1}(0)$ compact.
Consider the implicit atlas $A$ on $X:=s^{-1}(0)$ from Definition \ref{IAonvectorbundlezeroset}.
conclusions: there is a canonical isomorphism of sheaves $\mathfrak o_X=\mathfrak o_B\otimes\mathfrak o_E^\vee$ on $X$ (in particular, $A$ is locally orientable)
the image of $[X]^\mathrm{vir}$ in $H^{\dim B-\dim E}(B;\mathfrak o_B\otimes\mathfrak o_E^\vee)^\vee$ equals $e_c(E,s)\cap[B]$
nodes.label: actuallygiveseulerclass

nodes.name: Proposition 5.3.14 determines $[X]^\mathrm{vir}$ uniquely
nodes.statement: Note that $\check H^\bullet(X;\mathfrak o_X)=\varinjlim_{X\subseteq U}H^\bullet(U;\mathfrak o_B\otimes\mathfrak o_E^\vee)$ (direct limit over open neighborhoods $U\subseteq B$ of $X$), by the continuity axiom of \v Cech cohomology. The proposition applies equally well with $U$ in place of $B$, and thus determines $[X]^\mathrm{vir}\in\check H^\bullet(X;\mathfrak o_X)^\vee$ uniquely (note the use of either Lemma \ref{sameassubatlas} or \ref{openreduction}).
nodes.statement_short: By continuity of \v Cech cohomology, applying the proposition on neighborhoods $U$ of $X$ determines $[X]^\mathrm{vir}$ uniquely.

nodes.name: Proof
nodes.statement: The statement about orientation sheaves is a straightforward calculation which we omit. Choose some smooth family of sections $\tilde s:B\times[0,1]\to E$ with $\tilde s^{-1}(0)$ compact, so that $\tilde s(\cdot,0)=s$ and $s_1:=\tilde s(\cdot,1)$ is transverse to the zero section. Now $B\times[0,1]$ is a smooth manifold with boundary, so let $\tilde A$ be the implicit atlas on $\tilde X:=\tilde s^{-1}(0)$ from Definition \ref{IAonvectorbundlezeroset}. Similarly, let $A'$ be the implicit atlas on $X':=(s')^{-1}(0)$. Now we have two implicit atlases on $X$, namely $A$ and (the restriction to the boundary of) $\tilde A$. On the other hand, we can exhibit $A$ as a subatlas of $\tilde A$ by the map on thickening datums sending $V_\alpha$ to $V_\alpha\times[0,1]$ and $\lambda_\alpha$ to its obvious extension. Hence they induce the same virtual fundamental class (Lemma \ref{sameassubatlas}), so we may just write $[X]^\mathrm{vir}$ (dropping the subscript indicating which atlas we use). The same reasoning applies to $X'$. Now $\partial\tilde X=X\sqcup X'$, so we have $[X]^\mathrm{vir}=[X']^\mathrm{vir}$ as homology classes on $\tilde X$ (Lemmas \ref{disjointunionfc} and \ref{cobordismworks}). Hence we have: \begin{equation} [X]^\mathrm{vir}=[X']^\mathrm{vir} \end{equation} as elements of $H^{\dim B-\dim E}(B;\mathfrak o_B\otimes\mathfrak o_E^\vee)^\vee$. We know $X'=(X')^\mathrm{reg}$ (it is cut out transversally), so $X'$ is a closed smooth manifold and $[X']^\mathrm{vir}=[X']$ (Lemma \ref{fclasstransverse}). But now $[X']=e_c(E,s)\cap[B]$ by elementary Poincar\'e duality.
nodes.statement_short: Cobordism argument: deform $s$ to a transverse section through a family, use subatlas and cobordism invariance, then compute the transverse case by Poincar\'e duality.

nodes.name: $[X]^\mathrm{vir}=[X']^\mathrm{vir}$
nodes.statement: [X]^\mathrm{vir}=[X']^\mathrm{vir}

nodes.name: Practical limitation of Proposition 5.3.14
nodes.statement: Proposition \ref{actuallygiveseulerclass} in its present form is useless in practice, because the implicit atlases which arise in interesting examples are not literally isomorphic to the one given in Definition \ref{IAonvectorbundlezeroset}. One could, though, hope to show that they are equivalent (c.f.\ Remark \ref{equivalenceofIA}) and then apply Proposition \ref{actuallygiveseulerclass}.

nodes.name: Steenrod homology vs dual \v Cech cohomology
nodes.statement: The natural map $\overline H_\bullet(X,\partial X;\mathfrak o_X^\vee)\to\check H^\bullet(X;\mathfrak o_{X\operatorname{rel}\partial})^\vee$ is an isomorphism if the base ring $R$ is a field (this follows from Lemma \ref{steenrodisderiveddualofcech}), but for $R=\mathbb Z$ the kernel can be substantial (in particular, it contains all torsion).
nodes.statement_short: $\overline H_\bullet(X,\partial X;\mathfrak o_X^\vee)\to\check H^\bullet(X;\mathfrak o_{X\operatorname{rel}\partial})^\vee$ is an isomorphism over a field but can have large kernel (all torsion) over $\mathbb Z$.

nodes.name: Virtual fundamental class in Steenrod homology
nodes.statement: Let $X$ be a space with localy orientable implicit atlas $A$ of dimension $d$ with boundary. Let $B\subseteq A$ be a finite subatlas. By Propositions \ref{Cpure} and \ref{cechcohomologypurehomotopysheaf}, there is a canonical isomorphism $\check C^\bullet(X;\mathfrak o_{X\operatorname{rel}\partial})=C_\mathrm{vir}^\bullet(X\operatorname{rel}\partial;B)$ in $D(R)$ (observe that the isomorphisms in the proof of Proposition \ref{cechcohomologypurehomotopysheaf} all come from canonical quasi-isomorphisms on the chain level). There is also a canonical isomorphism $C_{-\bullet}(E;B)=R$ in $D(R)$. Since $C_\mathrm{vir}^\bullet(X\operatorname{rel}\partial;B)$ is free and bounded above, we have: \begin{equation} \operatorname{Hom}_R(C_\mathrm{vir}^\bullet(X\operatorname{rel}\partial;B),C_{-\bullet}(E;B))=R\operatorname{Hom}_{D(R)}(\check C^\bullet(X;\mathfrak o_{X\operatorname{rel}\partial}),R) \end{equation} Thus the map $s_\ast:C_\mathrm{vir}^{d+\bullet}(X\operatorname{rel}\partial;B)\to C_{-\bullet}(E;B)$ gives rise to an element: \begin{equation} [X]^\mathrm{vir}_A:=[s_\ast]\in\operatorname{Hom}_{D(R)}(\check C^\bullet(X;\mathfrak o_{X\operatorname{rel}\partial}),R[-d])\overset{\text{Lem \ref{steenrodisderiveddualofcech}}}=\overline H_d(X,\partial X;\mathfrak o_X^\vee) \end{equation} The commutativity of \eqref{sheafcommforFC} implies that this element is independent of the chosen finite subatlas $B\subseteq A$. By definition, this fundamental class \eqref{steenrodfclasseqndef} projects to the fundamental class of Definition \ref{fclassdefinition} under the map $\overline H_\bullet(X,\partial X;\mathfrak o_X^\vee)\to\check H^\bullet(X;\mathfrak o_{X\operatorname{rel}\partial})^\vee$. By chasing the various isomorphisms involved in its definition, it can be checked that $[X]^\mathrm{vir}\in\overline H_d(X,\partial X;\mathfrak o_X^\vee)$ is preserved under extension of scalars.
nodes.statement_short: Lifts $[X]^\mathrm{vir}$ to Steenrod homology as the class of $s_\ast$ in $\operatorname{Hom}_{D(R)}(\check C^\bullet(X;\mathfrak o_{X\operatorname{rel}\partial}),R[-d])$.

nodes.name: Derived Hom identification
nodes.statement: \operatorname{Hom}_R(C_\mathrm{vir}^\bullet(X\operatorname{rel}\partial;B),C_{-\bullet}(E;B))=R\operatorname{Hom}_{D(R)}(\check C^\bullet(X;\mathfrak o_{X\operatorname{rel}\partial}),R)

nodes.name: Steenrod virtual fundamental class
nodes.statement: [X]^\mathrm{vir}_A:=[s_\ast]\in\operatorname{Hom}_{D(R)}(\check C^\bullet(X;\mathfrak o_{X\operatorname{rel}\partial}),R[-d])\overset{\text{Lem \ref{steenrodisderiveddualofcech}}}=\overline H_d(X,\partial X;\mathfrak o_X^\vee)
nodes.label: steenrodfclasseqndef

nodes.name: Properties of the Steenrod virtual fundamental class
nodes.statement: The statements and proofs of Lemmas \ref{sameassubatlas}--\ref{fclasstransverse} and Proposition \ref{actuallygiveseulerclass} generalize readily to the case of $[X]^\mathrm{vir}\in\overline H_d(X,\partial X;\mathfrak o_X^\vee)$. Note that (the generalization of) Proposition \ref{actuallygiveseulerclass} does not determine $[X]^\mathrm{vir}\in\overline H_d(X,\partial X;\mathfrak o_X^\vee)$ uniquely since the map from the Steenrod homology of $X$ to the inverse limit of the homology of its neighborhoods is not necessarily an isomorphism (see \cite[p87, Theorem 4]{milnor}). However, it does at least determine the image of $[X]^\mathrm{vir}$ under any map from $X$ to a finite CW-complex, since any such map extends to some neighborhood of $X$.
nodes.statement_short: Lemmas 5.2.4--5.2.9 and Proposition 5.3.14 extend to the Steenrod class, though the latter only determines its image under maps to finite CW complexes.

nodes.name: Ground ring convention ($\#\Gamma_\alpha$ invertible in $R$)
nodes.statement: In this section, we work over a fixed ground ring $R$, and everything takes place in the category of $R$-modules. We restrict to implicit atlases $A$ for which $\#\Gamma_\alpha$ is invertible in $R$ for all $\alpha\in A$.
nodes.statement_short: Work over a fixed ground ring $R$ and only with implicit atlases whose covering group orders are invertible in $R$.

nodes.name: Stratification
nodes.statement: Let $X$ be a topological space and let $\mathcal S$ be a poset. A \emph{stratification} of $X$ by $\mathcal S$ is a lower semicontinuous function $X\to\mathcal S$. We let $X^{\leq\mathfrak s}$ (resp. $X^\mathfrak s$, $X^{\geq\mathfrak s}$) denote the inverse image of $\mathcal S^{\leq\mathfrak s}$ (resp.\ $\{\mathfrak s\}$, $\mathcal S^{\geq\mathfrak s}$); lower semicontinuity of $X\to\mathcal S$ means by definition that every $X^{\geq\mathfrak s}$ is open. For a pair of spaces $(X,\partial X)$, a stratification $(X,\partial X)\to(\mathcal S,\partial\mathcal S)$ shall mean a stratification $X\to\mathcal S$ along with a downward closed (i.e.\ closed under taking smaller elements) subset $\partial\mathcal S\subseteq\mathcal S$ such that $X^{\partial\mathcal S}=\partial X$ (note that this implies automatically that $\partial X\subseteq X$ is closed).
nodes.statement_short: A stratification of $X$ by a poset $\mathcal S$ is a lower semicontinuous map $X\to\mathcal S$; for pairs, $\partial X$ is the preimage of a downward closed $\partial\mathcal S$.
nodes.label: stratificationdefinition

nodes.name: Cell-like stratification
nodes.statement: Let $(M,\partial M)$ be a topological manifold with boundary and stratification by $(\mathcal S,\partial\mathcal S)$, and fix a map $\dim:\mathcal S\to\mathbb Z$. This stratification is called \emph{cell-like} iff each pair $(M^{\leq\mathfrak s},M^{<\mathfrak s})$ is a topological manifold with boundary of dimension $\dim\mathfrak s$. If $(M,\partial M)\to(\mathcal S,\partial\mathcal S)$ is cell-like, then so is $\partial M\to\partial\mathcal S$ (with empty boundary) and $(M^{\leq\mathfrak s},M^{<\mathfrak s})\to(\mathcal S^{\leq\mathfrak s},\mathcal S^{<\mathfrak s})$.
differentia: each pair $(M^{\leq\mathfrak s},M^{<\mathfrak s})$ is a topological manifold with boundary of dimension $\dim\mathfrak s$
nodes.label: celllikedef

nodes.name: Face poset stratification of a triangulated manifold is cell-like
nodes.statement: Let $T$ be a simplicial complex, and suppose that its geometric realization $M:=\left|T\right|$ is a topological manifold with boundary (then $\partial M$ necessarily corresponds to a subcomplex $\partial T\subseteq T$). Let $(\mathcal S,\partial\mathcal S):=(\mathcal F(T),\mathcal F(\partial T))$ be the face poset of $T$ (resp.\ $\partial T$). Then the stratification $(M,\partial M)\to(\mathcal S,\partial\mathcal S)$ is cell-like (note that $T$ need not be a PL manifold).
nodes.label: celllikeexample

nodes.name: Corner stratifications of $\mathbb R_{\geq0}^k\times\mathbb R^{n-k}$
nodes.statement: The natural stratification $\mathbb R_{\geq 0}^k\times\mathbb R^{n-k}\to\{(0,\infty)>\{0\}\}^k$ is cell-like. The natural stratification $\mathbb R_{\geq 0}^k\times\mathbb R^{n-k}\to\mathbb Z$ given by ($n$ minus) the number of zeros in the first $k$ coordinates is \emph{not} cell-like for $k\geq 2$.
nodes.label: celllikecornerexample

nodes.statement_short: Local structure of cell-like stratifications: dimension bounds, top strata open, and codimension-one strata border exactly one (boundary) or two (interior) top strata.
assumptions: Let $(M,\partial M)\to(\mathcal S,\partial\mathcal S)$ be cell-like.
conclusions: If $\mathfrak s\prec\mathfrak t$ then $M^\mathfrak s\subseteq\partial M^{\leq\mathfrak t}$.
If $M^\mathfrak s\ne\varnothing$, then $\dim\mathfrak s\leq\dim M$.
If $\dim\mathfrak s=\dim M$, then $M^\mathfrak s\subseteq M$ is open.
nodes.label: celllikelocalstructure

nodes.name: Proof
nodes.statement: Since $\mathfrak s\prec\mathfrak t$, we have $M^\mathfrak s\subseteq M^{<\mathfrak t}=\partial M^{\leq\mathfrak t}$, giving (\ref{inbdry}). Recall Brouwer's ``invariance of domain'', which implies that if a subset $X\subseteq\mathbb R^n$ is (in the subspace topology) locally homeomorphic to $\mathbb R^m$, then $m\leq n$, with equality iff $X$ is open. This immediately gives (\ref{toplessdim}), (\ref{topopen}). We prove (\ref{bdrystratumstruct}). Fix $p\in M^\mathfrak s$. A neighborhood of $p$ is covered by strata $\succ\mathfrak s$, so since $M^\mathfrak s\subseteq M$ is not open, there exists a stratum $\mathfrak t\succ\mathfrak s$. Now $M^\mathfrak s\subseteq\partial M^{\leq\mathfrak t}$ is open by (\ref{topopen}) (applied to $M^{<\mathfrak t}\to\mathcal S^{<\mathfrak t}$). A doubling argument (and invariance of domain) near $p\in\partial M$ shows that $M^s\cup M^\mathfrak t$ contains a neighborhood of $p$. Since we have exhausted a neighborhood of $p\in M^\mathfrak s$, it follows using (\ref{inbdry}) that there is no other stratum $\succ\mathfrak s$. We prove (\ref{intstratumstruct}). Fix $p\in M^\mathfrak s$. A neighborhood of $p$ is covered by strata $\succ\mathfrak s$, so since $M^\mathfrak s\subseteq M$ is not open, there exists a stratum $\mathfrak t\succ\mathfrak s$. Now $M^\mathfrak s\subseteq\partial M^{\leq\mathfrak t}$ is open by (\ref{topopen}), as is $M^\mathfrak t\subseteq M$. This gives a collar on one side of $M^\mathfrak s\subseteq M$. This still does not fill out a neighborhood of $p$, so there exists $\mathfrak t'\ne\mathfrak t$ with $\mathfrak t'\succ\mathfrak s$, giving a collar on the other side of $M^\mathfrak s\subseteq M$. Now by invariance of domain, we have thus exhausted a neighborhood of $p\in M^\mathfrak s$ inside $M$, and hence it follows using (\ref{inbdry}) that there are no more strata $\succ\mathfrak s$ other than $\mathfrak t,\mathfrak t'$.
nodes.statement_short: Each part in turn: (i) from the definition, (ii)--(iii) by invariance of domain, (iv)--(v) by exhausting a neighborhood of a point with adjacent strata using doubling and invariance of domain.

nodes.name: Implicit atlas with cell-like stratification
nodes.statement: Let $(X,\partial X)$ be a pair of compact Hausdorff spaces equipped with a stratification $(X,\partial X)\to(\mathcal S,\partial\mathcal S)$ ($\mathcal S$ finite) along with a map $\dim:\mathcal S\to\mathbb Z$. Also fix ``orientation data'': \begin{rlist} \item For every $\mathfrak s\in\mathcal S$, an orientation line $\mathfrak o_\mathfrak s$ (i.e.\ a free $\mathbb Z/2$-graded $\mathbb Z$-module of rank one). \item For $\operatorname{codim}(\mathfrak s\preceq\mathfrak t)=1$, an odd ``coboundary'' map $\mathfrak o_\mathfrak s\to\mathfrak o_\mathfrak t$. \end{rlist} An \emph{implicit atlas of dimension $d$ with boundary and cell-like stratification} on $(X,\partial X)\to(\mathcal S,\partial\mathcal S)$ consists of the same data as an implicit atlas with boundary, except that in addition we specify a $\Gamma_I$-invariant stratification $(X_I,\partial X_I)\to(\mathcal S,\partial\mathcal S)$ for all $I\subseteq A$, whose restriction to $X_\varnothing$ is the given stratification. We add the following ``compatibiltiy axiom'': \begin{rlist} \item The restriction of the stratification on $X_J$ to $(s_{J\setminus I}|X_J)^{-1}(0)$ coincides with the pullback of the stratification on $X_I$ via $\psi_{IJ}$. \setcounter{rcountsave}{\value{rcounti}} \end{rlist} and we modify one ``transversality axiom'': \begin{rlist} \setcounter{rcounti}{\value{rcountsave}} \item(Submersion axiom) In the local model $\mathbb R^{d+\dim E_I}\times\mathbb R^{\dim E_{J\setminus I}}\to\mathbb R^{\dim E_{J\setminus I}}$ (or $(\mathbb R_{\geq 0}\times\mathbb R^{d+\dim E_I-1})\times\mathbb R^{\dim E_{J\setminus I}}\to\mathbb R^{\dim E_{J\setminus I}}$), we require the stratification on the domain to be pulled back from a cell-like stratification on the first factor (for $\mathfrak s\mapsto\dim\mathfrak s+\dim E_I$). \end{rlist} We also specify isomorphisms of sheaves $\mathfrak o_{(X_I^\mathrm{reg})^{\leq\mathfrak s}}\otimes\mathfrak o_\mathfrak s\xrightarrow\sim\mathfrak o_{X_I^\mathrm{reg}}$ over $(X_I^\mathrm{reg})^{\leq\mathfrak s}$ which are compatible with $\psi_{IJ}$ and such that the following diagram commutes: \begin{equation} \begin{tikzcd} \mathfrak o_{(X_I^\mathrm{reg})^{\leq\mathfrak s}}\otimes\mathfrak o_\mathfrak s\ar{r}\ar{d}&\mathfrak o_{X_I^\mathrm{reg}}\ar[equals]{d}\\ \mathfrak o_{(X_I^\mathrm{reg})^{\leq\mathfrak t}}\otimes\mathfrak o_\mathfrak t\ar{r}&\mathfrak o_{X_I^\mathrm{reg}} \end{tikzcd} \end{equation} for $\operatorname{codim}(\mathfrak s\preceq\mathfrak t)=1$ (the left vertical map is the tensor product of the coboundary map $\mathfrak o_\mathfrak s\to\mathfrak o_\mathfrak t$ and the inverse of the boundary map $\mathfrak o_{(X_I^\mathrm{reg})^{\leq\mathfrak t}}\to\mathfrak o_{(X_I^\mathrm{reg})^{\leq\mathfrak s}}$). In other words, we identify $\mathfrak o_\mathfrak s$ with the orientation line of the normal bundle of $(X_I^\mathrm{reg})^{\leq\mathfrak s}\subseteq X_I^\mathrm{reg}$, so that the coboundary maps $\mathfrak o_\mathfrak s\to\mathfrak o_\mathfrak t$ coincide with the geometric coboundary maps on normal bundles. Given an implicit atlas with boundary and cell-like stratification $A$ on $(X,\partial X)\to(\mathcal S,\partial\mathcal S)$, we may obtain by restriction to the corresponding strata an implicit atlas with cell-like stratification on $\partial X\to\partial\mathcal S$ (empty boundary, tensor every orientation line with $\mathfrak o_\mathbb R$) and an implicit atlas with boundary and cell-like stratification on $(X^{\leq\mathfrak s},X^{<\mathfrak s})\to(\mathcal S^{\leq\mathfrak s},\mathcal S^{<\mathfrak s})$ (tensor every orientation line with $\mathfrak o_\mathfrak s^\vee$).
nodes.statement_short: An implicit atlas with boundary plus compatible stratifications of all thickenings, locally pulled back from cell-like ones, with orientation data identifying $\mathfrak o_\mathfrak s$ with normal orientation lines.
nodes.definiendum: implicit atlas of dimension $d$ with boundary and cell-like stratification
nodes.genus: the same data as an implicit atlas with boundary
differentia: a $\Gamma_I$-invariant stratification $(X_I,\partial X_I)\to(\mathcal S,\partial\mathcal S)$ for all $I\subseteq A$, whose restriction to $X_\varnothing$ is the given stratification
nodes.label: IAwithstratification

nodes.name: Compatibility of stratum orientation identifications
nodes.statement: \begin{tikzcd} \mathfrak o_{(X_I^\mathrm{reg})^{\leq\mathfrak s}}\otimes\mathfrak o_\mathfrak s\ar{r}\ar{d}&\mathfrak o_{X_I^\mathrm{reg}}\ar[equals]{d}\\ \mathfrak o_{(X_I^\mathrm{reg})^{\leq\mathfrak t}}\otimes\mathfrak o_\mathfrak t\ar{r}&\mathfrak o_{X_I^\mathrm{reg}} \end{tikzcd}

nodes.name: Weaker cell-like hypothesis (non-embedded faces)
nodes.statement: There should be a slightly more general setting for the results of this section (and their proofs), which takes as input a weakened version of Definition \ref{celllikedef}. For example, it is probably enough to require that in a neighborhood of any $p\in M$, the closure of any (local) component of $M^\mathfrak s$ is a manifold with boundary whose interior is this local component (this is satisfied by both stratifications in Example \ref{celllikecornerexample}); basically this allows ``non-embedded faces''.

nodes.name: Stratified chains on a manifold with cell-like stratification
nodes.statement: As a first step towards understanding the main construction of this section, let us first describe a similar construction in a more familiar setting. Let $M$ be a topological manifold with cell-like stratification by $\mathcal S$. Define: \begin{equation} C_\bullet(M;\mathcal S):=\bigoplus_{\mathfrak s\in\mathcal S}C_{\bullet-(\dim M-\dim\mathfrak s)}(M^{\leq\mathfrak s};\mathfrak o_M\otimes\mathfrak o_{M^{\leq\mathfrak s}}^\vee) \end{equation} equipped with the differential given by the sum over $\operatorname{codim}(\mathfrak s\preceq\mathfrak t)=1$ of the pushforwards $C_\bullet(M^{\leq\mathfrak s})\to C_\bullet(M^{\leq\mathfrak t})$ (covered by the dual of the boundary map $\mathfrak o_{M^{\leq\mathfrak t}}\to\mathfrak o_{M^{\leq\mathfrak s}}$) plus the internal differential. This differential squares to zero by Lemma \ref{celllikelocalstructure} (the square of the differential is a sum over $\operatorname{codim}(\mathfrak s\preceq\mathfrak t)=2$ of maps $C_\bullet(M^{\leq\mathfrak s})\to C_\bullet(M^{\leq\mathfrak t})$, each of which can be seen to vanish by applying Lemma \ref{celllikelocalstructure}(\ref{intstratumstruct}) to $M^{<\mathfrak t}\to\mathcal S^{<\mathfrak t}$). Now there is a natural map: \begin{align} C_\bullet(M;\mathcal S)&\to C_\bullet(M)\\ \bigoplus_{\mathfrak s\in\mathcal S}\gamma_\mathfrak s&\mapsto\sum_{\begin{smallmatrix}\mathfrak s\in\mathcal S\cr\dim\mathfrak s=\dim M\end{smallmatrix}}\gamma_\mathfrak s \end{align} (it follows from Lemma \ref{celllikelocalstructure} that this is a chain map) which we claim is a quasi-isomorphism. To see that \eqref{stratchainstousual} is a quasi-isomorphism, observe that it is the map on global sections of a corresponding map of complexes of $\mathcal K$-presheaves $C_\bullet(M,M\setminus K;\mathcal S)\to C_\bullet(M,M\setminus K)$ on the one-point compactification $M_+$ of $M$. Both are homotopy $\mathcal K$-sheaves by Lemma \ref{singularchainshomotopyKsheaf}. Thus by Corollary \ref{homotopysheafcheckqionstalks}, it suffices to show that the map $C_\bullet(M,M\setminus p;\mathcal S)\to C_\bullet(M,M\setminus p)$ is a quasi-isomorphism for every $p\in M$. This holds by the following local argument. Note that $H_\bullet(M,M\setminus p;\mathcal S)$ is isomorphic to $\mathbb Z$ (to see this, consider the filtration by $\dim\mathfrak s$), so it suffices to construct a cycle in $C_\bullet(M,M\setminus p;\mathcal S)$ representing a generator of $\mathbb Z$ and show that its image in $H_\bullet(M,M\setminus p)=\mathbb Z$ is a generator. Such a cycle may be constructed by induction on $\mathcal S$ (starting from the stratum containing $p$ and going up), and its image in $H_\bullet(M,M\setminus p)$ generates since its degree at $p$ coincides with its degree at any nearby point in an open stratum, which is one by construction. A similar argument appears in Barraud--Cornea \cite[p670, Lemma 2.2]{barraudcornea}. Thus we can think of $C_\bullet(M;\mathcal S)$ as a model for chains on $M$ (the reader should make sure they understand what this means geometrically).
nodes.statement_short: Builds $C_\bullet(M;\mathcal S)$ from chains on closed strata with boundary pushforwards, and shows its map to $C_\bullet(M)$ is a quasi-isomorphism.
nodes.label: stratifiedchainsremark

nodes.name: Stratified chain complex $C_\bullet(M;\mathcal S)$
nodes.statement: C_\bullet(M;\mathcal S):=\bigoplus_{\mathfrak s\in\mathcal S}C_{\bullet-(\dim M-\dim\mathfrak s)}(M^{\leq\mathfrak s};\mathfrak o_M\otimes\mathfrak o_{M^{\leq\mathfrak s}}^\vee)

nodes.name: Stratified chains compute singular chains
nodes.statement: Now there is a natural map: \begin{align} C_\bullet(M;\mathcal S)&\to C_\bullet(M)\\ \bigoplus_{\mathfrak s\in\mathcal S}\gamma_\mathfrak s&\mapsto\sum_{\begin{smallmatrix}\mathfrak s\in\mathcal S\cr\dim\mathfrak s=\dim M\end{smallmatrix}}\gamma_\mathfrak s \end{align} (it follows from Lemma \ref{celllikelocalstructure} that this is a chain map) which we claim is a quasi-isomorphism.
conclusions: which we claim is a quasi-isomorphism.
nodes.statement_short: The natural map $C_\bullet(M;\mathcal S)\to C_\bullet(M)$ is a quasi-isomorphism.

nodes.name: Map from stratified chains to chains
nodes.statement: C_\bullet(M;\mathcal S)&\to C_\bullet(M)\\ \bigoplus_{\mathfrak s\in\mathcal S}\gamma_\mathfrak s&\mapsto\sum_{\begin{smallmatrix}\mathfrak s\in\mathcal S\cr\dim\mathfrak s=\dim M\end{smallmatrix}}\gamma_\mathfrak s
nodes.label: stratchainstousual

nodes.name: Proof that stratified chains compute singular chains
nodes.statement: To see that \eqref{stratchainstousual} is a quasi-isomorphism, observe that it is the map on global sections of a corresponding map of complexes of $\mathcal K$-presheaves $C_\bullet(M,M\setminus K;\mathcal S)\to C_\bullet(M,M\setminus K)$ on the one-point compactification $M_+$ of $M$. Both are homotopy $\mathcal K$-sheaves by Lemma \ref{singularchainshomotopyKsheaf}. Thus by Corollary \ref{homotopysheafcheckqionstalks}, it suffices to show that the map $C_\bullet(M,M\setminus p;\mathcal S)\to C_\bullet(M,M\setminus p)$ is a quasi-isomorphism for every $p\in M$. This holds by the following local argument. Note that $H_\bullet(M,M\setminus p;\mathcal S)$ is isomorphic to $\mathbb Z$ (to see this, consider the filtration by $\dim\mathfrak s$), so it suffices to construct a cycle in $C_\bullet(M,M\setminus p;\mathcal S)$ representing a generator of $\mathbb Z$ and show that its image in $H_\bullet(M,M\setminus p)=\mathbb Z$ is a generator. Such a cycle may be constructed by induction on $\mathcal S$ (starting from the stratum containing $p$ and going up), and its image in $H_\bullet(M,M\setminus p)$ generates since its degree at $p$ coincides with its degree at any nearby point in an open stratum, which is one by construction. A similar argument appears in Barraud--Cornea \cite[p670, Lemma 2.2]{barraudcornea}.
nodes.statement_short: Sheafify over the one-point compactification and check on stalks; locally build a generating cycle by induction up the strata and compare degrees with an open stratum.

nodes.name: Stratified virtual cochain complexes
nodes.statement: Let $(X,\partial X)\to(\mathcal S,\partial\mathcal S)$ be equipped with a finite implicit atlas with boundary and cell-like stratification $A$. For any compact $K\subseteq X$, we define: \begin{equation} C^\bullet_\mathrm{vir}(K,\mathcal S;A):=\bigoplus_{\mathfrak s\in\mathcal S}C^\bullet_\mathrm{vir}(K\cap X^{\leq\mathfrak s}\operatorname{rel}\partial;A)\otimes\mathfrak o_\mathfrak s \end{equation} (on the right, $A$ refers to the restriction of the atlas to $X^{\leq\mathfrak s}$) equipped with the differential given by the sum over $\operatorname{codim}(\mathfrak s\preceq\mathfrak t)=1$ of the pushforwards: \begin{equation} C^\bullet_\mathrm{vir}(K\cap X^{\leq\mathfrak s}\operatorname{rel}\partial;A)\to C^{\bullet+1}_\mathrm{vir}(K\cap X^{\leq\mathfrak t}\operatorname{rel}\partial;A) \end{equation} tensored with the specified coboundary map $\mathfrak o_\mathfrak s\to\mathfrak o_\mathfrak t$ (plus the internal differential). The fact that this differential squares to zero follows from Lemma \ref{celllikelocalstructure} and the compatibility of the coboundary maps $\mathfrak o_\mathfrak s\to\mathfrak o_\mathfrak t$ with the geometric boundary maps $\mathfrak o_{(X_I^\mathrm{reg})^{\leq\mathfrak t}}\to\mathfrak o_{(X_I^\mathrm{reg})^{\leq\mathfrak s}}$. There is a natural map: \begin{align} C^\bullet_\mathrm{vir}(K,\mathcal S;A)&\xrightarrow\sim C^\bullet(K;A)\\ \{\gamma_\mathfrak s\}_{\mathfrak s\in\mathcal S}&\mapsto\biggl(\sum_{\begin{smallmatrix}\mathfrak s\in\partial\mathcal S\cr\dim\mathfrak s=d-1\end{smallmatrix}}\gamma_\mathfrak s,\sum_{\begin{smallmatrix}\mathfrak s\in\mathcal S\cr\dim\mathfrak s=d\end{smallmatrix}}\gamma_\mathfrak s\biggr) \end{align} Note that for $\dim s=d$, the identification $\mathfrak o_{(X_I^\mathrm{reg})^{\leq\mathfrak s}}\otimes\mathfrak o_\mathfrak s=\mathfrak o_{X_I^\mathrm{reg}}$ gives a (locally constant, but possibly not constant) isomorphism $\mathfrak o_\mathfrak s=\mathbb Z$ over $(X_I^\mathrm{reg})^{\leq\mathfrak s}$ (and similarly for $\mathfrak s\in\partial\mathcal S$ with $\dim\mathfrak s=d-1$, see also Remark \ref{bdryorrmk}) which is used implicitly in \eqref{stratifiedtounformula}. This is a chain map by Lemma \ref{celllikelocalstructure}.
nodes.statement_short: Defines $C^\bullet_\mathrm{vir}(K,\mathcal S;A)$ as the sum over strata of virtual cochains of closed strata rel boundary, with stratum pushforward differentials and a map to $C^\bullet_\mathrm{vir}(K;A)$.
nodes.label: stratifiedvirtualdef

nodes.name: Stratified virtual cochain complex
nodes.statement: C^\bullet_\mathrm{vir}(K,\mathcal S;A):=\bigoplus_{\mathfrak s\in\mathcal S}C^\bullet_\mathrm{vir}(K\cap X^{\leq\mathfrak s}\operatorname{rel}\partial;A)\otimes\mathfrak o_\mathfrak s
nodes.label: virtualchainswithcornersdef

nodes.name: Stratum pushforward
nodes.statement: C^\bullet_\mathrm{vir}(K\cap X^{\leq\mathfrak s}\operatorname{rel}\partial;A)\to C^{\bullet+1}_\mathrm{vir}(K\cap X^{\leq\mathfrak t}\operatorname{rel}\partial;A)
nodes.label: stratumpushforward

nodes.name: Stratified-to-unstratified map
nodes.statement: C^\bullet_\mathrm{vir}(K,\mathcal S;A)&\xrightarrow\sim C^\bullet(K;A)\\ \{\gamma_\mathfrak s\}_{\mathfrak s\in\mathcal S}&\mapsto\biggl(\sum_{\begin{smallmatrix}\mathfrak s\in\partial\mathcal S\cr\dim\mathfrak s=d-1\end{smallmatrix}}\gamma_\mathfrak s,\sum_{\begin{smallmatrix}\mathfrak s\in\mathcal S\cr\dim\mathfrak s=d\end{smallmatrix}}\gamma_\mathfrak s\biggr)
nodes.label: stratifiedtounstratifiedpushforward

nodes.name: $C^\bullet_\mathrm{vir}(-,\mathcal S;A)\to C^\bullet_\mathrm{vir}(-;A)$ is a quasi-isomorphism
nodes.statement: Let $(X,\partial X)\to(\mathcal S,\partial\mathcal S)$ be equipped with a finite locally orientable implicit atlas with boundary and cell-like stratification $A$. Then \eqref{stratifiedtounstratifiedpushforward} is a quasi-isomorphism, and the following diagram of sheaves on $X$ commutes: \begin{equation*} \begin{tikzcd} H^0_\mathrm{vir}(-,\mathcal S;A)\ar{d}\ar{r}{\eqref{stratifiedtounstratifiedpushforward}}&H^0_\mathrm{vir}(-;A)\ar{r}{\text{Prop \ref{Cpure}}}&\mathfrak o_X\ar{d}\\ H^0_\mathrm{vir}(-\cap X^{\leq\mathfrak s},\mathcal S^{\leq\mathfrak s};A)\otimes\mathfrak o_\mathfrak s\ar{r}{\eqref{stratifiedtounstratifiedpushforward}}&H^0_\mathrm{vir}(-\cap X^{\leq\mathfrak s};A)\otimes\mathfrak o_\mathfrak s\ar{r}{\text{Prop \ref{Cpure}}}&\mathfrak o_{X^{\leq\mathfrak s}}\otimes\mathfrak o_\mathfrak s\\ H^0_\mathrm{vir}(-\cap X^{\leq\mathfrak s}\operatorname{rel}\partial;A)\otimes\mathfrak o_\mathfrak s\ar{u}\ar{rr}{\text{Prop \ref{Cpure}}}&&\mathfrak o_{X^{\leq\mathfrak s}\operatorname{rel}\partial}\otimes\mathfrak o_\mathfrak s\ar{u} \end{tikzcd} \end{equation*}
nodes.statement_short: The stratified virtual cochain complex maps quasi-isomorphically to the virtual cochain complex, compatibly with orientation sheaves on strata.
assumptions: Let $(X,\partial X)\to(\mathcal S,\partial\mathcal S)$ be equipped with a finite locally orientable implicit atlas with boundary and cell-like stratification $A$.
conclusions: \eqref{stratifiedtounstratifiedpushforward} is a quasi-isomorphism
nodes.label: stratifiedispurehomotopysheaf

nodes.name: Stratum inclusion is an isomorphism over a stratum
nodes.statement: Note that $C^\bullet_\mathrm{vir}(K\cap X^{\leq\mathfrak s}\operatorname{rel}\partial;A)\to C^\bullet_\mathrm{vir}(K\cap X^{\leq\mathfrak s},\mathcal S^{\leq\mathfrak s};A)$ is an isomorphism for $K\subseteq X^\mathfrak s$.

nodes.name: Proof
nodes.statement: Filter $C^\bullet_\mathrm{vir}(-,\mathcal S;A)$ by $\dim\mathfrak s$; the associated graded of this filtration is the direct sum of $C^\bullet_\mathrm{vir}(-\cap X^{\leq\mathfrak s}\operatorname{rel}\partial;A)$. Each these is a homotopy $\mathcal K$-sheaf on $X$ (pushforward from $X^{\leq\mathfrak s}$ to $X$ preserves homotopy $\mathcal K$-sheaves by Definition \ref{pushforwardofHsheavesworks}), and hence $C^\bullet_\mathrm{vir}(-,\mathcal S;A)$ is also a homotopy $\mathcal K$-sheaf (Lemma \ref{associatedgradedhomotopysheaf}). Now the map \eqref{stratifiedtounstratifiedpushforward} is a map of homotopy $\mathcal K$-sheaves, so to check that it is a quasi-isomorphism, it suffices to check it is a quasi-isomorphism on stalks (Corollary \ref{homotopysheafcheckqionstalks}). For this, we may use the argument from Example \ref{stratifiedchainsremark} (adapted to the case with boundary) along with Lemma \ref{localdescofISO}. Moreover, this local construction also gives us the desired commutativity of the diagram of sheaves on $X$.
nodes.statement_short: Filter by $\dim\mathfrak s$ to get a homotopy $\mathcal K$-sheaf; check quasi-isomorphism on stalks using the local argument of Example 6.2.9.

nodes.name: Product implicit atlas
nodes.statement: Let $X_1$ and $X_2$ be spaces with implicit atlases $A_1$ and $A_2$ respectively. The \emph{product implicit atlas} $A_1\sqcup A_2$ on $X_1\times X_2$ is defined by setting $(X_1\times X_2)_{I_1\sqcup I_2}:=(X_1)_{I_1}\times(X_2)_{I_2}$ and $(X_1\times Y_2)^\mathrm{reg}_{I_1\sqcup I_2}:=(X_1)_{I_1}^\mathrm{reg}\times(X_2)_{I_2}^\mathrm{reg}$, with the rest of the data extended in the obvious manner. Of course, this extends naturally to the setting of implicit atlases with boundary and cell-like stratification (given $X_1$ and $X_2$ stratified by $\mathcal S_1$ and $\mathcal S_2$ respectively, their product $X_1\times X_2$ is stratified by $\mathcal S_1\times\mathcal S_2$, with $\partial(\mathcal S_1\times\mathcal S_2):=(\partial\mathcal S_1\times\mathcal S_2)\cup(\mathcal S_1\times\partial\mathcal S_2)$).
nodes.statement_short: The product implicit atlas $A_1\sqcup A_2$ on $X_1\times X_2$ has thickenings $(X_1)_{I_1}\times(X_2)_{I_2}$; extends to boundary and stratifications.
nodes.label: productimplicitatlas

nodes.name: Product map on virtual cochain complexes
nodes.statement: Let $X_1$ and $X_2$ be spaces with finite implicit atlases $A_1$ and $A_2$; equip $X_1\times X_2$ with the product implicit atlas $A_1\sqcup A_2$. Let us define a canonical map: \begin{equation} C^\bullet_\mathrm{vir}(X_1\operatorname{rel}\partial;A_1)\otimes C^\bullet_\mathrm{vir}(X_2\operatorname{rel}\partial;A_2)\to C^\bullet_\mathrm{vir}(X_1\times X_2\operatorname{rel}\partial;A_1\sqcup A_2) \end{equation} which is compatible with the maps \eqref{Fpushforward} and \eqref{Fpushforward1} and is associative. There are isomorphisms $(X_1)_{I_1,J_1,A_1}\times(X_2)_{I_2,J_2,A_2}\to(X_1\times X_2)_{I_1\sqcup I_2,J_1\sqcup J_2,A_1\sqcup A_2}$ which are compatible with the maps \eqref{pushforward}. This induces maps: \begin{equation} C^\bullet_\mathrm{vir}(X_1\operatorname{rel}\partial;A_1)_{I_1,J_1}\otimes C^\bullet_\mathrm{vir}(X_2\operatorname{rel}\partial;A_2)_{I_2,J_2}\to C^\bullet_\mathrm{vir}(X_1\times X_2\operatorname{rel}\partial;A_1\sqcup A_2)_{I_1\sqcup I_2,J_1\sqcup J_2} \end{equation} These maps are compatible with the maps \eqref{Epushforward1more} (note that this compatibility uses the commutativity of \eqref{chainproductcommutes}). It follows using Definition \ref{simplicialproduct} that they induce the desired map \eqref{productatlaspushforward}. Note also that \eqref{productatlaspushforward} extends to a collection of maps: \begin{equation} C^\bullet_\mathrm{vir}(K_1\operatorname{rel}\partial;A_1)\otimes C^\bullet_\mathrm{vir}(K_2\operatorname{rel}\partial;A_2)\to C^\bullet_\mathrm{vir}(K_1\times K_2\operatorname{rel}\partial;A_1\sqcup A_2) \end{equation} for compact $K_1\subseteq X_1$ and $K_2\subseteq X_2$, which are compatible with restriction, thus inducing a map of sheaves $p_1^\ast\mathfrak o_{X_1}\otimes p_2^\ast\mathfrak o_{X_2}\to\mathfrak o_{X_1\times X_2}$. It can be checked that this is the tautological such map by checking locally (i.e.\ for $K_1$ and $K_2$ single points) using Lemma \ref{localdescofISO}.
nodes.statement_short: Constructs an associative product $C^\bullet_\mathrm{vir}(X_1\operatorname{rel}\partial;A_1)\otimes C^\bullet_\mathrm{vir}(X_2\operatorname{rel}\partial;A_2)\to C^\bullet_\mathrm{vir}(X_1\times X_2\operatorname{rel}\partial;A_1\sqcup A_2)$ compatible with $s_\ast$.
nodes.label: productatlasF

nodes.name: Product map on virtual cochains
nodes.statement: C^\bullet_\mathrm{vir}(X_1\operatorname{rel}\partial;A_1)\otimes C^\bullet_\mathrm{vir}(X_2\operatorname{rel}\partial;A_2)\to C^\bullet_\mathrm{vir}(X_1\times X_2\operatorname{rel}\partial;A_1\sqcup A_2)
nodes.label: productatlaspushforward

nodes.name: Product map on partial virtual cochains
nodes.statement: C^\bullet_\mathrm{vir}(X_1\operatorname{rel}\partial;A_1)_{I_1,J_1}\otimes C^\bullet_\mathrm{vir}(X_2\operatorname{rel}\partial;A_2)_{I_2,J_2}\to C^\bullet_\mathrm{vir}(X_1\times X_2\operatorname{rel}\partial;A_1\sqcup A_2)_{I_1\sqcup I_2,J_1\sqcup J_2}

nodes.name: Product map on virtual cochains over compact subsets
nodes.statement: C^\bullet_\mathrm{vir}(K_1\operatorname{rel}\partial;A_1)\otimes C^\bullet_\mathrm{vir}(K_2\operatorname{rel}\partial;A_2)\to C^\bullet_\mathrm{vir}(K_1\times K_2\operatorname{rel}\partial;A_1\sqcup A_2)
nodes.label: productatlaspushforwardonK

nodes.name: Ground ring convention for Floer-type homology
nodes.statement: In this section, we work over a fixed ground ring $R$, and everything takes place in the category of $R$-modules unless stated otherwise. We restrict to implicit atlases $A$ for which $\#\Gamma_\alpha$ is invertible in $R$ for all $\alpha\in A$.
nodes.statement_short: Work over a ground ring $R$ in which every $\#\Gamma_\alpha$ is invertible.

nodes.name: Diagram $\widetilde\mathbb H$ over the resolution (introduction)
nodes.statement: \begin{CD} \tilde Z_\bullet@>\widetilde\mathbb H>>\mathsf{N}_{\mathsf{dg}}(\mathsf{Ch}_R)\cr @V\pi VV\cr Z_\bullet \end{CD}

nodes.name: Restricting to the 2-skeleton of $Z_\bullet$
nodes.statement: If one is satisfied with working in the homotopy category (i.e.\ constructing a diagram $Z_\bullet\to H^0(\mathsf{Ch}_R)$), then one needs only the $2$-skeleton of $Z_\bullet$. On the other hand, there is little simplification to be gained by using $2$-truncated semisimplicial sets instead of semisimplicial sets. Moreover, the ``higher homotopies'' which are kept track of in $\mathsf{N}_{\mathsf{dg}}(\mathsf{Ch}_R)$ are known to contain interesting information in certain settings (for example, they can be used to obstruct isotopies between symplectic embeddings, as in Floer--Hofer--Wysocki \cite{floerhoferwysockiSHI}).
nodes.statement_short: For diagrams into the homotopy category only the 2-skeleton of $Z_\bullet$ is needed, but higher homotopies carry interesting information.
nodes.label: restricttotwoskeleton

nodes.name: Simplicial set and semisimplicial set
nodes.statement: Let $\Delta$ be the category of finite nonempty totally ordered sets with morphisms weakly order-preserving maps. Let $\Delta_\mathrm{inj}$ be the subcategory of injective morphisms. A \emph{simplicial set} $Z_\bullet$ is a functor $Z:\Delta^\mathrm{op}\to\mathsf{Set}$, and a \emph{semisimplicial set} $Z_\bullet$ is a functor $Z:\Delta_\mathrm{inj}^\mathrm{op}\to\mathsf{Set}$. In both cases, we write $Z_n$ for $Z(\{0,\ldots,n\})$. For $\sigma\in Z_n$ and $0\leq j_0<\cdots<j_m\leq n$, we denote by $\sigma|[j_0\ldots j_m]$ the image of $\sigma$ under the map $Z_n\to Z_m$ induced by the map $\{0,\ldots,m\}\to\{0,\ldots,n\}$ given by $i\mapsto j_i$ ($\sigma|[j_0\ldots j_m]$ is called a facet of $\sigma$); if $m=0$ we also write $\sigma(j)$ for $\sigma|[j]$.
nodes.statement_short: Simplicial sets are functors $\Delta^{op}\to\mathsf{Set}$, semisimplicial sets functors $\Delta_{inj}^{op}\to\mathsf{Set}$; facets $\sigma|[j_0\ldots j_m]$.

nodes.name: Set of generators
nodes.statement: Let $Z$ be a set. A \emph{set of generators} $\mathcal P/Z$ is a collection of sets $\{\mathcal P_z\}_{z\in Z}$, each equipped with a grading $\operatorname{gr}:\mathcal P_z\to\mathbb Z$ and an ``action'' $a:\mathcal P_z\to\mathbb R$. Given a set of generators $\mathcal P/Z$ and a map $f:Y\to Z$, we can form the pullback set of generators $f^\ast\mathcal P/Y$ defined by $(f^\ast\mathcal P)_y:=\mathcal P_{f(y)}$.
nodes.statement_short: Sets $\mathcal P_z$ over $z\in Z$ with grading and action; pullback along maps.
nodes.genus: a collection of sets $\{\mathcal P_z\}_{z\in Z}$
differentia: each equipped with a grading $\operatorname{gr}:\mathcal P_z\to\mathbb Z$ and an ``action'' $a:\mathcal P_z\to\mathbb R$

nodes.name: Triples $(\sigma,p,q)$ and strict precedence
nodes.statement: Let $Z_\bullet$ be a semisimplicial set, and let $\mathcal P/Z_0$ be a set of generators. The notation $(\sigma,p,q)$ \emph{always} means a triple where $\sigma\in Z_n$ is an $n$-simplex and $(p,q)\in\mathcal P_{\sigma(0)}\times\mathcal P_{\sigma(n)}$, where either $\dim\sigma>0$ or $a(p)<a(q)$. We say that $(\sigma',p',q')\prec(\sigma,p,q)$ (``strictly precedes'') iff one of the two conditions holds: \begin{rlist} \item$\sigma'\subsetneqq\sigma$ (i.e.\ $\sigma'$ is a facet of positive codimension of $\sigma$). \item$\sigma'=\sigma$ and $a(p)\leq a(p')$ and $a(q')\leq a(q)$ with at least one inequality being strict. \end{rlist} It is easy to see that $\prec$ is a partial order.
nodes.statement_short: Triples of a simplex and generators at its first/last vertices, partially ordered by facet inclusion and action.

nodes.name: $\mathsf{F}$-module
nodes.statement: Let $Z_\bullet$ be a semisimplicial set, and let $\mathcal P/Z_0$ be a set of generators. Let $\mathcal C^\otimes$ be a monoidal category with an initial object $0\in\mathcal C$ such that $X\otimes 0=0=0\otimes X$ for all $X\in\mathcal C$. An \emph{$\mathsf{F}(\mathcal P/Z_\bullet)$-module} $\mathcal W$ (often abbreviated ``$\mathsf{F}$-module'') in $\mathcal C$ is a collection of objects $\mathcal W=\{\mathcal W(\sigma,p,q)\in\mathcal C\}_{(\sigma,p,q)}$ equipped with: \begin{align} \text{\emph{Product maps}:}&&\mathcal W(\sigma|[0\ldots k],p,q)\otimes\mathcal W(\sigma|[k\ldots n],q,r)&\to\mathcal W(\sigma,p,r)\quad\text{for }0\leq k\leq n\\ \text{\emph{Face maps}:}&&\mathcal W(\sigma|[0\ldots\hat k\ldots n],p,q)&\to\mathcal W(\sigma,p,q)\quad\text{for }0<k<n \end{align} which are compatible in a sense we will now describe. Note that for both \eqref{Wcomposition} and \eqref{Wsimplexextension}, the triples indexing the domain strictly precede the triple indexing the target (because we always restrict to triples $(\sigma,p,q)$ with $\dim\sigma>0$ or $a(p)<a(q)$). Now given any $\sigma\in Z_\bullet$ spanning vertices $0,\ldots,n$ and a choice of: \begin{align} 0&=j_0<\cdots<j_\ell=n\\ 0&=a_0\leq\cdots\leq a_m=\ell\\ p_i&\in\mathcal P_{\sigma(j_{a_i})}\quad\text{for }0\leq i\leq m \end{align} we can apply the product map $m-1$ times and the face map $n-\ell$ times in some order to obtain a map: \begin{equation} \mathcal W(\sigma|[j_{a_0}\ldots j_{a_1}],p_0,p_1)\otimes\cdots\otimes\mathcal W(\sigma|[j_{a_{m-1}}\ldots j_{a_m}],p_{m-1},p_m)\to\mathcal W(\sigma,p_0,p_m) \end{equation} We say that the product/face maps are \emph{compatible} iff this map is independent of the order in which they are applied (this reduces to three basic commutation identities). Given an $\mathsf{F}(\mathcal P/Z_\bullet)$-module $\mathcal W$ and a map $f:Y_\bullet\to Z_\bullet$, we can form the pullback $f^\ast\mathcal W$ which is an $\mathsf{F}(f^\ast\mathcal P/Y_\bullet)$-module defined by $(f^\ast\mathcal W)(\sigma,p,q):=\mathcal W(f(\sigma),p,q)$. The categories $\mathcal C$ relevant for this paper are: \begin{rlist} \item The category of spaces with the product monoidal structure (``$\mathsf{F}$-module space''). \item The category of posets with the product monoidal structure (``$\mathsf{F}$-module poset''). \item The category of chain complexes with the tensor product monoidal structure (``$\mathsf{F}$-module complex''). \end{rlist} All are in fact symmetric monoidal (noting that the relevant symmetric monoidal structure on complexes is the super tensor product).
nodes.statement_short: A collection of objects $\mathcal W(\sigma,p,q)$ in a monoidal category with compatible product maps and face maps; pullbacks along maps of semisimplicial sets.
nodes.genus: a collection of objects $\mathcal W=\{\mathcal W(\sigma,p,q)\in\mathcal C\}_{(\sigma,p,q)}$
differentia: equipped with:
We say that the product/face maps are \emph{compatible} iff this map is independent of the order in which they are applied
nodes.label: flowobjectdef

nodes.name: Product and face maps of an $\mathsf{F}$-module
nodes.statement: \text{\emph{Product maps}:}&&\mathcal W(\sigma|[0\ldots k],p,q)\otimes\mathcal W(\sigma|[k\ldots n],q,r)&\to\mathcal W(\sigma,p,r)\quad\text{for }0\leq k\leq n\\ \text{\emph{Face maps}:}&&\mathcal W(\sigma|[0\ldots\hat k\ldots n],p,q)&\to\mathcal W(\sigma,p,q)\quad\text{for }0<k<n
nodes.label: Wcomposition

nodes.name: Decomposition data for a simplex
nodes.statement: 0&=j_0<\cdots<j_\ell=n\\ 0&=a_0\leq\cdots\leq a_m=\ell\\ p_i&\in\mathcal P_{\sigma(j_{a_i})}\quad\text{for }0\leq i\leq m
nodes.label: SdataA

nodes.name: Total composition map of an $\mathsf{F}$-module
nodes.statement: \mathcal W(\sigma|[j_{a_0}\ldots j_{a_1}],p_0,p_1)\otimes\cdots\otimes\mathcal W(\sigma|[j_{a_{m-1}}\ldots j_{a_m}],p_{m-1},p_m)\to\mathcal W(\sigma,p_0,p_m)
nodes.label: Wtotalcomposition

nodes.name: $\mathsf{F}$-module space of broken Morse trajectories on simplices
nodes.statement: Let $Z_\bullet$ be any semisimplicial set, and let us take as set of generators $\mathcal P:=Z_0$ (i.e.\ a single generator over every vertex of $Z_\bullet$). We define an $\mathsf{F}(\mathcal P/Z_\bullet)$-module space $\mathcal W$ by $\mathcal W(\sigma,p,q):=\mathcal F(\sigma)$, where $\mathcal F$ is the space of broken Morse trajectories from Definition \ref{simplexflows}. The reader may easily verify that this forms an $\mathsf{F}$-module space, with product/face maps given by \eqref{Fproduct}--\eqref{Fface}.
nodes.statement_short: Taking one generator per vertex, the spaces $\mathcal F(\sigma)$ of broken Morse trajectories form an $\mathsf{F}$-module space.
nodes.label: Fmoduleexample

nodes.name: Support of an $\mathsf{F}$-module
nodes.statement: Let $\mathcal W$ be an $\mathsf{F}$-module. We define the \emph{support} of $\mathcal W$, denoted $\operatorname{supp}\mathcal W$, as the smallest collection of triples containing those for which $\mathcal W(\sigma,p,q)\ne 0$ that is closed under product/face operations (meaning that if the triples on the left side of \eqref{Wcomposition} or \eqref{Wsimplexextension} are in the set, then so is the triple on the right). Equivalently, $(\sigma,p,q)\in\operatorname{supp}\mathcal W$ iff there is some choice of \eqref{SdataA}--\eqref{SdataB} for which $p_0=p$ and $p_m=q$ and for which every factor on the left hand side of \eqref{Wtotalcomposition} is $\ne 0$.
nodes.statement_short: Smallest product/face-closed set of triples containing those with $\mathcal W(\sigma,p,q)\ne 0$.

nodes.name: Strata of an $\mathsf{F}$-module
nodes.statement: Let $\mathcal W$ be an $\mathsf{F}$-module. We let $\mathcal S_\mathcal W(\sigma,p,q)$ denote the set of choices of \eqref{SdataA}--\eqref{SdataB} for which $p_0=p$ and $p_m=q$ and for which every factor on the left hand side of \eqref{Wtotalcomposition} is in $\operatorname{supp}\mathcal W$. We equip $\mathcal S_\mathcal W(\sigma,p,q)$ with the partial order induced by formally applying product/face maps. The reader may easily convince themselves that $\mathcal S_\mathcal W$ is itself an $\mathsf{F}$-module poset. There is an order-reversing map $\operatorname{codim}:\mathcal S_\mathcal W(\sigma,p,q)\to\mathbb Z_{\geq 0}$ defined by $\operatorname{codim}\mathfrak s:=(m-1)+(n-\ell)$ for $\mathfrak s\in\mathcal S_\mathcal W(\sigma,p,q)$. We let $\mathfrak s^\mathrm{top}\in\mathcal S_\mathcal W(\sigma,p,q)$ denote the unique maximal element (the only element $\mathfrak s$ with $\operatorname{codim}\mathfrak s=0$; it is given by $\ell=n$ and $m=1$). For $\mathfrak s\in\mathcal S_\mathcal W(\sigma,p,q)$, we let $\mathcal W(\sigma,p,q,\mathfrak s)$ denote the left hand side of \eqref{Wtotalcomposition}. The following \emph{boundary inclusion map}: \begin{equation} \operatornamewithlimits{colim}_{\mathfrak s\in\partial\mathcal S_\mathcal W(\sigma,p,q)}\mathcal W(\sigma,p,q,\mathfrak s)\to\mathcal W(\sigma,p,q) \end{equation} (where $\partial\mathcal S_\mathcal W(\sigma,p,q)$ denotes $\mathcal S_\mathcal W(\sigma,p,q)\setminus\mathfrak s^\mathrm{top}$) will play an important role.
nodes.statement_short: The poset $\mathcal S_\mathcal W(\sigma,p,q)$ of formal product/face decompositions, with codimension, top element, and the boundary inclusion map.

nodes.name: Boundary inclusion map
nodes.statement: \operatornamewithlimits{colim}_{\mathfrak s\in\partial\mathcal S_\mathcal W(\sigma,p,q)}\mathcal W(\sigma,p,q,\mathfrak s)\to\mathcal W(\sigma,p,q)
nodes.label: boundaryinclusion

nodes.name: Flow category diagram
nodes.statement: Let $Z_\bullet$ be a semisimplicial set. A \emph{flow category diagram} $\mathcal X/Z_\bullet$ (read ``$\mathcal X$ over $Z_\bullet$'') is: \begin{rlist} \item A set of generators $\mathcal P/Z_0$. \item An $\mathsf{F}$-module space $\mathcal X$ where each $\mathcal X(\sigma,p,q)$ is compact Hausdorff and each $\mathcal S_\mathcal X(\sigma,p,q)$ is finite. \item A stratification of each $\mathcal X(\sigma,p,q)$ by $\mathcal S_\mathcal X(\sigma,p,q)$ which is compatible with the product/face maps and so that $\mathcal X(\sigma,p,q,\mathfrak s)\to\mathcal X(\sigma,p,q)$ is a homeomorphism onto $\mathcal X(\sigma,p,q)^{\leq\mathfrak s}$. \setcounter{rcountsave}{\value{rcounti}} \end{rlist} with the following finiteness properties: \begin{rlist} \setcounter{rcounti}{\value{rcountsave}} \itemFor all $\sigma$, $p$, and $M<\infty$, we have $\#\{q:\mathcal X(\sigma,p,q)\ne\varnothing\text{ and }a(q)<a(p)+M\}<\infty$. \itemFor all $\sigma$, we have $\inf\{a(q)-a(p):\mathcal X(\sigma,p,q)\ne\varnothing\}>-\infty$. \setcounter{rcountsave}{\value{rcounti}} \end{rlist} Let $H$ be a group. An \emph{$H$-equivariant flow category diagram} is a flow category diagram along with: \begin{rlist} \setcounter{rcounti}{\value{rcountsave}} \item A free action of $H$ on $\mathcal P$. \item An action of $H$ on $\mathcal X$ (meaning compatible maps $h:\mathcal X(\sigma,p,q)\to\mathcal X(\sigma,hp,hq)$). \item Homomorphisms $\operatorname{gr}:H\to\mathbb Z$ and $a:H\to\mathbb R$ such that $\operatorname{gr}(hp)=\operatorname{gr}(h)+\operatorname{gr}(p)$ and $a(hp)=a(h)+a(p)$ for all $h\in H$ and $p\in\mathcal P$. \end{rlist} Given an $H$-equivariant flow category diagram $\mathcal X/Z_\bullet$ and a map $f:Y_\bullet\to Z_\bullet$, we can form the pullback $H$-equivariant flow category diagram $f^\ast\mathcal X/Y_\bullet$.
nodes.section: 7.2 Flow category diagrams and their implicit atlases
nodes.statement_short: Generators over $Z_0$ plus an $\mathsf{F}$-module space of compact stratified flow spaces with Novikov finiteness; $H$-equivariant version and pullback.
nodes.label: semisimplicialfcdef

nodes.name: Morse--Smale flow category diagram
nodes.statement: A \emph{Morse--Smale} flow category diagram is one in which each $\mathcal X(\sigma,p,q)$ is a (compact) topological manifold with corners of dimension $\operatorname{gr}(q)-\operatorname{gr}(p)+\dim\sigma-1$ (the corner structure being induced by the stratification by $\mathcal S_\mathcal X(\sigma,p,q)$).
nodes.section: 7.2 Flow category diagrams and their implicit atlases
differentia: each $\mathcal X(\sigma,p,q)$ is a (compact) topological manifold with corners of dimension $\operatorname{gr}(q)-\operatorname{gr}(p)+\dim\sigma-1$
nodes.label: MSflowcatediag

nodes.name: $\infty$-category $\mathsf{FlowCat}$
nodes.statement: Let $\mathsf{FlowCat}$ be the semisimplicial set which represents the functor $Z_\bullet\mapsto\{$Flow category diagrams over $Z_\bullet\}$. The reader familiar with $\infty$-categories may wish to think of $\mathsf{FlowCat}$ as an $\infty$-category of flow categories (though only in a vague sense, since we have not given it the structure of a simplicial set, nor have we verified the weak Kan condition). All of the constructions in this section involving flow category diagrams over a semisimplicial set $Z_\bullet$ are compatible with pullback, and thus can be equivalently thought of as ``universal'' constructions over $\mathsf{FlowCat}^{\mathsf{IA}}$ (which represents the functor of flow category diagrams equipped with implicit atlases).
nodes.section: 7.2 Flow category diagrams and their implicit atlases
nodes.statement_short: Flow category diagrams are represented by a semisimplicial set $\mathsf{FlowCat}$, vaguely an $\infty$-category; all constructions are compatible with pullback.

nodes.name: Implicit atlas on flow category diagram
nodes.statement: Let $\mathcal X/Z_\bullet$ be a flow category diagram. An implicit atlas $\mathcal A$ on $\mathcal X/Z_\bullet$ consists of the following data. We give index sets $\bar\mathcal A(\sigma,p,q)$, and we define:\footnote{Warning: a particular set $\bar\mathcal A(\sigma',p',q')$ may appear many times on the right hand side.} \begin{equation} \mathcal A(\sigma,p,q)^{\geq\mathfrak s}:=\coprod_{\begin{smallmatrix}0\leq i_0<\cdots<i_m\leq n\cr(p',q')\in\mathcal P_{\sigma(i_0)}\times\mathcal P_{\sigma(i_m)}\cr\exists\mathfrak t\in\mathcal S_\mathcal X(\sigma,p,q)^{\geq\mathfrak s}\text{ containing }([i_0\ldots i_m],p',q')\end{smallmatrix}}\bar\mathcal A(\sigma|[i_0\ldots i_m],p',q') \end{equation} We explain the notation: recall that $\mathcal S_\mathcal X(\sigma,p,q)$ parameterizes the ``possible left hand sides'' of \eqref{Wtotalcomposition}; the coproduct is over all $([i_0\ldots i_m],p',q')$ which appear as a factor in some $\mathfrak t\in\mathcal S_\mathcal X(\sigma,p,q)$ with $\mathfrak s\preceq\mathfrak t$. For all $(\sigma,p,q)$ and $\mathfrak s\in\mathcal S_\mathcal X(\sigma,p,q)$, we give an implicit atlas with boundary with cell-like stratification $\mathcal A(\sigma,p,q)^{\geq\mathfrak s}$ on $\mathcal X(\sigma,p,q)^{\leq\mathfrak s}$ (stratified by $\mathcal S_\mathcal X(\sigma,p,q)^{\leq\mathfrak s}$, of virtual dimension $\operatorname{gr}(q)-\operatorname{gr}(p)+\dim\sigma-1-\operatorname{codim}\mathfrak s$), for which the stratification conforms to the following local model. Given $\mathfrak s'\preceq\mathfrak s$, let $G=G(\mathfrak s',\mathfrak s)$ denote the set of possible product/face operations which may be applied to $\mathfrak s'$ for which the result is still $\preceq\mathfrak s$. There is a tautological isomorphism of posets $2^G\to\mathcal S_\mathcal X(\sigma,p,q)^{\mathfrak s'\leq\cdot\leq\mathfrak s}$ sending a given set of product/face operations to the result of applying them to $\mathfrak s'$. Now the local model for the stratification on (regular thickened moduli spaces of) $\mathcal X(\sigma,p,q)^{\leq\mathfrak s}$ near a point of type $\mathfrak s'$ is given by $\mathbb R_{\geq 0}^G\times\mathbb R^N$, stratified in the obvious way by $\mathcal S_\mathcal X(\sigma,p,q)^{\mathfrak s'\leq\cdot\leq\mathfrak s}$. Clearly this stratification is cell-like. Moreover, the normal bundle to the $\mathfrak s'$ stratum is canonically identified with $\mathfrak o_\mathbb R^{\otimes G(\mathfrak s',\mathfrak s)}$, and the implicit atlas should use this as the orientation data. In addition, we give compatible identifications between these atlases as follows: \begin{rlist} \itemLet $\mathfrak s\preceq\mathfrak t\in\mathcal S_\mathcal X(\sigma,p,q)$. Then by definition: \begin{equation*} \mathcal A(\sigma,p,q)^{\geq\mathfrak t}\subseteq\mathcal A(\sigma,p,q)^{\geq\mathfrak s} \end{equation*} Both are implicit atlases on $\mathcal X(\sigma,p,q)^{\leq\mathfrak s}$ (the former by restriction to this substratum of $\mathcal X(\sigma,p,q)^{\leq\mathfrak t}$), and we identify the former with the subatlas of the latter corresponding to this tautological inclusion of index sets. \itemLet $\mathfrak s\in\mathcal S_\mathcal X(\sigma|[0\ldots\hat k\ldots n],p,q)\subseteq\mathcal S_\mathcal X(\sigma,p,q)$. Then by definition: \begin{equation*} \mathcal A(\sigma|[0\ldots\hat k\ldots n],p,q)^{\geq\mathfrak s}\subseteq\mathcal A(\sigma,p,q)^{\geq\mathfrak s} \end{equation*} Both are implicit atlases on: \begin{equation*} \mathcal X(\sigma|[0\ldots\hat k\ldots n],p,q)^{\leq\mathfrak s}=\mathcal X(\sigma,p,q)^{\leq\mathfrak s} \end{equation*} and we identify the former with the subatlas of the latter corresponding to this tautological inclusion of index sets. \itemLet $\mathfrak s_1\times\mathfrak s_2\in\mathcal S_\mathcal X(\sigma|[0\ldots k],p,q)\times\mathcal S_\mathcal X(\sigma|[k\ldots n],q,r)\subseteq\mathcal S_\mathcal X(\sigma,p,r)$. Then by definition: \begin{equation*} \mathcal A(\sigma|[0\ldots k],p,q)^{\geq\mathfrak s_1}\sqcup\mathcal A(\sigma|[k\ldots n],q,r)^{\geq\mathfrak s_2}\subseteq\mathcal A(\sigma,p,r)^{\geq(\mathfrak s_1\times\mathfrak s_2)} \end{equation*} Both are implicit atlases on: \begin{equation*} \mathcal X(\sigma|[0\ldots k],p,q)^{\leq\mathfrak s_1}\times\mathcal X(\sigma|[k\ldots n],q,r)^{\leq\mathfrak s_2}=\mathcal X(\sigma,p,r)^{\leq(\mathfrak s_1\times\mathfrak s_2)} \end{equation*} and we identify the former with the subatlas of the latter corresponding to this tautological inclusion of index sets. \end{rlist} An implicit atlas on an $H$-equivariant flow category $\mathcal X/Z_\bullet$ is an implicit atlas along with a lift of the action of $H$ to the implicit atlas structure. Given an implicit atlas $\mathcal A$ on $\mathcal X/Z_\bullet$ and a map $f:Y_\bullet\to Z_\bullet$, we can form the pullback implicit atlas $f^\ast\mathcal A$ on $f^\ast\mathcal X/Y_\bullet$.
nodes.section: 7.2 Flow category diagrams and their implicit atlases
nodes.statement_short: Index sets $\bar{\mathcal A}(\sigma,p,q)$ giving implicit atlases with boundary and cell-like stratification on each $\mathcal X(\sigma,p,q)^{\leq\mathfrak s}$, compatibly identified under substratum, face and product maps.
nodes.definiendum: implicit atlas on a flow category diagram
nodes.label: IAonflowcategorydiagramdef

nodes.name: Index set $\mathcal A(\sigma,p,q)^{\geq\mathfrak s}$ as a coproduct
nodes.statement: \mathcal A(\sigma,p,q)^{\geq\mathfrak s}:=\coprod_{\begin{smallmatrix}0\leq i_0<\cdots<i_m\leq n\cr(p',q')\in\mathcal P_{\sigma(i_0)}\times\mathcal P_{\sigma(i_m)}\cr\exists\mathfrak t\in\mathcal S_\mathcal X(\sigma,p,q)^{\geq\mathfrak s}\text{ containing }([i_0\ldots i_m],p',q')\end{smallmatrix}}\bar\mathcal A(\sigma|[i_0\ldots i_m],p',q')
nodes.section: 7.2 Flow category diagrams and their implicit atlases
nodes.label: coproductforA

nodes.name: Remark on the definition of implicit atlas on flow category diagram
nodes.statement: The above definition has been formulated to reflect the collection of atlases which is the simplest to construct, yet still sufficient to define Floer-type homology groups.
nodes.section: 7.2 Flow category diagrams and their implicit atlases

nodes.name: Coherent orientations
nodes.statement: Let $\mathcal X/Z_\bullet$ be a flow category diagram with locally orientable implicit atlas $\mathcal A$. A set of \emph{coherent orientations} $\omega$ is a choice of global sections $\omega(\sigma,p,q)\in\check H^0(\mathcal X(\sigma,p,q);\mathfrak o_{\mathcal X(\sigma,p,q)})$ with the following property. Note that covering each of the product/face maps: \begin{align} \mathcal X(\sigma|[0\ldots k],p,q)\times\mathcal X(\sigma|[k\ldots n],q,r)&\to\partial\mathcal X(\sigma,p,r)\\ \mathcal X(\sigma|[0\ldots\hat k\ldots n],p,q)&\to\partial\mathcal X(\sigma,p,q) \end{align} is an isomorphism of orientation sheaves. We require that $\omega$ transform in the following way under this isomorphism: \begin{align} \omega(\sigma|[0\ldots k],p,q)\times\omega(\sigma|[k\ldots n],q,r)&=(-1)^{k+\operatorname{gr}(p)}d\omega(\sigma,p,r)\\ -\omega(\sigma|[0\ldots\hat k\ldots n],p,q)&=(-1)^{k+\operatorname{gr}(p)}d\omega(\sigma,p,q) \end{align} where $d\omega\in\check H^0(\partial\mathcal X;\mathfrak o_{\partial\mathcal X})$ is the boundary orientation induced by $\omega$. Each of the following: \begin{gather} \omega(\sigma|[0\ldots k],p,p')\times\omega(\sigma|[k\ldots\ell],p',p'')\times\omega(\sigma|[\ell\ldots n],p'',q)\\ \omega(\sigma|[0\ldots\hat k\ldots\ell],p,p')\times\omega(\sigma|[\ell\ldots n],p',q)\\ \omega(\sigma|[0\ldots k],p,p')\times\omega(\sigma|[k\ldots\hat\ell\ldots n],p',q)\\ \omega(\sigma|[0\ldots\hat k\ldots\hat\ell\ldots n],p,q) \end{gather} can be expressed in terms of $\omega(\sigma,p,q)$ in two different ways using \eqref{coherentOproduct}--\eqref{coherentOface}. One can easily check that with the choice of signs in \eqref{coherentOproduct}--\eqref{coherentOface}, these two expressions coincide for each of \eqref{multiorientationI}--\eqref{multiorientationIV} (the Koszul rule of signs applies to calculating the boundary of a product of orientations, which means that this coherence condition involves $\operatorname{vdim}\mathcal X(\sigma|[0\ldots k],p,p')$ for both \eqref{multiorientationI} and \eqref{multiorientationIII}). Coherent orientations on an $H$-equivariant flow category diagram with implicit atlas are coherent orientations which are invariant under the action of $H$. Given coherent orientations $\omega$ on $\mathcal X/Z_\bullet$ and a map $f:Y_\bullet\to Z_\bullet$, we can form the pullback coherent orientations $f^\ast\omega$ on $f^\ast\mathcal X/Y_\bullet$.
nodes.section: 7.2 Flow category diagrams and their implicit atlases
nodes.statement_short: Global orientation sections $\omega(\sigma,p,q)$ transforming with prescribed signs under product/face maps; the sign choices are consistent.
nodes.label: cohordefabstract

nodes.name: Product/face maps into boundaries of flow spaces
nodes.statement: \mathcal X(\sigma|[0\ldots k],p,q)\times\mathcal X(\sigma|[k\ldots n],q,r)&\to\partial\mathcal X(\sigma,p,r)\\ \mathcal X(\sigma|[0\ldots\hat k\ldots n],p,q)&\to\partial\mathcal X(\sigma,p,q)
nodes.section: 7.2 Flow category diagrams and their implicit atlases

nodes.name: Coherent orientation sign rules
nodes.statement: \omega(\sigma|[0\ldots k],p,q)\times\omega(\sigma|[k\ldots n],q,r)&=(-1)^{k+\operatorname{gr}(p)}d\omega(\sigma,p,r)\\ -\omega(\sigma|[0\ldots\hat k\ldots n],p,q)&=(-1)^{k+\operatorname{gr}(p)}d\omega(\sigma,p,q)
nodes.section: 7.2 Flow category diagrams and their implicit atlases
nodes.label: coherentOproduct

nodes.name: Multi-orientation products for sign coherence
nodes.statement: \omega(\sigma|[0\ldots k],p,p')\times\omega(\sigma|[k\ldots\ell],p',p'')\times\omega(\sigma|[\ell\ldots n],p'',q)\\ \omega(\sigma|[0\ldots\hat k\ldots\ell],p,p')\times\omega(\sigma|[\ell\ldots n],p',q)\\ \omega(\sigma|[0\ldots k],p,p')\times\omega(\sigma|[k\ldots\hat\ell\ldots n],p',q)\\ \omega(\sigma|[0\ldots\hat k\ldots\hat\ell\ldots n],p,q)
nodes.section: 7.2 Flow category diagrams and their implicit atlases
nodes.label: multiorientationI

nodes.name: Alternative sign conventions for coherent orientations
nodes.statement: One can obtain alternative sign conventions in \eqref{coherentOproduct}--\eqref{coherentOface} by ``twisting'' $\omega(\sigma,p,q)$. For example, multiplying $\omega(\sigma,p,q)$ by $(-1)$ flips the sign of \eqref{coherentOproduct}, multiplying by $(-1)^{\dim\sigma}$ flips the sign of \eqref{coherentOface}, and multiplying by $(-1)^{\operatorname{gr}(p)}$ or $(-1)^{\operatorname{gr}(q)}$ multiplies \eqref{coherentOproduct} by $(-1)^{\operatorname{gr}(q)}$.
nodes.section: 7.2 Flow category diagrams and their implicit atlases
nodes.statement_short: Twisting $\omega$ by signs depending on $\dim\sigma$ or gradings changes the sign conventions for coherent orientations.

nodes.name: Naive product/face maps on virtual cochain complexes
