nodes.statement: C^\bullet_\mathrm{vir}(\mathcal X(\sigma|[0\ldots k],p,q)\operatorname{rel}\partial)\otimes C^\bullet_\mathrm{vir}(\mathcal X(\sigma|[k\ldots n],q,r)\operatorname{rel}\partial)&\to C^\bullet_\mathrm{vir}(\partial\mathcal X(\sigma,p,r))\\ C^\bullet_\mathrm{vir}(\mathcal X(\sigma|[0\ldots\hat k\ldots n],p,q)\operatorname{rel}\partial)&\to C^\bullet_\mathrm{vir}(\partial\mathcal X(\sigma,p,q))
nodes.label: Ccompositionnaive

nodes.name: Augmented virtual cochain complexes $C^\bullet_\mathrm{vir}(-;\mathcal A)^+$
nodes.statement: Let $\mathcal X/Z_\bullet$ be a flow category diagram with implicit atlas $\mathcal A$, where every $\bar\mathcal A(\sigma,p,q)$ is finite and we have fixed fundamental cycles $[E_\alpha]\in C_\bullet(E;\alpha)$ for all $\alpha\in\bar\mathcal A(\sigma,p,q)$. We define the following complexes: \begin{align} C^\bullet_\mathrm{vir}(\mathcal X\operatorname{rel}\partial;\mathcal A)^+(\sigma,p,q)&:=\operatornamewithlimits{hocolim}_{\mathfrak s\preceq\mathfrak t\in\mathcal S_\mathcal X(\sigma,p,q)}\hphantom{\Biggl\{}C^{\bullet-\operatorname{codim}\mathfrak s}_\mathrm{vir}(\mathcal X(\sigma,p,q)^{\leq\mathfrak s}\operatorname{rel}\partial;\mathcal A(\sigma,p,q)^{\geq\mathfrak t})\\ C^{\bullet-1}_\mathrm{vir}(\partial\mathcal X;\mathcal A)^+(\sigma,p,q)&:=\operatornamewithlimits{hocolim}_{\mathfrak s\preceq\mathfrak t\in\mathcal S_\mathcal X(\sigma,p,q)}\begin{cases}\hfill C^{\bullet-1}_\mathrm{vir}(\partial\mathcal X(\sigma,p,q);\mathcal A(\sigma,p,q)^{\geq\mathfrak t})&\mathfrak s=\mathfrak t=\mathfrak s^\mathrm{top}\cr C^{\bullet-\operatorname{codim}\mathfrak s}_\mathrm{vir}(\mathcal X(\sigma,p,q)^{\leq\mathfrak s}\operatorname{rel}\partial;\mathcal A(\sigma,p,q)^{\geq\mathfrak t})&\text{otherwise}\end{cases} \end{align} The structure maps of the homotopy diagrams come from the obvious pushforward maps (for increasing $\mathfrak s$) and the maps \eqref{Fpushforward1} using the fixed fundamental cycles $[E_\alpha]$ (for decreasing $\mathfrak t$). These are compatible because of the commutativity of \eqref{chainproductcommutes}. Next, let us observe that we have a natural commutative diagram: \begin{equation} \begin{tikzcd} C^{\bullet-1}_\mathrm{vir}(\partial\mathcal X(\sigma,p,q);\mathcal A(\sigma,p,q)^{\geq\mathfrak s^\mathrm{top}})\ar{d}\ar[hook]{r}{\sim}&C^{\bullet-1}_\mathrm{vir}(\partial\mathcal X;\mathcal A)^+(\sigma,p,q)\ar{d}\\ C^\bullet_\mathrm{vir}(\mathcal X(\sigma,p,q)\operatorname{rel}\partial;\mathcal A(\sigma,p,q)^{\geq\mathfrak s^\mathrm{top}})\ar[hook]{r}{\sim}&C^\bullet_\mathrm{vir}(\mathcal X\operatorname{rel}\partial;\mathcal A)^+(\sigma,p,q) \end{tikzcd} \end{equation} The horizontal maps (inclusions of the $\mathfrak s=\mathfrak t=\mathfrak s^\mathrm{top}$ subcomplexes) are quasi-isomorphisms by Lemma \ref{comboretraction} (which morally says that $\mathfrak s^\mathrm{top}\in\mathcal S_\mathcal X(\sigma,p,q)$ acts as a final object in the homotopy colimits \eqref{GmasterI}--\eqref{GmasterII}) which applies because each of the structure maps from $(\mathfrak s,\mathfrak t)$ to $(\mathfrak s,\mathfrak t')$ is a quasi-isomorphism. Note that by definition, the support of $C^\bullet_\mathrm{vir}(\mathcal X\operatorname{rel}\partial;\mathcal A)^+$ and of $C^\bullet_\mathrm{vir}(\partial\mathcal X;\mathcal A)^+$ are contained in the support of $\mathcal X$.
nodes.statement_short: Homotopy colimits over pairs $\mathfrak s\preceq\mathfrak t$ of virtual cochain complexes of strata, quasi-isomorphic to the non-augmented ones.
nodes.label: Gsheavesdef

nodes.name: Augmented virtual cochain complexes as homotopy colimits
nodes.statement: C^\bullet_\mathrm{vir}(\mathcal X\operatorname{rel}\partial;\mathcal A)^+(\sigma,p,q)&:=\operatornamewithlimits{hocolim}_{\mathfrak s\preceq\mathfrak t\in\mathcal S_\mathcal X(\sigma,p,q)}\hphantom{\Biggl\{}C^{\bullet-\operatorname{codim}\mathfrak s}_\mathrm{vir}(\mathcal X(\sigma,p,q)^{\leq\mathfrak s}\operatorname{rel}\partial;\mathcal A(\sigma,p,q)^{\geq\mathfrak t})\\ C^{\bullet-1}_\mathrm{vir}(\partial\mathcal X;\mathcal A)^+(\sigma,p,q)&:=\operatornamewithlimits{hocolim}_{\mathfrak s\preceq\mathfrak t\in\mathcal S_\mathcal X(\sigma,p,q)}\begin{cases}\hfill C^{\bullet-1}_\mathrm{vir}(\partial\mathcal X(\sigma,p,q);\mathcal A(\sigma,p,q)^{\geq\mathfrak t})&\mathfrak s=\mathfrak t=\mathfrak s^\mathrm{top}\cr C^{\bullet-\operatorname{codim}\mathfrak s}_\mathrm{vir}(\mathcal X(\sigma,p,q)^{\leq\mathfrak s}\operatorname{rel}\partial;\mathcal A(\sigma,p,q)^{\geq\mathfrak t})&\text{otherwise}\end{cases}
nodes.label: GmasterI

nodes.name: Top stratum inclusion into augmented complexes
nodes.statement: \begin{tikzcd} C^{\bullet-1}_\mathrm{vir}(\partial\mathcal X(\sigma,p,q);\mathcal A(\sigma,p,q)^{\geq\mathfrak s^\mathrm{top}})\ar{d}\ar[hook]{r}{\sim}&C^{\bullet-1}_\mathrm{vir}(\partial\mathcal X;\mathcal A)^+(\sigma,p,q)\ar{d}\\ C^\bullet_\mathrm{vir}(\mathcal X(\sigma,p,q)\operatorname{rel}\partial;\mathcal A(\sigma,p,q)^{\geq\mathfrak s^\mathrm{top}})\ar[hook]{r}{\sim}&C^\bullet_\mathrm{vir}(\mathcal X\operatorname{rel}\partial;\mathcal A)^+(\sigma,p,q) \end{tikzcd}
nodes.label: topiscofinal

nodes.name: Product/face maps for $C^\bullet_\mathrm{vir}(-;\mathcal A)^+$
nodes.statement: Let $\mathcal X/Z_\bullet$ be a flow category diagram with implicit atlas $\mathcal A$, where every $\bar\mathcal A(\sigma,p,q)$ is finite and we have fixed fundamental cycles $[E_\alpha]$. Let us now define face and product maps for $C^\bullet_\mathrm{vir}(\mathcal X\operatorname{rel}\partial;\mathcal A)^+$. These will be of degree $1$ and will be equipped with a canonical factorization through $C^{\bullet-1}_\mathrm{vir}(\partial\mathcal X;\mathcal A)^+\to C^\bullet_\mathrm{vir}(\mathcal X\operatorname{rel}\partial;\mathcal A)^+$. In other words, we really are going to construct maps: \begin{align} C^\bullet_\mathrm{vir}(\mathcal X\operatorname{rel}\partial;\mathcal A)^+(\sigma|[0\ldots k],p,q)\otimes C^\bullet_\mathrm{vir}(\mathcal X\operatorname{rel}\partial;\mathcal A)^+(\sigma|[k\ldots n],q,r)&\to C^\bullet_\mathrm{vir}(\partial\mathcal X;\mathcal A)^+(\sigma,p,r)\\ C^\bullet_\mathrm{vir}(\mathcal X\operatorname{rel}\partial;\mathcal A)^+(\sigma|[0\ldots\hat k\ldots n],p,q)&\to C^\bullet_\mathrm{vir}(\partial\mathcal X;\mathcal A)^+(\sigma,p,q) \end{align} We construct \eqref{Csimplexextension}. The corresponding face map for $\mathcal S_\mathcal X$ is covered by a corresponding morphism of the homotopy diagrams \eqref{GmasterI}--\eqref{GmasterII} (namely \eqref{Fpushforward1} using the fixed fundamental cycle $[E_{\mathcal A(\sigma,p,q)^{\geq\mathfrak t}\setminus\mathcal A(\sigma|[0,\ldots,\hat k,\ldots,n],p,q)^{\geq\mathfrak t}}]$). This gives rise to a corresponding map \eqref{Csimplexextension} on homotopy colimits. We construct \eqref{Ccomposition}. We construct a morphism of homotopy diagrams \eqref{GmasterI}--\eqref{GmasterII} covering the corresponding product map for $\mathcal S_\mathcal X$. Using the product operation on homotopy diagrams (Definition \ref{simplicialproduct}), it suffices to construct compatible maps: \begin{multline} C^\bullet_\mathrm{vir}(\mathcal X(\sigma|[0,\ldots,k],p,q)^{\leq\mathfrak s_1}\operatorname{rel}\partial;\mathcal A(\sigma|[0,\ldots,k],p,q)^{\geq\mathfrak t_1})\otimes\\mathcal C^\bullet_\mathrm{vir}(\mathcal X(\sigma|[k,\ldots,n],q,r)^{\leq\mathfrak s_2}\operatorname{rel}\partial;\mathcal A(\sigma|[k,\ldots,n],q,r)^{\geq\mathfrak t_2})\\\to C^\bullet_\mathrm{vir}(\mathcal X(\sigma,p,q)^{\leq\mathfrak s_1\times\mathfrak s_2}\operatorname{rel}\partial;\mathcal A(\sigma,p,q)^{\geq\mathfrak t_1\times\mathfrak t_2}) \end{multline} for $\mathfrak s_1\preceq\mathfrak t_1\in\mathcal S(\sigma|[0,\ldots,k],p,q)$ and $\mathfrak s_2\preceq\mathfrak t_2\in\mathcal S(\sigma|[k,\ldots,n],q,r)$. By definition, the subatlas $\mathcal A(\sigma|[0,\ldots,k],p,q)^{\geq\mathfrak t_1}\sqcup\mathcal A(\sigma|[k,\ldots,n],q,r)^{\geq\mathfrak t_2}\subseteq\mathcal A(\sigma,p,q)^{\geq\mathfrak t_1\times\mathfrak t_2}$ is the product implicit atlas on $\mathcal X(\sigma,p,q)^{\leq\mathfrak s_1\times\mathfrak s_2}=\mathcal X(\sigma|[0,\ldots,k],p,q)^{\leq\mathfrak s_1}\times\mathcal X(\sigma|[k,\ldots,n],q,r)^{\leq\mathfrak s_2}$. Thus the desired map is constructed in Definition \ref{productatlasF}.
nodes.statement_short: Construct degree-1 face and product maps on augmented virtual cochain complexes, the latter via the product implicit atlas.
nodes.label: Cproductface

nodes.name: Product/face maps on augmented virtual cochains
nodes.statement: C^\bullet_\mathrm{vir}(\mathcal X\operatorname{rel}\partial;\mathcal A)^+(\sigma|[0\ldots k],p,q)\otimes C^\bullet_\mathrm{vir}(\mathcal X\operatorname{rel}\partial;\mathcal A)^+(\sigma|[k\ldots n],q,r)&\to C^\bullet_\mathrm{vir}(\partial\mathcal X;\mathcal A)^+(\sigma,p,r)\\ C^\bullet_\mathrm{vir}(\mathcal X\operatorname{rel}\partial;\mathcal A)^+(\sigma|[0\ldots\hat k\ldots n],p,q)&\to C^\bullet_\mathrm{vir}(\partial\mathcal X;\mathcal A)^+(\sigma,p,q)
nodes.label: Ccomposition

nodes.name: Product map on stratum virtual cochain complexes
nodes.statement: C^\bullet_\mathrm{vir}(\mathcal X(\sigma|[0,\ldots,k],p,q)^{\leq\mathfrak s_1}\operatorname{rel}\partial;\mathcal A(\sigma|[0,\ldots,k],p,q)^{\geq\mathfrak t_1})\otimes\\mathcal C^\bullet_\mathrm{vir}(\mathcal X(\sigma|[k,\ldots,n],q,r)^{\leq\mathfrak s_2}\operatorname{rel}\partial;\mathcal A(\sigma|[k,\ldots,n],q,r)^{\geq\mathfrak t_2})\\\to C^\bullet_\mathrm{vir}(\mathcal X(\sigma,p,q)^{\leq\mathfrak s_1\times\mathfrak s_2}\operatorname{rel}\partial;\mathcal A(\sigma,p,q)^{\geq\mathfrak t_1\times\mathfrak t_2})

nodes.name: Complexes $C_\bullet(E;\mathcal A)^+$
nodes.statement: Let $\mathcal X/Z_\bullet$ be a flow category diagram with implicit atlas $\mathcal A$, where every $\bar\mathcal A(\sigma,p,q)$ is finite and we have fixed fundamental cycles $[E_\alpha]$. We define: \begin{equation} C_\bullet(E;\mathcal A)^+(\sigma,p,q):=\operatornamewithlimits{hocolim}_{\mathfrak s\preceq\mathfrak t\in\mathcal S_\mathcal X(\sigma,p,q)}C_\bullet(E;\mathcal A^{\geq\mathfrak t}(\sigma,p,q)) \end{equation} where the maps in the homotopy diagram are $\times[E_{A(\sigma,p,q,\mathfrak t')\setminus A(\sigma,p,q,\mathfrak t)}]$. We equip $C_\bullet(E;\mathcal A)^+$ with product/face maps just as in Definition \ref{Cproductface}. Now there are natural maps: \begin{equation} C^{\operatorname{vdim}\mathcal X(\sigma,p,q)+\bullet}_\mathrm{vir}(\mathcal X\operatorname{rel}\partial;\mathcal A)^+(\sigma,p,q)\xrightarrow{s_\ast}C_{-\bullet}(E;\mathcal A)^+(\sigma,p,q) \end{equation} (induced by \eqref{Fpushforward}), which are maps of $\mathsf{F}$-modules (that is, they respect the product/face maps). Note that by definition, the support of $C_\bullet(E;\mathcal A)^+$ is contained in the support of $\mathcal X$.
nodes.statement_short: Augmented chain complexes of obstruction spaces with $\mathsf{F}$-module structure and the pushforward $s_\ast$ from augmented virtual cochains.
nodes.label: CEcomplexaugmented

nodes.name: Augmented complex $C_\bullet(E;\mathcal A)^+$
nodes.statement: C_\bullet(E;\mathcal A)^+(\sigma,p,q):=\operatornamewithlimits{hocolim}_{\mathfrak s\preceq\mathfrak t\in\mathcal S_\mathcal X(\sigma,p,q)}C_\bullet(E;\mathcal A^{\geq\mathfrak t}(\sigma,p,q))
nodes.label: Cmaster

nodes.name: Pushforward $s_\ast$ to $C_\bullet(E;\mathcal A)^+$
nodes.statement: C^{\operatorname{vdim}\mathcal X(\sigma,p,q)+\bullet}_\mathrm{vir}(\mathcal X\operatorname{rel}\partial;\mathcal A)^+(\sigma,p,q)\xrightarrow{s_\ast}C_{-\bullet}(E;\mathcal A)^+(\sigma,p,q)
nodes.label: GtoCpushforward

nodes.name: Injections with projective cokernel split
nodes.statement: Recall that an injection of modules with projective cokernel automatically splits.
conclusions: an injection of modules with projective cokernel automatically splits.

nodes.name: Cofibrations of complexes
nodes.statement: We say a complex is \emph{cofibrant} iff it is projective (as a module). We say a map of complexes is a \emph{cofibration} iff it is injective and its cokernel is cofibrant; we use the arrow $\rightarrowtail$ to indicate that a map is a cofibration. It is easy to check that a composition of cofibrations is again a cofibration.
nodes.statement_short: Cofibrant complexes are projective; cofibrations are injections with cofibrant cokernel.
differentia: it is injective and its cokernel is cofibrant

nodes.name: Cofibrant $\mathsf{F}$-module complex
nodes.statement: Let $\mathcal W_\bullet$ be an $\mathsf{F}$-module complex. We say that $\mathcal W_\bullet$ is \emph{cofibrant} iff for all $(\sigma,p,q)$: \begin{rlist} \item$\mathcal W_\bullet(\sigma,p,q)$ is cofibrant. \item The map: \begin{equation} \operatornamewithlimits{colim}_{\mathfrak s\in\partial\mathcal S_\mathcal W(\sigma,p,q)}\mathcal W_\bullet(\sigma,p,q,\mathfrak s)\rightarrowtail\mathcal W_\bullet(\sigma,p,q) \end{equation} is a cofibration. \end{rlist}
nodes.statement_short: Each term is cofibrant and each boundary inclusion map from the colimit over boundary strata is a cofibration.
nodes.label: Fmodulecofibrantdef

nodes.name: Boundary map is a cofibration
nodes.statement: \operatornamewithlimits{colim}_{\mathfrak s\in\partial\mathcal S_\mathcal W(\sigma,p,q)}\mathcal W_\bullet(\sigma,p,q,\mathfrak s)\rightarrowtail\mathcal W_\bullet(\sigma,p,q)
nodes.label: boundaryinjective

nodes.name: Generalized boundary maps of cofibrant $\mathsf{F}$-modules are cofibrations
nodes.statement: Let $\mathcal W_\bullet$ be a cofibrant $\mathsf{F}$-module complex. Then the map: \begin{equation} \operatornamewithlimits{colim}_{\begin{smallmatrix}\mathfrak s\in\mathcal S_\mathcal W(\sigma,p,q)\cr\mathfrak s\prec\mathfrak s_0\end{smallmatrix}}\mathcal W(\sigma,p,q,\mathfrak s)\rightarrowtail\mathcal W(\sigma,p,q,\mathfrak s_0) \end{equation} a cofibration for all $\mathfrak s_0\in\mathcal S(\sigma,p,q)$.
nodes.statement_short: For a cofibrant $\mathsf{F}$-module complex, the map to $\mathcal W(\sigma,p,q,\mathfrak s_0)$ from the colimit over strata strictly below is a cofibration.
assumptions: Let $\mathcal W_\bullet$ be a cofibrant $\mathsf{F}$-module complex.
conclusions: a cofibration for all $\mathfrak s_0\in\mathcal S(\sigma,p,q)$.
nodes.label: cofibrantinjectivelemma

nodes.name: Generalized boundary map is a cofibration
nodes.statement: \operatornamewithlimits{colim}_{\begin{smallmatrix}\mathfrak s\in\mathcal S_\mathcal W(\sigma,p,q)\cr\mathfrak s\prec\mathfrak s_0\end{smallmatrix}}\mathcal W(\sigma,p,q,\mathfrak s)\rightarrowtail\mathcal W(\sigma,p,q,\mathfrak s_0)
nodes.label: generalizedboundaryinjective

nodes.name: Proof
nodes.statement: Write $\mathfrak s_0$ in the form \eqref{SdataA}--\eqref{SdataB}. Then we have: \begin{equation} \mathcal S_\mathcal W(\sigma,p,q)^{\leq\mathfrak s_0}=\mathcal S_\mathcal W(\sigma|[j_{a_0}\ldots j_{a_1}],p_0,p_1)\times\cdots\times\mathcal S_\mathcal W(\sigma|[j_{a_{m-1}}\ldots j_{a_m}],p_{m-1},p_m) \end{equation} Now we consider the $m$-cubical diagram: \begin{equation} \bigotimes_{i=1}^m\left[\operatornamewithlimits{colim}_{\mathfrak s\in\partial\mathcal S_\mathcal W(\sigma|[j_{a_{i-1}}\ldots j_{a_i}],p_{i-1},p_i)}\mathcal W_\bullet(\sigma|[j_{a_{i-1}}\ldots j_{a_i}],p_{i-1},p_i,\mathfrak s)\rightarrowtail\mathcal W_\bullet(\sigma|[j_{a_{i-1}}\ldots j_{a_i}],p_{i-1},p_i)\right] \end{equation} Now \eqref{generalizedboundaryinjective} is simply the map to the maximal vertex of the $m$-cube from the colimit over the $m$-cube minus the maximal vertex. This is a cofibration for any cubical diagram of the form $\bigotimes_{i=1}^m[A_i\rightarrowtail B_i]$ where each $A_i\rightarrowtail B_i$ is a cofibration. To see this, write $B_i=A_i\oplus P_i$ where $P_i$ is projective, and then the map is obviously injective with cokernel $\bigotimes_{i=1}^mP_i$. A tensor product of projective modules is projective, as can be seen using either the tensor-hom adjunction or the fact that a module is projective iff it is a direct summand of a free module.
nodes.statement_short: Write the stratum poset below $\mathfrak s_0$ as a product and view the map as a cubical tensor product of cofibrations; split each and compute the projective cokernel.

nodes.name: Stratum poset below $\mathfrak s_0$ as a product
nodes.statement: \mathcal S_\mathcal W(\sigma,p,q)^{\leq\mathfrak s_0}=\mathcal S_\mathcal W(\sigma|[j_{a_0}\ldots j_{a_1}],p_0,p_1)\times\cdots\times\mathcal S_\mathcal W(\sigma|[j_{a_{m-1}}\ldots j_{a_m}],p_{m-1},p_m)

nodes.name: Cubical tensor product of cofibrations
nodes.statement: \bigotimes_{i=1}^m\left[\operatornamewithlimits{colim}_{\mathfrak s\in\partial\mathcal S_\mathcal W(\sigma|[j_{a_{i-1}}\ldots j_{a_i}],p_{i-1},p_i)}\mathcal W_\bullet(\sigma|[j_{a_{i-1}}\ldots j_{a_i}],p_{i-1},p_i,\mathfrak s)\rightarrowtail\mathcal W_\bullet(\sigma|[j_{a_{i-1}}\ldots j_{a_i}],p_{i-1},p_i)\right]

nodes.name: Cofibrant $\mathsf{F}$-modules have many cofibrations
nodes.statement: Let $\mathcal W_\bullet$ be a cofibrant $\mathsf{F}$-module complex. Let $\mathcal S\subseteq\mathcal T\subseteq\mathcal S_\mathcal W(\sigma,p,q)$ be finite downward closed subsets. Then the map: \begin{equation} \operatornamewithlimits{colim}_{\mathfrak s\in\mathcal S}\mathcal W_\bullet(\sigma,p,q,\mathfrak s)\rightarrowtail\operatornamewithlimits{colim}_{\mathfrak s\in\mathcal T}\mathcal W_\bullet(\sigma,p,q,\mathfrak s) \end{equation} is a cofibration. In particular, $\operatornamewithlimits{colim}_{\mathfrak s\in\mathcal T}\mathcal W_\bullet(\sigma,p,q,\mathfrak s)$ is projective (take $\mathcal S=\varnothing$ above).
nodes.statement_short: For finite downward closed $\mathcal S\subseteq\mathcal T$, the map of colimits over $\mathcal S$ and $\mathcal T$ is a cofibration; colimits are projective.
assumptions: Let $\mathcal W_\bullet$ be a cofibrant $\mathsf{F}$-module complex.
Let $\mathcal S\subseteq\mathcal T\subseteq\mathcal S_\mathcal W(\sigma,p,q)$ be finite downward closed subsets.
conclusions: is a cofibration.
In particular, $\operatornamewithlimits{colim}_{\mathfrak s\in\mathcal T}\mathcal W_\bullet(\sigma,p,q,\mathfrak s)$ is projective
nodes.label: cofibranthaslotsofcofibrations

nodes.name: Map of colimits over $\mathcal S\subseteq\mathcal T$
nodes.statement: \operatornamewithlimits{colim}_{\mathfrak s\in\mathcal S}\mathcal W_\bullet(\sigma,p,q,\mathfrak s)\rightarrowtail\operatornamewithlimits{colim}_{\mathfrak s\in\mathcal T}\mathcal W_\bullet(\sigma,p,q,\mathfrak s)

nodes.name: Proof
nodes.statement: Let us abbreviate $A_\mathfrak s:=\mathcal W_\bullet(\sigma,p,q,\mathfrak s)$. We proceed by induction on the cardinality of $\mathcal T$, the case $\mathcal T=\varnothing$ being clear. Using the fact that a composition of cofibrations is again a cofibration, it suffices to consider the case $(\mathcal S,\mathcal T)=(\mathcal S\setminus\mathfrak s_0,\mathcal S)$ where $\mathfrak s_0\in\mathcal S$ is a maximal element. Now $\operatornamewithlimits{colim}_{\mathfrak s\in\mathcal S}A_\mathfrak s$ is the colimit of the following diagram: \begin{equation} \begin{tikzcd}[row sep = tiny] &A_{\mathfrak s_0}\\ \smash{\displaystyle\operatornamewithlimits{colim}_{\begin{smallmatrix}\mathfrak s\in\mathcal S\cr\mathfrak s\prec\mathfrak s_0\end{smallmatrix}}}A_\mathfrak s\ar[tail]{ur}\ar[tail]{rd}\\ &\displaystyle\operatornamewithlimits{colim}_{\mathfrak s\in\mathcal S\setminus\mathfrak s_0}A_\mathfrak s \end{tikzcd} \end{equation} where the top arrow is a cofibration by Lemma \ref{cofibrantinjectivelemma} and the bottom arrow is a cofibration by the induction hypothesis. It follows that $\operatornamewithlimits{colim}_{\mathfrak s\in\mathcal S\setminus\mathfrak s_0}A_\mathfrak s\to\operatornamewithlimits{colim}_{\mathfrak s\in\mathcal S}A_\mathfrak s$ is injective, with cokernel isomorphic to the cokernel of the top map above. Hence it is a cofibration as needed.
nodes.statement_short: Induction on $\#\mathcal T$, adding one maximal element at a time; the colimit is a pushout of cofibrations, using Lemma 7.4.22.

nodes.name: Pushout diagram building up the colimit
nodes.statement: \begin{tikzcd}[row sep = tiny] &A_{\mathfrak s_0}\\ \smash{\displaystyle\operatornamewithlimits{colim}_{\begin{smallmatrix}\mathfrak s\in\mathcal S\cr\mathfrak s\prec\mathfrak s_0\end{smallmatrix}}}A_\mathfrak s\ar[tail]{ur}\ar[tail]{rd}\\ &\displaystyle\operatornamewithlimits{colim}_{\mathfrak s\in\mathcal S\setminus\mathfrak s_0}A_\mathfrak s \end{tikzcd}
nodes.label: colimitdiagrambuildup

nodes.name: Cofibrant replacement functor $Q$
nodes.statement: Let $\mathcal W_\bullet$ be an $\mathsf{F}$-module complex. Suppose that $\mathcal W_\bullet$ satisfies the following properties: \begin{rlist} \item Each $\mathcal W_\bullet(\sigma,p,q)$ is cofibrant. \item Each $\mathcal S_\mathcal W(\sigma,p,q)$ is finite. \end{rlist} In this case, we define (functorially) an $\mathsf{F}$-module complex $Q\mathcal W_\bullet$ (called the \emph{cofibrant replacement}) with the following properties: \begin{rlist} \item$Q\mathcal W_\bullet$ is cofibrant. \item$\operatorname{supp} Q\mathcal W_\bullet=\operatorname{supp}\mathcal W_\bullet$. \item There is a (functorial) surjective quasi-isomorphism $Q\mathcal W_\bullet\overset\sim\twoheadrightarrow\mathcal W_\bullet$ (compatible with product/face maps). \end{rlist} We define $Q\mathcal W_\bullet(\sigma,p,q)$ and the product/face maps with target $(\sigma,p,q)$ by induction on the set of triples $(\sigma,p,q)$, equipped with the partial order $\preceq_\mathcal W$ in which $(\sigma',p',q')\preceq_\mathcal W(\sigma,p,q)$ iff $(\sigma',p',q')$ appears as a ``factor'' of some element of $\mathcal S_\mathcal W(\sigma,p,q)$. This partial order is \emph{well-founded} (i.e.\ there is no strictly decreasing infinite sequence) since each $\mathcal S_\mathcal W(\sigma,p,q)$ is finite, and thus it is valid for induction. The inductive step for $(\sigma,p,q)$ works as follows. By the induction hypothesis, we have defined $Q\mathcal W_\bullet(\sigma,p,q,\mathfrak s)$ for all $\mathfrak s\in\partial\mathcal S_\mathcal W(\sigma,p,q)$. Hence it suffices to construct (functorially) $Q\mathcal W_\bullet(\sigma,p,q)$ fitting into the following commutative diagram: \begin{equation} \begin{tikzcd}[column sep = huge] \smash{\displaystyle\operatornamewithlimits{colim}_{\mathfrak s\in\partial\mathcal S_\mathcal W(\sigma,p,q)}}Q\mathcal W_\bullet(\sigma,p,q,\mathfrak s)\ar{d}\ar[dashed, tail]{r}{\text{product/face}}&?\exists\,Q\mathcal W_\bullet(\sigma,p,q)\ar[dashed, two heads]{d}{\sim}\\ \displaystyle\operatornamewithlimits{colim}_{\mathfrak s\in\partial\mathcal S_\mathcal W(\sigma,p,q)}\mathcal W_\bullet(\sigma,p,q,\mathfrak s)\ar{r}{\text{product/face}}&\mathcal W_\bullet(\sigma,p,q) \end{tikzcd} \end{equation} Now we define $Q\mathcal W_\bullet(\sigma,p,q)$ to be the mapping cylinder of the diagonal composition. Since the domain and codomain of this map are both cofibrant (for the domain, use Lemma \ref{cofibranthaslotsofcofibrations}, which applies since $\mathcal S_\mathcal W(\sigma,p,q)$ has been assumed to be finite), it follows that the top map is a cofibration and that $Q\mathcal W_\bullet(\sigma,p,q)$ is cofibrant. The product/face maps with target $Q\mathcal W_\bullet(\sigma,p,q)$ are defined using the top horizontal map; they are compatible since by construction they factor through the colimit in the upper left corner. Certainly $\operatorname{supp} Q\mathcal W_\bullet\supseteq\operatorname{supp}\mathcal W_\bullet$. Conversely, suppose $Q\mathcal W_\bullet(\sigma,p,q)$ is nonzero. Then either $\mathcal W_\bullet(\sigma,p,q)\ne 0$ (so $(\sigma,p,q)\in\operatorname{supp}\mathcal W_\bullet$), or $Q\mathcal W_\bullet(\sigma,p,q,\mathfrak s)\ne 0$ for some $\mathfrak s\in\partial\mathcal S(\sigma,p,q)$ (so by induction, the triples comprising $\mathfrak s$ are in $\operatorname{supp}\mathcal W_\bullet$, and hence so is $(\sigma,p,q)$).
nodes.statement_short: Inductively build a cofibrant $\mathsf{F}$-module complex $Q\mathcal W$ with same support and a surjective quasi-isomorphism to $\mathcal W$, via mapping cylinders.
nodes.label: cofibrantreplacements

nodes.name: Inductive cofibrant replacement diagram
nodes.statement: \begin{tikzcd}[column sep = huge] \smash{\displaystyle\operatornamewithlimits{colim}_{\mathfrak s\in\partial\mathcal S_\mathcal W(\sigma,p,q)}}Q\mathcal W_\bullet(\sigma,p,q,\mathfrak s)\ar{d}\ar[dashed, tail]{r}{\text{product/face}}&?\exists\,Q\mathcal W_\bullet(\sigma,p,q)\ar[dashed, two heads]{d}{\sim}\\ \displaystyle\operatornamewithlimits{colim}_{\mathfrak s\in\partial\mathcal S_\mathcal W(\sigma,p,q)}\mathcal W_\bullet(\sigma,p,q,\mathfrak s)\ar{r}{\text{product/face}}&\mathcal W_\bullet(\sigma,p,q) \end{tikzcd}
nodes.label: cofibrantdefdiagram

nodes.name: Tensor products of connective cofibrant complexes are connective
nodes.statement: Let $\{C_\bullet^k\}_{k=1}^n$ be cofibrant complexes over $\mathbb Z$ such that $H_iC_\bullet^k=0$ for $i<0$. Then $H_i(\bigotimes_{k=1}^nC_\bullet^k)=0$ for $i<0$.
assumptions: Let $\{C_\bullet^k\}_{k=1}^n$ be cofibrant complexes over $\mathbb Z$ such that $H_iC_\bullet^k=0$ for $i<0$.
conclusions: Then $H_i(\bigotimes_{k=1}^nC_\bullet^k)=0$ for $i<0$.
nodes.label: tensorproductvanishing

nodes.name: Proof
nodes.statement: Since the tensor product of projective modules is projective, we may use induction to reduce to the case $k=2$. Thus, we have two cofibrant complexes $A_\bullet$ and $B_\bullet$ with $H_iA_\bullet=H_iB_\bullet=0$ for $i<0$ and we would like to conclude that $H_i(A_\bullet\otimes B_\bullet)=0$ for $i<0$. This follows from the K\"unneth theorem, specifically in the form of \cite[p301, Theorem 9.16]{osborne} or \cite[p679, Theorem 10.81]{rotman} (both of which apply because $\operatorname{Tor}^i_\mathbb Z(\cdot,\cdot)=0$ for $i>1$).\footnote{If we were assuming $A_\bullet$ and $B_\bullet$ to be bounded below, then we could apply the K\"unneth spectral sequence $\bigoplus_{i+j=q}\operatorname{Tor}_p(H_iA_\bullet,H_jB_\bullet)\Rightarrow H_{p+q}(A_\bullet\otimes B_\bullet)$ (see \cite[p686, Theorem 10.90]{rotman}) to reach the desired conclusion without any assumptions on the ground ring.}
nodes.statement_short: Reduce by induction to two factors, then apply the K\"unneth theorem over $\mathbb Z$.

nodes.name: $H_0$ of colimits of cofibrant $\mathsf{F}$-modules
nodes.statement: Let $\mathcal W_\bullet$ be a cofibrant $\mathsf{F}$-module complex over $\mathbb Z$ such that $H_i\mathcal W_\bullet=0$ for $i<0$. Then for any finite downward closed subset $\mathcal S\subseteq\mathcal S_\mathcal W(\sigma,p,q)$, the map: \begin{equation} H_i\bigoplus_{\mathfrak s\in\mathcal S}\mathcal W_\bullet(\sigma,p,q,\mathfrak s)\twoheadrightarrow H_i\operatornamewithlimits{colim}_{\mathfrak s\in\mathcal S}\mathcal W_\bullet(\sigma,p,q,\mathfrak s) \end{equation} is surjective for $i\leq 0$. Moreover, both sides vanish for $i<0$.
nodes.statement_short: For connective cofibrant $\mathsf{F}$-modules, homology of the direct sum over strata surjects onto that of the colimit in degrees $\leq 0$.
assumptions: Let $\mathcal W_\bullet$ be a cofibrant $\mathsf{F}$-module complex over $\mathbb Z$ such that $H_i\mathcal W_\bullet=0$ for $i<0$.
for any finite downward closed subset $\mathcal S\subseteq\mathcal S_\mathcal W(\sigma,p,q)$
conclusions: is surjective for $i\leq 0$.
Moreover, both sides vanish for $i<0$.
nodes.label: Hzeroofcofibrantcolimit

nodes.name: Surjection onto homology of the colimit
nodes.statement: H_i\bigoplus_{\mathfrak s\in\mathcal S}\mathcal W_\bullet(\sigma,p,q,\mathfrak s)\twoheadrightarrow H_i\operatornamewithlimits{colim}_{\mathfrak s\in\mathcal S}\mathcal W_\bullet(\sigma,p,q,\mathfrak s)
nodes.label: tocolimitsurjective

nodes.name: Proof
nodes.statement: Let us abbreviate $A_\mathfrak s:=\mathcal W_\bullet(\sigma,p,q,\mathfrak s)$. Since $A_\mathfrak s$ is a tensor product of various $\mathcal W_\bullet(\sigma',p',q')$, it follows (using Lemma \ref{tensorproductvanishing}) that $H_iA_\mathfrak s$ for $i<0$, so the left hand side of \eqref{tocolimitsurjective} vanishes for $i<0$. Hence it remains just to show that \eqref{tocolimitsurjective} is surjective for $i\leq 0$. We proceed by induction on the cardinality of $\mathcal S$, the case $\mathcal S=\varnothing$ being clear. Let $\mathfrak s_0\in\mathcal S$ be any maximal element. Now $\operatornamewithlimits{colim}_{\mathfrak s\in\mathcal S}A_\mathfrak s$ is the colimit of \eqref{colimitdiagrambuildup}; it follows that we have the following exact sequence: \begin{equation} 0\to\operatornamewithlimits{colim}_{\begin{smallmatrix}\mathfrak s\in\mathcal S\cr\mathfrak s\prec\mathfrak s_0\end{smallmatrix}}A_\mathfrak s\to A_{\mathfrak s_0}\oplus\operatornamewithlimits{colim}_{\mathfrak s\in\mathcal S\setminus\mathfrak s_0}A_\mathfrak s\to\operatornamewithlimits{colim}_{\mathfrak s\in\mathcal S}A_\mathfrak s\to 0 \end{equation} By the induction hypothesis, it suffices to show that the second map above is surjective on $H_i$ for $i\leq 0$. By the long exact sequence induced by \eqref{colimitSEScofibrant}, it suffices to show that $H_i\operatornamewithlimits{colim}_{\begin{smallmatrix}\mathfrak s\in\mathcal S\cr\mathfrak s\prec\mathfrak s_0\end{smallmatrix}}A_\mathfrak s=0$ for $i<0$. Now this follows from the induction hypothesis.
nodes.statement_short: Vanishing from Lemma 7.4.25; surjectivity by induction on $\#\mathcal S$ using the short exact sequence for adding a maximal element.

nodes.name: Short exact sequence for adding a maximal stratum
nodes.statement: 0\to\operatornamewithlimits{colim}_{\begin{smallmatrix}\mathfrak s\in\mathcal S\cr\mathfrak s\prec\mathfrak s_0\end{smallmatrix}}A_\mathfrak s\to A_{\mathfrak s_0}\oplus\operatornamewithlimits{colim}_{\mathfrak s\in\mathcal S\setminus\mathfrak s_0}A_\mathfrak s\to\operatornamewithlimits{colim}_{\mathfrak s\in\mathcal S}A_\mathfrak s\to 0
nodes.label: colimitSEScofibrant

nodes.name: Lifting cycles along a fibration
nodes.statement: Let $\tilde A^\bullet\twoheadrightarrow A^\bullet$ be surjective. Fix a cycle $a\in A^0$ and a homology class $\tilde{\mathfrak a}\in H^0\tilde A^\bullet$, whose images in $H^0A^\bullet$ coincide. Then there exists a cycle $\tilde a\in\tilde A^0$ which maps to $a$ and which represents $\tilde{\mathfrak a}$.
assumptions: Let $\tilde A^\bullet\twoheadrightarrow A^\bullet$ be surjective.
Fix a cycle $a\in A^0$ and a homology class $\tilde{\mathfrak a}\in H^0\tilde A^\bullet$, whose images in $H^0A^\bullet$ coincide.
conclusions: Then there exists a cycle $\tilde a\in\tilde A^0$ which maps to $a$ and which represents $\tilde{\mathfrak a}$.
nodes.label: cycleliftinglemma

nodes.name: Proof
nodes.statement: Pick any cycle $\tilde a'\in\tilde A^0$ representing $\tilde{\mathfrak a}$. Then $\tilde a'-a\in A^0$ is a boundary $db$, and lifting $b\in A^{-1}$ to $\tilde b\in\tilde A^{-1}$, we let $\tilde a:=\tilde a'-d\tilde b$.
nodes.statement_short: Correct an arbitrary representative by the boundary of a lift of the primitive.

nodes.name: Representing homology classes in mapping cones
nodes.statement: Fix $f:A^\bullet\to B^\bullet$ and $\omega\in H^0[A^\bullet\to B^{\bullet-1}]$. Let $a\in A^0$ be a cycle representing $\delta\omega\in H^0(A^\bullet)$. Then there exists $b\in B^{-1}$ with $db=f(a)$ such that $a\oplus b$ represents $\omega$.
assumptions: Fix $f:A^\bullet\to B^\bullet$ and $\omega\in H^0[A^\bullet\to B^{\bullet-1}]$.
Let $a\in A^0$ be a cycle representing $\delta\omega\in H^0(A^\bullet)$.
conclusions: Then there exists $b\in B^{-1}$ with $db=f(a)$ such that $a\oplus b$ represents $\omega$.
nodes.label: mappingconechoiceboundary

nodes.name: Proof
nodes.statement: This is a special case of Lemma \ref{cycleliftinglemma} for the surjection $[A^\bullet\to B^{\bullet-1}]\twoheadrightarrow A^\bullet$.
nodes.statement_short: Special case of Lemma 7.4.27 for the surjection from the mapping cone.

nodes.name: Universal coefficient theorem
nodes.statement: Let $A_\bullet$ be a cofibrant complex over $\mathbb Z$. Then there is a natural short exact sequence: \begin{equation} 0\to\operatorname{Ext}^1(H_{i-1}A_\bullet,\mathbb Z)\to H^i\operatorname{Hom}(A_\bullet,\mathbb Z)\to\operatorname{Hom}(H_iA_\bullet,\mathbb Z)\to 0 \end{equation}
assumptions: Let $A_\bullet$ be a cofibrant complex over $\mathbb Z$.
conclusions: Then there is a natural short exact sequence:
nodes.label: universalcoefficient

nodes.name: Universal coefficient short exact sequence
nodes.statement: 0\to\operatorname{Ext}^1(H_{i-1}A_\bullet,\mathbb Z)\to H^i\operatorname{Hom}(A_\bullet,\mathbb Z)\to\operatorname{Hom}(H_iA_\bullet,\mathbb Z)\to 0

nodes.name: Proof
nodes.statement: Well-known.
nodes.statement_short: Cited as well known.

nodes.name: Extending cocycles along a cofibration
nodes.statement: Suppose we have the following commuting diagrams (solid arrows) of complexes over $\mathbb Z$ and their homology (where $\mathbb Z$ is concentrated in degree zero): \begin{equation} \begin{tikzcd} A_\bullet\ar[tail]{r}\ar{d}&\tilde A_\bullet\ar[dashed]{dl}\\ \mathbb Z \end{tikzcd} \overset{H_\bullet}\Longrightarrow \begin{tikzcd} H_\bullet A_\bullet\ar{r}\ar{d}&H_\bullet\tilde A_\bullet\ar{dl}\\ \mathbb Z \end{tikzcd} \end{equation} where $A_\bullet$ and $\tilde A_\bullet$ are cofibrant and $H_{-1}A_\bullet=0$. Then there exists a dashed arrow compatible with the rest of the diagram.
nodes.statement_short: A map $A_\bullet\to\mathbb Z$ extends along a cofibration $A\rightarrowtail\tilde A$ compatibly with a given map on homology.
assumptions: where $A_\bullet$ and $\tilde A_\bullet$ are cofibrant and $H_{-1}A_\bullet=0$.
conclusions: Then there exists a dashed arrow compatible with the rest of the diagram.
nodes.label: cocycleextendinglemma

nodes.name: Extension of a cocycle along a cofibration (diagram)
nodes.statement: \begin{tikzcd} A_\bullet\ar[tail]{r}\ar{d}&\tilde A_\bullet\ar[dashed]{dl}\\ \mathbb Z \end{tikzcd} \overset{H_\bullet}\Longrightarrow \begin{tikzcd} H_\bullet A_\bullet\ar{r}\ar{d}&H_\bullet\tilde A_\bullet\ar{dl}\\ \mathbb Z \end{tikzcd}

nodes.name: Proof
nodes.statement: By Lemma \ref{universalcoefficient}, we have: \begin{align} H^0\operatorname{Hom}(A_\bullet,\mathbb Z)&\xrightarrow\sim\operatorname{Hom}(H_0A_\bullet,\mathbb Z)\\ H^0\operatorname{Hom}(\tilde A_\bullet,\mathbb Z)&\twoheadrightarrow\operatorname{Hom}(H_0\tilde A_\bullet,\mathbb Z) \end{align} Let $f:A_0\to\mathbb Z$ denote the vertical map in the first diagram. Using the surjectivity of \eqref{tildesurj}, there exists a cocycle $\tilde f:\tilde A_0\to\mathbb Z$ giving the desired map on homology. Denote by $i:A_\bullet\rightarrowtail\tilde A_\bullet$ the inclusion. Now by the commutativity of the second diagram, the difference $f-\tilde fi$ acts as zero on $H_0A_\bullet$. Since \eqref{notildeiso} is an isomorphism, this difference is thus a coboundary $\delta g$ for some $g:A_{-1}\to\mathbb Z$. Now extend $g$ to $\tilde g:\tilde A_{-1}\to\mathbb Z$ (using the fact that $A_{-1}\rightarrowtail\tilde A_{-1}$ splits) and let the dotted arrow be $\tilde f+\delta\tilde g$.
nodes.statement_short: Use the universal coefficient theorem to pick a cocycle on $\tilde A$, then fix the discrepancy by a coboundary extended via the splitting.

nodes.name: Universal coefficient isomorphism and surjection
nodes.statement: H^0\operatorname{Hom}(A_\bullet,\mathbb Z)&\xrightarrow\sim\operatorname{Hom}(H_0A_\bullet,\mathbb Z)\\ H^0\operatorname{Hom}(\tilde A_\bullet,\mathbb Z)&\twoheadrightarrow\operatorname{Hom}(H_0\tilde A_\bullet,\mathbb Z)
nodes.label: notildeiso

nodes.name: System of chains
nodes.statement: Let $\mathcal W^\bullet$ be an $\mathsf{F}$-module complex with each $\mathcal S_\mathcal W(\sigma,p,q)$ finite. A \emph{system of chains} $\lambda\in\mathcal W^\bullet$ (of degree $d(\sigma,p,q)$) is a collection of elements $\lambda_{\sigma,p,q}\in\mathcal W^{d(\sigma,p,q)}(\sigma,p,q)$ satisfying $d\lambda_{\sigma,p,q}=\mu_{\sigma,p,q}$ where: \begin{equation} \mu_{\sigma,p,r}:=\sum_{k=0}^n\sum_{q\in\mathcal P_{\sigma(k)}}(-1)^{k+\operatorname{gr}(p)}\lambda_{\sigma|[0\ldots k],p,q}\cdot\lambda_{\sigma|[k\ldots n],q,r}-\sum_{k=1}^{n-1}(-1)^{k+\operatorname{gr}(p)}\lambda_{\sigma|[0\ldots\hat k\ldots n],p,r}\in\mathcal W^\bullet(\sigma,p,r) \end{equation} (using the product/face maps on the right hand side). Note that this sum is finite since $\mathcal S_\mathcal W(\sigma,p,q)$ is finite. Also, note that the triples on the right hand side all strictly precede the triple on the left hand side. We also require that the parity (in the sense of Convention \ref{signconventions}) of $\lambda_{\sigma,p,q}$ equals $\operatorname{gr}(q)-\operatorname{gr}(p)+\dim\sigma-1\in\mathbb Z/2$. This ensures (via the Koszul rule of signs) that expanding $d\mu_{\sigma,p,q}$ using the identity $d\lambda_{\sigma,p,q}=\mu_{\sigma,p,q}$ yields zero (the signs work out correctly as a consequence of the discussion surrounding \eqref{multiorientationI}--\eqref{multiorientationIV}). In practice the degrees $d(\sigma,p,q)$ are chosen so that $\mu_{\sigma,p,q}$ (as defined by \eqref{lambdamaster}) is formally homogeneous of the same degree as $d\lambda_{\sigma,p,q}$.
nodes.section: 7.5 Resolution \texorpdfstring{$\tilde Z_\bullet\to Z_\bullet$}{tilde Z to Z}
nodes.statement_short: Elements $\lambda_{\sigma,p,q}$ whose differentials equal the signed sum $\mu$ of products and faces of lower $\lambda$'s, with prescribed parity.
differentia: satisfying $d\lambda_{\sigma,p,q}=\mu_{\sigma,p,q}$
nodes.label: systemofcycles

nodes.name: Master equation term $\mu_{\sigma,p,r}$
nodes.statement: \mu_{\sigma,p,r}:=\sum_{k=0}^n\sum_{q\in\mathcal P_{\sigma(k)}}(-1)^{k+\operatorname{gr}(p)}\lambda_{\sigma|[0\ldots k],p,q}\cdot\lambda_{\sigma|[k\ldots n],q,r}-\sum_{k=1}^{n-1}(-1)^{k+\operatorname{gr}(p)}\lambda_{\sigma|[0\ldots\hat k\ldots n],p,r}\in\mathcal W^\bullet(\sigma,p,r)
nodes.section: 7.5 Resolution \texorpdfstring{$\tilde Z_\bullet\to Z_\bullet$}{tilde Z to Z}
nodes.label: lambdamaster

nodes.name: Systems of chains as maps of $\mathsf{F}$-modules
nodes.statement: There is a natural bijection between systems of chains $\lambda\in\mathcal W^\bullet$ and maps of $\mathsf{F}$-modules $R[\mathcal S_\mathcal W]\to\mathcal W^\bullet$, where $R[\mathcal S_\mathcal W](\sigma,p,q)$ is the free $R$-module on $\mathcal S_\mathcal W(\sigma,p,q)$ with differential $d\mathfrak s:=\sum_{\operatorname{codim}(\mathfrak s'\preceq\mathfrak s)=1}\mathfrak s'$ (with appropriate signs) and equipped with the obvious product/face maps coming from the $\mathsf{F}$-module structure on $\mathcal S_\mathcal W$ (more intrinsically, $R[\mathcal S_\mathcal W](\sigma,p,q)$ is the direct sum over $\mathfrak s\in\mathcal S_\mathcal W(\sigma,p,q)$ of the orientation lines from Definition \ref{IAonflowcategorydiagramdef}). This perspective is relevant for the key step of the proof of Proposition \ref{trivialKanfibration} below.
nodes.section: 7.5 Resolution \texorpdfstring{$\tilde Z_\bullet\to Z_\bullet$}{tilde Z to Z}
nodes.statement_short: Systems of chains correspond bijectively to $\mathsf{F}$-module maps from the free module on strata $R[\mathcal S_\mathcal W]$.

nodes.name: Resolution $\pi:\tilde Z_\bullet\to Z_\bullet$
nodes.statement: Let $\mathcal X/Z_\bullet$ be an $H$-equivariant flow category diagram with implicit atlas $\mathcal A$ and coherent orientations $\omega$. We construct a \emph{resolution} $\pi:\tilde Z_\bullet\to Z_\bullet$ (which depends on $\mathcal X$, $\mathcal A$, $\omega$) as follows. A simplex $\Delta^n\to\tilde Z_\bullet$ consists of the following data: \begin{rlist} \item A map $f:\Delta^n\to Z_\bullet$ (where $\Delta^n$ is the semisimplicial $n$-simplex). \item An $H$-invariant subatlas $\mathcal B\subseteq f^\ast\mathcal A$ (meaning choices of $\bar\mathcal B(\sigma,p,q)\subseteq\bar\mathcal A(f(\sigma),p,q)$) where each $\bar\mathcal B(\sigma,p,q)$ is finite. \item An $H$-invariant collection of fundamental cycles $[E_\alpha]\in C_\bullet(E;\alpha)$ for all $\alpha\in\bar\mathcal B$. \itemAn $H$-invariant system of chains $\lambda\in C^\bullet_\mathrm{vir}(f^\ast\mathcal X\operatorname{rel}\partial;\mathcal B)^+$ (degree $0$ and supported inside $\operatorname{supp}\mathcal X$) with the following property. Note that $(\mu,\lambda)$ is a cycle in the mapping cone $[C^\bullet_\mathrm{vir}(\partial f^\ast\mathcal X;\mathcal B)^+\to C^\bullet_\mathrm{vir}(f^\ast\mathcal X\operatorname{rel}\partial;\mathcal B)^+]$, whose homology is identified with $\check H^\bullet(f^\ast\mathcal X;\mathfrak o_{f^\ast\mathcal X})$. We require that the homology class of $(\mu,\lambda)$ equal $f^\ast\omega\in\check H^0(f^\ast\mathcal X;\mathfrak o_{f^\ast\mathcal X})$. \itemAn $H$-invariant system of chains $\tilde\lambda$ for $QC_\bullet(E;\mathcal B)^+$ (degree $\operatorname{gr}(q)-\operatorname{gr}(p)+\dim\sigma-1$ and supported inside $\operatorname{supp}\mathcal X$) whose image in $C_\bullet(E;\mathcal B)^+$ coincides with $s_\ast\lambda$ (recall \eqref{GtoCpushforward}). \itemAn $H$-invariant map of $\mathsf{F}$-modules $[[E]]:QC_\bullet(E;\mathcal B)^+_\mathbb Z\to\mathbb Z$ which sends the fundamental class to $1$. The left hand side $QC_\bullet(E;\mathcal B)^+_\mathbb Z$ is defined over $\mathbb Z$, and the right hand side is the $\mathsf{F}$-module which for every $(\sigma,p,q)$ is $\mathbb Z$ concentrated in degree zero (with the product/face maps being multiplication/identity respectively). \end{rlist}
nodes.section: 7.5 Resolution \texorpdfstring{$\tilde Z_\bullet\to Z_\bullet$}{tilde Z to Z}
nodes.statement_short: Simplices of $\tilde Z_\bullet$ are coherent choices over a simplex: finite subatlases, fundamental cycles, systems of chains $\lambda$, lifts $\tilde\lambda$, and augmentations $[[E]]$.
nodes.label: Lambdadef

nodes.name: Resolution commutes with pullback
nodes.statement: Let $\mathcal X/Z_\bullet$ be an $H$-equivariant flow category diagram with implicit atlas $\mathcal A$ and coherent orientations $\omega$. Let $f:Y_\bullet\to Z_\bullet$ be a map, and consider $f^\ast\mathcal X/Y_\bullet$ with implicit atlas $f^\ast\mathcal A$ and coherent orientations $f^\ast\omega$. Then there is a canonical fiber diagram relating the resolutions: \begin{equation} \begin{CD} \tilde Y_\bullet@>>>\tilde Z_\bullet\cr @VVV@VVV\cr Y_\bullet@>>>Z_\bullet \end{CD} \end{equation}
nodes.section: 7.5 Resolution \texorpdfstring{$\tilde Z_\bullet\to Z_\bullet$}{tilde Z to Z}
nodes.statement_short: Pulling back the flow category diagram along $f:Y_\bullet\to Z_\bullet$ gives a fiber square of resolutions.
nodes.label: Lambdaandpullback

nodes.name: Fiber square of resolutions under pullback
nodes.statement: \begin{CD} \tilde Y_\bullet@>>>\tilde Z_\bullet\cr @VVV@VVV\cr Y_\bullet@>>>Z_\bullet \end{CD}
nodes.section: 7.5 Resolution \texorpdfstring{$\tilde Z_\bullet\to Z_\bullet$}{tilde Z to Z}

nodes.name: $\pi:\tilde Z_\bullet\to Z_\bullet$ is a trivial Kan fibration
nodes.statement: The map $\pi:\tilde Z_\bullet\to Z_\bullet$ has the right lifting property with respect to the boundary inclusions $\partial\Delta^n\hookrightarrow\Delta^n$ for all $n\geq 0$ (where $\Delta^n$ is the semisimplicial $n$-simplex). In other words, given any commuting diagram of solid arrows below: \begin{equation} \begin{tikzcd} \partial\Delta^n\arrow{r}\arrow{d}&\tilde Z_\bullet\arrow{d}\\ \Delta^n\arrow{r}\arrow[dashrightarrow]{ur}&Z_\bullet \end{tikzcd} \end{equation} there exists a dashed arrow making the diagram commute.
nodes.section: 7.5 Resolution \texorpdfstring{$\tilde Z_\bullet\to Z_\bullet$}{tilde Z to Z}
nodes.statement_short: Coherent choices over $\partial\Delta^n$ always extend over $\Delta^n$: the resolution is a trivial Kan fibration.
assumptions: The map $\pi:\tilde Z_\bullet\to Z_\bullet$
conclusions: has the right lifting property with respect to the boundary inclusions $\partial\Delta^n\hookrightarrow\Delta^n$ for all $n\geq 0$
nodes.label: trivialKanfibration

nodes.name: Right lifting property diagram
nodes.statement: \begin{tikzcd} \partial\Delta^n\arrow{r}\arrow{d}&\tilde Z_\bullet\arrow{d}\\ \Delta^n\arrow{r}\arrow[dashrightarrow]{ur}&Z_\bullet \end{tikzcd}
nodes.section: 7.5 Resolution \texorpdfstring{$\tilde Z_\bullet\to Z_\bullet$}{tilde Z to Z}

nodes.name: Proof
nodes.statement: It is equivalent to show that given any $f:\Delta^n\to Z_\bullet$ along with data (\ref{subatlaschoice})--(\ref{augmentationschoice}) over $\partial\Delta^n$, the data can be extended over $\Delta^n$. For ease of notation, let us rename $(f^\ast\mathcal X,f^\ast\mathcal A,f^\ast\omega)$ as $(\mathcal X,\mathcal A,\omega)$. We construct (\ref{subatlaschoice})--(\ref{augmentationschoice}) via $H$-equivariant induction on the set of triples $(\sigma,p,q)$, equipped with the partial order $\preceq_\mathcal X$ in which $(\sigma',p',q')\preceq_\mathcal X(\sigma,p,q)$ iff $(\sigma',p',q')$ appears as a ``factor'' of some element of $\mathcal S_\mathcal X(\sigma,p,q)$. This partial order is \emph{well-founded} (i.e.\ there is no strictly decreasing infinite sequence) since each $\mathcal S_\mathcal X(\sigma,p,q)$ is finite, and thus it is valid for induction. The induction works $H$-equivariantly since the action of $H$ on $\mathcal P$ is free, and $(\sigma,p,q)$ and $(\sigma,hp,hq)$ are always incomparable for $h\in H$ (so we may henceforth ignore the action of $H$). The inductive step is as follows. \textbf{Choosing $\mathcal B(\sigma,p,q)$.}\ We must choose a finite $\bar\mathcal B(\sigma,p,q)\subseteq\bar\mathcal A(\sigma,p,q)$ so that the corresponding subatlas of $\mathcal A(\sigma,p,q)^{\geq\mathfrak s^\mathrm{top}}=\bar\mathcal A(\sigma,p,q)$ on $\mathcal X(\sigma,p,q)$ satisfies the covering axiom (and thus is an implicit atlas). This is possible by compactness. \textbf{Choosing $[E_\alpha]$.}\ Trivial. \textbf{Choosing $[[E]]_{\sigma,p,q}:QC_\bullet(E;\mathcal B)^+_\mathbb Z(\sigma,p,q)\to\mathbb Z$.}\ We need to construct $[[E]]_{\sigma,p,q}$ fitting into the following diagram: \begin{equation} \begin{tikzcd}[column sep = huge] \smash{\displaystyle\operatornamewithlimits{colim}_{\mathfrak s\in\partial\mathcal S_\mathcal X(\sigma,p,q)}}QC_\bullet(E;\mathcal B)^+_\mathbb Z(\sigma,p,q,\mathfrak s)\ar[tail]{r}{\text{product/face}}\ar{d}[swap]{[[E]]}&QC_\bullet(E;\mathcal B)^+_\mathbb Z(\sigma,p,q)\ar[dashed]{dl}{?\exists\,[[E]]_{\sigma,p,q}}\\ \mathbb Z\\ H_\bullet\smash{\displaystyle\operatornamewithlimits{colim}_{\mathfrak s\in\partial\mathcal S_\mathcal X(\sigma,p,q)}}QC_\bullet(E;\mathcal B)^+_\mathbb Z(\sigma,p,q,\mathfrak s)\ar{r}{\text{product/face}}\ar{d}[swap]{[[E]]}&H_\bullet QC_\bullet(E;\mathcal B)^+_\mathbb Z(\sigma,p,q)\ar{dl}{[E]\mapsto 1}\\ \mathbb Z \end{tikzcd} \end{equation} Since $QC_\bullet(E;\mathcal B)^+_\mathbb Z$ is cofibrant, it follows that the top horizontal map is a cofibration between cofibrant complexes (this uses Lemma \ref{cofibranthaslotsofcofibrations}). Now Lemma \ref{Hzeroofcofibrantcolimit} tells us that the direct sum of $H_0QC_\bullet(E;\mathcal B)^+_\mathbb Z(\sigma,p,q,\mathfrak s)$ surjects onto $H_0$ on the left, and this makes it easy to check that the second diagram commutes. Lemma \ref{Hzeroofcofibrantcolimit} also tells us that $H_{-1}$ on the left vanishes. Hence we may apply Lemma \ref{cocycleextendinglemma} to conclude the existence of a suitable $[[E]]_{\sigma,p,q}$. \textbf{Choosing $\lambda_{\sigma,p,q}$ (the key step).}\ According to Lemma \ref{mappingconechoiceboundary}, we may choose a $\lambda_{\sigma,p,q}$ with the required property iff the homology class of $\mu_{\sigma,p,q}\in H^\bullet_\mathrm{vir}(\partial\mathcal X;\mathcal B)^+(\sigma,p,q)$ coincides with $d\omega(\sigma,p,q)\in\check H^0(\partial\mathcal X(\sigma,p,q);\mathfrak o_{\partial\mathcal X(\sigma,p,q)})$. Let us now prove this desired statement $[\mu_{\sigma,p,q}]=d\omega(\sigma,p,q)$. Let us fix $\mathfrak r_0\in\partial\mathcal S_\mathcal X(\sigma,p,q)$ and verify equality over $\mathcal X(\sigma,p,q)^{\mathfrak r_0}$ (this is clearly enough). We consider the following diagram: \begin{align} \mu_{\sigma,p,q}\in&&&C_\mathrm{vir}^\bullet(\partial\mathcal X;\mathcal B)^+(\sigma,p,q)\\ &&&\qquad\uparrow\cr \bigoplus_{\mathfrak r\in\partial\mathcal S_\mathcal X(\sigma,p,q)}\mu_{\sigma,p,q,\mathfrak r}\in&&\bigoplus_{\mathfrak r\in\partial\mathcal S_\mathcal X(\sigma,p,q)}\operatornamewithlimits{hocolim}_{\mathfrak s\prec\mathfrak t\in\mathcal S_\mathcal X(\sigma,p,q)^{\leq\mathfrak r}}&C_\mathrm{vir}^\bullet(\mathcal X(\sigma,p,q)^{\leq\mathfrak s}\operatorname{rel}\partial;\mathcal B(\sigma,p,q)^{\geq\mathfrak t})\\ &&&\qquad\downarrow\cr \bigoplus_{\mathfrak r\in\partial\mathcal S_\mathcal X(\sigma,p,q)^{\leq\mathfrak r_0}}\mu_{\sigma,p,q,\mathfrak r}\in&&\bigoplus_{\mathfrak r\in\partial\mathcal S_\mathcal X(\sigma,p,q)^{\leq\mathfrak r_0}}\operatornamewithlimits{hocolim}_{\mathfrak s\prec\mathfrak t\in\mathcal S_\mathcal X(\sigma,p,q)^{\leq\mathfrak r}}&C_\mathrm{vir}^\bullet(\mathcal X(\sigma,p,q)^{\leq\mathfrak s}\operatorname{rel}\partial;\mathcal B(\sigma,p,q)^{\geq\mathfrak t})\\ &&&\qquad\uparrow\cr \mu_{\sigma,p,q,\mathfrak r_0}\in&&\operatornamewithlimits{hocolim}_{\mathfrak s\prec\mathfrak t\in\mathcal S_\mathcal X(\sigma,p,q)^{\leq\mathfrak r_0}}&C_\mathrm{vir}^\bullet(\mathcal X(\sigma,p,q)^{\leq\mathfrak s}\operatorname{rel}\partial;\mathcal B(\sigma,p,q)^{\geq\mathfrak t}) \end{align} The differentials in \eqref{muallstrat}--\eqref{musomestrat} are given by the sum over $\operatorname{codim}(\mathfrak r\preceq\mathfrak r')=1$ of the obvious pushforward maps (plus the internal differentials of each $\operatornamewithlimits{hocolim}$). The first vertical map is the sum over $\operatorname{codim}\mathfrak r=0$ (i.e.\ over maximal elements of $\partial\mathcal S_\mathcal X(\sigma,p,q)$); clearly this is a chain map. The remaining vertical maps are clear. The easiest way to keep track of signs in the present discussion is to use the orientation lines associated to elements of $\mathcal S_\mathcal X(\sigma,p,q)$, as in Definition \ref{stratifiedvirtualdef}, though we will supress them from the notation. Note that there is a natural diagram of complexes of $\mathcal K$-presheaves on $\partial\mathcal X(\sigma,p,q)$ whose diagram of global sections is \eqref{mucareabout}--\eqref{muonestratum}. We will see below that these complexes of $\mathcal K$-presheaves are in fact pure homotopy $\mathcal K$-sheaves and that the induced diagram of sheaves (obtained by taking $H^0$) is given by the tautological maps: \begin{equation} \mathfrak o_{\partial\mathcal X(\sigma,p,q)}\leftarrow\mathfrak o_{\partial\mathcal X(\sigma,p,q)}\to\mathfrak o_{\mathcal X(\sigma,p,q)^{\leq\mathfrak r_0}}\leftarrow\mathfrak o_{\mathcal X(\sigma,p,q)^{\leq\mathfrak r_0}\operatorname{rel}\partial} \end{equation} First, though, let us argue that this claim implies the desired result. The cycle $\mu_{\sigma,p,q}\in\eqref{mucareabout}$ lifts to a cycle $\bigoplus_{\mathfrak r\in\partial\mathcal S_\mathcal X(\sigma,p,q)}\mu_{\sigma,p,q,\mathfrak r}\in\eqref{muallstrat}$, where $\mu_{\sigma,p,q,\mathfrak r}$ is obtained by applying the product/face maps to the tensor product of the various $\lambda$'s corresponding to the factors on the left hand side of \eqref{Wtotalcomposition} corresponding to $\mathfrak r$ (this is a cycle by \eqref{lambdamaster}). Obviously $\bigoplus_{\mathfrak r\in\partial\mathcal S_\mathcal X(\sigma,p,q)}\mu_{\sigma,p,q,\mathfrak r}\in\eqref{muallstrat}$ maps to $\bigoplus_{\mathfrak r\in\partial\mathcal S_\mathcal X(\sigma,p,q)^{\leq\mathfrak r_0}}\mu_{\sigma,p,q,\mathfrak r}\in\eqref{musomestrat}$. On sections over $K\subseteq\mathcal X(\sigma,p,q)^{\mathfrak r_0}$, the last vertical map is an isomorphism, and (the restriction to $K$ of) $\bigoplus_{\mathfrak r\in\partial\mathcal S_\mathcal X(\sigma,p,q)^{\leq\mathfrak r_0}}\mu_{\sigma,p,q,\mathfrak r}\in\eqref{musomestrat}$ lifts to (the restriction to $K$ of) $\mu_{\sigma,p,q,\mathfrak r_0}\in\eqref{muonestratum}$. Finally, observe that over any $K\subseteq\mathcal X(\sigma,p,q)^{\mathfrak r_0}$, the homology class of $\mu_{\sigma,p,q,\mathfrak r_0}\in\eqref{muonestratum}$ coincides with the restriction of $d\omega(\sigma,p,q)$ to the $\mathfrak r_0$ stratum (this follows from the induction hypothesis, using the fact that the orientations are coherent and the observation at the end of Definition \ref{productatlasF}). Clearly this implies that $\mu_{\sigma,p,q}$ coincides with $d\omega(\sigma,p,q)$ in homology over $\mathcal X(\sigma,p,q)^{\mathfrak r_0}$. Thus it remains only to show that \eqref{mucareabout}--\eqref{muonestratum} are pure homotopy $\mathcal K$-sheaves and that the induced maps on $H^0$ coincide with the tautological maps on orientation sheaves \eqref{orientationdiagramforHFbdry}. Note that by Proposition \ref{stratifiedispurehomotopysheaf}, the following closely related diagram satisfies all of the desired properties (i.e.\ is a diagram of pure homotopy $\mathcal K$-sheaves inducing \eqref{orientationdiagramforHFbdry} on $H^0$): \begin{align} &C_\mathrm{vir}^\bullet(\partial\mathcal X(\sigma,p,q);\mathcal B(\sigma,p,q)^{\geq\mathfrak s^\mathrm{top}})\\ &\qquad\uparrow\cr \bigoplus_{\mathfrak r\in\partial\mathcal S_\mathcal X(\sigma,p,q)}&C_\mathrm{vir}^\bullet(\mathcal X(\sigma,p,q)^{\leq\mathfrak r}\operatorname{rel}\partial;\mathcal B(\sigma,p,q)^{\geq\mathfrak s^\mathrm{top}})\\ &\qquad\downarrow\cr \bigoplus_{\mathfrak r\in\partial\mathcal S_\mathcal X(\sigma,p,q)^{\leq\mathfrak r_0}}&C_\mathrm{vir}^\bullet(\mathcal X(\sigma,p,q)^{\leq\mathfrak r}\operatorname{rel}\partial;\mathcal B(\sigma,p,q)^{\geq\mathfrak s^\mathrm{top}})\\ &\qquad\uparrow\cr &C_\mathrm{vir}^\bullet(\mathcal X(\sigma,p,q)^{\leq\mathfrak r_0}\operatorname{rel}\partial;\mathcal B(\sigma,p,q)^{\geq\mathfrak s^\mathrm{top}}) \end{align} Hence it is enough to relate this diagram to \eqref{mucareabout}--\eqref{muonestratum} via quasi-isomorphisms. The diagram obtained from \eqref{mucareabout}--\eqref{muonestratum} by replacing every occurence of $\mathcal B(\sigma,p,q)^{\geq\mathfrak t}$ with $\mathcal B(\sigma,p,q)^{\geq\mathfrak s^\mathrm{top}}$ maps quasi-isomorphically to \eqref{mucareabout}--\eqref{muonestratum} (by pairing with the fixed fundamental cycles), and it also maps quasi-isomorphically to the diagram above (use the obvious pushforwards on the $p=0$ level of the homotopy colimits, and zero for $p>0$), thus giving the desired result. \textbf{Choosing $\tilde\lambda_{\sigma,p,q}$.}\ We must find $\tilde\lambda_{\sigma,p,q}$ lifting $s_\ast\lambda_{\sigma,p,q}$ and satisfying $d\tilde\lambda_{\sigma,p,q}=\tilde\mu_{\sigma,p,q}$. Now we know that $\tilde\mu_{\sigma,p,q}$ is a cycle (see Definition \ref{systemofcycles}); furthermore its image in $C_\bullet(E;\mathcal B)^+$ is $s_\ast\mu_{\sigma,p,q}=d(s_\ast\lambda_{\sigma,p,q})$ which is null-homologous. Since $Q\mathcal W_\bullet\overset\sim\twoheadrightarrow\mathcal W_\bullet$ is always a quasi-isomorphism, it follows that $\tilde\mu_{\sigma,p,q}$ is null-homologous. Hence there exists $\tilde\lambda_{\sigma,p,q}'$ with $d\tilde\lambda_{\sigma,p,q}'=\tilde\mu_{\sigma,p,q}$; now we must modify $\tilde\lambda_{\sigma,p,q}'$ so that it lifts $s_\ast\lambda_{\sigma,p,q}$. The difference of $s_\ast\lambda_{\sigma,p,q}$ and the image of $\tilde\lambda_{\sigma,p,q}'$ is a cycle in $C_\bullet(E;\mathcal B)^+$. It can be lifted to a cycle in $QC_\bullet(E;\mathcal B)^+$ using Lemma \ref{cycleliftinglemma} (again using that $Q\mathcal W_\bullet\overset\sim\twoheadrightarrow\mathcal W_\bullet$ is a quasi-isomorphism), which is enough.
nodes.section: 7.5 Resolution \texorpdfstring{$\tilde Z_\bullet\to Z_\bullet$}{tilde Z to Z}
nodes.statement_short: Well-founded induction on triples $(\sigma,p,q)$, choosing subatlas, fundamental cycles, augmentation, $\lambda$ and $\tilde\lambda$ in turn. Key step: $[\mu_{\sigma,p,q}]=d\omega(\sigma,p,q)$, shown via a diagram of pure homotopy $\mathcal K$-sheaves inducing the tautological maps of orientation sheaves.

nodes.name: Differential graded $S$-module
nodes.statement: Let $S$ be a graded ring. A \emph{differential graded $S$-module} is a graded module $A^\bullet$ over $S$ along with a map $d:A^\bullet\to A^{\bullet+1}$ satisfying $d^2=0$.
differentia: along with a map $d:A^\bullet\to A^{\bullet+1}$ satisfying $d^2=0$

nodes.name: Category $\mathsf{Ch}_S$
nodes.statement: Let $S$ be a graded ring. We let $\mathsf{Ch}_S$ denote the category whose objects are differential graded $S$-modules and whose morphisms are chain maps.
nodes.label: ChRdef

nodes.name: Category $H^0(\mathsf{Ch}_S)$
nodes.statement: Let $S$ be a graded ring. We let $H^0(\mathsf{Ch}_S)$ denote the category whose objects are objects of $\mathsf{Ch}_S$ and whose morphisms are chain maps modulo chain homotopy.
nodes.label: HChRdef

nodes.name: Differential graded nerve $\mathsf{N}_{\mathsf{dg}}(\mathsf{Ch}_S)$
nodes.statement: Let $S$ be a graded ring. We let $\mathsf{N}_{\mathsf{dg}}(\mathsf{Ch}_S)$ denote the differential graded nerve of $\mathsf{Ch}_S$ (see Lurie \cite[Construction 1.3.1.6]{lurieha} or Definition \ref{NdgdefII} below).
nodes.label: Ndgdef

nodes.name: Diagram $X_\bullet\to\mathcal C$
nodes.statement: Recall that if $\mathcal C$ is a category and $X_\bullet$ is a simplicial set, a \emph{diagram} $X_\bullet\to\mathcal C$ is a map of simplicial sets $X_\bullet\to N_\bullet\mathcal C$ where $N_\bullet\mathcal C$ denotes the \emph{nerve}\footnote{An $n$-simplex $\Delta^n\to N_\bullet\mathcal C$ is a diagram $A_0\xrightarrow{f_{01}}A_1\xrightarrow{f_{12}}\cdots\xrightarrow{f_{n-1,n}}A_n$ in $\mathcal C$. Strictly speaking, $N_\bullet\mathcal C$ is not a simplicial \emph{set} unless $\mathcal C$ is small.} of $\mathcal C$. Concretely, a diagram $F:X_\bullet\to\mathcal C$ is the data of: \begin{rlist} \item For every vertex $v\in X_0$, an object $A_v\in\mathcal C$. \item For every edge $e\in X_1$ from $v_0$ to $v_1$, a morphism $f_e:A_{v_0}\to A_{v_1}$ in $\mathcal C$. \setcounter{rcountsave}{\value{rcounti}} \end{rlist} such that: \begin{rlist} \setcounter{rcounti}{\value{rcountsave}} \item For every degenerate edge $e\in X_1$ over vertex a $v$, we have $f_e=\operatorname{id}_{A_v}$. \item For every face in $X_2$ spanning edges $e_{01},e_{12},e_{02}$, we have $f_{e_{12}}\circ f_{e_{01}}=f_{e_{02}}$. \end{rlist} We often speak of a diagram $X_\bullet\to\mathcal C$ where $X_\bullet$ is only a \emph{semi}simplicial set, in which case we ignore condition (\ref{degenerateisIDdiagram}).
nodes.genus: a map of simplicial sets $X_\bullet\to N_\bullet\mathcal C$
nodes.statement_short: A diagram from a (semi)simplicial set to a category is a map to its nerve: objects at vertices, morphisms on edges, identities on degenerate edges, compositions on faces.

nodes.name: Diagram $X_\bullet\to\mathsf{N}_{\mathsf{dg}}(\mathsf{Ch}_S)$
nodes.statement: Let $S$ be a graded ring and let $X_\bullet$ be a simplicial set. A diagram $X_\bullet\to\mathsf{N}_{\mathsf{dg}}(\mathsf{Ch}_S)$ consists of:\footnote{For the reader familiar with $\infty$-categories: the notion of a diagram $X_\bullet\to\mathsf{N}_{\mathsf{dg}}(\mathsf{Ch}_S)$ suffices to define $\mathsf{N}_{\mathsf{dg}}(\mathsf{Ch}_S)$ by Yoneda's Lemma.} \begin{rlist} \item For every $v\in X_0$, a graded $S$-module $A_v^\bullet$. \item For every $\sigma\in X_n$ spanning $v_0,\ldots,v_n\in X_0$, a map $f_\sigma:A_{v_0}\to A_{v_n}$ of degree $1-n$, such that: \begin{equation} \sum_{k=0}^n(-1)^kf_{\sigma|[k\ldots n]}\circ f_{\sigma|[0\ldots k]}=\sum_{k=1}^{n-1}(-1)^kf_{\sigma|[0\ldots\hat k\ldots n]} \end{equation} and if $\sigma$ is degenerate, then: \begin{equation} f_\sigma=\begin{cases}\operatorname{id}&\dim\sigma=1\cr 0&\text{otherwise}\end{cases} \end{equation} \end{rlist} If $X_\bullet$ is only a \emph{semi}simplicial set, then we ignore \eqref{Ndgdegenerate}.
nodes.statement_short: Graded modules at vertices and maps $f_\sigma$ of degree $1-n$ on $n$-simplices satisfying the $A_\infty$-type relation, identities on degenerate edges.
nodes.label: NdgdefII

nodes.name: dg nerve relation
nodes.statement: \sum_{k=0}^n(-1)^kf_{\sigma|[k\ldots n]}\circ f_{\sigma|[0\ldots k]}=\sum_{k=1}^{n-1}(-1)^kf_{\sigma|[0\ldots\hat k\ldots n]}
nodes.label: Ndgmaster

nodes.name: Degenerate simplices in a dg nerve diagram
nodes.statement: f_\sigma=\begin{cases}\operatorname{id}&\dim\sigma=1\cr 0&\text{otherwise}\end{cases}
nodes.label: Ndgdegenerate

nodes.name: Low-dimensional meaning of the dg nerve relation
nodes.statement: Let us now explain this definition by examining what \eqref{Ndgmaster} says for low-dimensional simplices $\sigma:\Delta^n\to X_\bullet$ (following \cite[Example 1.3.1.8]{lurieha}). \begin{rlist} \item Let $n=0$. Then $f_0:A_0^\bullet\to A_0^\bullet$ has degree $1$, and \eqref{Ndgmaster} asserts that $f_0\circ f_0=0$. Thus $(A_0,f_0)$ is a chain complex. \item Let $n=1$. Then $f_{01}:A_0^\bullet\to A_1^\bullet$ has degree $0$, and \eqref{Ndgmaster} asserts that $f_{01}\circ f_0-f_1\circ f_{01}=0$. Thus $f_{01}:(A^\bullet_0,f_0)\to(A^\bullet_1,f_1)$ is a chain map. For a degenerate $1$-simplex, \eqref{Ndgdegenerate} asserts that $f_{01}:(A^\bullet_0,f_0)\to(A^\bullet_1,f_1)$ is the identity map. \item Let $n=2$. Then $f_{012}:A^\bullet_0\to A^\bullet_2$ has degree $-1$, and \eqref{Ndgmaster} asserts that $f_{012}f_0-f_{12}f_{01}+f_2f_{012}=-f_{02}$. Thus $f_{012}$ is a chain homotopy between $f_{02},f_{12}f_{01}:A^\bullet_0\to A^\bullet_2$.
nodes.statement_short: For $n=0,1,2$ the dg nerve relation says: a chain complex, a chain map (identity on degenerate edges), and a chain homotopy.

nodes.name: Forgetful functors $\mathsf{Ch}_S\to\mathsf{N}_{\mathsf{dg}}(\mathsf{Ch}_S)\to H^0(\mathsf{Ch}_S)$
nodes.statement: We can now relate $\mathsf{N}_{\mathsf{dg}}(\mathsf{Ch}_S)$ to the more familiar categories $\mathsf{Ch}_S$ and $H^0(\mathsf{Ch}_S)$ by introducing natural forgetful functors: \begin{equation} \mathsf{Ch}_S\to\mathsf{N}_{\mathsf{dg}}(\mathsf{Ch}_S)\to H^0(\mathsf{Ch}_S) \end{equation} which should be clear given the above interpretation of diagrams to $\mathsf{N}_{\mathsf{dg}}(\mathsf{Ch}_S)$. More precisely, a diagram $X_\bullet\to\mathsf{Ch}_S$ gives rise to a diagram $X_\bullet\to\mathsf{N}_{\mathsf{dg}}(\mathsf{Ch}_S)$ where the higher homotopies $\{f_\sigma\}_{\dim\sigma\geq 2}$ are all zero. A diagram $X_\bullet\to\mathsf{N}_{\mathsf{dg}}(\mathsf{Ch}_S)$ gives rise to a diagram $X_\bullet\to H^0(\mathsf{Ch}_S)$ which forgets about the choice of higher homotopies $\{f_\sigma\}_{\dim\sigma\geq 2}$, remembering only the existence of $\{f_\sigma\}_{\dim\sigma=2}$ satisfying \eqref{Ndgmaster}.
nodes.statement_short: Diagrams to $\mathsf{Ch}_S$ give dg-nerve diagrams with zero higher homotopies; dg-nerve diagrams give homotopy-category diagrams by forgetting higher homotopies.

nodes.name: Forgetful functors $\mathsf{Ch}_S\to\mathsf{N}_{\mathsf{dg}}(\mathsf{Ch}_S)\to H^0(\mathsf{Ch}_S)$
nodes.statement: \mathsf{Ch}_S\to\mathsf{N}_{\mathsf{dg}}(\mathsf{Ch}_S)\to H^0(\mathsf{Ch}_S)
nodes.label: forgetfulonchaincomplexes

nodes.name: Diagram $\widetilde\mathbb H(\mathcal X)$ over $\tilde Z_\bullet$ (schematic)
nodes.statement: \begin{CD} \tilde Z_\bullet@>\widetilde\mathbb H(\mathcal X)>>\mathsf{N}_{\mathsf{dg}}(\mathsf{Ch}_{R[[H]]})\cr @V\pi VV\cr Z_\bullet \end{CD}

nodes.name: Refined descent to $\mathsf{N}_{\mathsf{dg}}$ (omitted)
nodes.statement: There should also be a (more refined) descent with target $\mathsf{N}_{\mathsf{dg}}(\mathsf{Ch}_{R[[H]]})$ (c.f.\ Remark \ref{restricttotwoskeleton}), though we have decided to omit this for sake of brevity (the correct uniqueness statement is more complicated to state).
nodes.statement_short: There should be a refined descent with target the dg nerve, omitted here.

nodes.name: Novikov rings
nodes.statement: Let $T$ be a set equipped with a ``grading'' $\operatorname{gr}:T\to\mathbb Z$ and an ``action'' $a:T\to\mathbb R$. We let $R[[T]]$ denote the graded $R$-module consisting of formal sums $\sum_{t\in T}c_t\cdot t$ with $c_t\in R$, satisfying the following two finiteness conditions: \begin{rlist} \item$\#\{n\in\mathbb Z:\exists t$ such that $c_t\ne 0$ and $\operatorname{gr}(t)=n\}<\infty$. \item$\#\{t\in T:c_t\ne 0$ and $a(t)<M\}<\infty$ for all $M<\infty$. \end{rlist} In other words, $R[[T]]$ is the graded completion of $R[T]$ with respect to the non-archimedean $a$-adic norm $\left|t\right|_a:=e^{-a(t)}$. If $T$ is a group and $\operatorname{gr}$, $a$ are group homomorphisms, then $R[[T]]$ is a graded ring.
nodes.statement_short: Formal sums over a graded set with action, with finitely many degrees and finitely many terms below each action level; a ring when $T$ is a group.
nodes.label: gradedcompletion

nodes.name: (Co)homology groups $\widetilde\mathbb H(\mathcal X):\tilde Z_\bullet\to\mathsf{N}_{\mathsf{dg}}(\mathsf{Ch}_{R[[H]]})$
nodes.statement: Let $\mathcal X/Z_\bullet$ be an $H$-equivariant flow category diagram with implicit atlas $\mathcal A$ and coherent orientations $\omega$. We define a diagram: \begin{equation} \widetilde\mathbb H(\mathcal X)_{A,\omega}:\tilde Z_\bullet\to\mathsf{N}_{\mathsf{dg}}(\mathsf{Ch}_{R[[H]]}) \end{equation} We will write $\widetilde\mathbb H(\mathcal X)$ for $\widetilde\mathbb H(\mathcal X)_{A,\omega}$ when the atlas and orientations are clear from context. To a vertex of $\tilde Z_\bullet$, we associate $R[[\mathcal P_z]]$ where $z$ is the corresponding vertex in $Z_\bullet$. This is clearly a graded $R[[H]]$-module. Now for a simplex $\sigma\in\tilde Z_n$, we aim to define the map $f_\sigma:R[[\mathcal P_{\sigma(0)}]]\to R[[\mathcal P_{\sigma(n)}]]$ by the formula: \begin{equation} f_\sigma(p):=\sum_{q\in\mathcal P_{\sigma(n)}}([[E]]_{\sigma,p,q}\otimes\operatorname{id}_R)(\tilde\lambda_{\sigma,p,q})\cdot q \end{equation} Let us now argue that \eqref{diagramndgformula} makes sense and that the resulting maps $f_\sigma$ satisfy \eqref{Ndgmaster}. First, observe that since $\tilde\lambda_{\sigma,p,q}$ is of degree $\operatorname{gr}(q)-\operatorname{gr}(p)+\dim\sigma-1$ and $[[E]]_{\sigma,p,q}$ has degree $0$, all terms on the right hand side of \eqref{diagramndgformula} are of degree $\operatorname{gr}(p)+1-\dim\sigma$. Now, we have $\tilde\lambda_{\sigma,p,q}=0$ if $\mathcal X(\sigma,p,q)=\varnothing$. Hence finiteness condition Definition \ref{semisimplicialfcdef}(\ref{novikovfiniteness}) implies that \eqref{diagramndgformula} converges in the $a$-adic topology, and hence defines an $R$-linear map $f_\sigma:R[\mathcal P_{\sigma(0)}]\to R[[\mathcal P_{\sigma(0)}]]$. Finiteness condition (\ref{novikovfinitenessII}) implies that there exists $M<\infty$ such that $\left|f_\sigma(p)\right|_a\leq M\left|p\right|_a$. Thus $f_\sigma$ extends uniquely to a continuous (in fact, bounded) $R$-linear map $f_\sigma:R[[\mathcal P_{\sigma(0)}]]\to R[[\mathcal P_{\sigma(0)}]]$. Clearly $f_\sigma$ is $R[[H]]$-linear since $[[E]]$ and $\tilde\lambda$ are both $H$-invariant. Now it remains to verify that the $f_\sigma$ defined by \eqref{diagramndgformula} satisfy \eqref{Ndgmaster}. To see this, write: \begin{align*} 0&=(-1)^{\operatorname{gr}(p)}\cdot[[E]]_{\sigma,p,r}(d\tilde\lambda_{\sigma,p,r})\cr &=(-1)^{\operatorname{gr}(p)}\cdot[[E]]_{\sigma,p,r}(\tilde\mu_{\sigma,p,r})\cr &=[[E]]_{\sigma,p,r}\left(\sum_{k=0}^n\sum_{q\in\mathcal P_{\sigma(k)}}(-1)^k\tilde\lambda_{\sigma|[0\ldots k],p,q}\cdot\tilde\lambda_{\sigma|[k\ldots n],q,r}-\sum_{k=1}^{n-1}(-1)^k\tilde\lambda_{\sigma|[0\ldots\hat k\ldots n],p,r}\right)\cr &=\sum_{k=0}^n\sum_{q\in\mathcal P_{\sigma(k)}}(-1)^k[[E]]_{\sigma|[0\ldots k],p,q}(\tilde\lambda_{\sigma|[0\ldots k],p,q})\cdot[[E]]_{\sigma|[k\ldots n],q,r}(\tilde\lambda_{\sigma|[k\ldots n],q,r})\cr&\qquad-\sum_{k=1}^{n-1}(-1)^k[[E]]_{\sigma|[0\ldots\hat k\ldots n],p,r}(\tilde\lambda_{\sigma|[0\ldots\hat k\ldots n],p,r})\cr &=\text{coefficient of }r\text{ in }\sum_{k=0}^n(-1)^kf_{\sigma|[k\ldots n]}(f_{\sigma|[0\ldots k]}(p))-\sum_{k=1}^{n-1}(-1)^kf_{\sigma|[0\ldots\hat k\ldots n]}(p) \end{align*} The first equality follows because $[[E]]_{\sigma,p,r}$ is a chain map, the second equality follows from the definition of a system of chains, the third equality is \eqref{lambdamaster}, the fourth equality follows from the fact that $[[E]]$ is compatible with the product/face maps, and the fifth equality follows from the definition of $f_\sigma$ \eqref{diagramndgformula}.
nodes.statement_short: Assign Novikov modules $R[[\mathcal P_z]]$ to vertices and maps $f_\sigma$ counting $[[E]](\tilde\lambda)$ to simplices; verify convergence and the dg-nerve relations.
nodes.label: diagramoverZtilde

nodes.name: Diagram $\widetilde\mathbb H(\mathcal X)_{A,\omega}$
nodes.statement: \widetilde\mathbb H(\mathcal X)_{A,\omega}:\tilde Z_\bullet\to\mathsf{N}_{\mathsf{dg}}(\mathsf{Ch}_{R[[H]]})

nodes.name: Matrix coefficients of $f_\sigma$ via $[[E]](\tilde\lambda)$
nodes.statement: f_\sigma(p):=\sum_{q\in\mathcal P_{\sigma(n)}}([[E]]_{\sigma,p,q}\otimes\operatorname{id}_R)(\tilde\lambda_{\sigma,p,q})\cdot q
nodes.label: diagramndgformula

nodes.name: Degenerate edges in $\tilde Z_\bullet$ give the identity map up to homotopy
nodes.statement: Let $Z_\bullet=\ast$ be the semisimplicial set with a single simplex $\sigma^i$ in dimension $i$ for all $i\geq 0$ (i.e.\ the simplicial $0$-simplex). Let $\mathcal X/Z_\bullet$ be an $H$-equivariant flow category diagram with implicit atlas and coherent orientations. Suppose that: \begin{rlist} \item$\mathcal X(\sigma^1,p,p)=\mathcal X(\sigma^1,p,p)^\mathrm{reg}$ is a single point and $\omega(\sigma^1,p,p)=1$, for all $p$. \item$\mathcal X(\sigma^0,p,q)=\varnothing\implies\mathcal X(\sigma^i,p,q)=\varnothing$ for all $i$ and all $p\ne q$. \end{rlist} Then for any $\sigma\in\tilde Z_1$ whose two vertices coincide, the associated map in $\widetilde\mathbb H(\mathcal X)$ is homotopic to the identity map.
assumptions: Let $Z_\bullet=\ast$ be the semisimplicial set with a single simplex $\sigma^i$ in dimension $i$ for all $i\geq 0$ (i.e.\ the simplicial $0$-simplex).
Let $\mathcal X/Z_\bullet$ be an $H$-equivariant flow category diagram with implicit atlas and coherent orientations.
$\mathcal X(\sigma^1,p,p)=\mathcal X(\sigma^1,p,p)^\mathrm{reg}$ is a single point and $\omega(\sigma^1,p,p)=1$, for all $p$.
$\mathcal X(\sigma^0,p,q)=\varnothing\implies\mathcal X(\sigma^i,p,q)=\varnothing$ for all $i$ and all $p\ne q$.
conclusions: Then for any $\sigma\in\tilde Z_1$ whose two vertices coincide, the associated map in $\widetilde\mathbb H(\mathcal X)$ is homotopic to the identity map.
nodes.label: degenerateID

nodes.name: Proof
nodes.statement:
Let $d:R[[\mathcal P]]	o R[[\mathcal P]]$ denote the boundary operator associated to the vertex of $\sigma$, and let $1-\epsilon:R[[\mathcal P]]	o R[[\mathcal P]]$ denote the chain map associated to $\sigma$. We must show that $\epsilon$ is chain homotopic to the zero map. Since $	ilde Z_ ullet	o Z_ ullet$ is a trivial Kan fibration (Proposition ef{trivialKanfibration}), there exists a $2$-simplex in $	ilde Z_ ullet$ all of whose edges are $\sigma$. Associated to this $2$-simplex is a chain homotopy $h:R[[\mathcal P]]	o R[[\mathcal P]]$ between $(1-\epsilon)$ and $(1-\epsilon)\circ(1-\epsilon)$; in other words:  egin{equation} \epsilon=dh+hd+\epsilon^2 \end{equation} Now we claim that the only nonzero ``matrix coefficients'' $c_{p,q}$ of $d,\epsilon,h$ are those for which $\mathcal X(\sigma^0,p,q)
e\varnothing$. By definition, $f_\sigma$ can have nonzero matrix coefficients $c_{p,q}$ only for $\mathcal X(\sigma,p,q)
e\varnothing$. Hence hypothesis (ef{highernonemptyissameaszero}) gives the desired claim as long as $p
e q$. For the diagonal matrix coefficients $c_{p,p}$, we argue separately as follows. By degree considerations, only $\epsilon$ can have nonzero $c_{p,p}$. It thus suffices to show that the matrix coefficient $c_{p,p}=[[E]]_{\sigma^1,p,p}(	ilde\lambda_{\sigma^1,p,p})$ of $f_{\sigma^1}=1-\epsilon$ equals $1$. Note that no product/face maps have target $(\sigma^1,p,p)$, so $\lambda_{\sigma^1,p,p}$ is a cycle representing $\omega(\sigma^1,p,p)=1$. Hence $	ilde\lambda_{\sigma^1,p,p}$ is a cycle representing $[E]$, and so $[[E]]_{\sigma^1,p,p}(	ilde\lambda_{\sigma,p,p})=1$ as needed. Hence the claim is valid. From the claim, we make the following two observations:  egin{rlist} \itemWe have $\left|d(p)ight|_a,\left|\epsilon(p)ight|_a,\left|h(p)ight|_a\leq\left|pight|_a$. \itemFor all $M<\infty$ and $p\in\mathcal P$, there exists $N<\infty$ such that any length $N$ composition of $d,\epsilon,h$ applied to $p$ has $a$-adic norm $\leq e^{-M}$. \end{rlist} (the second observation also uses Definition ef{semisimplicialfcdef}(ef{novikovfiniteness})). Now iterating the identity $\epsilon=dh+hd+\epsilon^2$, we are led to the following infinite series: ootnote{The coefficients $ rac 1n inom{2n-2}{n-1}$ are integers (Catalan numbers $C_{n-1}$), so writing this expression does not make any implicit assumptions on the ring $R$.}  egin{equation} \epsilon=\sum_{n=1}^\infty rac 1n inom{2n-2}{n-1}(hd+dh)^n \end{equation} which by observations (ef{firstO})--(ef{secondO}) converges in the $a$-adic topology when applied to any element of $R[[\mathcal P]]$. Now we have $(hd+dh)^n=\sum_{k=0}^n(dh)^k(hd)^{n-k}=H_nd+dH_n$ where $H_n=\sum_{k=1}^nh(dh)^{k-1}(hd)^{n-k}$. This gives the desired chain homotopy between $\epsilon$ and zero (again using observations (ef{firstO})--(ef{secondO}) to justify convergence of infinite sums).
nodes.statement_short: Lift a degenerate 2-simplex to get $\epsilon=dh+hd+\epsilon^2$; matrix-coefficient support plus $a$-adic convergence lets one solve this by a Catalan-number series. The key step shows the diagonal coefficients of $f_{\sigma^1}$ equal $1$.

nodes.statement: \epsilon=dh+hd+\epsilon^2
