nodes.name: Criterion for descent along a trivial Kan fibration
nodes.statement: Let $\pi:\tilde Z_\bullet\to Z_\bullet$ be a trivial Kan fibration of semisimplicial sets, and let $\widetilde\mathbb H:\tilde Z_\bullet\to\mathcal C$ be a diagram in some category $\mathcal C$. A \emph{descent} of $\widetilde\mathbb H$ to $Z_\bullet$ is a diagram $\mathbb H:Z_\bullet\to\mathcal C$ along with an isomorphism $\widetilde\mathbb H\to\mathbb H\circ\pi$: \begin{equation} \begin{tikzcd} \tilde Z_\bullet\arrow{r}{\widetilde\mathbb H}\arrow{d}[swap]{\pi}&\mathcal C\\ Z_\bullet\arrow[dashed]{ur}[swap]{\mathbb H} \end{tikzcd} \end{equation} Suppose that: \begin{rlist} \item$Z_\bullet$ is a simplicial set. \itemFor any edge $\sigma^1$ in $\tilde Z_\bullet$ whose endpoints coincide and which projects to a degenerate edge in $Z_\bullet$, the associated map in $\mathcal C$ is the identity map. \end{rlist} Then a descent exists and is unique up to unique isomorphism.
nodes.statement_short: A diagram on $\tilde Z_\bullet$ that is the identity on lifts of degenerate loops descends uniquely along a trivial Kan fibration.
assumptions: Let $\pi:\tilde Z_\bullet\to Z_\bullet$ be a trivial Kan fibration of semisimplicial sets, and let $\widetilde\mathbb H:\tilde Z_\bullet\to\mathcal C$ be a diagram in some category $\mathcal C$.
$Z_\bullet$ is a simplicial set.
For any edge $\sigma^1$ in $\tilde Z_\bullet$ whose endpoints coincide and which projects to a degenerate edge in $Z_\bullet$, the associated map in $\mathcal C$ is the identity map.
conclusions: Then a descent exists and is unique up to unique isomorphism.
nodes.label: descentofdiagram

nodes.name: Descent diagram
nodes.statement: \begin{tikzcd} \tilde Z_\bullet\arrow{r}{\widetilde\mathbb H}\arrow{d}[swap]{\pi}&\mathcal C\\ Z_\bullet\arrow[dashed]{ur}[swap]{\mathbb H} \end{tikzcd}

nodes.name: Proof
nodes.statement: The proof below shows that we may define $\mathbb H:=\widetilde\mathbb H\circ s$ for any section $s:Z_\bullet\to\tilde Z_\bullet$. \textbf{Defining $\mathbb H$ over $0$-simplices.}\ Fix some $0$-simplex $v$ of $Z_\bullet$. For every lift $\tilde v$, we have an object $\widetilde\mathbb H(\tilde v)$. Furthermore, for every lift $\tilde e$ of the degenerate $1$-simplex $e$ over $v$, we get a map $\widetilde\mathbb H(\tilde v_1)\xrightarrow{\widetilde\mathbb H(\tilde e)}\widetilde\mathbb H(\tilde v_2)$, which is the identity map if $\tilde v_1=\tilde v_2$. Finally, for every lift $\tilde f$ of the degenerate $2$-simplex $f$ over $v$, the following diagram commutes: \begin{equation} \begin{tikzcd}[row sep = small] &\widetilde\mathbb H(\tilde v_2)\ar{rd}{\widetilde\mathbb H(\tilde e_{23})}&{}\cr \widetilde\mathbb H(\tilde v_1)\ar{ur}{\widetilde\mathbb H(\tilde e_{12})}\ar{rr}[swap]{\widetilde\mathbb H(\tilde e_{13})}&&{\widetilde\mathbb H(\tilde v_3)} \end{tikzcd} \end{equation} where $\tilde e_{12},\tilde e_{23},\tilde e_{13}$ are the edges of $\tilde f$. Using that $\tilde Z_\bullet\to Z_\bullet$ is a trivial Kan fibration to conclude that we can always find lifts with specified boundary conditions, it follows that all $\widetilde\mathbb H(\tilde v)$ are canonically isomorphic. Thus there exists a unique choice for $\mathbb H(v)$. \textbf{Defining $\mathbb H$ over $1$-simplices.}\ Fix some $1$-simplex $e$ of $Z_\bullet$ with vertices $v_1,v_2$. If $\tilde e$ is any lift of $e$, then we get a map $\mathbb H(v_1)=\widetilde\mathbb H(\tilde v_1)\xrightarrow{\widetilde\mathbb H(\tilde e)}\widetilde\mathbb H(\tilde v_2)=\mathbb H(v_2)$. Furthermore, this map $\mathbb H(v_1)\to\mathbb H(v_2)$ is seen to be independent of the choice of lift $\tilde e$ by lifting degenerate $2$-simplices over $e$. Thus there exists a unique choice for $\mathbb H(e)$. \textbf{Defining $\mathbb H$ over $n$-simplices for $n\geq 2$.}\ We just need to check that the following diagram commutes for all $2$-simplices $f$ in $Z_\bullet$: \begin{equation} \begin{tikzcd}[row sep = small] &\mathbb H(v_2)\ar{rd}{\mathbb H(e_{23})}&{}\cr \mathbb H(v_1)\ar{ur}{\mathbb H(e_{12})}\ar{rr}[swap]{\mathbb H(e_{13})}&&{\mathbb H(v_3)} \end{tikzcd} \end{equation} where $e_{12},e_{23},e_{13}$ are the edges of $f$. This follows from lifting $f$ and the commutativity of \eqref{liftedF}.
nodes.statement_short: Define $\mathbb H$ skeleton by skeleton, using lifts with prescribed boundary to show independence of choices over $0$-, $1$- and $2$-simplices.

nodes.name: Commuting triangle over lifted degenerate 2-simplex
nodes.statement: \begin{tikzcd}[row sep = small] &\widetilde\mathbb H(\tilde v_2)\ar{rd}{\widetilde\mathbb H(\tilde e_{23})}&{}\cr \widetilde\mathbb H(\tilde v_1)\ar{ur}{\widetilde\mathbb H(\tilde e_{12})}\ar{rr}[swap]{\widetilde\mathbb H(\tilde e_{13})}&&{\widetilde\mathbb H(\tilde v_3)} \end{tikzcd}
nodes.label: liftedF

nodes.name: Commuting triangle over a 2-simplex of $Z_\bullet$
nodes.statement: \begin{tikzcd}[row sep = small] &\mathbb H(v_2)\ar{rd}{\mathbb H(e_{23})}&{}\cr \mathbb H(v_1)\ar{ur}{\mathbb H(e_{12})}\ar{rr}[swap]{\mathbb H(e_{13})}&&{\mathbb H(v_3)} \end{tikzcd}

nodes.name: (Co)homology groups $\mathbb H(\mathcal X):Z_\bullet\to H^0(\mathsf{Ch}_{R[[H]]})$
nodes.statement: Let $Z_\bullet$ be a simplicial set. Let $\mathcal X/Z_\bullet$ be an $H$-equivariant flow category diagram with implicit atlas $\mathcal A$ and coherent orientations $\omega$. Suppose that for any vertex $\sigma^0$ of $Z_\bullet$, we have: \begin{rlist} \item$\mathcal X(\sigma^1,p,p)=\mathcal X(\sigma^1,p,p)^\mathrm{reg}$ is a single point and $\omega(\sigma^1,p,p)=1$, for all $p$. \item$\mathcal X(\sigma^0,p,q)=\varnothing\implies\mathcal X(\sigma^i,p,q)=\varnothing$ for all $i$ and $p\ne q$ \end{rlist} (where $\sigma^i$ denotes the completely degenerate $i$-simplex over $\sigma^0$). We have: \begin{equation} \begin{tikzcd} \tilde Z_\bullet\arrow{r}{\widetilde\mathbb H(\mathcal X)}\arrow{d}[swap]{\pi}&H^0(\mathsf{Ch}_{R[[H]]})\\ Z_\bullet \end{tikzcd} \end{equation} (abusing notation and use $\widetilde\mathbb H(\mathcal X):\tilde Z_\bullet\to H^0(\mathsf{Ch}_{R[[H]]})$ to denote the composition of $\widetilde\mathbb H(\mathcal X)$ with the forgetful functor $\mathsf{N}_{\mathsf{dg}}\to H^0$). The hypotheses of Lemma \ref{descentofdiagram} are satisfied by Propositions \ref{trivialKanfibration} and \ref{degenerateID}, and hence we get a canonical descent: \begin{equation} \mathbb H(\mathcal X)_{A,\omega}:Z_\bullet\to H^0(\mathsf{Ch}_{R[[H]]}) \end{equation} We will write $\mathbb H(\mathcal X)$ for $\mathbb H(\mathcal X)_{A,\omega}$ when the atlas and orientations are clear from context.
nodes.statement_short: Floer-type homology is the canonical descent of $\widetilde\mathbb H(\mathcal X)$ along the trivial Kan fibration $\pi$ to a diagram in the homotopy category.
nodes.label: defofhomologygroups

nodes.name: Diagram $\widetilde\mathbb H(\mathcal X)$ into the homotopy category
nodes.statement: \begin{tikzcd} \tilde Z_\bullet\arrow{r}{\widetilde\mathbb H(\mathcal X)}\arrow{d}[swap]{\pi}&H^0(\mathsf{Ch}_{R[[H]]})\\ Z_\bullet \end{tikzcd}

nodes.name: Descended diagram $\mathbb H(\mathcal X)_{A,\omega}$
nodes.statement: \mathbb H(\mathcal X)_{A,\omega}:Z_\bullet\to H^0(\mathsf{Ch}_{R[[H]]})

nodes.name: Passing to a subatlas preserves $\mathbb H(\mathcal X)$
nodes.statement: Let $Z_\bullet$, $\mathcal X/Z_\bullet$, $\mathcal A$, and $\omega$ be as in Definition \ref{defofhomologygroups}. If $\mathcal B\subseteq\mathcal A$ is any subatlas, then there is a canonical isomorphism $\mathbb H(\mathcal X)_\mathcal A=\mathbb H(\mathcal X)_\mathcal B$.
assumptions: If $\mathcal B\subseteq\mathcal A$ is any subatlas
conclusions: then there is a canonical isomorphism $\mathbb H(\mathcal X)_\mathcal A=\mathbb H(\mathcal X)_\mathcal B$.
nodes.label: homologysameassubatlas

nodes.name: Proof
nodes.statement: Indeed, we have $\tilde Z_\bullet^\mathcal B\subseteq\tilde Z_\bullet^\mathcal A$ compatibly with $\widetilde\mathbb H(\mathcal X)$.
nodes.statement_short: $\tilde Z^\mathcal B\subseteq\tilde Z^\mathcal A$ compatibly with $\widetilde\mathbb H$.

nodes.name: Shrinking the charts preserves $\mathbb H(\mathcal X)$
nodes.statement: Let $Z_\bullet$, $\mathcal X/Z_\bullet$, $\mathcal A$, and $\omega$ be as in Definition \ref{defofhomologygroups}. Let $\mathcal A'$ be obtained from $\mathcal A$ by using instead some open subsets $U_{IJ}'\subseteq U_{IJ}$, $X_I'\subseteq X_I$, $X_I^{\mathrm{reg}\prime}\subseteq X_I^\mathrm{reg}$, and restricting $\psi_{IJ}$, $s_I$ to these subsets, so that $\mathcal A'$ is also an implicit atlas. Then there is a canonical isomorphism $\mathbb H(\mathcal X)_\mathcal A=\mathbb H(\mathcal X)_{\mathcal A'}$.
assumptions: Let $\mathcal A'$ be obtained from $\mathcal A$ by using instead some open subsets $U_{IJ}'\subseteq U_{IJ}$, $X_I'\subseteq X_I$, $X_I^{\mathrm{reg}\prime}\subseteq X_I^\mathrm{reg}$, and restricting $\psi_{IJ}$, $s_I$ to these subsets, so that $\mathcal A'$ is also an implicit atlas.
conclusions: Then there is a canonical isomorphism $\mathbb H(\mathcal X)_\mathcal A=\mathbb H(\mathcal X)_{\mathcal A'}$.
nodes.label: homologyopenreduction

nodes.name: Proof
nodes.statement: There is a natural map $\tilde Z_\bullet^{\mathcal A'}\to\tilde Z_\bullet^\mathcal A$ for which the pullback of $\widetilde\mathbb H(\mathcal X)_\mathcal A$ is canonically isomorphic to $\widetilde\mathbb H(\mathcal X)_{\mathcal A'}$. This is enough.
nodes.statement_short: Natural map $\tilde Z^{\mathcal A'}\to\tilde Z^\mathcal A$ pulling back $\widetilde\mathbb H$ to $\widetilde\mathbb H$.

nodes.name: Universal coefficients for $\mathbb H(\mathcal X)$
nodes.statement: Let $Z_\bullet$, $\mathcal X/Z_\bullet$, $\mathcal A$, and $\omega$ be as in Definition \ref{defofhomologygroups}. Let $R\to S$ a homomorphism of base rings. Then there is a canonical isomorphism $\mathbb H(\mathcal X)^S=\mathbb H(\mathcal X)^R\otimes_{R[[H]]}S[[H]]$ (denoting $\otimes_{R[[H]]}S[[H]]:H^0(\mathsf{Ch}_{R[[H]]})\to H^0(\mathsf{Ch}_{S[[H]]})$).
assumptions: Let $R\to S$ a homomorphism of base rings.
conclusions: Then there is a canonical isomorphism $\mathbb H(\mathcal X)^S=\mathbb H(\mathcal X)^R\otimes_{R[[H]]}S[[H]]$

nodes.name: Proof
nodes.statement: There is a natural base change map $b:\tilde Z_\bullet^R\to\tilde Z_\bullet^S$ and a canonical isomorphism $\widetilde\mathbb H(\mathcal X)^S\circ b=\widetilde\mathbb H(\mathcal X)^R\otimes_{R[[H]]}S[[H]]$. Now the result follows since $\widetilde\mathbb H(\mathcal X)^S\circ b$ and $\widetilde\mathbb H(\mathcal X)^S$ have the same descent to $Z_\bullet$.
nodes.statement_short: Base change map $\tilde Z^R\to\tilde Z^S$ intertwines $\widetilde\mathbb H$, and both have the same descent.

nodes.name: If $\mathcal X=\mathcal X^\mathrm{reg}$, then $\mathbb H(\mathcal X)$ is given by counting $0$-dimensional flow spaces
nodes.statement: Let $Z_\bullet$, $\mathcal X/Z_\bullet$, $\mathcal A$, and $\omega$ be as in Definition \ref{defofhomologygroups}. Suppose that $\mathcal X(\sigma,p,q)=\mathcal X(\sigma,p,q)^\mathrm{reg}$ for all $(\sigma,p,q)$ (so, in particular, $\mathcal X/Z_\bullet$ is Morse--Smale in the sense of Remark \ref{MSflowcatediag}). Define a diagram $\mathbb H'(\mathcal X):Z_\bullet\to\mathsf{N}_{\mathsf{dg}}(\mathsf{Ch}_{R[[H]]})$ as follows. The graded $R[[H]]$-module associated to a vertex $z$ of $\tilde Z_\bullet$ is $R[[\mathcal P_z]]$. For a simplex $\sigma\in\tilde Z_n$, we define the map $f_\sigma:R[[\mathcal P_{\sigma(0)}]]\to R[[\mathcal P_{\sigma(n)}]]$ by the formula: \begin{equation} f_\sigma(p):=\sum_{\begin{smallmatrix}q\in\mathcal P_{\sigma(n)}\cr\operatorname{gr}(q)-\operatorname{gr}(p)=1-\dim\sigma\end{smallmatrix}}\langle\omega(\sigma,p,q),[\mathcal X(\sigma,p,q)]\rangle\cdot q \end{equation} It is easy to verify that the maps $f_\sigma$ are well-defined and satisfy \eqref{Ndgmaster}. Now there is a canonical isomorphism $\mathbb H(\mathcal X)=\mathbb H'(\mathcal X)$ (where on the right hand side we implicitly compose with the forgetful functor $\mathsf{N}_{\mathsf{dg}}\to H^0$).
nodes.statement_short: When all flow spaces are transversely cut out, Floer-type homology agrees with the diagram counting $0$-dimensional flow spaces with orientations.
assumptions: Suppose that $\mathcal X(\sigma,p,q)=\mathcal X(\sigma,p,q)^\mathrm{reg}$ for all $(\sigma,p,q)$
conclusions: Now there is a canonical isomorphism $\mathbb H(\mathcal X)=\mathbb H'(\mathcal X)$
nodes.label: iftransversejustcountzero

nodes.name: Counting formula for Morse--Smale flow category diagrams
nodes.statement: f_\sigma(p):=\sum_{\begin{smallmatrix}q\in\mathcal P_{\sigma(n)}\cr\operatorname{gr}(q)-\operatorname{gr}(p)=1-\dim\sigma\end{smallmatrix}}\langle\omega(\sigma,p,q),[\mathcal X(\sigma,p,q)]\rangle\cdot q
nodes.label: diagramndgformulaMS

nodes.name: Proof
nodes.statement: We will show an equality of ``matrix coefficients'': \begin{equation} ([[E]]_{\sigma,p,q}\otimes\operatorname{id}_R)(\tilde\lambda_{\sigma,p,q})=\langle\omega(\sigma,p,q),[\mathcal X(\sigma,p,q)]\rangle \end{equation} for $(\sigma,p,q)\in\tilde Z_\bullet$ with $\operatorname{vdim}\mathcal X(\sigma,p,q)=0$. Thus comparing \eqref{diagramndgformula} and \eqref{diagramndgformulaMS}, it follows that the two diagrams $\tilde Z_\bullet\to\mathsf{N}_{\mathsf{dg}}(\mathsf{Ch}_{R[[H]]})$ in question, namely $\widetilde\mathbb H(\mathcal X)$ and $\mathbb H'(\mathcal X)\circ\pi$, coincide. The desired isomorphism thus follows from the definition of $\mathbb H(\mathcal X)$ as the descent of $\widetilde\mathbb H(\mathcal X)$. To prove \eqref{matrixcoeffsame}, argue as follows. Since $\mathcal X(\sigma,p,q)=\mathcal X(\sigma,p,q)^\mathrm{reg}$, we know that if $\operatorname{vdim}\mathcal X(\sigma,p,q)<0$ then $\mathcal X(\sigma,p,q)=\varnothing$ and hence $\lambda_{\sigma,p,q}=0$ and $\tilde\lambda_{\sigma,p,q}=0$. Now when $\operatorname{vdim}\mathcal X(\sigma,p,q)=0$, we see that $\mu_{\sigma,p,q}=0$ and $\tilde\mu_{\sigma,p,q}=0$ (because all of the terms defining them involve a triple with negative dimension), so $\lambda_{\sigma,p,q}$ and $\tilde\lambda_{\sigma,p,q}$ are cycles. Since the homology class of $\lambda_{\sigma,p,q}$ coincides with $\omega(\sigma,p,q)$, the left hand side of \eqref{matrixcoeffsame} coincides with the evaluation of $\omega(\sigma,p,q)$ on $[\mathcal X(\sigma,p,q)]^\mathrm{vir}\in\check H^0(\mathcal X(\sigma,p,q);\mathfrak o_{\mathcal X(\sigma,p,q)})^\vee$. Now we are done since $[\mathcal X(\sigma,p,q)]^\mathrm{vir}=[\mathcal X(\sigma,p,q)]$ by Lemma \ref{fclasstransverse}.
nodes.statement_short: Show matrix coefficients agree: in virtual dimension $0$, $\lambda$ and $\tilde\lambda$ are cycles, so $[[E]](\tilde\lambda)$ evaluates $\omega$ on $[\mathcal X]^\mathrm{vir}=[\mathcal X]$.

nodes.name: Equality of matrix coefficients
nodes.statement: ([[E]]_{\sigma,p,q}\otimes\operatorname{id}_R)(\tilde\lambda_{\sigma,p,q})=\langle\omega(\sigma,p,q),[\mathcal X(\sigma,p,q)]\rangle
nodes.label: matrixcoeffsame

nodes.statement: In this section, we prove vanishing results for virtual fundamental cycles on almost free\footnote{An ``almost free'' action is one for which the stabilizer group of every point is finite.} $S^1$-spaces equipped with an \emph{$S^1$-equivariant implicit atlas}.
nodes.name: Almost free $S^1$-action
nodes.statement_short: An almost free action is one whose stabilizers are all finite.

nodes.name: Ground ring and invertibility convention (S^1-localization)
nodes.statement: In this section, we work over a fixed ground ring $R$, and everything takes place in the category of $R$-modules. We restrict to implicit atlases $A$ for which $\#\Gamma_\alpha$ is invertible in $R$ for all $\alpha\in A$. We restrict to $S^1$-equivariant implicit atlases for which $\#(S^1)_p$ is invertible in $R$ for all $p\in X_\varnothing$.
nodes.statement_short: Work over ground ring $R$ with $\#\Gamma_\alpha$ and all $S^1$-stabilizer orders invertible in $R$.

nodes.name: Comparison maps $C^\bullet_{S^1,\mathrm{vir}}\to C^\bullet_\mathrm{vir}$
nodes.statement: C^\bullet_{S^1,\mathrm{vir}}(X;A)&\to C^\bullet_\mathrm{vir}(X;A)\\ C^\bullet_{S^1,\mathrm{vir}}(X\operatorname{rel}\partial;A)&\to C^\bullet_\mathrm{vir}(X\operatorname{rel}\partial;A)
nodes.label: CSScompare

nodes.name: Compatibility of pushforward with the Gysin map
nodes.statement: \begin{CD} C^{d+\bullet}_{S^1,\mathrm{vir}}(X\operatorname{rel}\partial;A)@>s_\ast>>C_{\dim E_A-\bullet-1}^{S^1}(E_A,E_A\setminus 0;\mathfrak o_{E_A}^\vee)^{\Gamma_A}\cr @VVV@VV\pi^!V\cr C^{d+\bullet}_\mathrm{vir}(X\operatorname{rel}\partial;A)@>s_\ast>>C_{\dim E_A-\bullet}(E_A,E_A\setminus 0;\mathfrak o_{E_A}^\vee)^{\Gamma_A} \end{CD}
nodes.label: SSpushforwardcompatiblity

nodes.name: Isomorphisms $H^\bullet_{S^1,\mathrm{vir}}(X;A)=\check H^\bullet(X/S^1;\pi_\ast\mathfrak o_X)$ (preview)
nodes.statement: H^\bullet_{S^1,\mathrm{vir}}(X;A)&=\check H^\bullet(X/S^1;\pi_\ast\mathfrak o_X)\\ H^\bullet_{S^1,\mathrm{vir}}(X\operatorname{rel}\partial;A)&=\check H^\bullet(X/S^1;\pi_\ast\mathfrak o_{X\operatorname{rel}\partial})
nodes.label: HXSSiso

nodes.name: Gysin sequence
nodes.statement: Let $\pi:E\to B$ be a principal $S^1$-bundle. Analysis of the associated Serre spectral sequence gives the following Gysin long exact sequence: \begin{equation} \cdots\xrightarrow{\cap e}H_{\bullet-1}(B)\xrightarrow{\pi^!}H_\bullet(E)\xrightarrow{\pi_\ast}H_\bullet(B)\xrightarrow{\cap e}H_{\bullet-2}(B)\xrightarrow{\pi^!}\cdots \end{equation} The $\cap e$ map is cap product with the Euler class $e(E)\in H^2(B)$. To see this, observe that the sequence \eqref{gysinserregeneral} coincides with the long exact sequence of the pair for (the mapping cone of) $\pi:E\to B$, and that there is a natural isomorphism $H_{\bullet+2}(B,E)\xrightarrow{\cap\tau}H_\bullet(B)$ where $\tau=\tau(E)\in H^2(B,E)$ is the Thom class (e.g.\ as argued in \cite[p444]{hatcher} for the corresponding sequence in cohomology). For any $S^1$-space $X$. there is a principal $S^1$-bundle $\pi:X\times ES^1\to(X\times ES^1)/S^1$, and thus a long exact sequence: \begin{equation} \cdots\xrightarrow{\cap e}H_{\bullet-1}^{S^1}(X)\xrightarrow{\pi^!}H_\bullet(X)\xrightarrow{\pi_\ast}H_\bullet^{S^1}(X)\xrightarrow{\cap e}H_{\bullet-2}^{S^1}(X)\xrightarrow{\pi^!}\cdots \end{equation} for $e(X)\in H^2_{S^1}(X)$. The same reasoning applies for pairs of spaces, so the same exact sequence exists for relative homology as well.
nodes.statement_short: A principal $S^1$-bundle (and the Borel construction of an $S^1$-space) yields the Gysin long exact sequence via cap product with the Euler class.
assumptions: Let $\pi:E\to B$ be a principal $S^1$-bundle.
conclusions: Analysis of the associated Serre spectral sequence gives the following Gysin long exact sequence:

nodes.name: Gysin long exact sequence of a principal $S^1$-bundle
nodes.statement: \cdots\xrightarrow{\cap e}H_{\bullet-1}(B)\xrightarrow{\pi^!}H_\bullet(E)\xrightarrow{\pi_\ast}H_\bullet(B)\xrightarrow{\cap e}H_{\bullet-2}(B)\xrightarrow{\pi^!}\cdots
nodes.label: gysinserregeneral

nodes.name: Gysin sequence for $S^1$-equivariant homology
nodes.statement: \cdots\xrightarrow{\cap e}H_{\bullet-1}^{S^1}(X)\xrightarrow{\pi^!}H_\bullet(X)\xrightarrow{\pi_\ast}H_\bullet^{S^1}(X)\xrightarrow{\cap e}H_{\bullet-2}^{S^1}(X)\xrightarrow{\pi^!}\cdots
nodes.label: gysinserre

nodes.name: Gysin sequence for trivial $S^1$-action
nodes.statement: Let $X$ be a trivial $S^1$-space. Then the $\pi^!$ map in the Gysin sequence vanishes, turning it into a short exact sequence: \begin{equation} 0\to H_\bullet(X)\xrightarrow{\pi_\ast}H_\bullet^{S^1}(X)\xrightarrow{\cap e}H_{\bullet-2}^{S^1}(X)\to 0 \end{equation} The same statement applies to relative homology of trivial $S^1$-spaces.
nodes.statement_short: For a trivial $S^1$-space the Gysin map $\pi^!$ vanishes, so the Gysin sequence splits into short exact sequences.
assumptions: Let $X$ be a trivial $S^1$-space.
conclusions: Then the $\pi^!$ map in the Gysin sequence vanishes, turning it into a short exact sequence:
The same statement applies to relative homology of trivial $S^1$-spaces.
nodes.label: trivialactiongysin

nodes.name: Short exact Gysin sequence for trivial action
nodes.statement: 0\to H_\bullet(X)\xrightarrow{\pi_\ast}H_\bullet^{S^1}(X)\xrightarrow{\cap e}H_{\bullet-2}^{S^1}(X)\to 0

nodes.name: Proof
nodes.statement: The composition $H_\bullet(X)\to H_\bullet(X\times BS^1)\to H_\bullet(X)$ is the identity map, and so the first map is injective. On the other hand, this map is precisely $\pi_\ast:H_\bullet(X)\to H_\bullet^{S^1}(X)$ since the $S^1$-action is trivial, so $\pi_\ast$ is injective which is sufficient. The same argument applies in the relative setting as well.
nodes.statement_short: The composition $H_\bullet(X)\to H_\bullet(X\times BS^1)\to H_\bullet(X)$ is the identity, so $\pi_\ast$ is injective and $\pi^!$ vanishes.

nodes.name: Euler class vanishes near an almost free orbit
nodes.statement: Let $X$ be a locally compact Hausdorff $S^1$-space which is almost free at $p\in X$, and suppose that the order of the stabilizer $\#(S^1)_p$ is invertible in the ground ring $R$. Then there exists an $S^1$-invariant neighborhood $S^1p\subseteq K\subseteq X$ so that the Euler class $e(K)\in H^2_{S^1}(K)$ vanishes.
nodes.statement_short: Near an orbit with finite stabilizer of invertible order, the Euler class of a small invariant neighborhood vanishes.
assumptions: Let $X$ be a locally compact Hausdorff $S^1$-space which is almost free at $p\in X$, and suppose that the order of the stabilizer $\#(S^1)_p$ is invertible in the ground ring $R$.
conclusions: Then there exists an $S^1$-invariant neighborhood $S^1p\subseteq K\subseteq X$ so that the Euler class $e(K)\in H^2_{S^1}(K)$ vanishes.
nodes.label: freeactionislocallytrivial

nodes.name: Proof
nodes.statement: Apply the Tietze extension theorem to the identity map $S^1p\to S^1p$ to obtain an $S^1$-invariant neighborhood $K$ of $S^1p$ and a retraction $r:K\to S^1p$. By averaging and passing to a smaller neighborhood, we may assume without loss of generality that $r$ is $S^1$-equivariant. Now by the naturality of the Euler class, we have $e(K)=r^\ast e(S^1p)$. Thus it suffices to show that $e(S^1p)\in H^2_{S^1}(S^1p)$ vanishes. Now we have $H^2_{S^1}(S^1p)=H^2_{(S^1)_p}(p)=H^2((S^1)_p)$, where the latter is the group cohomology of the finite stabilizer group $(S^1)_p$. It is a standard fact that the group cohomology of a finite group is annihilated by the order of the group. Hence our assumption that $\#(S^1)_p$ is invertible in $R$ guarantees that this cohomology group vanishes.
nodes.statement_short: Retract an invariant neighborhood equivariantly onto the orbit; the Euler class pulls back from $H^2((S^1)_p)$, group cohomology of a finite group, which is killed by its order.

nodes.name: Equivariant local homology at an almost free orbit
nodes.statement: Let $M$ be a topological $S^1$-manifold of dimension $d$ which is almost free near $p\in M$. Suppose that $\#(S^1)_p$ is invertible in the ground ring $R$. Then there is a canonical isomorphism: \begin{equation} H_\bullet^{S^1}(M,M\setminus S^1p)=\begin{cases}H^1(S^1p;\mathfrak o_M)&\bullet=d-1\cr 0&\bullet\ne d-1\end{cases} \end{equation} (note also that $H^1(S^1p;\mathfrak o_M)=H^0(S^1p;\mathfrak o_M\otimes\mathfrak o_{S^1p}^\vee)$).
nodes.statement_short: For an $S^1$-manifold almost free near $p$, $H^{S^1}_\bullet(M,M\setminus S^1p)$ is concentrated in degree $d-1$, equal to $H^1(S^1p;\mathfrak o_M)$.
assumptions: Let $M$ be a topological $S^1$-manifold of dimension $d$ which is almost free near $p\in M$.
Suppose that $\#(S^1)_p$ is invertible in the ground ring $R$.
conclusions: Then there is a canonical isomorphism:
nodes.label: SSmanifoldPDbase

nodes.name: Equivariant local homology at an orbit
nodes.statement: H_\bullet^{S^1}(M,M\setminus S^1p)=\begin{cases}H^1(S^1p;\mathfrak o_M)&\bullet=d-1\cr 0&\bullet\ne d-1\end{cases}

nodes.name: Proof
nodes.statement: By Poincar\'e duality, we have canonical isomorphisms: \begin{equation} H_\bullet(M,M\setminus S^1p)=\begin{cases}H^0(S^1p;\mathfrak o_M)&\bullet=d\cr H^1(S^1p;\mathfrak o_M)&\bullet=d-1\cr 0&\text{otherwise}\end{cases} \end{equation} By excision and Lemma \ref{freeactionislocallytrivial}, the Gysin sequence reduces to a short exact sequence: \begin{equation} 0\to H_{\bullet-1}^{S^1}(M,M\setminus S^1p)\xrightarrow{\pi^!}H_\bullet(M,M\setminus S^1p)\xrightarrow{\pi_\ast}H_\bullet^{S^1}(M,M\setminus S^1p)\to 0 \end{equation} Combining this with \eqref{PDforSSPD}, we see that $H_\bullet^{S^1}(M,M\setminus S^1p)=0$ for $\bullet\ne d-1$, and that the following are both isomorphisms: \begin{equation} H_{d-1}(M,M\setminus S^1p)\xrightarrow{\pi_\ast}H_{d-1}^{S^1}(M,M\setminus S^1p)\xrightarrow{\pi^!}H_d(M,M\setminus S^1p) \end{equation} which yields the desired result.
nodes.statement_short: Combine Poincaré duality for $H_\bullet(M,M\setminus S^1p)$ with the Gysin sequence, which becomes short exact since the Euler class vanishes locally.

nodes.name: Poincaré duality for local homology at an orbit
nodes.statement: H_\bullet(M,M\setminus S^1p)=\begin{cases}H^0(S^1p;\mathfrak o_M)&\bullet=d\cr H^1(S^1p;\mathfrak o_M)&\bullet=d-1\cr 0&\text{otherwise}\end{cases}
nodes.label: PDforSSPD

nodes.name: Reduced Gysin short exact sequence at an orbit
nodes.statement: 0\to H_{\bullet-1}^{S^1}(M,M\setminus S^1p)\xrightarrow{\pi^!}H_\bullet(M,M\setminus S^1p)\xrightarrow{\pi_\ast}H_\bullet^{S^1}(M,M\setminus S^1p)\to 0
nodes.label: reducedgysinserreforSSPD

nodes.name: Gysin composition isomorphisms
nodes.statement: H_{d-1}(M,M\setminus S^1p)\xrightarrow{\pi_\ast}H_{d-1}^{S^1}(M,M\setminus S^1p)\xrightarrow{\pi^!}H_d(M,M\setminus S^1p)
nodes.label: gysinweirdcomposition

nodes.name: $S^1$-equivariant implicit atlas
nodes.statement: Let $X$ be an $S^1$-space. An \emph{$S^1$-equivariant implicit atlas} $A$ on $X$ is an implicit atlas $A$ along with an action of $S^1$ on each thickening $X_I$ (commuting with the $\Gamma_I$-action) such that each map $\psi_{IJ}$ is $S^1$-equivariant, each function $s_\alpha$ is $S^1$-invariant, and each subset $X_I^\mathrm{reg}$ is $S^1$-invariant. Similarly, we define an $S^1$-equivariant implicit atlas with boundary and/or stratification by in addition requiring that the boundary loci $\partial X_I$ and/or stratifications $X_I\to\mathcal S$ be $S^1$-invariant.
nodes.statement_short: An implicit atlas with $S^1$-actions on all thickenings commuting with $\Gamma_I$, with equivariant footprint maps, invariant Kuranishi maps and invariant regular loci.
differentia: along with an action of $S^1$ on each thickening $X_I$ (commuting with the $\Gamma_I$-action) such that each map $\psi_{IJ}$ is $S^1$-equivariant, each function $s_\alpha$ is $S^1$-invariant, and each subset $X_I^\mathrm{reg}$ is $S^1$-invariant.
nodes.label: SSimplicitatlasdef

nodes.statement: Note that in the above definition, $S^1$ does not act on any of the obstruction spaces $E_\alpha$ (or, alternatively, it acts trivially on them).
nodes.name: $S^1$ acts trivially on obstruction spaces

nodes.statement: We begin with the trivial observation that if $X$ is equipped with a locally orientable $S^1$-equivariant implicit atlas $A$, then the $S^1$-action on $X$ lifts canonically to the orientation sheaf $\mathfrak o_X$.
nodes.name: $S^1$-action lifts to the orientation sheaf
assumptions: if $X$ is equipped with a locally orientable $S^1$-equivariant implicit atlas $A$
conclusions: the $S^1$-action on $X$ lifts canonically to the orientation sheaf $\mathfrak o_X$

nodes.name: Locally $S^1$-orientable implicit atlas
nodes.statement: Let $X$ be an $S^1$-space with $S^1$-equivariant implicit atlas with boundary. We say that $A$ is \emph{locally $S^1$-orientable} iff it is locally orientable and for all $p\in X$, the stabilizer $(S^1)_p$ acts trivially on $(\mathfrak o_X)_p$ (this action is always by a sign $(S^1)_p\to\{\pm 1\}$). This notion is independent of the ring $R$ (due to our restriction that $\#(S^1)_p$ be invertible in $R$).
nodes.statement_short: A locally orientable $S^1$-equivariant atlas where each stabilizer $(S^1)_p$ acts trivially on the orientation stalk $(\mathfrak o_X)_p$.
differentia: for all $p\in X$, the stabilizer $(S^1)_p$ acts trivially on $(\mathfrak o_X)_p$
nodes.label: virtualorSS

nodes.statement: It is easy to see that if $A$ is locally $S^1$-orientable, then $\pi_\ast\mathfrak o_X$ is locally isomorphic to the constant sheaf $\underline R$ (where $\pi:X\to X/S^1$).
nodes.name: $\pi_\ast\mathfrak o_X$ is locally constant
assumptions: if $A$ is locally $S^1$-orientable
conclusions: $\pi_\ast\mathfrak o_X$ is locally isomorphic to the constant sheaf $\underline R$

nodes.name: Oriented atlases are locally $S^1$-orientable
nodes.statement: If $A$ is locally orientable and $\mathfrak o_X$ has a global section, then $A$ is automatically locally $S^1$-orientable ($S^1$ is connected, so the section must be $S^1$-invariant, hence the claim).
nodes.statement_short: If $\mathfrak o_X$ has a global section, connectedness of $S^1$ forces it to be invariant, so $A$ is locally $S^1$-orientable.
nodes.label: orientedthenSSoriented

nodes.name: Chain models unnecessary with $\infty$-categories (equivariant chains)
nodes.statement: If we used the language of $\infty$-categories, there would be no need to construct models of chains with good (chain level) functoriality properties (c.f.\ Remark \ref{independenceofchainmodel}).
nodes.section: 8.4 \texorpdfstring{$S^1$}{S{\textasciicircum}1}-equivariant virtual cochain complexes \texorpdfstring{$C^\bullet_{S^1,\mathrm{vir}}(X;A)$}{C\_S{\textasciicircum}1,vir(X;A)} and \texorpdfstring{$C^\bullet_{S^1,\mathrm{vir}}(X\operatorname{rel}\partial;A)$}{C\_S{\textasciicircum}1,vir(X rel d;A)}

nodes.statement: We want a functor $C_\bullet^{S^1}$ from spaces to chain complexes of free $\mathbb Z$-modules (and then we can tensor up to any base ring $R$); we also demand that $C_\bullet^{S^1}(A)\to C_\bullet^{S^1}(X)$ be injective for $A\subseteq X$ (and then we define relative chains $C_\bullet^{S^1}(X,A)$ as the cokernel). Now we need there to be functorial maps: \begin{align} C_\bullet^{S^1}(X)&\xrightarrow{\pi^!}C_{\bullet+1}(X)\\ C_\bullet^{S^1}(X)\otimes C_\bullet(Y)&\to C_\bullet^{S^1}(X\times Y) \end{align} realizing (respectively) the Gysin map and the obvious product map. The map \eqref{chainproducteq2} must be compatible with the Eilenberg--Zilber map on $C_\bullet$ in that the two ways of building up the following map coincide: \begin{equation} C_\bullet^{S^1}(X)\otimes C_\bullet(Y)\otimes C_\bullet(Z)\to C_\bullet^{S^1}(X\times Y\times Z) \end{equation} Moreover, \eqref{pishriek} and \eqref{chainproducteq2} must be compatible in that the following diagram commutes: \begin{equation} \begin{CD} C_\bullet^{S^1}(X)\otimes C_\bullet(Y)@>>>C_\bullet^{S^1}(X\times Y)\cr @VVV@VVV\cr C_{\bullet+1}(X)\otimes C_\bullet(Y)@>>>C_{\bullet+1}(X\times Y)\cr \end{CD} \end{equation}
nodes.name: Required properties of a model $C^{S^1}_\bullet$ of equivariant chains
nodes.statement_short: A functor to free chain complexes, injective on subspaces, with Gysin maps $\pi^!$ and products with $C_\bullet$ compatible with Eilenberg--Zilber and with each other.
nodes.section: 8.4 \texorpdfstring{$S^1$}{S{\textasciicircum}1}-equivariant virtual cochain complexes \texorpdfstring{$C^\bullet_{S^1,\mathrm{vir}}(X;A)$}{C\_S{\textasciicircum}1,vir(X;A)} and \texorpdfstring{$C^\bullet_{S^1,\mathrm{vir}}(X\operatorname{rel}\partial;A)$}{C\_S{\textasciicircum}1,vir(X rel d;A)}

nodes.name: Gysin map and product map on equivariant chains
nodes.statement: C_\bullet^{S^1}(X)&\xrightarrow{\pi^!}C_{\bullet+1}(X)\\ C_\bullet^{S^1}(X)\otimes C_\bullet(Y)&\to C_\bullet^{S^1}(X\times Y)
nodes.section: 8.4 \texorpdfstring{$S^1$}{S{\textasciicircum}1}-equivariant virtual cochain complexes \texorpdfstring{$C^\bullet_{S^1,\mathrm{vir}}(X;A)$}{C\_S{\textasciicircum}1,vir(X;A)} and \texorpdfstring{$C^\bullet_{S^1,\mathrm{vir}}(X\operatorname{rel}\partial;A)$}{C\_S{\textasciicircum}1,vir(X rel d;A)}
nodes.label: pishriek

nodes.name: Triple product compatibility for equivariant chains
nodes.statement: C_\bullet^{S^1}(X)\otimes C_\bullet(Y)\otimes C_\bullet(Z)\to C_\bullet^{S^1}(X\times Y\times Z)
nodes.section: 8.4 \texorpdfstring{$S^1$}{S{\textasciicircum}1}-equivariant virtual cochain complexes \texorpdfstring{$C^\bullet_{S^1,\mathrm{vir}}(X;A)$}{C\_S{\textasciicircum}1,vir(X;A)} and \texorpdfstring{$C^\bullet_{S^1,\mathrm{vir}}(X\operatorname{rel}\partial;A)$}{C\_S{\textasciicircum}1,vir(X rel d;A)}

nodes.name: Compatibility of Gysin and product maps
nodes.statement: \begin{CD} C_\bullet^{S^1}(X)\otimes C_\bullet(Y)@>>>C_\bullet^{S^1}(X\times Y)\cr @VVV@VVV\cr C_{\bullet+1}(X)\otimes C_\bullet(Y)@>>>C_{\bullet+1}(X\times Y)\cr \end{CD}
nodes.section: 8.4 \texorpdfstring{$S^1$}{S{\textasciicircum}1}-equivariant virtual cochain complexes \texorpdfstring{$C^\bullet_{S^1,\mathrm{vir}}(X;A)$}{C\_S{\textasciicircum}1,vir(X;A)} and \texorpdfstring{$C^\bullet_{S^1,\mathrm{vir}}(X\operatorname{rel}\partial;A)$}{C\_S{\textasciicircum}1,vir(X rel d;A)}

nodes.statement: For a Serre fibration $\pi:E\to B$, we consider diagrams of the form: \begin{equation} \begin{CD} \Delta^p\times\Delta^q@>>>E\cr @VVV@VV\pi V\cr \Delta^p@>>>B \end{CD} \end{equation} Let $C_{p,q}(\pi:E\to B)$ denote the free abelian group generated by such diagrams.
nodes.name: Dress complex $C_{p,q}(\pi:E\to B)$
nodes.section: 8.4 \texorpdfstring{$S^1$}{S{\textasciicircum}1}-equivariant virtual cochain complexes \texorpdfstring{$C^\bullet_{S^1,\mathrm{vir}}(X;A)$}{C\_S{\textasciicircum}1,vir(X;A)} and \texorpdfstring{$C^\bullet_{S^1,\mathrm{vir}}(X\operatorname{rel}\partial;A)$}{C\_S{\textasciicircum}1,vir(X rel d;A)}

nodes.name: Dress diagram for a Serre fibration
nodes.statement: \begin{CD} \Delta^p\times\Delta^q@>>>E\cr @VVV@VV\pi V\cr \Delta^p@>>>B \end{CD}
nodes.section: 8.4 \texorpdfstring{$S^1$}{S{\textasciicircum}1}-equivariant virtual cochain complexes \texorpdfstring{$C^\bullet_{S^1,\mathrm{vir}}(X;A)$}{C\_S{\textasciicircum}1,vir(X;A)} and \texorpdfstring{$C^\bullet_{S^1,\mathrm{vir}}(X\operatorname{rel}\partial;A)$}{C\_S{\textasciicircum}1,vir(X rel d;A)}

nodes.statement: Then the direct sum of all of these $C_{\bullet,\bullet}(\pi:E\to B)$ is a double complex (differentials corresponding to the two pieces of boundary $\partial\Delta^p\times\Delta^q$ and $\Delta^p\times\partial\Delta^q$). We let $C_\bullet(\pi:E\to B)$ denote the corresponding total complex.
nodes.name: Total Dress complex $C_\bullet(\pi:E\to B)$
nodes.section: 8.4 \texorpdfstring{$S^1$}{S{\textasciicircum}1}-equivariant virtual cochain complexes \texorpdfstring{$C^\bullet_{S^1,\mathrm{vir}}(X;A)$}{C\_S{\textasciicircum}1,vir(X;A)} and \texorpdfstring{$C^\bullet_{S^1,\mathrm{vir}}(X\operatorname{rel}\partial;A)$}{C\_S{\textasciicircum}1,vir(X rel d;A)}

nodes.statement: There is a natural map $C_\bullet(\pi:E\to B)\to C_\bullet(E)$, where we subdivide $\Delta^p\times\Delta^q$ in the usual way. By considering the spectral sequence associated to the filtration by $q$, Dress showed that this map is a quasi-isomorphism. Dress also showed that the spectral sequence associated to the filtration by $p$ is the Serre spectral sequence; in particular, the $E^2_{p,q}$ term is $H_p(B,H_q(F))$.
nodes.name: Dress's construction of the Serre spectral sequence
nodes.statement_short: The natural map from the Dress complex of a Serre fibration to $C_\bullet(E)$ is a quasi-isomorphism, and the $p$-filtration spectral sequence is the Serre spectral sequence.
assumptions: There is a natural map $C_\bullet(\pi:E\to B)\to C_\bullet(E)$, where we subdivide $\Delta^p\times\Delta^q$ in the usual way.
conclusions: Dress showed that this map is a quasi-isomorphism.
Dress also showed that the spectral sequence associated to the filtration by $p$ is the Serre spectral sequence; in particular, the $E^2_{p,q}$ term is $H_p(B,H_q(F))$.
nodes.section: 8.4 \texorpdfstring{$S^1$}{S{\textasciicircum}1}-equivariant virtual cochain complexes \texorpdfstring{$C^\bullet_{S^1,\mathrm{vir}}(X;A)$}{C\_S{\textasciicircum}1,vir(X;A)} and \texorpdfstring{$C^\bullet_{S^1,\mathrm{vir}}(X\operatorname{rel}\partial;A)$}{C\_S{\textasciicircum}1,vir(X rel d;A)}

nodes.statement: To define $C_\bullet^{S^1}$, fix once and for all an $ES^1$. Then for any space $X$, the map $\pi:X\times ES^1\to(X\times ES^1)/S^1$ is a principal $S^1$-bundle, so \emph{a fortiori} it is a Serre fibration. We define: \begin{multline} C_{\bullet-1}^{S^1}(X):=\Bigl\{\gamma\in C_\bullet(\pi:X\times ES^1\to(X\times ES^1)/S^1)\Bigm|\\ \gamma,d\gamma\text{ have no component with $q$-degree}<1\Bigr\} \end{multline}
nodes.name: Model $C^{S^1}_\bullet$ of $S^1$-equivariant chains
nodes.statement_short: Equivariant chains are the Dress chains of $X\times ES^1\to(X\times ES^1)/S^1$ having (with their boundary) no component of $q$-degree $<1$, shifted by one.
nodes.section: 8.4 \texorpdfstring{$S^1$}{S{\textasciicircum}1}-equivariant virtual cochain complexes \texorpdfstring{$C^\bullet_{S^1,\mathrm{vir}}(X;A)$}{C\_S{\textasciicircum}1,vir(X;A)} and \texorpdfstring{$C^\bullet_{S^1,\mathrm{vir}}(X\operatorname{rel}\partial;A)$}{C\_S{\textasciicircum}1,vir(X rel d;A)}

nodes.name: Definition of $C^{S^1}_{\bullet-1}(X)$ via $q$-degree
nodes.statement: C_{\bullet-1}^{S^1}(X):=\Bigl\{\gamma\in C_\bullet(\pi:X\times ES^1\to(X\times ES^1)/S^1)\Bigm|\\ \gamma,d\gamma\text{ have no component with $q$-degree}<1\Bigr\}
nodes.section: 8.4 \texorpdfstring{$S^1$}{S{\textasciicircum}1}-equivariant virtual cochain complexes \texorpdfstring{$C^\bullet_{S^1,\mathrm{vir}}(X;A)$}{C\_S{\textasciicircum}1,vir(X;A)} and \texorpdfstring{$C^\bullet_{S^1,\mathrm{vir}}(X\operatorname{rel}\partial;A)$}{C\_S{\textasciicircum}1,vir(X rel d;A)}
nodes.label: qdegreedef

nodes.statement: The inclusion $C_{\bullet-1}^{S^1}(X)\hookrightarrow C_\bullet(\pi:X\times ES^1\to(X\times ES^1)/S^1)$ is compatible with the $p$-grading on each. Let us consider the associated morphism of spectral sequences (induced by the $p$-filtration). The latter has $E^2_{p,q}$ term $H_p^{S^1}(X,H_q(S^1))$ by Dress. It follows from the definition \eqref{qdegreedef} that the $E^2_{p,q}$ term of the former is the same in degrees $q\geq 1$ and zero otherwise. Since $H_q(S^1)$ is nonzero only for $q\leq 1$, it follows that the former spectral sequence has no further differentials, and we conclude that the homology of $C_\bullet^{S^1}(X)$ is indeed $H_\bullet^{S^1}(X)$ as needed.
nodes.name: $C^{S^1}_\bullet$ computes equivariant homology
nodes.statement_short: Comparing $p$-filtration spectral sequences (Dress) shows the homology of $C^{S^1}_\bullet(X)$ is $H^{S^1}_\bullet(X)$.
nodes.section: 8.4 \texorpdfstring{$S^1$}{S{\textasciicircum}1}-equivariant virtual cochain complexes \texorpdfstring{$C^\bullet_{S^1,\mathrm{vir}}(X;A)$}{C\_S{\textasciicircum}1,vir(X;A)} and \texorpdfstring{$C^\bullet_{S^1,\mathrm{vir}}(X\operatorname{rel}\partial;A)$}{C\_S{\textasciicircum}1,vir(X rel d;A)}

nodes.statement: The map \eqref{pishriek} is obtained by the standard subdivision of $\Delta^p\times\Delta^q$ into simplices along with the projection map $X\times ES^1\to X$.
nodes.name: Gysin map $\pi^!$ on $C^{S^1}_\bullet$
nodes.section: 8.4 \texorpdfstring{$S^1$}{S{\textasciicircum}1}-equivariant virtual cochain complexes \texorpdfstring{$C^\bullet_{S^1,\mathrm{vir}}(X;A)$}{C\_S{\textasciicircum}1,vir(X;A)} and \texorpdfstring{$C^\bullet_{S^1,\mathrm{vir}}(X\operatorname{rel}\partial;A)$}{C\_S{\textasciicircum}1,vir(X rel d;A)}

nodes.statement: The map \eqref{chainproducteq2} is defined as follows. Given maps $\Delta^p\times\Delta^q\to X\times ES^1$ and $\Delta^{p'}\to Y$, we obtain a map $\Delta^{p'}\times\Delta^p\times\Delta^q\to Y\times X\times ES^1$ and we subdivide $\Delta^{p'}\times\Delta^p$.
nodes.name: Product map on $C^{S^1}_\bullet$
nodes.section: 8.4 \texorpdfstring{$S^1$}{S{\textasciicircum}1}-equivariant virtual cochain complexes \texorpdfstring{$C^\bullet_{S^1,\mathrm{vir}}(X;A)$}{C\_S{\textasciicircum}1,vir(X;A)} and \texorpdfstring{$C^\bullet_{S^1,\mathrm{vir}}(X\operatorname{rel}\partial;A)$}{C\_S{\textasciicircum}1,vir(X rel d;A)}

nodes.name: $S^1$-equivariant virtual cochain complexes $C_{S^1,\mathrm{vir}}^\bullet(-;A)$
nodes.statement: Let $X$ be an $S^1$-space with finite $S^1$-equivariant implicit atlas with boundary $A$. For any $S^1$-invariant compact $K\subseteq X$, we define: \begin{align} C^\bullet_{S^1,\mathrm{vir}}(K;A)_{IJ}\quad&C^\bullet_{S^1,\mathrm{vir}}(K\operatorname{rel}\partial;A)_{IJ}\\ C^\bullet_{S^1,\mathrm{vir}}(K;A)\phantom{_{IJ}}\quad&C^\bullet_{S^1,\mathrm{vir}}(K\operatorname{rel}\partial;A) \end{align} as in Definitions \ref{CSTcomplexdef}--\ref{Ccomplexdef}, except using $C_{\bullet-1}^{S^1}$ in place of $C_\bullet$ in \eqref{CcomplexcriticaldefI}--\eqref{CcomplexcriticaldefII}. It is clear that \eqref{bigSSpartial}--\eqref{bigSS} are complexes of $\mathcal K$-presheaves on $X/S^1$ (replace $K$ with $\pi^{-1}(K)$, where $\pi:X\to X/S^1$). The Gysin map \eqref{pishriek} induces ``comparison maps'': \begin{equation} C^\bullet_{S^1,\mathrm{vir}}(-;A)_{(IJ)}\to C^\bullet_\mathrm{vir}(-;A)_{(IJ)} \end{equation} for all flavors \eqref{bigSSpartial}--\eqref{bigSS} Analogously with \eqref{Erelpartialpullback}--\eqref{Epushforward1} and \eqref{Frelpartialpullback}--\eqref{Fpushforward}, there are natural maps (compatible with \eqref{CSStimesSS}): \begin{align} C^\bullet_{S^1,\mathrm{vir}}(K\operatorname{rel}\partial;A)_{IJ}&\to C^\bullet_{S^1,\mathrm{vir}}(K;A)_{IJ}\\ C^{d+\bullet}_{S^1,\mathrm{vir}}(X\operatorname{rel}\partial;A)_{IJ}&\xrightarrow{s_\ast}C_{-\bullet-1}^{S^1}(E;A)\\ C^\bullet_{S^1,\mathrm{vir}}(-;A)_{IJ}&\to C^\bullet_{S^1,\mathrm{vir}}(-;A)_{I',J'}\\ C^\bullet_{S^1,\mathrm{vir}}(K\operatorname{rel}\partial;A)&\to C^\bullet_{S^1,\mathrm{vir}}(K;A)\\ C^{d+\bullet}_{S^1,\mathrm{vir}}(X\operatorname{rel}\partial;A)&\xrightarrow{s_\ast}C_{-\bullet-1}^{S^1}(E;A) \end{align} Analogously with \eqref{Epushforward1more}--\eqref{Fpushforward1}, there are natural maps (compatible with \eqref{CSStimesSS}): \begin{align} C^\bullet_{S^1,\mathrm{vir}}(-;A)_{IJ}\otimes C_{-\bullet}(E;A'\setminus A)&\to C^\bullet_{S^1,\mathrm{vir}}(-;A')_{I',J'}\\ C^\bullet_{S^1,\mathrm{vir}}(-;A)\otimes C_{-\bullet}(E;A'\setminus A)&\to C^\bullet_{S^1,\mathrm{vir}}(-;A') \end{align}
nodes.section: 8.4 \texorpdfstring{$S^1$}{S{\textasciicircum}1}-equivariant virtual cochain complexes \texorpdfstring{$C^\bullet_{S^1,\mathrm{vir}}(X;A)$}{C\_S{\textasciicircum}1,vir(X;A)} and \texorpdfstring{$C^\bullet_{S^1,\mathrm{vir}}(X\operatorname{rel}\partial;A)$}{C\_S{\textasciicircum}1,vir(X rel d;A)}
nodes.statement_short: Define $C^\bullet_{S^1,\mathrm{vir}}$ (and rel $\partial$, and $_{IJ}$ versions) as for $C^\bullet_\mathrm{vir}$ but with $C^{S^1}_{\bullet-1}$ in place of $C_\bullet$, with comparison, pushforward and product maps.

nodes.name: $S^1$-equivariant virtual cochain complexes (flavors)
nodes.statement: C^\bullet_{S^1,\mathrm{vir}}(K;A)_{IJ}\quad&C^\bullet_{S^1,\mathrm{vir}}(K\operatorname{rel}\partial;A)_{IJ}\\ C^\bullet_{S^1,\mathrm{vir}}(K;A)\phantom{_{IJ}}\quad&C^\bullet_{S^1,\mathrm{vir}}(K\operatorname{rel}\partial;A)
nodes.section: 8.4 \texorpdfstring{$S^1$}{S{\textasciicircum}1}-equivariant virtual cochain complexes \texorpdfstring{$C^\bullet_{S^1,\mathrm{vir}}(X;A)$}{C\_S{\textasciicircum}1,vir(X;A)} and \texorpdfstring{$C^\bullet_{S^1,\mathrm{vir}}(X\operatorname{rel}\partial;A)$}{C\_S{\textasciicircum}1,vir(X rel d;A)}
nodes.label: bigSSpartial

nodes.statement: C^\bullet_{S^1,\mathrm{vir}}(-;A)_{(IJ)}\to C^\bullet_\mathrm{vir}(-;A)_{(IJ)}

nodes.name: $C^\bullet_{S^1,\mathrm{vir}}(-;A)_{IJ}$ are pure homotopy $\mathcal K$-sheaves
nodes.statement: Let $X$ be an almost free $S^1$-space with finite locally $S^1$-orientable $S^1$-equivariant implicit atlas with boundary $A$. Then $C^\bullet_{S^1,\mathrm{vir}}(-;A)_{IJ}$ and $C^\bullet_{S^1,\mathrm{vir}}(-\operatorname{rel}\partial;A)_{IJ}$ are pure homotopy $\mathcal K$-sheaves on $X/S^1$. Furthermore, there are canonical isomorphisms of sheaves on $X/S^1$: \begin{align} H^0_{S^1,\mathrm{vir}}(-;A)_{IJ}&=\pi_\ast j_!j^\ast\mathfrak o_X\\ H^0_{S^1,\mathrm{vir}}(-\operatorname{rel}\partial;A)_{IJ}&=\pi_\ast j_!j^\ast\mathfrak o_{X\operatorname{rel}\partial} \end{align} where $j:V_I\cap V_J\hookrightarrow X$ for $V_I:=\psi_{\varnothing I}((s_I|X_I^\mathrm{reg})^{-1}(0))\subseteq X$ and $\pi:X\to X/S^1$.
nodes.statement_short: On an almost free $S^1$-space with locally $S^1$-orientable atlas, the equivariant complexes $_{IJ}$ are pure homotopy $\mathcal K$-sheaves on $X/S^1$ with $H^0=\pi_\ast j_!j^\ast\mathfrak o_X$.
assumptions: Let $X$ be an almost free $S^1$-space with finite locally $S^1$-orientable $S^1$-equivariant implicit atlas with boundary $A$.
conclusions: Then $C^\bullet_{S^1,\mathrm{vir}}(-;A)_{IJ}$ and $C^\bullet_{S^1,\mathrm{vir}}(-\operatorname{rel}\partial;A)_{IJ}$ are pure homotopy $\mathcal K$-sheaves on $X/S^1$.
Furthermore, there are canonical isomorphisms of sheaves on $X/S^1$:
nodes.label: CSTpureSS

nodes.name: $H^0$ of $C^\bullet_{S^1,\mathrm{vir}}(-;A)_{IJ}$
nodes.statement: H^0_{S^1,\mathrm{vir}}(-;A)_{IJ}&=\pi_\ast j_!j^\ast\mathfrak o_X\\ H^0_{S^1,\mathrm{vir}}(-\operatorname{rel}\partial;A)_{IJ}&=\pi_\ast j_!j^\ast\mathfrak o_{X\operatorname{rel}\partial}

nodes.name: Proof
nodes.statement: As in the proof of Lemma \ref{CSTpure}, we use Lemmas \ref{singularchainshomotopyKsheaf} and \ref{associatedgradedhomotopysheaf} to see that $C^\bullet_{S^1,\mathrm{vir}}(-;A)_{IJ}$ and $C^\bullet_{S^1,\mathrm{vir}}(-\operatorname{rel}\partial;A)_{IJ}$ are homotopy $\mathcal K$-sheaves. More precisely, in the present context we need the statement of Lemma \ref{singularchainshomotopyKsheaf} for $C_\bullet^{S^1}$ in place of $C_\bullet$. The proof of this lemma applies equally well to $C_\bullet^{S^1}$, noting that since $C_\bullet^{S^1}$ is a model of $S^1$-equivariant chains, it in particular satisfies Mayer--Vietoris in that following (total complex) is acyclic: \begin{equation} C_\bullet^{S^1}(U\cap U')\to C_\bullet^{S^1}(U)\oplus C_\bullet^{S^1}(U')\to C_\bullet^{S^1}(U\cup U') \end{equation} Now let us show purity. By Lemma \ref{openclosedpurity}, it suffices to show that the restrictions of $C^\bullet_{S^1,\mathrm{vir}}(-;A)_{IJ}$ and $C^\bullet_{S^1,\mathrm{vir}}(-\operatorname{rel}\partial;A)_{IJ}$ to $(V_I\cap V_J)/S^1$ and to $X/S^1\setminus(V_I\cap V_J)/S^1$ are pure. The latter restriction is trivially pure, since both complexes are simply zero for $K\cap V_I\cap V_J=\varnothing$. Hence it suffices to show that the restrictions of both complexes to $(V_I\cap V_J)/S^1$ are pure. We consider the comparison maps: \begin{align} H^\bullet_{S^1,\mathrm{vir}}(K;A)_{IJ}&\to H^\bullet_\mathrm{vir}(K;A)_{IJ}\\ H^\bullet_{S^1,\mathrm{vir}}(K\operatorname{rel}\partial;A)_{IJ}&\to H^\bullet_\mathrm{vir}(K\operatorname{rel}\partial;A)_{IJ} \end{align} These are Gysin maps $\pi^!$, and hence by the Gysin sequence, their kernels coincide (respectively) with the images of: \begin{align} H^{\bullet-2}_{S^1,\mathrm{vir}}(K;A)_{IJ}&\xrightarrow{\cap e}H^\bullet_{S^1,\mathrm{vir}}(K;A)_{IJ}\\ H^{\bullet-2}_{S^1,\mathrm{vir}}(K\operatorname{rel}\partial;A)_{IJ}&\xrightarrow{\cap e}H^\bullet_{S^1,\mathrm{vir}}(K\operatorname{rel}\partial;A)_{IJ} \end{align} where $e$ is (the pullback of) $e\in H^2_{S^1}(X_J^\mathrm{reg}/\Gamma_J)$. Pick any $p\in V_J\subseteq X$. By Lemma \ref{freeactionislocallytrivial}, this $e$ vanishes when restricted to small $S^1$-invariant compact neighborhoods of $S^1p\subseteq V_J=(s_J|X_J^\mathrm{reg})^{-1}(0)/\Gamma_J\subseteq X_J^\mathrm{reg}/\Gamma_J$. It follows that \eqref{HSTzero}--\eqref{HSTzerorel} vanish for small $S^1$-invariant compact neighborhoods $K$ of $S^1p\subseteq V_J$. Hence \eqref{HSTinjective}--\eqref{HSTinjectiverel} are injective for such $K$. Now, using this injectivity and the fact that $C^\bullet_\mathrm{vir}(-;A)_{IJ}$ and $C^\bullet_\mathrm{vir}(-\operatorname{rel}\partial;A)_{IJ}$ are pure homotopy $\mathcal K$-sheaves (Lemma \ref{CSTpure}), it follows that $C^\bullet_{S^1,\mathrm{vir}}(-;A)_{IJ}$ and $C^\bullet_{S^1,\mathrm{vir}}(-\operatorname{rel}\partial;A)_{IJ}$ are pure on $V_J/S^1$, and hence on all of $X/S^1$. It remains to identify $H^0_{S^1,\mathrm{vir}}(-;A)_{IJ}$ and $H^0_{S^1,\mathrm{vir}}(-\operatorname{rel}\partial;A)_{IJ}$. Consider the comparison maps: \begin{align} H^0_{S^1,\mathrm{vir}}(-;A)_{IJ}&\to\pi_\ast H^0_\mathrm{vir}(-;A)_{IJ}\\ H^0_{S^1,\mathrm{vir}}(-\operatorname{rel}\partial;A)_{IJ}&\to\pi_\ast H^0_\mathrm{vir}(-\operatorname{rel}\partial;A)_{IJ} \end{align} which are maps of sheaves on $X/S^1$. It suffices (by Lemma \ref{CSTpure}) to show that these are isomorphisms (which we will check on stalks, i.e.\ for $K=S^1p$). Now this is just a calculation, similar to that in the proof of Lemma \ref{CSTpure}, except using an $S^1$-equivariant version of Poincar\'e--Lefschetz duality based on Lemma \ref{SSmanifoldPDbase} in place of Lemma \ref{poincareduality} (and it is in this calculation where we use the local $S^1$-orientability of $A$).
nodes.statement_short: Homotopy-sheaf property as for $C_\mathrm{vir}$ (Mayer--Vietoris for $C^{S^1}_\bullet$); purity via injectivity of Gysin comparison maps, since the Euler class vanishes locally. $H^0$ identified by an equivariant Poincaré--Lefschetz calculation.

nodes.name: Mayer--Vietoris for equivariant chains
nodes.statement: C_\bullet^{S^1}(U\cap U')\to C_\bullet^{S^1}(U)\oplus C_\bullet^{S^1}(U')\to C_\bullet^{S^1}(U\cup U')

nodes.name: $C^\bullet_{S^1,\mathrm{vir}}(-;A)$ are pure homotopy $\mathcal K$-sheaves
nodes.statement: Let $X$ be an almost free $S^1$-space with finite locally $S^1$-orientable $S^1$-equivariant implicit atlas with boundary $A$. Then $C^\bullet_{S^1,\mathrm{vir}}(-;A)$ and $C^\bullet_{S^1,\mathrm{vir}}(-\operatorname{rel}\partial;A)$ are pure homotopy $\mathcal K$-sheaves on $X/S^1$. Furthermore, there are canonical isomorphisms of sheaves on $X/S^1$: \begin{align} H^0_{S^1,\mathrm{vir}}(-;A)&=\pi_\ast\mathfrak o_X\\ H^0_{S^1,\mathrm{vir}}(-\operatorname{rel}\partial;A)&=\pi_\ast\mathfrak o_{X\operatorname{rel}\partial} \end{align} where $\pi:X\to X/S^1$.
nodes.statement_short: The equivariant virtual cochain complexes are pure homotopy $\mathcal K$-sheaves on $X/S^1$ with $H^0=\pi_\ast\mathfrak o_X$ (resp. rel $\partial$).
assumptions: Let $X$ be an almost free $S^1$-space with finite locally $S^1$-orientable $S^1$-equivariant implicit atlas with boundary $A$.
conclusions: Then $C^\bullet_{S^1,\mathrm{vir}}(-;A)$ and $C^\bullet_{S^1,\mathrm{vir}}(-\operatorname{rel}\partial;A)$ are pure homotopy $\mathcal K$-sheaves on $X/S^1$.
Furthermore, there are canonical isomorphisms of sheaves on $X/S^1$:
nodes.label: CpureSS
