nodes.statement: H^0_{S^1,\mathrm{vir}}(-;A)&=\pi_\ast\mathfrak o_X\\ H^0_{S^1,\mathrm{vir}}(-\operatorname{rel}\partial;A)&=\pi_\ast\mathfrak o_{X\operatorname{rel}\partial}

nodes.name: Proof
nodes.statement: This is exactly analogous to Proposition \ref{Cpure} and has the same proof (using Lemma \ref{CSTpureSS} in place of Lemma \ref{CSTpure}).
nodes.statement_short: Same proof as Proposition Cpure, using Lemma CSTpureSS in place of Lemma CSTpure.

nodes.name: Calculation of $H^\bullet_{S^1,\mathrm{vir}}$
nodes.statement: Let $X$ be an almost free $S^1$-space with finite locally $S^1$-orientable $S^1$-equivariant implicit atlas with boundary $A$. Then there are canonical isomorphisms fitting (as the top horizontal maps) into commutative diagrams: \begin{equation*} \begin{CD} H^\bullet_{S^1,\mathrm{vir}}(X;A)@>\sim>>\check H^\bullet(X/S^1,\pi_\ast\mathfrak o_X)\cr @V\eqref{CSStimesSS}VV@V\pi^\ast VV\cr H^\bullet_\mathrm{vir}(X;A)@>\text{Thm \ref{Fsheaffundamentaliso}}>>\check H^\bullet(X,\mathfrak o_X) \end{CD} \qquad \begin{CD} H^\bullet_{S^1,\mathrm{vir}}(X\operatorname{rel}\partial;A)@>\sim>>\check H^\bullet(X/S^1,\pi_\ast\mathfrak o_{X\operatorname{rel}\partial})\cr @V\eqref{CSStimesSS}VV@V\pi^\ast VV\cr H^\bullet_\mathrm{vir}(X\operatorname{rel}\partial;A)@>\text{Thm \ref{Fsheaffundamentaliso}}>>\check H^\bullet(X,\mathfrak o_{X\operatorname{rel}\partial}) \end{CD} \end{equation*}
nodes.statement_short: $H^\bullet_{S^1,\mathrm{vir}}(X;A)\cong\check H^\bullet(X/S^1;\pi_\ast\mathfrak o_X)$ (and rel $\partial$), compatibly with the non-equivariant isomorphism via $\pi^\ast$.
assumptions: Let $X$ be an almost free $S^1$-space with finite locally $S^1$-orientable $S^1$-equivariant implicit atlas with boundary $A$.
conclusions: Then there are canonical isomorphisms fitting (as the top horizontal maps) into commutative diagrams:
nodes.label: Slocalfundamentaliso

nodes.name: Proof
nodes.statement: Consider the following diagram: \begin{equation*} \begin{tikzcd} H^\bullet_{S^1,\mathrm{vir}}(X;A)\ar{d}{\sim}\ar{rr}{\eqref{CSStimesSS}}&&H^\bullet_\mathrm{vir}(X;A)\ar{d}{\sim}\\ \check H^\bullet(X/S^1;C^\bullet_{S^1,\mathrm{vir}}(-;A))\ar{r}{\eqref{CSStimesSS}}\ar{d}{\sim}&\check H^\bullet(X/S^1,\pi_\ast C^\bullet_\mathrm{vir}(-;A))\ar{r}{\pi^\ast}\ar{d}{\sim}&\check H^\bullet(X;C^\bullet_\mathrm{vir}(-;A))\ar{d}{\sim}\\ \check H^\bullet(X/S^1;\tau_{\geq 0}C^\bullet_{S^1,\mathrm{vir}}(-;A))\ar{r}{\eqref{CSStimesSS}}&\check H^\bullet(X/S^1,\pi_\ast\tau_{\geq 0}C^\bullet_\mathrm{vir}(-;A))\ar{r}{\pi^\ast}&\check H^\bullet(X;\tau_{\geq 0}C^\bullet_\mathrm{vir}(-;A))\\ \check H^\bullet(X/S^1;H^0_{S^1,\mathrm{vir}}(-;A))\ar{u}[swap]{\sim}\ar{r}{\eqref{CSStimesSS}}\ar{d}{\sim}&\check H^\bullet(X/S^1,\pi_\ast H^0_\mathrm{vir}(-;A))\ar{r}{\pi^\ast}\ar{u}\ar{d}{\sim}&\check H^\bullet(X;H^0_\mathrm{vir}(-;A))\ar{u}[swap]{\sim}\ar{d}{\sim}\\ \check H^\bullet(X/S^1;\pi_\ast\mathfrak o_X)\ar[equal]{r}&\check H^\bullet(X/S^1,\pi_\ast\mathfrak o_X)\ar{r}{\pi^\ast}&\check H^\bullet(X;\mathfrak o_X) \end{tikzcd} \end{equation*} where the vertical isomorphisms are by Propositions \ref{CpureSS} and \ref{Cpure} (see also \eqref{isosforpurehtpysheafcech}). Now each small square of this diagram above commutes (only the bottom left requires an argument; one shows that the corresponding diagram of sheaves commutes by checking it locally, where it is just a calculation). Now the first square in Theorem \ref{Slocalfundamentaliso} is the same as the big square above, which commutes by a diagram chase (for which one should be careful of the fact that one of the vertical arrows is not an isomorphism). An identical argument applies to the second square in Theorem \ref{Slocalfundamentaliso}.
nodes.statement_short: Diagram chase: a ladder of isomorphisms from purity (Propositions CpureSS and Cpure) whose small squares commute by local checks.

nodes.name: $S^1$-localization for $[X]^\mathrm{vir}$
nodes.statement: Let $X$ be an almost free $S^1$-space with locally $S^1$-orientable $S^1$-equivariant implicit atlas with boundary $A$. Then $\pi_\ast[X]^\mathrm{vir}=0$, where $\pi_\ast=(\pi^\ast)^\vee:\check H^\bullet(X;\mathfrak o_{X\operatorname{rel}\partial})^\vee\to\check H^\bullet(X/S^1;\pi_\ast\mathfrak o_{X\operatorname{rel}\partial})^\vee$.
nodes.statement_short: For an almost free $S^1$-space with locally $S^1$-orientable equivariant atlas, the pushforward of the virtual fundamental class to $X/S^1$ vanishes.
assumptions: Let $X$ be an almost free $S^1$-space with locally $S^1$-orientable $S^1$-equivariant implicit atlas with boundary $A$.
conclusions: Then $\pi_\ast[X]^\mathrm{vir}=0$
nodes.label: fclocalization

nodes.name: Proof
nodes.statement: We may assume that $A$ is finite. Now by Theorem \ref{Slocalfundamentaliso}, we have a commutative diagram: \begin{equation*} \begin{tikzcd} \check H^{d+\bullet}(X/S^1;\pi_\ast\mathfrak o_{X\operatorname{rel}\partial})\ar{d}{\pi^\ast}\ar[equal]{r}{\text{Thm \ref{Slocalfundamentaliso}}}&H^{d+\bullet}_{S^1,\mathrm{vir}}(X\operatorname{rel}\partial;A)\ar{d}{\eqref{CSStimesSS}}\ar{r}{\eqref{CSSpushforward}}&H_{-\bullet-1}^{S^1}(E;A)\ar{d}{\pi^!}\\ \check H^{d+\bullet}(X;\mathfrak o_{X\operatorname{rel}\partial})\ar[equal]{r}{\text{Thm \ref{Fsheaffundamentaliso}}}&H^{d+\bullet}_\mathrm{vir}(X\operatorname{rel}\partial;A)\ar{r}{\eqref{Fpushforward}}&H_{-\bullet}(E;A)\ar{r}{[E_A]\mapsto 1}&R \end{tikzcd} \end{equation*} By definition, $[X]^\mathrm{vir}$ is the total composition of the bottom row for $\bullet=0$. Now the desired statement follows since the rightmost vertical map is zero (by Lemma \ref{trivialactiongysin}, because $S^1$ acts trivially on $E_A$).
nodes.statement_short: Factor $[X]^\mathrm{vir}$ through equivariant virtual cochains; the Gysin map on $E_A$ (trivial action) vanishes, killing $\pi_\ast[X]^\mathrm{vir}$.

nodes.name: Vanishing of $0$-dimensional virtual class under almost free $S^1$-action
nodes.statement: Let $X$ be an almost free $S^1$-space with locally $S^1$-orientable $S^1$-equivariant implicit atlas with boundary $A$ of dimension $0$. Then $[X]^\mathrm{vir}=0$.
nodes.statement_short: A $0$-dimensional almost free $S^1$-space with locally $S^1$-orientable equivariant atlas has $[X]^\mathrm{vir}=0$.
assumptions: Let $X$ be an almost free $S^1$-space with locally $S^1$-orientable $S^1$-equivariant implicit atlas with boundary $A$ of dimension $0$.
conclusions: Then $[X]^\mathrm{vir}=0$.

nodes.name: Proof
nodes.statement: This follows from Theorem \ref{fclocalization} since $\pi^\ast:\check H^0(X/S^1;\pi_\ast\mathfrak o_{X\operatorname{rel}\partial})\to\check H^0(X;\mathfrak o_{X\operatorname{rel}\partial})$ is an isomorphism (since $S^1$ is connected and $A$ is locally $S^1$-orientable).
nodes.statement_short: Theorem fclocalization plus $\pi^\ast$ being an isomorphism on $\check H^0$.

nodes.name: Towards an $S^1$-equivariant virtual fundamental cycle
nodes.statement: We expect that the machinery of this section can be used to define an $S^1$-equivariant virtual fundamental cycle $[X]^{S^1,\mathrm{vir}}\in\check H^{d-1}(X/S^1;\pi_\ast\mathfrak o_{X\operatorname{rel}\partial})^\vee\xrightarrow{(\pi_!)^\vee}\check H^d(X;\mathfrak o_{X\operatorname{rel}\partial})^\vee$ lifting $[X]^\mathrm{vir}$, via the diagram: \begin{equation*} \begin{tikzcd} \check H^{d+\bullet}(X;\mathfrak o_{X\operatorname{rel}\partial})\ar{d}{\pi_!}\ar[equal]{r}{\text{Thm \ref{Fsheaffundamentaliso}}}&H^{d+\bullet}_\mathrm{vir}(X\operatorname{rel}\partial;A)\ar{d}\ar{r}{\eqref{Fpushforward}}&H_{-\bullet}(E;A)\ar{d}{\pi_\ast}\ar{r}{[E_A]\mapsto 1}&R\ar[equal]{d}\\ \check H^{d+\bullet-1}(X/S^1;\pi_\ast\mathfrak o_{X\operatorname{rel}\partial})\ar[equal]{r}{\text{Thm \ref{Slocalfundamentaliso}}}&H^{d+\bullet-1}_{S^1,\mathrm{vir}}(X\operatorname{rel}\partial;A)\ar{r}{\eqref{CSSpushforward}}&H_{-\bullet}^{S^1}(E;A)\ar{r}{[E_A]\mapsto 1}&R \end{tikzcd} \end{equation*} where the second vertical map is induced by pushforward $\pi_\ast$ on chains. Note that we would need to show that the first square commutes. This would provide another proof of Theorem \ref{fclocalization}. This should also be applicable without any restriction on the $S^1$-action on $X$ (provided we use $S^1$-equivariant (co)homology in the appropriate places).
nodes.statement_short: Expected construction of an $S^1$-equivariant virtual fundamental cycle lifting $[X]^\mathrm{vir}$, giving another proof of $S^1$-localization.
nodes.label: SSequivariantvfcmaybe

nodes.name: Chain models unnecessary with $\infty$-categories (MF-sets)
nodes.statement: If we used the language of $\infty$-categories, there would be no need to construct models of chains with good (chain level) functoriality properties (c.f.\ Remark \ref{independenceofchainmodel}).

nodes.name: PL manifold with cells
nodes.statement: A \emph{PL manifold with cells} $(M,\mathcal S)$ is a compact connected nonempty orientable PL-manifold with boundary $M$ with stratification by a finite poset $\mathcal S$ (see Definition \ref{stratificationdefinition}) such that: \begin{rlist} \item$M^{\leq\mathfrak s}$ is a connected nonempty orientable PL-submanifold with boundary. \item$(M^{\leq\mathfrak s})^\circ=M^\mathfrak s$. \item$\mathcal S$ has a unique maximal element. \end{rlist} For every $\mathfrak s\in\mathcal S$, there corresponds a \emph{face} $(M^{\leq\mathfrak s},\mathcal S^{\leq\mathfrak s})$, which is also a PL manifold with cells.
nodes.statement_short: A compact connected orientable PL manifold with boundary, stratified by a finite poset with a unique maximum, whose closed strata are connected orientable PL submanifolds with interior the open stratum.
nodes.genus: a compact connected nonempty orientable PL-manifold with boundary $M$ with stratification by a finite poset $\mathcal S$

nodes.name: MF-set
nodes.statement: An \emph{MF-set} is a set $\mathcal Y$ along with: \begin{rlist} \item For every $i\in\mathcal Y$, a PL manifold with cells $(M_i,\mathcal S_i)$. \item(Face identifications). For every $i\in\mathcal Y$ and every $\mathfrak s\in\mathcal S_i$, an index $j\in\mathcal Y$ and an isomorphism $(M_i^{\leq\mathfrak s},\mathcal S_i^{\leq\mathfrak s})\xrightarrow\sim(M_j,\mathcal S_j)$. These indices and isomorphisms must be (strictly) transitive in the following obvious sense. If $\mathfrak s\in\mathcal S$ is maximal, then $j=i$ and $(M_i,\mathcal S_i)=(M_i^{\leq\mathfrak s},\mathcal S_i^{\leq\mathfrak s})\xrightarrow\sim(M_j,\mathcal S_j)=(M_i,\mathcal S_i)$ is the identity map. If $\mathfrak s'\preceq\mathfrak s$ is a nested pair of faces with identifications $(M_i^{\leq\mathfrak s},\mathcal S_i^{\leq\mathfrak s})\xrightarrow\sim(M_j,\mathcal S_j)$ and $(M_i^{\leq\mathfrak s'},\mathcal S_i^{\leq\mathfrak s'})\xrightarrow\sim(M_{j'},\mathcal S_{j'})$, and the $\mathfrak s'$ face of $(M_j,\mathcal S_j)$ is identified $(M_j^{\leq\mathfrak s'},\mathcal S_j^{\leq\mathfrak s'})\xrightarrow\sim(M_k,\mathcal S_k)$, then $k=j'$ and the two identifications of $(M_i^{\leq\mathfrak s'},\mathcal S_i^{\leq\mathfrak s'})$ with $(M_k,\mathcal S_k)=(M_{j'},\mathcal S_{j'})$ are the same. \end{rlist} A morphism of MF-sets $f:\mathcal Y\to\mathcal Y'$ is a map of sets covered by isomorphisms $(M_i,\mathcal S_i)\to(M_{f(i)},\mathcal S_{f(i)})$, compatible with the face identifications for $\mathcal Y$ and $\mathcal Y'$ in the obvious way. The category of MF-sets has a natural symmetric monoidal structure: given MF-sets $\{M_i\}_{i\in\mathcal Y}$ and $\{M_j'\}_{j\in\mathcal Y'}$, their product is defined to be $\{M_i\times M_j'\}_{(i,j)\in\mathcal Y\times\mathcal Y'}$, which is again an MF-set. For an MF-set $\mathcal Y$, let $C^\mathcal Y_\bullet(X)$ denote the complex freely generated\footnote{A given map $M_i\to X$ contributes a copy of the orientation module of $M_i$, which is isomorphic to $\mathbb Z$ but not canonically so.} by maps $M_i\to X$ (for $i\in\mathcal Y$), with differential given by the obvious sum over all codimension one faces. Note that there is a natural map: \begin{equation} C_\bullet^\mathcal Y(X)\otimes\mathcal C_\bullet^{\mathcal Y'}(X')\to C_\bullet^{\mathcal Y\times\mathcal Y'}(X\times X') \end{equation}
nodes.statement_short: A set indexing PL manifolds with cells together with strictly transitive face identifications; with morphisms, products, and the chain complex $C^\mathcal Y_\bullet(X)$ of maps $M_i\to X$.

nodes.name: Product map on MF-chains
nodes.statement: C_\bullet^\mathcal Y(X)\otimes\mathcal C_\bullet^{\mathcal Y'}(X')\to C_\bullet^{\mathcal Y\times\mathcal Y'}(X\times X')

nodes.name: MF-sets in the DIFF category
nodes.statement: It would perhaps be more natural to work with MF-sets in the DIFF category, although in that case it is not clear precisely what sort of stratifications and corner structure one should allow so that the proof of Lemma \ref{saturatedcalculatesH} goes through.

nodes.name: Standard simplicial MF-set
nodes.statement: The collection of standard simplices $\{\Delta^n\}_{n\geq 0}$ equipped with their standard simplicial stratifications and the standard identifications of the faces of $\Delta^n$ with the various $\Delta^i$, forms an MF-set.
nodes.statement_short: Standard simplices with standard face identifications form an MF-set.
nodes.label: standardsimplicialMFset

nodes.name: Saturated MF-set
nodes.statement: An MF-set $\mathcal Y$ is called \emph{saturated} iff for every PL manifold with cells $(M,\mathcal S)$ along with, for every $\mathfrak s\in\mathcal S$ of positive codimension, an index $j\in\mathcal Y$ and an isomorphism $(M_j,\mathcal S_j)\xrightarrow\sim(M^{\leq\mathfrak s},\mathcal S^{\leq\mathfrak s})$, such that these indices and isomorphisms are (strictly) transitive in the obvious sense, there exists $i\in\mathcal Y$ and an isomorphism $(M_i,\mathcal S_i)\xrightarrow\sim(M,\mathcal S)$ respecting these given face identifications.
nodes.statement_short: Every PL manifold with cells whose proper faces are identified with members of $\mathcal Y$ is itself isomorphic to some member of $\mathcal Y$.
nodes.label: saturateddef

nodes.statement: Every MF-set $\mathcal Y$ embeds into a saturated MF-set $\mathcal Y_\infty$, which may be constructed (non-canonically) as follows.
nodes.name: Every MF-set embeds into a saturated one
conclusions: Every MF-set $\mathcal Y$ embeds into a saturated MF-set $\mathcal Y_\infty$

nodes.statement: We define a sequence of inclusions $\mathcal Y=\mathcal Y_{-1}\hookrightarrow\mathcal Y_0\hookrightarrow\mathcal Y_1\hookrightarrow\cdots$, and we let $\mathcal Y_\infty:=\varinjlim\mathcal Y_n$. To define $\mathcal Y_n$, we consider all PL manifolds with cells of dimension $n$ with face identifications to elements of $\mathcal Y_{n-1}$ as in Definition \ref{saturateddef}. The collection of isomorphism classes of such data (manifold along with face identifications) forms a set, so we may choose (non-canonically) a set $\mathcal Z_n$ parameterizing all of them. We then set $\mathcal Y_n:=\mathcal Y_{n-1}\sqcup\mathcal Z_n$. Now it is easy to check that $\mathcal Y_\infty$ is saturated.
nodes.name: Construction of the saturation $\mathcal Y_\infty$
nodes.statement_short: Inductively adjoin all PL manifolds with cells of dimension $n$ whose faces lie in $\mathcal Y_{n-1}$; the union is saturated.

nodes.name: Saturated MF-sets compute singular homology
nodes.statement: Let $\mathcal Y$ be a saturated MF-set. Then there is a canonical isomorphism between singular homology $H_\bullet(X)$ and $H^\mathcal Y_\bullet(X)$ (the homology of $C^\mathcal Y_\bullet(X)$).
assumptions: Let $\mathcal Y$ be a saturated MF-set.
conclusions: Then there is a canonical isomorphism between singular homology $H_\bullet(X)$ and $H^\mathcal Y_\bullet(X)$ (the homology of $C^\mathcal Y_\bullet(X)$).
nodes.label: saturatedcalculatesH

nodes.name: Proof
nodes.statement: Since $\mathcal Y$ is saturated, there exists a morphism of MF-sets $\{\Delta^n\}_{n\geq 0}\to\{M_i\}_{i\in\mathcal Y}$ (where $\{\Delta^n\}_{n\geq 0}$ is as in Example \ref{standardsimplicialMFset}). Since $C_\bullet(X)=C^{\{\Delta^n\}_{n\geq 0}}_\bullet(X)$ by definition, we obtain a chain map $C_\bullet(X)\to C_\bullet^\mathcal Y(X)$. The resulting map: \begin{equation} H_\bullet(X)\to H_\bullet^\mathcal Y(X) \end{equation} is independent of the choice of morphism $\{\Delta^n\}_{n\geq 0}\to\{M_i\}_{i\in\mathcal Y}$, as can be seen as follows. There is an MF-set $\{\Delta^n\}_{n\geq 0}\sqcup\{\Delta^n\times[0,1]\}_{n\geq 0}\sqcup\{\Delta^n\}_{n\geq 0}$ where each $\{\Delta^n\}_{n\geq 0}$ is as in Example \ref{standardsimplicialMFset}, where $\Delta^n\times[0,1]$ is given the product stratification ($[0,1]$ stratified by $\{\{0\},\{1\},(0,1)\}$), and $\Delta^n\times\{0\}$ (resp.\ $\Delta^n\times\{1\}$) is identified with the first (resp.\ second) copy of $\Delta^n$. Since $\mathcal Y$ is saturated, it follows that for any pair of morphisms $\{\Delta^n\}_{n\geq 0}\to\{M_i\}_{i\in\mathcal Y}$ there is a morphism $\{\Delta^n\}_{n\geq 0}\sqcup\{\Delta^n\times[0,1]\}_{n\geq 0}\sqcup\{\Delta^n\}_{n\geq 0}\to\{M_i\}_{i\in\mathcal Y}$ whose restriction to the two copies of $\{\Delta^n\}_{n\geq 0}$ are the two given morphisms. From this data one easily constructs a chain homotopy between the two maps $C_\bullet(X)\to C_\bullet^\mathcal Y(X)$. Hence the map \eqref{homologyYcomparison} is canonical. Now let us show that \eqref{homologyYcomparison} is an isomorphism. Fix a map $\{\Delta^n\}_{n\geq 0}\to\{M_i\}_{i\in\mathcal Y}$. Fix triangulations $T_i$ of $M_i$ for which each $M_i^{\leq\mathfrak s}$ is a union of simplices, which are compatible with the face identifications, and which restrict to the tautological triangulation of $\{\Delta^n\}_{n\geq 0}$. Such triangulations may be constructed by induction. By triangulation, we mean a triangulation in which each simplex is equipped with a total order on its set of vertices, compatible with its faces (i.e.\ a semisimplicial set rather than a simplicial complex). Such triangluations induce a map of complexes $C_\bullet^\mathcal Y(X)\to C_\bullet(X)$, and the composition $C_\bullet(X)\to C_\bullet^\mathcal Y(X)\to C_\bullet(X)$ is clearly the identity map. It suffices to show that the other composition is chain homotopic to the identity map. Now let us define a new MF-set in terms of the map $\{\Delta^n\}_{n\geq 0}\to\{M_i\}_{i\in\mathcal Y}$ and the triangulations $T_i$. Note that the stratification of $M_i$ by the face poset $\mathcal F(T_i)$ of $T_i$ refines the stratification by $\mathcal S_i$; in other words we have maps $M_i\to\mathcal F(T_i)\to\mathcal S_i$. The objects of the new MF-set are $\{M_i\}_{i\in\mathcal Y}\sqcup\{M_i\times[0,1]\}_{i\in\mathcal Y}$, where $M_i\times[0,1]$ is stratified by the following strata: \begin{align} M_i^\mathfrak s\times\{0\}&\quad\mathfrak s\in\mathcal S_i\\ M_i^\mathfrak s\times(0,1)&\quad\mathfrak s\in\mathcal S_i\\ M_i^\mathfrak t\times\{1\}&\quad\mathfrak t\in\mathcal F(T_i) \end{align} Thus the poset of strata of $M_i\times[0,1]$ is $\mathcal S_i\sqcup\mathcal S_i\sqcup\mathcal F(T_i)$. For the face identifications, $M_i\times\{0\}$ is identified tautologically with $M_i$, and each of the closed strata $M_i^{\leq\mathfrak t}\times\{1\}$ ($\mathfrak t\in\mathcal F(T_i)$) is identified with the corresponding $\Delta^n$ (considered as an object of $\{M_i\}_{i\in\mathcal Y}$ via the inclusion $\{\Delta^n\}_{n\geq 0}\to\{M_i\}_{i\in\mathcal Y}$). Now we have a chain of inclusions $\{\Delta^n\}_{n\geq 0}\hookrightarrow\{M_i\}_{i\in\mathcal Y}\hookrightarrow\{M_i\}_{i\in\mathcal Y}\sqcup\{M_i\times[0,1]\}_{i\in\mathcal Y}$. Since $\mathcal Y$ is saturated, there in fact exists a map backwards $\{M_i\}_{i\in\mathcal Y}\sqcup\{M_i\times[0,1]\}_{i\in\mathcal Y}\to\{M_i\}_{i\in\mathcal Y}$ (acting identically on $\{M_i\}_{i\in\mathcal Y}$). Using this map, we obtain a chain map $C_\bullet^\mathcal Y(X)\to C_{\bullet+1}^\mathcal Y(X)$ (precompose chains with the projection $M_i\times[0,1]\to M_i$). This map is a chain homotopy between the identity map and the composition $C_\bullet^\mathcal Y(X)\to C_\bullet(X)\to C_\bullet^\mathcal Y(X)$, so we are done.
nodes.statement_short: Use saturation to map simplices into $\mathcal Y$ (canonical up to homotopy via cylinders), and triangulations for a map back. A cylinder MF-set built from triangulations gives the chain homotopy to the identity.

nodes.name: Comparison map $H_\bullet\to H^\mathcal Y_\bullet$
nodes.statement: H_\bullet(X)\to H_\bullet^\mathcal Y(X)
nodes.label: homologyYcomparison

nodes.name: Strata of $M_i\times[0,1]$
nodes.statement: M_i^\mathfrak s\times\{0\}&\quad\mathfrak s\in\mathcal S_i\\ M_i^\mathfrak s\times(0,1)&\quad\mathfrak s\in\mathcal S_i\\ M_i^\mathfrak t\times\{1\}&\quad\mathfrak t\in\mathcal F(T_i)

nodes.name: $S^1$-MF-set
nodes.statement: An \emph{$S^1$-MF-set} is an MF-set $\mathcal Y$ along with a principal $S^1$-bundle $(ES^1)_\mathcal Y\to(BS^1)_\mathcal Y$ where $(BS^1)_\mathcal Y$ (and hence also $(ES^1)_\mathcal Y$) is an increasing union of compact polyhedra (we do not require $(ES^1)_\mathcal Y$ to be contractible), and for every $i\in\mathcal Y$, a pullback diagram: \begin{equation} \begin{tikzcd} M_i\ar{r}\ar{d}&(ES^1)_\mathcal Y\ar{d}\\ N_i\ar{r}&(BS^1)_\mathcal Y \end{tikzcd} \end{equation} with PL maps where $N_i$ (and hence also $M_i$) is a PL manifold, and where the stratification on $M_i$ is pulled back from $N_i$, such that these diagrams are compatible with the face identifications. A map of $S^1$-MF-sets $\mathcal Y\to\mathcal Y'$ is said to be injective iff it is injective as a map of sets and the map $(ES^1)_\mathcal Y\to(ES^1)_{\mathcal Y'}$ is injective. There is a forgetful functor from $S^1$-MF-sets to MF-sets, where we remember $M_i$ (of course, there is another natural forgetful functor remembering $N_i$, though we will never use it). When speaking of a morphism $\mathcal Y\to\mathcal Y'$ where $\mathcal Y$ is an $S^1$-MF-set and $\mathcal Y'$ is an MF-set, we implicitly apply the forgetful functor to $\mathcal Y$. The category of $S^1$-MF-sets has a natural symmetric monoidal structure: given $S^1$-MF-sets $\{M_i\}_{i\in\mathcal Y}$ and $\{M_j'\}_{j\in\mathcal Y'}$, we may define their product $\{M_i\times M_j'\}_{(i,j)\in\mathcal Y\times\mathcal Y'}$, which is again an $S^1$-MF-set, via the diagonal $S^1$-action on $M_i\times M_j'$ and $(ES^1)_{\mathcal Y\times\mathcal Y'}:=(ES^1)_\mathcal Y\times(ES^1)_{\mathcal Y'}$ with the diagonal action. The forgetful functor from $S^1$-MF-sets to MF-sets is clearly a symmetric monoidal functor. It also makes sense to take the product of an $S^1$-MF-set and an MF-set. For an $S^1$-MF-set $\mathcal Y$, let $C^{S^1,\mathcal Y}_\bullet(X)$ (for $X$ an $S^1$-space) denote the complex generated by commuting diagrams of $S^1$-equivariant maps: \begin{equation} \begin{tikzcd} M_i\ar{r}\ar{d}&X\times(ES^1)_\mathcal Y\ar{r}\ar{d}&(ES^1)_\mathcal Y\ar{d}\\ N_i\ar{r}&(X\times(ES^1)_\mathcal Y)/S^1\ar{r}&(BS^1)_\mathcal Y \end{tikzcd} \end{equation} ($i\in\mathcal Y$), where the outer square coincides with \eqref{SSMFstructuremaps}, with differential given by the obvious sum over all codimension one faces. A generator \eqref{SSchaindiagram} resides in degree $\dim N_i$. Note that there are natural compatible maps: \begin{align} \mathcal C_\bullet^{S^1,\mathcal Y}(X')&\to C_{\bullet+1}^\mathcal Y(X)\\ C_\bullet^\mathcal Y(X)\otimes\mathcal C_\bullet^{S^1,\mathcal Y'}(X')&\to C_\bullet^{S^1,\mathcal Y\times\mathcal Y'}(X\times X')\\ C_\bullet^{S^1,\mathcal Y}(X)\otimes\mathcal C_\bullet^{S^1,\mathcal Y'}(X')&\to C_{\bullet+1}^{S^1,\mathcal Y\times\mathcal Y'}(X\times X') \end{align}
nodes.statement_short: An MF-set with a principal $S^1$-bundle $(ES^1)_\mathcal Y\to(BS^1)_\mathcal Y$ and compatible pullback squares $M_i\to N_i$; with products and equivariant chain complexes $C^{S^1,\mathcal Y}_\bullet$.
nodes.label: SSMFdef

nodes.name: $S^1$-MF-set structure maps
nodes.statement: \begin{tikzcd} M_i\ar{r}\ar{d}&(ES^1)_\mathcal Y\ar{d}\\ N_i\ar{r}&(BS^1)_\mathcal Y \end{tikzcd}
nodes.label: SSMFstructuremaps

nodes.name: Generators of $C^{S^1,\mathcal Y}_\bullet(X)$
nodes.statement: \begin{tikzcd} M_i\ar{r}\ar{d}&X\times(ES^1)_\mathcal Y\ar{r}\ar{d}&(ES^1)_\mathcal Y\ar{d}\\ N_i\ar{r}&(X\times(ES^1)_\mathcal Y)/S^1\ar{r}&(BS^1)_\mathcal Y \end{tikzcd}
nodes.label: SSchaindiagram

nodes.name: Gysin and product maps on MF-chains
nodes.statement: \mathcal C_\bullet^{S^1,\mathcal Y}(X')&\to C_{\bullet+1}^\mathcal Y(X)\\ C_\bullet^\mathcal Y(X)\otimes\mathcal C_\bullet^{S^1,\mathcal Y'}(X')&\to C_\bullet^{S^1,\mathcal Y\times\mathcal Y'}(X\times X')\\ C_\bullet^{S^1,\mathcal Y}(X)\otimes\mathcal C_\bullet^{S^1,\mathcal Y'}(X')&\to C_{\bullet+1}^{S^1,\mathcal Y\times\mathcal Y'}(X\times X')

nodes.name: Saturated $S^1$-MF-set
nodes.statement: An $S^1$-MF-set $\mathcal Y$ is called \emph{saturated} iff $(ES^1)_\mathcal Y$ is contractible and every pullback diagram: \begin{equation} \begin{tikzcd} M\ar{r}\ar{d}&(ES^1)_\mathcal Y\ar{d}\\ N\ar{r}&(BS^1)_\mathcal Y \end{tikzcd} \end{equation} where $N$ (and thus $M$) is a PL manifold with cells, along with strictly transitive identifications of the faces of positive codimension with elements of $\mathcal Y$ (as in Definition \ref{SSMFdef}), is isomorphic to some $i\in\mathcal Y$. Note that the notions of saturation for MF-sets and $S^1$-MF-sets are different: an $S^1$-MF-set is \emph{never} saturated as an MF-set.
nodes.statement_short: $(ES^1)_\mathcal Y$ contractible and every pullback square over $(BS^1)_\mathcal Y$ with faces identified in $\mathcal Y$ is isomorphic to a member.

nodes.name: Pullback square for saturation
nodes.statement: \begin{tikzcd} M\ar{r}\ar{d}&(ES^1)_\mathcal Y\ar{d}\\ N\ar{r}&(BS^1)_\mathcal Y \end{tikzcd}

Every $S^1$-MF-set $\mathcal Y$ embeds into a saturated $S^1$-MF-set $\mathcal Y_\infty$, which may be constructed (again, non-canonically) by first embedding $(ES^1)_\mathcal Y$ into something contractible, and then proceeding as in the case of MF-sets.
nodes.name: Every $S^1$-MF-set embeds into a saturated one
conclusions: Every $S^1$-MF-set $\mathcal Y$ embeds into a saturated $S^1$-MF-set $\mathcal Y_\infty$

nodes.name: Saturated $S^1$-MF-sets compute equivariant homology
nodes.statement: Let $\mathcal Y$ be a saturated $S^1$-MF-set. Then there is a canonical isomorphism between $S^1$-equivariant singular homology $H^{S^1}_\bullet(X)$ and $H^{S^1,\mathcal Y}_\bullet(X)$ (the homology of $C^{S^1,\mathcal Y}_\bullet(X)$). Furthermore, the natural map $C_\bullet^{S^1,\mathcal Y}(X)\to C_{\bullet+1}^{\mathcal Y'}(X)$ induces the Gysin map on homology, for $\mathcal Y'$ a saturated MF-set.
assumptions: Let $\mathcal Y$ be a saturated $S^1$-MF-set.
conclusions: Then there is a canonical isomorphism between $S^1$-equivariant singular homology $H^{S^1}_\bullet(X)$ and $H^{S^1,\mathcal Y}_\bullet(X)$ (the homology of $C^{S^1,\mathcal Y}_\bullet(X)$).
Furthermore, the natural map $C_\bullet^{S^1,\mathcal Y}(X)\to C_{\bullet+1}^{\mathcal Y'}(X)$ induces the Gysin map on homology, for $\mathcal Y'$ a saturated MF-set.
nodes.label: saturatedcalculatesHSS

nodes.name: Proof
nodes.statement: All $S^1$-MF-sets in this proof will share the same $(ES^1)_\mathcal Y\to(BS^1)_\mathcal Y$, so we will omit the subscript $_\mathcal Y$ from the notation. Let $\{\Delta^n\}_{n\geq 0,f:\Delta^n\to BS^1}$ denote the $S^1$-MF-set indexed by pairs $(n,f)$ consisting of an integer $n\geq 0$ and a PL map $f:\Delta^n\to BS^1$, where the stratifications and face identifications are as in Example \ref{standardsimplicialMFset}. Now the complex $C^{S^1,\{\Delta^n\}_{n\geq 0,f:\Delta^n\to BS^1}}_\bullet(X)$ is freely generated by maps $\Delta^n\to(X\times ES^1)/S^1$ whose composition with the projection $(X\times ES^1)/S^1\to BS^1$ is PL. A straightforward approximation argument shows that the inclusion of this complex into the complex generated by all maps $\Delta^n\to(X\times ES^1)/S^1$ is a quasi-isomorphism. Hence there is a canonical isomorphism: \begin{equation} H^{S^1,\{\Delta^n\}_{n\geq 0,f:\Delta^n\to BS^1}}_\bullet(X)\xrightarrow\sim H_\bullet((X\times ES^1)/S^1)=H_\bullet^{S^1}(X) \end{equation} As in the proof of Lemma \ref{saturatedcalculatesH} there exists a morphism of $S^1$-MF-sets $\{\Delta^n\}_{n\geq 0,f:\Delta^n\to BS^1}\to\mathcal Y$ since $\mathcal Y$ is saturated. This induces a chain map $C^{S^1,\{\Delta^n\}_{n\geq 0,f:\Delta^n\to BS^1}}_\bullet(X)\to C^{S^1,\mathcal Y}_\bullet(X)$, which as before induces a canonical map on homology: \begin{equation} H^{S^1,\{\Delta^n\}_{n\geq 0,f:\Delta^n\to BS^1}}_\bullet(X)\to H^{S^1,\mathcal Y}_\bullet(X) \end{equation} which is independent of the choice of morphism $\{\Delta^n\}_{n\geq 0,f:\Delta^n\to BS^1}\to\mathcal Y$. It suffices to show that this map is an isomorphism. Fix a map $\{\Delta^n\}_{n\geq 0,f:\Delta^n\to BS^1}\to\mathcal Y$, which we observe is necessarily injective. Fix triangulations $T_i$ of $M_i$ as in the proof of Lemma \ref{saturatedcalculatesH}. Such triangulations induce a map of complexes $C^{S^1,\mathcal Y}_\bullet(X)\to C^{S^1,\{\Delta^n\}_{n\geq 0,f:\Delta^n\to BS^1}}_\bullet(X)$. The composition $C^{S^1,\{\Delta^n\}_{n\geq 0,f:\Delta^n\to BS^1}}_\bullet(X)\to C^{S^1,\mathcal Y}_\bullet(X)\to C^{S^1,\{\Delta^n\}_{n\geq 0,f:\Delta^n\to BS^1}}_\bullet(X)$ is clearly the identity map. It thus suffices to show that the reverse composition is chain homotopic to the identity. As in the proof of Lemma \ref{saturatedcalculatesH}, we construct a new $S^1$-MF-set, namely $\{M_i\}_{i\in\mathcal Y}\sqcup\{M_i\times[0,1]\}_{i\in\mathcal Y}$, from the inclusion $\{\Delta^n\}_{n\geq 0,f:\Delta^n\to BS^1}\hookrightarrow\{M_i\}_{i\in\mathcal Y}$ and the triangulations $T_i$. There are inclusions $\{\Delta^n\}_{n\geq 0,f:\Delta^n\to BS^1}\hookrightarrow\{M_i\}_{i\in\mathcal Y}\hookrightarrow\{M_i\}_{i\in\mathcal Y}\sqcup\{M_i\times[0,1]\}_{i\in\mathcal Y}$. The desired chain homotopy may then be constructed as in the proof of Lemma \ref{saturatedcalculatesH}. The fact that the induced map $H^{S^1}_\bullet(X)\to H_{\bullet+1}(X)$ is the Gysin map is left to the reader.
nodes.statement_short: As for Lemma saturatedcalculatesH: compare with the simplicial $S^1$-MF-set over $BS^1$ (PL approximation), then build a chain homotopy from triangulations and cylinders.

nodes.name: Simplicial $S^1$-MF-set computes equivariant homology
nodes.statement: H^{S^1,\{\Delta^n\}_{n\geq 0,f:\Delta^n\to BS^1}}_\bullet(X)\xrightarrow\sim H_\bullet((X\times ES^1)/S^1)=H_\bullet^{S^1}(X)

nodes.name: Canonical map to $H^{S^1,\mathcal Y}_\bullet$
nodes.statement: H^{S^1,\{\Delta^n\}_{n\geq 0,f:\Delta^n\to BS^1}}_\bullet(X)\to H^{S^1,\mathcal Y}_\bullet(X)

Plugging the category of MF-sets into Definition \ref{flowobjectdef}, we may talk about $\mathsf{F}$-modules valued in MF-sets. In other words, an $\mathsf{F}$-module MF-set is a collection of MF-sets $\mathcal Y(\sigma,p,q)$ along with product/face maps: \begin{align} \mathcal Y(\sigma|[0\ldots\hat k\ldots n],p,q)&\to\mathcal Y(\sigma,p,q)\\ \mathcal Y(\sigma|[0\ldots k],p,q)\times\mathcal Y(\sigma|[k\ldots n],q,r)&\to\mathcal Y(\sigma,p,r) \end{align} which are compatible in the sense of Definition \ref{flowobjectdef}.
nodes.name: $\mathsf F$-module MF-set
nodes.statement_short: A collection of MF-sets $\mathcal Y(\sigma,p,q)$ with compatible product/face maps, i.e. an $\mathsf F$-module valued in MF-sets.

nodes.name: Product/face maps of an $\mathsf F$-module MF-set
nodes.statement: \mathcal Y(\sigma|[0\ldots\hat k\ldots n],p,q)&\to\mathcal Y(\sigma,p,q)\\ \mathcal Y(\sigma|[0\ldots k],p,q)\times\mathcal Y(\sigma|[k\ldots n],q,r)&\to\mathcal Y(\sigma,p,r)

Similarly, we may talk about $\mathsf{F}$-modules of $S^1$-MF-sets. We may also talk about morphisms from $\mathsf{F}$-module $S^1$-MF-sets to $\mathsf{F}$-module MF-sets using the forgetful functor described earlier.
nodes.name: $\mathsf F$-module of $S^1$-MF-sets
Existence of cofibrant $\mathsf F$-module MF-set models
nodes.statement: Let $\mathcal X/Z_\bullet$ be a flow category diagram. There exists an $\mathsf{F}$-module of MF-sets $\mathcal Y$ and an $\mathsf{F}$-module of $S^1$-MF-sets $\mathcal Y_{S^1}$ (both supported inside $\operatorname{supp}\mathcal X$) along with a morphism $\mathcal Y_{S^1}\to\mathcal Y$, satisfying the following property. For all $(\sigma,p,q)\in\operatorname{supp}\mathcal X$, both $\mathcal Y(\sigma,p,q)$ and $\mathcal Y_{S^1}(\sigma,p,q)$ are saturated, and the tautologous maps: \begin{align} \operatornamewithlimits{colim}_{\mathfrak s\in\partial\mathcal S_\mathcal X(\sigma,p,q)}\mathcal Y(\sigma,p,q,\mathfrak s)&\hookrightarrow\mathcal Y(\sigma,p,q)\\ \operatornamewithlimits{colim}_{\mathfrak s\in\partial\mathcal S_\mathcal X(\sigma,p,q)}\mathcal Y_{S^1}(\sigma,p,q,\mathfrak s)&\hookrightarrow\mathcal Y_{S^1}(\sigma,p,q) \end{align} are injective (and the colimits on the left exist). Moreover, such $\mathcal Y_{S^1}\to\mathcal Y$ may be constructed by induction on $(\sigma,p,q)$, partially ordered by $\preceq_\mathcal X$ ($\preceq_\mathcal X$ is well-founded, see Definition \ref{cofibrantreplacements} or the proof of Proposition \ref{trivialKanfibration}).
nodes.statement_short: For a flow category diagram there are $\mathsf F$-modules of saturated MF-sets and $S^1$-MF-sets $\mathcal Y_{S^1}\to\mathcal Y$ with injective boundary-colimit maps, built inductively.
assumptions: Let $\mathcal X/Z_\bullet$ be a flow category diagram.
conclusions: There exists an $\mathsf{F}$-module of MF-sets $\mathcal Y$ and an $\mathsf{F}$-module of $S^1$-MF-sets $\mathcal Y_{S^1}$ (both supported inside $\operatorname{supp}\mathcal X$) along with a morphism $\mathcal Y_{S^1}\to\mathcal Y$, satisfying the following property.
Moreover, such $\mathcal Y_{S^1}\to\mathcal Y$ may be constructed by induction on $(\sigma,p,q)$, partially ordered by $\preceq_\mathcal X$
nodes.label: inductionformodels

nodes.name: Injective boundary-colimit maps
nodes.statement: \operatornamewithlimits{colim}_{\mathfrak s\in\partial\mathcal S_\mathcal X(\sigma,p,q)}\mathcal Y(\sigma,p,q,\mathfrak s)&\hookrightarrow\mathcal Y(\sigma,p,q)\\ \operatornamewithlimits{colim}_{\mathfrak s\in\partial\mathcal S_\mathcal X(\sigma,p,q)}\mathcal Y_{S^1}(\sigma,p,q,\mathfrak s)&\hookrightarrow\mathcal Y_{S^1}(\sigma,p,q)
nodes.label: colimitYone

nodes.name: Proof
nodes.statement: It suffices to perform the inductive step for a given $(\sigma,p,q)$. First, we show that the colimits \eqref{colimitYone}--\eqref{colimitYtwo} exist, essentially by rewriting the proofs of Lemmas \ref{cofibrantinjectivelemma} and \ref{cofibranthaslotsofcofibrations} in the present context. We actually show the more general statement that the colimits: \begin{equation} \operatornamewithlimits{colim}_{\mathfrak t\in\mathcal T}\mathcal Y(\sigma,p,q,\mathfrak t)\qquad\operatornamewithlimits{colim}_{\mathfrak t\in\mathcal T}\mathcal Y_{S^1}(\sigma,p,q,\mathfrak t) \end{equation} exist for any $\mathcal T\subseteq\partial\mathcal S_\mathcal X(\sigma,p,q)$ which is downward closed. We show this by induction on the cardinality of $\mathcal T$. If $\mathcal T=\varnothing$, existence is trivial. For $\mathcal T$ nonempty, let $\mathfrak t_0\in\mathcal T$ be any maximal element, and observe that \eqref{Tcolimit} can be written as the colimit of the diagram: \begin{equation} \begin{tikzcd}[row sep = tiny] &\mathcal Y(\sigma,p,q,\mathfrak t_0)\\ \smash{\displaystyle\operatornamewithlimits{colim}_{\begin{smallmatrix}\mathfrak t\in\mathcal T\cr\mathfrak t\prec\mathfrak t_0\end{smallmatrix}}}\mathcal Y(\sigma,p,q,\mathfrak t)\ar[hook]{ur}\ar{rd}\\ &\displaystyle\operatornamewithlimits{colim}_{\mathfrak t\in\mathcal T\setminus\mathfrak t_0}\mathcal Y(\sigma,p,q,\mathfrak t) \end{tikzcd} \end{equation} Let us show that the top arrow is injective. Write $\mathfrak t_0$ in the form \eqref{SdataA}--\eqref{SdataB}. Then we have: \begin{equation} \mathcal S_\mathcal X(\sigma,p,q)^{\leq\mathfrak t_0}=\mathcal S_\mathcal X(\sigma|[j_{a_0}\ldots j_{a_1}],p_0,p_1)\times\cdots\times\mathcal S_\mathcal X(\sigma|[j_{a_{m-1}}\ldots j_{a_m}],p_{m-1},p_m) \end{equation} Now we consider the $m$-cubical diagram: \begin{equation} \prod_{i=1}^m\left[\operatornamewithlimits{colim}_{\mathfrak s\in\partial\mathcal S_\mathcal X(\sigma|[j_{a_{i-1}}\ldots j_{a_i}],p_{i-1},p_i)}\mathcal Y(\sigma|[j_{a_{i-1}}\ldots j_{a_i}],p_{i-1},p_i,\mathfrak s)\hookrightarrow\mathcal Y(\sigma|[j_{a_{i-1}}\ldots j_{a_i}],p_{i-1},p_i)\right] \end{equation} Now the top arrow of \eqref{colimitdiagramnice} is simply the map to the maximal vertex of this $m$-cube from the colimit over the $m$-cube minus the maximal vertex (this is where we use the fact that $\mathcal T$ is downward closed). This is injective for any cubical diagram of the form $\prod_{i=1}^m[A_i\hookrightarrow B_i]$ where each $A_i\hookrightarrow B_i$ is injective. Now that the top arrow in \eqref{colimitdiagramnice} is injective, the existence of the colimit is clear (first take the colimit of underlying sets and then the rest of the structure extends in an obvious way), and hence the colimit in \eqref{Tcolimit} exists. This reasoning applies equally well to $\mathcal Y_{S^1}$ (including $(ES^1)_\mathcal Y\to(BS^1)_\mathcal Y$). Now that we have shown that the colimits on the left hand side of \eqref{colimitYone}--\eqref{colimitYtwo} exist, it remains to define $\mathcal Y(\sigma,p,q)$ and $\mathcal Y_{S^1}(\sigma,p,q)$. We observed earlier that any $S^1$-MF-set injects into a saturated $S^1$-MF-set. Let $\mathcal Y_{S^1}(\sigma,p,q)$ be any saturated $S^1$-MF-set with an injection \eqref{colimitYtwo}. Note that with this definition, the product/face maps with target $\mathcal Y_{S^1}(\sigma,p,q)$ are obvious, as is their compatibility. To define $\mathcal Y(\sigma,p,q)$, consider the following diagram: \begin{equation} \begin{tikzcd} \displaystyle\operatornamewithlimits{colim}_{\mathfrak s\in\partial\mathcal S_\mathcal X(\sigma,p,q)}\mathcal Y(\sigma,p,q,\mathfrak s)\\ \displaystyle\operatornamewithlimits{colim}_{\mathfrak s\in\partial\mathcal S_\mathcal X(\sigma,p,q)}\mathcal Y_{S^1}(\sigma,p,q,\mathfrak s)\ar{u}\ar[hook]{r}&\mathcal Y_{S^1}(\sigma,p,q) \end{tikzcd} \end{equation} The lower colimit is in the category of $S^1$-MF-sets. It is clear from the inductive proof of its existence that this particular colimit commutes with the forgetful functor to MF-sets. Hence we may equally well think of this colimit as taking place in the category of MF-sets, and with this perspective the definition of the vertical map is clear. Now since the horizontal map is injective, the colimit of this diagram (in the category of MF-sets) clearly exists (first take the colimit in sets and then the rest of the structure is obvious). We pick any saturated MF-set into which the colimit of \eqref{biggluingcolimit} embeds, and we call this saturated MF-set $\mathcal Y(\sigma,p,q)$. Via the embedding of the upper colimit into $\mathcal Y(\sigma,p,q)$, it is tautological that the face/product maps with target $\mathcal Y(\sigma,p,q)$ exist and are compatible. The map $\mathcal Y_{S^1}(\sigma,p,q)\to\mathcal Y(\sigma,p,q)$ is similarly tautological, as is the fact that it is compatible with the product/face maps.
nodes.statement_short: Induction on $(\sigma,p,q)$. Existence of colimits by induction on $\#\mathcal T$ using injectivity of cubical diagrams; then embed into saturated (S^1-)MF-sets.

nodes.statement: Now it remains only to show that our models of chains and $S^1$-equivariant chains described above do actually calculate singular homology and $S^1$-equivariant singular homology.\footnote{Technically speaking, we must also show that the pushforward maps, product maps, and Gysin maps have the expected action on homology, though this verification is safely left to the reader.}
nodes.name: Chain models compute (equivariant) singular homology
nodes.statement_short: The $(\sigma,p,q)$-dependent chain models compute singular homology and $S^1$-equivariant singular homology.

nodes.statement: We show that our model of chains (generated by diagrams \eqref{bigcomplex}) calculates singular homology as follows. Let us abbreviate $\mathcal Y=\mathcal Y(\sigma,p,q)$. Our complex generated by maps \eqref{bigcomplex} is in fact a double complex with bigrading $p=\sum_\alpha i_\alpha$ and $q=\dim M_i$. Now let us consider the associated spectral sequence. We calculate the $E^1_{p,q}$ term as follows. By definition $E^1_{p,q}$ is simply the homology of the complex with only the differentials decreasing $q$. Clearly this breaks up as a direct sum over tuples $\{i_\alpha\in\mathbb Z_{\geq 0}\}$. For a given tuple $\{i_\alpha\in\mathbb Z_{\geq 0}\}$, we must calculate the homology of the complex: \begin{equation} \bigoplus_{\begin{smallmatrix}i\in\mathcal Y\cr M_i\times\prod_\alpha\Delta^{i_\alpha}\to X\end{smallmatrix}}\mathbb Z \end{equation} We claim that this is the same as the homology of the complex: \begin{equation} \bigoplus_{\begin{smallmatrix}i\in\mathcal Y\cr M_i\to X\end{smallmatrix}}\mathbb Z \end{equation} There is a clearly a map $\eqref{withoutDelta}\to\eqref{withDelta}$ (precompose with the projection $M_i\times\prod_\alpha\Delta^{i_\alpha}\to M_i$), and picking a point $x\in\prod_\alpha\Delta^{i_\alpha}$ gives a map in the opposite direction. The composition $\eqref{withoutDelta}\to\eqref{withDelta}\to\eqref{withoutDelta}$ is clearly the identity. The other composition is chain homotopic to the identity by the following argument. Since $\mathcal Y$ is saturated, we can choose a map $I:\mathcal Y\to\mathcal Y$ and isomorphisms $(M_{I(i)},\mathcal S_{I(i)})\xrightarrow\sim(M_i\times[0,1],\mathcal S_i\times\mathcal S)$ compatible with the face identifications, where $([0,1],\mathcal S)$ is the PL manifold $[0,1]$ with strata $\{\{0\},\{1\},(0,1)\}$, and $M_i\times\{0\}$, $M_i\times\{1\}$ have the obvious face identifications with $M_i$ (construct $I$ and the isomorphisms by induction on dimension). Using this coherent choice of ``cylinder objects'', it is easy to define a chain homotopy between the identity map and the composition $\eqref{withDelta}\to\eqref{withoutDelta}\to\eqref{withDelta}$ (using the fact that $\prod_\alpha\Delta^{i_\alpha}$ is contractible). It follows that the canonical map $\eqref{withoutDelta}\to\eqref{withDelta}$ is a quasi-isomorphism. By Lemma \ref{saturatedcalculatesH}, the complex $\eqref{withoutDelta}$ calculates singular homology. Hence we conclude that the $E^1$ term is: \begin{equation} E^1_{p,q}=\bigoplus_{\sum_\alpha i_\alpha=p}H_q(X) \end{equation} The differentials on the $E^1$ page are easy to understand (essentially we have $H_q(X)$ tensored with the restricted tensor product $\bigotimes_\alpha C_\bullet(\mathrm{pt})$). We conclude that: \begin{equation} E^2_{p,q}=\begin{cases}H_q(X)&p=0\cr 0&p\ne 0\end{cases} \end{equation} Hence there are no further differentials and we are done.
nodes.name: Proof that the chain model computes singular homology
nodes.statement_short: Spectral sequence of the double complex: $E^1$ reduces (via cylinder objects from saturation) to $H_q(X)$ per tuple, and $E^2$ is concentrated in $p=0$.

nodes.statement: We now use a similar argument to show that our model of $S^1$-equivariant chains calculates $S^1$-equivariant singular homology. Let us abbreviate $\mathcal Y_{S^1}=\mathcal Y_{S^1}(\sigma,p,q)$. Our complex generated by maps \eqref{bigcomplexSS} is a double complex as before, and we consider the associated spectral sequence. As before, $E^1_{p,q}$ splits up as a direct sum over tuples $\{i_\alpha\in\mathbb Z_{\geq 0}\}$. For a given tuple $\{i_\alpha\in\mathbb Z_{\geq 0}\}$, the corresponding direct summand is the homology of the complex: \begin{equation} \bigoplus_{\begin{smallmatrix}&i\in\mathcal Y_{S^1}\cr M_i\times\prod_\alpha\Delta^{i_\alpha}&\to&X\times(ES^1)_{\mathcal Y_{S^1}}\cr\downarrow&&\downarrow\cr M_i&\to&(ES^1)_{\mathcal Y_{S^1}}\end{smallmatrix}}\mathbb Z \end{equation} As in the non-equivariant case, this is canonically quasi-isomorphic to: \begin{equation} \bigoplus_{\begin{smallmatrix}&i\in\mathcal Y_{S^1}\cr M_i&\to&X\times(ES^1)_{\mathcal Y_{S^1}}\cr\downarrow&&\downarrow\cr M_i&\to&(ES^1)_{\mathcal Y_{S^1}}\end{smallmatrix}}\mathbb Z \end{equation} Thus by Lemma \ref{saturatedcalculatesHSS} the $E^1$ term is: \begin{equation} E^1_{p,q}=\bigoplus_{\sum_\alpha i_\alpha=p}H_q^{S^1}(X) \end{equation} The differentials on the $E^1$ page are as before, and thus: \begin{equation} E^2_{p,q}=\begin{cases}H_q^{S^1}(X)&p=0\cr 0&p\ne 0\end{cases} \end{equation} so we are done.

nodes.statement: We now give a new definition of Floer-type homology groups identical to Definition \ref{defofhomologygroups} except using the chain models from \S\ref{SSaugmentedsec}. Precisely, we define a new resolution $\tilde Z_\bullet\to Z_\bullet$ by including the data\footnote{For the reader concerned with set-theoretic issues: so that the collection of all possible choices of this data forms a set, one may add ``rigidifying data'' to the definition of an ($S^1$-)MF-set, e.g.\ require $\mathcal Y$ to be countable, equip $\mathcal Y$ with an injection into $\omega_1$ (the first uncountable ordinal), and equip each $M_i$ and $(ES^1)_\mathcal Y$ with an embedding into $\mathbb R^\infty$ (note that this rigidifying data is not required to be compatible in any way with the rest of the structure, and thus it does not affect any of our previous arguments).} of $\mathsf{F}$-module ($S^1$-)MF-sets $\mathcal Y_{S^1}\to\mathcal Y$ over $\Delta^n$ for $f^\ast\mathcal X$ satisfying the conclusion of Proposition \ref{inductionformodels}.

Suppose that $S^1$ acts compatibly on this entire structure ($S^1$-actions on $\mathcal X(\sigma,p,q)$ and $S^1$-equivariant implicit atlases, so that all the relevant structure maps are $S^1$-equivariant). Fix partitions (into disjoint closed subsets): \begin{equation} \mathcal X(\sigma,p,q)=\mathcal X(\sigma,p,q)^0\sqcup\mathcal X(\sigma,p,q)^1 \end{equation} where $S^1$ acts almost freely on $\mathcal X(\sigma,p,q)^1$, and suppose that the product/face maps specialize to maps: \begin{align} \mathcal X(\sigma|[0\ldots k],p,q)^0\times\mathcal X(\sigma|[k\ldots n],q,r)^0&\to\mathcal X(\sigma,p,r)^0\\ \mathcal X(\sigma|[0\ldots k],p,q)^0\times\mathcal X(\sigma|[k\ldots n],q,r)^1&\to\mathcal X(\sigma,p,r)^1\\ \mathcal X(\sigma|[0\ldots k],p,q)^1\times\mathcal X(\sigma|[k\ldots n],q,r)^0&\to\mathcal X(\sigma,p,r)^1\\ \mathcal X(\sigma|[0\ldots k],p,q)^1\times\mathcal X(\sigma|[k\ldots n],q,r)^1&\to\mathcal X(\sigma,p,r)^1\\ \mathcal X(\sigma|[0\ldots\hat k\ldots n],p,q)^0&\to\mathcal X(\sigma,p,q)^0\\ \mathcal X(\sigma|[0\ldots\hat k\ldots n],p,q)^1&\to\mathcal X(\sigma,p,q)^1 \end{align} Assume in addition that for any vertex $\sigma^0\in Z_\bullet$, we have $\mathcal X(\sigma^0,p,q)^0=\varnothing\implies\mathcal X(\sigma^i,p,q)^0=\varnothing$ for all $i$ and $p\ne q$. nodes.name: Proof
nodes.statement: \textbf{Part I.}\ We begin by reducing to a situation in which the partition \eqref{partitionsfreefixedII} is extended to every thickened moduli space, so that the product/face maps on thickened moduli spaces also take the form \eqref{PFfirst}--\eqref{PFlast}. Precisely, consider a new implicit atlas $\tilde\mathcal A$ (on the same index set $\mathcal A$) in which the thickened moduli spaces are: \begin{equation} \mathcal X(\sigma,p,q)_{\tilde I}^{\leq\mathfrak s}:=[\mathcal X(\sigma,p,q)_I^{\leq\mathfrak s}\setminus\mathcal X(\sigma,p,q)^1]\sqcup[\mathcal X(\sigma,p,q)_I^{\leq\mathfrak s}\setminus\mathcal X(\sigma,p,q)^0] \end{equation} Now these thickened moduli spaces are by definition equipped with a partition $\mathcal X(\sigma,p,q)_{\tilde I}^{\leq\mathfrak s}=(\mathcal X(\sigma,p,q)_{\tilde I}^{\leq\mathfrak s})^0\sqcup(\mathcal X(\sigma,p,q)_{\tilde I}^{\leq\mathfrak s})^1$ (namely the partition \eqref{newatlastrickSS}), and the natural product/face maps for the implicit atlas $\tilde\mathcal A$ take the form \eqref{PFfirst}--\eqref{PFlast}. The thickened moduli spaces of $\tilde\mathcal A$ are equipped with natural maps to those of $\mathcal A$ (compatibile with the product/face maps); these maps are not open embeddings, but nevertheless the proof of Lemma \ref{homologyopenreduction} applies to give a canonical isomorphism $\mathbb H(\mathcal X)_\mathcal A=\mathbb H(\mathcal X)_{\tilde\mathcal A}$. Thus it suffices to produce an isomorphism $\mathbb H(\mathcal X)_{\tilde\mathcal A}=\mathbb H(\mathcal X^0)_{\tilde\mathcal A^0}$, where $\tilde\mathcal A^0$ is the implicit atlas on $\mathcal X^0$ with thickened moduli spaces $(\mathcal X(\sigma,p,q)_{\tilde I}^{\leq\mathfrak s})^0$. From now on, we will work exclusively with the atlas $\tilde\mathcal A$, which we now rather abusively rename as $\mathcal A$. \textbf{Part II.}\ We will define an isomorphism $\mathbb H(\mathcal X)_\mathcal A=\mathbb H(\mathcal X^0)_{\mathcal A^0}$, where $\mathcal A^0$ is the implicit atlas on $\mathcal X^0$ with thickened moduli spaces $(\mathcal X(\sigma,p,q)_I^{\leq\mathfrak s})^0$. Note that since we have coherent orientations $\omega$ and $S^1$ is connected, it follows that all the flow spaces are locally $S^1$-orientable (see Remark \ref{orientedthenSSoriented}), so we may use the $S^1$-localization machinery freely. Let $\tilde Z_\bullet\to Z_\bullet$ denote the resolution (as in \S\ref{floerhomologyfromMFsets}) associated to $\mathcal X/Z_\bullet$ with the implicit atlas $\mathcal A$, and let $\tilde Z_\bullet^0\to Z_\bullet$ denote the resolution associated to $\mathcal X^0/Z_\bullet$ with the implicit atlas $\mathcal A^0$. We will construct a diagram of the following shape: \begin{equation} \begin{tikzcd}[row sep = large, column sep = tiny] \tilde Z_\bullet\ar{drr}&\tilde Z_\bullet^a\ar{l}\ar{r}\ar{dr}&\tilde Z_\bullet^b\ar{d}&\tilde Z_\bullet^c\ar{l}\ar{r}\ar{dl}&\tilde Z_\bullet^0\ar{dll}\\ &&Z_\bullet \end{tikzcd} \end{equation} and natural diagrams $\widetilde\mathbb H,\widetilde\mathbb H^a,\widetilde\mathbb H^b,\widetilde\mathbb H^c,\widetilde\mathbb H^0$ from $\tilde Z_\bullet,\tilde Z_\bullet^a,\tilde Z_\bullet^b,\tilde Z_\bullet^c,\tilde Z_\bullet^0$ to $\mathsf{N}_{\mathsf{dg}}(\mathsf{Ch}_{R[[H]]})$ (respectively). We will also construct natural isomorphisms relating these and their pullbacks under the horizontal maps in \eqref{differentresolutions}. Finally, we will show that each of the vertical maps \eqref{differentresolutions} satisfies the conclusions of Propositions \ref{trivialKanfibration} and \ref{degenerateID}. The desired result follows easily from these statements; let us now start on the proof. We may consider $\mathcal A(\sigma,p,q)$ as a system of implicit atlases on $\mathcal X(\sigma,p,q)^0$ and on $\mathcal X(\sigma,p,q)^1$ separately. Now consider the following maps (where the complexes on the left are defined analogously to those on the right as in \S\ref{SSaugmentedsec}): \begin{align} C^\bullet_\mathrm{vir}(\partial\mathcal X^0,\mathcal A)^+&\oplus C^\bullet_{S^1,\mathrm{vir}}(\partial\mathcal X^1,\mathcal A)^+&&\to C^\bullet_\mathrm{vir}(\partial\mathcal X;\mathcal A)^+\\ C^\bullet_\mathrm{vir}(\mathcal X^0\operatorname{rel}\partial,\mathcal A)^+&\oplus C^\bullet_{S^1,\mathrm{vir}}(\mathcal X^1\operatorname{rel}\partial,\mathcal A)^+&&\to C^\bullet_\mathrm{vir}(\mathcal X\operatorname{rel}\partial;\mathcal A)^+ \end{align} We give $C^\bullet_\mathrm{vir}(\mathcal X^0\operatorname{rel}\partial,\mathcal A)^+\oplus C^\bullet_{S^1,\mathrm{vir}}(\mathcal X^1\operatorname{rel}\partial,\mathcal A)^+$ the structure of an $\mathsf{F}$-module with product/face maps: \begin{align} C^\bullet_\mathrm{vir}(\mathcal X^0\operatorname{rel}\partial;\mathcal A)^+(\cdots)\otimes C^\bullet_\mathrm{vir}(\mathcal X^0\operatorname{rel}\partial;\mathcal A)^+(\cdots)&\to C^\bullet_\mathrm{vir}(\partial\mathcal X^0;\mathcal A)^+(\cdots)\\ C^\bullet_\mathrm{vir}(\mathcal X^0\operatorname{rel}\partial;\mathcal A)^+(\cdots)\otimes C^\bullet_{S^1,\mathrm{vir}}(\mathcal X^1\operatorname{rel}\partial;\mathcal A)^+(\cdots)&\to C^\bullet_{S^1,\mathrm{vir}}(\partial\mathcal X^1;\mathcal A)^+(\cdots)\\ C^\bullet_{S^1,\mathrm{vir}}(\mathcal X^1\operatorname{rel}\partial;\mathcal A)^+(\cdots)\otimes C^\bullet_\mathrm{vir}(\mathcal X^0\operatorname{rel}\partial;\mathcal A)^+(\cdots)&\to C^\bullet_{S^1,\mathrm{vir}}(\partial\mathcal X^1;\mathcal A)^+(\cdots)\\ C^\bullet_{S^1,\mathrm{vir}}(\mathcal X^1\operatorname{rel}\partial;\mathcal A)^+(\cdots)\otimes C^\bullet_{S^1,\mathrm{vir}}(\mathcal X^1\operatorname{rel}\partial;\mathcal A)^+(\cdots)&\to C^\bullet_{S^1,\mathrm{vir}}(\partial\mathcal X^1;\mathcal A)^+(\cdots)\\ C^\bullet_\mathrm{vir}(\mathcal X^0\operatorname{rel}\partial;\mathcal A)^+(\cdots)&\to C^\bullet_\mathrm{vir}(\partial\mathcal X^0;\mathcal A)^+(\cdots)\\ C^\bullet_{S^1,\mathrm{vir}}(\mathcal X^1\operatorname{rel}\partial;\mathcal A)^+(\cdots)&\to C^\bullet_{S^1,\mathrm{vir}}(\partial\mathcal X^1;\mathcal A)^+(\cdots) \end{align} just as in Definition \ref{Cproductface} (and using the chain models from \S\ref{SSaugmentedsec}). These are compatible with \eqref{partialSSpushforwardbigcomplex}--\eqref{relpartialSSpushforwardbigcomplex} and \eqref{Ccomposition}--\eqref{Csimplexextension}. Next, we consider $C_\bullet(E;\mathcal A)^+\oplus C_{\bullet-1}^{S^1}(E;\mathcal A)^+$ (as in \S\ref{SSaugmentedsec}). Now, there are \emph{two} natural maps: \begin{equation} \begin{tikzcd} C_\bullet(E;\mathcal A)^+\oplus C_{\bullet-1}^{S^1}(E;\mathcal A)^+\ar[yshift=0.5ex]{r}{\operatorname{id}\oplus{\pi^!}}\ar[yshift=-0.5ex]{r}[swap]{\operatorname{id}\oplus 0}&C_\bullet(E;\mathcal A)^+ \end{tikzcd} \end{equation} We give $C_\bullet(E;\mathcal A)^+\oplus C_{\bullet-1}^{S^1}(E;\mathcal A)^+$ the structure of an $\mathsf{F}$-module with product/face maps of the shape \eqref{CSSproductfacesplitfirst}--\eqref{CSSproductfacesplitlast} just as in Definition \ref{CEcomplexaugmented}. Then both maps \eqref{CESSpushforward} are maps of $\mathsf{F}$-modules. There is also a pushforward map: \begin{equation*} C^{\operatorname{vdim}\mathcal X+\bullet}_\mathrm{vir}(\mathcal X^0\operatorname{rel}\partial,\mathcal A)^+\oplus C^{\operatorname{vdim}\mathcal X+\bullet}_{S^1,\mathrm{vir}}(\mathcal X^1\operatorname{rel}\partial,\mathcal A)^+\to C_{-\bullet}(E;\mathcal A)^+\oplus C_{-\bullet-1}^{S^1}(E;\mathcal A)^+ \end{equation*} which is a map of $\mathsf{F}$-modules. Now let us define $\tilde Z_\bullet^a$, $\tilde Z_\bullet^b$, and $\tilde Z_\bullet^c$. We modify the definition of $\tilde Z_\bullet\to Z_\bullet$ (i.e.\ Definition \ref{Lambdadef} as amended in \S\ref{floerhomologyfromMFsets}) as follows. For $\tilde Z_\bullet^a=\tilde Z_\bullet^c$ we replace Definition \ref{Lambdadef}(\ref{lambdachoice},\ref{liftschoice}) with (\ref{lambdachoiceSS},\ref{liftschoiceSS}) below, and for $\tilde Z_\bullet^b$ we replace Definition \ref{Lambdadef}(\ref{lambdachoice},\ref{liftschoice},\ref{augmentationschoice}) with (\ref{lambdachoiceSS},\ref{liftschoiceSS},\ref{augmentationschoiceSS}) below. \begin{rlist} \itemAn $H$-invariant system of chains: \begin{equation*} \lambda=\lambda^0\oplus\lambda^1\in C^\bullet_\mathrm{vir}(\mathcal X^0\operatorname{rel}\partial,\mathcal B)^+\oplus C^\bullet_{S^1,\mathrm{vir}}(\mathcal X^1\operatorname{rel}\partial,\mathcal B)^+ \end{equation*} (degree $0$ and supported inside $\operatorname{supp}\mathcal X$) with the following property. Note that $(\mu,\lambda)$ is a cycle in the mapping cone: \begin{equation*} \begin{matrix} C^\bullet_\mathrm{vir}(\partial f^\ast\mathcal X^0;\mathcal B)^+\cr\oplus\cr C^\bullet_{S^1,\mathrm{vir}}(\partial f^\ast\mathcal X^1;\mathcal B)^+ \end{matrix} \longrightarrow \begin{matrix} C^\bullet_{\mathrm{vir}}(f^\ast\mathcal X^0\operatorname{rel}\partial;\mathcal B)^+\cr\oplus\cr C^\bullet_{S^1,\mathrm{vir}}(f^\ast\mathcal X^1\operatorname{rel}\partial;\mathcal B)^+ \end{matrix} \end{equation*} whose homology is identified with $\check H^\bullet(f^\ast\mathcal X^0;\mathfrak o_{f^\ast\mathcal X^0})\oplus\check H^\bullet((f^\ast\mathcal X^1)/S^1;\pi_\ast\mathfrak o_{f^\ast\mathcal X^1})$, which in degree zero simply equals $\check H^0(f^\ast\mathcal X;\mathfrak o_{f^\ast\mathcal X})$. We require that the homology class of $(\mu,\lambda)$ equal $f^\ast\omega\in\check H^0(f^\ast\mathcal X;\mathfrak o_{f^\ast\mathcal X})$. \itemAn $H$-invariant system of chains $\tilde\lambda$ for $Q[C_\bullet(E;\mathcal A)^+\oplus C_{\bullet-1}^{S^1}(E;\mathcal A)^+]$ (degree $\operatorname{gr}(q)-\operatorname{gr}(p)+\dim\sigma-1$ and supported inside $\operatorname{supp}\mathcal X$) whose image in $C_\bullet(E;\mathcal A)^+\oplus C_{\bullet-1}^{S^1}(E;\mathcal A)^+$ coincides with the image of $\lambda$. \itemAn $H$-invariant map of $\mathsf{F}$-modules $[[E]]:Q[C_\bullet(E;\mathcal A)^+_\mathbb Z\oplus C_{\bullet-1}^{S^1}(E;\mathcal A)^+_\mathbb Z]\to\mathbb Z$ which sends the fundamental class in $H_\bullet(E;\mathcal A)^+_\mathbb Z$ to $1$ and is zero on $H_{\bullet-1}^{S^1}(E;\mathcal A)^+_\mathbb Z$. \end{rlist} The maps $\tilde Z_\bullet\leftarrow\tilde Z_\bullet^a\to\tilde Z_\bullet^b\leftarrow\tilde Z_\bullet^c\to\tilde Z_\bullet^0$ are defined as follows: \begin{equation} \begin{tikzcd} \tilde Z_\bullet&\ar{l}\tilde Z_\bullet^a\ar{r}&\tilde Z_\bullet^b&\ar{l}\tilde Z_\bullet^c\ar{r}&\tilde Z_\bullet^0\cr \lambda&\ar[mapsto]{l}[swap]{\eqref{relpartialSSpushforwardbigcomplex}}\lambda&&\lambda\ar[mapsto]{r}{\lambda=\lambda^0\oplus\lambda^1}&\lambda^0\cr \tilde\lambda&\ar[mapsto]{l}[swap]{Q[\operatorname{id}\oplus\pi^!]}\tilde\lambda&&\tilde\lambda\ar[mapsto]{r}{Q[\operatorname{id}\oplus 0]}&\tilde\lambda^0\cr &{}[[E]]\ar[mapsto]{r}{\circ Q[\operatorname{id}\oplus\pi^!]}&{}[[E]]&\ar[mapsto]{l}[swap]{\circ Q[\operatorname{id}\oplus 0]}\null[[E]] \end{tikzcd} \end{equation} Note that Lemma \ref{trivialactiongysin} shows that the map $\tilde Z^a\to\tilde Z^b$ above produces an $[[E]]$ satisfying (\ref{augmentationschoiceSS}). Now $\widetilde\mathbb H,\widetilde\mathbb H^a,\widetilde\mathbb H^b,\widetilde\mathbb H^c,\widetilde\mathbb H^0$ are defined via the matrix coefficients $c_{\sigma,p,q}$ defined as follows: \begin{align*} \text{for $\widetilde\mathbb H$:}\quad c_{\sigma,p,q}&:=([[E]]_{\sigma,p,q}\otimes\operatorname{id}_R)(\tilde\lambda_{\sigma,p,q})\\ \text{for $\widetilde\mathbb H^a$:}\quad c_{\sigma,p,q}&:=([[E]]_{\sigma,p,q}\otimes\operatorname{id}_R)(\operatorname{id}\oplus\pi^!)(\tilde\lambda_{\sigma,p,q})\\ \text{for $\widetilde\mathbb H^b$:}\quad c_{\sigma,p,q}&:=([[E]]_{\sigma,p,q}\otimes\operatorname{id}_R)(\tilde\lambda_{\sigma,p,q})\\ \text{for $\widetilde\mathbb H^c$:}\quad c_{\sigma,p,q}&:=([[E]]_{\sigma,p,q}\otimes\operatorname{id}_R)(\operatorname{id}\oplus 0)(\tilde\lambda_{\sigma,p,q})\\ \text{for $\widetilde\mathbb H^0$:}\quad c_{\sigma,p,q}&:=([[E]]_{\sigma,p,q}\otimes\operatorname{id}_R)(\tilde\lambda_{\sigma,p,q}) \end{align*} These matrix coefficients give rise to diagrams in $\mathsf{N}_{\mathsf{dg}}(\mathsf{Ch}_{R[[H]]})$ since $[[E]]$ is a map of $\mathsf{F}$-modules. The isomorphisms between these diagrams and their pullbacks under the maps \eqref{defofZabcmaps} are evident. It now remains to show that each of the maps $\tilde Z_\bullet^a,\tilde Z_\bullet^b,\tilde Z_\bullet^c\to\tilde Z_\bullet$ satisfies the conclusions of Propositions \ref{trivialKanfibration} and \ref{degenerateID}. The proof of Proposition \ref{trivialKanfibration} applies to $\tilde Z_\bullet^a,\tilde Z_\bullet^b,\tilde Z_\bullet^c\to\tilde Z_\bullet$ as written (for $\tilde Z_\bullet^b$, the extension of $[[E]]$ step uses the fact that $H_\bullet(E;\mathcal A)\oplus H_{\bullet-1}^{S^1}(E;\mathcal A)$ is concentrated in degrees $\geq 0$ so that Lemma \ref{Hzeroofcofibrantcolimit} still applies). The proof of Proposition \ref{degenerateID} also applies to $\tilde Z_\bullet^a,\tilde Z_\bullet^b,\tilde Z_\bullet^c\to\tilde Z_\bullet$ as written. Now the uniqueness of descent from Lemma \ref{descentofdiagram} shows that there are canonical isomorphisms of the descents $\mathbb H=\mathbb H^a=\mathbb H^b=\mathbb H^c=\mathbb H^0$.
nodes.statement_short: Reduce to an atlas whose thickenings are partitioned too. Then compare resolutions via a zigzag $\tilde Z\leftarrow\tilde Z^a\to\tilde Z^b\leftarrow\tilde Z^c\to\tilde Z^0$ using equivariant chains on $\mathcal X^1$, where the vanishing Gysin map on $E$ kills the $\mathcal X^1$ contribution.

nodes.statement: Let us now fix a smooth almost complex structure $J$ on $X$ which is tamed by $\omega$.
nodes.name: Fixed almost complex structure $J$ on $X$
Nodal curve of type $(g,n)$
nodes.statement: A \emph{nodal curve of type $(g,n)$} is a compact nodal Riemann surface $C$ of arithmetic genus $g$ along with an injective function $l:\{1,\ldots,n\}\to C$ (the ``$n$ marked points'') whose image is disjoint from the nodes of $C$. An \emph{isomorphism $(C,l)\to(C',l')$ of curves of type $(g,n)$} is an isomorphism of Riemann surfaces $\iota:C\to C'$ such that $l'=\iota\circ l$. We usually omit $l$ from the notation. Such a curve is called \emph{stable} iff its automorphism group is finite.
nodes.statement_short: A nodal curve of type (g,n) is a compact nodal Riemann surface of genus g with n distinct marked smooth points; stable iff finite automorphism group.
differentia: arithmetic genus $g$

nodes.statement: We denote by $\overline{\mathcal M}_{g,n}$ the Deligne--Mumford moduli space of stable nodal curves of type $(g,n)$, and we denote by $\overline{\mathcal C}_{g,n}\to\overline{\mathcal M}_{g,n}$ the universal family (which coincides with the ``forget the last marked point and stabilize'' map $\overline{\mathcal M}_{g,n+1}\to\overline{\mathcal M}_{g,n}$).
nodes.name: Deligne--Mumford moduli space
nodes.statement_short: Mbar_{g,n} is the Deligne-Mumford space of stable (g,n)-curves, Cbar_{g,n} its universal family.

nodes.name: $J$-holomorphic map
nodes.statement: A \emph{$J$-holomorphic map of type $(g,n)$} is a pair $(C,u)$ where $C$ is a nodal curve of type $(g,n)$ and $u:C\to X$ is smooth and satisfies $\bar\partial u=0$. An \emph{isomorphism $(C,u)\to(C',u')$ of $J$-holomorphic maps of type $(g,n)$} is an isomorphism $\iota:C\to C'$ of curves of type $(g,n)$ such that $u=u'\circ\iota$. We say a $J$-holomorphic map is \emph{stable} iff its automorphism group (i.e.\ group of self-isomorphisms) is finite.
nodes.statement_short: A J-holomorphic map of type (g,n) is a nodal curve with a smooth map u satisfying the Cauchy-Riemann equation; stable iff finite automorphisms.

nodes.name: Moduli space of stable maps
nodes.statement: Let $\beta\in H_2(X,\mathbb Z)$. We define $\overline{\mathcal M}_{g,n}^\beta(X)$ as the set of stable $J$-holomorphic maps of type $(g,n)$ for which $u_\ast[C]=\beta$. We equip $\overline{\mathcal M}_{g,n}^\beta(X)$ with the Gromov topology, which is well-known to be compact Hausdorff.
nodes.statement_short: The moduli space of stable J-holomorphic maps of type (g,n) in class beta, with the compact Hausdorff Gromov topology.

nodes.statement: A neighborhood base\footnote{A \emph{neighborhood} of a point $x$ in a topological space $X$ is a subset $N\subseteq X$ such that $x\in N^\circ$ (the interior). A \emph{neighborhood base} at a point $x\in X$ is a collection of neighborhoods $\{N_\alpha\}$ of $x$ such that for every open $U\subseteq X$ containing $x$, there exists some $N_\alpha\subseteq U$. A neighborhood base is necessarily nonempty and \emph{filtered}, i.e.\ for all $\alpha,\beta$, there exists $\gamma$ with $N_\gamma\subseteq N_\alpha\cap N_\beta$. Conversely, given a set $X$ and for every $x\in X$ a nonempty filtered collection of subsets $\{N_\alpha^x\}$ each containing $x$, there is a unique topology on $X$ such that $\{N^x_\alpha\}$ is a neighborhood base at $x$ for all $x\in X$.} at a pair $(C,u)$ may be obtained as follows. We choose some additional $\ell$ marked points on $C$ so that it has no automorphisms fixing these points, and we consider the graph $\Gamma_u\subseteq X\times\overline{\mathcal C}_{g,n+\ell}$ where $\overline{\mathcal C}_{g,n+\ell}\to\overline{\mathcal M}_{g,n+\ell}$ denotes the universal curve. A neighborhood base at $(C,u)$ is obtained taking all $J$-holomorphic maps from curves in $\overline{\mathcal M}_{g,n+\ell}$ whose graph is close to $\Gamma_u$ in the Hausdorff topology (and forgetting the $\ell$ extra marked points). Choosing different $\ell'$ marked points yields an equivalent neighborhood base.
nodes.name: Gromov topology
nodes.statement_short: Neighborhoods of a stable map: maps from stabilized nearby curves whose graphs are Hausdorff-close to the graph of u.

nodes.name: Index set $A^\mathrm{GW}$ (Gromov--Witten thickening datum)
nodes.statement: A \emph{(Gromov--Witten) thickening datum} $\alpha$ is a 6-tuple $(D_\alpha,r_\alpha,\Gamma_\alpha,\overline{\mathcal M}_\alpha,E_\alpha,\lambda_\alpha)$ where: \begin{rlist} \item$D_\alpha\to X$ is a compact smooth embedded codimension two submanifold with boundary. \item$r_\alpha\geq 0$ is an integer such that $2g+n+r_\alpha>2$. \item$\Gamma_\alpha$ is a finite group. \item$\overline{\mathcal M}_\alpha$ is a smooth $\Gamma_\alpha$-manifold\footnote{Note that we do not assume $\Gamma_\alpha$ acts effectively on $\overline{\mathcal M}_\alpha$. Indeed, $\overline{\mathcal M}_{1,1}$ and $\overline{\mathcal M}_{2,0}$ are ineffective orbifolds, so we must allow ineffective actions if we want $\overline{\mathcal M}_\alpha/\Gamma_\alpha$ to be isomorphic to an open subset of one of these spaces.} equipped with an isomorphism of orbifolds between $\overline{\mathcal M}_\alpha/\Gamma_\alpha$ and an open subset of $\overline{\mathcal M}_{g,n+r_\alpha}/S_{r_\alpha}$ (let $\overline{\mathcal C}_\alpha\to\overline{\mathcal M}_\alpha$ be the pullback\footnote{Pullback here means the orbifold fiber product (see Remark \ref{orbifoldfiberproductrmk}). Note that the fibers of $\overline{\mathcal C}_\alpha\to\overline{\mathcal M}_\alpha$ are nodal curves of type $(g,n+r_\alpha)$ (not quotiented by their automorphism group).} of the universal family; the action of $\Gamma_\alpha$ on $\overline{\mathcal M}_\alpha$ lifts canonically to $\overline{\mathcal C}_\alpha$ by the universal property of the pullback). \item$E_\alpha$ is a finitely generated $\mathbb R[\Gamma_\alpha]$-module. \item$\lambda_\alpha:E_\alpha\to C^\infty(\overline{\mathcal C}_\alpha\times X,\Omega^{0,1}_{\overline{\mathcal C}_\alpha/\overline{\mathcal M}_\alpha}\otimes_\mathbb C TX)$ is a $\Gamma_\alpha$-equivariant linear map supported away from the nodes and marked points of the fibers of $\overline{\mathcal C}_\alpha\to\overline{\mathcal M}_\alpha$. \end{rlist} Let $A^{\mathrm{GW}}$ denote the set\footnote{The reader concerned with set theoretic issues may wish to add ``rigidifying data'' to the definition of a thickening datum as in Remark \ref{notsetremark}.} of all thickening datums.
nodes.statement_short: A GW thickening datum is a divisor D, a count r, a finite group, a local chart of Mbar_{g,n+r}, an obstruction space E and a perturbation map lambda; A^GW is the set of all of them.
nodes.label: divisorthicken

nodes.name: Transversality of smooth maps
nodes.statement: Let $u:C\to X$ be a smooth map from a nodal curve of type $(g,n)$, and let $D\subseteq X$ be a smooth codimension two submanifold with boundary. We say \emph{$u$ is transverse to $D$} (written $u\pitchfork D$) iff $u^{-1}(\partial D)=0$ and $\forall\,p\in u^{-1}(D)$, the derivative $du:T_pC\to T_{u(p)}X/T_{u(p)}D$ is surjective and $p$ is neither a node nor a marked point of $C$.
nodes.statement_short: u is transverse to a codimension-two submanifold D if it misses the boundary of D and meets D transversally away from nodes and marked points.

nodes.name: $I$-thickened $J$-holomorphic map
nodes.statement: Let $I\subseteq A^\mathrm{GW}$ be a finite subset. An \emph{$I$-thickened $J$-holomorphic map of type $(g,n)$} is a quadruple $(C,u,\{\phi_\alpha\}_{\alpha\in I},\{e_\alpha\}_{\alpha\in I})$ where: \begin{rlist} \item$C$ is a nodal curve of type $(g,n)$. \item$u:C\to X$ is a smooth map such that $u\pitchfork D_\alpha$ with exactly $r_\alpha$ intersections for all $\alpha\in I$. \item$\phi_\alpha:C\to\overline{\mathcal C}_\alpha$ an isomorphism between $C$ (with $r_\alpha$ extra marked points $u^{-1}(D_\alpha)$) and some fiber of $\overline{\mathcal C}_\alpha\to\overline{\mathcal M}_\alpha$. \item$e_\alpha\in E_\alpha$. \item The following \emph{$I$-thickened $\bar\partial$-equation} is satisfied: \begin{equation} \bar\partial u+\sum_{\alpha\in I}\lambda_\alpha(e_\alpha)(\phi_\alpha,u)=0 \end{equation} This equation takes place in $C^\infty(\tilde C,\Omega^{0,1}_{\tilde C}\otimes_\mathbb C u^\ast TX)$. Certainly $\bar\partial u$ is a smooth section of $\Omega^{0,1}_{\tilde C}\otimes_\mathbb C u^\ast TX$ over $\tilde C$. To interpret $\lambda_\alpha(e_\alpha)(\phi_\alpha,u)$ as such a section, consider the following composition: \begin{equation} C\xrightarrow{(\phi_\alpha,u)}\overline{\mathcal C}_\alpha\times X\xrightarrow{\lambda(e_\alpha)}\Omega^{0,1}_{\overline{\mathcal C}_\alpha/\overline{\mathcal M}_\alpha}\otimes_\mathbb C TX \end{equation} This sends a point $p\in C$ to an element of $(\Omega^{0,1}_{\overline{\mathcal C}_\alpha/\overline{\mathcal M}_\alpha})_{\phi_\alpha(p)}\otimes T_{u(p)}X$, which we identify via $\phi_\alpha$ with $(\Omega^{0,1}_C\otimes_\mathbb C u^\ast TX)_p$. This is what we mean by $\lambda_\alpha(e_\alpha)(\phi_\alpha,u)$. \end{rlist} An \emph{isomorphism} $\iota:(C,u,\{\phi_\alpha\}_{\alpha\in I},\{e_\alpha\}_{\alpha\in I})\to(C',u',\{\phi_\alpha'\}_{\alpha\in I},\{e_\alpha'\}_{\alpha\in I})$ between two $I$-thickened $J$-holomorphic maps of type $(g,n)$ is an isomorphism $\iota:C\to C'$ of curves of $(g,n)$-type such that $u=u'\circ\iota$, $\phi_\alpha=\phi_\alpha'\circ\iota$, and $e_\alpha=e_\alpha'$. We say an $I$-thickened $J$-holomorphic map is \emph{stable} iff its automorphism group (i.e.\ group of self-isomorphisms) is finite.
nodes.statement_short: An I-thickened J-holomorphic map is a curve with map u transverse to the divisors D_alpha, identifications phi_alpha with fibers, and e_alpha solving the perturbed dbar-equation.
nodes.label: thickendefs

nodes.name: $I$-thickened $\bar\partial$-equation
nodes.statement: \bar\partial u+\sum_{\alpha\in I}\lambda_\alpha(e_\alpha)(\phi_\alpha,u)=0
nodes.label: complementeddelbar

nodes.name: Composition interpreting $\lambda_\alpha(e_\alpha)(\phi_\alpha,u)$
nodes.statement: C\xrightarrow{(\phi_\alpha,u)}\overline{\mathcal C}_\alpha\times X\xrightarrow{\lambda(e_\alpha)}\Omega^{0,1}_{\overline{\mathcal C}_\alpha/\overline{\mathcal M}_\alpha}\otimes_\mathbb C TX

nodes.name: Atlas data for $A^\mathrm{GW}$
nodes.statement: We define $\overline{\mathcal M}_{g,n}^\beta(X)_I$ as the set of isomorphism classes of stable $I$-thickened $J$-holomorphic maps of type $(g,n)$ such that $u_\ast[C]=\beta$. Equip $\overline{\mathcal M}_{g,n}^\beta(X)_I$ with the Gromov topology\footnote{When $I\ne\varnothing$, this topology is easy to define: it is simply given by using the Hausdorff distance on the image $C\subseteq X\times\prod_{\alpha\in I}\overline{\mathcal C}_\alpha$.} for $(u,\phi_\alpha)$ and with the obvious topology for $e_\alpha$. It is clear by definition that $\overline{\mathcal M}_{g,n}^\beta(X)=\overline{\mathcal M}_{g,n}^\beta(X)_\varnothing$. There is an evident action $\Gamma_I$ on $\overline{\mathcal M}_{g,n}^\beta(X)_I$, namely $\{g_\alpha\}_{\alpha\in I}\cdot(u,\{\phi_\alpha\}_{\alpha\in I},\{e_\alpha\}_{\alpha\in I})=(u,\{g_\alpha\cdot\phi_\alpha\}_{\alpha\in I},\{g_\alpha\cdot e_\alpha\}_{\alpha\in I})$ which works since $\lambda_\alpha(e_\alpha)(\phi_\alpha,u)=\lambda_\alpha(g_\alpha\cdot e_\alpha)(g_\alpha\cdot\phi_\alpha,u)$ by $\Gamma_\alpha$-equivariance. There are evident maps $s_\alpha:\overline{\mathcal M}_{g,n}^\beta(X)_I\to E_\alpha$ simply picking out $e_\alpha$. For $I\subseteq J\subseteq A^\mathrm{GW}$, there is an obvious forgetful map $\psi_{IJ}:(s_{J\setminus I}|\overline{\mathcal M}_{g,n}^\beta(X)_J)^{-1}(0)\to\overline{\mathcal M}_{g,n}^\beta(X)_I$. Let $U_{IJ}\subseteq\overline{\mathcal M}_{g,n}^\beta(X)_I$ consist of those elements such that $u\pitchfork D_\alpha$ with exactly $r_\alpha$ intersections for all $\alpha\in J\setminus I$ and such that adding these extra marked points makes $C$ isomorphic to a fiber of $\overline{\mathcal C}_\alpha\to\overline{\mathcal M}_\alpha$. It's not too hard to see that this is an open set (using elliptic regularity).
nodes.statement_short: Thickened moduli spaces of stable I-thickened maps, with Gamma_I action, Kuranishi maps s_alpha picking e_alpha, forgetful footprint maps psi_IJ and open footprints U_IJ.
nodes.label: GWatlasdatadef

nodes.statement: The compatibility axioms are all immediate, though let us justify the homeomorphism axiom. First, we claim that the map $(s_{J\setminus I}|\overline{\mathcal M}_{g,n}^\beta(X)_J)^{-1}(0)/\Gamma_{J\setminus I}\to U_{IJ}\subseteq\overline{\mathcal M}_{g,n}^\beta(X)_I$ induced by $\psi_{IJ}$ is a bijection. This is more or less clear: fixing an element of $U_{IJ}$, an inverse image must have $e_\alpha=0$ for $\alpha\in J\setminus I$, and by definition of $U_{IJ}$, there exists a suitable $\phi_\alpha$ which is clearly unique up to the action of $\Gamma_\alpha$ for $\alpha\in J\setminus I$. That the topologies coincide can be checked directly from their definition.
nodes.name: Homeomorphism axiom for $A^\mathrm{GW}$
nodes.statement_short: The GW atlas data satisfy the compatibility axioms; psi_IJ induces a bijection from the zero set mod Gamma onto U_IJ which is a homeomorphism.

nodes.name: Regular locus for $A^\mathrm{GW}$
nodes.statement: We define $\overline{\mathcal M}_{g,n}^\beta(X)_I^\mathrm{reg}\subseteq\overline{\mathcal M}_{g,n}^\beta(X)_I$. Let $(C,u_0,\{\phi_\alpha\}_{\alpha\in I},\{e_\alpha\}_{\alpha\in I})\in\overline{\mathcal M}_{g,n}^\beta(X)_I$. Roughly speaking, this point is contained in $\overline{\mathcal M}_{g,n}^\beta(X)_I^\mathrm{reg}$ iff it has trivial automorphism group and the ``vertical'' (i.e.\ from a fixed domain curve) linearized version of the $I$-thickened $\bar\partial$-equation \eqref{complementeddelbar} is surjective. Let us now make this precise. Consider the smooth Banach manifold $W^{k,p}(C,X)$ for some large integer $k$ and some $p\in(1,\infty)$. Note that the condition $u\pitchfork D_\alpha$ with exactly $r_\alpha$ intersections making $C$ isomorphic to a fiber of $\overline{\mathcal C}_\alpha/\overline{\mathcal M}_\alpha$ (for all $\alpha\in I$) forms an open subset of $W^{k,p}(C,X)$ containing $u_0$. Furthermore, there is a unique continuous choice of: \begin{equation} C\times W^{k,p}(C,X)\to\overline{\mathcal C}_\alpha \end{equation} over $C$ times a neighborhood of $u_0$ which extends $\phi_\alpha$ on $C\times\{u_0\}$ (this holds because $\overline{\mathcal M}_\alpha\to\overline{\mathcal M}_{g,n+r_\alpha}/S_{r_\alpha}$ is an \'etale map of orbifolds). One can also check that this map \eqref{phiparametric} is highly differentiable (this depends on $k$ being large). Now we consider the smooth Banach bundle whose fiber over $(u,\{e_\alpha\}_{\alpha\in I})\in W^{k,p}(C,X)\times E_I$ is $W^{k-1,p}(\tilde C,\Omega^{0,1}_{\tilde C}\otimes_\mathbb C u^\ast TX)$ (where $\tilde C$ is the normalization of $C$). Now the left hand side of \eqref{complementeddelbar} (using \eqref{phiparametric} in place of $\phi_\alpha$) is a highly differentiable section of this bundle. We say that $(C,u_0,\{\phi_\alpha\}_{\alpha\in I},\{e_\alpha\}_{\alpha\in I})\in\overline{\mathcal M}_{g,n}^\beta(X)_I^\mathrm{reg}$ iff the following two conditions hold: \begin{rlist} \item This section is transverse to the zero section at $(u_0,e_\alpha)$. \item The automorphism group of $(C,u_0,\{\phi_\alpha\}_{\alpha\in I},\{e_\alpha\}_{\alpha\in I})$ is trivial. \end{rlist} It is an easy exercise in elliptic regularity to show that the first condition is independent of the choice of $(k,p)$ (as long as $k$ is sufficiently large so that the condition makes sense).
nodes.statement_short: A thickened map is regular iff its automorphism group is trivial and the vertical linearized thickened dbar-operator is transverse to zero.
nodes.label: regularsubsetdefinition

nodes.name: Parametric extension of $\phi_\alpha$
nodes.statement: C\times W^{k,p}(C,X)\to\overline{\mathcal C}_\alpha
nodes.label: phiparametric

nodes.name: Virtual dimension of $\overline{\mathcal M}_{g,n}^\beta(X)$
nodes.statement: \operatorname{vdim}\overline{\mathcal M}_{g,n}^\beta(X):=\dim\overline{\mathcal M}_{g,n}+(1-g)\dim X+2\langle c_1(X),\beta\rangle

Let us now verify the transversality axioms. Freeness of the action of $\Gamma_{J\setminus I}$ on $\psi_{IJ}^{-1}(X_I^\mathrm{reg})$ follows from the fact that points in $X_I^\mathrm{reg}$ have trivial automorphism group. The openness and submersion axioms follow from the following result, whose proof is given in Appendix \ref{gluingappendix}.
nodes.name: Transversality axioms for $A^\mathrm{GW}$
nodes.statement_short: Freeness follows from trivial automorphism groups of regular points; openness and submersion follow from the gluing proposition.

nodes.name: Formal regularity implies topological regularity (Gromov--Witten)
nodes.statement: For all $I\subseteq J\subseteq A^\mathrm{GW}$, we have: \begin{rlist} \item$\overline{\mathcal M}_{g,n}^\beta(X)^\mathrm{reg}_I\subseteq\overline{\mathcal M}_{g,n}^\beta(X)_I$ is an open subset. \itemThe map $s_{J\setminus I}:\overline{\mathcal M}_{g,n}^\beta(X)_J\to E_{J\setminus I}$ is locally modeled on the projection: \begin{equation} \mathbb R^{\operatorname{vdim}\overline{\mathcal M}_{g,n}^\beta(X)+\dim E_I}\times\mathbb R^{\dim E_{J\setminus I}}\to\mathbb R^{\dim E_{J\setminus I}} \end{equation} over $\psi_{IJ}^{-1}(\overline{\mathcal M}_{g,n}^\beta(X)_I^\mathrm{reg}))\subseteq\overline{\mathcal M}_{g,n}^\beta(X)_J$. \itemThere is a canonical identification of the orientation local system $\mathfrak o_{\overline{\mathcal M}_{g,n}^\beta(X)_I^\mathrm{reg}}$ with $\mathfrak o_{E_I}$ (by the standard reduction to the canonical orientation of a complex linear Fredholm operator as in McDuff--Salamon \cite{mcduffsalamonJholquant,mcduffsalamonJholsymp}). \end{rlist}
nodes.statement_short: The regular loci of the GW thickenings are open, s_{J\I} is locally a projection (submersion) there, and their orientation sheaves are identified with that of E_I.
assumptions: For all $I\subseteq J\subseteq A^\mathrm{GW}$
conclusions: $\overline{\mathcal M}_{g,n}^\beta(X)^\mathrm{reg}_I\subseteq\overline{\mathcal M}_{g,n}^\beta(X)_I$ is an open subset.

The map $s_{J\setminus I}:\overline{\mathcal M}_{g,n}^\beta(X)_J\to E_{J\setminus I}$ is locally modeled on the projection: \begin{equation} \mathbb R^{\operatorname{vdim}\overline{\mathcal M}_{g,n}^\beta(X)+\dim E_I}\times\mathbb R^{\dim E_{J\setminus I}}\to\mathbb R^{\dim E_{J\setminus I}} \end{equation} over $\psi_{IJ}^{-1}(\overline{\mathcal M}_{g,n}^\beta(X)_I^\mathrm{reg}))\subseteq\overline{\mathcal M}_{g,n}^\beta(X)_J$.

There is a canonical identification of the orientation local system $\mathfrak o_{\overline{\mathcal M}_{g,n}^\beta(X)_I^\mathrm{reg}}$ with $\mathfrak o_{E_I}$ (by the standard reduction to the canonical orientation of a complex linear Fredholm operator as in McDuff--Salamon \cite{mcduffsalamonJholquant,mcduffsalamonJholsymp}).
nodes.label: GWgluingneeded

nodes.name: Local model projection (Gromov--Witten)
nodes.statement: \mathbb R^{\operatorname{vdim}\overline{\mathcal M}_{g,n}^\beta(X)+\dim E_I}\times\mathbb R^{\dim E_{J\setminus I}}\to\mathbb R^{\dim E_{J\setminus I}}
