Near points of $\overline{\mathcal M}_{g,n}^\beta(X)^\mathrm{reg}_I$ with smooth domain curve, the proposition follows from standard techniques (implicit function theorem, elliptic regularity, and an index theorem). The real content of the proposition is that it holds near points with nodal domain curve.
nodes.name: Content of the gluing proposition
Sard-type divisor lemma
nodes.statement: Let $f:N^n\to M^m$ be a smooth map of smooth manifolds with $n\leq m$. Then for every $p\in N$ with $df_p$ injective and every neighborhood $U$ of $f(p)$, there exists a codimension $n$ smooth submanifold with boundary $D\subseteq M$ contained in $U$ such that $f\pitchfork D$ and $f^{-1}(D)$ contains a point arbitrarily close to $p$.
nodes.statement_short: Near a point where df is injective one can find a codimension-n submanifold D transverse to f meeting f near that point.
assumptions: Let $f:N^n\to M^m$ be a smooth map of smooth manifolds with $n\leq m$.
conclusions: for every $p\in N$ with $df_p$ injective and every neighborhood $U$ of $f(p)$, there exists a codimension $n$ smooth submanifold with boundary $D\subseteq M$ contained in $U$ such that $f\pitchfork D$ and $f^{-1}(D)$ contains a point arbitrarily close to $p$.
nodes.label: sortofsard

nodes.name: Proof
nodes.statement: After possibly shrinking $U$, choose a local projection $\pi:U\to T_pN$. Then let $D$ be $\pi^{-1}$ of a regular value of $\pi\circ f$ (which exists by Sard's theorem).
nodes.statement_short: Take D as the preimage of a regular value of a local projection composed with f, which exists by Sard's theorem.

nodes.name: Domain stabilization for stable $J$-holomorphic maps
nodes.statement: Let $u:C\to X$ be a stable $J$-holomorphic map. Then there exists a smooth codimension two submanifold with boundary $D\subseteq X$ such that $u\pitchfork D$ and adding $u^{-1}(D)$ to $C$ as extra marked points makes $C$ stable.
nodes.statement_short: Every stable J-holomorphic map admits a transverse codimension-two divisor whose preimages stabilize the domain.
assumptions: Let $u:C\to X$ be a stable $J$-holomorphic map.
conclusions: there exists a smooth codimension two submanifold with boundary $D\subseteq X$ such that $u\pitchfork D$ and adding $u^{-1}(D)$ to $C$ as extra marked points makes $C$ stable.
nodes.label: stabilizationlemma

nodes.name: Proof
nodes.statement: Let us observe that if $C_0\subseteq C$ is any unstable irreducible component, we must have $u:C_0\to X$ is nonconstant. Hence since $u$ is $J$-holomorphic, it follows that there is a point on $C_0$ (which is not a node or marked point) where $du$ is injective. It follows using Lemma \ref{sortofsard} that there exists $D\subseteq X$ such that $u\pitchfork D$ and adding $u^{-1}(D)$ to $C$ as marked points makes $C$ stable.
nodes.statement_short: Unstable components are nonconstant so du is injective somewhere; apply the Sard-type divisor lemma there.

nodes.name: Covering axiom for $A^\mathrm{GW}$
nodes.statement: We have: \begin{equation} \overline{\mathcal M}_{g,n}^\beta(X)=\bigcup_{I\subseteq A^\mathrm{GW}}\psi_{\varnothing I}((s_I|\overline{\mathcal M}_{g,n}^\beta(X)_I^\mathrm{reg})^{-1}(0)) \end{equation}
nodes.statement_short: Every stable map lies in the footprint of the zero set of the regular locus of some thickening datum.
conclusions: \overline{\mathcal M}_{g,n}^\beta(X)=\bigcup_{I\subseteq A^\mathrm{GW}}\psi_{\varnothing I}((s_I|\overline{\mathcal M}_{g,n}^\beta(X)_I^\mathrm{reg})^{-1}(0))
nodes.label: everythingcanbethickened

nodes.name: Covering identity for $A^\mathrm{GW}$
nodes.statement: \overline{\mathcal M}_{g,n}^\beta(X)=\bigcup_{I\subseteq A^\mathrm{GW}}\psi_{\varnothing I}((s_I|\overline{\mathcal M}_{g,n}^\beta(X)_I^\mathrm{reg})^{-1}(0))

nodes.name: Proof
nodes.statement: Fix a point in $\overline{\mathcal M}_{g,n}^\beta(X)$ (that is, a curve $u:C\to X$). We will construct $\alpha\in A^\mathrm{GW}$ so that this point is contained in $\psi_{\varnothing\{\alpha\}}((s_\alpha|\overline{\mathcal M}_{g,n}^\beta(X)_{\{\alpha\}}^\mathrm{reg})^{-1}(0))$. First, pick $D_\alpha\subseteq X$ satisfying the conclusion of Lemma \ref{stabilizationlemma}. Now let $r_\alpha=\#u^{-1}(D_\alpha)$. Adding $u^{-1}(D_\alpha)$ as extra marked points to $C$ gives a point in $\overline{\mathcal M}_{g,n+r_\alpha}/S_{r_\alpha}$, and we pick some local orbifold chart $\overline{\mathcal M}_\alpha/\Gamma_\alpha\to\overline{\mathcal M}_{g,n+r_\alpha}/S_{r_\alpha}$ covering this point. Now let us consider the linearized $\bar\partial$ operator: \begin{equation} D\bar\partial(u,\cdot):C^\infty(C,u^\ast TX)\to C^\infty(\tilde C,\Omega^{0,1}_{\tilde C}\otimes_\mathbb C u^\ast TX) \end{equation} ($\tilde C$ being the normalization of $C$) where $C^\infty(C,u^\ast TX)\subseteq C^\infty(\tilde C,u^\ast TX)$ is the subspace of functions descending continuously to $C$. If $(k,p)\in\mathbb Z_{\geq 1}\times(1,\infty)$ with $kp>2$, then we get a corresponding $D\bar\partial(u,\cdot)$ map $W^{k,p}\to W^{k-1,p}$ (the restriction on $(k,p)$ comes from the need to define $W^{k,p}(C,u^\ast TX)\subseteq W^{k,p}(\tilde C,u^\ast TX)$). This operator is Fredholm; in particular its cokernel is finite-dimensional. Suppose we have a finite-dimensional vector space $E_0$ equipped with a linear map: \begin{equation} \tilde\lambda_0:E_0\to C^\infty(\tilde C,\Omega^{0,1}_{\tilde C}\otimes_\mathbb C u^\ast TX) \end{equation} supported away from (the inverse image in $\tilde C$ of) the nodes and marked points of $C$. Then the following conditions are equivalent (exercise using elliptic regularity): \begin{rlist} \item\eqref{lambdazero} is surjective onto the cokernel of $D\bar\partial(u,\cdot):C^\infty\to C^\infty$. \item\eqref{lambdazero} is surjective onto the cokernel of $D\bar\partial(u,\cdot):W^{k,p}\to W^{k-1,p}$ for some $(k,p)$. \item\eqref{lambdazero} is surjective onto the cokernel of $D\bar\partial(u,\cdot):W^{k,p}\to W^{k-1,p}$ for all $(k,p)$. \end{rlist} There exists such a pair $E_0$ and $\tilde\lambda_0$ satisfying these conditions since we may choose $k=1$ and $p>2$ and then remember that $C^\infty$ functions supported away from the nodes and marked points are dense in $W^{0,p}=L^p$. Now pick any isomorphism to a fiber $\phi_\alpha:C\to\overline{\mathcal C}_\alpha$ and extend $\tilde\lambda_0$ to a map $\lambda_0:E_0\to C^\infty(\overline{\mathcal C}_\alpha\times X,\Omega^{0,1}_{\overline{\mathcal C}_\alpha/\overline{\mathcal M}_\alpha}\otimes_\mathbb C TX)$ supported away from the nodes and marked points of the fibers. Define $E_\alpha=E_0[\Gamma]$ and define $\lambda_\alpha:E_\alpha\to C^\infty(\overline{\mathcal C}_\alpha\times X,\Omega^{0,1}_{\overline{\mathcal C}_\alpha/\overline{\mathcal M}_\alpha}\otimes_\mathbb C TX)$ by $\Gamma_\alpha$-linear extension from $\lambda_0$. It is now clear by definition that $u:C\to X$ is covered by $\overline{\mathcal M}_{g,n}^\beta(X)_{\{\alpha\}}^\mathrm{reg}$, where $\alpha\in A^\mathrm{GW}$ is the element just constructed.
nodes.statement_short: Construct a single thickening datum: stabilizing divisor, local orbifold chart, and an obstruction space E_0 mapping onto the cokernel of the linearized dbar-operator, made Gamma-equivariant.

nodes.name: Linearized $\bar\partial$ operator
nodes.statement: D\bar\partial(u,\cdot):C^\infty(C,u^\ast TX)\to C^\infty(\tilde C,\Omega^{0,1}_{\tilde C}\otimes_\mathbb C u^\ast TX)
nodes.label: linearizeddelbarforthickening

nodes.name: Perturbation map $\tilde\lambda_0$
nodes.statement: \tilde\lambda_0:E_0\to C^\infty(\tilde C,\Omega^{0,1}_{\tilde C}\otimes_\mathbb C u^\ast TX)
nodes.label: lambdazero

nodes.statement: We have now shown the following.
nodes.name: Proof that $A^\mathrm{GW}$ is an implicit atlas
nodes.statement_short: Assemble the verified compatibility, transversality and covering axioms.

nodes.name: $A^\mathrm{GW}$ is an implicit atlas
nodes.statement: $A^\mathrm{GW}$ is an implicit atlas on $\overline{\mathcal M}_{g,n}^\beta(X)$.
conclusions: $A^\mathrm{GW}$ is an implicit atlas on $\overline{\mathcal M}_{g,n}^\beta(X)$.

nodes.name: Gromov--Witten invariants
nodes.statement: Fix nonnegative integers $g$ and $n$ with $2g+n>2$, and fix $\beta\in H_2(X;\mathbb Z)$. By Proposition \ref{GWgluingneeded}, the virtual orientation sheaf induced by $A^\mathrm{GW}$ is canonically trivialized. Thus the implicit atlas $A^\mathrm{GW}$ induces a virtual fundamental class $[\overline{\mathcal M}_{g,n}^\beta(X)]^\mathrm{vir}\in\check H^\bullet(\overline{\mathcal M}_{g,n}^\beta(X);\mathbb Q)^\vee$. We define the \emph{Gromov--Witten invariant}: \begin{equation} \mathrm{GW}_{g,n}^\beta(X)\in H_\bullet(\overline{\mathcal M}_{g,n}\times X^n;\mathbb Q) \end{equation} as the pushforward of $[\overline{\mathcal M}_{g,n}^\beta(X)]^\mathrm{vir}$ under the tautological map $\overline{\mathcal M}_{g,n}^\beta(X)\to\overline{\mathcal M}_{g,n}\times X^n$. This is well-defined by the next lemma.
nodes.statement_short: GW_{g,n}^beta(X) is the pushforward of the virtual fundamental class of the stable map moduli space to H_*(Mbar_{g,n} x X^n; Q).

nodes.name: Gromov--Witten invariant class
nodes.statement: \mathrm{GW}_{g,n}^\beta(X)\in H_\bullet(\overline{\mathcal M}_{g,n}\times X^n;\mathbb Q)

nodes.name: Independence of Gromov--Witten invariants from $J$
nodes.statement: $\mathrm{GW}_{g,n}^\beta(X)\in H_\bullet(\overline{\mathcal M}_{g,n}\times X^n)$ is independent of the choice of $J$.
conclusions: $\mathrm{GW}_{g,n}^\beta(X)\in H_\bullet(\overline{\mathcal M}_{g,n}\times X^n)$ is independent of the choice of $J$.

nodes.name: Proof
nodes.statement: Let $J_0$ and $J_1$ be any two smooth $\omega$-tame almost complex structures on $X$. We denote by $\overline{\mathcal M}_{g,n}^\beta(X,J_0)$ and $\overline{\mathcal M}_{g,n}^\beta(X,J_1)$ the corresponding moduli spaces of stable maps (denoted earlier by simply $\overline{\mathcal M}_{g,n}^\beta(X)$ when we considered just a fixed $J$). There exists a smooth path of $\omega$-tame almost complex structures $J_{[0,1]}=\{J_t\}_{t\in[0,1]}$ connecting $J_0$ and $J_1$. Let us consider the corresponding ``parameterized'' moduli space of stable maps $\overline{\mathcal M}_{g,n}^\beta(X,J_{[0,1]})$. The construction from \S\ref{gromovwittenimplicitatlassubsection} gives an implicit atlas with boundary $A^\mathrm{GW}$ on $\overline{\mathcal M}_{g,n}^\beta(X,J_{[0,1]})$ whose restriction to $\partial\overline{\mathcal M}_{g,n}^\beta(X,J_{[0,1]}):=\overline{\mathcal M}_{g,n}^\beta(X,J_0)\sqcup\overline{\mathcal M}_{g,n}^\beta(X,J_1)$ agrees with $A^\mathrm{GW}$ on these spaces. Hence it follows using Lemmas \ref{disjointunionfc} and \ref{cobordismworks} that $[\overline{\mathcal M}_{g,n}^\beta(X,J_0)]^\mathrm{vir}=[\overline{\mathcal M}_{g,n}^\beta(X,J_1)]^\mathrm{vir}$ in $\check H^\bullet(\overline{\mathcal M}_{g,n}^\beta(X,J_{[0,1]}))^\vee$, which is enough.
nodes.statement_short: Cobordism argument: the parameterized moduli space over a path J_t carries an implicit atlas with boundary, so the two virtual classes agree.

nodes.name: Abelian cover of free loop space
nodes.statement: Let $L_0M$ denote the space of null-homotopic smooth maps $S^1\to M$, and let $\widetilde{L_0M}$ denote the space of such loops together with a homology class of bounding $2$-disk. Then $\widetilde{L_0M}\to L_0M$ is a $\pi$-cover where $\pi=\operatorname{im}(\pi_2(M)\to H_2(M;\mathbb Z))$.\footnote{We could just as easily work on the smaller cover corresponding to the image of $\omega\oplus c_1(M):\pi_2(M)\to\mathbb R\oplus\mathbb Z$. The corresponding equivalence relation is that $f_1,f_2:D^2\to M$ with $f_1|_{S^1}=f_2|_{S^1}$ are equivalent iff $\omega$ and $c_1(M)$ both vanish on ``$f_1-f_2$''$\in\pi_2(M)$.}
nodes.statement_short: The cover of null-homotopic loops by loops with a homology class of bounding disk; a pi-cover with pi the image of pi_2 in H_2.

nodes.name: Hamiltonian flows
nodes.statement: For a smooth function $H:M\times S^1\to\mathbb R$, let $X_H:M\times S^1\to TM$ denote the Hamiltonian vector field induced by $H$, and let $\phi_H:M\to M$ denote the time $1$ flow map of $X_H$. A \emph{periodic orbit} of $H$ is a smooth function $\gamma:S^1\to M$ satisfying $\gamma'(t)=X_{H(t)}(\gamma(t))$. Let $C^\infty(M\times S^1)^\mathrm{reg}\subseteq C^\infty(M\times S^1)$ denote those functions $H$ for which $\phi_H$ has non-degenerate fixed points.
nodes.statement_short: Defines the Hamiltonian vector field X_H, time-1 map phi_H, periodic orbits, and the nondegenerate Hamiltonians C^infty(M x S^1)^reg.

nodes.name: Simplicial sets of $H$ and $J$
nodes.statement: Define the simplicial set $H_\bullet(M)$ where $H_n(M)$ is the set of smooth functions $H:\Delta^n\to C^\infty(M\times S^1)$ which are constant near the vertices and send the vertices to $C^\infty(M\times S^1)^\mathrm{reg}$. Define the simplicial set $J_\bullet(M)$ where $J_n(M)$ is the set of smooth functions $J:\Delta^n\to J(M)$ which are constant near the vertices ($J(M)$ is the space of smooth almost complex structures tamed by $\omega$) and which send the vertices to almost complex structures which are $\omega$-compatible. It is easy to see that $H_\bullet(M)$ and $J_\bullet(M)$ are both \emph{contractible Kan complexes}. A semisimplicial set $Z_\bullet$ is a contractible Kan complex iff every map $\partial\Delta^n\to Z_\bullet$ can be extended to a map $\Delta^n\to Z_\bullet$ for all $n\geq 0$ (where $\Delta^n$ is the semisimplicial $n$-simplex). Let $J\!H_\bullet(M)=J_\bullet(M)\times H_\bullet(M)$, which of course is also a contractible Kan complex.
nodes.statement_short: Simplicial sets of simplex-families of Hamiltonians and almost complex structures (nondegenerate/compatible at vertices); both and their product are contractible Kan complexes.
nodes.label: JHdef

nodes.name: Standard Morse function on $\Delta^n$
nodes.statement:
For this definition, let us view the $n$-simplex $\Delta^n$ as:  egin{equation} \Delta^n=\{\underline x\in[0,1]^{n+1}:0=x_0\leq\cdots\leq x_n\leq 1\} \end{equation} The $i$th vertex of $\Delta^n$ is given by $x_{n-i}=0$ and $x_{n-i+1}=1$. We now consider the Morse function on $\Delta^n$ given by $f(x):=\sum_{i=1}^n\cos\pi x_i$. Its gradient:  egin{equation} 
abla f(x)=\sum_{i=1}^n\pi\sin(\pi x_i) rac\partial{\partial x_i} \end{equation} is tangent to the boundary of $\Delta^n$, and its critical points are precisely the vertices of $\Delta^n$, the index at vertex $i$ being $n-i$. Note also that for any facet inclusion $\Delta^k\hookrightarrow\Delta^n$, the pushforward of $
abla f$ is again $
abla f$. Let us consider the space $\mathcal F(\Delta^n)$ of broken Morse flow lines from vertex $0$ (index $n$) to vertex $n$ (index $0$). This space is homeomorphic to a cube $[0,1]^{n-1}$, the factors $[0,1]$ being naturally indexed by the ``middle vertices'' $1,\ldots,n-1$ of $\Delta^n$. A flow line is broken at a vertex $i\in\{1,\ldots,n-1\}$ iff the corresponding coordinate in $[0,1]^{n-1}$ equals $1$. Note that for any simplex $\sigma$ there are canonical compatible product/face maps:  egin{align} \mathcal F(\sigma|[0\ldots k])	imes\mathcal F(\sigma|[k\ldots n])&	o\mathcal F(\sigma)\ \mathcal F(\sigma|[0\ldots\hat k\ldots n])&	o\mathcal F(\sigma) \end{align} See also \Sef{simplexflowsorsec} for more details. Adams \cite{adamscobar} considered spaces of paths on $\Delta^n$ with the same key properties (though it is important that our flow lines are smooth, whereas Adams' are not).
nodes.statement_short: The Morse function sum cos(pi x_i) on the simplex has the vertices as critical points; its broken flow lines from vertex 0 to n form a cube with product/face maps.
nodes.label: simplexflows

nodes.name: Simplex coordinates
nodes.statement: \Delta^n=\{\underline x\in[0,1]^{n+1}:0=x_0\leq\cdots\leq x_n\leq 1\}

nodes.name: Gradient of the standard Morse function on $\Delta^n$
nodes.statement: \nabla f(x)=\sum_{i=1}^n\pi\sin(\pi x_i)\frac\partial{\partial x_i}
nodes.label: simplexmorsefunctiongradient

nodes.name: Product/face maps on $\mathcal F(\sigma)$
nodes.statement: \mathcal F(\sigma|[0\ldots k])\times\mathcal F(\sigma|[k\ldots n])&\to\mathcal F(\sigma)\\ \mathcal F(\sigma|[0\ldots\hat k\ldots n])&\to\mathcal F(\sigma)
nodes.label: Fproduct

nodes.name: Capped periodic orbits $\mathcal P_H$
nodes.statement: For $H\in C^\infty(M\times S^1)^\mathrm{reg}$, let $\mathcal P_H\subseteq\widetilde{L_0M}$ denote the set of null-homotopic periodic orbits equipped with a homology class of bounding $2$-disk.

nodes.name: Floer trajectory
nodes.statement: Let $\sigma\in J_n(M)\times H_n(M)$ be an $n$-simplex; we denote by $H^\sigma:\Delta^n\times M\times S^1\to\mathbb R$ and $J^\sigma:\Delta^n\to J(M)$ the corresponding smooth families. Let $p\in\mathcal P_{H_0}$ and $q\in\mathcal P_{H_n}$ be periodic orbits, where $H_i=H^\sigma(i\in\Delta^n,\cdot,\cdot)$ is the Hamiltonian associated to the $i$th vertex of $\Delta^n$. A \emph{Floer trajectory of type $(\sigma,p,q)$} is a triple $(C,\ell,u)$ where: \begin{rlist} \item$C$ is a nodal curve of type $(0,2)$. Let us call the two marked points $x^-,x^+\in C$, and let $k=k(C)$ be the number of vertices (irreducible components of $C$) on the unique path from $x^-$ to $x^+$ in the dual graph of $C$. \item$\ell:\coprod_{i=1}^k\mathbb R\to\Delta^n$ is a broken Morse flow line from vertex $0$ to vertex $n$ (for the Morse function in Definition \ref{simplexflows}). Let $0=v_0\leq\cdots\leq v_k=n$ be the corresponding sequence of vertices. We allow $\ell$ to contain constant flow lines, i.e.\ we allow $v_i=v_{i+1}$. \item$u:C\to M\times S^1\times\coprod_{i=1}^k\mathbb R$ is a smooth \emph{building} of type $(\sigma,p,q)$, by which we mean the following. Let $C^\circ$ be $C$ punctured at $\{x^-,x^+\}$ and at the nodes corresponding to the edges in the unique path in the dual graph of $C$ from $x^-$ to $x^+$. The connected components $\{C^\circ_1,\ldots,C^\circ_k\}$ are naturally ordered ($x^-$ on the $1$st component and $x^+$ on the $k$th component). There must be periodic orbits $\{\gamma_0,\ldots,\gamma_k\}$ where $\gamma_i\in\mathcal P_{H_{v_i}}$ with $\gamma_0=p$ and $\gamma_k=q$. Then the negative (resp.\ positive) end of $C^\circ_i$ must be asymptotic to $(\gamma_{i-1}(t),t)$ (resp.\ $(\gamma_i(t),t)$) (with multiplicity one). We also require that $u$ have ``finite energy''. In addition, $u|C_i^\circ$ must be in the correct homology class: the element of $\pi_2(M)$ obtained by gluing together $u|C_i^\circ$ (resolving any nodes of $C_i^\circ$) with the given disks bounding $\gamma_i$ and $\gamma_{i-1}$ must vanish in homology. \item$u$ is pseudo-holomorphic with respect to the almost complex structure on $M\times S^1\times\coprod_{i=1}^k\mathbb R$ defined as follows. Use coordinates $(t,s)\in S^1\times\coprod_{i=1}^k\mathbb R$. Fix the standard almost complex structure on $S^1\times\coprod_{i=1}^k\mathbb R$, namely $J_{S^1\times\coprod_{i=1}^k\mathbb R}(\frac\partial{\partial s})=\frac\partial{\partial t}$. Also fix the ($s$-dependent) almost complex structure $J^\sigma(\ell(s))$ on $M$. We let $A:T[S^1\times\coprod_{i=1}^k\mathbb R]\to TM$ be defined by $A(\frac\partial{\partial s})=X_{H^\sigma(\ell(s),t,\cdot)}$ and extended anti-holomorphically. Now we use the following almost complex structure on $M\times S^1\times\coprod_{i=1}^k\mathbb R$: \begin{equation} J=\left(\begin{matrix} J^\sigma(\ell(s))&A\cr 0&J_{S^1\times\coprod_{i=1}^k\mathbb R} \end{matrix}\right) \end{equation} Note that the projection $M\times S^1\times\coprod_{i=1}^k\mathbb R\to S^1\times\coprod_{i=1}^k\mathbb R$ is holomorphic. \end{rlist} An \emph{isomorphism} $\iota:(C,\ell,u)\to(C',\ell',u')$ of Floer trajectories is an isomorphism $\iota_1:C\to C'$ of curves of type $(0,2)$ and an isomorphism $\iota_2:\coprod_{i=1}^k\mathbb R\to\coprod_{i=1}^k\mathbb R$ (acting by translation on each factor and respecting the ordering of the terms; note that the existence of $\iota_1$ implies that $k(C)=k(C')$) such that $u=(\operatorname{id}_{M\times S^1}\times\iota_2^{-1})\circ u'\circ\iota_1$ and $\ell=\ell'\circ\iota_2$. We say a Floer trajectory is \emph{stable} iff its automorphism group (i.e.\ group of self-isomorphisms) is finite.
nodes.statement_short: A Floer trajectory of type (sigma,p,q) is a nodal (0,2)-curve with a broken Morse flow line on the simplex and a finite-energy pseudo-holomorphic building asymptotic to periodic orbits.
nodes.label: floertrajdef

nodes.name: Almost complex structure on $M\times S^1\times\coprod\mathbb R$
nodes.statement: J=\left(\begin{matrix} J^\sigma(\ell(s))&A\cr 0&J_{S^1\times\coprod_{i=1}^k\mathbb R} \end{matrix}\right)
nodes.label: compositeJoncylinder

nodes.name: Hamiltonian Floer flow category diagram
nodes.statement: We define a $\pi$-equivariant flow category diagram $\overline{\mathcal M}/J\!H_\bullet(M)$ as follows. \begin{rlist} \item For a vertex $(J,H)\in J_0(M)\times H_0(M)$, we let $\mathcal P_{(J,H)}=\mathcal P_H$. \item The grading $\operatorname{gr}:\mathcal P\to\mathbb Z$ is the usual Conley--Zehnder index, and $\operatorname{gr}:\pi\to\mathbb Z$ is given by $\operatorname{gr}(h)=2\langle c_1(TM),h\rangle$. \item The action $a:\mathcal P\to\mathbb R$ is the usual symplectic action, and $a:\pi\to\mathbb R$ is given by $a(h)=\langle\omega,h\rangle$. \item We let $\overline{\mathcal M}(\sigma,p,q)$ be the set of stable Floer trajectories of type $(\sigma,p,q)$, equipped with the Gromov topology. It is well-known that $\overline{\mathcal M}(\sigma,p,q)$ is compact Hausdorff. The finiteness conditions required on $\overline{\mathcal M}(\sigma,p,q)$ also follow from Gromov compactness. The product/face maps on $\overline{\mathcal M}(\sigma,p,q)$ are evident. \item The action of $\pi$ on everything is clear. \end{rlist}
nodes.statement_short: The pi-equivariant flow category diagram over JH_(M): generators are capped periodic orbits graded by Conley-Zehnder index, flow spaces are moduli of stable Floer trajectories.

nodes.name: Index set $A^\mathrm{HF}(\Delta^n)$
nodes.statement: A \emph{(Hamiltonian Floer) thickening datum} $\alpha$ on the simplex $\Delta^n$ is a quadruple $(D_\alpha,r_\alpha,E_\alpha,\lambda_\alpha)$ where: \begin{rlist} \item$D_\alpha\subseteq M\times S^1\times\Delta^n$ is a compact smooth submanifold with corners locally modeled on $\mathbb R_{\geq 0}^N\times\mathbb R^{N'}\subseteq\mathbb R_{\geq 0}^N\times\mathbb R^{N'+2}$ or $\mathbb R_{\geq 0}^{N+1}\times\mathbb R^{N'}\subseteq\mathbb R_{\geq 0}^N\times\mathbb R^{N'+3}$. Let us denote by $\partial^\mathrm{ess} D_\alpha\subseteq\partial D_\alpha$ the closure of $\partial D_\alpha\setminus[M\times S^1\times\partial\Delta^n]$ (which is precisely the set of points with local model of the second type). \item$r_\alpha\geq 1$ is an integer; let $\Gamma_\alpha=S_{r_\alpha}$. \item$E_\alpha$ is a finitely generated $\mathbb R[S_{r_\alpha}]$-module. \item$\lambda_\alpha:E_\alpha\to C^\infty(\overline{\mathcal C}_{0,2+r_\alpha}\times M,\Omega^{0,1}_{\overline{\mathcal C}_{0,2+r_\alpha}/\overline{\mathcal M}_{0,2+r_\alpha}}\otimes_\mathbb R TM)$ is an $S_{r_\alpha}$-equivariant linear map supported away from the nodes and marked points of the fibers of $\overline{\mathcal C}_{0,2+r_\alpha}\to\overline{\mathcal M}_{0,2+r_\alpha}$ (the universal family). \end{rlist} Let $A^\mathrm{HF}(\Delta^n)$ denote the set of all thickening datums on $\Delta^n$.
nodes.statement_short: A Hamiltonian Floer thickening datum on a simplex is a divisor-with-corners D, an integer r, an S_r-module E and a perturbation map lambda.
nodes.label: implicitatlasonFloer

nodes.statement: We define a $\pi$-equivariant implicit atlas $\mathcal A$ on the flow category diagram $\overline{\mathcal M}/J\!H_\bullet(M)$ as follows.
nodes.name: Implicit atlas $\mathcal A$ on $\overline{\mathcal M}/J\!H_\bullet(M)$

nodes.statement: We set $\bar\mathcal A(\sigma,p,q):=A^\mathrm{HF}(\sigma)$.
nodes.name: Index sets $\bar\mathcal A(\sigma,p,q)$
Atlas data for $\mathcal A(\sigma,p,q)^{\geq\mathfrak s}$
nodes.statement: For $I\subseteq\mathcal A(\sigma,p,q)^{\geq\mathfrak s}$, an \emph{$I$-thickened Floer trajectory of type $(\sigma,p,q)^{\leq\mathfrak s}$} is a $5$-tuple $(C,\ell,u,\{\phi_\alpha\}_{\alpha\in I},\{e_\alpha\}_{\alpha\in I})$ where: \begin{rlist} \item$C$ is a nodal curve of type $(0,2)$. \item$\ell:\coprod_{i=1}^k\mathbb R\to\Delta^n$ is a broken flow line from vertex $0$ to vertex $n$. \item$u:C\to M\times S^1\times\coprod_{i=1}^k\mathbb R$ is a smooth building of type $(\sigma,p,q)$ (in the sense of Definition \ref{floertrajdef}(\ref{buildingdef})), with combinatorial type of $u$ belonging to $\mathcal S_{\overline{\mathcal M}}(\sigma,p,q)^{\leq\mathfrak s}$. Recall that by definition (see \eqref{coproductforA}), $\mathcal A(\sigma,p,q)^{\geq\mathfrak s}$ is a disjoint union of various $\bar\mathcal A(\sigma|[i_0\ldots i_n],p',q'):=A^\mathrm{HF}(\sigma|[i_0\ldots i_n])$. Hence any given $\alpha\in I$ comes from one of these, say $\bar\mathcal A(\sigma|[i_0^\alpha\ldots i_n^\alpha],p'_\alpha,q'_\alpha)$. Let $C_\alpha\subseteq C$ denote the union of irreducible components corresponding to this triple, which exists because the combinatorial type of $u$ belongs to $\mathcal S_{\overline{\mathcal M}}(\sigma,p,q)^{\leq\mathfrak s}$ (this $C_\alpha$ is a key notion for the present construction of an implicit atlas). \item For all $\alpha\in I$, we must have $u|_{C_\alpha}\pitchfork D_\alpha$ with exactly $r_\alpha$ intersections. By $u|_{C_\alpha}\pitchfork D_\alpha$, we mean that under the map $(\operatorname{id}_{M\times S^1}\times\ell)\circ u:C_\alpha\to M\times S^1\times\Delta^{\sigma|[i_0\ldots i_m]}$, we have\footnote{The closure of the image $\overline{C_\alpha}$ is precisely the image of $C_{\alpha}$ union the asymptotic periodic orbits.} $\overline{C_\alpha}\cap\partial^\mathrm{ess} D_\alpha=\varnothing$ and for every point $p\in C_\alpha$ mapping to $D_\alpha$, the derivative $d((\operatorname{id}_{M\times S^1}\times\ell)\circ u):T_pC\to T_{u(p)}[M\times S^1\times\Delta^{\sigma|[i_0\ldots i_m]}]/T_{u(p)}D_\alpha$ is surjective and $p$ is not a node or marked point of $C$. \item$\phi_\alpha:C_\alpha\to\overline{\mathcal C}_{0,2+r_\alpha}$ is an isomorphism with a fiber (where $C_\alpha$ is considered to have two marked points $x^-,x^+$ corresponding to $p_\alpha',q_\alpha'$ plus the $r_\alpha$ marked points $(u|C_\alpha)^{-1}(D_\alpha)$). \item$e_\alpha\in E_\alpha$. \item The following \emph{$I$-thickened $\bar\partial$-equation} is satisfied: \begin{equation} \bar\partial u+\sum_{\alpha\in I}\lambda_\alpha(e_\alpha)(\phi_\alpha,u)=0 \end{equation} where we use the almost complex structure on $M\times S^1\times\coprod_{i=1}^k\mathbb R$ defined in \eqref{compositeJoncylinder}. The term $\lambda_\alpha(e_\alpha)(\phi_\alpha,u)$ only makes sense over $C_\alpha$; we interpret it as zero over the rest of $C$. Note that for \eqref{approxJholforHF}, we project $\lambda_\alpha$ onto $\Omega^{0,1}_{\overline{\mathcal C}_{0,2+r_\beta}/\overline{\mathcal M}_{0,2+r_\beta}}\otimes_\mathbb C TM_{J^\sigma(\ell(s))}$. \end{rlist} An \emph{isomorphism} between two $I$-thickened Floer trajectories $(C,\ell,u,\{e_\alpha\},\{\phi_\alpha\})$ and $(C',\ell',u',\{e_\alpha'\},\{\phi_\alpha'\})$ is an isomorphism $\iota_1:C\to C'$ of curves of type $(0,2)$ and an isomorphism $\iota_2:\coprod_{i=1}^k\mathbb R\to\coprod_{i=1}^k\mathbb R$ (acting by translation on each factor and respecting the ordering of the terms; note that the existence of $\iota_1$ implies that $k(C)=k(C')$) such that $u=(\operatorname{id}_{M\times S^1}\times\iota_2^{-1})\circ u'\circ\iota_1$, $\ell=\ell'\circ\iota_2$, $\phi_\alpha=\phi_\alpha'\circ\iota_1$, and $e_\alpha=e_\alpha'$ for all $\alpha\in I$. We say an $I$-thickened Floer trajectory is \emph{stable} iff its automorphism group (i.e.\ group of self-isomorphisms) is finite. Let $\overline{\mathcal M}(\sigma,p,q)^{\leq\mathfrak s}_I$ denote the set of stable $I$-thickened Floer trajectories of type $(\sigma,p,q)^{\leq\mathfrak s}$, and equip it with the Gromov topology. The actions of $\Gamma_I$ on the thickened moduli spaces, the functions $s_I$, the projections $\psi_{IJ}$, and the sets $U_{IJ}$ are all defined as in Definition \ref{GWatlasdatadef} from the Gromov--Witten setting. The stratification of $\overline{\mathcal M}(\sigma,p,q)^{\leq\mathfrak s}_I$ by $\mathcal S_{\overline{\mathcal M}}(\sigma,p,q)^{\leq\mathfrak s}$ is evident.
nodes.statement_short: I-thickened Floer trajectories: buildings with components C_alpha transverse to D_alpha, fiber identifications phi_alpha and e_alpha solving the perturbed equation; thickened spaces and maps as in the GW case.
nodes.label: IAonfloerthickeningsdef

nodes.name: $I$-thickened $\bar\partial$-equation (Floer)
nodes.statement: \bar\partial u+\sum_{\alpha\in I}\lambda_\alpha(e_\alpha)(\phi_\alpha,u)=0
nodes.label: approxJholforHF

nodes.statement: The compatibility axioms for $\mathcal A(\sigma,p,q)^{\geq\mathfrak s}$ on $\overline{\mathcal M}(\sigma,p,q)^{\leq\mathfrak s}$ are all immediate; the homeomorphism axiom can again be verified directly as in the Gromov--Witten setting.
nodes.name: Compatibility axioms for the Floer atlas

nodes.statement: The regular loci for $\mathcal A(\sigma,p,q)^{\geq\mathfrak s}$ on $\overline{\mathcal M}(\sigma,p,q)^{\leq\mathfrak s}$ are defined following Definition \ref{regularsubsetdefinition}, meaning that a $5$-tuple $(C,\ell,u,\{\phi_\alpha\}_{\alpha\in I},\{e_\alpha\}_{\alpha\in I})$ is regular iff it has trival automorphism group and the linearized operator (fixing $C$ and varying $u$, $\ell$, and $\{e_\alpha\}_{\alpha\in I}$) is surjective (see \S\ref{regularlocusdef} for more details).
nodes.name: Regular locus for the Floer atlas
nodes.statement_short: A thickened Floer trajectory is regular iff it has trivial automorphisms and its linearized operator (fixed domain) is surjective.

nodes.statement: Let $\operatorname{vdim}\overline{\mathcal M}(\sigma,p,q)^{\leq\mathfrak s}:=\operatorname{gr}(q)-\operatorname{gr}(p)+\dim\sigma-1-\operatorname{codim}\mathfrak s$.
nodes.name: Virtual dimension of Floer moduli spaces

nodes.statement: Let us now discuss the (nontrivial) transversality axioms for $\mathcal A(\sigma,p,q)^{\geq\mathfrak s}$ on $\overline{\mathcal M}(\sigma,p,q)^{\leq\mathfrak s}$. The openness and submersion axioms follow from the following result, whose proof is given in Appendix \ref{gluingHF}.
nodes.name: Transversality axioms for the Floer atlas
Formal regularity implies topological regularity (Hamiltonian Floer)
nodes.statement: For all $I\subseteq J\subseteq\mathcal A(\sigma,p,q)^{\geq\mathfrak s}$, we have: \begin{rlist} \item$(\overline{\mathcal M}(\sigma,p,q)^{\leq\mathfrak s}_I)^\mathrm{reg}\subseteq\overline{\mathcal M}(\sigma,p,q)^{\leq\mathfrak s}_I$ is an open subset. \item The map $s_{J\setminus I}:\overline{\mathcal M}(\sigma,p,q)^{\leq\mathfrak s}_J\to E_{J\setminus I}$ over the locus $\psi_{IJ}^{-1}((\overline{\mathcal M}(\sigma,p,q)_I^{\leq\mathfrak s})^\mathrm{reg})\subseteq\overline{\mathcal M}(\sigma,p,q)^{\leq\mathfrak s}_J$ is locally modeled on the projection: \begin{equation} \mathbb R^{\operatorname{vdim}\overline{\mathcal M}(\sigma,p,q)^{\leq\mathfrak s}+\dim E_I}\times\mathbb R^{\dim E_{J\setminus I}}\to\mathbb R^{\dim E_{J\setminus I}} \end{equation} over the top stratum $\mathfrak s\in\mathcal S_{\overline{\mathcal M}}(\sigma,p,q)^{\leq\mathfrak s}$. More generally, the local model (compatible with stratifications) is given by replacing the first factor on the left by $\mathbb R_{\geq 0}^n\times\mathbb R^{n'}$ stratified appropriately by $\mathcal S_{\overline{\mathcal M}}(\sigma,p,q)$. \item There exist $\pi$-invariant coherent trivializations of the local systems $\mathfrak o_{(\overline{\mathcal M}(\sigma,p,q)^{\leq\mathfrak s}_I)^\mathrm{reg}}\otimes\mathfrak o_{E_I}^\vee$ (in the sense of Definition \ref{cohordefabstract}). \end{rlist}
nodes.statement_short: For the Floer atlas, regular loci are open, s_{J\I} is a stratified submersion, and there are coherent orientations.
assumptions: For all $I\subseteq J\subseteq\mathcal A(\sigma,p,q)^{\geq\mathfrak s}$
conclusions: $(\overline{\mathcal M}(\sigma,p,q)^{\leq\mathfrak s}_I)^\mathrm{reg}\subseteq\overline{\mathcal M}(\sigma,p,q)^{\leq\mathfrak s}_I$ is an open subset.

The map $s_{J\setminus I}:\overline{\mathcal M}(\sigma,p,q)^{\leq\mathfrak s}_J\to E_{J\setminus I}$ over the locus $\psi_{IJ}^{-1}((\overline{\mathcal M}(\sigma,p,q)_I^{\leq\mathfrak s})^\mathrm{reg})\subseteq\overline{\mathcal M}(\sigma,p,q)^{\leq\mathfrak s}_J$ is locally modeled on the projection: \begin{equation} \mathbb R^{\operatorname{vdim}\overline{\mathcal M}(\sigma,p,q)^{\leq\mathfrak s}+\dim E_I}\times\mathbb R^{\dim E_{J\setminus I}}\to\mathbb R^{\dim E_{J\setminus I}} \end{equation} over the top stratum $\mathfrak s\in\mathcal S_{\overline{\mathcal M}}(\sigma,p,q)^{\leq\mathfrak s}$. More generally, the local model (compatible with stratifications) is given by replacing the first factor on the left by $\mathbb R_{\geq 0}^n\times\mathbb R^{n'}$ stratified appropriately by $\mathcal S_{\overline{\mathcal M}}(\sigma,p,q)$.

There exist $\pi$-invariant coherent trivializations of the local systems $\mathfrak o_{(\overline{\mathcal M}(\sigma,p,q)^{\leq\mathfrak s}_I)^\mathrm{reg}}\otimes\mathfrak o_{E_I}^\vee$ (in the sense of Definition \ref{cohordefabstract}).
nodes.label: HFgluingneeded

nodes.name: Local model projection (Hamiltonian Floer)
nodes.statement: \mathbb R^{\operatorname{vdim}\overline{\mathcal M}(\sigma,p,q)^{\leq\mathfrak s}+\dim E_I}\times\mathbb R^{\dim E_{J\setminus I}}\to\mathbb R^{\dim E_{J\setminus I}}

nodes.name: Domain stabilization for stable Floer trajectories
nodes.statement: Let $\ell:\coprod_{i=1}^k\mathbb R\to\Delta^n$ and $u:C\to M\times S^1\times\coprod_{i=1}^k\mathbb R$ be a point in $\overline{\mathcal M}(\sigma,p,q)$. Then there exists $D\subseteq M\times S^1\times\Delta^n$ as in Definition \ref{implicitatlasonFloer}(\ref{implicitatlasFloerD}) such that $C\pitchfork D$ in the sense of Definition \ref{IAonfloerthickeningsdef}(\ref{transversalitypartIAfloer}) and so that adding the intersections to $C$ as extra marked points makes $C$ stable.
nodes.statement_short: Every stable Floer trajectory admits a transverse divisor in M x S^1 x Delta^n whose intersections stabilize the domain.
assumptions: Let $\ell:\coprod_{i=1}^k\mathbb R\to\Delta^n$ and $u:C\to M\times S^1\times\coprod_{i=1}^k\mathbb R$ be a point in $\overline{\mathcal M}(\sigma,p,q)$.
conclusions: there exists $D\subseteq M\times S^1\times\Delta^n$ as in Definition \ref{implicitatlasonFloer}(\ref{implicitatlasFloerD}) such that $C\pitchfork D$ in the sense of Definition \ref{IAonfloerthickeningsdef}(\ref{transversalitypartIAfloer}) and so that adding the intersections to $C$ as extra marked points makes $C$ stable.
nodes.label: stabilizationlemmaforHF

nodes.name: Proof
nodes.statement: As in the proof of Lemma \ref{stabilizationlemma}, we use (an appropriate variant for manifolds with corners of) Lemma \ref{sortofsard} (which we may also use to avoid the periodic orbits in question). It thus suffices to show that for any unstable component $C_0$ of $C$, there exists a point $p\in C_0$ where $d((\operatorname{id}_{M\times S^1}\times\ell)\circ u):TC_0\to TM\times TS^1\times T\Delta^n$ injective. To find such a point, we split into two cases. First, suppose $u:C_0\to S^1\times\mathbb R$ is constant. Then $u:C_0\to M$ is a (nonconstant!) $J$-holomorphic sphere, and thus has a point of injectivity of $du$. Second, suppose $u:C_0\to S^1\times\mathbb R$ is not constant. Then $u:C_0\to S^1\times\mathbb R$ is an isomorphism; let us use $(t,s)\in S^1\times\mathbb R$ as coordinates on $C_0$. Now $\frac{\partial u}{\partial t}\in TM\times TS^1$ has nonzero coordinate in the $TS^1$ component (everywhere), and $\frac{\partial u}{\partial s}\in TM\times TS^1$ has zero coordinate in the $TS^1$ coordinate (everywhere). Hence if $du$ is everywhere noninjective, we find that $\frac{\partial u}{\partial s}=0\in TM\times TS^1$ everywhere. It follows that $u:C_0\to M\times S^1$ is independent of the $\mathbb R$ coordinate, and thus is simply a trivial cylinder mapping onto a periodic orbit. Now the stability condition (the automorphism group being finite) implies that the corresponding (piece of a) flow line $\ell:\mathbb R\to\Delta^n$ is nontrivial. It follows that we have the desired injectivity.
nodes.statement_short: Reduce to finding an injectivity point of the derivative on each unstable component; case split on whether the component projects constantly to the cylinder.

nodes.name: Implicit atlas on the Hamiltonian Floer flow category diagram
nodes.statement: $\mathcal A$ is a $\pi$-equivariant implicit atlas on $\overline{\mathcal M}/J\!H_\bullet(M)$.
conclusions: $\mathcal A$ is a $\pi$-equivariant implicit atlas on $\overline{\mathcal M}/J\!H_\bullet(M)$.
nodes.label: IAonFloerworks

nodes.name: Proof
nodes.statement: We have shown above that each individual $\mathcal A(\sigma,p,q)^{\geq\mathfrak s}$ is an implicit atlas on $\overline{\mathcal M}(\sigma,p,q)^{\leq\mathfrak s}$. The required compatibility isomorphisms between these implicit atlases follow directly from the definition.
nodes.statement_short: Each A(sigma,p,q) was shown to be an implicit atlas; compatibility isomorphisms follow from the definitions.

nodes.name: Hamiltonian Floer homology
nodes.statement: We have a $\pi$-equivariant flow category diagram $\overline{\mathcal M}/J\!H_\bullet(M)$ equipped with an implicit atlas $\mathcal A$. Moreover, Proposition \ref{HFgluingneeded} gives coherent orientations $\omega$. Hence according to Definition \ref{defofhomologygroups}, we get a diagram $F\mathbb H:J\!H_\bullet(M)\to H^0(\mathsf{Ch}_{\mathbb Q[[\pi]]})$ (the hypotheses of Definition \ref{defofhomologygroups} can be easily verified). Since $J\!H_\bullet(M)$ is a contractible Kan complex, this is really just a single object $F\mathbb H^\bullet(M)\in H^0(\mathsf{Ch}_{\mathbb Q[[\pi]]})$ which we call the \emph{Hamiltonian Floer homology of $M$}.
nodes.statement_short: Applying the Floer-type homology construction to the Floer flow category diagram with its implicit atlas gives a single object FH(M) since JH_(M) is contractible.

nodes.name: Graded completion $\mathbb Q[[\pi]]$
nodes.statement: The ring $\mathbb Q[[\pi]]$ is the \emph{graded} completion of $\mathbb Q[\pi]$, see Definition \ref{gradedcompletion}.
Fix a smooth almost complex structure $J$ on $M$ compatible with $\omega$.
nodes.name: Fixed compatible almost complex structure on $M$

nodes.statement: Let $H:M\to\mathbb R$ be a Morse function for which the time $1$ Hamiltonian flow map of $H$ has non-degerate fixed points, all of which are critical points of $H$ (for example, $H=\epsilon\cdot H_0$ is such a function for any Morse function $H_0:M\to\mathbb R$ and sufficiently small $\epsilon>0$).
nodes.name: Time-independent Morse Hamiltonian $H$

nodes.statement: Consider the inclusion $\ast\hookrightarrow J\!H_\bullet(M)$ (where $\ast$ is the simplicial $0$-simplex, i.e.\ the simplicial set with a single $n$-simplex for all $n$) defined by mapping everything to the constant families of almost complex structures and Hamiltonians given by $J$ and $H$.
nodes.name: Inclusion $\ast\hookrightarrow J\!H_\bullet(M)$

nodes.statement: We will restrict attention to the (pullback) flow category diagram $\overline{\mathcal M}/\ast$.
nodes.name: Pullback flow category diagram $\overline{\mathcal M}/\ast$

nodes.statement: With our assumptions on $H$, the set of generators is $\mathcal P=\operatorname{crit}(H)\times\pi$ canonically, and the grading on $\mathcal P$ is given by the Morse index on $\operatorname{crit}(H)$ plus $\operatorname{gr}:\pi\to\mathbb Z$.
nodes.name: Generators for a Morse Hamiltonian
assumptions: With our assumptions on $H$
conclusions: the set of generators is $\mathcal P=\operatorname{crit}(H)\times\pi$ canonically, and the grading on $\mathcal P$ is given by the Morse index on $\operatorname{crit}(H)$ plus $\operatorname{gr}:\pi\to\mathbb Z$

nodes.statement: Now there is a canonical $S^1$-action on the spaces of stable Floer trajectories in $\overline{\mathcal M}/\ast$ (postcompose $u$ with a rotation of $S^1$) which is compatible with the product/face maps (this action exists since $H$ is independent of the $S^1$-coordinate).
nodes.name: $S^1$-action on Floer trajectories
nodes.statement_short: Rotating the S^1 coordinate gives a canonical S^1-action on Floer trajectories for an S^1-invariant Hamiltonian.

nodes.statement: It follows that $\overline{\mathcal M}^{S^1}/\ast$ is also a flow category diagram (defined using the fixed locus $\overline{\mathcal M}(\sigma,p,q)^{S^1}\subseteq\overline{\mathcal M}(\sigma,p,q)$).
nodes.name: Fixed-locus flow category diagram $\overline{\mathcal M}^{S^1}/\ast$
Morse trajectory
nodes.statement: Let $\sigma\in\ast$ be the $n$-simplex, and let $p,q\in\mathcal P=\operatorname{crit}(H)\times\pi$. A \emph{Morse trajectory of type $(\sigma,p,q)$} is a triple $(k,\ell,u)$ where: \begin{rlist} \item$k\geq 1$ is a positive integer. \item$\ell:\coprod_{i=1}^k\mathbb R\to\Delta^n$ is a broken Morse flow line from vertex $0$ to vertex $n$ (for the Morse function in Definition \ref{simplexflows}). Let $0=v_0\leq\cdots\leq v_k=n$ be the corresponding sequence of vertices. We allow $\ell$ to contain constant flow lines, i.e.\ we allow $v_i=v_{i+1}$. \item$u:\coprod_{i=1}^k\mathbb R\to M$ is a broken Morse flow line from $p$ to $q$ for the function $H$. We allow $u$ to contain constant flow lines. \item The $\pi$-components of $p$ and $q$ agree. \end{rlist} An \emph{isomorphism} $\iota:(k,\ell,u)\to(k',\ell',u')$ of Morse trajectories is an isomorphism $\iota:\coprod_{i=1}^k\mathbb R\to\coprod_{i=1}^{k'}\mathbb R$ (acting by translation on each factor and respecting the ordering of the terms; we require $k=k'$) such that $u=u'\circ\iota$ and $\ell=\ell'\circ\iota$. We say a Morse trajectory is \emph{stable} iff its automorphism group (i.e.\ group of self-isomorphisms) is finite. Let $\overline{\mathcal M}_\mathrm{morse}(\sigma,p,q)$ denote the space of stable Morse trajectories.
nodes.statement_short: A Morse trajectory is a broken flow line on the simplex together with a broken Morse flow line of H from p to q; Mbar_morse is the space of stable ones.
nodes.label: morseTdef

nodes.name: Morse moduli spaces are manifolds with corners
nodes.statement: Suppose $H$ is Morse--Smale. Then with the stratification by $k$, the spaces $\overline{\mathcal M}_\mathrm{morse}(\sigma,p,q)$ are compact topological manifolds with corners.
nodes.statement_short: For Morse-Smale H, the spaces of stable broken Morse trajectories are compact topological manifolds with corners.
assumptions: Suppose $H$ is Morse--Smale.
conclusions: with the stratification by $k$, the spaces $\overline{\mathcal M}_\mathrm{morse}(\sigma,p,q)$ are compact topological manifolds with corners.
nodes.label: morseassumptionMS

nodes.statement: For the case of the zero simplex $\sigma=\sigma^0$, this is proved by Wehrheim \cite{wehrheimMS}. In fact, the general case also follows from \cite{wehrheimMS} since $\overline{\mathcal M}_\mathrm{morse}(\sigma,p,q)$ is the space of broken Morse flow lines on $M\times\Delta^n$ from $p\times 0$ to $q\times n$ for the Morse function $H+f$ (and $f$ is defined and smooth on a neighborhood of $\Delta^n\subseteq\mathbb R^n$). Alternatively, one may restrict to $H$ which have a particular normal form near each critical point in which case this result holds by more elementary arguments (see also \cite{wehrheimMS}).
nodes.name: Proof of Proposition 10.5.16
nodes.statement_short: Cite Wehrheim: the spaces are broken Morse flow lines on M x Delta^n for H+f.

nodes.name: $S^1$-fixed Floer trajectories are Morse trajectories
nodes.statement: There is canonical homeomorphism $\overline{\mathcal M}(\sigma,p,q)^{S^1}=\overline{\mathcal M}_\mathrm{morse}(\sigma,p,q)$.
conclusions: There is canonical homeomorphism $\overline{\mathcal M}(\sigma,p,q)^{S^1}=\overline{\mathcal M}_\mathrm{morse}(\sigma,p,q)$.
nodes.label: fixedismorse

nodes.name: Proof
nodes.statement: Suppose a stable Floer trajectory $(C,\ell,u)$ is $S^1$-invariant. Then each of the components $\{C_1^\circ,\ldots,C_k^\circ\}$ must be smooth (no nodes) and hence isomorphic to $S^1\times\mathbb R$. Using the holomorphic projection $M\times S^1\times\coprod_{i=1}^k\mathbb R\to S^1\times\coprod_{i=1}^k\mathbb R$, we get holomorphic identifications $C_i^\circ=S^1\times\mathbb R$. Since $(C,\ell,u)$ is $S^1$-invariant, the function $u:C_i^\circ\to M$ must be independent of the $S^1$-coordinate, and hence (examining the $\bar\partial$-equation) is simply a Morse flow line of $H$. Running this argument in reverse, we also see that every stable Morse trajectory gives rise to a stable Floer trajectory which is $S^1$-invariant.
nodes.statement_short: An S^1-invariant Floer trajectory has smooth cylindrical components on which u is S^1-independent, hence a Morse flow line; and conversely.

nodes.name: Morse trajectories are cut out transversally
nodes.statement: Fix a Morse function $H_0:M\to\mathbb R$ whose gradient flow is Morse--Smale and suppose $H=\epsilon\cdot H_0$ with $\epsilon>0$ sufficiently small. Then $\overline{\mathcal M}(\sigma,p,q)^{S^1}\subseteq\overline{\mathcal M}(\sigma,p,q)$ is open and cut out transversally (meaning $\overline{\mathcal M}(\sigma,p,q)^{S^1}\subseteq\overline{\mathcal M}(\sigma,p,q)^\mathrm{reg}$). Hence we have a partition into disjoint closed subsets: \begin{equation} \overline{\mathcal M}(\sigma,p,q)=\overline{\mathcal M}(\sigma,p,q)^{S^1}\sqcup[\overline{\mathcal M}(\sigma,p,q)\setminus\overline{\mathcal M}(\sigma,p,q)^{S^1}] \end{equation}
nodes.statement_short: For H a small multiple of a Morse-Smale function, the S^1-fixed locus is open and transversally cut out, giving a partition into closed pieces.
assumptions: Fix a Morse function $H_0:M\to\mathbb R$ whose gradient flow is Morse--Smale
suppose $H=\epsilon\cdot H_0$ with $\epsilon>0$ sufficiently small
conclusions: $\overline{\mathcal M}(\sigma,p,q)^{S^1}\subseteq\overline{\mathcal M}(\sigma,p,q)$ is open and cut out transversally (meaning $\overline{\mathcal M}(\sigma,p,q)^{S^1}\subseteq\overline{\mathcal M}(\sigma,p,q)^\mathrm{reg}$).

Hence we have a partition into disjoint closed subsets: \begin{equation} \overline{\mathcal M}(\sigma,p,q)=\overline{\mathcal M}(\sigma,p,q)^{S^1}\sqcup[\overline{\mathcal M}(\sigma,p,q)\setminus\overline{\mathcal M}(\sigma,p,q)^{S^1}] \end{equation}
nodes.label: morseistransverse

nodes.name: Partition into $S^1$-fixed and free parts
nodes.statement: \overline{\mathcal M}(\sigma,p,q)=\overline{\mathcal M}(\sigma,p,q)^{S^1}\sqcup[\overline{\mathcal M}(\sigma,p,q)\setminus\overline{\mathcal M}(\sigma,p,q)^{S^1}]

nodes.name: Proof
nodes.statement: Salamon--Zehnder \cite[p1342, Theorem 7.3(1)]{salamonzehnder} show that $\overline{\mathcal M}(\sigma^0,p,q)^{S^1}\subseteq\overline{\mathcal M}(\sigma^0,p,q)^\mathrm{reg}$ for the $0$-simplex $\sigma^0$ and sufficiently small $\epsilon>0$. Since we only consider constant families of $J$ and $H$, the linearized operators for the higher $\sigma^i$ can be written in terms of the linearized operators for $\sigma^0$, and it follows that $\overline{\mathcal M}(\sigma,p,q)^{S^1}\subseteq\overline{\mathcal M}(\sigma,p,q)^\mathrm{reg}$ for all $\sigma$. Now we have $\overline{\mathcal M}_\mathrm{morse}(\sigma,p,q)=\overline{\mathcal M}(\sigma,p,q)^{S^1}\subseteq\overline{\mathcal M}(\sigma,p,q)^\mathrm{reg}$. It remains to show that this is an open inclusion. This can likely be seen by following closely the gluing argument used to prove Propositions \ref{HFgluingneeded} and \ref{morseassumptionMS}, however we can argue directly as follows. Both $\overline{\mathcal M}_\mathrm{morse}(\sigma,p,q)$ and $\overline{\mathcal M}(\sigma,p,q)^\mathrm{reg}$ are topological manifolds with corners, and the stratification for the former is the pullback of the stratification for the latter. Their dimensions are dictated by the Morse index and the Conley--Zehnder index respectively, which in this case coincide. Hence we are done by Lemma \ref{cornersinvarianceofdomain} below.
nodes.statement_short: Transversality from Salamon-Zehnder for the 0-simplex extends to all simplices; openness follows from equal dimensions and invariance of domain for manifolds with corners.

nodes.name: Invariance of domain for manifolds with corners
nodes.statement: Let $M$ be a topological manifold with corners and $K\subseteq M$ a closed subset. Suppose that the restriction of the corner stratification on $M$ induces a topological manifold with corners structure on $K$ of the same dimension. Then $K\subseteq M$ is open.
nodes.statement_short: A closed subset that inherits a manifold-with-corners structure of full dimension from the corner stratification is open.
assumptions: Let $M$ be a topological manifold with corners and $K\subseteq M$ a closed subset.
Suppose that the restriction of the corner stratification on $M$ induces a topological manifold with corners structure on $K$ of the same dimension.
conclusions: $K\subseteq M$ is open.
nodes.label: cornersinvarianceofdomain

nodes.name: Proof
nodes.statement: The question is local on $M$, so we may assume that $M=\mathbb R^n\times\mathbb R_{\geq 0}^m$. Let $\tilde K\subseteq\mathbb R^n\times\mathbb R^m$ be obtained by reflecting $K$ across the last $m$ coordinate hyperplanes. The hypotheses then imply that $\tilde K$ is a manifold of dimension $n+m$. Now we have $\tilde K\subseteq\mathbb R^{n+m}$ is open by Brouwer's ``invariance of domain''. This is enough.
nodes.statement_short: Localize, reflect across the boundary hyperplanes to get a full-dimensional manifold in R^{n+m}, and apply Brouwer's invariance of domain.

nodes.statement: We consider the subatlas $\mathcal A^{S^1}\subseteq\mathcal A$ consisting of those thickening datums $\alpha$ for which $D_\alpha$ is $S^1$-invariant.
nodes.name: Subatlas $\mathcal A^{S^1}$
differentia: $D_\alpha$ is $S^1$-invariant

nodes.statement: Now there is clearly a canonical $S^1$-action on the thickenings $\overline{\mathcal M}(\sigma,p,q)^{\leq\mathfrak s}_I$ (postcomposition of $u$ with a rotation of $S^1$) for $I\subseteq\mathcal A^{S^1}(\sigma,p,q)^{\geq\mathfrak s}$.\footnote{Note that we do not need to put any restrictions on $\lambda_\alpha$.} Now $\mathcal A^{S^1}\subseteq\mathcal A$ forms an implicit atlas if and only if it satisfies the covering axiom. However, the covering axiom for $\mathcal A^{S^1}$ fails: we cannot stabilize the domains of Morse flow lines (points of $\overline{\mathcal M}^{S^1}$) using $S^1$-invariant divisors $D_\alpha$ (more generally, we cannot stabilize the domain of any broken trajectory containing a Morse flow line).
nodes.name: Covering axiom fails for $\mathcal A^{S^1}$
nodes.statement_short: A^{S^1} carries an S^1-action but fails the covering axiom: Morse flow lines cannot be stabilized by S^1-invariant divisors.

nodes.name: Implicit atlas $\mathcal B$ on $\overline{\mathcal M}/\ast$
nodes.statement: We define an implicit atlas $\mathcal B$ on $\overline{\mathcal M}/\ast$ as follows. On the level of index sets, we define $\mathcal B:=\mathcal A$. However, we modify the definition of an $I$-thickened Floer trajectory as follows. We require that when $C_\alpha$ is considered with the $r_\alpha$ extra marked points $(u|C_\alpha)^{-1}(D_\alpha)$, the only unstable components are mapped by $u$ to Morse flow lines; let $C_\alpha\to C_\alpha^\mathrm{st}$ be the map contracting all such unstable components. Now instead of $\phi_\alpha:C_\alpha\to\overline{\mathcal C}_{0,2+r_\alpha}$, we use $\phi_\alpha:C_\alpha^\mathrm{st}\to\overline{\mathcal C}_{0,2+r_\alpha}$. The rest of the atlas data is defined analogously with that of $\mathcal A$ without any serious difference. Note, however, that to verify that the locus $U_{IJ}\subseteq X_I$ is open, we must appeal to Lemma \ref{morseistransverse}.
nodes.statement_short: Same index set as A, but thickened trajectories may have unstable components mapping to Morse flow lines, which are contracted before identifying with a fiber.
nodes.label: modifiedatlasforMorse

nodes.statement: Note that the thickened moduli spaces for $\mathcal A$ are open subsets of those for $\mathcal B$, so the covering axiom for $\mathcal A$ implies the covering axiom for $\mathcal B$. Now to verify that $\mathcal B$ is an implicit atlas, everything is the same as for $\mathcal A$ except for the openness and submersion axioms, which follow from the following result (identical to Proposition \ref{HFgluingneeded}), whose proof is given in Appendix \ref{gluingHF}.
nodes.name: Proof that $\mathcal B$ is an implicit atlas
nodes.statement_short: Covering for B follows from covering for A (open inclusion of thickenings); openness and submersion from the gluing proposition for B.

nodes.name: Formal regularity implies topological regularity ($\mathcal B$)
nodes.statement: For all $I\subseteq J\subseteq\mathcal B(\sigma,p,q)^{\geq\mathfrak s}$, we have: \begin{rlist} \item$(\overline{\mathcal M}(\sigma,p,q)^{\leq\mathfrak s}_I)^\mathrm{reg}\subseteq\overline{\mathcal M}(\sigma,p,q)^{\leq\mathfrak s}_I$ is an open subset. \item The map $s_{J\setminus I}:\overline{\mathcal M}(\sigma,p,q)^{\leq\mathfrak s}_J\to E_{J\setminus I}$ over the locus $\psi_{IJ}^{-1}((\overline{\mathcal M}(\sigma,p,q)_I^{\leq\mathfrak s})^\mathrm{reg})\subseteq\overline{\mathcal M}(\sigma,p,q)^{\leq\mathfrak s}_J$ is locally modeled on the projection: \begin{equation} \mathbb R^{\operatorname{vdim}\overline{\mathcal M}(\sigma,p,q)^{\leq\mathfrak s}+\dim E_I}\times\mathbb R^{\dim E_{J\setminus I}}\to\mathbb R^{\dim E_{J\setminus I}} \end{equation} over the top stratum $\mathfrak s\in\mathcal S_{\overline{\mathcal M}}(\sigma,p,q)^{\leq\mathfrak s}$. More generally, the local model (compatible with stratifications) is given by replacing the first factor on the left by $\mathbb R_{\geq 0}^n\times\mathbb R^{n'}$ stratified appropriately by $\mathcal S_{\overline{\mathcal M}}(\sigma,p,q)$. \item There exist $\pi$-invariant coherent trivializations of the local systems $\mathfrak o_{(\overline{\mathcal M}(\sigma,p,q)^{\leq\mathfrak s}_I)^\mathrm{reg}}\otimes\mathfrak o_{E_I}^\vee$ (in the sense of Definition \ref{cohordefabstract}), agreeing by restriction with those for $\mathcal A$, and coinciding with the usual orientations from Morse theory on $\overline{\mathcal M}_\mathrm{morse}(\sigma,p,q)=\overline{\mathcal M}(\sigma,p,q)^{S^1}\subseteq\overline{\mathcal M}(\sigma,p,q)^\mathrm{reg}$. \end{rlist}
nodes.statement_short: For atlas B: open regular loci, stratified submersion, and coherent orientations restricting to those of A and to the Morse orientations.
assumptions: For all $I\subseteq J\subseteq\mathcal B(\sigma,p,q)^{\geq\mathfrak s}$
conclusions: $(\overline{\mathcal M}(\sigma,p,q)^{\leq\mathfrak s}_I)^\mathrm{reg}\subseteq\overline{\mathcal M}(\sigma,p,q)^{\leq\mathfrak s}_I$ is an open subset.

The map $s_{J\setminus I}:\overline{\mathcal M}(\sigma,p,q)^{\leq\mathfrak s}_J\to E_{J\setminus I}$ over the locus $\psi_{IJ}^{-1}((\overline{\mathcal M}(\sigma,p,q)_I^{\leq\mathfrak s})^\mathrm{reg})\subseteq\overline{\mathcal M}(\sigma,p,q)^{\leq\mathfrak s}_J$ is locally modeled on the projection: \begin{equation} \mathbb R^{\operatorname{vdim}\overline{\mathcal M}(\sigma,p,q)^{\leq\mathfrak s}+\dim E_I}\times\mathbb R^{\dim E_{J\setminus I}}\to\mathbb R^{\dim E_{J\setminus I}} \end{equation} over the top stratum $\mathfrak s\in\mathcal S_{\overline{\mathcal M}}(\sigma,p,q)^{\leq\mathfrak s}$. More generally, the local model (compatible with stratifications) is given by replacing the first factor on the left by $\mathbb R_{\geq 0}^n\times\mathbb R^{n'}$ stratified appropriately by $\mathcal S_{\overline{\mathcal M}}(\sigma,p,q)$.

There exist $\pi$-invariant coherent trivializations of the local systems $\mathfrak o_{(\overline{\mathcal M}(\sigma,p,q)^{\leq\mathfrak s}_I)^\mathrm{reg}}\otimes\mathfrak o_{E_I}^\vee$ (in the sense of Definition \ref{cohordefabstract}), agreeing by restriction with those for $\mathcal A$, and coinciding with the usual orientations from Morse theory on $\overline{\mathcal M}_\mathrm{morse}(\sigma,p,q)=\overline{\mathcal M}(\sigma,p,q)^{S^1}\subseteq\overline{\mathcal M}(\sigma,p,q)^\mathrm{reg}$.
nodes.label: HFgluingSS

nodes.name: Local model projection ($\mathcal B$)
nodes.statement: \mathbb R^{\operatorname{vdim}\overline{\mathcal M}(\sigma,p,q)^{\leq\mathfrak s}+\dim E_I}\times\mathbb R^{\dim E_{J\setminus I}}\to\mathbb R^{\dim E_{J\setminus I}}
Thus $\mathcal B$ is an implicit atlas on $\overline{\mathcal M}/\ast$.
nodes.name: $\mathcal B$ is an implicit atlas
conclusions: $\mathcal B$ is an implicit atlas on $\overline{\mathcal M}/\ast$

nodes.name: $S^1$-equivariant implicit atlas $\mathcal B^{S^1}$
nodes.statement: Let $\mathcal B^{S^1}\subseteq\mathcal B$ consist of those thickening datums $\alpha$ for which $D_\alpha$ is $S^1$-invariant. There is a canonical $S^1$-action on the thickenings $\overline{\mathcal M}(\sigma,p,q)^{\leq\mathfrak s}_I$ (postcomposition of $u$ with a rotation of $S^1$) for $I\subseteq\mathcal B^{S^1}(\sigma,p,q)^{\geq\mathfrak s}$, and this $S^1$-action is compatible with the rest of the structure.
differentia: $D_\alpha$ is $S^1$-invariant

nodes.statement: To verify that $\mathcal B^{S^1}\subseteq\mathcal B$ is an implicit atlas, we just need to verify the covering axiom. We follow the usual proof of the covering axiom as in Lemma \ref{everythingcanbethickened} and use the fact that Morse components are already cut out transversally (Lemma \ref{morseistransverse}). To complete the proof, we just need Lemma \ref{stabilizationlemmaforHFSS} below, which says that for any stable Floer trajectory, we can stabilize the domain using $S^1$-invariant divisors (except, of course, for any irreducible components mapping to Morse flow lines).
nodes.name: $\mathcal B^{S^1}$ is an implicit atlas (covering axiom)
nodes.statement_short: B^{S^1} is an implicit atlas once the covering axiom holds, which follows from S^1-equivariant domain stabilization.

nodes.name: $S^1$-equivariant domain stabilization for stable Floer trajectories
nodes.statement: Let $\ell:\coprod_{i=1}^k\mathbb R\to\Delta^n$ and $u:C\to M\times S^1\times\coprod_{i=1}^k\mathbb R$ be a point in $\overline{\mathcal M}(\sigma,p,q)$. Then there exists $D\subseteq M\times S^1\times\Delta^n$ as in Definition \ref{implicitatlasonFloer}(\ref{implicitatlasFloerD}) which is $S^1$-invariant with $C\pitchfork D$ in the sense of Definition \ref{IAonfloerthickeningsdef}(\ref{transversalitypartIAfloer}) and so that adding these intersections to $C$ as extra marked points makes $C$ stable, except for irreducible components $S^1\times\mathbb R\subseteq C$ on which $u$ is independent of the $S^1$-coordinate (``Morse flow lines'').
nodes.statement_short: Stable Floer trajectories can be domain-stabilized with S^1-invariant divisors, except on components that are Morse flow lines.
assumptions: Let $\ell:\coprod_{i=1}^k\mathbb R\to\Delta^n$ and $u:C\to M\times S^1\times\coprod_{i=1}^k\mathbb R$ be a point in $\overline{\mathcal M}(\sigma,p,q)$.
conclusions: there exists $D\subseteq M\times S^1\times\Delta^n$ as in Definition \ref{implicitatlasonFloer}(\ref{implicitatlasFloerD}) which is $S^1$-invariant with $C\pitchfork D$ in the sense of Definition \ref{IAonfloerthickeningsdef}(\ref{transversalitypartIAfloer}) and so that adding these intersections to $C$ as extra marked points makes $C$ stable, except for irreducible components $S^1\times\mathbb R\subseteq C$ on which $u$ is independent of the $S^1$-coordinate (``Morse flow lines'').
nodes.label: stabilizationlemmaforHFSS

nodes.name: Proof
nodes.statement:
Instead of finding an $S^1$-invariant $D\subseteq M	imes S^1	imes\Delta^n$, we find a $D\subseteq M	imes\Delta^n$ (which is clearly equivalent) and we ignore the $S^1$ factor in the codomain of $u$. As in Lemma ef{stabilizationlemmaforHF}, it suffices to show that for any unstable component $C_0\subseteq C$, either $C_0$ is a Morse flow line or there exists a point (other than a node) where $d((\operatorname{id}_M	imes\ell)\circ u):TC_0	o TM	imes T\Delta^n$ is injective. If the projection $C_0	o S^1	imes\mathbb R$ is constant, then $u:C_0	o M$ is a (nonconstant!) $J$-holomorphic sphere and we are done as in Lemma ef{stabilizationlemmaforHF}. Hence it suffices to treat the case when $u:C_0	o S^1	imes\mathbb R$ is not constant. Thus $u:C_0	o S^1	imes\mathbb R$ is an isomorphism, so we can use $(t,s)\in S^1	imes\mathbb R$ as coordinates on $C_0$. Now we split into two cases. First, suppose $\ell:\mathbb R	o\Delta^n$ is not constant. If $u:C_0	o M$ is independent of the $S^1$ coordinate, then it is a Morse flow line, and we do not need to stabilize. Otherwise, there is a point where $ rac{\partial u}{\partial t}
e 0$, and since $\ell:\mathbb R	o\Delta^n$ has nonvanishing derivative everywhere, it follows that $du$ is injective at this point. Second, suppose $\ell:\mathbb R	o\Delta^n$ is constant. Then our map $u:C_0	o M$ satisfies:  egin{equation}  rac{\partial u}{\partial t}+J\circ rac{\partial u}{\partial s}=
abla H \end{equation} Certainly $u:C_0	o M$ is not constant; otherwise it would be unstable (infinite automorphism group). Thus $du$ is nonzero somewhere. If $du$ has rank two somewhere, then we are done. Thus let us suppose that this is not the case and show that $u|C_0$ is independent of the $t$ coordinate (and thus is a Morse flow line). Thus there exists some open set $U\subseteq C_0=S^1	imes\mathbb R$ where $du$ has rank $1$. Inside $U$, we have $\ker du\subseteq TC_0=T(S^1	imes\mathbb R)$ is an (integrable!) $1$-dimensional distribution, so $U$ is equipped with a $1$-dimensional foliation and $u$ is constant on the leaves. Thus we have (locally) a factorization $u:S^1	imes\mathbb R\xrightarrow r(-\epsilon,\epsilon)\xrightarrow wM$, the leaves of the foliation being given by $r^{-1}(\delta)$ for $\delta\in(-\epsilon,\epsilon)$. Now \eqref{pseudoholoncylinderformorseHamiltonian} becomes:  egin{equation} \Bigl( rac{\partial r}{\partial t}+ rac{\partial r}{\partial s}\cdot J\Bigr)\cdot w'(r(s,t))=(
abla H)(w(r(s,t))) \end{equation} Since $du$ has rank $1$, we know that $w'(r(s,t))
e 0$. Hence the value of $r(s,t)$ determines the value of its derivative uniquely, i.e.\ $dr$ is constant along the leaves $r^{-1}(\delta)$ of the foliation. It follows that the foliation is (locally) linear(!) and that we can follow any leaf infinitely in both directions and it never exits $U$ (since $dr=0$ outside $U$). Now if any leaf had nonzero slope, it would force $u:C_0	o M$ to be constant, a contradiction. Thus all leaves have slope zero; in other words $u$ is independent of the $S^1$-coordinate over $U=S^1	imes U'$. But now we see that $U'=\mathbb R$, since if $U'$ had boundary, it would imply that we have a Morse flow line reaching a critical point in finite time. Thus $u$ is (globally) a Morse flow line.
nodes.statement_short: Find an injectivity point on each unstable non-Morse component, by cases on whether the flow line on the simplex is constant. In the constant case a rank-one foliation argument shows u is S^1-independent, i.e. a Morse flow line.

nodes.name: Floer equation for an $S^1$-invariant Hamiltonian
nodes.statement: \frac{\partial u}{\partial t}+J\circ\frac{\partial u}{\partial s}=\nabla H
nodes.label: pseudoholoncylinderformorseHamiltonian

nodes.name: Floer equation in foliation coordinates
nodes.statement: \Bigl(\frac{\partial r}{\partial t}+\frac{\partial r}{\partial s}\cdot J\Bigr)\cdot w'(r(s,t))=(\nabla H)(w(r(s,t)))

Arnold conjectured that the minimal number of fixed points of a non-degenerate Hamiltonian symplectomorphism $M\to M$ enjoys a lower bound similar to the minimal number of critical points of a Morse function on $M$ (known as the Morse number of $M$).
nodes.name: Arnold conjecture
nodes.statement_short: The number of fixed points of a nondegenerate Hamiltonian symplectomorphism is bounded below like the Morse number of M.
nodes.section: 10.7 Calculation of Hamiltonian Floer homology and the Arnold conjecture

nodes.statement: It remains an open problem to obtain a sharp bound on the minimal number of symplectic fixed points, though much progress has been made.
nodes.name: Sharp bound on symplectic fixed points
nodes.section: 10.7 Calculation of Hamiltonian Floer homology and the Arnold conjecture

nodes.statement: Arnold's conjecture was proved for surfaces by Eliashberg \cite{eliashbergsurfaces} and for tori by Conley--Zehnder \cite{conleyzehnder}.
nodes.name: Arnold conjecture for surfaces and tori
nodes.section: 10.7 Calculation of Hamiltonian Floer homology and the Arnold conjecture

nodes.statement: The existence of at least one fixed point was shown by Gromov \cite[p331, 2.3$B_4'$]{gromov} under the assumption $\omega|_{\pi_2(M)}=0$.
nodes.name: Gromov's fixed point theorem
conclusions: The existence of at least one fixed point
nodes.section: 10.7 Calculation of Hamiltonian Floer homology and the Arnold conjecture

nodes.statement: A major breakthrough was made by Floer \cite{floersfhs}, who introduced Hamiltonian Floer homology and showed (under some assumptions) that it is isomorphic to singular homology.
nodes.name: Floer's theorem (Hamiltonian Floer homology = singular homology)
nodes.section: 10.7 Calculation of Hamiltonian Floer homology and the Arnold conjecture

nodes.statement: Indeed, if Hamiltonian Floer homology can be defined and shown to be isomorphic to singular homology, then we get a lower bound towards the Arnold conjecture of the form: \begin{equation} \min\left\{\operatorname{rk} D_\bullet\,\middle|\,(D_\bullet,d)\;\begin{matrix}\text{a free differential graded $\Lambda$-module}\hfill\cr\text{homotopy equivalent to }C_\bullet(M;\Lambda)\hfill\end{matrix}\right\} \end{equation} where $\Lambda$ is the Novikov ring: \begin{equation} \Lambda:=\mathbb Z[\operatorname{im}(\pi_2(M)\xrightarrow{\omega\oplus 2c_1(M)}\mathbb R\oplus\mathbb Z)]^\wedge \end{equation} completed with respect to $\omega$ and graded by $2c_1$ (note that if the grading on $\Lambda$ is nontrivial, a ``differential graded $\Lambda$-module'' is not the same as a ``complex of $\Lambda$-modules'').
nodes.name: Floer-theoretic lower bound towards Arnold
nodes.statement_short: If HF is defined and isomorphic to singular homology, #fixed points is at least the minimal rank of a free dg Lambda-module homotopy equivalent to C_*(M;Lambda).
nodes.section: 10.7 Calculation of Hamiltonian Floer homology and the Arnold conjecture

nodes.name: Minimal rank lower bound
nodes.statement: \min\left\{\operatorname{rk} D_\bullet\,\middle|\,(D_\bullet,d)\;\begin{matrix}\text{a free differential graded $\Lambda$-module}\hfill\cr\text{homotopy equivalent to }C_\bullet(M;\Lambda)\hfill\end{matrix}\right\}
nodes.section: 10.7 Calculation of Hamiltonian Floer homology and the Arnold conjecture
nodes.label: mingenerators

nodes.name: Novikov ring $\Lambda$
nodes.statement: \Lambda:=\mathbb Z[\operatorname{im}(\pi_2(M)\xrightarrow{\omega\oplus 2c_1(M)}\mathbb R\oplus\mathbb Z)]^\wedge
nodes.section: 10.7 Calculation of Hamiltonian Floer homology and the Arnold conjecture

nodes.statement: Note that for $\Lambda=\mathbb Z[\pi_1(M)]$ and ``simple homotopy equivalent'' in place of ``homotopy equivalent'', the lower bound \eqref{mingenerators} is precisely the stable Morse number of $M$ (see Damian \cite[p424, Corollary 2.6]{damian}).
nodes.name: Lower bound equals stable Morse number
nodes.section: 10.7 Calculation of Hamiltonian Floer homology and the Arnold conjecture

nodes.name: Calculation of Hamiltonian Floer homology
nodes.statement: $F\mathbb H^\bullet(M)$ is isomorphic to $H^\bullet(M;\mathbb Z)\otimes\mathbb Q[[\pi]]$ as modules over $\mathbb Q[[\pi]]$.
nodes.section: 10.7 Calculation of Hamiltonian Floer homology and the Arnold conjecture
nodes.statement_short: Hamiltonian Floer homology is isomorphic to H^*(M; Z) tensor Q[[pi]].
conclusions: $F\mathbb H^\bullet(M)$ is isomorphic to $H^\bullet(M;\mathbb Z)\otimes\mathbb Q[[\pi]]$ as modules over $\mathbb Q[[\pi]]$.
nodes.label: HFcalculation

nodes.name: Proof
nodes.statement: We use the setup of \S\ref{SSham}--\ref{SSequivariantFloeratlassec}. The homology groups associated to the flow category diagram $\overline{\mathcal M}/\ast$ and the implicit atlas $\mathcal A$ are by definition $F\mathbb H^\bullet(M)$. Now, as we observed previously, the thickened moduli spaces of $\mathcal A$ are open subsets of those of $\mathcal B$, so by Lemma \ref{homologyopenreduction}, $F\mathbb H^\bullet(M)$ may also be defined using the implicit atlas $\mathcal B$ on $\overline{\mathcal M}/\ast$. Now $\mathcal B^{S^1}\subseteq\mathcal B$ is a subatlas, so by Lemma \ref{homologysameassubatlas} it may also be used to define $F\mathbb H^\bullet(M)$. Thus let us restrict attention to the atlas $\mathcal B^{S^1}$ on $\overline{\mathcal M}/\ast$. Recall that by Lemma \ref{morseistransverse}, there is a partition into closed subsets: \begin{equation} \overline{\mathcal M}(\sigma,p,q)=\overline{\mathcal M}(\sigma,p,q)^{S^1}\sqcup[\overline{\mathcal M}(\sigma,p,q)\setminus\overline{\mathcal M}(\sigma,p,q)^{S^1}] \end{equation} Now we apply $S^1$-localization to $\mathcal B^{S^1}$ on $\overline{\mathcal M}/\ast$ in the form of Theorem \ref{circlelocalizationhomology}, which applies since $S^1$ acts with finite stabilizers on $\overline{\mathcal M}(\sigma,p,q)\setminus\overline{\mathcal M}(\sigma,p,q)^{S^1}$ and our coefficient group is $\mathbb Q$. It follows that $F\mathbb H^\bullet(M)$ may be defined using the flow category diagram $\overline{\mathcal M}^{S^1}/\ast$ with the implicit atlas obtained from $\mathcal B^{S^1}$ by removing $\overline{\mathcal M}\setminus\overline{\mathcal M}^{S^1}$ from every thickening. All the flow spaces of $\overline{\mathcal M}^{S^1}/\ast$ are cut out transversally by Lemma \ref{morseistransverse}, so by Proposition \ref{iftransversejustcountzero}, the homology groups of $\overline{\mathcal M}^{S^1}/\ast$ can be defined by simply counting the $0$-dimensional flow spaces according to the orientations $\omega$. Now $\overline{\mathcal M}^{S^1}$ coincides with the Morse flow category diagram $\overline{\mathcal M}_\mathrm{morse}/\ast$ of $H$ by Lemma \ref{fixedismorse} (with the same orientations by Proposition \ref{HFgluingSS}), and this gives the desired isomorphism.
nodes.section: 10.7 Calculation of Hamiltonian Floer homology and the Arnold conjecture
nodes.statement_short: Pass from atlas A to B to the S^1-equivariant subatlas B^{S^1}, apply S^1-localization to reduce to the fixed locus, which is the transversally cut out Morse flow category.

nodes.name: Partition into $S^1$-fixed and free parts (restated)
nodes.statement: \overline{\mathcal M}(\sigma,p,q)=\overline{\mathcal M}(\sigma,p,q)^{S^1}\sqcup[\overline{\mathcal M}(\sigma,p,q)\setminus\overline{\mathcal M}(\sigma,p,q)^{S^1}]
nodes.section: 10.7 Calculation of Hamiltonian Floer homology and the Arnold conjecture

nodes.name: Canonicity of the isomorphism (expected)
nodes.statement: One expects to be able show that the isomorphism in Theorem \ref{HFcalculation} is canonical by considering continuation maps and chain homotopies associated to families of Morse functions.
nodes.section: 10.7 Calculation of Hamiltonian Floer homology and the Arnold conjecture
nodes.statement_short: The isomorphism FH = H(M) should be canonical via continuation maps.

nodes.name: Arnold conjecture
nodes.statement: Let $H:M\times S^1\to\mathbb R$ be a smooth function whose time $1$ Hamiltonian flow $\phi_H:M\to M$ has non-degenerate fixed points. Then $\#\operatorname{Fix}\phi_H\geq\dim H_\bullet(M;\mathbb Q)$ (in fact, we may replace $\operatorname{Fix}\phi_H$ with those fixed points whose associated periodic orbit is null-homotopic in $M$).
nodes.section: 10.7 Calculation of Hamiltonian Floer homology and the Arnold conjecture
nodes.statement_short: A nondegenerate Hamiltonian diffeomorphism has at least dim H_*(M;Q) fixed points.
assumptions: Let $H:M\times S^1\to\mathbb R$ be a smooth function whose time $1$ Hamiltonian flow $\phi_H:M\to M$ has non-degenerate fixed points.
conclusions: $\#\operatorname{Fix}\phi_H\geq\dim H_\bullet(M;\mathbb Q)$

nodes.name: Proof
nodes.statement: Pick any $\omega$-compatible almost complex structure $J$ and consider the vertex $(J,H)\in J\!H_\bullet(M)$. Over this vertex, pick any complex $F\mathbb C^\bullet(M)$ which calculates $F\mathbb H^\bullet(M)$. Then $F\mathbb C^\bullet(M)$ is a free $\mathbb Q[[\pi]]$-module of rank: \begin{equation} \operatorname{rk}_{\mathbb Q[[\pi]]}F\mathbb C^\bullet(M)\leq\#\operatorname{Fix}\phi_H \end{equation} (its rank equals the number of null-homotopic periodic orbits). By Theorem \ref{HFcalculation}, the homology $F\mathbb H^\bullet(M)$ is free of rank: \begin{equation} \operatorname{rk}_{\mathbb Q[[\pi]]}F\mathbb H^\bullet(M)=\dim H_\bullet(M;\mathbb Q) \end{equation} Now by definition, there is a $\mathbb Q[[\pi]]$-linear boundary map $d:F\mathbb C^\bullet(M)\to F\mathbb C^{\bullet+1}(M)$ and by definition $\operatorname{rk}_{\mathbb Q[[\pi]]}F\mathbb H^\bullet(M)=\ker d/\operatorname{im} d$. Now apply Lemma \ref{homologyhassmallerrank} to conclude that: \begin{equation} \operatorname{rk}_{\mathbb Q[[\pi]]}F\mathbb H^\bullet(M)\leq\operatorname{rk}_{\mathbb Q[[\pi]]}F\mathbb C^\bullet(M) \end{equation} Thus we are done.
nodes.section: 10.7 Calculation of Hamiltonian Floer homology and the Arnold conjecture
nodes.statement_short: Compare ranks: the Floer complex has rank at most #Fix, its homology has rank dim H_*(M;Q) by the calculation, and homology rank is at most chain rank.

nodes.name: Rank of Floer complex bound
nodes.statement: \operatorname{rk}_{\mathbb Q[[\pi]]}F\mathbb C^\bullet(M)\leq\#\operatorname{Fix}\phi_H
nodes.section: 10.7 Calculation of Hamiltonian Floer homology and the Arnold conjecture

nodes.name: Rank of Floer homology
nodes.statement: \operatorname{rk}_{\mathbb Q[[\pi]]}F\mathbb H^\bullet(M)=\dim H_\bullet(M;\mathbb Q)
nodes.section: 10.7 Calculation of Hamiltonian Floer homology and the Arnold conjecture

nodes.name: Homology rank at most chain rank
nodes.statement: \operatorname{rk}_{\mathbb Q[[\pi]]}F\mathbb H^\bullet(M)\leq\operatorname{rk}_{\mathbb Q[[\pi]]}F\mathbb C^\bullet(M)
nodes.section: 10.7 Calculation of Hamiltonian Floer homology and the Arnold conjecture

nodes.name: Homology of a free complex has smaller rank
nodes.statement: Let $M$ be a free module over a commutative ring $R$, and let $d:M\to M$ satisfy $d^2=0$. If $H=\ker d/\operatorname{im} d$ is free, then $\operatorname{rk} H\leq\operatorname{rk} M$.
assumptions: Let $M$ be a free module over a commutative ring $R$, and let $d:M\to M$ satisfy $d^2=0$.
$H=\ker d/\operatorname{im} d$ is free
conclusions: $\operatorname{rk} H\leq\operatorname{rk} M$
nodes.label: homologyhassmallerrank

nodes.name: Proof
nodes.statement: Since $H$ is free, it is projective, so the surjection $\ker d\twoheadrightarrow H$ has a section $H\hookrightarrow\ker d\subseteq M$. Hence there is an injection $H\hookrightarrow M$. Now use Lemma \ref{freesubhassmallerrank}.
nodes.statement_short: H free so projective; lift H into ker d inside M and apply the rank inequality for free submodules.

nodes.name: Rank of free submodules
nodes.statement: Let $\phi:R^{\oplus A}\hookrightarrow R^{\oplus B}$ be an inclusion of free modules over a commutative ring $R$. Then $A\leq B$.
assumptions: Let $\phi:R^{\oplus A}\hookrightarrow R^{\oplus B}$ be an inclusion of free modules over a commutative ring $R$.
conclusions: $A\leq B$
nodes.label: freesubhassmallerrank

nodes.name: Proof
nodes.statement: This is a standard yet tricky exercise. We recall one of the (many) standard proofs. The map $\phi$ is described by some matrix of $A\times B$ elements of $R$. Certainly the kernel of this matrix remains zero over the subring of $R$ generated by its entries. Thus we may assume without loss of generality that $R$ is a finitely generated $\mathbb Z$-algebra. Now localize at a prime ideal $\mathfrak p\subset R$ of height zero. Localization is exact, so again $\phi$ remains injective. Thus we may assume without loss of generality that $R$ is a local Noetherian ring of dimension zero, and thus $R$ is an Artin local ring \cite[p90, Theorem 8.5]{atiyahmacdonald}. Since $R$ is Artinian, all finitely generated modules have finite length \cite[pp76--77, Propositions 6.5 and 6.8]{atiyahmacdonald}, and hence there is a length homomorphism $K_0(R)\to\mathbb Z$ \cite[p77, Proposition 6.9]{atiyahmacdonald} (which is clearly an isomorphism since $R$ is local). It thus follows from the short exact sequence $0\to R^{\oplus A}\xrightarrow\phi R^{\oplus B}\to\operatorname{coker}\phi\to 0$ that $A\leq B$.
nodes.statement_short: Reduce to a finitely generated Z-algebra, localize at a height-zero prime to get an Artin local ring, and use the length homomorphism on K_0.

nodes.name: Space (locally compact Hausdorff)
nodes.statement: In this appendix, by \emph{space} we mean locally compact Hausdorff space.

nodes.name: Complex, homology, acyclicity, quasi-isomorphism, shift, truncation, total complex
nodes.statement: By a \emph{complex} $C^\bullet$ we mean a $\mathbb Z$-graded object $\bigoplus_{i\in\mathbb Z}C^i$ (in some abelian category) along with a degree $1$ endomorphism $d$ with $d^2=0$. The \emph{homology} of a complex $C^\bullet$ is denoted $H^\bullet C^\bullet$ (defined by $H^iC^\bullet:=\ker(C^i\xrightarrow dC^{i+1})/\operatorname{im}(C^{i-1}\xrightarrow dC^i)$). A complex is called \emph{acyclic} iff its homology vanishes. A map of complexes $f:A^\bullet\to B^\bullet$ is a called a \emph{quasi-isomorphism} iff it induces an isomorphism on homology. We will often use the fact that a map of complexes is a quasi-isomorphism iff its mapping cone is acyclic. The \emph{shift} of a complex $C^\bullet[n]$ is defined by $(C^\bullet[n])^i:=C^{i+n}$. We use the \emph{truncation functors} defined by: \begin{equation*} (\tau_{\geq i}C^\bullet)^j:=\begin{cases}C^j&j>i\cr\operatorname{coker}(C^{i-1}\xrightarrow dC^i)&j=i\cr 0&j<i\end{cases}\qquad (\tau_{\leq i}C^\bullet)^j:=\begin{cases}0&j>i\cr\ker(C^i\xrightarrow dC^{i+1})&j=i\cr C^j&j<i\end{cases} \end{equation*} Given a sequence of maps of complexes $A_0^\bullet\to\cdots\to A_n^\bullet$ such that adjacent maps compose to zero, we denote by $[A_0^\bullet\to\cdots\to A_n^{\bullet-n}]$ the associated total complex of this double complex. For example, $f:A^\bullet\to B^\bullet$ denotes a map, and $[A^\bullet\xrightarrow fB^{\bullet-1}]$ denotes its mapping cone.
nodes.statement_short: Standard conventions for complexes: homology, acyclic, quasi-isomorphism (iff acyclic cone), shift, truncations, total complexes and mapping cones.
nodes.label: complexconventions

nodes.name: Sign conventions (super tensor product)
nodes.statement: We fix sign conventions by making everything $\mathbb Z/2$-graded and always using the super tensor product $\otimes$ (namely, where the isomorphism $A\otimes B\xrightarrow\sim B\otimes A$ is given by $a\otimes b\mapsto(-1)^{\left|a\right|\left|b\right|}b\otimes a$ and where $(f\otimes g)(a\otimes b):=(-1)^{\left|g\right|\left|a\right|}f(a)\otimes g(b)$). We fix $\operatorname{Hom}(A,B)\otimes A\to B$ as given by $f\otimes a\mapsto f(a)$. Complexes are $(\mathbb Z,\mathbb Z/2)$-bigraded; differentials are always odd and chain maps are always even. Note that the $\mathbb Z/2$-grading of a complex is often, but not always, the reduction modulo $2$ of the $\mathbb Z$-grading.
