nodes.statement_short: Everything is Z/2-graded with the Koszul sign rule for the super tensor product; differentials odd, chain maps even.
nodes.label: signconventions

nodes.name: Limits over directed sets
nodes.statement: Direct limits and inverse limits always take place over directed sets.

nodes.name: Presheaf and K-presheaf
nodes.statement: Let $X$ be a space. A \emph{presheaf} (resp.\ \emph{$\mathcal K$-presheaf}) on $X$ is a contravariant functor from the category of open (resp.\ compact) sets of $X$ to the category of abelian groups. A morphism of presheaves is simply a natural transformation of functors. The category of presheaves (resp.\ $\mathcal K$-presheaves) is denoted $\operatorname{Prshv} X$ (resp.\ $\operatorname{Prshv}_\mathcal K X$).
nodes.statement_short: (K-)presheaves: contravariant functors from open (resp. compact) subsets of X to abelian groups.
nodes.origin_citation: standard; Lurie, Higher Topos Theory, Def. 7.3.4.1
differentia: from the category of open (resp.\ compact) sets of $X$ to the category of abelian groups

nodes.name: Stalk
nodes.statement: For a presheaf $\mathcal F$, let $\mathcal F_p:=\varinjlim_{p\in U}\mathcal F(U)$, and for a $\mathcal K$-presheaf $\mathcal F$ let $\mathcal F_p:=\mathcal F(\{p\})$. In both cases we say $\mathcal F_p$ is the \emph{stalk} of $\mathcal F$ at $p$.

nodes.name: Sheaf
nodes.statement: A \emph{sheaf} is a presheaf $\mathcal F$ satisfying the following condition: \begin{equation*} \tag{Sh}0\to\mathcal F\Bigl(\bigcup_{\alpha\in A}U_\alpha\Bigr)\to\prod_{\alpha\in A}\mathcal F(U_\alpha)\to\prod_{\alpha,\beta\in A}\mathcal F(U_\alpha\cap U_\beta)\quad\text{ is exact }\forall\text{ }\{U_\alpha\subseteq X\}_{\alpha\in A} \end{equation*} The category of sheaves on a space $X$ is denoted $\operatorname{Shv} X$ (a full subcategory of $\operatorname{Prshv} X$, meaning a morphism between sheaves is the same as a morphism of the corresponding presheaves).
differentia: satisfying the following condition

nodes.name: Sheaf axiom (Sh)
nodes.statement: \tag{Sh}0\to\mathcal F\Bigl(\bigcup_{\alpha\in A}U_\alpha\Bigr)\to\prod_{\alpha\in A}\mathcal F(U_\alpha)\to\prod_{\alpha,\beta\in A}\mathcal F(U_\alpha\cap U_\beta)\quad\text{ is exact }\forall\text{ }\{U_\alpha\subseteq X\}_{\alpha\in A}
nodes.label: opensheafproperty

nodes.name: K-sheaf
nodes.statement: A \emph{$\mathcal K$-sheaf} is a $\mathcal K$-presheaf $\mathcal F$ satisfying the following three conditions:\footnote{A similar set of axioms appears in Lurie \cite[Definition 7.3.4.1]{luriehtt}.} \begin{align*} \tag{Sh$_\mathcal K$1}\mathcal F(\varnothing)&=0\\ \tag{Sh$_\mathcal K$2}0\to\mathcal F(K_1\cup K_2)\to\mathcal F(K_1)\oplus\mathcal F(K_2)\to\mathcal F(K_1\cap K_2)&\text{ is exact }\forall\text{ }K_1,K_2\subseteq X\\ \tag{Sh$_\mathcal K$3}\varinjlim_{\begin{smallmatrix}K\subseteq U\cr U\textrm{ open}\end{smallmatrix}}\mathcal F(\overline U)\to\mathcal F(K)&\text{ is an isomorphism }\forall\text{ }K\subseteq X \end{align*} The category of $\mathcal K$-sheaves on a space $X$ is denoted $\operatorname{Shv}_\mathcal K X$ (a full subcategory of $\operatorname{Prshv}_\mathcal K X$).
nodes.statement_short: A K-presheaf vanishing on the empty set, satisfying Mayer-Vietoris exactness for pairs of compacts, and continuity under shrinking neighborhoods.

nodes.name: K-sheaf axioms (Sh_K1)-(Sh_K3)
nodes.statement: \tag{Sh$_\mathcal K$1}\mathcal F(\varnothing)&=0\\ \tag{Sh$_\mathcal K$2}0\to\mathcal F(K_1\cup K_2)\to\mathcal F(K_1)\oplus\mathcal F(K_2)\to\mathcal F(K_1\cap K_2)&\text{ is exact }\forall\text{ }K_1,K_2\subseteq X\\ \tag{Sh$_\mathcal K$3}\varinjlim_{\begin{smallmatrix}K\subseteq U\cr U\textrm{ open}\end{smallmatrix}}\mathcal F(\overline U)\to\mathcal F(K)&\text{ is an isomorphism }\forall\text{ }K\subseteq X
nodes.label: sheafvanishing

nodes.name: Compact set as intersection of closed neighborhoods
nodes.statement: It is always the case that $K=\bigcap_{\begin{smallmatrix}K\subseteq U\cr U\textrm{ open}\end{smallmatrix}}\overline U$ for compact $K\subseteq X$.
nodes.label: nbhdintersectiongood

nodes.name: Functors alpha^* and alpha_* between K-presheaves and presheaves
nodes.statement: We define functors: \begin{equation} \begin{tikzcd}\operatorname{Prshv}_\mathcal K X\ar[yshift=0.5ex]{r}{\alpha_\ast}&\ar[yshift=-0.5ex]{l}{\alpha^\ast}\operatorname{Prshv} X\end{tikzcd} \end{equation} by the formulas: \begin{align} (\alpha^\ast\mathcal F)(K)&:=\varinjlim_{\begin{smallmatrix}K\subseteq U\cr U\textrm{ open}\end{smallmatrix}}\mathcal F(U)\\ (\alpha_\ast\mathcal F)(U)&:=\varprojlim_{\begin{smallmatrix}K\subseteq U\cr K\textrm{ compact}\end{smallmatrix}}\mathcal F(K) \end{align} It is easy to see that there is an adjunction $\operatorname{Hom}_{\operatorname{Prshv}_\mathcal K X}(\alpha^\ast\mathcal F,\mathcal G)=\operatorname{Hom}_{\operatorname{Prshv} X}(\mathcal F,\alpha_\ast\mathcal G)$ (giving an element of either $\operatorname{Hom}$-set is the same as giving a compatible system of maps $\mathcal F(U)\to\mathcal G(K)$ for pairs $K\subseteq U$).
nodes.statement_short: alpha^* takes the direct limit over open neighborhoods, alpha_* the inverse limit over compact subsets; they are adjoint.
nodes.label: opencptrelationfunctors

nodes.name: Functors alpha_* and alpha^*
nodes.statement: \begin{tikzcd}\operatorname{Prshv}_\mathcal K X\ar[yshift=0.5ex]{r}{\alpha_\ast}&\ar[yshift=-0.5ex]{l}{\alpha^\ast}\operatorname{Prshv} X\end{tikzcd}

nodes.name: Formulas for alpha^* and alpha_*
nodes.statement: (\alpha^\ast\mathcal F)(K)&:=\varinjlim_{\begin{smallmatrix}K\subseteq U\cr U\textrm{ open}\end{smallmatrix}}\mathcal F(U)\\ (\alpha_\ast\mathcal F)(U)&:=\varprojlim_{\begin{smallmatrix}K\subseteq U\cr K\textrm{ compact}\end{smallmatrix}}\mathcal F(K)
nodes.label: alphaast

nodes.name: Intersections of neighborhoods are cofinal
nodes.statement: Let $K_1,\ldots,K_n\subseteq X$ be compact. Then $\{U_1\cap\cdots\cap U_n\}_{\text{open }U_i\supseteq K_i}$ forms a cofinal system of neighborhoods of $K_1\cap\cdots\cap K_n$.
assumptions: Let $K_1,\ldots,K_n\subseteq X$ be compact.
conclusions: $\{U_1\cap\cdots\cap U_n\}_{\text{open }U_i\supseteq K_i}$ forms a cofinal system of neighborhoods of $K_1\cap\cdots\cap K_n$
nodes.label: intersectioncofinal

nodes.name: Proof
nodes.statement: We may assume without loss of generality that $X$ is compact. By induction, it suffices to treat the case $n=2$. The rest is an exercise (use the fact that a compact Hausdorff space is normal).
nodes.statement_short: Reduce to $X$ compact and $n=2$ by induction; the rest is left as an exercise using normality of compact Hausdorff spaces.

nodes.name: Equivalence of sheaves and K-sheaves
nodes.statement: We have: \begin{equation} \begin{tikzcd}\operatorname{Shv}_\mathcal K X\ar[yshift=0.5ex]{r}{\alpha_\ast}&\ar[yshift=-0.5ex]{l}{\alpha^\ast}\operatorname{Shv} X\end{tikzcd} \end{equation} and this is an equivalence of categories.\footnote{A similar result appears in Lurie \cite[Corollary 7.3.4.10]{luriehtt}.}
nodes.statement_short: alpha^* and alpha_* restrict to an equivalence between K-sheaves and sheaves on X.
conclusions: and this is an equivalence of categories.
nodes.label: opencptshvequivalence

nodes.name: Equivalence Shv_K X = Shv X
nodes.statement: \begin{tikzcd}\operatorname{Shv}_\mathcal K X\ar[yshift=0.5ex]{r}{\alpha_\ast}&\ar[yshift=-0.5ex]{l}{\alpha^\ast}\operatorname{Shv} X\end{tikzcd}

nodes.name: Proof
nodes.statement: Suppose $\mathcal F$ is a sheaf, and let us verify $\alpha^\ast\mathcal F$ is a $\mathcal K$-sheaf. Axiom \eqref{sheafvanishing} is clear (take $A=\varnothing$ in \eqref{opensheafproperty}). Axiom \eqref{sheafproperty} follows from \eqref{opensheafproperty} and Lemma \ref{intersectioncofinal} since direct limits are exact. Axiom \eqref{sheafcontinuity} is clear from the definition also. Suppose $\mathcal F$ is a $\mathcal K$-sheaf, and let us verify that $\alpha_\ast\mathcal F$ is a sheaf. Let us first observe that (by induction using \eqref{sheafvanishing} and \eqref{sheafproperty}) if $\{K_\alpha\subseteq X\}_{\alpha\in A}$ is any collection of compact sets, all but finitely many of which are empty, then the following is exact: \begin{equation} 0\to\mathcal F\Bigl(\bigcup_{\alpha\in A}K_\alpha\Bigr)\to\prod_{\alpha\in A}\mathcal F(K_\alpha)\to\prod_{\alpha,\beta\in A}\mathcal F(K_\alpha\cap K_\beta) \end{equation} Let us now verify axiom \eqref{opensheafproperty} for $\alpha_\ast\mathcal F$ for open sets $\{U_\alpha\subseteq X\}_{\alpha\in A}$. Certainly \eqref{opensheafproperty} is the inverse limit of \eqref{compactfiniteexact} over all collections of compact subsets $\{K_\alpha\subseteq U_\alpha\}_{\alpha\in A}$ for which $K_\alpha=\varnothing$ except for finitely many $\alpha\in A$. This is sufficient since inverse limit is left exact. Now to see that the adjoint pair $\alpha^\ast\dashv\alpha_\ast$ is actually an equivalence of categories, it suffices to show that the natural morphisms $\mathcal F\to\alpha_\ast\alpha^\ast\mathcal F$ and $\alpha^\ast\alpha_\ast\mathcal G\to\mathcal G$ are isomorphisms. In other words, we must show that following natural maps are isomorphisms: \begin{align} \mathcal F(U)&\to\varprojlim_{\begin{smallmatrix}K\subseteq U\cr K\textrm{ compact}\end{smallmatrix}}\varinjlim_{\begin{smallmatrix}K\subseteq U'\cr U'\textrm{ open}\end{smallmatrix}}\mathcal F(U')\\ \varinjlim_{\begin{smallmatrix}K\subseteq U\cr U\textrm{ open}\end{smallmatrix}}\varprojlim_{\begin{smallmatrix}K'\subseteq U\cr K'\textrm{ compact}\end{smallmatrix}}\mathcal G(K')&\to\mathcal G(K) \end{align} The right hand side of \eqref{Funit} can be thought of as the inverse limit of $\mathcal F(U')$ over all open $U'\subseteq U$ with $\overline{U'}\subseteq U$ and $\overline{U'}$ compact. It is easy to see that the map from $\mathcal F(U)$ to this inverse limit is an isomorphism if $\mathcal F$ is a sheaf. The left hand side of \eqref{Gunit} can be identified with the left hand side of \eqref{sheafcontinuity}, and thus the map to $\mathcal G(K)$ is an isomorphism if $\mathcal F$ is a $\mathcal K$-sheaf.
nodes.statement_short: Check each functor preserves the sheaf axioms (using cofinality and exactness of limits), then show unit and counit are isomorphisms.

nodes.name: Exactness for finite compact collections
nodes.statement: 0\to\mathcal F\Bigl(\bigcup_{\alpha\in A}K_\alpha\Bigr)\to\prod_{\alpha\in A}\mathcal F(K_\alpha)\to\prod_{\alpha,\beta\in A}\mathcal F(K_\alpha\cap K_\beta)
nodes.label: compactfiniteexact

nodes.name: Unit and counit maps
nodes.statement: \mathcal F(U)&\to\varprojlim_{\begin{smallmatrix}K\subseteq U\cr K\textrm{ compact}\end{smallmatrix}}\varinjlim_{\begin{smallmatrix}K\subseteq U'\cr U'\textrm{ open}\end{smallmatrix}}\mathcal F(U')\\ \varinjlim_{\begin{smallmatrix}K\subseteq U\cr U\textrm{ open}\end{smallmatrix}}\varprojlim_{\begin{smallmatrix}K'\subseteq U\cr K'\textrm{ compact}\end{smallmatrix}}\mathcal G(K')&\to\mathcal G(K)
nodes.label: Funit

nodes.name: Convention: the word sheaf
nodes.statement: In view of the canonical equivalence of categories $\operatorname{Shv} X=\operatorname{Shv}_\mathcal K X$ from Lemma \ref{opencptshvequivalence}, we use the single word ``sheaf'' for an object of either category.

nodes.name: Filtered intersections for K-presheaves
nodes.statement: Let $\{K_\alpha\}_{\alpha\in A}$ be a filtered directed system of compact subsets of $X$ (i.e.\ for all $\alpha,\beta\in A$ there exists $\gamma\in A$ with $K_\gamma\subseteq K_\alpha\cap K_\beta$). Then for any $\mathcal F$ satisfying \eqref{sheafcontinuity}, the following is an isomorphism: \begin{equation} \varinjlim_{\alpha\in A}\mathcal F(K_\alpha)\to\mathcal F\Bigl(\bigcap_{\alpha\in A}K_\alpha\Bigr) \end{equation}
nodes.statement_short: For F satisfying (Sh_K3), F of a filtered intersection of compacts is the direct limit of F over the system.
assumptions: Let $\{K_\alpha\}_{\alpha\in A}$ be a filtered directed system of compact subsets of $X$
for any $\mathcal F$ satisfying \eqref{sheafcontinuity}
conclusions: the following is an isomorphism:
nodes.label: anycompactintersectionworksSH

nodes.name: Filtered intersection isomorphism
nodes.statement: \varinjlim_{\alpha\in A}\mathcal F(K_\alpha)\to\mathcal F\Bigl(\bigcap_{\alpha\in A}K_\alpha\Bigr)

nodes.name: Proof
nodes.statement: Write $K:=\bigcap_{\alpha\in A}K_\alpha$. Now consider the diagram: \begin{equation} \begin{tikzcd} \varinjlim\limits_{\alpha\in A}\varinjlim\limits_{\begin{smallmatrix}K_\alpha\subseteq U\cr U\textrm{ open}\end{smallmatrix}}\mathcal F(\overline U)\ar{r}\ar{d}& \varinjlim\limits_{\begin{smallmatrix}\exists\alpha\in A:K_\alpha\subseteq U\cr U\textrm{ open}\end{smallmatrix}}\mathcal F(\overline U)\ar{r}& \varinjlim\limits_{\begin{smallmatrix}K\subseteq U\cr U\textrm{ open}\end{smallmatrix}}\mathcal F(\overline U)\ar{d}\\ \varinjlim\limits_{\alpha\in A}\mathcal F(K_\alpha)\ar{rr}&&\mathcal F(K) \end{tikzcd} \end{equation} The vertical maps are both isomorphisms by \eqref{sheafcontinuity}. The first horizontal map is an isomorphism since $\{K_\alpha\}_{\alpha\in A}$ is filtered. It thus remains to show that if $K\subseteq U$ and $U$ is open, then there exists $\alpha\in A$ such that $K_\alpha\subseteq U$. Since $K\subseteq U$, we have $(X\setminus U)\cap K=\varnothing$, so $\bigcap_{\alpha\in A}(X\setminus U)\cap K_\alpha=\varnothing$. This is a filtered directed system of compact sets, and so the intersection being empty implies that one of the terms $(X\setminus U)\cap K_\alpha$ is empty, so $K_\alpha\subseteq U$ as desired.
nodes.statement_short: Compare both sides via a diagram whose vertical maps are isomorphisms by (Sh_K3); a compactness argument shows the neighborhood systems are cofinal.

nodes.name: Comparison diagram for filtered intersections
nodes.statement: \begin{tikzcd} \varinjlim\limits_{\alpha\in A}\varinjlim\limits_{\begin{smallmatrix}K_\alpha\subseteq U\cr U\textrm{ open}\end{smallmatrix}}\mathcal F(\overline U)\ar{r}\ar{d}& \varinjlim\limits_{\begin{smallmatrix}\exists\alpha\in A:K_\alpha\subseteq U\cr U\textrm{ open}\end{smallmatrix}}\mathcal F(\overline U)\ar{r}& \varinjlim\limits_{\begin{smallmatrix}K\subseteq U\cr U\textrm{ open}\end{smallmatrix}}\mathcal F(\overline U)\ar{d}\\ \varinjlim\limits_{\alpha\in A}\mathcal F(K_\alpha)\ar{rr}&&\mathcal F(K) \end{tikzcd}

nodes.name: Objectwise notions for complexes of (K-)presheaves
nodes.statement: Let $\mathcal F^\bullet$ be a complex of ($\mathcal K$-)presheaves. The notions from Convention \ref{complexconventions} are applied ``objectwise'', that is, to each complex $\mathcal F^\bullet(U)$ (resp.\ $F^\bullet(K)$) individually. For example, the homology $H^i\mathcal F^\bullet$ is again a ($\mathcal K$-)presheaf, and a map of ($\mathcal K$-)presheaves $f:\mathcal F^\bullet\to\mathcal G^\bullet$ is a quasi-isomorphism iff it induces an isomorphism of ($\mathcal K$-)presheaves $H^i\mathcal F^\bullet\to H^i\mathcal G^\bullet$ for all $i$. The homology ($\mathcal K$-)presheaves $H^i\mathcal F^\bullet$ should not be confused with the various flavors of \v Cech (hyper)cohomology $\check H^i(X;\mathcal F^\bullet)$ we introduce in \S\ref{cechsection}.
nodes.statement_short: Homology, quasi-isomorphism etc. of complexes of (K-)presheaves are taken objectwise; distinct from Čech hypercohomology.

nodes.name: Homotopy sheaf
nodes.statement: A \emph{homotopy sheaf} is a complex of presheaves $\mathcal F^\bullet$ satisfying the following condition: \begin{equation*} \tag{hSh}\hspace{-20pt}\biggl[\mathcal F^\bullet\Bigl(\bigcup_{\alpha\in A}U_\alpha\Bigr)\to\prod_{\alpha\in A}\mathcal F^{\bullet-1}(U_\alpha)\to\prod_{\alpha,\beta\in A}\mathcal F^{\bullet-2}(U_\alpha\cap U_\beta)\to\cdots\biggr]\text{ is acyclic }\forall\text{ }\{U_\alpha\subseteq X\}_{\alpha\in A} \end{equation*} The category of homotopy sheaves on a space $X$ is denoted $\operatorname{hShv} X$ (morphisms are morphisms of complexes of presheaves).
nodes.statement_short: A complex of presheaves whose Čech total complex for every open cover is acyclic.
differentia: satisfying the following condition

nodes.name: Homotopy sheaf condition (hSh)
nodes.statement: \tag{hSh}\hspace{-20pt}\biggl[\mathcal F^\bullet\Bigl(\bigcup_{\alpha\in A}U_\alpha\Bigr)\to\prod_{\alpha\in A}\mathcal F^{\bullet-1}(U_\alpha)\to\prod_{\alpha,\beta\in A}\mathcal F^{\bullet-2}(U_\alpha\cap U_\beta)\to\cdots\biggr]\text{ is acyclic }\forall\text{ }\{U_\alpha\subseteq X\}_{\alpha\in A}
nodes.label: openhomotopysheafproperty

nodes.name: Homotopy sheaf definition is illustrative
nodes.statement: The definition above is given for illustrative purposes only. It is probably only a good definition for $\mathcal F^\bullet$ which is bounded below, and it would perhaps be better to impose \eqref{openhomotopysheafproperty} for all \emph{hypercovers} of open subsets $U\subseteq X$.

nodes.name: Bounded below complexes of flasque sheaves are homotopy sheaves
nodes.statement: A sheaf $\mathcal F$ is \emph{flasque} iff all restriction maps $\mathcal F(U)\to\mathcal F(U')$ are surjective. It is easy to see that any bounded below complex of flasque sheaves $\mathcal F^\bullet$ is a homotopy sheaf. For example, let $\mathcal F^\bullet(U):=C^\bullet(U)$ be the presheaf of singular cochain complexes. Then the sheafification of $\mathcal F^\bullet$ is a complex of flasque sheaves, and thus is a homotopy sheaf. One can show (using barycentric subdivision) that the map from $\mathcal F^\bullet$ to its sheafification is a quasi-isomorphism, and hence $\mathcal F^\bullet$ is a homotopy sheaf as well.
nodes.statement_short: Flasque sheaf complexes, and singular cochains, are homotopy sheaves.
nodes.label: flasquehomotopysheafresolution

nodes.name: Homotopy K-sheaf
nodes.statement: A \emph{homotopy $\mathcal K$-sheaf} is a complex of $\mathcal K$-presheaves $\mathcal F^\bullet$ satisfying the following three conditions: \begin{align*} \tag{hSh$_\mathcal K$1}\mathcal F^\bullet(\varnothing)&\text{ is acyclic}\\ \tag{hSh$_\mathcal K$2}\hspace{-10pt}\bigl[\mathcal F^\bullet(K_1\cup K_2)\to\mathcal F^{\bullet-1}(K_1)\oplus\mathcal F^{\bullet-1}(K_2)\to\mathcal F^{\bullet-2}(K_1\cap K_2)\bigr]&\text{ is acyclic }\forall\text{ }K_1,K_2\subseteq X\\ \tag{hSh$_\mathcal K$3}\smash{\varinjlim_{\begin{smallmatrix}K\subseteq U\cr U\textrm{ open}\end{smallmatrix}}}\mathcal F^\bullet(\overline U)\to\mathcal F^\bullet(K)&\text{ is a quasi-isomorphism }\forall\text{ }K\subseteq X \end{align*} The category of homotopy $\mathcal K$-sheaves on a space $X$ is denoted $\operatorname{hShv}_\mathcal K X$ (morphisms are morphisms of complexes of $\mathcal K$-presheaves).
nodes.statement_short: A complex of K-presheaves acyclic on the empty set, with homotopy Mayer-Vietoris for pairs of compacts and quasi-isomorphic continuity.
differentia: satisfying the following three conditions
nodes.label: homotopyKsheaf

nodes.name: Homotopy K-sheaf axioms (hSh_K1)-(hSh_K3)
nodes.statement: \tag{hSh$_\mathcal K$1}\mathcal F^\bullet(\varnothing)&\text{ is acyclic}\\ \tag{hSh$_\mathcal K$2}\hspace{-10pt}\bigl[\mathcal F^\bullet(K_1\cup K_2)\to\mathcal F^{\bullet-1}(K_1)\oplus\mathcal F^{\bullet-1}(K_2)\to\mathcal F^{\bullet-2}(K_1\cap K_2)\bigr]&\text{ is acyclic }\forall\text{ }K_1,K_2\subseteq X\\ \tag{hSh$_\mathcal K$3}\smash{\varinjlim_{\begin{smallmatrix}K\subseteq U\cr U\textrm{ open}\end{smallmatrix}}}\mathcal F^\bullet(\overline U)\to\mathcal F^\bullet(K)&\text{ is a quasi-isomorphism }\forall\text{ }K\subseteq X
nodes.label: homotopysheafacyclic

nodes.name: Mayer-Vietoris sequence for homotopy K-sheaves
nodes.statement: Note that \eqref{homotopysheafproperty} gives rise to a ``Mayer--Vietoris'' long exact sequence in cohomology.

nodes.name: Complexes of soft K-sheaves are homotopy K-sheaves
nodes.statement: A $\mathcal K$-sheaf $\mathcal F$ is \emph{soft} iff all restriction maps $\mathcal F(K)\to\mathcal F(K')$ are surjective. It is easy to see that any complex of soft $\mathcal K$-sheaves $\mathcal F^\bullet$ is a homotopy $\mathcal K$-sheaf.
nodes.label: softhomotopysheafresolution

nodes.name: Expected equivalence of homotopy sheaves and homotopy K-sheaves
nodes.statement: In analogy with Definition \ref{opencptrelationfunctors}, we expect there are functors: \begin{equation} \begin{tikzcd}\operatorname{hShv}_\mathcal K X\ar[yshift=0.5ex]{r}{R\alpha_\ast}&\ar[yshift=-0.5ex]{l}{\alpha^\ast}\operatorname{hShv} X\end{tikzcd} \end{equation} where $\alpha^\ast$ is the direct limit \eqref{alphaast} and $R\alpha_\ast$ is the \emph{homotopy} (or \emph{derived}) version $R\varprojlim$ of the inverse limit \eqref{alphaupperast} (the naive inverse limit functor $\alpha_\ast$ is the ``wrong'' functor since inverse limit is not exact). In analogy with Lemma \ref{opencptshvequivalence}, it seems likely\footnote{A similar result appears in Lurie \cite[Corollary 7.3.4.10]{luriehtt}.} that there is an adjunction $\alpha^\ast\dashv R\alpha_\ast$ which is an equivalence (in the sense of model categories or $\infty$-categories), though perhaps only after restricting to the (possibly better-behaved) subcategory of homotopy ($\mathcal K$-)sheaves which are bounded below.
nodes.statement_short: One expects derived functors alpha^*, R alpha_* giving an equivalence of homotopy sheaves and homotopy K-sheaves (bounded below).
nodes.label: homotopyKnotsheavesequivalencermk

nodes.name: Expected functors alpha^* and R alpha_*
nodes.statement: \begin{tikzcd}\operatorname{hShv}_\mathcal K X\ar[yshift=0.5ex]{r}{R\alpha_\ast}&\ar[yshift=-0.5ex]{l}{\alpha^\ast}\operatorname{hShv} X\end{tikzcd}

nodes.name: Focus on homotopy K-sheaves
nodes.statement: Guided by the needs of the rest of the paper, we proceed to focus on homotopy $\mathcal K$-sheaves rather than on homotopy sheaves.

nodes.name: Homotopy K-sheaf properties are quasi-isomorphism invariant
nodes.statement: Properties \eqref{homotopysheafacyclic}--\eqref{homotopysheafcontinuity} are preserved by quasi-isomorphisms.
nodes.statement_short: Axioms (hSh_K1)-(hSh_K3) are invariant under quasi-isomorphism.
nodes.label: qihomotopysheaf

nodes.name: Proof
nodes.statement: For \eqref{homotopysheafacyclic} and \eqref{homotopysheafcontinuity} this is trivial. For \eqref{homotopysheafproperty}, suppose $\mathcal F^\bullet\xrightarrow\sim\mathcal G^\bullet$ is a quasi-isomorphism. Now the sequence \eqref{homotopysheafproperty} applied to the mapping cone $[\mathcal F^\bullet\to\mathcal G^{\bullet-1}]$ is certainly acyclic (since it has a finite filtration whose associated graded is acyclic). Thus \eqref{homotopysheafproperty} holds for $\mathcal F^\bullet$ iff it holds for $\mathcal G^\bullet$.
nodes.statement_short: (hSh_K1),(hSh_K3) trivial; for (hSh_K2) the sequence for the mapping cone is acyclic by a finite filtration argument.

nodes.name: Extensions of homotopy $\mathcal K$-sheaves are homotopy $\mathcal K$-sheaves
nodes.statement: Let $\mathcal F^\bullet$ be a complex of $\mathcal K$-presheaves. If $\mathcal F^\bullet$ has a finite filtration whose associated graded is a homotopy $\mathcal K$-sheaf, then $\mathcal F^\bullet$ is a homotopy $\mathcal K$-sheaf.
assumptions: Let $\mathcal F^\bullet$ be a complex of $\mathcal K$-presheaves.
If $\mathcal F^\bullet$ has a finite filtration whose associated graded is a homotopy $\mathcal K$-sheaf
conclusions: then $\mathcal F^\bullet$ is a homotopy $\mathcal K$-sheaf.
nodes.label: associatedgradedhomotopysheaf

nodes.name: Proof
nodes.statement: This follows from the fact that if a complex $C^\bullet$ has a finite filtration whose associated graded is acyclic then $C^\bullet$ is itself acyclic.
nodes.statement_short: A complex with a finite filtration with acyclic associated graded is acyclic.

nodes.name: Lowest nonzero homology $\mathcal K$-presheaf of a homotopy $\mathcal K$-sheaf is a $\mathcal K$-sheaf
nodes.statement: If $\mathcal F^\bullet$ is a homotopy $\mathcal K$-sheaf and $H^{-1}\mathcal F^\bullet=0$, then $H^0\mathcal F^\bullet$ is a $\mathcal K$-sheaf.
assumptions: If $\mathcal F^\bullet$ is a homotopy $\mathcal K$-sheaf and $H^{-1}\mathcal F^\bullet=0$
conclusions: then $H^0\mathcal F^\bullet$ is a $\mathcal K$-sheaf.
nodes.label: lowervanishingimpliessheaf

nodes.name: Proof
nodes.statement: Properties \eqref{sheafvanishing} and \eqref{sheafcontinuity} follow directly from \eqref{homotopysheafacyclic} and \eqref{homotopysheafcontinuity}. To show \eqref{sheafproperty} for $H^0\mathcal F^\bullet$, use the long exact sequence induced by \eqref{homotopysheafproperty} and the vanishing of $H^{-1}\mathcal F^\bullet(K_1\cap K_2)$.
nodes.statement_short: Axioms follow from the homotopy axioms; the gluing axiom from the Mayer-Vietoris long exact sequence and vanishing H^{-1}.

nodes.name: Filtered intersections for homotopy K-sheaves
nodes.statement: Let $\{K_\alpha\}_{\alpha\in A}$ be a filtered directed system of compact subsets of $X$ (i.e.\ for all $\alpha,\beta\in A$ there exists $\gamma\in A$ with $K_\gamma\subseteq K_\alpha\cap K_\beta$). Then for any $\mathcal F^\bullet$ satisfying \eqref{homotopysheafcontinuity}, the following is a quasi-isomorphism: \begin{equation} \varinjlim_{\alpha\in A}\mathcal F^\bullet(K_\alpha)\to\mathcal F^\bullet\Bigl(\bigcap_{\alpha\in A}K_\alpha\Bigr) \end{equation}
assumptions: Let $\{K_\alpha\}_{\alpha\in A}$ be a filtered directed system of compact subsets of $X$
for any $\mathcal F^\bullet$ satisfying \eqref{homotopysheafcontinuity}
conclusions: the following is a quasi-isomorphism:
nodes.label: anycompactintersectionworks

nodes.name: Filtered intersection quasi-isomorphism
nodes.statement: \varinjlim_{\alpha\in A}\mathcal F^\bullet(K_\alpha)\to\mathcal F^\bullet\Bigl(\bigcap_{\alpha\in A}K_\alpha\Bigr)

nodes.name: Proof
nodes.statement: Same as for Lemma \ref{anycompactintersectionworksSH}.
nodes.statement_short: Same argument as for the sheaf version.

nodes.name: Pushforward of ($\mathcal K$-)presheaves
nodes.statement: Let $f:X\to Y$ be a map of spaces. We define functors: \begin{rlist} \item$f_\ast:\operatorname{Prshv} X\to\operatorname{Prshv} Y$ by $(f_\ast\mathcal F)(U):=\mathcal F(f^{-1}(U))$. \item$f_\ast:\operatorname{Prshv}_\mathcal K X\to\operatorname{Prshv}_\mathcal K Y$ by $(f_\ast\mathcal F)(K):=\mathcal F(f^{-1}(K))$ (if $f$ is proper). \end{rlist} (the action of $f_\ast$ on morphism spaces is obvious).
nodes.section: A.3 Pushforward, exceptional pushforward, and pullback
nodes.label: presheafpushforward

nodes.name: Preimages of neighborhoods are cofinal under proper maps
nodes.statement: Let $f:X\to Y$ be proper. Then $\{f^{-1}(U)\}_{K\subseteq U}$ is a cofinal system of neighborhoods of $f^{-1}(K)$ for any compact $K\subseteq X$.
nodes.section: A.3 Pushforward, exceptional pushforward, and pullback
assumptions: Let $f:X\to Y$ be proper.
conclusions: $\{f^{-1}(U)\}_{K\subseteq U}$ is a cofinal system of neighborhoods of $f^{-1}(K)$ for any compact $K\subseteq X$
nodes.label: properpullbackfinalneighborhood

nodes.name: Proof
nodes.statement: Exercise (use the fact that a compact Hausdorff space is normal).
nodes.section: A.3 Pushforward, exceptional pushforward, and pullback
nodes.statement_short: Exercise using normality of compact Hausdorff spaces.

nodes.name: Pushforward preserves (homotopy) sheaf axioms
nodes.statement: $f_\ast$ preserves \eqref{opensheafproperty}, \eqref{openhomotopysheafproperty}, \eqref{sheafvanishing}--\eqref{sheafcontinuity}, and \eqref{homotopysheafacyclic}--\eqref{homotopysheafcontinuity}.
nodes.section: A.3 Pushforward, exceptional pushforward, and pullback
nodes.label: pushforwardandsheafproperties

nodes.name: Proof
nodes.statement: These are trivial except for \eqref{sheafcontinuity} and \eqref{homotopysheafcontinuity}, which use Lemma \ref{properpullbackfinalneighborhood}.
nodes.section: A.3 Pushforward, exceptional pushforward, and pullback
nodes.statement_short: Trivial except for the continuity axioms, which use cofinality of preimages under proper maps.

nodes.name: Pushforward of ($\mathcal K$-)sheaves and homotopy $\mathcal K$-sheaves
nodes.statement: Let $f:X\to Y$ be a map of spaces. By Lemma \ref{pushforwardandsheafproperties}, Definition \ref{presheafpushforward} gives rise to functors: \begin{rlist} \item$f_\ast:\operatorname{Shv} X\to\operatorname{Shv} Y$. \item$f_\ast:\operatorname{hShv} X\to\operatorname{hShv} Y$. \item$f_\ast:\operatorname{Shv}_\mathcal K X\to\operatorname{Shv}_\mathcal K Y$ (if $f$ is proper). \item$f_\ast:\operatorname{hShv}_\mathcal K X\to\operatorname{hShv}_\mathcal K Y$ (if $f$ is proper). \end{rlist} (the action on morphism spaces is induced from the $f_\ast$ at the level of (complexes of) \mbox{($\mathcal K$-)presheaves}). It is easy to see that $f_\ast$ commutes with the equivalence $\operatorname{Shv} X=\operatorname{Shv}_\mathcal K X$ (if $f$ is proper).
nodes.section: A.3 Pushforward, exceptional pushforward, and pullback
nodes.definiendum: pushforward $f_\ast$ of sheaves and homotopy $\mathcal K$-sheaves
nodes.label: pushforwardofHsheavesworks

nodes.name: Pullback and exceptional pushforward of sheaves
nodes.statement: Let $f:X\to Y$ be a map of spaces. We define: \begin{rlist} \item$f^\ast:\operatorname{Shv} Y\to\operatorname{Shv} X$ the standard sheaf pullback (namely $f^\ast\mathcal F$ is the sheafification of the presheaf $U\mapsto\varinjlim_{f(U)\subseteq V}\mathcal F(V)$). \item$f_!:\operatorname{Shv} X\to\operatorname{Shv} Y$ by $(f_!\mathcal F)(U)\subseteq(f_\ast\mathcal F)(U)$ being the subspace of sections which vanish in a neighborhood of $Y\setminus X$ (if $f$ is the inclusion of an open set). \end{rlist}
nodes.section: A.3 Pushforward, exceptional pushforward, and pullback

nodes.name: Pullback of homotopy $\mathcal K$-sheaves
nodes.statement: Let $f:X\to Y$ be an injective map of spaces. We define: \begin{rlist} \item$f^\ast:\operatorname{hShv}_\mathcal K Y\to\operatorname{hShv}_\mathcal K X$ by $(f^\ast\mathcal F^\bullet)(K):=\mathcal F^\bullet(f(K))$. \end{rlist} We check the properties: \eqref{homotopysheafacyclic} is clear, and \eqref{homotopysheafproperty} follows since $f$ is injective. For \eqref{homotopysheafcontinuity}, use Remark \ref{nbhdintersectiongood}, the injectivity of $f$, and Lemma \ref{anycompactintersectionworks}.
nodes.section: A.3 Pushforward, exceptional pushforward, and pullback
nodes.statement_short: For injective f, (f^*F)(K)=F(f(K)); the homotopy K-sheaf axioms are preserved.

nodes.name: Refinements of covers
nodes.statement: A \emph{refinement} of a cover $\{U_\alpha\}_{\alpha\in A}$ is a cover $\{U_\beta\}_{\beta\in B}$ along with a map $f:B\to A$ such that $U_\beta\subseteq U_{f(\alpha)}$. Refinements are the morphisms used in the directed systems used to define (all flavors of) \v Cech cohomology. Different refinements $\{U_\alpha\}_{\alpha\in A}\to\{U_\beta\}_{\beta\in B}$ induce different maps on \v Cech complexes, but they all agree after passing to cohomology (more precisely, the ``space'' of such refinements is contractible or empty). In particular, it follows that the directed systems used in defining \v Cech cohomology are \emph{filtered}.
nodes.statement_short: Refinements are the morphisms of the directed systems defining Čech cohomology; induced maps agree on cohomology so the systems are filtered.
nodes.label: coveringscategoryrmk

nodes.name: Čech cohomology of the empty set vanishes
nodes.statement: The empty covering is a final object in the category of coverings of $\varnothing$, so we always have $\check H^\bullet(\varnothing;-)=0$.

nodes.name: $\check H^\bullet$ and $\check H^\bullet_c$ of sheaves
nodes.statement: Let $\mathcal F$ be a sheaf on a space $X$. We define the \v Cech cohomology: \begin{equation} \check H^\bullet(X;\mathcal F):=\varinjlim_{\begin{smallmatrix}X=\bigcup_{\alpha\in A}U_\alpha\cr\text{open cover}\end{smallmatrix}}H^\bullet\biggl[\bigoplus_{p\geq 0}\prod_{\begin{smallmatrix}S\subseteq A\cr\left|S\right|=p+1\end{smallmatrix}}\mathcal F\Bigl(\bigcap_{\alpha\in S}U_\alpha\Bigr)[-p]\biggr] \end{equation} with the standard \v Cech differential.\footnote{Technically speaking, so that the signs in the differential can be defined canonically, we should really tensor each term of the direct product with $(\mathbb Zo_1\oplus\mathbb Zo_2)/(o_1+o_2)\cong\mathbb Z$ where $o_1,o_2$ denote the two orientations of the $p$-simplex on vertex set $S$.} For any compact $K\subseteq X$, define $\check H^\bullet_K(X;\mathcal F)$ (\v Cech cohomology with supports in $K$) via \eqref{cechcomplexI} except replacing every instance of $\mathcal F(U)$ with $\ker[\mathcal F(U)\to\mathcal F(U\setminus K)]$. We let $\check H^\bullet_c(X;\mathcal F):=\varinjlim_{K\subseteq X}\check H^\bullet_K(X;\mathcal F)$ (\v Cech cohomology with compact supports).
nodes.statement_short: Čech cohomology of a sheaf as a direct limit over open covers, with supports in K, and with compact supports.
nodes.label: cechdefnI

nodes.name: Čech cohomology of a sheaf
nodes.statement: \check H^\bullet(X;\mathcal F):=\varinjlim_{\begin{smallmatrix}X=\bigcup_{\alpha\in A}U_\alpha\cr\text{open cover}\end{smallmatrix}}H^\bullet\biggl[\bigoplus_{p\geq 0}\prod_{\begin{smallmatrix}S\subseteq A\cr\left|S\right|=p+1\end{smallmatrix}}\mathcal F\Bigl(\bigcap_{\alpha\in S}U_\alpha\Bigr)[-p]\biggr]
nodes.label: cechcomplexI

nodes.name: Finite covers suffice on compact spaces
nodes.statement: If $X$ is compact, then the natural map $\check H^\bullet_\mathrm{fin}(X;\mathcal F)\to\check H^\bullet(X;\mathcal F)$ is an isomorphism, where the left hand side is defined as in \eqref{cechcomplexI} except using only finite open covers.
assumptions: If $X$ is compact
conclusions: then the natural map $\check H^\bullet_\mathrm{fin}(X;\mathcal F)\to\check H^\bullet(X;\mathcal F)$ is an isomorphism

nodes.name: Proof
nodes.statement: Since $X$ is compact, it follows that finite open covers are cofinal (every open cover has a finite refinement).
nodes.statement_short: Finite open covers are cofinal on a compact space.

nodes.name: Compactly supported Čech cohomology on compact spaces
nodes.statement: If $X$ is compact, then the natural map $\check H_c^\bullet(X;\mathcal F)\to\check H^\bullet(X;\mathcal F)$ is an isomorphism.
assumptions: If $X$ is compact
conclusions: then the natural map $\check H_c^\bullet(X;\mathcal F)\to\check H^\bullet(X;\mathcal F)$ is an isomorphism.

nodes.name: Proof
nodes.statement: Trivial.
nodes.statement_short: Trivial.

nodes.name: Pullback on $\check H^\bullet$ and $\check H^\bullet_c$
nodes.statement: Let $f:X\to Y$ be a map of spaces. An open cover of $Y$ pulls back to give an open cover of $X$, and this gives an identification of the \v Cech complex for the cover of $Y$ with coefficients in $f_\ast\mathcal F$ with the \v Cech complex for the cover of $X$ with coefficients in $\mathcal F$. Hence we get natural maps: \begin{rlist} \item$f^\ast:\check H^\bullet(Y;f_\ast\mathcal F)\to\check H^\bullet(X;\mathcal F)$ for $\mathcal F\in\operatorname{Shv} X$. \item$f^\ast:\check H^\bullet_c(Y;f_\ast\mathcal F)\to\check H^\bullet_c(X;\mathcal F)$ for $\mathcal F\in\operatorname{Shv} X$ (if $f$ is proper). \end{rlist}
nodes.label: pullbackdefn

nodes.name: $\check H_c^\bullet$ commutes with $f_!$
nodes.statement: Let $f:X\hookrightarrow Y$ be the inclusion of an open subset. Then there is a natural isomorphism $f_!:\check H^\bullet_c(X;\mathcal F)\to\check H^\bullet_c(Y;f_!\mathcal F)$.
assumptions: Let $f:X\hookrightarrow Y$ be the inclusion of an open subset.
conclusions: there is a natural isomorphism $f_!:\check H^\bullet_c(X;\mathcal F)\to\check H^\bullet_c(Y;f_!\mathcal F)$
nodes.label: cptcechembeddingproperty

nodes.name: Proof
nodes.statement: For $K\subseteq X$, there are natural maps: \begin{equation} \begin{tikzcd} \check H^\bullet_K(Y;f_!\mathcal F)\ar[yshift=0.5ex]{r}{f^\ast}&\ar[yshift=-0.5ex]{l}{f_!}\check H^\bullet_K(X;\mathcal F) \end{tikzcd} \end{equation} (for $f^\ast$: pull back the open cover) (for $f_!$: add $Y\setminus K$ to the open cover and extend by zero). It is easy to see that $f_!$ and $f^\ast$ are inverses. The desired map $f_!:\check H^\bullet_c(X;\mathcal F)\to\check H^\bullet_c(Y;f_!\mathcal F)$ is defined as the composition: \begin{equation} \varinjlim_{K\subseteq X}\check H^\bullet_K(X;\mathcal F)\overset{\eqref{trivialKequivalence}}=\varinjlim_{K\subseteq X}\check H^\bullet_K(Y;f_!\mathcal F)\to\varinjlim_{K\subseteq Y}\check H^\bullet_K(Y;f_!\mathcal F) \end{equation} We must show that the second map is an isomorphism; to see this, it suffices to show that the following is an isomorphism for all $K\subseteq Y$: \begin{equation} \varinjlim_{K'\subseteq X\cap K}\check H^\bullet_{K'}(Y;f_!\mathcal F)\to\check H^\bullet_K(Y;f_!\mathcal F) \end{equation} We claim that for any \v Cech cochain $\beta$ for $f_!\mathcal F$ with supports in $K$ subordinate to an open cover of $Y$, there is a refinement on which the restriction of $\beta$ has supports in some $K'\subseteq X\cap K$. It follows from the claim (using a cofinality argument) that \eqref{supportcompactinXorY} is an isomorphism. To prove the claim, argue as follows. First, choose a refinement for which only finitely many open sets $U_1,\ldots,U_n$ intersect $K$ and for which the remaining open sets cover $Y\setminus K$. Pick open sets $V_i\subseteq U_i$ which cover $K$ and for which $\overline{V_i}$ is compact and $\overline{V_i}\subseteq U_i$ (this is always possible). Now $\beta$ is a finite collection $\{\beta_I\in(f_!\mathcal F)(\bigcap_{i\in I}U_i)\}_{\varnothing\ne I\subseteq\{1,\ldots,n\}}$. We have: \begin{equation} \operatorname{supp}\Bigl(\beta_I|\bigcap_{i\in I}V_i\Bigr)\subseteq\operatorname{supp}\beta_I\cap\bigcap_{i\in I}\overline{V_i} \end{equation} Since $\operatorname{supp}\beta_I\subseteq\bigcap_{i\in I}U_i$ is (relatively) closed and $\bigcap_{i\in I}\overline{V_i}\subseteq\bigcap_{i\in I}U_i$ is compact, it follows that the right hand side is compact. Also, we have $\operatorname{supp}\beta_I\subseteq X$ (by definition of $f_!\mathcal F$). Hence the right hand side of \eqref{restrictionsupport} is a compact subset of $X$. It follows that the restriction of $\beta$ to the refinement obtained by replacing $U_i$ with $V_i$ for $i=1,\ldots,n$ has support in a compact subset of $X$.
nodes.statement_short: Compare supports-in-K cohomology on X and Y, then show by refining covers that every cochain supported in K becomes supported in a compact subset of X.

nodes.name: Supports-in-K maps f^* and f_!
nodes.statement: \begin{tikzcd} \check H^\bullet_K(Y;f_!\mathcal F)\ar[yshift=0.5ex]{r}{f^\ast}&\ar[yshift=-0.5ex]{l}{f_!}\check H^\bullet_K(X;\mathcal F) \end{tikzcd}
nodes.label: trivialKequivalence

nodes.name: Definition of f_! on compactly supported Čech cohomology
nodes.statement: \varinjlim_{K\subseteq X}\check H^\bullet_K(X;\mathcal F)\overset{\eqref{trivialKequivalence}}=\varinjlim_{K\subseteq X}\check H^\bullet_K(Y;f_!\mathcal F)\to\varinjlim_{K\subseteq Y}\check H^\bullet_K(Y;f_!\mathcal F)

nodes.name: Support comparison map
nodes.statement: \varinjlim_{K'\subseteq X\cap K}\check H^\bullet_{K'}(Y;f_!\mathcal F)\to\check H^\bullet_K(Y;f_!\mathcal F)
nodes.label: supportcompactinXorY

nodes.name: Support of restricted cochain
nodes.statement: \operatorname{supp}\Bigl(\beta_I|\bigcap_{i\in I}V_i\Bigr)\subseteq\operatorname{supp}\beta_I\cap\bigcap_{i\in I}\overline{V_i}
nodes.label: restrictionsupport

nodes.name: Pullback is an isomorphism for finite-fiber proper maps
nodes.statement: Let $f:X\to Y$ be proper with finite fibers. Then $f^\ast:\check H^\bullet(Y;f_\ast\mathcal F)\to\check H^\bullet(X;\mathcal F)$ is an isomorphism, as is $f^\ast:\check H^\bullet_c(Y;f_\ast\mathcal F)\to\check H^\bullet_c(X;\mathcal F)$.
assumptions: Let $f:X\to Y$ be proper with finite fibers.
conclusions: $f^\ast:\check H^\bullet(Y;f_\ast\mathcal F)\to\check H^\bullet(X;\mathcal F)$ is an isomorphism, as is $f^\ast:\check H^\bullet_c(Y;f_\ast\mathcal F)\to\check H^\bullet_c(X;\mathcal F)$
nodes.label: finitemap

nodes.name: Proof
nodes.statement: Given an open cover containing $U=U_1\sqcup\cdots\sqcup U_n$ (finite disjoint union), we get a refinement by replacing $U$ with $\{U_1,\ldots,U_n\}$. A \emph{partition} of an open cover is a refinement obtained by doing such a replacement on some (possibly infinitely many) open sets of the cover. Note that a partition induces an isomorphism on \v Cech cochains since $\mathcal F$ is a sheaf. We claim that partitions of pullbacks of open covers of $Y$ form a cofinal system of open covers of $X$. This is clear using Lemma \ref{properpullbackfinalneighborhood} and the fact that $f$ has finite fibers. It follows from this cofinality that $f^\ast$ is an isomorphism.
nodes.statement_short: Partitions of pulled-back covers are cofinal among covers of X and induce isomorphisms on Čech cochains.

nodes.name: Čech cohomology commutes with finite quotients
nodes.statement: Let $X$ be a space and let $\pi:X\to X/\Gamma$ be the quotient map under a finite group action. Let $\mathcal F$ be any sheaf of $\mathbb Z[\frac 1{\#\Gamma}]$-modules on $X/\Gamma$. Then the following maps are all isomorphisms: \begin{align*} \check H^\bullet(X/\Gamma;\mathcal F)\to\check H^\bullet(X/\Gamma;(\pi_\ast\pi^\ast\mathcal F)^\Gamma)\to\check H^\bullet(X/\Gamma;\pi_\ast\pi^\ast\mathcal F)^\Gamma\to\check H^\bullet(X;\pi^\ast\mathcal F)^\Gamma\\ \check H^\bullet_c(X/\Gamma;\mathcal F)\to\check H^\bullet_c(X/\Gamma;(\pi_\ast\pi^\ast\mathcal F)^\Gamma)\to\check H^\bullet_c(X/\Gamma;\pi_\ast\pi^\ast\mathcal F)^\Gamma\to\check H^\bullet_c(X;\pi^\ast\mathcal F)^\Gamma \end{align*} (here we note that by functoriality, $\pi^\ast\mathcal F$ is $\Gamma$-equivariant, and thus $\Gamma$ acts on $\pi_\ast\pi^\ast\mathcal F$).
assumptions: Let $X$ be a space and let $\pi:X\to X/\Gamma$ be the quotient map under a finite group action.
Let $\mathcal F$ be any sheaf of $\mathbb Z[\frac 1{\#\Gamma}]$-modules on $X/\Gamma$.
conclusions: Then the following maps are all isomorphisms:
nodes.label: cechcohomologyfinitequotient

nodes.name: Proof
nodes.statement: Isomorphism one: the natural map $\mathcal F\to(\pi_\ast\pi^\ast)^\Gamma$ is in fact an isomorphism of sheaves (check on stalks). Isomorphism two: obvious since taking $\Gamma$-invariants is exact on $\mathbb Z[\frac 1{\#\Gamma}]$-modules. Isomorphism three: use Lemma \ref{finitemap}, which applies since $\pi$ is automatically proper.
nodes.statement_short: Check the three isomorphisms in turn: on stalks, by exactness of invariants with #Gamma inverted, and by the finite-fiber pullback lemma.

nodes.name: $\check H^\bullet$ of complexes of $\mathcal K$-presheaves
nodes.statement: Let $\mathcal F^\bullet$ be a complex of $\mathcal K$-presheaves on a compact space $X$. We define: \begin{equation} \check H^\bullet(X;\mathcal F^\bullet):=\varinjlim_{\begin{smallmatrix}X=\bigcup_{i=1}^nK_i\cr\text{finite compact cover}\end{smallmatrix}}H^\bullet\biggl[\bigoplus_{p\geq 0}\bigoplus_{1\leq i_0<\cdots<i_p\leq n}\mathcal F^{\bullet-p}\Bigl(\bigcap_{j=0}^pK_{i_j}\Bigr)\biggr] \end{equation} with the standard \v Cech differential (plus the internal differential of $\mathcal F^\bullet$). We also define $\check H^\bullet(X;\mathcal F)$ for any $\mathcal K$-presheaf $\mathcal F$ by viewing it as a complex concentrated in degree zero.
nodes.statement_short: Čech hypercohomology of a complex of K-presheaves on a compact space, as a direct limit over finite compact covers.
nodes.label: cechdefnII

nodes.name: Čech hypercohomology over finite compact covers
nodes.statement: \check H^\bullet(X;\mathcal F^\bullet):=\varinjlim_{\begin{smallmatrix}X=\bigcup_{i=1}^nK_i\cr\text{finite compact cover}\end{smallmatrix}}H^\bullet\biggl[\bigoplus_{p\geq 0}\bigoplus_{1\leq i_0<\cdots<i_p\leq n}\mathcal F^{\bullet-p}\Bigl(\bigcap_{j=0}^pK_{i_j}\Bigr)\biggr]
nodes.label: cechcomplexII

nodes.name: Two definitions of $\check H^\bullet$ on $\operatorname{Shv} X=\operatorname{Shv}_\mathcal K X$ agree
nodes.statement: Let $\mathcal F$ be a sheaf on a compact space $X$. Then there is a natural isomorphism $\check H^\bullet(X;\mathcal F)\to\check H^\bullet(X;\alpha^\ast\mathcal F)$ ($\alpha^\ast\mathcal F$ is a $\mathcal K$-sheaf; c.f.\ Definition \ref{opencptrelationfunctors}).
assumptions: Let $\mathcal F$ be a sheaf on a compact space $X$.
conclusions: there is a natural isomorphism $\check H^\bullet(X;\mathcal F)\to\check H^\bullet(X;\alpha^\ast\mathcal F)$
nodes.label: cHsameforopencompactcovers

nodes.name: Proof
nodes.statement: Let us denote by $\check H^\bullet(X;\mathcal F;\{U_\alpha\}_{\alpha\in A})$ (resp.\ $\check H^\bullet(X;\alpha^\ast\mathcal F;\{K_i\}_{i=1}^n)$) the argument of the direct limit \eqref{cechcomplexI} (resp.\ \eqref{cechcomplexII}). Since $X$ is compact, every open cover has a finite compact refinement. This gives a map $\check H^\bullet(X;\mathcal F)\to\check H^\bullet(X;\alpha^\ast\mathcal F)$. To show that this map is an isomorphism, it suffices to show that for any fixed finite compact cover $\{K_i\}_{i=1}^n$, the following is an isomorphism: \begin{equation} \varinjlim_{\begin{smallmatrix}X=\bigcup_{\alpha\in A}U_\alpha\cr\text{open cover refined by }\{K_i\}_{i=1}^n\end{smallmatrix}}\check H^\bullet(X;\mathcal F;\{U_\alpha\}_{\alpha\in A})\to\check H^\bullet(X;\alpha^\ast\mathcal F;\{K_i\}_{i=1}^n) \end{equation} By a cofinality argument, we can change the directed system on the left side to be open covers $\{U_i\}_{i=1}^n$ with $U_i\supseteq K_i$. Hence it suffices to show that the following is an isomorphism: \begin{equation} \varinjlim_{\{U_i\supseteq K_i\}_{i=1}^n}\check H^\bullet(X;\mathcal F;\{U_i\}_{i=1}^n)\to\check H^\bullet(X;\alpha^\ast\mathcal F;\{K_i\}_{i=1}^n) \end{equation} This is clear from the definition of $\alpha^\ast$ and from Lemma \ref{intersectioncofinal}.
nodes.statement_short: Compact refinements give the map; by cofinality reduce to open covers U_i containing K_i, then use the definition of alpha^* and cofinal intersections.

nodes.name: Reduction to a fixed compact cover
nodes.statement: \varinjlim_{\begin{smallmatrix}X=\bigcup_{\alpha\in A}U_\alpha\cr\text{open cover refined by }\{K_i\}_{i=1}^n\end{smallmatrix}}\check H^\bullet(X;\mathcal F;\{U_\alpha\}_{\alpha\in A})\to\check H^\bullet(X;\alpha^\ast\mathcal F;\{K_i\}_{i=1}^n)

nodes.name: Reduction to open thickenings of a compact cover
nodes.statement: \varinjlim_{\{U_i\supseteq K_i\}_{i=1}^n}\check H^\bullet(X;\mathcal F;\{U_i\}_{i=1}^n)\to\check H^\bullet(X;\alpha^\ast\mathcal F;\{K_i\}_{i=1}^n)

nodes.name: Čech cohomology preserves quasi-isomorphisms
nodes.statement: If $\mathcal F^\bullet\to\mathcal G^\bullet$ is a quasi-isomorphism of complexes of $\mathcal K$-presheaves, then the induced map $\check H^\bullet(X;\mathcal F^\bullet)\to\check H^\bullet(X,\mathcal G^\bullet)$ is an isomorphism.
assumptions: If $\mathcal F^\bullet\to\mathcal G^\bullet$ is a quasi-isomorphism of complexes of $\mathcal K$-presheaves
conclusions: then the induced map $\check H^\bullet(X;\mathcal F^\bullet)\to\check H^\bullet(X,\mathcal G^\bullet)$ is an isomorphism.
nodes.label: qicech

nodes.name: Proof
nodes.statement: There is clearly a long exact sequence: \begin{equation} \cdots\to\check H^{\bullet-1}(X;\mathcal G^\bullet)\to\check H^\bullet(X;[\mathcal F^\bullet\to\mathcal G^{\bullet-1}])\to\check H^\bullet(X;\mathcal F^\bullet)\to\check H^\bullet(X;\mathcal G^\bullet)\to\cdots \end{equation} Hence it suffices to show that if $\mathcal F^\bullet$ is acyclic then $\check H^\bullet(X;\mathcal F^\bullet)=0$. This is true because then each \v Cech complex has a finite filtration whose associated graded is acyclic.
nodes.statement_short: Mapping cone long exact sequence reduces to acyclic complexes, whose Čech complexes have finite filtrations with acyclic graded pieces.

nodes.name: Mapping cone long exact sequence for Čech cohomology
nodes.statement: \cdots\to\check H^{\bullet-1}(X;\mathcal G^\bullet)\to\check H^\bullet(X;[\mathcal F^\bullet\to\mathcal G^{\bullet-1}])\to\check H^\bullet(X;\mathcal F^\bullet)\to\check H^\bullet(X;\mathcal G^\bullet)\to\cdots
nodes.label: cechmappingconeles

nodes.name: Hypercohomology spectral sequence
nodes.statement: Let $\mathcal F^\bullet$ be a bounded below complex of $\mathcal K$-presheaves. Then there is a convergent spectral sequence $E_1^{p,q}=\check H^q(X;\mathcal F^p)\Rightarrow\check H^{p+q}(X;\mathcal F^\bullet)$.
assumptions: Let $\mathcal F^\bullet$ be a bounded below complex of $\mathcal K$-presheaves.
conclusions: there is a convergent spectral sequence $E_1^{p,q}=\check H^q(X;\mathcal F^p)\Rightarrow\check H^{p+q}(X;\mathcal F^\bullet)$
nodes.label: hypercohomologyss

nodes.name: Proof
nodes.statement: This is just the spectral sequence of the \v Cech double complex.
nodes.statement_short: The spectral sequence of the Čech double complex.

nodes.name: A homotopy K-sheaf calculates its own Čech cohomology
nodes.statement: If $\mathcal F^\bullet$ satisfies \eqref{homotopysheafacyclic} and \eqref{homotopysheafproperty}, then the canonical map $H^\bullet\mathcal F^\bullet(X)\to\check H^\bullet(X;\mathcal F^\bullet)$ is an isomorphism.
assumptions: If $\mathcal F^\bullet$ satisfies \eqref{homotopysheafacyclic} and \eqref{homotopysheafproperty}
conclusions: then the canonical map $H^\bullet\mathcal F^\bullet(X)\to\check H^\bullet(X;\mathcal F^\bullet)$ is an isomorphism.
nodes.label: homotopysheafcechquasiisomorphism

nodes.name: Proof
nodes.statement: We prove that $\mathcal F^\bullet(X)\to\check C^\bullet(X;\mathcal F^\bullet;K_1,\ldots,K_n)$ (the right hand side denotes \v Cech complex for the finite compact cover $X=K_1\cup\cdots\cup K_n$) is a quasi-isomorphism by induction on $n$. The base case $n=1$ is obvious since $\check C^\bullet(X;\mathcal F^\bullet;X)=\mathcal F^\bullet(X)$ by definition. For the inductive step, it suffices to show that the natural map $\check C^\bullet(X;\mathcal F^\bullet;K_1\cup K_2,K_3,\ldots,K_n)\to\check C^\bullet(X;\mathcal F^\bullet;K_1,K_2,K_3,\ldots,K_n)$ is a quasi-isomorphism. We will show that the mapping cone is acyclic; to see this, let us filter it according to how many of the $K_3,\ldots,K_n$ are chosen among $i_0,\ldots,i_p$. This is a finite filtration, so it suffices to show that the associated graded is acyclic. The associated graded is a direct sum of complexes of the form $[\mathcal F^\bullet(K)\to\mathcal F^{\bullet-1}(K)]$ (which is obviously acyclic) and $[\mathcal F^\bullet(K\cap(K_1\cup K_2))\to\mathcal F^{\bullet-1}(K\cap K_1)\oplus\mathcal F^{\bullet-1}(K\cap K_2)\to\mathcal F^{\bullet-2}(K\cap K_1\cap K_2)]$ (which is acyclic by \eqref{homotopysheafproperty}). The above argument works when $X\ne\varnothing$; if $X=\varnothing$, use \eqref{homotopysheafacyclic}.
nodes.statement_short: Induction on the number of sets in a finite compact cover; merging two sets is a quasi-isomorphism since the cone has a finite filtration with acyclic graded pieces by (hSh_K2).

nodes.name: A $\mathcal K$-sheaf calculates its own $\check H^0$
nodes.statement: If $\mathcal F$ satisfies \eqref{sheafvanishing} and \eqref{sheafproperty}, then the canonical map $\mathcal F(X)\to\check H^0(X;\mathcal F)$ is an isomorphism.
assumptions: If $\mathcal F$ satisfies \eqref{sheafvanishing} and \eqref{sheafproperty}
conclusions: then the canonical map $\mathcal F(X)\to\check H^0(X;\mathcal F)$ is an isomorphism.
nodes.label: sheafcechHzero

nodes.name: Proof
nodes.statement: Use induction as in the proof of Proposition \ref{homotopysheafcechquasiisomorphism}.
nodes.statement_short: Induction on the cover size, as for the homotopy K-sheaf case.

nodes.name: $\check H^\bullet$ is determined by stalks I
nodes.statement: Let $\mathcal F$ satisfy \eqref{sheafcontinuity}. If the stalks of $\mathcal F$ vanish, then $\check H^\bullet(X;\mathcal F)=0$.
assumptions: Let $\mathcal F$ satisfy \eqref{sheafcontinuity}.
If the stalks of $\mathcal F$ vanish
conclusions: then $\check H^\bullet(X;\mathcal F)=0$.
nodes.label: localvanishingcechzero

nodes.name: Proof
nodes.statement: It suffices to show that for all $\alpha\in\mathcal F(K)$, there exists a finite compact cover $X=\bigcup_{i=1}^nK_i$ such that $\mathcal F(K)\to\bigoplus_{i=1}^n\mathcal F(K\cap K_i)$ annihilates $\alpha$. We consider the commutative diagram: \begin{equation} \begin{CD} \varinjlim_{K\subseteq U}\mathcal F(\overline U)@>>>\prod_{p\in K}\varinjlim_{p\in U}\mathcal F(\overline U)\cr @VVV@VVV\cr \mathcal F(K)@>>>\prod_{p\in K}\mathcal F_p \end{CD} \end{equation} where the vertical maps are both isomorphisms. Now the vanishing of $\mathcal F_p$ and a compactness argument shows that there are finitely many open sets $U_i\subseteq X$ covering $K$ such that $\alpha$ vanishes in $\mathcal F(K\cap\overline{U_i})$ for all $i$. Thus the compact cover $X=(X\setminus\bigcup_{i=1}^nU_i)\cup\overline{U_1}\cup\cdots\cup\overline{U_n}$ has the desired properties.
nodes.statement_short: Use (Sh_K3) to identify sections with neighborhood germs, then a compactness argument finds a finite compact cover killing any section.

nodes.name: Sections versus stalks diagram
nodes.statement: \begin{CD} \varinjlim_{K\subseteq U}\mathcal F(\overline U)@>>>\prod_{p\in K}\varinjlim_{p\in U}\mathcal F(\overline U)\cr @VVV@VVV\cr \mathcal F(K)@>>>\prod_{p\in K}\mathcal F_p \end{CD}

nodes.name: $\check H^\bullet$ is determined by stalks II
nodes.statement: Let $\mathcal F^\bullet$ satisfy \eqref{homotopysheafcontinuity} and $H^i\mathcal F^\bullet=0$ for $i<<0$. If $\mathcal F^\bullet$ has acyclic stalks, then $\check H^\bullet(X;\mathcal F^\bullet)=0$.
assumptions: Let $\mathcal F^\bullet$ satisfy \eqref{homotopysheafcontinuity} and $H^i\mathcal F^\bullet=0$ for $i<<0$.
If $\mathcal F^\bullet$ has acyclic stalks
conclusions: then $\check H^\bullet(X;\mathcal F^\bullet)=0$.
nodes.label: cechlocalglobalvanishingcomplex

nodes.name: Proof
nodes.statement: We show that for all $i$, the map $\check H^\bullet(X;\mathcal F^\bullet)\to\check H^\bullet(X;\tau_{\geq i}\mathcal F^\bullet)$ is an isomorphism (this is sufficient since $\check H^j(X;\tau_{\geq i}\mathcal F^\bullet)=0$ for $j<i$). We proceed by induction on $i$. Since $H^i\mathcal F^\bullet=0$ for $i<<0$, we have that $\mathcal F^\bullet\to\tau_{\geq i}\mathcal F^\bullet$ is a quasi-isomorphism, so $\check H^\bullet(X;\mathcal F^\bullet)\to\check H^\bullet(X;\tau_{\geq i}\mathcal F^\bullet)$ is an isomorphism for $i<<0$ (Lemma \ref{qicech}). Thus we have the base case of the induction. For the inductive step, it suffices to show that $\check H^\bullet(X;H^{i-1}\mathcal F^\bullet)=0$. This follows from Lemma \ref{localvanishingcechzero}.
nodes.statement_short: Induction on truncation degree i, using quasi-isomorphism invariance for the base and the sheaf-level vanishing lemma for the inductive step.

nodes.name: $\check H^\bullet$ is determined by stalks III
nodes.statement: Let $\mathcal F^\bullet,\mathcal G^\bullet$ satisfy \eqref{homotopysheafcontinuity} and $H^i\mathcal F^\bullet=H^i\mathcal G^\bullet=0$ for $i<<0$. If $\mathcal F^\bullet\to\mathcal G^\bullet$ induces a quasi-isomorphism on stalks, then it induces an isomorphism $\check H^\bullet(X;\mathcal F^\bullet)\to\check H^\bullet(X;\mathcal G^\bullet)$.
assumptions: Let $\mathcal F^\bullet,\mathcal G^\bullet$ satisfy \eqref{homotopysheafcontinuity} and $H^i\mathcal F^\bullet=H^i\mathcal G^\bullet=0$ for $i<<0$.
If $\mathcal F^\bullet\to\mathcal G^\bullet$ induces a quasi-isomorphism on stalks
conclusions: then it induces an isomorphism $\check H^\bullet(X;\mathcal F^\bullet)\to\check H^\bullet(X;\mathcal G^\bullet)$.
nodes.label: cechdeterminedbystalks

nodes.name: Proof
nodes.statement: Recall the long exact sequence \eqref{cechmappingconeles} and apply Lemma \ref{cechlocalglobalvanishingcomplex} to the mapping cone $[\mathcal F^\bullet\to\mathcal G^{\bullet-1}]$.
nodes.statement_short: Apply stalk-vanishing to the mapping cone and use the mapping cone long exact sequence.

nodes.name: A map of homotopy $\mathcal K$-sheaves being a quasi-isomorphism can be checked on stalks
nodes.statement: Let $\mathcal F^\bullet\to\mathcal G^\bullet$ be a map of homotopy $\mathcal K$-sheaves which satisfy $H^i\mathcal F^\bullet=H^i\mathcal G^\bullet=0$ for $i<<0$. Then $\mathcal F^\bullet\to\mathcal G^\bullet$ is a quasi-isomorphism iff $\mathcal F^\bullet_p\to\mathcal G^\bullet_p$ is a quasi-isomorphism for all $p\in X$.
assumptions: Let $\mathcal F^\bullet\to\mathcal G^\bullet$ be a map of homotopy $\mathcal K$-sheaves which satisfy $H^i\mathcal F^\bullet=H^i\mathcal G^\bullet=0$ for $i<<0$.
conclusions: Then $\mathcal F^\bullet\to\mathcal G^\bullet$ is a quasi-isomorphism iff $\mathcal F^\bullet_p\to\mathcal G^\bullet_p$ is a quasi-isomorphism for all $p\in X$.
nodes.label: homotopysheafcheckqionstalks

nodes.name: Proof
nodes.statement: For any $K\subseteq X$, we have a commutative diagram: \begin{equation} \begin{CD} H^\bullet\mathcal F^\bullet(K)@>\sim>>\check H^\bullet(K;\mathcal F^\bullet)\cr @VVV@VVV\cr H^\bullet\mathcal G^\bullet(K)@>\sim>>\check H^\bullet(K;\mathcal G^\bullet) \end{CD} \end{equation} The rows are isomorphisms by Proposition \ref{homotopysheafcechquasiisomorphism}. If $\mathcal F^\bullet_p\to\mathcal G^\bullet_p$ is a quasi-isomorphism, then the right vertical map is a quasi-isomorphism by Proposition \ref{cechdeterminedbystalks}.
nodes.statement_short: Homotopy K-sheaves compute their own Čech cohomology, which is determined by stalks.

nodes.name: Comparison square of sections and Čech cohomology
nodes.statement: \begin{CD} H^\bullet\mathcal F^\bullet(K)@>\sim>>\check H^\bullet(K;\mathcal F^\bullet)\cr @VVV@VVV\cr H^\bullet\mathcal G^\bullet(K)@>\sim>>\check H^\bullet(K;\mathcal G^\bullet) \end{CD}

nodes.name: Long exact sequence for Čech cohomology
nodes.statement: Let $\mathcal F,\mathcal G,\mathcal H$ satisfy \eqref{sheafcontinuity}. If $0\to\mathcal F\to\mathcal G\to\mathcal H\to 0$ is exact on stalks, then it induces a long exact sequence on $\check H^\bullet$.
assumptions: Let $\mathcal F,\mathcal G,\mathcal H$ satisfy \eqref{sheafcontinuity}.
If $0\to\mathcal F\to\mathcal G\to\mathcal H\to 0$ is exact on stalks
conclusions: then it induces a long exact sequence on $\check H^\bullet$.
nodes.label: cechles

nodes.name: Proof
nodes.statement: By Lemma \ref{cechlocalglobalvanishingcomplex}, we have $\check H^\bullet(X;[\mathcal F\to\mathcal G[-1]\to\mathcal H[-2]])=0$. Now inspection of the hypercohomology spectral sequence (Lemma \ref{hypercohomologyss}) gives the desired long exact sequence.
nodes.statement_short: The three-term complex has vanishing Čech cohomology by stalk vanishing; the hypercohomology spectral sequence gives the long exact sequence.

nodes.name: Pullback on $\check H^\bullet$
nodes.statement: Let $f:X\to Y$ be a map of compact spaces. A finite compact cover of $Y$ pulls back to give a finite compact cover of $X$, and this gives an identification of the \v Cech complex for the cover of $Y$ with coefficients in $f_\ast\mathcal F^\bullet$ with the \v Cech complex for the cover of $X$ with coefficients in $\mathcal F^\bullet$. Hence we get a natural map: \begin{rlist} \item$f^\ast:\check H^\bullet(Y;f_\ast\mathcal F^\bullet)\to\check H^\bullet(X;\mathcal F^\bullet)$ for $\mathcal F^i\in\operatorname{Prshv}_\mathcal K X$. \end{rlist}
nodes.definiendum: pullback $f^\ast$ on $\check H^\bullet$ of complexes of $\mathcal K$-presheaves
nodes.label: pullbackcHKprshv

nodes.name: Pure homotopy K-sheaf
nodes.statement: We say that a homotopy $\mathcal K$-sheaf $\mathcal F^\bullet$ on $X$ is \emph{pure} iff: \begin{rlist} \item(Stalk cohomology) $H^i\mathcal F^\bullet_p=0$ for $i\ne 0$ and all $p\in X$. \item(Weak vanishing) $H^i\mathcal F^\bullet=0$ for $i<<0$ locally on $X$ (meaning that for all $p\in X$, there exists an open set $U\subseteq X$ containing $p$ and an integer $N>-\infty$ such that $H^i\mathcal F^\bullet(K)=0$ for all $K\subseteq U$ and $i\leq N$). \end{rlist}
nodes.statement_short: A homotopy K-sheaf whose stalk cohomology is concentrated in degree 0 and whose cohomology vanishes locally in very negative degrees.
differentia: (Stalk cohomology) $H^i\mathcal F^\bullet_p=0$ for $i\ne 0$ and all $p\in X$.
(Weak vanishing) $H^i\mathcal F^\bullet=0$ for $i<<0$ locally on $X$
nodes.label: purehomotopyKsheaf

nodes.name: Does stalk cohomology imply weak vanishing?
nodes.statement: It would be nice to know whether the stalk cohomology condition implies the weak vanishing condition in general (it would be much easier to check purity).

nodes.name: Basic properties of pure homotopy K-sheaves
nodes.statement: Let $\mathcal F^\bullet$ be a pure homotopy $\mathcal K$-sheaf. Then: \begin{rlist} \item(Strong vanishing) $H^i\mathcal F^\bullet=0$ for $i<0$. \item$H^0\mathcal F^\bullet$ is a $\mathcal K$-sheaf. \end{rlist}
assumptions: Let $\mathcal F^\bullet$ be a pure homotopy $\mathcal K$-sheaf.
conclusions: (Strong vanishing) $H^i\mathcal F^\bullet=0$ for $i<0$.
$H^0\mathcal F^\bullet$ is a $\mathcal K$-sheaf.
nodes.label: cechsimplebasic

nodes.name: Proof
nodes.statement: By Lemma \ref{lowervanishingimpliessheaf}, strong vanishing implies that $H^0\mathcal F^\bullet$ is a $\mathcal K$-sheaf. Now let us prove strong vanishing. By restricting to a compact subset, it suffices to treat the case when the underlying space is compact. Now from \eqref{homotopysheafproperty}, compactness, and weak vanishing, it follows that $H^i\mathcal F^\bullet=0$ for $i<<0$. Now let us prove strong vanishing by induction on $i<0$ (we have just proven the base case). For the inductive step, observe that $H^i\mathcal F^\bullet$ is a sheaf by the induction hypothesis ($H^{i-1}\mathcal F^\bullet=0$) and Lemma \ref{lowervanishingimpliessheaf}, and thus $H^i\mathcal F^\bullet_p=0\implies H^i\mathcal F^\bullet=0$.
nodes.statement_short: H^0 is a K-sheaf given strong vanishing; strong vanishing by reducing to compact spaces and inducting upward from very negative degrees, using that the lowest homology is a sheaf with zero stalks.

nodes.name: Čech cohomology of a pure homotopy K-sheaf
nodes.statement: Let $\mathcal F^\bullet$ be a pure homotopy $\mathcal K$-sheaf. Then there is a canonical isomorphism: \begin{equation} H^\bullet\mathcal F^\bullet(X)=\check H^\bullet(X;H^0\mathcal F^\bullet) \end{equation} More generally, let $[\mathcal F^\bullet_0\to\mathcal F^{\bullet-1}_1\to\cdots\to\mathcal F^{\bullet-n}_n]$ be a complex of $\mathcal K$-presheaves where each $\mathcal F^\bullet_i$ is a pure homotopy $\mathcal K$-sheaf. Then there is a canonical isomorphism: \begin{equation} H^\bullet[\mathcal F^\bullet_0(X)\to\cdots\to\mathcal F^{\bullet-n}_n(X)]=\check H^\bullet(X;[H^0\mathcal F^\bullet_0\to\cdots\to(H^0\mathcal F^\bullet_n)[-n]]) \end{equation}
nodes.statement_short: Global sections of a pure homotopy K-sheaf (or a finite complex of them) compute Čech cohomology of H^0.
assumptions: Let $\mathcal F^\bullet$ be a pure homotopy $\mathcal K$-sheaf.

let $[\mathcal F^\bullet_0\to\mathcal F^{\bullet-1}_1\to\cdots\to\mathcal F^{\bullet-n}_n]$ be a complex of $\mathcal K$-presheaves where each $\mathcal F^\bullet_i$ is a pure homotopy $\mathcal K$-sheaf.
conclusions: Then there is a canonical isomorphism:
nodes.label: cechcohomologypurehomotopysheaf

nodes.name: Global sections compute Čech cohomology of H^0
nodes.statement: H^\bullet\mathcal F^\bullet(X)=\check H^\bullet(X;H^0\mathcal F^\bullet)

nodes.name: Canonical isomorphism for complexes of pure homotopy K-sheaves
nodes.statement: H^\bullet[\mathcal F^\bullet_0(X)\to\cdots\to\mathcal F^{\bullet-n}_n(X)]=\check H^\bullet(X;[H^0\mathcal F^\bullet_0\to\cdots\to(H^0\mathcal F^\bullet_n)[-n]])
nodes.label: cechsimplecanonicaliso

nodes.name: Proof
nodes.statement: The isomorphism \eqref{cechsimplecanonicaliso} is defined as the composition of the following isomorphisms: \begin{equation} \begin{matrix} H^\bullet[\mathcal F^\bullet_0(X)\to\cdots\to\mathcal F^{\bullet-n}_n(X)]\cr \downarrow\cr \check H^\bullet(X;[\mathcal F^\bullet_0\to\cdots\to\mathcal F^{\bullet-n}_n])\cr \downarrow\cr \check H^\bullet(X;[\tau_{\geq 0}\mathcal F^\bullet_0\to\cdots\to\tau_{\geq n}\mathcal F^{\bullet-n}_n])\cr \uparrow\cr \check H^\bullet(X;[H^0\mathcal F^\bullet_0\to\cdots\to H^n\mathcal F^{\bullet-n}_n]) \end{matrix} \end{equation} The maps are isomorphisms for the following reasons. Map one: $[\mathcal F^\bullet_0\to\cdots\to\mathcal F^{\bullet-n}_n]$ is a homotopy $\mathcal K$-sheaf (Lemma \ref{associatedgradedhomotopysheaf}), and a homotopy $\mathcal K$-sheaf calculates its own $\check H^\bullet$ (Proposition \ref{homotopysheafcechquasiisomorphism}). Map two: the map of coefficient $\mathcal K$-presheaves is a quasi-isomorphism (Lemma \ref{cechsimplebasic}) and thus induces an isomorphism on $\check H^\bullet$ (Lemma \ref{qicech}). Map three: the map of coefficient $\mathcal K$-presheaves is a quasi-isomorphism on stalks (by purity), and thus induces an isomorphism on $\check H^\bullet$ (Proposition \ref{cechdeterminedbystalks}).
nodes.statement_short: Compose three isomorphisms: self-computation of Čech cohomology, truncation quasi-isomorphism, and stalkwise quasi-isomorphism by purity.

nodes.name: Chain of isomorphisms for pure homotopy K-sheaf Čech cohomology
nodes.statement: \begin{matrix} H^\bullet[\mathcal F^\bullet_0(X)\to\cdots\to\mathcal F^{\bullet-n}_n(X)]\cr \downarrow\cr \check H^\bullet(X;[\mathcal F^\bullet_0\to\cdots\to\mathcal F^{\bullet-n}_n])\cr \downarrow\cr \check H^\bullet(X;[\tau_{\geq 0}\mathcal F^\bullet_0\to\cdots\to\tau_{\geq n}\mathcal F^{\bullet-n}_n])\cr \uparrow\cr \check H^\bullet(X;[H^0\mathcal F^\bullet_0\to\cdots\to H^n\mathcal F^{\bullet-n}_n]) \end{matrix}
nodes.label: isosforpurehtpysheafcech

nodes.name: Checking purity on a cover
nodes.statement: Let $\mathcal F^\bullet$ be a homotopy $\mathcal K$-sheaf. Write $X=U\cup Z$ with $U$ open and $Z$ closed, and suppose that $i^\ast\mathcal F^\bullet$ and $j^\ast\mathcal F^\bullet$ are both pure ($i:Z\hookrightarrow X$ and $j:U\hookrightarrow X$). Then $\mathcal F^\bullet$ is pure.
assumptions: Let $\mathcal F^\bullet$ be a homotopy $\mathcal K$-sheaf.
Write $X=U\cup Z$ with $U$ open and $Z$ closed, and suppose that $i^\ast\mathcal F^\bullet$ and $j^\ast\mathcal F^\bullet$ are both pure ($i:Z\hookrightarrow X$ and $j:U\hookrightarrow X$).
conclusions: Then $\mathcal F^\bullet$ is pure.
nodes.label: openclosedpurity

nodes.name: Proof
nodes.statement: It suffices to show the weak vanishing property for $\mathcal F^\bullet$. Let $\alpha\in H^i\mathcal F^\bullet(K)$ be arbitrary with $i<0$. By Remark \ref{nbhdintersectiongood} and Lemma \ref{anycompactintersectionworks}, the following is a quasi-isomorphism: \begin{equation} \varinjlim_{\begin{smallmatrix}Z\subseteq V\cr V\textrm{ open}\end{smallmatrix}}\mathcal F^\bullet(K\cap\overline V)\to\mathcal F^\bullet(K\cap Z) \end{equation} Since $H^i\mathcal F^\bullet(K\cap Z)=0$ by strong vanishing for $i^\ast\mathcal F^\bullet$, we see that the image of $\alpha$ in $H^i\mathcal F^\bullet(K\cap\overline V)$ vanishes for some open $V\supseteq Z$. Now applying \eqref{homotopysheafproperty} to $K=(K\cap\overline V)\cup(K\setminus V)$, we see that the vanishing of the image of $\alpha$ in $H^i\mathcal F^\bullet(K\cap\overline V)$ implies that $\alpha$ ``comes from'' the cohomology of $[\mathcal F^\bullet(K\setminus V)\to\mathcal F^{\bullet-1}(K\cap\overline V\cap(K\setminus V))$]. On the other hand, this latter group vanishes in degrees $i<0$ by strong vanishing for $j^\ast\mathcal F^\bullet$. Thus $\alpha=0$, so we have even shown strong vanishing for $\mathcal F^\bullet$.
nodes.statement_short: Kill a negative-degree class near Z using strong vanishing on Z, then use Mayer-Vietoris to push it to the part in U where strong vanishing again kills it.

nodes.name: Neighborhood limit quasi-isomorphism near Z
nodes.statement: \varinjlim_{\begin{smallmatrix}Z\subseteq V\cr V\textrm{ open}\end{smallmatrix}}\mathcal F^\bullet(K\cap\overline V)\to\mathcal F^\bullet(K\cap Z)

nodes.name: No countability assumptions on manifolds
nodes.statement: Throughout this paper, we make no second countability or paracompactness assumptions on manifolds (topological or smooth).

nodes.name: Orientation sheaf of manifold
nodes.statement: Let $M$ be a topological manifold. We let $\mathfrak o_M$ denote the \emph{orientation sheaf}\footnote{Note that the fundamental class lies in homology twisted by $\mathfrak o_M^\vee$.} of $M$ (the corresponding $\mathcal K$-sheaf is defined by $\mathfrak o_M(K):=H_{\dim M}(M,M\setminus K)$); it is locally isomorphic to the constant sheaf $\underline\mathbb Z$ (and following Convention \ref{signconventions}, it has parity $\dim M\in\mathbb Z/2$). Now let $M$ be a topological manifold with boundary, and define orientation sheaves on $M$: \begin{align} \mathfrak o_M&:=j_*\mathfrak o_{M\setminus\partial M}\\ \mathfrak o_{M\operatorname{rel}\partial}&:=j_!\mathfrak o_{M\setminus\partial M} \end{align} where $j:M\setminus\partial M\hookrightarrow M$. Then $\mathfrak o_M$ is locally isomorphic to the constant sheaf $\underline\mathbb Z$, and there is a sequence of sheaves which is exact on stalks: \begin{equation} 0\to\mathfrak o_{M\operatorname{rel}\partial}\to\mathfrak o_M\to i_\ast\mathfrak o_{\partial M}\to 0 \end{equation} where $i:\partial M\hookrightarrow M$, and the second map comes from the boundary map in the long exact sequence of the pair $(M,\partial M)$.
nodes.statement_short: Orientation sheaf o_M (K-sheaf H_dim(M,M-K)), and for manifolds with boundary o_M and o_{M rel ∂} via j_*, j_!, with a short exact sequence to the boundary.
nodes.label: manordef

nodes.name: Orientation sheaves on a manifold with boundary
nodes.statement: \mathfrak o_M&:=j_*\mathfrak o_{M\setminus\partial M}\\ \mathfrak o_{M\operatorname{rel}\partial}&:=j_!\mathfrak o_{M\setminus\partial M}

nodes.name: Orientation sheaf short exact sequence
nodes.statement: 0\to\mathfrak o_{M\operatorname{rel}\partial}\to\mathfrak o_M\to i_\ast\mathfrak o_{\partial M}\to 0

nodes.name: Homotopy K-sheaf axioms for singular chains
nodes.statement: Let $X$ be a topological space. Then we have: \begin{rlist} \item$C_\bullet(X,X)$ is acyclic. \itemLet $A,B\subseteq X$ be closed. Then the complex: \begin{equation*} \bigl[C_\bullet(X,X\setminus(A\cup B))\to C_{\bullet+1}(X,X\setminus A)\oplus C_{\bullet+1}(X,X\setminus B)\to C_{\bullet+2}(X,X\setminus(A\cap B))\bigr] \end{equation*} is acyclic. \itemLet $K=\bigcap_{\alpha\in A}K_\alpha$ where $\{K_\alpha\}_{\alpha\in A}$ is a family of closed subsets of $X$ which is \emph{filtered} in the sense that for all $\alpha_1,\alpha_2\in A$, there exists $\beta\in A$ with $K_\beta\subseteq K_{\alpha_1}\cap K_{\alpha_2}$. Then $\varinjlim_{\alpha\in A}C_\bullet(X,X\setminus K_\alpha)\to C_\bullet(X,X\setminus K)$ is a quasi-isomorphism. \end{rlist}
nodes.statement_short: Relative singular chains C(X, X-K) satisfy the homotopy K-sheaf axioms: acyclic for K empty, Mayer-Vietoris for closed pairs, continuity for filtered intersections.
assumptions: Let $X$ be a topological space.
conclusions: $C_\bullet(X,X)$ is acyclic.
Then $\varinjlim_{\alpha\in A}C_\bullet(X,X\setminus K_\alpha)\to C_\bullet(X,X\setminus K)$ is a quasi-isomorphism.
nodes.label: singularchainshomotopyKsheaf

nodes.name: Proof
nodes.statement: Statement (\ref{scacyc}) is obvious. Statement (\ref{scpatch}) can be deduced from Mayer--Vietoris using a form of the nine lemma as we now explain. Let us write $U:=X\setminus A$ and $V:=X\setminus B$. Now consider the following total complex: \begin{equation} \begin{CD} C_\bullet(U\cap V)@>>>C_{\bullet+1}(U)\oplus C_{\bullet+1}(V)@>>>C_{\bullet+2}(U\cup V)\cr @VVV@VVV@VVV\cr C_{\bullet+1}(X)@>>>C_{\bullet+2}(X)\oplus C_{\bullet+2}(X)@>>>C_{\bullet+3}(X)\cr @VVV@VVV@VVV\cr C_{\bullet+2}(X,U\cap V)@>>>C_{\bullet+3}(X,U)\oplus C_{\bullet+3}(X,V)@>>>C_{\bullet+4}(X,U\cup V)\cr \end{CD} \end{equation} The columns are acyclic (by definition of relative chains), and hence the total complex is acyclic as well. The first row is acyclic by Mayer--Vietoris, and the second row is obviously acyclic. Thus the third row is acyclic, as needed. Statement (\ref{sccont}) is true because the map is in fact an isomorphism on the chain level. It is clearly surjective; to show injectivity we must show that a singular chain on $X$ which is disjoint from $K$ is in fact disjoint from $K_\alpha$ for some $\alpha\in A$. This follows because the standard $n$-simplex is compact.
nodes.statement_short: (i) obvious; (ii) via Mayer-Vietoris and a nine-lemma argument on a 3x3 total complex; (iii) chain-level isomorphism by compactness of simplices.

nodes.name: Nine-lemma total complex for relative chains
nodes.statement: \begin{CD} C_\bullet(U\cap V)@>>>C_{\bullet+1}(U)\oplus C_{\bullet+1}(V)@>>>C_{\bullet+2}(U\cup V)\cr @VVV@VVV@VVV\cr C_{\bullet+1}(X)@>>>C_{\bullet+2}(X)\oplus C_{\bullet+2}(X)@>>>C_{\bullet+3}(X)\cr @VVV@VVV@VVV\cr C_{\bullet+2}(X,U\cap V)@>>>C_{\bullet+3}(X,U)\oplus C_{\bullet+3}(X,V)@>>>C_{\bullet+4}(X,U\cup V)\cr \end{CD}

nodes.name: Poincaré–Lefschetz duality
nodes.statement: Let $M$ be a topological manifold of dimension $n$ with boundary. Let $i:X\hookrightarrow M$ be a closed subset. Let $N\subseteq\partial M$ (closed) be a tamely embedded codimension zero submanifold with boundary.\footnote{In other words, $N\subseteq\partial M$ is a closed subset which locally looks like either $\varnothing\subseteq\mathbb R^{n-1}$, $\mathbb R_{\geq 0}\times\mathbb R^{n-2}\subseteq\mathbb R^{n-1}$, or $\mathbb R^{n-1}\subseteq\mathbb R^{n-1}$.} Then there is a canonical isomorphism: \begin{equation} H^\bullet[C_{n-1-\bullet}(N,N\setminus X)\to C_{n-\bullet}(M,M\setminus X)]=\check H^\bullet_c(X;i^\ast j_!j^\ast\mathfrak o_M) \end{equation} where $j:M^\circ\cup N^\circ\hookrightarrow M$. In particular, specializing to $N=\varnothing$, there is a canonical isomorphism: \begin{equation} H_{n-\bullet}(M,M\setminus X)=\check H^\bullet_c(X;i^\ast\mathfrak o_{M\operatorname{rel}\partial M}) \end{equation}
nodes.statement_short: For a closed subset X of a manifold with boundary and N ⊆ ∂M, relative singular homology of (M,N) near X equals compactly supported Čech cohomology of X with orientation coefficients.
assumptions: Let $M$ be a topological manifold of dimension $n$ with boundary.
Let $i:X\hookrightarrow M$ be a closed subset.
Let $N\subseteq\partial M$ (closed) be a tamely embedded codimension zero submanifold with boundary.
conclusions: Then there is a canonical isomorphism:
nodes.label: poincareduality

nodes.name: Poincaré–Lefschetz duality isomorphism
nodes.statement: H^\bullet[C_{n-1-\bullet}(N,N\setminus X)\to C_{n-\bullet}(M,M\setminus X)]=\check H^\bullet_c(X;i^\ast j_!j^\ast\mathfrak o_M)
nodes.label: poincaredualitygoal

nodes.name: Poincaré duality for closed subsets (N empty)
nodes.statement: H_{n-\bullet}(M,M\setminus X)=\check H^\bullet_c(X;i^\ast\mathfrak o_{M\operatorname{rel}\partial M})

nodes.name: Proof
nodes.statement: Let $X^+$ be the one-point compactification of $X$. Define a complex of $\mathcal K$-presheaves $\mathcal F^\bullet$ on $X^+$: \begin{equation} \mathcal F^\bullet(K):=[C_{n-1-\bullet}(N,N\setminus K)\to C_{n-\bullet}(M,M\setminus K)] \end{equation} (where on the right hand side by $K$ we really mean $K\cap X$). Applying Lemmas \ref{singularchainshomotopyKsheaf} and \ref{associatedgradedhomotopysheaf}, we see that $\mathcal F^\bullet$ is a homotopy $\mathcal K$-sheaf. We claim that $\mathcal F^\bullet$ is a pure homotopy $\mathcal K$-sheaf. Certainly the homology of $\mathcal F^\bullet$ is bounded below, because the singular chain complex of a topological manifold has homology bounded above and $\mathcal F^\bullet$ is built out of these. Now, it is easy to calculate: \begin{equation} H^\bullet\mathcal F^\bullet_p=\begin{cases}\mathbb Z&p\in M^\circ\cup N^\circ\cr 0&p\notin M^\circ\cup N^\circ\end{cases} \end{equation} concentrated in degree zero (see \cite[p231 \S3.3]{hatcher} for the special case $N=\partial M=\varnothing$). Hence $\mathcal F^\bullet$ is a pure homotopy $\mathcal K$-sheaf. In fact, it is not hard to see (using the adjunction $j_!\dashv j^\ast$) that \eqref{stalkhomologyofPDpure} lifts to an isomorphism of sheaves $f_!i^\ast j_!j^\ast\mathfrak o_M\to H^0\mathcal F^\bullet$ where $f:X\hookrightarrow X^+$. Now we conclude: \begin{equation*} H^\bullet\mathcal F^\bullet(X^+)\overset{\text{Prop \ref{cechcohomologypurehomotopysheaf}}}=\check H^\bullet(X^+;f_!i^\ast j_!j^\ast\mathfrak o_M)\overset{\text{Lem \ref{cptcechembeddingproperty}}}=\check H^\bullet_c(X;i^\ast j_!j^\ast\mathfrak o_M) \end{equation*} Now observe that $H^\bullet\mathcal F^\bullet(X^+)$ is the left hand side of \eqref{poincaredualitygoal}.
nodes.statement_short: Show the relative chain complex K ↦ C(M,M−K) is a pure homotopy K-sheaf on X^+ with H^0 the orientation sheaf, then apply the pure-sheaf Čech computation and compact-support comparison.

nodes.name: Relative chain K-presheaf for Poincaré duality
nodes.statement: \mathcal F^\bullet(K):=[C_{n-1-\bullet}(N,N\setminus K)\to C_{n-\bullet}(M,M\setminus K)]
nodes.label: purehomotopyKsheafinPD

nodes.name: Stalk homology of the duality K-presheaf
nodes.statement: H^\bullet\mathcal F^\bullet_p=\begin{cases}\mathbb Z&p\in M^\circ\cup N^\circ\cr 0&p\notin M^\circ\cup N^\circ\end{cases}
nodes.label: stalkhomologyofPDpure

nodes.name: Why homotopy K-sheaves instead of homotopy sheaves?
nodes.statement: The naive modification of \eqref{purehomotopyKsheafinPD} substituting open $U\subseteq X$ in place of compact $K\subseteq X$ does not yield a homotopy sheaf. To get a homotopy sheaf, one could apply the proposed functor $R\alpha_\ast:\operatorname{hShv}_\mathcal K X\to\operatorname{hShv} X$ from Remark \ref{homotopyKnotsheavesequivalencermk} to the homotopy $\mathcal K$-sheaf \eqref{purehomotopyKsheafinPD}. It is somewhat easier, though, to just work directly in the setting of homotopy $\mathcal K$-sheaves (which has some advantages, for example stalks of $\mathcal K$-presheaves are easier to define/understand). It is for this reason that throughout this paper we work with homotopy $\mathcal K$-sheaves instead of homotopy sheaves.
nodes.statement_short: Open-set version of the duality complex is not a homotopy sheaf; working with homotopy K-sheaves avoids derived inverse limits.

nodes.name: Homotopy diagram
nodes.statement: Let $\mathcal S$ be a finite poset. A \emph{homotopy diagram over $\mathcal S$} is a collection of complexes $\{A^\bullet_{\mathfrak s,\mathfrak t}\}_{\mathfrak s\preceq\mathfrak t\in\mathcal S}$ equipped with compatible maps $A^\bullet_{\mathfrak s,\mathfrak t}\to A^\bullet_{\mathfrak s',\mathfrak t'}$ for $\mathfrak s\preceq\mathfrak s'\preceq\mathfrak t'\preceq\mathfrak t$ (meaning that $A^\bullet_{\mathfrak s,\mathfrak t}\to A^\bullet_{\mathfrak s',\mathfrak t'}\to A^\bullet_{\mathfrak s'',\mathfrak t''}$ and $A^\bullet_{\mathfrak s,\mathfrak t}\to A^\bullet_{\mathfrak s'',\mathfrak t''}$ agree).
nodes.statement_short: Complexes A_{s,t} indexed by pairs s ⪯ t in a finite poset, with compatible maps when the interval shrinks.
differentia: equipped with compatible maps $A^\bullet_{\mathfrak s,\mathfrak t}\to A^\bullet_{\mathfrak s',\mathfrak t'}$ for $\mathfrak s\preceq\mathfrak s'\preceq\mathfrak t'\preceq\mathfrak t$

nodes.name: Homotopy colimit
nodes.statement: Let $\mathcal S$ be a finite poset and let $\{A^\bullet_{\mathfrak s,\mathfrak t}\}_{\mathfrak s\preceq\mathfrak t\in\mathcal S}$ be a homotopy diagram over $\mathcal S$.
