We define the \emph{homotopy colimit}: \begin{equation} \operatornamewithlimits{hocolim}_{\mathfrak s\preceq\mathfrak t\in\mathcal S}A^\bullet_{\mathfrak s,\mathfrak t}:=\bigoplus_{p\geq 0}\bigoplus_{\mathfrak s_0\prec\cdots\prec\mathfrak s_p\in\mathcal S}A^{\bullet+p}_{\mathfrak s_0,\mathfrak s_p} \end{equation} with differential (decreasing $p$) given by the alternating sum over forgetting one of the $\mathfrak s_i$ (plus the internal differential).\footnote{This can be interpreted as the complex of simplicial chains on the nerve of $\mathcal S$ using a coefficient system determined by $\{A^\bullet_{\mathfrak s,\mathfrak t}\}$.} Loosely speaking, we are ``gluing together'' the $\{A^\bullet_{\mathfrak s,\mathfrak s}\}_{\mathfrak s\in\mathcal S}$ along the ``morphisms'' $A^\bullet_{\mathfrak s,\mathfrak s}\leftarrow A^\bullet_{\mathfrak s,\mathfrak t}\to A^\bullet_{\mathfrak t,\mathfrak t}$ for $\mathfrak s\preceq\mathfrak t$.
nodes.statement_short: hocolim of a homotopy diagram: direct sum over chains s_0<...<s_p of A_{s_0,s_p} shifted by p, with alternating face differential.
nodes.label: homotopycolimit

nodes.name: Homotopy colimit formula
nodes.statement: \operatornamewithlimits{hocolim}_{\mathfrak s\preceq\mathfrak t\in\mathcal S}A^\bullet_{\mathfrak s,\mathfrak t}:=\bigoplus_{p\geq 0}\bigoplus_{\mathfrak s_0\prec\cdots\prec\mathfrak s_p\in\mathcal S}A^{\bullet+p}_{\mathfrak s_0,\mathfrak s_p}

nodes.name: Terminal object for hocolim
nodes.statement: Let $\mathcal S$ be a finite poset with unique maximal element $\mathfrak s^\mathrm{top}$, and let $\{A^\bullet_{\mathfrak s,\mathfrak t}\}_{\mathfrak s\preceq\mathfrak t\in\mathcal S}$ be a homotopy diagram with the property that every map $A^\bullet_{\mathfrak s,\mathfrak t}\to A^\bullet_{\mathfrak s,\mathfrak t'}$ ($\mathfrak s\preceq\mathfrak t'\preceq\mathfrak t$) is a quasi-isomorphism. Then the natural inclusion $A^\bullet_{\mathfrak s^\mathrm{top},\mathfrak s^\mathrm{top}}\to\operatornamewithlimits{hocolim}_{\mathfrak s\preceq\mathfrak t\in\mathcal S}A^\bullet_{\mathfrak s,\mathfrak t}$ is a quasi-isomorphism.
assumptions: Let $\mathcal S$ be a finite poset with unique maximal element $\mathfrak s^\mathrm{top}$
every map $A^\bullet_{\mathfrak s,\mathfrak t}\to A^\bullet_{\mathfrak s,\mathfrak t'}$ ($\mathfrak s\preceq\mathfrak t'\preceq\mathfrak t$) is a quasi-isomorphism.
conclusions: Then the natural inclusion $A^\bullet_{\mathfrak s^\mathrm{top},\mathfrak s^\mathrm{top}}\to\operatornamewithlimits{hocolim}_{\mathfrak s\preceq\mathfrak t\in\mathcal S}A^\bullet_{\mathfrak s,\mathfrak t}$ is a quasi-isomorphism.
nodes.label: comboretraction

nodes.name: Proof
nodes.statement: We filter $\operatornamewithlimits{hocolim}_{\mathfrak s\preceq\mathfrak t\in\mathcal S}A^\bullet_{\mathfrak s,\mathfrak t}$ by the number of $\mathfrak s_0,\ldots,\mathfrak s_p$ which are not equal to $\mathfrak s^\mathrm{top}$. The zeroth associated graded piece is the subcomplex $A^\bullet_{\mathfrak s^\mathrm{top},\mathfrak s^\mathrm{top}}$, so it suffices to show that all the other associated graded pieces are acyclic. Each of these is a direct sum of mapping cones $[A^{\bullet+1}_{\mathfrak s,\mathfrak s^\mathrm{top}}\to A^\bullet_{\mathfrak s,\mathfrak t}]$, which are acyclic by assumption.
nodes.statement_short: Filter by the number of chain elements different from the top; nonzero graded pieces are sums of acyclic mapping cones.

nodes.name: hocolim preserves quasi-isomorphisms
nodes.statement: Fix a finite poset $\mathcal S$ and let $\{A^\bullet_{\mathfrak s,\mathfrak t}\}_{\mathfrak s\preceq\mathfrak t\in\mathcal S}$ and $\{B^\bullet_{\mathfrak s,\mathfrak t}\}_{\mathfrak s\preceq\mathfrak t\in\mathcal S}$ be homotopy diagrams over $\mathcal S$. Suppose that there are compatible quasi-isomorphisms $A^\bullet_{\mathfrak s,\mathfrak t}\to B^\bullet_{\mathfrak s,\mathfrak t}$. Then the induced map $\operatornamewithlimits{hocolim}_{\mathfrak s\preceq\mathfrak t\in\mathcal S}A^\bullet_{\mathfrak s,\mathfrak t}\to\operatornamewithlimits{hocolim}_{\mathfrak s\preceq\mathfrak t\in\mathcal S}B^\bullet_{\mathfrak s,\mathfrak t}$ is a quasi-isomorphism.
assumptions: Suppose that there are compatible quasi-isomorphisms $A^\bullet_{\mathfrak s,\mathfrak t}\to B^\bullet_{\mathfrak s,\mathfrak t}$.
conclusions: is a quasi-isomorphism.
nodes.label: simplicialchainsquasiisomorphism

nodes.name: Proof
nodes.statement: Since the functor $\operatornamewithlimits{hocolim}_{\mathfrak s\preceq\mathfrak t\in\mathcal S}$ commutes with the formation of mapping cones, it suffices to show that if each $A^\bullet_{\mathfrak s,\mathfrak t}$ is acyclic, then so is $\operatornamewithlimits{hocolim}_{\mathfrak s\preceq\mathfrak t\in\mathcal S}A^\bullet_{\mathfrak s,\mathfrak t}$. This holds since in this case it has a finite filtration whose associated graded is acyclic.
nodes.statement_short: hocolim commutes with mapping cones; acyclic inputs give a finitely filtered complex with acyclic graded pieces.

nodes.name: Tensor product of homotopy diagrams
nodes.statement: Let $\mathcal S$ and $\mathcal T$ be two finite posets, and let $\{A^\bullet_{\mathfrak s,\mathfrak s'}\}$ and $\{B^\bullet_{\mathfrak t,\mathfrak t'}\}$ be homotopy diagrams over $\mathcal S$ and $\mathcal T$ respectively. Their tensor product $\{A^\bullet_{\mathfrak s,\mathfrak s'}\otimes B^\bullet_{\mathfrak t,\mathfrak t'}\}$ is naturally a homotopy diagram over $\mathcal S\times\mathcal T$. Now there is a natural morphism: \begin{equation} \operatornamewithlimits{hocolim}_{\mathfrak s\preceq\mathfrak s'\in\mathcal S}A^\bullet_{\mathfrak s,\mathfrak s'}\otimes\operatornamewithlimits{hocolim}_{\mathfrak t\preceq\mathfrak t'\in\mathcal T}B^\bullet_{\mathfrak t,\mathfrak t'}\to\operatornamewithlimits{hocolim}_{\mathfrak s\times\mathfrak t\preceq\mathfrak s'\times\mathfrak t'\in\mathcal S\times\mathcal T}A^\bullet_{\mathfrak s,\mathfrak s'}\otimes B^\bullet_{\mathfrak t,\mathfrak t'} \end{equation} To define this morphism, we simply observe that the nerve of $\mathcal S\times\mathcal T$ is the standard simplicial subdivision of the product of the nerves of $\mathcal S$ and $\mathcal T$, and this is covered by a morphism of coefficient systems.\footnote{In fact, from this perspective one easily sees that \eqref{tensorproductdirectlimitmorphism} is always a quasi-isomorphism.}
nodes.statement_short: Tensor product of homotopy diagrams over S and T is a diagram over S×T with a natural map from the tensor product of hocolims (via subdivision of nerves).
nodes.label: simplicialproduct

nodes.name: Tensor product of homotopy colimits morphism
nodes.statement: \operatornamewithlimits{hocolim}_{\mathfrak s\preceq\mathfrak s'\in\mathcal S}A^\bullet_{\mathfrak s,\mathfrak s'}\otimes\operatornamewithlimits{hocolim}_{\mathfrak t\preceq\mathfrak t'\in\mathcal T}B^\bullet_{\mathfrak t,\mathfrak t'}\to\operatornamewithlimits{hocolim}_{\mathfrak s\times\mathfrak t\preceq\mathfrak s'\times\mathfrak t'\in\mathcal S\times\mathcal T}A^\bullet_{\mathfrak s,\mathfrak s'}\otimes B^\bullet_{\mathfrak t,\mathfrak t'}
nodes.label: tensorproductdirectlimitmorphism

nodes.name: hocolim preserves homotopy K-sheaves
nodes.statement: Let $\mathcal S$ be a finite poset and let $\{\mathcal F^\bullet_{\mathfrak s,\mathfrak t}\}_{\mathfrak s\preceq\mathfrak t\in\mathcal S}$ be a homotopy diagram of homotopy $\mathcal K$-sheaves. Then $\operatornamewithlimits{hocolim}_{\mathfrak s\preceq\mathfrak t\in\mathcal S}\mathcal F^\bullet_{\mathfrak s,\mathfrak t}$ is a homotopy $\mathcal K$-sheaf.
nodes.section: A.8 Homotopy colimits of pure homotopy \texorpdfstring{$\mathcal K$}{K}-sheaves
assumptions: let $\{\mathcal F^\bullet_{\mathfrak s,\mathfrak t}\}_{\mathfrak s\preceq\mathfrak t\in\mathcal S}$ be a homotopy diagram of homotopy $\mathcal K$-sheaves.
conclusions: Then $\operatornamewithlimits{hocolim}_{\mathfrak s\preceq\mathfrak t\in\mathcal S}\mathcal F^\bullet_{\mathfrak s,\mathfrak t}$ is a homotopy $\mathcal K$-sheaf.
nodes.label: pihomotopysheaf

nodes.name: Proof
nodes.statement: The associated graded of the $p$-filtration on $\operatornamewithlimits{hocolim}_{\mathfrak s\preceq\mathfrak t\in\mathcal S}\mathcal F^\bullet_{\mathfrak s,\mathfrak t}$ is a homotopy $\mathcal K$-sheaf by assumption; now use Lemma \ref{associatedgradedhomotopysheaf}.
nodes.section: A.8 Homotopy colimits of pure homotopy \texorpdfstring{$\mathcal K$}{K}-sheaves
nodes.statement_short: The p-filtration has homotopy K-sheaf graded pieces; apply the extension lemma.

nodes.name: Gluing pure homotopy K-sheaves
nodes.statement: Let $A$ be a finite set. Let $\{U_I\}_{I\subseteq A}$ be an open cover of a space $X$ satisfying: \begin{rlist} \item$U_I\cap U_K\subseteq U_J$ for $I\subseteq J\subseteq K$. \item$U_I\cap U_{I'}\subseteq U_{I\cup I'}$ for $I,I'\subseteq A$. \end{rlist} Let $\mathcal G$ be a sheaf on $X$ and let $\mathcal G_{IJ}:=(j_{IJ})_!(j_{IJ})^\ast\mathcal G$ where $j_{IJ}:U_I\cap U_J\hookrightarrow X$. By property (\ref{nestedintersectionOK}), this gives rise to a homotopy diagram $\{\mathcal G_{IJ}\}_{I\subseteq A}$ over $2^A$ of sheaves on $X$. Let $\{\mathcal F_{IJ}^\bullet\}_{I\subseteq J\subseteq A}$ be a homotopy diagram over $2^A$ of pure homotopy $\mathcal K$-sheaves on $X$, and suppose we give a compatible system of isomorphisms $\mathcal G_{IJ}\xrightarrow\sim H^0\mathcal F^\bullet_{IJ}$. Then $\mathcal F^\bullet:=\operatornamewithlimits{hocolim}_{I\subseteq J\subseteq A}\mathcal F^\bullet_{IJ}$ is a pure homotopy $\mathcal K$-sheaf and there is a canonical induced isomorphism $\mathcal G\xrightarrow\sim H^0\mathcal F^\bullet$.
nodes.section: A.8 Homotopy colimits of pure homotopy \texorpdfstring{$\mathcal K$}{K}-sheaves
nodes.statement_short: The hocolim over 2^A of pure homotopy K-sheaves resolving extensions by zero of a sheaf G from a suitable open cover is pure with H^0 = G.
assumptions: Let $A$ be a finite set.
$U_I\cap U_K\subseteq U_J$ for $I\subseteq J\subseteq K$.
$U_I\cap U_{I'}\subseteq U_{I\cup I'}$ for $I,I'\subseteq A$.

Let $\{\mathcal F_{IJ}^\bullet\}_{I\subseteq J\subseteq A}$ be a homotopy diagram over $2^A$ of pure homotopy $\mathcal K$-sheaves on $X$, and suppose we give a compatible system of isomorphisms $\mathcal G_{IJ}\xrightarrow\sim H^0\mathcal F^\bullet_{IJ}$.
conclusions: Then $\mathcal F^\bullet:=\operatornamewithlimits{hocolim}_{I\subseteq J\subseteq A}\mathcal F^\bullet_{IJ}$ is a pure homotopy $\mathcal K$-sheaf and there is a canonical induced isomorphism $\mathcal G\xrightarrow\sim H^0\mathcal F^\bullet$.
nodes.label: gluingcechsimple

nodes.name: Proof
nodes.statement: Certainly $\mathcal F^\bullet$ is a homotopy $\mathcal K$-sheaf by Lemma \ref{pihomotopysheaf}. Since $A$ is finite, it is easy to see that $H^i\mathcal F^\bullet_{IJ}$ being bounded below implies that $H^i\mathcal F^\bullet$ is bounded below. Now let us calculate $\mathcal F^\bullet_p$ using the spectral sequence associated to the $p$-filtration. The $E_1$ term is concentrated along the $q=0$ row since $(H^q\mathcal F^\bullet_{IJ})_p$ is concentrated in degree zero; thus there are no further differentials after the $E_1$ page. On the $E_1$ page the differentials coincide precisely with the differentials in the definition of $\operatornamewithlimits{hocolim}_{I\subseteq J\subseteq A}(\mathcal G_{IJ})_p$ (regarding $\mathcal G_{IJ}$ as complexes concentrated in degree zero). Hence we have an isomorphism: \begin{equation} H^\bullet\mathcal F^\bullet_p=H^\bullet\operatornamewithlimits{hocolim}_{I\subseteq J\subseteq A}(\mathcal G_{IJ})_p \end{equation} To calculate the right hand side of \eqref{FGiso}, let us start with the trivial observation that: \begin{equation} (\mathcal G_{IJ})_p=\begin{cases}\mathcal G_p&p\in U_I\cap U_J\cr 0&p\notin U_I\cap U_J\end{cases} \end{equation} Now consider $(2^A)_p:=\{I\subseteq A:p\in U_I\}$, which satisfies the following properties: \begin{rlist} \item$(2^A)_p$ has a maximal element (restatement of (\ref{nonnestedintersectionbig})). \item$I,K\in(2^A)_p$ implies $J\in(2^A)_p$ for $I\subseteq J\subseteq K$ (restatement of (\ref{nestedintersectionOK})). \end{rlist} These two properties imply that $\operatornamewithlimits{hocolim}_{I\subseteq J\subseteq A}(\mathcal G_{IJ})_p$ is simply $\mathcal G_p$ tensored with the simplicial chain complex of the nerve of $(2^A)_p$ (which is contractible). Hence \eqref{FGiso} gives a canonical isomorphism of stalks $H^0\mathcal F^\bullet_p=\mathcal G_p$ (and thus in particular $\mathcal F^\bullet$ is pure). Now it remains to construct a canonical isomorphism of sheaves $\mathcal G\xrightarrow\sim H^0\mathcal F^\bullet$. Over the open set $U_I$, we define this isomorphism to be the composition $\mathcal G_{II}\xrightarrow\sim H^0\mathcal F_{II}^\bullet\to H^0\mathcal F^\bullet$ (the second map being the inclusion of a $p=0$ subcomplex in the homotopy colimit). At any point $p\in U_I$, this specializes to the isomorphism of stalks $\mathcal G_p=H^0\mathcal F^\bullet_p$ defined earlier. Hence since $\{U_I\}_{I\subseteq A}$ is an open cover of $X$, these isomorphisms patch together to give the desired global isomorphism.
nodes.section: A.8 Homotopy colimits of pure homotopy \texorpdfstring{$\mathcal K$}{K}-sheaves
nodes.statement_short: Compute stalks by the p-filtration spectral sequence, which degenerates; the stalk hocolim is G_p tensored with chains on a contractible nerve. Patch the local isomorphisms over the cover.

nodes.name: Stalk homology of hocolim
nodes.statement: H^\bullet\mathcal F^\bullet_p=H^\bullet\operatornamewithlimits{hocolim}_{I\subseteq J\subseteq A}(\mathcal G_{IJ})_p

nodes.name: Steenrod homology
nodes.statement: Steenrod homology $\overline H_\bullet$ is a homology theory for compact Hausdorff spaces.
differentia: for compact Hausdorff spaces

nodes.name: Axiomatic characterization of Steenrod homology
nodes.statement: It is characterized uniquely by a certain set of axioms due to Berikashvili \cite{berikashviliI,berikashviliII} (see also Goldfarb \cite[p355, \S7.4]{goldfarb} and Inassaridze \cite{inassaridze}); a simpler axiomatic characterization of Steenrod homology on compact metrizable spaces is due to Milnor \cite{milnor}.
nodes.statement_short: Steenrod homology is uniquely characterized by axioms (Berikashvili; Milnor for compact metrizable spaces).
conclusions: It is characterized uniquely by a certain set of axioms due to Berikashvili \cite{berikashviliI,berikashviliII} (see also Goldfarb \cite[p355, \S7.4]{goldfarb} and Inassaridze \cite{inassaridze}); a simpler axiomatic characterization of Steenrod homology on compact metrizable spaces is due to Milnor \cite{milnor}.

nodes.name: Steenrod homology agrees with singular homology on finite CW-complexes
nodes.statement: Note that it follows as usual from these axioms that Steenrod homology coincides with singular homology on finite CW-complexes.
conclusions: Note that it follows as usual from these axioms that Steenrod homology coincides with singular homology on finite CW-complexes.

nodes.name: Rigid open cover
nodes.statement: A \emph{rigid open cover} of a compact space $X$ consists of open sets $\{U_x\subseteq X\}_{x\in X}$ such that $x\in U_x$, $\overline{\{x:U_x=U\}}\subseteq U$, and $\#\{U:U=U_x\text{ for some }x\}<\infty$. Warning: even if $U_x=U_y$ for some $x\ne y$, they are still different elements of the cover; in particular, the nerve of a rigid cover is always infinite unless $X$ is finite.
nodes.statement_short: An open cover indexed by the points of X with x in U_x, finitely many distinct sets, and closure conditions; its nerve is typically infinite.

nodes.name: Rigid covers form a poset
nodes.statement: For doing \v Cech theory, the category of rigid open covers is technically more convenient than the usual cateory of open covers (c.f.\ Remark \ref{coveringscategoryrmk}). Specifically, the collection of rigid covers forms a set, and there is at most one morphism between any pair of rigid covers (we only consider refinements which act as the identity on the index set $X$).
nodes.statement_short: Rigid open covers form a set with at most one refinement between any two, which is convenient for Čech theory.

nodes.name: Čech cochains of sheaves (rigid covers)
nodes.statement: Let $\mathcal F$ be a sheaf. We define the \v Cech cochains: \begin{equation} \check C^\bullet(X;\mathcal F):=\varinjlim_{\begin{smallmatrix}\{U_x\subseteq X\}_{x\in X}\cr\text{rigid open cover}\end{smallmatrix}}\bigoplus_{p\geq 0}\prod_{\begin{smallmatrix}S\subseteq X\cr\left|S\right|=p+1\end{smallmatrix}}\mathcal F\Bigl(\bigcap_{x\in S}U_x\Bigr)[-p] \end{equation} with the standard \v Cech differential. For any compact $K\subseteq X$, define $\check C^\bullet_K(X;\mathcal F)$ (\v Cech cochains with supports in $K$) via \eqref{cechcomplexIderived} except replacing every instance of $\mathcal F(U)$ with $\ker[\mathcal F(U)\to\mathcal F(U\setminus K)]$. We let $\check C^\bullet_c(X;\mathcal F):=\varinjlim_{K\subseteq X}\check C^\bullet_K(X;\mathcal F)$ (\v Cech cochains with compact supports). Clearly the homology of $\check C^\bullet(X;\mathcal F)$ (resp.\ $\check C^\bullet_K(X;\mathcal F)$, $\check C^\bullet_c(X;\mathcal F)$) is $\check H^\bullet(X;\mathcal F)$ (resp.\ $\check H^\bullet_K(X;\mathcal F)$, $\check H^\bullet_c(X;\mathcal F)$).
nodes.statement_short: Chain-level Čech complexes (also with supports in K and compact supports) as direct limits over rigid open covers; their homology is Čech cohomology.

nodes.name: Čech cochains over rigid covers
nodes.statement: \check C^\bullet(X;\mathcal F):=\varinjlim_{\begin{smallmatrix}\{U_x\subseteq X\}_{x\in X}\cr\text{rigid open cover}\end{smallmatrix}}\bigoplus_{p\geq 0}\prod_{\begin{smallmatrix}S\subseteq X\cr\left|S\right|=p+1\end{smallmatrix}}\mathcal F\Bigl(\bigcap_{x\in S}U_x\Bigr)[-p]
nodes.label: cechcomplexIderived

nodes.name: Čech cochains of complexes of K-presheaves
nodes.statement: Let $\mathcal F^\bullet$ be a complex of $\mathcal K$-presheaves on a compact space $X$. We define: \begin{equation} \check C^\bullet(X;\mathcal F^\bullet):=\varinjlim_{\begin{smallmatrix}\{U_x\subseteq X\}_{x\in X}\cr\text{rigid open cover}\end{smallmatrix}}\bigoplus_{p\geq 0}\prod_{\begin{smallmatrix}S\subseteq X\cr\left|S\right|=p+1\end{smallmatrix}}\mathcal F^{\bullet-p}\Bigl(\bigcap_{x\in S}\overline{U_x}\Bigr) \end{equation} with the standard \v Cech differential (plus the internal differential of $\mathcal F^\bullet$). We also define $\check C^\bullet(X;\mathcal F)$ for any $\mathcal K$-presheaf $\mathcal F$ by viewing it as a complex concentrated in degree zero. The homology of $\check C^\bullet(X;\mathcal F^\bullet)$ is $\check H^\bullet(X;\mathcal F^\bullet)$, as can be seen by applying the arguments from the proof of Lemma \ref{cHsameforopencompactcovers}. Note that for a sheaf $\mathcal F$, the complexes \eqref{cechcomplexIderived} and \eqref{cechcomplexIIderived} are canonically isomorphic.
nodes.statement_short: Chain-level Čech complex of a complex of K-presheaves using closures of rigid cover sets; computes Čech hypercohomology.

nodes.name: Čech cochains of K-presheaf complexes
nodes.statement: \check C^\bullet(X;\mathcal F^\bullet):=\varinjlim_{\begin{smallmatrix}\{U_x\subseteq X\}_{x\in X}\cr\text{rigid open cover}\end{smallmatrix}}\bigoplus_{p\geq 0}\prod_{\begin{smallmatrix}S\subseteq X\cr\left|S\right|=p+1\end{smallmatrix}}\mathcal F^{\bullet-p}\Bigl(\bigcap_{x\in S}\overline{U_x}\Bigr)
nodes.label: cechcomplexIIderived

nodes.name: Pullback on $\check C^\bullet$ and $\check C^\bullet_c$; c.f.\ Definitions \ref{pullbackdefn}, \ref{pullbackcHKprshv}
nodes.statement: Let $f:X\to Y$ be a map of spaces. A rigid open cover $\{U_y\}_{y\in X}$ pulls back to a rigid open cover $\{f^{-1}(U_{f(x)})\}_{x\in X}$, and this gives natural maps: \begin{rlist} \item$f^\ast:\check C^\bullet(Y;f_\ast\mathcal F)\to\check C^\bullet(X;\mathcal F)$ for $\mathcal F\in\operatorname{Prshv} X$. \item$f^\ast:\check C^\bullet_c(Y;f_\ast\mathcal F)\to\check C^\bullet_c(X;\mathcal F)$ for $\mathcal F\in\operatorname{Shv} X$ (if $f$ is proper). \item$f^\ast:\check C^\bullet(Y;f_\ast\mathcal F^\bullet)\to\check C^\bullet(X;\mathcal F^\bullet)$ for $\mathcal F^i\in\operatorname{Prshv}_\mathcal K X$. \end{rlist} whose action on homology coincide with the maps $f^\ast$ defined earlier.
nodes.label: cechcochainspullback

nodes.name: Derived inverse limit
nodes.statement: Let $\{C^\bullet_\lambda\}_{\lambda\in\Lambda}$ be an inverse system of complexes. We define: \begin{equation} \mathop{R\varprojlim}_{\lambda\in\Lambda}C^\bullet_\lambda:=\prod_{q\geq 0}\prod_{\lambda_0\leq\ldots\leq\lambda_q}C^{\bullet-q}_{\lambda_0} \end{equation} with differential obtained by viewing this as cochains on the nerve of $\Lambda$ with a particular coefficient system. See Marde\v si\'c \cite[\S 17]{mardesic} for more details on and basic properties of $\mathop{R\varprojlim}$.

nodes.name: Derived inverse limit formula
nodes.statement: \mathop{R\varprojlim}_{\lambda\in\Lambda}C^\bullet_\lambda:=\prod_{q\geq 0}\prod_{\lambda_0\leq\ldots\leq\lambda_q}C^{\bullet-q}_{\lambda_0}

nodes.name: Derived functors of inverse limit
nodes.statement: Let $\{A_\lambda\}_{\lambda\in\Lambda}$ be an inverse system of abelian groups. We define: \begin{equation} \mathop{\textstyle\varprojlim^i}\limits_{\lambda\in\Lambda}A_\lambda:=H^i\Bigl[\mathop{R\varprojlim}_{\lambda\in\Lambda}A_\lambda\Bigr] \end{equation} (viewing $A_\lambda$ as an inverse system of complex concentrated in degree zero). The inverse limit functor $\varprojlim$ from inverse systems of abelian groups indexed by $\Lambda$ to abelian groups is left exact, and $\varprojlim^i$ are its right derived functors (see Marde\v si\'c \cite[Corollary 11.47]{mardesic}). See Marde\v si\'c \cite[\S\S 11--15]{mardesic} for more details on and basic properties of $\varprojlim^i$.

nodes.name: lim^i as homology of R lim
nodes.statement: \mathop{\textstyle\varprojlim^i}\limits_{\lambda\in\Lambda}A_\lambda:=H^i\Bigl[\mathop{R\varprojlim}_{\lambda\in\Lambda}A_\lambda\Bigr]
nodes.label: limidef

nodes.name: Cofinality for lim^i and R lim
nodes.statement: Let $f:\Lambda'\to\Lambda$ be weakly increasing ($\lambda_1\leq\lambda_2\implies f(\lambda_1)\leq f(\lambda_2)$) and cofinal ($f(\Lambda')\subseteq\Lambda$ cofinal). Then the following natural map is an isomorphism: \begin{equation} \mathop{\textstyle\varprojlim^i}\limits_{\lambda\in\Lambda}A_\lambda\xrightarrow\sim\mathop{\textstyle\varprojlim^i}\limits_{\lambda'\in\Lambda'}A_{f(\lambda')} \end{equation} More generally, the following natural map is a quasi-isomorphism: \begin{equation} \mathop{R\varprojlim}_{\lambda\in\Lambda}C^\bullet_\lambda\xrightarrow\sim\mathop{R\varprojlim}_{\lambda'\in\Lambda'}C^\bullet_{f(\lambda')} \end{equation}
assumptions: Let $f:\Lambda'\to\Lambda$ be weakly increasing ($\lambda_1\leq\lambda_2\implies f(\lambda_1)\leq f(\lambda_2)$) and cofinal ($f(\Lambda')\subseteq\Lambda$ cofinal).
