nodes.statement: \mathop{R\varprojlim}_{\lambda\in\Lambda}C^\bullet_\lambda\xrightarrow\sim\mathop{R\varprojlim}_{\lambda'\in\Lambda'}C^\bullet_{f(\lambda')}

nodes.name: Proof
nodes.statement: For $\textstyle\varprojlim^i$, see \cite[p291, Theorem 14.9]{mardesic}, and for $\mathop{R\varprojlim}$, see \cite[p349, Corollary 17.18]{mardesic}.
nodes.statement_short: Cited from Mardešić.

nodes.name: R lim preserves level-wise quasi-isomorphisms
nodes.statement: If $C_\lambda^\bullet\xrightarrow\sim D_\lambda^\bullet$ is a morphism of inverse systems which is a level-wise quasi-isomorphism (i.e.\ for every $\lambda$), then the natural map: \begin{equation} \mathop{R\varprojlim}_{\lambda\in\Lambda}C^\bullet_\lambda\xrightarrow\sim\mathop{R\varprojlim}_{\lambda\in\Lambda}D^\bullet_\lambda \end{equation} is a quasi-isomorphism.
assumptions: If $C_\lambda^\bullet\xrightarrow\sim D_\lambda^\bullet$ is a morphism of inverse systems which is a level-wise quasi-isomorphism (i.e.\ for every $\lambda$)
conclusions: is a quasi-isomorphism.
nodes.label: quasiisomorphismforRlim

nodes.name: Induced quasi-isomorphism of derived inverse limits
nodes.statement: \mathop{R\varprojlim}_{\lambda\in\Lambda}C^\bullet_\lambda\xrightarrow\sim\mathop{R\varprojlim}_{\lambda\in\Lambda}D^\bullet_\lambda

nodes.name: Proof
nodes.statement: See \cite[p348, Theorem 17.16]{mardesic}.
nodes.statement_short: Cited from Mardešić.

nodes.name: Partitions and their nerves (Chogoshvili)
nodes.statement: A partition $X=\bigsqcup_{i=1}^nE_i$ shall mean an \emph{unordered} partition into finitely many disjoint nonempty subsets $E_1,\ldots,E_n\subseteq X$; there is an associated finite closed covering $X=\bigcup_{i=1}^n\overline{E_i}$, whose nerve is denoted $N(X;\{\overline{E_i}\}_{i=1}^n)$ (the simplicial complex with vertices $\{1,\ldots,n\}$ where $S\subseteq\{1,\ldots,n\}$ spans a simplex iff $\bigcap_{i\in S}\overline{E_i}\ne\varnothing$). A partition $\{F_j\}_{j=1}^m$ refines $\{E_i\}_{i=1}^n$ iff for all $j$, there exists a (necessarily unique) $i$ with $F_j\subseteq E_i$. For a refinement $\{E_i\}_{i=1}^n\to\{F_j\}_{j=1}^m$, there is an associated map of nerves $N(X;\{\overline{F_j}\})\to N(X;\{\overline{E_i}\})$.
nodes.statement_short: Finite unordered partitions of X, the nerve of the closures, refinement of partitions, and induced maps of nerves.

nodes.name: Properties of Chogoshvili partitions
nodes.statement: For doing \v Cech theory, Chogoshvili's construction has exceptionally nice properties. The collection of partitions is a set, and there is at most one morphism between any pair of partitions. The poset of partitions is cofinite (a given partition refines only finitely many other partitions). Each nerve $N(X;\{\overline{E_i}\})$ is a finite simplicial complex, and the transition maps $N(X;\{\overline{F_j}\})\to N(X;\{\overline{E_i}\})$ are all surjective. Also, any pair of partitions has a minimal common refinement. Given a map $f:X\to Y$, a partition $\{E_i\}$ of $Y$ pulls back to a partition $\{f^{-1}(E_i)\}$ of $X$, and there is an associated map on nerves $N(X;\{\overline{f^{-1}(E_i)}\})\to N(Y,\{\overline{E_i}\})$.
nodes.statement_short: Partitions form a cofinite poset with unique morphisms, finite nerves with surjective transition maps, common refinements, and pullbacks along maps.

nodes.name: Inverse limit of partition nerves has the same Čech cohomology
nodes.statement: Let $X$ be compact. There is a natural map: \begin{equation} \varprojlim_{X=\bigsqcup_{i=1}^nE_i}N(X;\{\overline{E_i}\})\to X \end{equation} which induces an isomorphism on \v Cech cohomology.
assumptions: Let $X$ be compact.
conclusions: which induces an isomorphism on \v Cech cohomology.
nodes.label: inverselimithassamecech

nodes.name: Map from the inverse limit of nerves
nodes.statement: \varprojlim_{X=\bigsqcup_{i=1}^nE_i}N(X;\{\overline{E_i}\})\to X
nodes.label: chogoshvilinervecomparison

nodes.name: Proof
nodes.statement: There is a natural correspondence $C\subseteq X\times N(X;\{\overline E_i\})$, whose fiber over $x\in X$ is the complete simplex on $\{i:x\in\overline{E_i}\}$. Now it is not hard to check that the inverse limit of these correspondences maps bijectively (and thus homeomorphically) to $\varprojlim_{X=\bigsqcup_{i=1}^nE_i}N(X;\{\overline{E_i}\})$, thus giving rise to the desired map \eqref{chogoshvilinervecomparison}. Now the inverse image of $p\in X$ under \eqref{chogoshvilinervecomparison} is an inverse limit of complete simplices with surjective transition maps (``the complete simplex on a profinite set''), and this has the \v Cech cohomology of a point. Indeed, for any inverse system of compact spaces $\{X_\alpha\}$, the natural map $\varinjlim_\alpha\check H^\bullet(X_\alpha)\to\check H^\bullet(\varprojlim_\alpha X_\alpha)$ is an isomorphism (since open covers of $\varprojlim_\alpha X_\alpha$ pulled back from some $X_\alpha$ are cofinal among all open covers). Thus it follows from the Leray spectral sequence that \eqref{chogoshvilinervecomparison} induces an isomorphism on \v Cech cohomology.
nodes.statement_short: Build the map from a correspondence; its fibers are complete simplices on profinite sets with trivial Čech cohomology, so Leray's spectral sequence gives the isomorphism.

nodes.name: Steenrod chains and homology
nodes.statement: Let $X$ be compact. We define: \begin{equation} \overline C_\bullet(X):=\mathop{R\varprojlim}_{X=\bigsqcup_{i=1}^nE_i}\bigoplus_{p\geq 0}\bigoplus_{\begin{smallmatrix}S\subseteq\{1,\ldots,n\}\cr\left|S\right|=p+1\cr\bigcap_{i\in S}\overline{E_i}\ne\varnothing\end{smallmatrix}}\mathbb Z[-p] \end{equation} For a map $f:X\to Y$, there is an induced pushforward map $f_\ast:\overline C_\bullet(X)\to\overline C_\bullet(Y)$. We denote by $\overline H_\bullet(X;\mathcal F)$ the homology of $\overline C_\bullet(X;\mathcal F)$, and we define relative homology $\overline H_\bullet(X,Y;\mathcal F)$ as the homology of the relevant mapping cone. More generally, let $\mathcal F$ be a locally constant sheaf of abelian groups on $X$. Fix a partition $X=\bigsqcup_{i=1}^nE_i^0$ and trivializations of $\mathcal F|_{\overline{E_i^0}}$. This gives rise to a local system $\mathcal F$ on $N(\{\overline{E_i}\}_{i=1}^n)$ for any partition $\{E_i\}$ refining $\{E_i^0\}$. We now define $\overline C_\bullet(X;\mathcal F)$ as in \eqref{steenrodchainsRlimeqn}, restricted to partitions refining $\{E_i^0\}$ and using the coefficient system on the nerve induced by $\mathcal F$ and the fixed trivializations of $\mathcal F|_{\overline{E_i^0}}$. Since any two choices of trivializations of $\mathcal F|_{\overline{E_i}}$ become isomorphic (in the sense that that their sets of ``constant sections'' coincide) after pulling back to some common refinement, it follows that $\overline C_\bullet(X;\mathcal F)$ is well-defined up to essentially unique quasi-isomorphism (by Lemma \ref{cofinalityforRlim}). For a map $f:X\to Y$ and $\mathcal F\to f^\ast\mathcal G$, there is a pushforward map $\overline C_\bullet(X;\mathcal F)\to\overline C_\bullet(Y;\mathcal G)$.
nodes.statement_short: Steenrod chains as the derived inverse limit over partitions of simplicial chains on nerves, with local-system coefficients, pushforwards and relative versions.
nodes.label: steenrodhomdef

nodes.name: Steenrod chains as derived inverse limit
nodes.statement: \overline C_\bullet(X):=\mathop{R\varprojlim}_{X=\bigsqcup_{i=1}^nE_i}\bigoplus_{p\geq 0}\bigoplus_{\begin{smallmatrix}S\subseteq\{1,\ldots,n\}\cr\left|S\right|=p+1\cr\bigcap_{i\in S}\overline{E_i}\ne\varnothing\end{smallmatrix}}\mathbb Z[-p]
nodes.label: steenrodchainsRlimeqn

nodes.name: Agreement with Mardešić's Steenrod (strong) homology
nodes.statement: Although not logically necessary for our purposes, we now argue that Steenrod homology as given in Definition \ref{steenrodhomdef} coincides with the definition from Marde\v si\'c \cite{mardesic} (at least for constant coefficient systems).
conclusions: Steenrod homology as given in Definition \ref{steenrodhomdef} coincides with the definition from Marde\v si\'c \cite{mardesic} (at least for constant coefficient systems)

nodes.name: Argument for agreement with Mardešić
nodes.statement: First of all, note that (a special case of) Marde\v si\'c's definition of strong homology is that if a compact space $X$ is an inverse limit of compact polyhedra $X_\alpha$ over a cofinite index set, then: \begin{equation} \overline H_\bullet(X)=H_\bullet\mathop{R\varprojlim}_\alpha C_\bullet(X_\alpha) \end{equation} (see \cite[p379, \S19.1]{mardesic}, and note that such an inverse system is a ``cofinite polyhedral resolution'' of its inverse limit \cite[p103, \S6]{mardesic}). In particular, $\overline C_\bullet(X)$ as defined in \eqref{steenrodchainsRlimeqn} computes the Steenrod homology of $\varprojlim_{X=\bigsqcup_{i=1}^nE_i}N(X;\{\overline{E_i}\})$ (using the morphism of inverse systems $C_\bullet^\mathrm{simp}(N(X;\{\overline{E_i}\}))\to C_\bullet^\mathrm{sing}(N(X;\{\overline{E_i}\}))$ given by barycentric subdivision, which is a level-wise quasi-isomorphism and thus induces a quasi-isomorphism on derived inverse limits by Lemma \ref{quasiisomorphismforRlim}). Finally, note that the map \eqref{chogoshvilinervecomparison} induces an isomorphism on strong homology by Lemma \ref{inverselimithassamecech} and \cite[p446, Theorem 21.15]{mardesic}.
nodes.statement_short: Use Mardešić's polyhedral-resolution description of strong homology, barycentric subdivision with level-wise quasi-isomorphism invariance of R lim, and the nerve comparison lemma.

nodes.name: Strong homology via polyhedral resolutions
nodes.statement: \overline H_\bullet(X)=H_\bullet\mathop{R\varprojlim}_\alpha C_\bullet(X_\alpha)

nodes.name: Steenrod homology is the derived dual of Čech cohomology
nodes.statement: Let $\mathcal F$ be a locally constant sheaf whose stalks are finitely generated free $R$-modules, and let $M$ be an $R$-module. Then there is a natural isomorphism: \begin{equation} \overline C_\bullet(X;\operatorname{Hom}(\mathcal F,M))=R\operatorname{Hom}_{D(R)}(\check C^\bullet(X;\mathcal F),M) \end{equation} in the derived category $D(R)$. The same holds for relative (co)chains of a closed subspace $Y\subseteq X$, and the isomorphisms are compatible with the relevant exact triangles relating $Y$, $X$ and $(X,Y)$.
nodes.statement_short: Steenrod chains with Hom(F,M) coefficients are RHom of Čech cochains of F into M, naturally and compatibly with relative triangles.
assumptions: Let $\mathcal F$ be a locally constant sheaf whose stalks are finitely generated free $R$-modules, and let $M$ be an $R$-module.
conclusions: Then there is a natural isomorphism:
The same holds for relative (co)chains of a closed subspace $Y\subseteq X$, and the isomorphisms are compatible with the relevant exact triangles relating $Y$, $X$ and $(X,Y)$.
nodes.label: steenrodisderiveddualofcech

nodes.name: Steenrod–Čech duality isomorphism
nodes.statement: \overline C_\bullet(X;\operatorname{Hom}(\mathcal F,M))=R\operatorname{Hom}_{D(R)}(\check C^\bullet(X;\mathcal F),M)
nodes.label: strongcechdualiso

nodes.name: Comparison with Milnor and Mardešić
nodes.statement: This result is very similar to Milnor \cite[p92, Definition, Lemma 5]{milnor} and Marde\v si\'c \cite[p446, Theorem 21.15]{mardesic}. Note also that morally, the above result should be thought of as following trivially from some derived universal property of the form $\mathop{R\varprojlim} R\operatorname{Hom}(A_\alpha^\bullet,B^\bullet)=R\operatorname{Hom}(\varinjlim A_\alpha^\bullet,B^\bullet)$ (hopefully this provides some motivation for the proof below).
nodes.statement_short: The lemma parallels Milnor and Mardešić and morally follows from a derived universal property of R lim and RHom.

nodes.name: Proof
nodes.statement: Let us relate $\check C^\bullet(X;\mathcal F)$ as defined using rigid open covers to a version using partitions. Specifically, we consider the following quasi-isomorphisms: \begin{align} \check C^\bullet(X;\mathcal F)=\varinjlim_{\begin{smallmatrix}\{U_x\subseteq X\}_{x\in X}\cr\text{rigid open cover}\end{smallmatrix}}&\bigoplus_{p\geq 0}\prod_{\begin{smallmatrix}S\subseteq X\cr\left|S\right|=p+1\end{smallmatrix}}\mathcal F\Bigl(\bigcap_{x\in S}U_x\Bigr)[-p]\\ &\quad\uparrow\cr \varinjlim_{\begin{smallmatrix}X=\bigsqcup_{i=1}^nE_i\cr\overline{E_i}\subseteq U_i\end{smallmatrix}}&\bigoplus_{p\geq 0}\prod_{\begin{smallmatrix}S\subseteq\{1,\ldots,n\}\cr\left|S\right|=p+1\end{smallmatrix}}\mathcal F\Bigl(\bigcap_{i\in S}U_i\Bigr)[-p]\\ &\quad\downarrow\cr \varinjlim_{X=\bigsqcup_{i=1}^nE_i}&\bigoplus_{p\geq 0}\prod_{\begin{smallmatrix}S\subseteq\{1,\ldots,n\}\cr\left|S\right|=p+1\end{smallmatrix}}\mathcal F\Bigl(\bigcap_{i\in S}\overline{E_i}\Bigr)[-p]\\ &\quad\uparrow\cr \bigoplus_{q\geq 0}\bigoplus_{\{E_i^{(0)}\}_{i=1}^{n_0}<\cdots<\{E_i^{(q)}\}_{i=1}^{n_q}}&\bigoplus_{p\geq 0}\prod_{\begin{smallmatrix}S\subseteq\{1,\ldots,n_0\}\cr\left|S\right|=p+1\end{smallmatrix}}\mathcal F\Bigl(\bigcap_{i\in S}\overline{E_i^{(0)}}\Bigr)[q-p]\\ &\quad\uparrow\downarrow\cr \bigoplus_{q\geq 0}\bigoplus_{\{E_i^{(0)}\}_{i=1}^{n_0}\leq\cdots\leq\{E_i^{(q)}\}_{i=1}^{n_q}}&\bigoplus_{p\geq 0}\prod_{\begin{smallmatrix}S\subseteq\{1,\ldots,n_0\}\cr\left|S\right|=p+1\end{smallmatrix}}\mathcal F\Bigl(\bigcap_{i\in S}\overline{E_i^{(0)}}\Bigr)[q-p] \end{align} The first map is induced by associating to a partition $\{E_i\}$ and $\overline{E_i}\subseteq U_i$ the rigid open cover assigning $U_i$ to $x\in E_i$, and pulling back along the induced map on nerves; it can be seen to be a quasi-isomorphism by a filtration argument (basically the Leray spectral sequence). The second map is a quasi-isomorphism by Lemma \ref{intersectioncofinal} and the definition of $\alpha^\ast$. The third map is defined as the tautological map on $q=0$ direct summands and zero for $q>0$; it can be seen to be a quasi-isomorphism by expressing the domain (resp.\ codomain) as the direct limit over partitions $\{E_i\}$ of the corresponding complex (resp.\ direct limit) restricted to partitions refined by $\{E_i\}$ and observing that for any fixed $\{E_i\}$ the map is a quasi-isomorphism by Lemma \ref{comboretraction}. Finally, the last pair of maps consists of the natural inclusion ($\downarrow$) and the retraction annihilating any component with $\{E_i^{(j)}\}_{i=1}^{n_j}=\{E_i^{(j+1)}\}_{i=1}^{n_{j+1}}$ for some $j$ ($\uparrow$); one can see that both are quasi-isomorphisms by filtering by $\{E_i\}$ (as before) and then by the number of distinct $\{E_i^{(j)}\}_{i=1}^{n_j}$. For any partition $\{E_i\}$ of $X$ and collection of trivializations of $\mathcal F|_{\overline E_i}$, there is a sub-$\mathcal K$-presheaf $\mathcal F^\mathrm{pre}\subseteq\mathcal F$ whose sections over $K$ are those sections of $\mathcal F$ whose restrictions to $K\cap\overline{E_i}$ are constant with respect to the specified trivializations. The complex \eqref{cechbychogoshvili} calculates \v Cech cohomology \eqref{cechcomplexII} by a cofinality argument, and the inclusion $\mathcal F^\mathrm{pre}\to\mathcal F$ induces an isomorphism on stalks and thus on \v Cech cohomology by Lemma \ref{cechdeterminedbystalks}. The third map above remains a quasi-isomorphism for $\mathcal F^\mathrm{pre}$ (for the same reason), and furthermore we may restrict \eqref{almosthomotopycolimitofchogoshvilicoverstodualize} to partitions refining the fixed $\{E_i\}$ by Lemma \ref{cofinalityforRlim}. The conclusion of the above discussion is that we have thus constructed a canonical (and functorial) quasi-isomorphism between $\check C^\bullet(X;\mathcal F)$ and: \begin{equation} \bigoplus_{q\geq 0}\bigoplus_{\{E_i\}\leq\{E_i^{(0)}\}_{i=1}^{n_0}\leq\cdots\leq\{E_i^{(q)}\}_{i=1}^{n_q}}\bigoplus_{p\geq 0}\prod_{\begin{smallmatrix}S\subseteq\{1,\ldots,n_0\}\cr\left|S\right|=p+1\end{smallmatrix}}\mathcal F^\mathrm{pre}\Bigl(\bigcap_{i\in S}\overline{E_i^{(0)}}\Bigr)[q-p] \end{equation} (for any fixed partition $\{E_i\}$ and trivializations of $\mathcal F|_{\overline{E_i}}$ giving rise to $\mathcal F^\mathrm{pre}\subseteq\mathcal F$). Note that $\overline C_\bullet(X,\operatorname{Hom}(\mathcal F,M))$ is precisely $\operatorname{Hom}(\eqref{homotopycolimitofchogoshvilicoverstodualize},M)$. Thus it suffices to show that this particular $\operatorname{Hom}$ is in fact the $R\operatorname{Hom}$. Recall that $R\operatorname{Hom}$ in $D(R)$ may be computed using a K-projective resolution of the first argument (see Spaltenstein \cite{spaltenstein}), where a complex $P^\bullet$ is called K-projective iff $\operatorname{Hom}^\bullet(P^\bullet,M^\bullet)$ is acyclic for every acyclic complex $M^\bullet$ (note that a bounded above complex of projective modules is K-projective). Thus it suffices to show that \eqref{homotopycolimitofchogoshvilicoverstodualize} is K-projective. We consider subsets $\wp$ of the poset of partitions of $X$ with the property that any partition refined by a partition in $\wp$ also lies in $\wp$. Since the poset of partitions is cofinite, we may use Zorn's lemma to choose a directed system $\{\wp_i\}_{i\in I}$ of such collections, indexed by a well-ordered set $I$, with the following properties: \begin{rlist} \item$\wp_0=\varnothing$, where $0\in I$ is the least element. \item$\left|\wp_i\setminus\wp_{i-1}\right|=1$ if $i\in I$ has a predecessor $i-1$. \item$\wp_i=\bigcup_{i'<i}\wp_{i'}$ if $i\in I$ has no predecessor. \end{rlist} Now for $i\in I$, let $\eqref{homotopycolimitofchogoshvilicoverstodualize}_i\subseteq\eqref{homotopycolimitofchogoshvilicoverstodualize}$ denote the subcomplex generated by restricting to partitions in $\wp_i$. It follows that: \begin{rlist} \item$\eqref{homotopycolimitofchogoshvilicoverstodualize}_0=0$, where $0\in I$ is the least element. \item$\eqref{homotopycolimitofchogoshvilicoverstodualize}_{i-1}\to\eqref{homotopycolimitofchogoshvilicoverstodualize}_i$ is injective and component-wise split with K-projective cokernel if $i\in I$ has a predecessor $i-1$ (this holds since the cokernel is a bounded above complex of free modules). \item$\varinjlim_{i'<i}\eqref{homotopycolimitofchogoshvilicoverstodualize}_{i'}\to\eqref{homotopycolimitofchogoshvilicoverstodualize}_i$ is an isomorphism if $i\in I$ has no predecessor. \end{rlist} It follows that $\eqref{homotopycolimitofchogoshvilicoverstodualize}=\varinjlim_i\eqref{homotopycolimitofchogoshvilicoverstodualize}_i$ is K-projective by Spaltenstein \cite[p131, 2.8 Corollary]{spaltenstein}. Since the construction of the isomorphism \eqref{strongcechdualiso} was given by a functorial chain-level construction, it can be checked that it is natural, applies in the relative case, and is compatibile with exact triangles.
nodes.statement_short: Replace Čech cochains by a quasi-isomorphic chain-level hocolim over partitions whose Hom into M is Steenrod chains. Show this complex is K-projective via a Zorn's-lemma transfinite filtration and Spaltenstein's criterion.

nodes.name: Zigzag from rigid-cover to partition Čech complexes
nodes.statement: \check C^\bullet(X;\mathcal F)=\varinjlim_{\begin{smallmatrix}\{U_x\subseteq X\}_{x\in X}\cr\text{rigid open cover}\end{smallmatrix}}&\bigoplus_{p\geq 0}\prod_{\begin{smallmatrix}S\subseteq X\cr\left|S\right|=p+1\end{smallmatrix}}\mathcal F\Bigl(\bigcap_{x\in S}U_x\Bigr)[-p]\\ &\quad\uparrow\cr \varinjlim_{\begin{smallmatrix}X=\bigsqcup_{i=1}^nE_i\cr\overline{E_i}\subseteq U_i\end{smallmatrix}}&\bigoplus_{p\geq 0}\prod_{\begin{smallmatrix}S\subseteq\{1,\ldots,n\}\cr\left|S\right|=p+1\end{smallmatrix}}\mathcal F\Bigl(\bigcap_{i\in S}U_i\Bigr)[-p]\\ &\quad\downarrow\cr \varinjlim_{X=\bigsqcup_{i=1}^nE_i}&\bigoplus_{p\geq 0}\prod_{\begin{smallmatrix}S\subseteq\{1,\ldots,n\}\cr\left|S\right|=p+1\end{smallmatrix}}\mathcal F\Bigl(\bigcap_{i\in S}\overline{E_i}\Bigr)[-p]\\ &\quad\uparrow\cr \bigoplus_{q\geq 0}\bigoplus_{\{E_i^{(0)}\}_{i=1}^{n_0}<\cdots<\{E_i^{(q)}\}_{i=1}^{n_q}}&\bigoplus_{p\geq 0}\prod_{\begin{smallmatrix}S\subseteq\{1,\ldots,n_0\}\cr\left|S\right|=p+1\end{smallmatrix}}\mathcal F\Bigl(\bigcap_{i\in S}\overline{E_i^{(0)}}\Bigr)[q-p]\\ &\quad\uparrow\downarrow\cr \bigoplus_{q\geq 0}\bigoplus_{\{E_i^{(0)}\}_{i=1}^{n_0}\leq\cdots\leq\{E_i^{(q)}\}_{i=1}^{n_q}}&\bigoplus_{p\geq 0}\prod_{\begin{smallmatrix}S\subseteq\{1,\ldots,n_0\}\cr\left|S\right|=p+1\end{smallmatrix}}\mathcal F\Bigl(\bigcap_{i\in S}\overline{E_i^{(0)}}\Bigr)[q-p]
nodes.label: cechbychogoshvili

nodes.name: Partition hocolim complex to dualize
nodes.statement: \bigoplus_{q\geq 0}\bigoplus_{\{E_i\}\leq\{E_i^{(0)}\}_{i=1}^{n_0}\leq\cdots\leq\{E_i^{(q)}\}_{i=1}^{n_q}}\bigoplus_{p\geq 0}\prod_{\begin{smallmatrix}S\subseteq\{1,\ldots,n_0\}\cr\left|S\right|=p+1\end{smallmatrix}}\mathcal F^\mathrm{pre}\Bigl(\bigcap_{i\in S}\overline{E_i^{(0)}}\Bigr)[q-p]
nodes.label: homotopycolimitofchogoshvilicoverstodualize

nodes.name: Almost complex manifold (X,J)
nodes.statement: Fix a smooth almost complex manifold: \begin{equation} (X,J) \end{equation}

nodes.name: Almost complex manifold (X,J)
nodes.statement: (X,J)

nodes.name: Codimension two submanifolds D, D_i
nodes.statement: Fix codimension two submanifolds with boundary: \begin{equation} D,D_1,\ldots,D_r\subseteq X \end{equation} (let $D^\circ:=D\setminus\partial D$, and similarly for $D_i$).

nodes.name: Divisors D, D_1,...,D_r
nodes.statement: D,D_1,\ldots,D_r\subseteq X

nodes.name: Etale chart of Deligne-Mumford space
nodes.statement: Fix a smooth manifold $\overline{\mathcal M}$ equipped with a smooth \'etale map $\overline{\mathcal M}\to\overline{\mathcal M}_{g,n+\ell}$\footnote{We give $\overline{\mathcal M}_{g,n+\ell}$ the standard smooth structure from its structure as a complex analytic orbifold. Every point in a smooth orbifold $M$ is in the image of a smooth \'etale map $M'\to M$. Indeed, $M$ is covered by open sets each diffeomorphic to $\mathbb R^n/G$ for some finite group $G\to GL_n(\mathbb R)$, and the map $\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R^n/G\hookrightarrow M$ is smooth \'etale.} (in the orbifold sense).

nodes.name: Family of curves over the chart
nodes.statement: Denote by $\overline{\mathcal C}_{g,n+\ell}\to\overline{\mathcal M}_{g,n+\ell}$ the universal family, and define a family of curves $\overline{\mathcal C}\to\overline{\mathcal M}$ via the following pullback square: \begin{equation} \begin{CD} \overline{\mathcal C}@>>>\overline{\mathcal C}_{g,n+\ell}\cr @VVV@VVV\cr \overline{\mathcal M}@>>>\overline{\mathcal M}_{g,n+\ell} \end{CD} \end{equation}

nodes.name: Pullback square defining the family of curves
nodes.statement: \begin{CD} \overline{\mathcal C}@>>>\overline{\mathcal C}_{g,n+\ell}\cr @VVV@VVV\cr \overline{\mathcal M}@>>>\overline{\mathcal M}_{g,n+\ell} \end{CD}

nodes.name: Smooth locus of the family
nodes.statement: Let $\overline{\mathcal C}^\circ\subseteq\overline{\mathcal C}$ denote the open subset where the fiber is smooth.

nodes.name: Obstruction space E and perturbation map lambda
nodes.statement: Fix a finite dimensional vector space $E$ and a linear map: \begin{equation} \lambda:E\to C^\infty(\overbrace{\overline{\mathcal C}^\circ\underset\overline{\mathcal M}\times\cdots\underset\overline{\mathcal M}\times\overline{\mathcal C}^\circ}^{r\text{ times}}{}\underset\overline{\mathcal M}\times\overline{\mathcal C}^\circ\times X,\Omega^{0,1}_{\overline{\mathcal C}^\circ/\overline{\mathcal M}}\otimes_\mathbb C TX) \end{equation} Here $\Omega^{0,1}_{\overline{\mathcal C}^\circ/\overline{\mathcal M}}$ is the $(0,1)$-part of the complexified vertical cotangent bundle $T^\ast_{\overline{\mathcal C}^\circ/\overline{\mathcal M}}\otimes_\mathbb R\mathbb C$ of (the last factor of) $\overline{\mathcal C}^\circ\to\overline{\mathcal M}$, and $C^\infty$ means smooth sections. We require that $\lambda$ be zero in a neighborhood of the nodes $\overline{\mathcal C}\setminus\overline{\mathcal C}^\circ$ of the last $\overline{\mathcal C}^\circ$ factor.
nodes.statement_short: A linear map $\lambda$ from a finite-dimensional space $E$ to (0,1)-forms on the universal curve, depending on r auxiliary points, vanishing near nodes.

nodes.name: Perturbation map lambda
nodes.statement: \lambda:E\to C^\infty(\overbrace{\overline{\mathcal C}^\circ\underset\overline{\mathcal M}\times\cdots\underset\overline{\mathcal M}\times\overline{\mathcal C}^\circ}^{r\text{ times}}{}\underset\overline{\mathcal M}\times\overline{\mathcal C}^\circ\times X,\Omega^{0,1}_{\overline{\mathcal C}^\circ/\overline{\mathcal M}}\otimes_\mathbb C TX)
nodes.label: lambdafix

nodes.name: Normalization of a nodal curve
nodes.statement: For a nodal curve $C$, we denote by $\tilde C$ its normalization, i.e.\ the unique smooth compact Riemann surface equipped with a map $\tilde C\to C$ which identifies points in pairs to form the nodes of $C$.
nodes.genus: the unique smooth compact Riemann surface equipped with a map $\tilde C\to C$
differentia: which identifies points in pairs to form the nodes of $C$

nodes.name: Homology class beta
nodes.statement: Fix a homology class $\beta\in H_2(X;\mathbb Z)$.

nodes.name: Thickened moduli space M(X)
nodes.statement: We are interested in the following moduli space: \begin{equation} \overline{\mathcal M}(X):=\left\{\begin{matrix}s\in\overline{\mathcal M}\hfill\cr u:C_s\to X\hfill\cr x_i\in C_s\quad 1\leq i\leq r\hfill\cr e\in E\hfill\end{matrix}\;\middle|\;\begin{matrix}u\text{ smooth and }u_\ast[C_s]=\beta\hfill\cr u(p_{n+i})\in D^\circ\quad\hfill(1\leq i\leq\ell)\cr u(x_i)\in D_i^\circ\text{ and }u\pitchfork D_i\text{ at }x_i\quad\hfill(1\leq i\leq r)\cr\bar\partial u+\lambda(e)(x_1,\ldots,x_r,\cdot,u(\cdot))=0\hfill\end{matrix}\right\} \end{equation} We let $C_s$ denote the fiber of $\overline{\mathcal C}\to\overline{\mathcal M}$ over $s$, with marked points $p_1,\ldots,p_{n+\ell}\in C_s$. Here $u\pitchfork D_i$ at $x_i$ means (by definition) that $x_i$ is not a node of $C_s$ and the map $T_{x_i}C_s\oplus T_{u(x_i)}D_i\xrightarrow{du\oplus\operatorname{id}}T_{u(x_i)}X$ is surjective. Now $\lambda(e)(x_1,\ldots,x_r,\cdot,u(\cdot))$ is a smooth section of $\Omega^{0,1}_{\tilde C_s}\otimes_\mathbb C u^\ast TX$ over $C_s$ supported away from the nodes; hence the last equation makes sense. We give $\overline{\mathcal M}(X)$ the topology of uniform convergence (i.e.\ using the Hausdorff distance between graphs $\subseteq\overline{\mathcal C}\times X$ to compare maps $u$).
nodes.statement_short: M(X) consists of maps u from fibers C_s with intersection points x_i on D_i and e in E solving the perturbed Cauchy-Riemann equation, with the C^0 topology.

nodes.name: Moduli space M(X)
nodes.statement: \overline{\mathcal M}(X):=\left\{\begin{matrix}s\in\overline{\mathcal M}\hfill\cr u:C_s\to X\hfill\cr x_i\in C_s\quad 1\leq i\leq r\hfill\cr e\in E\hfill\end{matrix}\;\middle|\;\begin{matrix}u\text{ smooth and }u_\ast[C_s]=\beta\hfill\cr u(p_{n+i})\in D^\circ\quad\hfill(1\leq i\leq\ell)\cr u(x_i)\in D_i^\circ\text{ and }u\pitchfork D_i\text{ at }x_i\quad\hfill(1\leq i\leq r)\cr\bar\partial u+\lambda(e)(x_1,\ldots,x_r,\cdot,u(\cdot))=0\hfill\end{matrix}\right\}
nodes.label: Mbarfirstdef

nodes.name: Subspace E'
nodes.statement: Fix a subspace $E'\subseteq E$.

nodes.name: E'-regular locus
nodes.statement: Let us now define the ``$E'$-regular locus'' $\overline{\mathcal M}(X)^\mathrm{reg}\subseteq\overline{\mathcal M}(X)$ (which for simplicity we will just call the ``regular locus''). Fix $(s_0,u_0,\{x_i^0\},e_0)\in\overline{\mathcal M}(X)$; we will describe when $(s_0,u_0,\{x_i^0\},e_0)\in\overline{\mathcal M}(X)^\mathrm{reg}$. We consider the smooth Banach manifold: \begin{equation} \mathcal B:=\Bigl\{(u,e)\in W^{k,p}(C_{s_0},X)\times E\Bigm|u(p_{n+i})\in D^\circ\;(1\leq i\leq\ell)\Bigr\} \end{equation} Over $\mathcal B$, we consider the smooth Banach bundle $\mathcal E$ whose fiber over a map $u:C_{s_0}\to X$ is $W^{k-1,p}(\tilde C_{s_0},\Omega^{0,1}_{\tilde C_{s_0}}\otimes_\mathbb C u^\ast TX)\oplus E/E'$. Now suppose $k$ is large; then there are unique continuous functions: \begin{equation} x_i:\mathcal B\to C_{s_0}\quad(1\leq i\leq r) \end{equation} defined in a neighborhood of $(u_0,e_0)\in\mathcal B$, which coincide with $x_i^0$ at $(u_0,e_0)$, and for which $u(x_i(u))\in D_i^\circ$. Moreover, \eqref{intersectionsfunction} are ``highly differentiable'', by which we mean that for all $\ell<\infty$, the function \eqref{intersectionsfunction} is of class $C^\ell$ provided $k\geq k_0(\ell)$. In the present situation, we can of course be more precise: $x_i$ is $C^\ell$ as a function of $u\in C^\ell$ (by the implicit function theorem), so \eqref{intersectionsfunction} is $C^\ell$ as long as $W^{k,p}\hookrightarrow C^\ell$ (which holds iff $(k-\ell)p>2$). It follows that: \begin{equation} (u,e)\mapsto\left[\bar\partial u+\lambda(e)(x_1,\ldots,x_r,\cdot,u(\cdot))\right]\oplus e \end{equation} is a highly differentiable section of $\mathcal E$ over $\mathcal B$ (the only nonsmoothness comes from how the $x_i$'s depend on $u$). Assume $1<p<\infty$. We say $(s_0,u_0,\{x_i^0\},e_0)\in\overline{\mathcal M}(X)^\mathrm{reg}$ iff \eqref{firstdelbarsection} is transverse to the zero section at $(u_0,e_0)$.
nodes.statement_short: A point of M(X) is regular iff the thickened del-bar section on the Banach manifold B, valued in the bundle E (with E/E' factor), is transverse to zero.

nodes.name: Banach manifold B
nodes.statement: \mathcal B:=\Bigl\{(u,e)\in W^{k,p}(C_{s_0},X)\times E\Bigm|u(p_{n+i})\in D^\circ\;(1\leq i\leq\ell)\Bigr\}

nodes.name: Intersection point functions x_i
nodes.statement: x_i:\mathcal B\to C_{s_0}\quad(1\leq i\leq r)
nodes.label: intersectionsfunction

nodes.name: Thickened del-bar section
nodes.statement: (u,e)\mapsto\left[\bar\partial u+\lambda(e)(x_1,\ldots,x_r,\cdot,u(\cdot))\right]\oplus e
nodes.label: firstdelbarsection

nodes.name: Regularity independent of Sobolev exponents
nodes.statement: It is an easy exercise using elliptic regularity to see that this notion is independent of $(k,p)$ (as long as $k$ is sufficiently large so that the condition makes sense).

nodes.name: Orientation module of a vector space
nodes.statement: For a vector space $E$, let $\mathfrak o_E$ denote its orientation module (canonically $H_{\dim E}(E,E\setminus 0;\mathbb Z)$).

nodes.name: Gluing theorem for the thickened moduli space M(X)
nodes.statement: In the above setup (from the beginning of \S\ref{setupforgluing} until here), we have: \begin{rlist} \item$\overline{\mathcal M}(X)^\mathrm{reg}\subseteq\overline{\mathcal M}(X)$ is open. \item$\overline{\mathcal M}(X)^\mathrm{reg}$ is a topological manifold of dimension $\dim\overline{\mathcal M}_{g,n+\ell}+(1-g)\dim X+2\langle c_1(X),\beta\rangle+\dim E-2\ell$. \itemThe projection $\overline{\mathcal M}(X)^\mathrm{reg}\to E/E'$ is a topological submersion, i.e.\ locally modeled on a projection $\mathbb R^n\times\mathbb R^m\to\mathbb R^n$. \itemThe orientation sheaf $\mathfrak o_{\overline{\mathcal M}(X)^\mathrm{reg}}$ is canonically isomorphic to $\mathfrak o_E\otimes\bigotimes_{i=1}^\ell\mathfrak o_{u(p_{n+i})^\ast N_{D/X}}^\vee$. \end{rlist}
nodes.statement_short: The regular locus of M(X) is open, is a topological manifold of the expected dimension, submerses onto E/E', and has canonically trivialized orientation sheaf.
assumptions: In the above setup (from the beginning of \S\ref{setupforgluing} until here)
conclusions: $\overline{\mathcal M}(X)^\mathrm{reg}\subseteq\overline{\mathcal M}(X)$ is open.
$\overline{\mathcal M}(X)^\mathrm{reg}$ is a topological manifold of dimension $\dim\overline{\mathcal M}_{g,n+\ell}+(1-g)\dim X+2\langle c_1(X),\beta\rangle+\dim E-2\ell$.
The projection $\overline{\mathcal M}(X)^\mathrm{reg}\to E/E'$ is a topological submersion, i.e.\ locally modeled on a projection $\mathbb R^n\times\mathbb R^m\to\mathbb R^n$.
The orientation sheaf $\mathfrak o_{\overline{\mathcal M}(X)^\mathrm{reg}}$ is canonically isomorphic to $\mathfrak o_E\otimes\bigotimes_{i=1}^\ell\mathfrak o_{u(p_{n+i})^\ast N_{D/X}}^\vee$.
nodes.label: mainresult

nodes.name: Openness of the regular locus
nodes.statement: $\overline{\mathcal M}(X)^\mathrm{reg}\subseteq\overline{\mathcal M}(X)$ is open.

nodes.name: Regular locus is a topological manifold
nodes.statement: $\overline{\mathcal M}(X)^\mathrm{reg}$ is a topological manifold of dimension $\dim\overline{\mathcal M}_{g,n+\ell}+(1-g)\dim X+2\langle c_1(X),\beta\rangle+\dim E-2\ell$.

nodes.name: Submersion onto E/E'
nodes.statement: The projection $\overline{\mathcal M}(X)^\mathrm{reg}\to E/E'$ is a topological submersion, i.e.\ locally modeled on a projection $\mathbb R^n\times\mathbb R^m\to\mathbb R^n$.

nodes.name: Orientation sheaf of the regular locus
nodes.statement: The orientation sheaf $\mathfrak o_{\overline{\mathcal M}(X)^\mathrm{reg}}$ is canonically isomorphic to $\mathfrak o_E\otimes\bigotimes_{i=1}^\ell\mathfrak o_{u(p_{n+i})^\ast N_{D/X}}^\vee$.

nodes.name: Proof of Proposition 9.2.9 from Theorem B.1.1
nodes.statement: Let us now explain how Theorem \ref{mainresult} implies Proposition \ref{GWgluingneeded}. Proposition \ref{GWgluingneeded} is a local statement, so let us prove it in a neighborhood of a specific point $(C,u,\{\phi_\alpha\}_{\alpha\in I},\{e_\alpha\}_{\alpha\in I})\in\overline{\mathcal M}^\beta_{g,n}(X)_I^\mathrm{reg}$. We will construct data $(X,J,D,D_1,\ldots,D_r,\overline{\mathcal M},E,\lambda,E')$ as in the above setup and a point $(s,u,\{x_i\},e)\in\overline{\mathcal M}(X)$. It will be clear from the construction that there is a natural homeomorphism between a small neighborhood of this point in $\overline{\mathcal M}(X)$ and a small neighborhood of the given point in $\overline{\mathcal M}_{g,n}^\beta(X)_I$, and using this we will infer Proposition \ref{GWgluingneeded} from Theorem \ref{mainresult}. We claim that every unstable irreducible component of $C$ has a point where $du$ is injective. If $I=\varnothing$, this follows from the domain stabilization step Lemma \ref{everythingcanbethickened}, and if $I\ne\varnothing$, then picking any $\alpha\in I$, this follows from the fact that $u\pitchfork D_\alpha$ and adding the intersections as marked points makes $C$ stable. It follows from the claim that we may pick $D\subseteq X$ with $u\pitchfork D$ such that adding these intersections as extra marked points makes $C$ stable, and none of these points are nodes or marked points. We take $\ell$ to be the \emph{minimum} number of points in $u^{-1}(D)$ necessary to stabilize $C$, and we fix an ordered $\ell$-tuple of such points, adding them as new marked points $p_{n+1},\ldots,p_{n+\ell}\in C$, so now $C$ is a curve of type $(g,n+\ell)$. Now we let $r=\sum_{\alpha\in I}r_\alpha$, we let $D_1,\ldots,D_r\subseteq X$ consist of $r_\alpha$ copies of $D_\alpha$ (union over $\alpha\in I$), and we let the $x_i$'s be the intersection points $u^{-1}(D_\alpha)$ (union over $\alpha\in I$). For the purposes of the present argument, let us reindex $\{x_i\}_{1\leq i\leq r}$ as $\{x^\alpha_i\}_{\alpha\in I,1\leq i\leq r_\alpha}$. Now since $C$ is a curve of type $(g,n+\ell)$, it corresponds to a point in $\overline{\mathcal M}_{g,n+\ell}$. Choose an \'etale map $\overline{\mathcal M}\to\overline{\mathcal M}_{g,n+\ell}$ covering this point, and choose a point $s\in\overline{\mathcal M}$ and an isomorphism $\iota:C\to C_s$. Now for every $\alpha\in I$, there is a unique map: \begin{equation} \tilde\phi_\alpha:\overbrace{\overline{\mathcal C}^\circ\underset\overline{\mathcal M}\times\cdots\underset\overline{\mathcal M}\times\overline{\mathcal C}^\circ}^{r_\alpha\text{ times}}{}\underset\overline{\mathcal M}\times\overline{\mathcal C}^\circ\to\overline{\mathcal C}_\alpha \end{equation} defined in a neighborhood of $\{x_1^\alpha\}\times\cdots\times\{x_{r_\alpha}^\alpha\}\times C_s$ so that $\tilde\phi_\alpha(x^\alpha_1,\ldots,x^\alpha_{r_\alpha},\iota(\cdot))=\phi_\alpha(\cdot)$ and $\tilde\phi_\alpha(y_1,\ldots,y_{r_\alpha},\cdot)$ classifies the curve in the last factor after forgetting the last $\ell$ marked points and adding $y_1,\ldots,y_{r_\alpha}$ as marked points (this follows from the fact that $\overline{\mathcal C}_\alpha\to\overline{\mathcal M}_{g,n+r_\alpha}/S_{r_\alpha}$ is \'etale). We let $E:=E_I=\bigoplus_{\alpha\in I}E_\alpha$, and we define: \begin{equation*} \lambda\biggl(\bigoplus_{\alpha\in I}e_\alpha\biggr)(\{y_i^\alpha\}_{\alpha\in I,1\leq i\leq r_\alpha},\cdot,\cdot)=\sum_{\alpha\in I}\lambda_\alpha(e_\alpha)(\tilde\phi_\alpha(y_1^\alpha,\ldots,y_{r_\alpha}^\alpha,\cdot),\cdot) \end{equation*} in a neighborhood of $\{x_i^\alpha\}_{\alpha\in I,1\leq i\leq r_\alpha}\times C_s\times X$ (and then we simply cut it off to be zero elsewhere). Finally, we observe that with this definition, a neighborhood of $(s,u\circ\iota^{-1},\{x^\alpha_i\}_{\alpha\in I,1\leq i\leq r_\alpha},\bigoplus_{\alpha\in I}e_\alpha)\in\overline{\mathcal M}(X)$ coincides with a neighborhood of $(C,u,\{\phi_\alpha\}_{\alpha\in I},\{e_\alpha\}_{\alpha\in I})\in\overline{\mathcal M}^\beta_{g,n}(X)_I$ (note that the point $(C,u,\{\phi_\alpha\}_{\alpha\in I},\{e_\alpha\}_{\alpha\in I})\in\overline{\mathcal M}^\beta_{g,n}(X)_I^\mathrm{reg}$ has trivial automorphism group by definition of $\overline{\mathcal M}^\beta_{g,n}(X)_I^\mathrm{reg}$). For $E'=E$, under this identification of a small open set in $\overline{\mathcal M}^\beta_{g,n}(X)_I$ and a small open set in $\overline{\mathcal M}(X)$, we have $\overline{\mathcal M}(X)^\mathrm{reg}\subseteq\overline{\mathcal M}^\beta_{g,n}(X)_I^\mathrm{reg}$ (for this it is important that we chose $\ell$ as the \emph{minimum} number of points necessary to stabilize $C$). It follows that Theorem \ref{mainresult}(\ref{openness},\ref{orientation}) implies Proposition \ref{GWgluingneeded}(\ref{GWgluingopen},\ref{GWgluingor}) (note that over this small open set, we have an identification $\mathfrak o_{u(p_{n+i})^\ast N_{D/X}}=\mathfrak o_{T_{p_{n+i}}C_s}$ and that the latter is canonically trivial using the complex structure on $C_s$). Taking the above construction with $J$ in place of $I$ and setting $E':=E_I\subseteq E_J=E$, we get Proposition \ref{GWgluingneeded}(\ref{GWgluingsubmersion}) from Theorem \ref{mainresult}(\ref{manifold},\ref{submersion}) as well.
nodes.statement_short: Reduction to the gluing theorem: stabilize the domain with a divisor D, encode the thickening data (E, lambda, D_i) in the setup of App. B, and identify neighborhoods.

nodes.name: Displayed equation in Section B.1
nodes.statement: \tilde\phi_\alpha:\overbrace{\overline{\mathcal C}^\circ\underset\overline{\mathcal M}\times\cdots\underset\overline{\mathcal M}\times\overline{\mathcal C}^\circ}^{r_\alpha\text{ times}}{}\underset\overline{\mathcal M}\times\overline{\mathcal C}^\circ\to\overline{\mathcal C}_\alpha

nodes.name: Central curve C_0 and number of nodes d
nodes.statement: Let $d$ be the number of nodes of $C_0:=C_{s_0}$.
nodes.section: B.2 Local model for resolution of a node

nodes.name: Cylindrical end
nodes.statement: On each side of each node of $C_0$, fix a ``cylindrical end'', that is, a map: \begin{equation} [0,\infty)\times S^1\to C_0 \end{equation} which is a biholomorphism onto some small neighborhood $D^2\setminus 0$ of the node.
nodes.section: B.2 Local model for resolution of a node

nodes.name: Cylindrical ends
nodes.statement: [0,\infty)\times S^1\to C_0
nodes.section: B.2 Local model for resolution of a node
nodes.label: cylindricalends

nodes.name: Locus of curves with d nodes
nodes.statement: Let $\overline{\mathcal M}^d\subseteq\overline{\mathcal M}$ denote the locus of curves with exactly $d$ nodes.
nodes.section: B.2 Local model for resolution of a node

nodes.name: Family of complex structures j_y
nodes.statement: Pick a smooth family of smooth almost complex structures $j_y$ on $C_0$ parameterized by $y\in\mathbb R^{\dim\overline{\mathcal M}^d}$, where $j_0$ is the given almost complex structure on $C_0$, which is constant over the cylindrical ends \eqref{cylindricalends}, and such that the induced map $\mathbb R^{\dim\overline{\mathcal M}^d}\to\overline{\mathcal M}^d$ is a diffeomorphism onto its image.
nodes.section: B.2 Local model for resolution of a node

nodes.name: Neck (gluing procedure)
nodes.statement: Now consider the following procedure, which takes a ``gluing parameter'' $\alpha=e^{-6S+i\theta}\in\mathbb C$ and two copies of the standard end $[0,\infty)\times S^1\sqcup[0,\infty)\times S^1$. We first truncate both ends, leaving just the subset $[0,6S]\times S^1\sqcup[0,6S]\times S^1$. We then identify $(s,t)$ in the first piece with $(6S-s,\theta-t)=(s',t')$ in the second piece. We call the resulting cylinder a ``neck''.
nodes.statement_short: Truncate two cylindrical ends at length 6S and identify them with a twist theta to form a neck, for gluing parameter alpha = e^{-6S+i theta}.
nodes.section: B.2 Local model for resolution of a node

nodes.name: Glued curve C_alpha
nodes.statement: Now given gluing parameters\footnote{In the present construction, and in many other constructions/definitions to come later, certain expressions, equalities, etc. only make sense or only hold if the gluing parameters $\alpha_i\in\mathbb C$ are sufficiently close to zero (i.e.\ $\left|\alpha_i\right|\leq\epsilon$ for some $\epsilon>0$ depending only on data which we have previously fixed). We will often leave this assumption implicit, since we only care about what happens for $\alpha$ in a neighborhood of $0\in\mathbb C^d$ anyway. The same goes for $y\in\mathbb R^{\dim\overline{\mathcal M}^d}$.} $\alpha=(\alpha_1,\ldots,\alpha_d)\in\mathbb C^d$, we may perform the gluing operation above on $C_0$, using the chosen cylindrical ends \eqref{cylindricalends}. We call the resulting curve $C_\alpha$, and it is equipped with cylindrical ends (corresponding to those $\alpha_i=0$) and necks (corresponding to those $\alpha_i\ne 0$): \begin{align} [0,\infty)\times S^1\to C_\alpha\\ [0,6S_i]\times S^1\to C_\alpha \end{align}
nodes.section: B.2 Local model for resolution of a node

nodes.name: Ends and necks of C_alpha
nodes.statement: [0,\infty)\times S^1\to C_\alpha\\ [0,6S_i]\times S^1\to C_\alpha
nodes.section: B.2 Local model for resolution of a node
nodes.label: Gend

nodes.name: Local coordinates on the chart near s_0
nodes.statement: Now since $\overline{\mathcal M}\to\overline{\mathcal M}_{g,n+\ell}$ is \'etale, there is an induced map: \begin{align} \mathbb C^d\times\mathbb R^{\dim\overline{\mathcal M}^d}&\to\overline{\mathcal M}\\ (\alpha,y)&\mapsto(C_\alpha,j_y,p_1,\ldots,p_{n+\ell}) \end{align} which is a local diffeomorphism near zero.
nodes.section: B.2 Local model for resolution of a node

nodes.name: Gluing coordinates (alpha,y) on the chart
nodes.statement: \mathbb C^d\times\mathbb R^{\dim\overline{\mathcal M}^d}&\to\overline{\mathcal M}\\ (\alpha,y)&\mapsto(C_\alpha,j_y,p_1,\ldots,p_{n+\ell})
nodes.section: B.2 Local model for resolution of a node

nodes.name: M(X) in gluing coordinates
nodes.statement: Using these local coordinates, we may alternatively define $\overline{\mathcal M}(X)$ as: \begin{equation} \overline{\mathcal M}(X):=\left\{\begin{matrix}\alpha\in\mathbb C^d\hfill\cr y\in\mathbb R^{\dim\overline{\mathcal M}^d}\hfill\cr u:C_\alpha\to X\hfill\cr x_i\in C_\alpha\quad 1\leq i\leq r\hfill\cr e\in E\hfill\end{matrix}\;\middle|\;\begin{matrix}u\text{ smooth and }u_\ast[C_\alpha]=\beta\hfill\cr u(p_{n+i})\in D^\circ\quad\hfill(1\leq i\leq\ell)\cr u(x_i)\in D_i^\circ\text{ and }u\pitchfork D_i\text{ at }x_i\quad\hfill(1\leq i\leq r)\cr\bar\partial_yu+\lambda(e)(\alpha,y,x_1,\ldots,x_r,\cdot,u(\cdot))=0\hfill\end{matrix}\right\} \end{equation} and this coincides with the definition \eqref{Mbarfirstdef} in a neighborhood of $(s_0,u_0,\{x_i^0\},e_0)=(0,0,u_0,\{x_i^0\},e_0)$. For the purposes of \eqref{modulispace}, $\lambda$ denotes the function: \begin{equation*} \lambda:E\to C^\infty(\mathbb C^d\times\mathbb R^{\dim\overline{\mathcal M}^d}\times\overbrace{C_0\times\cdots\times C_0}^{r\text{ times}}{}\times C_0\times X,\operatorname{Hom}_\mathbb R(T\tilde C_0,TX)) \end{equation*} for which $\lambda(\cdot)(\cdot,y,\ldots)$ lands in $\Omega^{0,1}_{\tilde C_0,j_y}\otimes_\mathbb C TX\subseteq\operatorname{Hom}_\mathbb R(T\tilde C_0,TX)$, defined in terms of the old $\lambda$ via: \begin{multline*} \lambda^\mathrm{new}(e)(\alpha,y,x_1,\ldots,x_r,p,x):=\\ \lambda^\mathrm{old}(e)(x_1\in(C_\alpha,j_y)\subseteq\overline{\mathcal C},\ldots,x_r\in (C_\alpha,j_y)\subseteq\overline{\mathcal C},p\in(C_\alpha,j_y)\subseteq\overline{\mathcal C},x) \end{multline*} We assume that the cylindrical ends were chosen disjoint from the support of $\lambda^\mathrm{old}$, so we can make sense of $\lambda^\mathrm{new}$ as giving sections on $C_\alpha$.
nodes.statement_short: Rewrite M(X) near the basepoint using gluing coordinates (alpha,y) and the transported perturbation lambda^new.
nodes.section: B.2 Local model for resolution of a node

nodes.name: Moduli space M(X) in local coordinates
nodes.statement: \overline{\mathcal M}(X):=\left\{\begin{matrix}\alpha\in\mathbb C^d\hfill\cr y\in\mathbb R^{\dim\overline{\mathcal M}^d}\hfill\cr u:C_\alpha\to X\hfill\cr x_i\in C_\alpha\quad 1\leq i\leq r\hfill\cr e\in E\hfill\end{matrix}\;\middle|\;\begin{matrix}u\text{ smooth and }u_\ast[C_\alpha]=\beta\hfill\cr u(p_{n+i})\in D^\circ\quad\hfill(1\leq i\leq\ell)\cr u(x_i)\in D_i^\circ\text{ and }u\pitchfork D_i\text{ at }x_i\quad\hfill(1\leq i\leq r)\cr\bar\partial_yu+\lambda(e)(\alpha,y,x_1,\ldots,x_r,\cdot,u(\cdot))=0\hfill\end{matrix}\right\}
nodes.section: B.2 Local model for resolution of a node
nodes.label: modulispace

nodes.name: Reduction to local structure near basepoint
nodes.statement: Now to prove the main result, it suffices to study the local structure of $\overline{\mathcal M}(X)$ (defined as in \eqref{modulispace}) near the basepoint: \begin{equation} (0,0,u_0:C_0\to X,\{x_i^0\},e_0) \end{equation} which we are assuming lies in $\overline{\mathcal M}(X)^\mathrm{reg}$.
nodes.section: B.2 Local model for resolution of a node

nodes.name: Basepoint (0,0,u_0,x_i^0,e_0)
nodes.section: B.2 Local model for resolution of a node

nodes.name: Exponential map exp
nodes.statement: Let $\exp:TX\to X$ denote the exponential map of some Riemannian metric on $X$ for which $D$ is totally geodesic.

nodes.name: J-linear connection nabla
nodes.statement:
Let $
abla$ denote any $J$-linear ootnote{Given any connection $
abla^0$, the connection $
abla_XY:= rac 12(
abla^0_XY-J(
abla^0_X(JY)))$ is $J$-linear.} connection on $TX$ (equivalently, a connection for which $
abla J=0$).

nodes.name: Parallel transport PT
nodes.statement: Let $\mathsf{PT}_{x\to y}:T_xX\to T_yX$ denote parallel transport via $\nabla$ along the shortest geodesic between $x$ and $y$ (we will only use this notation when it may be assumed that $x$ and $y$ are very close in $X$); note that $\mathsf{PT}_{x\to y}$ is $J$-linear.

nodes.name: Cutoff function chi
nodes.statement: Fix a smooth function $\chi:\mathbb R\to[0,1]$ satisfying: \begin{equation} \chi(x)=\begin{cases}0&x\leq 0\cr 1&x\geq 1\end{cases} \end{equation}

nodes.name: Cutoff function chi
nodes.statement: \chi(x)=\begin{cases}0&x\leq 0\cr 1&x\geq 1\end{cases}

nodes.name: Flattened map u_{0|alpha}
nodes.statement: For $\alpha\in\mathbb C^d$, we define the ``flattened'' map $u_{0|\alpha}:C_0\to X$ as follows. Away from the ends, $u_{0|\alpha}$ coincides with $u_0$. Over an end $[0,\infty)\times S^1$, we define it as follows: \begin{equation} u_{0|\alpha}(s,t):=\begin{cases} u_0(s,t)&s\leq S-1\cr \exp_{u_0(n)}\left[\chi(S-s)\cdot\exp_{u_0(n)}^{-1}u_0(s,t)\right]&S-1\leq s\leq S\cr u_0(n)&S\leq s \end{cases} \end{equation} where $n\in C_0$ denotes the corresponding node.
nodes.statement_short: u_{0|alpha} agrees with u_0 except in the ends, where it is cut off to the constant u_0(n) beyond s=S.

nodes.name: Flattening formula
nodes.statement: u_{0|\alpha}(s,t):=\begin{cases} u_0(s,t)&s\leq S-1\cr \exp_{u_0(n)}\left[\chi(S-s)\cdot\exp_{u_0(n)}^{-1}u_0(s,t)\right]&S-1\leq s\leq S\cr u_0(n)&S\leq s \end{cases}

nodes.name: Preglued map u_alpha
nodes.statement: For $\alpha\in\mathbb C^d$, we define the ``preglued'' map $u_\alpha:C_\alpha\to X$ as follows. Away from the necks, $u_\alpha$ coincides with $u_0$. Over a neck $[0,6S]\times S^1$, we define it as follows: \begin{equation} u_\alpha(s,t):=\begin{cases} u_0(s,t)&s\leq S-1\cr \exp_{u_0(n)}\left[\chi(S-s)\cdot\exp_{u_0(n)}^{-1}u_0(s,t)\right]&S-1\leq s\leq S\cr u_0(n)&S\leq s\leq 5S\cr \exp_{u_0(n)}\left[\chi(S-s')\cdot\exp_{u_0(n)}^{-1}u_0(s',t')\right]&5S\leq s\leq 5S+1\cr u_0(s',t')&5S+1\leq s \end{cases} \end{equation} ($u_\alpha$ should be thought of as the ``descent'' of $u_{0|\alpha}$ from $C_0$ to $C_\alpha$).
nodes.statement_short: u_alpha on C_alpha agrees with u_0 away from necks and is the constant u_0(n) in the middle of each neck, interpolated with chi.

nodes.name: Pregluing formula
nodes.statement: u_\alpha(s,t):=\begin{cases} u_0(s,t)&s\leq S-1\cr \exp_{u_0(n)}\left[\chi(S-s)\cdot\exp_{u_0(n)}^{-1}u_0(s,t)\right]&S-1\leq s\leq S\cr u_0(n)&S\leq s\leq 5S\cr \exp_{u_0(n)}\left[\chi(S-s')\cdot\exp_{u_0(n)}^{-1}u_0(s',t')\right]&5S\leq s\leq 5S+1\cr u_0(s',t')&5S+1\leq s \end{cases}

nodes.name: Pregluing of vector fields xi_alpha
nodes.statement: For $\xi\in C^\infty(C_0,u_0^\ast TX)$, we define: \begin{equation} \xi_\alpha\in C^\infty(C_\alpha,u_\alpha^\ast TX) \end{equation} as follows. Away from the necks, $\xi_\alpha$ coincides with $\xi$. Over a neck $[0,6S]\times S^1$, we define it as follows: \begin{equation} \xi_\alpha(s,t):=\begin{cases} \xi(s,t)&s\leq S-1\cr \mathsf{PT}_{u_0(s,t)\to u_\alpha(s,t)}\left[\xi(s,t)\right]&S-1\leq s\leq S\cr \mathsf{PT}_{u_0(s,t)\to u_\alpha(s,t)}\left[\xi(s,t)\right]\cdot(1-\chi(s-S))+\chi(s-S)\cdot \xi(n)&S\leq s\leq S+1\cr \xi(n)&S+1\leq s\leq 5S-1\cr \mathsf{PT}_{u_0(s',t')\to u_\alpha(s',t')}\left[\xi(s',t')\right]\cdot(1-\chi(s'-S))+\chi(s'-S)\cdot \xi(n)&5S-1\leq s\leq 5S\cr \mathsf{PT}_{u_0(s',t')\to u_\alpha(s',t')}\left[\xi(s',t')\right]&5S\leq s\leq 5S+1\cr \xi(s',t')&5S+1\leq s \end{cases} \end{equation}
nodes.statement_short: Transport a vector field xi along u_0 to C_alpha by parallel transport, interpolating to xi(n) in the neck middle.

nodes.name: Preglued vector field xi_alpha
nodes.statement: \xi_\alpha\in C^\infty(C_\alpha,u_\alpha^\ast TX)

nodes.name: Pregluing of vector fields formula
nodes.statement: \xi_\alpha(s,t):=\begin{cases} \xi(s,t)&s\leq S-1\cr \mathsf{PT}_{u_0(s,t)\to u_\alpha(s,t)}\left[\xi(s,t)\right]&S-1\leq s\leq S\cr \mathsf{PT}_{u_0(s,t)\to u_\alpha(s,t)}\left[\xi(s,t)\right]\cdot(1-\chi(s-S))+\chi(s-S)\cdot \xi(n)&S\leq s\leq S+1\cr \xi(n)&S+1\leq s\leq 5S-1\cr \mathsf{PT}_{u_0(s',t')\to u_\alpha(s',t')}\left[\xi(s',t')\right]\cdot(1-\chi(s'-S))+\chi(s'-S)\cdot \xi(n)&5S-1\leq s\leq 5S\cr \mathsf{PT}_{u_0(s',t')\to u_\alpha(s',t')}\left[\xi(s',t')\right]&5S\leq s\leq 5S+1\cr \xi(s',t')&5S+1\leq s \end{cases}
nodes.label: kernelpregluingformula

nodes.name: Sobolev parameters k and delta
nodes.statement: Fix $k\in\mathbb Z_{\geq 6}$ and fix $\delta\in(0,1)$.

nodes.name: Sobolev space W^{k,2}(C_alpha, u_alpha^*TX)
nodes.statement: We denote by $W^{k,2}(C_\alpha,u_\alpha^\ast TX)$ the space of sections of $u_\alpha^\ast TX$ over $C_\alpha$ whose pullback to $\tilde C_\alpha$ is $W^{k,2}$ (since $W^{k,2}\hookrightarrow C^0$ as $k\geq 6$, this is the same as $W^{k,2}$ sections over $\tilde C_\alpha$ which coincide on each pair of points identified in $\tilde C_\alpha\to C_\alpha$, where $\tilde C_\alpha$ denotes the normalization of $C_\alpha$).

nodes.name: Sobolev space W^{k-1,2} of (0,1)-forms
nodes.statement: Similarly we denote by $W^{k-1,2}(\tilde C_\alpha,\Omega^{0,1}_{\tilde C_\alpha,j_y}\otimes_\mathbb C u_\alpha^\ast TX)$ the space of sections of class $W^{k-1,2}$.

nodes.name: Parallel transport trivialization near nodes
nodes.statement: To make calculations in ends/necks easier, for each node $n\in C_0$ we fix the local trivialization of $TX$ given by parallel transport: \begin{equation} \mathsf{PT}_{u_0(n)\to p}:T_{u_0(n)}X\to T_pX \end{equation} over $p$ contained in a small ball centered at $u_0(n)$.

nodes.name: Parallel transport trivialization near nodes
nodes.statement: \mathsf{PT}_{u_0(n)\to p}:T_{u_0(n)}X\to T_pX
nodes.label: localPTcoords

nodes.name: Weighted Sobolev space W^{k,2,delta}(C_0,u_{0|alpha}^*TX)
nodes.statement: For $\alpha\in\mathbb C^d$, we define a weighted Sobolev space: \begin{equation} W^{k,2,\delta}(C_0,u_{0|\alpha}^\ast TX) \end{equation} using the following norm. We use the usual $(k,2)$ norm away from the ends. Over an end $[0,\infty)\times S^1\subseteq C_0$, we consider the local trivialization \eqref{localPTcoords}, in which a section of $u_{0|\alpha}^\ast TX$ simply becomes a function $\xi:[0,\infty)\times S^1\to T_{u_0(n)}X$. In terms of this function, the contribution from the end to the norm squared is: \begin{equation} \left|\xi(n)\right|^2+\int_{[0,\infty)\times S^1}\biggl[\left|\xi(s,t)-\xi(n)\right|^2+\sum_{j=1}^k\left|D^j\xi(s,t)\right|^2\biggr]e^{2\delta s}\;ds\,dt \end{equation} The derivatives of $\xi$ are measured with respect to the standard metric on $[0,\infty)\times S^1$. By Sobolev embedding $W^{2,2}\hookrightarrow C^0$ in two dimensions, in any end we have a uniform bound on $\left|\xi(s,t)-\xi(n)\right|e^{\delta s}$ and $\left|D^j\xi(s,t)\right|e^{\delta s}$ ($1\leq j\leq k-2$) linear in $\left\|\xi\right\|_{k,2,\delta}$.
nodes.statement_short: Weighted Sobolev norm on C_0: usual (k,2) norm away from ends; in ends, |xi(n)|^2 plus exponentially weighted (e^{2 delta s}) norm of xi - xi(n).

nodes.name: W^{k,2,delta}(C_0,u_{0|alpha}^*TX)
nodes.statement: W^{k,2,\delta}(C_0,u_{0|\alpha}^\ast TX)

nodes.name: Weighted end norm
nodes.statement: \left|\xi(n)\right|^2+\int_{[0,\infty)\times S^1}\biggl[\left|\xi(s,t)-\xi(n)\right|^2+\sum_{j=1}^k\left|D^j\xi(s,t)\right|^2\biggr]e^{2\delta s}\;ds\,dt
nodes.label: endnorm

nodes.name: Weighted Sobolev space W^{k,2,delta}(C_alpha,u_alpha^*TX)
nodes.statement: For $\alpha\in\mathbb C^d$, we define a weighted Sobolev space: \begin{equation} W^{k,2,\delta}(C_\alpha,u_\alpha^\ast TX) \end{equation} using the following norm. We use the usual $(k,2)$ norm away from the ends/necks. Over an end, the contribution to the norm squared is \eqref{endnorm}. Over a neck $[0,6S]\times S^1\subseteq C_\alpha$, we again think of a section as a function $\xi:[0,6S]\times S^1\to T_{u_0(n)}X$, and the contribution to the norm squared is: \begin{equation*} \biggl|\int_{S^1}\xi(3S,t)\,dt\biggr|^2+\int_{[0,6S]\times S^1}\biggl[\Bigl|\xi(s,t)-\int_{S^1}\xi(3S,t)\,dt\Bigr|^2+\sum_{j=1}^k\left|D^j\xi(s,t)\right|^2\biggr]e^{2\delta\min(s,6S-s)}\;ds\,dt \end{equation*} Of course, for fixed $\alpha\in\mathbb C^d$, this norm is equivalent to not weighting the necks, though the two norms are not uniformly equivalent as $\alpha\to 0$. The weight in the necks is important since the key point is to establish certain estimates which are uniform as $\alpha\to 0$. By Sobolev embedding $W^{2,2}\hookrightarrow C^0$ in two dimensions, in any neck we have a uniform bound on $\left|\xi(s,t)-\int_{S^1}\xi(3S,t)\,dt\right|e^{\delta\min(s,6S-s)}$ and $\left|D^j\xi(s,t)\right|e^{\delta\min(s,6S-s)}$ ($1\leq j\leq k-2$) linear in $\left\|\xi\right\|_{k,2,\delta}$.
nodes.statement_short: Weighted Sobolev norm on C_alpha: in each neck, weight e^{2 delta min(s,6S-s)} applied to xi minus its average over the middle circle.

nodes.name: W^{k,2,delta}(C_alpha,u_alpha^*TX)
nodes.statement: W^{k,2,\delta}(C_\alpha,u_\alpha^\ast TX)

nodes.name: Weighted Sobolev space W^{k-1,2,delta} of (0,1)-forms
nodes.statement: For $\alpha\in\mathbb C^d$, we define a weighted Sobolev space: \begin{equation} W^{k-1,2,\delta}(\tilde C_\alpha,\Omega^{0,1}_{\tilde C_\alpha,j_y}\otimes_\mathbb C u_\alpha^\ast TX) \end{equation} as follows. We use the usual $(k-1,2)$ norm away from the ends/necks. Over an end or neck, we trivialize $(T\tilde C_\alpha,j_y)$ over $\mathbb C$ by the basis vector $\frac\partial{\partial s}$, and we trivialize $TX$ via \eqref{localPTcoords}, and hence the section is simply a function $\eta$ from the end/neck to $T_{u_0(n)}X$. In terms of this function, the contribution to the norm squared is (for end/neck respectively): \begin{align} \int_{[0,\infty)\times S^1}&\sum_{j=0}^{k-1}\left|D^j\eta(s,t)\right|^2e^{2\delta s}\;ds\,dt\\ \int_{[0,6S]\times S^1}&\sum_{j=0}^{k-1}\left|D^j\eta(s,t)\right|^2e^{2\delta\min(s,6S-s)}\;ds\,dt \end{align} By Sobolev embedding $W^{2,2}\hookrightarrow C^0$ in two dimensions, in any end (resp.\ neck) we have a uniform bound on $\left|D^j\eta(s,t)\right|e^{\delta s}$ (resp.\ $\left|D^j\eta(s,t)\right|e^{\delta\min(s,6S-s)}$) ($1\leq j\leq k-3$) linear in $\left\|\eta\right\|_{k,2,\delta}$.
nodes.statement_short: Weighted norm on (0,1)-forms: (k-1,2) norm with weights e^{2 delta s} in ends and e^{2 delta min(s,6S-s)} in necks.

nodes.name: W^{k-1,2,delta} of (0,1)-forms
nodes.statement: W^{k-1,2,\delta}(\tilde C_\alpha,\Omega^{0,1}_{\tilde C_\alpha,j_y}\otimes_\mathbb C u_\alpha^\ast TX)

nodes.name: Weighted end/neck norms for (0,1)-forms
nodes.statement: \int_{[0,\infty)\times S^1}&\sum_{j=0}^{k-1}\left|D^j\eta(s,t)\right|^2e^{2\delta s}\;ds\,dt\\ \int_{[0,6S]\times S^1}&\sum_{j=0}^{k-1}\left|D^j\eta(s,t)\right|^2e^{2\delta\min(s,6S-s)}\;ds\,dt

nodes.name: Based del-bar section F_{alpha,y}
nodes.statement: We consider the following partially defined function: \begin{gather*} \mathcal F_{\alpha,y}:C^\infty(C_\alpha,u_\alpha^\ast TX)_D\oplus E\to C^\infty(\tilde C_\alpha,\Omega^{0,1}_{\tilde C_\alpha,j_y}\otimes_\mathbb C u_\alpha^\ast TX)\\ \xi\mapsto\mathsf{PT}_{\exp_{u_\alpha}\xi\to u_\alpha}\left[\bar\partial_y\exp_{u_\alpha}\xi+\lambda(e_0+\operatorname{proj}_E\xi)(\alpha,y,x_1,\ldots,x_r,\cdot,(\exp_{u_\alpha}\xi)(\cdot))\right] \end{gather*} This function $\mathcal F_{\alpha,y}$ is defined for $\xi$ in a $C^1$-neighborhood of zero; for these $\xi$ we define $x_i=x_i(\xi)$ as in \eqref{intersectionsfunction}. The subscript $D$ indicates restriction to sections which are tangent to $D$ at $p_{n+1},\ldots,p_{n+\ell}$.
nodes.statement_short: F_{alpha,y}(xi) is the perturbed del-bar of exp_{u_alpha} xi, transported back to u_alpha, on sections tangent to D at the extra marked points.

nodes.name: Reason for the vertical inclusions
nodes.statement: Let us remark on the reason for the vertical inclusions in \eqref{fredholmsquare}. For the leftmost vertical inclusion, one just needs to check that for a function $f:D^2\to\mathbb R$, the $W^{k,2,\delta}$ norm of its pullback to $[0,\infty)\times S^1$ is bounded linearly by its $W^{k,2}$ norm on $D^2$. For the rightmost vertical inclusion, one checks the same property for $1$-forms. In both of these calculations we use the fact that $\delta<1$.

nodes.name: Proof
nodes.statement:
The operator $D_{\alpha,y}$ equals $(
abla\xi)^{0,1}_y$ plus compact terms (by Lemma ef{linearizedformula}), so it is equivalent to show that $\xi\mapsto(
abla\xi)^{0,1}_y$ is Fredholm (and we may forget about $E$). Here $
abla$ is really the pullback of $
abla$ via $u_\alpha$. Thus it suffices to show that if $V$ is a smooth complex vector bundle over a nodal Riemann surface $C$ equipped with a smooth connection $
abla$, then the horizontal maps:  egin{equation}  egin{tikzcd}[column sep = large] W^{k,2,\delta}(C,V)\ar{r}{\xi\mapsto(
abla\xi)^{0,1}}&W^{k-1,2,\delta}(	ilde C,\Omega^{0,1}_{	ilde C}\otimes_\mathbb C V)\ W^{k,2}(C,V)\ar[hook]{u}\ar{r}{\xi\mapsto(
abla\xi)^{0,1}}&W^{k-1,2}(	ilde C,\Omega^{0,1}_{	ilde C}\otimes_\mathbb C V)\ar[hook]{u} \end{tikzcd} \end{equation} are Fredholm. For the bottom map, the Fredholm property is standard. Indeed, $W^{k,2}(C,V)$ lies inside $W^{k,2}(	ilde C,V)$ as a closed subspace of finite codimension, and $
abla^{0,1}:W^{k,2}(	ilde C,V)	o W^{k-1,2}(	ilde C,\Omega^{0,1}_{	ilde C}\otimes_\mathbb C V)$ is Fredholm by elliptic regularity on the compact Riemann surface $	ilde C$. For the top map, the Fredholm property follows from results of Lockhart--McOwen \cite{lockhartmcowen} concerning the Fredholmness (in weighted Sobolev spaces) of elliptic operators on manifolds with cylindrical ends. Specifically, $W^{k,2,\delta}(C,V)$ lies inside $W^{k,2,\delta}(	ilde C,V)$ as a closed subspace of finite codimension, and the map $
abla^{0,1}:W^{k,2,\delta}(	ilde C,V)	o W^{k-1,2,\delta}(	ilde C,\Omega^{0,1}_{	ilde C}\otimes_\mathbb C V)$ is Fredholm by the theory of Lockhart--McOwen \cite{lockhartmcowen}. This uses the fact that the weight $\delta\in(0,1)$ is not an eigenvalue of the asymptotic linearized operator in any end (the set of eigenvalues in any end is precisely $\mathbb Z$, corresponding to the powers $\{z^n\}_{n\in\mathbb Z}$ on $D^2\setminus 0$). Let us also remark that both of these Fredholmness statements are easier at $p=2$ than for general $p\in(1,\infty)$, since for $p=2$ one can use Fourier analysis (after localizing the problem with a partition of unity). Now it remains to show that the induced maps on kernel and cokernel are isomorphisms. The map on kernels is obviously injective, and the map on cokernels is easily seen to be surjective (use the fact that the image of the top horizontal map is closed and the fact that the rightmost vertical inclusion is dense). For the surjectivity of the map on kernels and the injectivity of the map on cokernels, it suffices to show that if $D_{\alpha,y}\xi=\eta$ for $\xi\in W^{k,2,\delta}$ and $\eta\in W^{k-1,2}$, then $\xi\in W^{k,2}$. To show $\xi\in W^{k,2}$, it suffices to argue locally on one side of a given node. Certainly (the vector field part of) $\xi$ extends continuously to $C_\alpha$ (by definition of $W^{k,2,\delta}$), and this continuous extension satisfies $D_{\alpha,y}\xi=\eta+\epsilon$ where $\epsilon$ is a distribution on $	ilde C_\alpha$ valued in $\Omega^{0,1}_{	ilde C_\alpha,j_y}\otimes_\mathbb C u_\alpha^\ast TX$ and supported inside the (inverse images of the) nodes. By elliptic regularity, it suffices to show that $\epsilon=0$. 
ewlength\arrowwidthawesome \settowidth{\arrowwidthawesome}{$
rightarrow$} Now for smooth test functions $\varphi$ supported inside a small neighborhood of the support of $\epsilon$, we have:  egin{equation} \langle\epsilon,\varphiangle=\langle D_{\alpha,y}\xi-\eta,\varphiangle=\langle\xi,D_{\alpha,y}^\ast\varphiangle-\langle\eta,\varphiangle \end{equation} We thus obtain the bound $\left|\langle\epsilon,\varphiangleight|\leq c\left\|\varphiight\|_{1,1}$ since $D_{\alpha,y}^\ast$ is a first order operator and $\xi,\eta$ are bounded (as they are continuous). On the other hand, $\epsilon$ is supported at a finite set of points, so it is a linear combination of $\delta$-functions and their derivatives. Hence $\epsilon$ does not satisfy the bound $\left|\langle\epsilon,\varphiangleight|\leq c\left\|\varphiight\|_{1,1}$ (recall that $W^{1,1}\hookrightarrow\hspace{-\arrowwidthawesome}
rightarrow C^0$ since we are in two dimensions) unless $\epsilon=0$, as desired.

nodes.name: Data previously fixed
nodes.statement: Data which has been previously fixed includes $(s_0,u_0,\{x_i^0\},e_0)$, the cylindrical ends, $j_y$, the metrics used to define $\exp$ and Sobolev norms, $k$, $\delta$, the cutoff function $\chi$, the norms on $E$, $K$, $\mathbb C^d$, $\mathbb R^{\dim\overline{\mathcal M}^d}$, etc.

nodes.name: Proof
nodes.statement: Away from the ends/necks of $C_\alpha$, the expression is zero when $y=0$ (since $(0,0,u_0,\{x_i^0\},e_0)\in\overline{\mathcal M}(X)$) and more generally it follows easily that its $j$th derivative is bounded pointwise by $c_j\left|y\right|$. In the ends of $C_\alpha$, the expression is zero. In a given neck $[0,6S]\times S^1\subseteq C_\alpha$, argue as follows. Recall that $\lambda$ vanishes in the ends/necks, so we just have to bound $\bar\partial_yu_\alpha$. Now $\bar\partial_yu_\alpha$ is only nonzero over $[S-1,S]\cup[5S,5S+1]$; by symmetry we may just work over $[S-1,S]$. Now since $u_0$ is smooth, it and all its derivatives decay exponentially in any cylindrical end $[0,\infty)\times S^1$ (since every end is holomorphically conjugate to the map $[0,\infty)\times S^1\to D^2$ given by $z=e^{-s-it}$). Precisely, we have the following pointwise bound over $[S-1,S]$: \begin{equation} \left|D^ju_0(s,t)\right|\leq c_je^{-S} \end{equation} (derivatives with respect to $s$ and $t$). It follows from the definition of $u_\alpha$ that the same bound holds for $u_\alpha$. Thus the contribution of $[S-1,S]$ to the norm of $\bar\partial_yu_\alpha$ is bounded by a constant times $e^{S\delta}e^{-S}$.
nodes.statement_short: Pointwise estimate: away from necks the error is O(|y|); in necks only the cutoff region contributes, where u_0 decays like e^{-S}, weighted by e^{delta S}.

nodes.name: Exponential decay of u_0 in ends
nodes.statement: \left|D^ju_0(s,t)\right|\leq c_je^{-S}
nodes.label: uzeroexponentialdecay

nodes.statement_short: Preglued kernel elements are approximately in the kernel: ||D_{alpha,y} kappa_alpha|| = O(|y| + sum e^{-(1-delta)S_i}) ||kappa||.
assumptions: For all $\kappa\in K$
uniformly over $(\alpha,y)$ in a neighborhood of zero, for $c<\infty$ depending on data which has been previously fixed.
conclusions: \left\|D_{\alpha,y}\kappa_\alpha\right\|_{k-1,2,\delta}\leq c\cdot\left[\left|y\right|+\sum_{i=1}^de^{-(1-\delta)S_i}\right]\left\|\kappa\right\|

nodes.name: Proof
nodes.statement: Away from the ends/necks, the norm is bounded by $c\cdot\left|y\right|\left\|\kappa\right\|$. In the ends, the expression is zero. In the necks, argue as follows. The expression is only nonzero over $[S-1,S+1]\cup[5S-1,5S+1]$; by symmetry we may just work over $[S-1,S+1]$. Then since $u_0$ and $\kappa$ are smooth, we have (by the same reasoning used to justify \eqref{uzeroexponentialdecay}) the following pointwise bound over $[S-1,S+1]$: \begin{equation} \left|D^j\kappa_\alpha(s,t)\right|\leq c_je^{-S}\left\|\kappa\right\| \end{equation} (derivatives with respect to $s$ and $t$, in local coordinates \eqref{localPTcoords}). Thus the overall contribution of $[S-1,S+1]$ to the total norm of the expression is bounded by a constant times $e^{S\delta}e^{-S}\left\|\kappa\right\|$.
nodes.statement_short: Same as the map pregluing estimate: only the cutoff region of each neck contributes, with e^{-S} decay against the e^{delta S} weight.
