nodes.statement: \left|D^j\kappa_\alpha(s,t)\right|\leq c_je^{-S}\left\|\kappa\right\|

nodes.name: Right inverse Q_{0,0}
nodes.statement: Recall that by assumption, the linearized operator: \begin{equation} D_{0,0}:W^{k,2,\delta}(C_0,u_0^\ast TX)_D\oplus E\to W^{k-1,2,\delta}(\tilde C_0,\Omega^{0,1}_{\tilde C_0,j_0}\otimes_\mathbb C u_0^\ast TX) \end{equation} is surjective (even if we replace $E$ with $E'$). We now proceed to fix a bounded right inverse: \begin{equation} Q_{0,0}:W^{k-1,2,\delta}(\tilde C_0,\Omega^{0,1}_{\tilde C_0,j_0}\otimes_\mathbb C u_0^\ast TX)\to W^{k,2,\delta}(C_0,u_0^\ast TX)_D\oplus E' \end{equation} whose image admits a simple description (the description of the image will be important for the proof that the gluing map is continuous (Proposition \ref{continuityofgluing})). Fix a collection of points $q_i\in C_0$ ($1\leq i\leq h$) not contained in any of the cylindrical ends, subspaces $V_i\subseteq T_{u_0(q_i)}X$, and a subspace $E''\subseteq E'$ so that the natural evaluation map: \begin{equation} L_0:K\xrightarrow\sim\biggl(\bigoplus_{i=1}^hT_{u_0(q_i)}X/V_i\biggr)\oplus E/E'' \end{equation} is an isomorphism (such choices exist since $K\twoheadrightarrow E/E'$ is surjective and elements of $K$ satisfy unique continuation). Now we can consider the same evaluation map on the larger space: \begin{equation} L_0:W^{k,2,\delta}(C_0,u_0^\ast TX)_D\oplus E\to W:=\biggl(\bigoplus_{i=1}^hT_{u_0(q_i)}X/V_i\biggr)\oplus E/E'' \end{equation} Since $L_0$ sends $K=\ker D_{0,0}$ isomorphically to $W$, it follows that the restriction of $D_{0,0}$ to $\ker L_0$ is an isomorphism of Banach spaces. Hence there is a unique right inverse: \begin{equation*} Q_{0,0}:W^{k-1,2,\delta}(\tilde C_0,\Omega^{0,1}_{\tilde C_0,j_0}\otimes_\mathbb C u_0^\ast TX)\to\ker L_0\subseteq W^{k,2,\delta}(C_0,u_0^\ast TX)_D\oplus E \end{equation*} and it is bounded. Since $E''\subseteq E'$, $\ker L_0$ is in fact contained in the right hand side of \eqref{chosenrightinverse}. We fix once and for all this $Q_{0,0}$.
nodes.statement_short: Choose points q_i, subspaces V_i and E'' so that evaluation L_0 identifies K with W; Q_{0,0} is the unique right inverse of D_{0,0} with image in ker L_0.

nodes.name: Surjective linearized operator D_{0,0}
nodes.statement: D_{0,0}:W^{k,2,\delta}(C_0,u_0^\ast TX)_D\oplus E\to W^{k-1,2,\delta}(\tilde C_0,\Omega^{0,1}_{\tilde C_0,j_0}\otimes_\mathbb C u_0^\ast TX)

nodes.name: Chosen right inverse Q_{0,0}
nodes.statement: Q_{0,0}:W^{k-1,2,\delta}(\tilde C_0,\Omega^{0,1}_{\tilde C_0,j_0}\otimes_\mathbb C u_0^\ast TX)\to W^{k,2,\delta}(C_0,u_0^\ast TX)_D\oplus E'
nodes.label: chosenrightinverse

nodes.name: Evaluation isomorphism L_0 on K
nodes.statement: L_0:K\xrightarrow\sim\biggl(\bigoplus_{i=1}^hT_{u_0(q_i)}X/V_i\biggr)\oplus E/E''

nodes.name: Evaluation map L_0
nodes.statement: L_0:W^{k,2,\delta}(C_0,u_0^\ast TX)_D\oplus E\to W:=\biggl(\bigoplus_{i=1}^hT_{u_0(q_i)}X/V_i\biggr)\oplus E/E''
nodes.label: lineartofixinverse

nodes.name: Approximate right inverse T_{alpha,y}
nodes.statement: We define a map: \begin{equation} T_{\alpha,y}:W^{k-1,2,\delta}(\tilde C_\alpha,\Omega^{0,1}_{\tilde C_\alpha,j_y}\otimes_\mathbb C u_\alpha^\ast TX)\to W^{k,2,\delta}(C_\alpha,u_\alpha^\ast TX)_D\oplus E \end{equation} as the composition: \begin{equation} T_{\alpha,y}:={\operatorname{glue}}\circ\mathsf{PT}\circ\operatorname{id}\circ Q_{0,0}\circ I_y\circ\mathsf{PT}\circ\operatorname{break} \end{equation} of maps in the following diagram, to be defined below: \begin{equation} \begin{tikzcd} W^{k,2,\delta}(C_\alpha,u_\alpha^\ast TX)_D\oplus E\ar{r}{D_{\alpha,y}}&W^{k-1,2,\delta}(\tilde C_\alpha,\Omega^{0,1}_{\tilde C_\alpha,j_y}\otimes_\mathbb C u_\alpha^\ast TX)\ar{d}{\mathrm{break}}\\ W^{k,2,\delta}(C_0,u_{0|\alpha}^\ast TX)_D\oplus E\ar{u}{\mathrm{glue}}\ar{r}{D_{0|\alpha,y}}&W^{k-1,2,\delta}(\tilde C_0,\Omega^{0,1}_{\tilde C_0,j_y}\otimes_\mathbb C u_{0|\alpha}^\ast TX)\ar[leftrightarrow]{d}{\mathsf{PT}}\\ W^{k,2,\delta}(C_0,u_0^\ast TX)_D\oplus E\ar[leftrightarrow]{u}{\mathsf{PT}}\ar{r}{D_{0,y}}&W^{k-1,2,\delta}(\tilde C_0,\Omega^{0,1}_{\tilde C_0,j_y}\otimes_\mathbb C u_0^\ast TX)\ar[leftrightarrow]{d}{I_y}\\ W^{k,2,\delta}(C_0,u_0^\ast TX)_D\oplus E\ar[equals]{u}{\operatorname{id}}\ar[yshift=0.5ex]{r}{D_{0,0}}&\ar[yshift=-0.5ex]{l}{Q_{0,0}}W^{k-1,2,\delta}(\tilde C_0,\Omega^{0,1}_{\tilde C_0,j_0}\otimes_\mathbb C u_0^\ast TX) \end{tikzcd} \end{equation} ($D_{0|\alpha,y}$ denotes the linearized operator at $u_{0|\alpha}$). We fix once and for all a smooth family of $(j_0,j_y)$-linear identifications $I_y:(T\tilde C_0,j_0)\to(T\tilde C_0,j_y)$ which are the identity over the ends/necks. This gives rise to the bottom right vertical map in \eqref{biginversediagram}. We define the middle vertical maps in \eqref{biginversediagram} using parallel transport (equivalently, using the local trivializations defined by \eqref{localPTcoords}). We define the map: \begin{equation} W^{k-1,2,\delta}(\tilde C_\alpha,\Omega^{0,1}_{\tilde C_\alpha,j_y}\otimes_\mathbb C u_\alpha^\ast TX)\xrightarrow{\mathrm{break}}W^{k-1,2,\delta}(\tilde C_0,\Omega^{0,1}_{\tilde C_0,j_0}\otimes_\mathbb C u_{0|\alpha}^\ast TX) \end{equation} as follows. Fix a smooth function $\bar\chi:\mathbb R\to[0,1]$ such that: \begin{equation} \bar\chi(x)=\begin{cases}1&x\leq-1\cr0&x\geq+1\end{cases}\qquad\bar\chi(x)+\bar\chi(-x)=1 \end{equation} Let $\eta\in W^{k-1,2,\delta}(\tilde C_\alpha,\Omega^{0,1}_{\tilde C_\alpha,j_y}\otimes_\mathbb C u_\alpha^\ast TX)$. Away from the ends with $\alpha\ne 0$, $\operatorname{break}(\eta)$ is simply $\eta$. In any particular end $[0,\infty)\times S^1\subseteq C_0$ with $\alpha\ne 0$, we define: \begin{equation} \operatorname{break}(\eta)(s,t):=\begin{cases} \eta(s,t)&s\leq 3S-1\cr \bar\chi(s-3S)\cdot\eta(s,t)&3S-1\leq s\leq 3S+1\cr 0&3S+1\leq s \end{cases} \end{equation} (noting the corresponding neck $[0,6S]\times S^1\subseteq C_\alpha$). We define the map: \begin{equation} W^{k,2,\delta}(C_0,u_{0|\alpha}^\ast TX)_D\xrightarrow{\mathrm{glue}}W^{k,2,\delta}(C_\alpha,u_\alpha^\ast TX)_D \end{equation} Let $\xi\in W^{k,2,\delta}(C_0,u_{0|\alpha}^\ast TX)_D$. Away from the necks of $C_\alpha$, $\operatorname{glue}(\xi)$ is simply $\xi$. In any particular neck $[0,6S]\times S^1\subseteq C_\alpha$, we define: \begin{equation} \operatorname{glue}(\xi)(s,t):=\begin{cases} \xi(s,t)&s\leq 2S\cr \xi(n)+\chi(4S-s)\cdot[\xi(s,t)-\xi(n)]+\chi(4S-s')\cdot[\xi(s',t')-\xi(n)]&2S\leq s\leq 4S\cr \xi(s',t')&4S\leq s \end{cases} \end{equation} (noting the corresponding ends $(s,t)\in[0,\infty)\times S^1\subseteq C_0$ and $(s',t')\in[0,\infty)\times S^1\subseteq C_0$). Note that the cutoff of $\xi(s,t)$ occurs around $4S\in[0,6S]$, where the weight $e^{2\delta\min(s,6S-s)}$ is much smaller than the weight $e^{2\delta s}$ at $4S\in[0,\infty)$. We will see in the proof of Lemma \ref{approxtop} that this makes it easy to derive the desired estimates on $\bar\partial\mathrm{glue}(\xi)$. This trick was explained to us by Abouzaid and attributed to Fukaya--Oh--Ohta--Ono \cite{foootechnicaldetails}.
nodes.statement_short: T_{alpha,y} = glue o PT o Q_{0,0} o I_y o PT o break: cut a form on C_alpha to C_0, invert there with Q_{0,0}, and glue back.

nodes.name: T_{alpha,y} domain and target
nodes.statement: T_{\alpha,y}:W^{k-1,2,\delta}(\tilde C_\alpha,\Omega^{0,1}_{\tilde C_\alpha,j_y}\otimes_\mathbb C u_\alpha^\ast TX)\to W^{k,2,\delta}(C_\alpha,u_\alpha^\ast TX)_D\oplus E

nodes.name: T_{alpha,y} as composition
nodes.statement: T_{\alpha,y}:={\operatorname{glue}}\circ\mathsf{PT}\circ\operatorname{id}\circ Q_{0,0}\circ I_y\circ\mathsf{PT}\circ\operatorname{break}

nodes.name: Approximate inverse diagram
nodes.statement: \begin{tikzcd} W^{k,2,\delta}(C_\alpha,u_\alpha^\ast TX)_D\oplus E\ar{r}{D_{\alpha,y}}&W^{k-1,2,\delta}(\tilde C_\alpha,\Omega^{0,1}_{\tilde C_\alpha,j_y}\otimes_\mathbb C u_\alpha^\ast TX)\ar{d}{\mathrm{break}}\\ W^{k,2,\delta}(C_0,u_{0|\alpha}^\ast TX)_D\oplus E\ar{u}{\mathrm{glue}}\ar{r}{D_{0|\alpha,y}}&W^{k-1,2,\delta}(\tilde C_0,\Omega^{0,1}_{\tilde C_0,j_y}\otimes_\mathbb C u_{0|\alpha}^\ast TX)\ar[leftrightarrow]{d}{\mathsf{PT}}\\ W^{k,2,\delta}(C_0,u_0^\ast TX)_D\oplus E\ar[leftrightarrow]{u}{\mathsf{PT}}\ar{r}{D_{0,y}}&W^{k-1,2,\delta}(\tilde C_0,\Omega^{0,1}_{\tilde C_0,j_y}\otimes_\mathbb C u_0^\ast TX)\ar[leftrightarrow]{d}{I_y}\\ W^{k,2,\delta}(C_0,u_0^\ast TX)_D\oplus E\ar[equals]{u}{\operatorname{id}}\ar[yshift=0.5ex]{r}{D_{0,0}}&\ar[yshift=-0.5ex]{l}{Q_{0,0}}W^{k-1,2,\delta}(\tilde C_0,\Omega^{0,1}_{\tilde C_0,j_0}\otimes_\mathbb C u_0^\ast TX) \end{tikzcd}
nodes.label: biginversediagram

nodes.name: Breaking map
nodes.statement: W^{k-1,2,\delta}(\tilde C_\alpha,\Omega^{0,1}_{\tilde C_\alpha,j_y}\otimes_\mathbb C u_\alpha^\ast TX)\xrightarrow{\mathrm{break}}W^{k-1,2,\delta}(\tilde C_0,\Omega^{0,1}_{\tilde C_0,j_0}\otimes_\mathbb C u_{0|\alpha}^\ast TX)

nodes.name: Cutoff function bar chi
nodes.statement: \bar\chi(x)=\begin{cases}1&x\leq-1\cr0&x\geq+1\end{cases}\qquad\bar\chi(x)+\bar\chi(-x)=1

nodes.name: Breaking formula
nodes.statement: \operatorname{break}(\eta)(s,t):=\begin{cases} \eta(s,t)&s\leq 3S-1\cr \bar\chi(s-3S)\cdot\eta(s,t)&3S-1\leq s\leq 3S+1\cr 0&3S+1\leq s \end{cases}

nodes.name: Gluing map on vector fields
nodes.statement: W^{k,2,\delta}(C_0,u_{0|\alpha}^\ast TX)_D\xrightarrow{\mathrm{glue}}W^{k,2,\delta}(C_\alpha,u_\alpha^\ast TX)_D

nodes.name: Gluing formula for vector fields
nodes.statement: \operatorname{glue}(\xi)(s,t):=\begin{cases} \xi(s,t)&s\leq 2S\cr \xi(n)+\chi(4S-s)\cdot[\xi(s,t)-\xi(n)]+\chi(4S-s')\cdot[\xi(s',t')-\xi(n)]&2S\leq s\leq 4S\cr \xi(s',t')&4S\leq s \end{cases}

nodes.name: Evaluation map L_alpha
nodes.statement: Let us make the elementary observation that the definition of $L_0$ extends perfectly well to give an analogous bounded linear map: \begin{equation} L_\alpha:W^{k,2,\delta}(C_\alpha,u_\alpha^\ast TX)_D\oplus E\to W \end{equation}

nodes.name: Evaluation map L_alpha
nodes.statement: L_\alpha:W^{k,2,\delta}(C_\alpha,u_\alpha^\ast TX)_D\oplus E\to W
nodes.label: newLonpreglued

nodes.name: Image of T_{alpha,y} lies in ker L_alpha
nodes.statement: Since $\operatorname{im} Q_{0,0}\subseteq\ker L_0$, it follows from the definition of $T_{\alpha,y}$ that $\operatorname{im} T_{\alpha,y}\subseteq\ker L_\alpha$ as well.

nodes.name: Approximation estimate for the bottom square
nodes.statement: Let: \begin{equation} \begin{CD} X@>D>>Y\cr @AGAA@VVBV\cr X'@>D'>>Y' \end{CD} \end{equation} denote the bottom square in \eqref{biginversediagram}. Then for $\xi\in X'$ and $\eta\in Y$ with $D'\xi=B\eta$, we have: \begin{equation} \left\|DG\xi-\eta\right\|\leq c\cdot\left\|\xi\right\|\left|y\right| \end{equation} uniformly over $(\alpha,y)$ in a neighborhood of zero, for $c<\infty$ depending on data which has been previously fixed.
nodes.statement_short: The bottom square of the inverse diagram commutes up to O(|y|).
assumptions: Then for $\xi\in X'$ and $\eta\in Y$ with $D'\xi=B\eta$
conclusions: \left\|DG\xi-\eta\right\|\leq c\cdot\left\|\xi\right\|\left|y\right|
nodes.label: approxbottom

nodes.name: Displayed equation in Section B.7
nodes.statement: \begin{CD} X@>D>>Y\cr @AGAA@VVBV\cr X'@>D'>>Y' \end{CD}

nodes.name: Displayed equation in Section B.7
nodes.statement: \left\|DG\xi-\eta\right\|\leq c\cdot\left\|\xi\right\|\left|y\right|

nodes.name: Proof
nodes.statement: In simpler terms, we have $\left\|D_{0,y}-I_y\circ D_{0,0}\right\|\leq c\cdot\left|y\right|$ (calculation left to the reader) and this trivially implies the claimed statement.
nodes.statement_short: Direct: ||D_{0,y} - I_y D_{0,0}|| = O(|y|) (calculation left to reader).

nodes.name: Approximation estimate for the middle square
nodes.statement: Let: \begin{equation} \begin{CD} X@>D>>Y\cr @AGAA@VVBV\cr X'@>D'>>Y' \end{CD} \end{equation} denote the middle square in \eqref{biginversediagram}. Then for $\xi\in X'$ and $\eta\in Y$ with $D'\xi=B\eta$, we have: \begin{equation} \left\|DG\xi-\eta\right\|\leq c\cdot\left\|\xi\right\|\sum_{i=1}^de^{-S_i} \end{equation} uniformly over $(\alpha,y)$ in a neighborhood of zero, for $c<\infty$ depending on data which has been previously fixed.
nodes.statement_short: The parallel-transport square commutes up to O(sum e^{-S_i}).
assumptions: Then for $\xi\in X'$ and $\eta\in Y$ with $D'\xi=B\eta$
conclusions: \left\|DG\xi-\eta\right\|\leq c\cdot\left\|\xi\right\|\sum_{i=1}^de^{-S_i}
nodes.label: approxmiddle

nodes.name: Displayed equation in Section B.7
nodes.statement: \begin{CD} X@>D>>Y\cr @AGAA@VVBV\cr X'@>D'>>Y' \end{CD}

nodes.name: Displayed equation in Section B.7
nodes.statement: \left\|DG\xi-\eta\right\|\leq c\cdot\left\|\xi\right\|\sum_{i=1}^de^{-S_i}

nodes.name: Proof
nodes.statement: In simpler terms, we bound the operator norm of the difference between the two diagonal compositions: \begin{equation} \left\|\mathsf{PT}\circ D_{0,y}-D_{0|\alpha,y}\circ\mathsf{PT}\right\|\leq c\cdot\sum_{i=1}^de^{-S_i} \end{equation} (this trivially implies the claimed statement). To show \eqref{betterPTcommutingoperatornormbound}, observe that the two operators only differ over the $[S-1,\infty)$ subset of each end $[0,\infty)\times S^1\subseteq C_0$. Using estimates \eqref{uzeroexponentialdecay} arising from the fact that $u_0$ is smooth, we obtain the desired bound.
nodes.statement_short: Bound the commutator of parallel transport with the linearized operator using exponential decay of u_0.

nodes.name: Parallel transport commutator bound
nodes.statement: \left\|\mathsf{PT}\circ D_{0,y}-D_{0|\alpha,y}\circ\mathsf{PT}\right\|\leq c\cdot\sum_{i=1}^de^{-S_i}
nodes.label: betterPTcommutingoperatornormbound

nodes.name: Approximation estimate for the top square
nodes.statement: Let: \begin{equation} \begin{CD} X@>D>>Y\cr @AGAA@VVBV\cr X'@>D'>>Y' \end{CD} \end{equation} denote the top square in \eqref{biginversediagram}. Then for $\xi\in X'$ and $\eta\in Y$ with $D'\xi=B\eta$, we have: \begin{equation} \left\|DG\xi-\eta\right\|\leq c\cdot\left\|\xi\right\|\sum_{i=1}^de^{-2\delta S_i} \end{equation} uniformly over $(\alpha,y)$ in a neighborhood of zero, for $c<\infty$ depending on data which has been previously fixed.
nodes.statement_short: The gluing square commutes up to O(sum e^{-2 delta S_i}), thanks to the neck weights.
assumptions: Then for $\xi\in X'$ and $\eta\in Y$ with $D'\xi=B\eta$
conclusions: \left\|DG\xi-\eta\right\|\leq c\cdot\left\|\xi\right\|\sum_{i=1}^de^{-2\delta S_i}
nodes.label: approxtop

nodes.name: Displayed equation in Section B.7
nodes.statement: \begin{CD} X@>D>>Y\cr @AGAA@VVBV\cr X'@>D'>>Y' \end{CD}

nodes.name: Displayed equation in Section B.7
nodes.statement: \left\|DG\xi-\eta\right\|\leq c\cdot\left\|\xi\right\|\sum_{i=1}^de^{-2\delta S_i}

nodes.name: Proof
nodes.statement: The difference $DG\xi-\eta$ is only nonzero in the necks over $s\in[2S,2S+1]$ and $s\in[4S-1,4S]$. By symmetry, we may just do the bound over $s\in[4S-1,4S]$. Over this region, one calculates that the norm of the difference is bounded as claimed. The factor of $e^{-2\delta S}$ comes as the ratio between the $e^{2\delta S}$ weight given to $[4S-1,4S]\times S^1\subseteq[0,6S]\times S^1\subseteq C_\alpha$ and the $e^{4\delta S}$ weight given to $[4S-1,4S]\times S^1\subseteq[0,\infty)\times S^1\subseteq C_0$.
nodes.statement_short: The error is supported on the cutoff region near s=4S, where the neck weight is e^{-2 delta S} times the end weight.

nodes.name: Neumann series right inverse
nodes.statement: Let $X$ and $Y$ be Banach spaces, let $D:X\to Y$ and $T:Y\to X$ be bounded, and suppose $\epsilon:=\left\|DT-\mathbf 1_Y\right\|<1$. Then: \begin{equation} Q:=T\cdot\sum_{n\geq 0}(\mathbf 1_Y-DT)^n \end{equation} converges and satisfies $DQ=\mathbf 1_Y$. In addition, we have the following estimates: \begin{equation} \left\|Q\right\|\leq\frac 1{1-\epsilon}\left\|T\right\|\qquad \left\|Q-T\right\|\leq\frac\epsilon{1-\epsilon}\left\|T\right\| \end{equation}
nodes.statement_short: If ||DT - 1|| < 1 then Q = T sum (1-DT)^n is a right inverse of D close to T.
assumptions: Let $X$ and $Y$ be Banach spaces, let $D:X\to Y$ and $T:Y\to X$ be bounded
suppose $\epsilon:=\left\|DT-\mathbf 1_Y\right\|<1$
conclusions: converges and satisfies $DQ=\mathbf 1_Y$
\left\|Q\right\|\leq\frac 1{1-\epsilon}\left\|T\right\|\qquad \left\|Q-T\right\|\leq\frac\epsilon{1-\epsilon}\left\|T\right\|
nodes.label: bootstrapinverse

nodes.name: Displayed equation in Section B.7
nodes.statement: Q:=T\cdot\sum_{n\geq 0}(\mathbf 1_Y-DT)^n

nodes.name: Displayed equation in Section B.7
nodes.statement: \left\|Q\right\|\leq\frac 1{1-\epsilon}\left\|T\right\|\qquad \left\|Q-T\right\|\leq\frac\epsilon{1-\epsilon}\left\|T\right\|

nodes.name: Proof
nodes.statement: Use the telescoping sum $(\mathbf 1-A)\sum_{n\geq 0}A^n=\mathbf 1$ for $\left\|A\right\|<1$.
nodes.statement_short: Telescoping (Neumann) series.

nodes.name: Bootstrapping approximate right inverses
nodes.statement: Suppose we have a diagram of Banach spaces as follows: \begin{equation} \begin{tikzcd} X_1\ar{r}{D_1}&Y_1\ar{d}{B_1}\\ \vdots\ar{u}{G_1}&\vdots\ar{d}{B_{n-2}}\\ X_{n-1}\ar{u}{G_{n-2}}\ar{r}{D_{n-1}}&Y_{n-1}\ar{d}{B_{n-1}}\\ X_n\ar{u}{G_{n-1}}\ar[yshift=0.5ex]{r}{D_n}&Y_n\ar[yshift=-0.5ex]{l}{Q_n} \end{tikzcd} \end{equation} where $\left\|D_i\right\|,\left\|G_i\right\|,\left\|B_i\right\|,\left\|Q_n\right\|\leq c$ and $D_nQ_n=\mathbf 1$. Then for all $\delta>0$ there exists $\epsilon=\epsilon(n,c,\delta)>0$ such that if for all $1<i\leq n$: \begin{equation} D_i\xi=B_{i-1}\eta\implies\left\|D_{i-1}G_{i-1}\xi-\eta\right\|\leq\epsilon\cdot\left\|\xi\right\| \end{equation} then we have: \begin{equation} \left\|D_1G_1\cdots G_{n-1}Q_nB_{n-1}\cdots B_1-\mathbf 1_{Y_1}\right\|\leq\delta \end{equation}
nodes.statement_short: A chain of approximately commuting squares ending in an honest right inverse yields an approximate right inverse at the top.
assumptions: where $\left\|D_i\right\|,\left\|G_i\right\|,\left\|B_i\right\|,\left\|Q_n\right\|\leq c$ and $D_nQ_n=\mathbf 1$
D_i\xi=B_{i-1}\eta\implies\left\|D_{i-1}G_{i-1}\xi-\eta\right\|\leq\epsilon\cdot\left\|\xi\right\|
conclusions: \left\|D_1G_1\cdots G_{n-1}Q_nB_{n-1}\cdots B_1-\mathbf 1_{Y_1}\right\|\leq\delta
nodes.label: bootstrappingapprox

nodes.name: Displayed equation in Section B.7
nodes.statement: \begin{tikzcd} X_1\ar{r}{D_1}&Y_1\ar{d}{B_1}\\ \vdots\ar{u}{G_1}&\vdots\ar{d}{B_{n-2}}\\ X_{n-1}\ar{u}{G_{n-2}}\ar{r}{D_{n-1}}&Y_{n-1}\ar{d}{B_{n-1}}\\ X_n\ar{u}{G_{n-1}}\ar[yshift=0.5ex]{r}{D_n}&Y_n\ar[yshift=-0.5ex]{l}{Q_n} \end{tikzcd}

nodes.name: Approximate commutation hypothesis
nodes.statement: D_i\xi=B_{i-1}\eta\implies\left\|D_{i-1}G_{i-1}\xi-\eta\right\|\leq\epsilon\cdot\left\|\xi\right\|
nodes.label: keytocheckforARI

nodes.name: Approximate right inverse conclusion
nodes.statement: \left\|D_1G_1\cdots G_{n-1}Q_nB_{n-1}\cdots B_1-\mathbf 1_{Y_1}\right\|\leq\delta
nodes.label: approxbootstrappingworks

nodes.name: Proof
nodes.statement: We work by induction on $n$. The case $n=1$ is clear: $\epsilon(1,c,\delta)=\infty$. Now assume $n\geq 2$. Let us also assume without loss of generality that $c\geq 1$. Applying \eqref{keytocheckforARI} to $i=n$ and $\xi=Q_nB_{n-1}\eta$, we see that: \begin{equation} \left\|D_{n-1}G_{n-1}Q_nB_{n-1}-\mathbf 1_{Y_{n-1}}\right\|\leq\epsilon\cdot\left\|Q_n\right\|\left\|B_{n-1}\right\|\leq\epsilon c^2 \end{equation} Let us require that $\epsilon\leq\frac 12c^{-2}$, so the above bound is $\leq\frac 12$. Then by Lemma \ref{bootstrapinverse} applied to $T=G_{n-1}Q_nB_{n-1}$, we see that there exists $Q_{n-1}$ with $D_{n-1}Q_{n-1}=\mathbf 1_{Y_{n-1}}$ and: \begin{equation} \left\|Q_{n-1}\right\|\leq 2c^3\qquad\left\|Q_{n-1}-G_{n-1}Q_nB_{n-1}\right\|\leq 2\epsilon c^5 \end{equation} Now we see that: \begin{multline} \left\|D_1G_1\cdots G_{n-2}G_{n-1}Q_nB_{n-1}B_{n-2}\cdots B_1-D_1G_1\cdots G_{n-2}Q_{n-1}B_{n-2}\cdots B_1\right\|\\ \leq c^{2n-3}\left\|G_{n-1}Q_nB_{n-1}-Q_{n-1}\right\|\leq 2\epsilon c^{2n+2} \end{multline} Let us require that $\epsilon\leq\frac 14\delta c^{-2n-2}$, so the above bound is $\leq\frac 12\delta$. Let us also require that $\epsilon\leq\epsilon(n-1,2c^3,\frac 12\delta)$ (which exists by the induction hypothesis), so that: \begin{equation} \left\|D_1G_1\cdots G_{n-2}Q_{n-1}B_{n-2}\cdots B_1-\mathbf 1_{Y_1}\right\|\leq\frac 12\delta \end{equation} Combining \eqref{approxclosetogiven} and \eqref{inductionbound}, we get the desired bound \eqref{approxbootstrappingworks}.
nodes.statement_short: Induction on n. Build Q_{n-1} from Q_n via the Neumann series lemma, then apply the induction hypothesis to the shorter chain.

nodes.name: Displayed equation in Section B.7
nodes.statement: \left\|D_{n-1}G_{n-1}Q_nB_{n-1}-\mathbf 1_{Y_{n-1}}\right\|\leq\epsilon\cdot\left\|Q_n\right\|\left\|B_{n-1}\right\|\leq\epsilon c^2

nodes.name: Displayed equation in Section B.7
nodes.statement: \left\|Q_{n-1}\right\|\leq 2c^3\qquad\left\|Q_{n-1}-G_{n-1}Q_nB_{n-1}\right\|\leq 2\epsilon c^5

nodes.name: Composition comparison estimate
nodes.statement: \left\|D_1G_1\cdots G_{n-2}G_{n-1}Q_nB_{n-1}B_{n-2}\cdots B_1-D_1G_1\cdots G_{n-2}Q_{n-1}B_{n-2}\cdots B_1\right\|\\ \leq c^{2n-3}\left\|G_{n-1}Q_nB_{n-1}-Q_{n-1}\right\|\leq 2\epsilon c^{2n+2}
nodes.label: approxclosetogiven

nodes.name: Induction bound
nodes.statement: \left\|D_1G_1\cdots G_{n-2}Q_{n-1}B_{n-2}\cdots B_1-\mathbf 1_{Y_1}\right\|\leq\frac 12\delta
nodes.label: inductionbound

nodes.name: Approximate right inverse T_{alpha,y} estimates
nodes.statement: We have: \begin{align} \left\|T_{\alpha,y}\right\|&\leq c\\ \left\|D_{\alpha,y} T_{\alpha,y}-\mathbf 1\right\|&\to 0\\ \operatorname{im} T_{\alpha,y}&\subseteq\ker L_\alpha \end{align} as $(\alpha,y)\to 0$, for $c<\infty$ depending on data which has been previously fixed.
nodes.statement_short: T_{alpha,y} is uniformly bounded, is an asymptotically exact right inverse of D_{alpha,y}, and has image in ker L_alpha.
assumptions: as $(\alpha,y)\to 0$, for $c<\infty$ depending on data which has been previously fixed.
conclusions: \left\|T_{\alpha,y}\right\|&\leq c
\left\|D_{\alpha,y} T_{\alpha,y}-\mathbf 1\right\|&\to 0
\operatorname{im} T_{\alpha,y}&\subseteq\ker L_\alpha
nodes.label: approxworks

nodes.name: Asymptotic right inverse property
nodes.statement: \left\|T_{\alpha,y}\right\|&\leq c\\ \left\|D_{\alpha,y} T_{\alpha,y}-\mathbf 1\right\|&\to 0\\ \operatorname{im} T_{\alpha,y}&\subseteq\ker L_\alpha
nodes.label: Tapproxeqn

nodes.name: Proof
nodes.statement: It is easy to see that all the maps in \eqref{biginversediagram} are uniformly bounded. Hence $\left\|T_{\alpha,y}\right\|\leq c$ as $(\alpha,y)\to 0$. Now Lemma \ref{bootstrappingapprox} combined with Lemmas \ref{approxbottom}, \ref{approxmiddle}, \ref{approxtop} show that for $(\alpha,y)\to 0$, we have $\left\|D_{\alpha,y} T_{\alpha,y}-\mathbf 1\right\|\to 0$. We observed earlier that $\operatorname{im} T_{\alpha,y}\subseteq\ker L_\alpha$.
nodes.statement_short: Uniform bounds on the diagram maps, plus the bootstrapping lemma fed by the three square estimates.

nodes.name: Right inverse Q_{alpha,y}
nodes.statement: We define a map: \begin{equation} Q_{\alpha,y}:W^{k-1,2,\delta}(\tilde C_\alpha,\Omega^{0,1}_{\tilde C_\alpha,j_y}\otimes_\mathbb C u_\alpha^\ast TX)\to W^{k,2,\delta}(C_\alpha,u_\alpha^\ast TX)_D\oplus E \end{equation} as the sum: \begin{equation} Q_{\alpha,y}:=T_{\alpha,y}\sum_{k=0}^\infty(\mathbf 1-D_{\alpha,y} T_{\alpha,y})^k \end{equation}
nodes.statement_short: Q_{alpha,y} is the Neumann-series correction of the approximate right inverse T_{alpha,y}.

nodes.name: Q_{alpha,y} domain and target
nodes.statement: Q_{\alpha,y}:W^{k-1,2,\delta}(\tilde C_\alpha,\Omega^{0,1}_{\tilde C_\alpha,j_y}\otimes_\mathbb C u_\alpha^\ast TX)\to W^{k,2,\delta}(C_\alpha,u_\alpha^\ast TX)_D\oplus E

nodes.name: Neumann series for Q_{alpha,y}
nodes.statement: Q_{\alpha,y}:=T_{\alpha,y}\sum_{k=0}^\infty(\mathbf 1-D_{\alpha,y} T_{\alpha,y})^k

nodes.name: Estimates for the right inverse Q_{alpha,y}
nodes.statement: We have: \begin{align} \left\|Q_{\alpha,y}\right\|&\leq c\\ D_{\alpha,y}Q_{\alpha,y}&=\mathbf 1\\ \operatorname{im} Q_{\alpha,y}&\subseteq\ker L_\alpha \end{align} uniformly over $(\alpha,y)$ in a neighborhood of zero, for $c<\infty$ depending on data which has been previously fixed.
nodes.statement_short: Q_{alpha,y} is a uniformly bounded right inverse of D_{alpha,y} with image in ker L_alpha.
assumptions: uniformly over $(\alpha,y)$ in a neighborhood of zero, for $c<\infty$ depending on data which has been previously fixed.
conclusions: \left\|Q_{\alpha,y}\right\|&\leq c
D_{\alpha,y}Q_{\alpha,y}&=\mathbf 1
\operatorname{im} Q_{\alpha,y}&\subseteq\ker L_\alpha
nodes.label: Qestimates

nodes.name: Displayed equation in Section B.7
nodes.statement: \left\|Q_{\alpha,y}\right\|&\leq c\\ D_{\alpha,y}Q_{\alpha,y}&=\mathbf 1\\ \operatorname{im} Q_{\alpha,y}&\subseteq\ker L_\alpha

nodes.name: Proof
nodes.statement: Apply Lemma \ref{bootstrapinverse} and Proposition \ref{approxworks}.
nodes.statement_short: Neumann series lemma applied to the approximate right inverse.

nodes.name: Quadratic estimate
nodes.statement: There exist $c'>0$ and $c<\infty$ (depending on data which has been previously fixed) such that for $\left\|\xi_1\right\|_{k,2,\delta},\left\|\xi_2\right\|_{k,2,\delta}\leq c'$, we have: \begin{equation} \bigl\|D_{\alpha,y}(\xi_1-\xi_2)-(\mathcal F_{\alpha,y}\xi_1-\mathcal F_{\alpha,y}\xi_2)\bigr\|_{k-1,2,\delta}\leq c\cdot\left\|\xi_1-\xi_2\right\|_{k,2,\delta}(\left\|\xi_1\right\|_{k,2,\delta}+\left\|\xi_2\right\|_{k,2,\delta}) \end{equation} (and $\mathcal F_{\alpha,y}\xi_1$ and $\mathcal F_{\alpha,y}\xi_2$ are both defined), uniformly over $(\alpha,y)$ in a neighborhood of zero.
nodes.statement_short: F_{alpha,y} differs from its linearization by a quadratic error, uniformly in (alpha,y).
assumptions: for $\left\|\xi_1\right\|_{k,2,\delta},\left\|\xi_2\right\|_{k,2,\delta}\leq c'$
uniformly over $(\alpha,y)$ in a neighborhood of zero.
conclusions: \bigl\|D_{\alpha,y}(\xi_1-\xi_2)-(\mathcal F_{\alpha,y}\xi_1-\mathcal F_{\alpha,y}\xi_2)\bigr\|_{k-1,2,\delta}\leq c\cdot\left\|\xi_1-\xi_2\right\|_{k,2,\delta}(\left\|\xi_1\right\|_{k,2,\delta}+\left\|\xi_2\right\|_{k,2,\delta})
nodes.label: quadestimate

nodes.name: Quadratic estimate goal
nodes.statement: \bigl\|D_{\alpha,y}(\xi_1-\xi_2)-(\mathcal F_{\alpha,y}\xi_1-\mathcal F_{\alpha,y}\xi_2)\bigr\|_{k-1,2,\delta}\leq c\cdot\left\|\xi_1-\xi_2\right\|_{k,2,\delta}(\left\|\xi_1\right\|_{k,2,\delta}+\left\|\xi_2\right\|_{k,2,\delta})
nodes.label: quadestgoal

nodes.name: Proof
nodes.statement: This is similar to McDuff--Salamon \cite[p68, Proposition 3.5.3]{mcduffsalamonJholsymp}. We have already remarked that $\mathcal F_{\alpha,y}\xi$ is defined for $\left\|\xi\right\|_{k,2,\delta}\leq c'$. Let $\mathcal F_{\alpha,y}'(\zeta,\xi)$ denote the derivative of $\mathcal F_{\alpha,y}$ at $\zeta$ applied to $\xi$. So, for instance, $D_{\alpha,y}(\xi):=\mathcal F_{\alpha,y}'(0,\xi)$. It suffices to show that: \begin{equation} \left\|\mathcal F_{\alpha,y}'(0,\xi)-\mathcal F_{\alpha,y}'(\zeta,\xi)\right\|_{k-1,2,\delta}\leq c\cdot\left\|\zeta\right\|_{k,2,\delta}\left\|\xi\right\|_{k,2,\delta} \end{equation} for $\left\|\zeta\right\|_{k,2,\delta}\leq c'$ uniformly as $(\alpha,y)\to 0$ (one recovers \eqref{quadestgoal} by integrating $\int_{\xi_1}^{\xi_2}\mathcal F_{\alpha,y}'(0,d\zeta)-\mathcal F_{\alpha,y}'(\zeta,d\zeta)$). For $\zeta\in W^{k,2,\delta}(C_\alpha,u_\alpha^\ast TX)_D\oplus E$, let: \begin{equation} \mathcal F_{\alpha,y,\zeta}:W^{k,2,\delta}(C_\alpha,(\exp_{u_\alpha}\zeta)^\ast TX)_D\oplus E\to W^{k-1,2,\delta}(\tilde C_\alpha,\Omega^{0,1}_{\tilde C_\alpha,j_y}\otimes_\mathbb C(\exp_{u_\alpha}\zeta)^\ast TX) \end{equation} denote the $\bar\partial$-section based at $\exp_{u_\alpha}\zeta:C_\alpha\to X$ and $e_0+\operatorname{proj}_E\zeta$ (so, for example, $\mathcal F_{\alpha,y}:=\mathcal F_{\alpha,y,0}$). Let: \begin{equation} D_{\alpha,y,\zeta}:W^{k,2,\delta}(C_\alpha,(\exp_{u_\alpha}\zeta)^\ast TX)_D\oplus E\to W^{k-1,2,\delta}(\tilde C_\alpha,\Omega^{0,1}_{\tilde C_\alpha,j_y}\otimes_\mathbb C(\exp_{u_\alpha}\zeta)^\ast TX) \end{equation} denote the derivative of $\mathcal F_{\alpha,y,\zeta}$ at zero. Of course, $D_{\alpha,y,\zeta}$ may be calculated as in Lemma \ref{linearizedformula}, and the result is the same (i.e.\ we just substitute $(\exp_{u_\alpha}\zeta,e_0+\operatorname{proj}_E\zeta)$ in place of $(u_\alpha,e_0)$). Now the first step in proving \eqref{derivislip} is to express $\mathcal F_{\alpha,y}'(\zeta,\xi)$ in terms of $D_{\alpha,y,\zeta}$. To do this, we observe that: \begin{equation} \mathcal F_{\alpha,y}(a)=\left[\mathsf{PT}_{\exp_{u_\alpha}a\to u_\alpha}\circ\mathsf{PT}_{\exp_{u_\alpha}\zeta\to\exp_{u_\alpha}a}\right]\left[\mathcal F_{\alpha,y,\zeta}\Bigl((\exp_{\exp_{u_\alpha}\zeta}^{-1}\exp_{u_\alpha}a)\oplus(\operatorname{proj}_Ea-\operatorname{proj}_E\zeta)\Bigr)\right] \end{equation} We now differentiate with respect to $a$ and evaluate at $a=\zeta$ and $\dot a=\xi$. We find: \begin{multline} \mathcal F_{\alpha,y}'(\zeta,\xi)=\Biggl[\frac d{da}\biggr|_{\begin{smallmatrix}a=\zeta\cr\dot a=\xi\end{smallmatrix}}\Bigl(\mathsf{PT}_{\exp_{u_\alpha}a\to u_\alpha}\circ\mathsf{PT}_{\exp_{u_\alpha}\zeta\to\exp_{u_\alpha}a}\Bigr)\Biggr]\bigl(\mathcal F_{\alpha,y,\zeta}(0)\bigr)\\ +\mathsf{PT}_{\exp_{u_\alpha}\zeta\to u_\alpha}\Biggl[D_{\alpha,y,\zeta}\Biggl(\frac d{da}\biggr|_{\begin{smallmatrix}a=\zeta\cr\dot a=\xi\end{smallmatrix}}\Bigl(\exp_{\exp_{u_\alpha}\zeta}^{-1}\exp_{u_\alpha}a\Bigr)\oplus\operatorname{proj}_E\xi\Biggr)\Biggr] \end{multline} We rewrite the first term: \begin{equation} \Biggl[\frac d{da}\biggr|_{\begin{smallmatrix}a=\zeta\cr\dot a=\xi\end{smallmatrix}}\Bigl(\mathsf{PT}_{\exp_{u_\alpha}a\to u_\alpha}\circ\mathsf{PT}_{\exp_{u_\alpha}\zeta\to\exp_{u_\alpha}a}\Bigr)\Biggr]\mathsf{PT}_{u_\alpha\to\exp_{u_\alpha}\zeta}\bigl(\mathcal F_{\alpha,y}(\zeta)\bigr) \end{equation} We know that $\left\|\mathcal F_{\alpha,y}(\zeta)\right\|_{k-1,2,\delta}$ is bounded uniformly for $(\alpha,y)\to 0$ and $\left\|\zeta\right\|_{k,2,\delta}\leq c'$ (Lemma \ref{mappregluingissmall} implies that $\left\|\mathcal F_{\alpha,y}(0)\right\|_{k-1,2,\delta}$ is bounded as $(\alpha,y)\to 0$, and from this one may derive a bound on $\left\|\mathcal F_{\alpha,y}(\zeta)\right\|_{k-1,2,\delta}$ in terms of $\left\|\zeta\right\|_{k,2,\delta}$). The operator $[\frac d{da}(\mathsf{PT}\circ\mathsf{PT})]\mathsf{PT}$ in front is of the form $H(\zeta,\xi)$ for a smooth (non-linear) bundle map $H:TX\oplus TX\to\operatorname{End}(TX)$ (defined in a neighborhood of $\zeta=\xi=0$). Since $H$ satisfies $H(0,\cdot)=H(\cdot,0)=0$, it follows that $\left\|H(\zeta,\xi)\right\|_{k,2,\delta}$ is bounded by $c\cdot\left\|\zeta\right\|_{k,2,\delta}\left\|\xi\right\|_{k,2,\delta}$ for $\left\|\zeta\right\|_{k,2,\delta},\left\|\xi\right\|_{k,2,\delta}\leq c'$. Hence the $\left\|\cdot\right\|_{k-1,2,\delta}$-norm of the first term in \eqref{changebasisderivative} is bounded by $c\cdot\left\|\zeta\right\|_{k,2,\delta}\left\|\xi\right\|_{k,2,\delta}$, so for the purposes of proving \eqref{derivislip} it may be ignored. The second term in \eqref{changebasisderivative} is approximated by $\mathsf{PT}_{\exp_{u_\alpha}\zeta\to u_\alpha}\left[D_{\alpha,y,\zeta}\left(\mathsf{PT}_{u_\alpha\to\exp_{u_\alpha}\zeta}\xi\right)\right]$ with error: \begin{equation} \mathsf{PT}_{\exp_{u_\alpha}\zeta\to u_\alpha}\Biggl[D_{\alpha,y,\zeta}\Biggl(\biggl[\mathsf{PT}_{u_\alpha\to\exp_{u_\alpha}\zeta}\xi-\frac d{da}\biggr|_{\begin{smallmatrix}a=\zeta\cr\dot a=\xi\end{smallmatrix}}\Bigl(\exp_{\exp_{u_\alpha}\zeta}^{-1}\exp_{u_\alpha}a\Bigr)\biggr]\oplus 0\Biggr)\Biggr] \end{equation} which we may write as: \begin{equation} \mathsf{PT}_{\exp_{u_\alpha}\zeta\to u_\alpha}\Biggl[D_{\alpha,y,\zeta}\Biggl(\mathsf{PT}_{u_\alpha\to\exp_{u_\alpha}\zeta}\biggl[\xi-\mathsf{PT}_{\exp_{u_\alpha}\zeta\to u_\alpha}\frac d{da}\biggr|_{\begin{smallmatrix}a=\zeta\cr\dot a=\xi\end{smallmatrix}}\Bigl(\exp_{\exp_{u_\alpha}\zeta}^{-1}\exp_{u_\alpha}a\Bigr)\biggr]\oplus 0\Biggr)\Biggr] \end{equation} Now the $\left\|\cdot\right\|_{(k-1,2,\delta)\to(k-1,2,\delta)}$ norm of the outer $\mathsf{PT}$ is bounded uniformly for $(\alpha,y)\to 0$ and $\left\|\zeta\right\|_{k,2,\delta}\leq c'$, as is the $\left\|\cdot\right\|_{(k,2,\delta)\to(k-1,2,\delta)}$ norm of $D_{\alpha,y,\zeta}$ and the $\left\|\cdot\right\|_{(k,2,\delta)\to(k,2,\delta)}$ norm of the following $\mathsf{PT}$. The difference $\xi-\mathsf{PT}\frac d{da}()$ is of the form $H(\zeta,\xi)$ for a smooth (non-linear) bundle map $H:TX\oplus TX\to TX$ (defined in a neighborhood of $\zeta=\xi=0$). Since $H$ satisfies $H(0,\cdot)=H(\cdot,0)=0$, it follows that $\left\|H(\zeta,\xi)\right\|_{k,2,\delta}$ is bounded by $c\cdot\left\|\zeta\right\|_{k,2,\delta}\left\|\xi\right\|_{k,2,\delta}$ for $\left\|\zeta\right\|_{k,2,\delta},\left\|\xi\right\|_{k,2,\delta}\leq c'$. Hence the error \eqref{errorexpression} has $\left\|\cdot\right\|_{k-1,2,\delta}$ bounded by $c\cdot\left\|\zeta\right\|_{k,2,\delta}\left\|\xi\right\|_{k,2,\delta}$. Thus we have reduced the estimate \eqref{derivislip} to proving: \begin{equation} \left\|D_{\alpha,y}-\mathsf{PT}_{\exp_{u_\alpha}\zeta\to u}\circ D_{\alpha,y,\zeta}\circ\mathsf{PT}_{u_\alpha\to\exp_{u_\alpha}\zeta}\right\|_{(k,2,\delta)\to(k-1,2,\delta)}\leq c\cdot\left\|\zeta\right\|_{k,2,\delta} \end{equation} We calculated $D_{\alpha,y}$ in Lemma \ref{linearizedformula}, and $D_{\alpha,y,\zeta}$ may be expressed in exactly the same way (specifically, it is obtained by taking the expression for $D_{\alpha,y}$ and replacing every occurence of $u_\alpha$ with $\exp_{u_\alpha}\zeta$ and $e_0$ by $e_0+\operatorname{proj}_E\zeta$). Now we compare term by term to prove \eqref{quadreducedtoPTcomp}. We omit the details of this calculation.
nodes.statement_short: Following McDuff-Salamon: reduce to a Lipschitz bound on the derivative of F, change base point to exp(zeta), and bound the error terms via bundle maps vanishing to second order; final term-by-term comparison omitted.

nodes.name: Lipschitz derivative estimate
nodes.statement: \left\|\mathcal F_{\alpha,y}'(0,\xi)-\mathcal F_{\alpha,y}'(\zeta,\xi)\right\|_{k-1,2,\delta}\leq c\cdot\left\|\zeta\right\|_{k,2,\delta}\left\|\xi\right\|_{k,2,\delta}
nodes.label: derivislip

nodes.name: Based section F_{alpha,y,zeta}
nodes.statement: \mathcal F_{\alpha,y,\zeta}:W^{k,2,\delta}(C_\alpha,(\exp_{u_\alpha}\zeta)^\ast TX)_D\oplus E\to W^{k-1,2,\delta}(\tilde C_\alpha,\Omega^{0,1}_{\tilde C_\alpha,j_y}\otimes_\mathbb C(\exp_{u_\alpha}\zeta)^\ast TX)

nodes.name: Linearization D_{alpha,y,zeta}
nodes.statement: D_{\alpha,y,\zeta}:W^{k,2,\delta}(C_\alpha,(\exp_{u_\alpha}\zeta)^\ast TX)_D\oplus E\to W^{k-1,2,\delta}(\tilde C_\alpha,\Omega^{0,1}_{\tilde C_\alpha,j_y}\otimes_\mathbb C(\exp_{u_\alpha}\zeta)^\ast TX)

nodes.name: Change of base point formula
nodes.statement: \mathcal F_{\alpha,y}(a)=\left[\mathsf{PT}_{\exp_{u_\alpha}a\to u_\alpha}\circ\mathsf{PT}_{\exp_{u_\alpha}\zeta\to\exp_{u_\alpha}a}\right]\left[\mathcal F_{\alpha,y,\zeta}\Bigl((\exp_{\exp_{u_\alpha}\zeta}^{-1}\exp_{u_\alpha}a)\oplus(\operatorname{proj}_Ea-\operatorname{proj}_E\zeta)\Bigr)\right]

nodes.name: Change of basis derivative
nodes.statement: \mathcal F_{\alpha,y}'(\zeta,\xi)=\Biggl[\frac d{da}\biggr|_{\begin{smallmatrix}a=\zeta\cr\dot a=\xi\end{smallmatrix}}\Bigl(\mathsf{PT}_{\exp_{u_\alpha}a\to u_\alpha}\circ\mathsf{PT}_{\exp_{u_\alpha}\zeta\to\exp_{u_\alpha}a}\Bigr)\Biggr]\bigl(\mathcal F_{\alpha,y,\zeta}(0)\bigr)\\ +\mathsf{PT}_{\exp_{u_\alpha}\zeta\to u_\alpha}\Biggl[D_{\alpha,y,\zeta}\Biggl(\frac d{da}\biggr|_{\begin{smallmatrix}a=\zeta\cr\dot a=\xi\end{smallmatrix}}\Bigl(\exp_{\exp_{u_\alpha}\zeta}^{-1}\exp_{u_\alpha}a\Bigr)\oplus\operatorname{proj}_E\xi\Biggr)\Biggr]
nodes.label: changebasisderivative

nodes.name: Displayed equation in Section B.8
nodes.statement: \Biggl[\frac d{da}\biggr|_{\begin{smallmatrix}a=\zeta\cr\dot a=\xi\end{smallmatrix}}\Bigl(\mathsf{PT}_{\exp_{u_\alpha}a\to u_\alpha}\circ\mathsf{PT}_{\exp_{u_\alpha}\zeta\to\exp_{u_\alpha}a}\Bigr)\Biggr]\mathsf{PT}_{u_\alpha\to\exp_{u_\alpha}\zeta}\bigl(\mathcal F_{\alpha,y}(\zeta)\bigr)

nodes.name: Error expression
nodes.statement: \mathsf{PT}_{\exp_{u_\alpha}\zeta\to u_\alpha}\Biggl[D_{\alpha,y,\zeta}\Biggl(\biggl[\mathsf{PT}_{u_\alpha\to\exp_{u_\alpha}\zeta}\xi-\frac d{da}\biggr|_{\begin{smallmatrix}a=\zeta\cr\dot a=\xi\end{smallmatrix}}\Bigl(\exp_{\exp_{u_\alpha}\zeta}^{-1}\exp_{u_\alpha}a\Bigr)\biggr]\oplus 0\Biggr)\Biggr]
nodes.label: errorexpression

nodes.name: Displayed equation in Section B.8
nodes.statement: \mathsf{PT}_{\exp_{u_\alpha}\zeta\to u_\alpha}\Biggl[D_{\alpha,y,\zeta}\Biggl(\mathsf{PT}_{u_\alpha\to\exp_{u_\alpha}\zeta}\biggl[\xi-\mathsf{PT}_{\exp_{u_\alpha}\zeta\to u_\alpha}\frac d{da}\biggr|_{\begin{smallmatrix}a=\zeta\cr\dot a=\xi\end{smallmatrix}}\Bigl(\exp_{\exp_{u_\alpha}\zeta}^{-1}\exp_{u_\alpha}a\Bigr)\biggr]\oplus 0\Biggr)\Biggr]

nodes.name: Reduced estimate via parallel transport
nodes.statement: \left\|D_{\alpha,y}-\mathsf{PT}_{\exp_{u_\alpha}\zeta\to u}\circ D_{\alpha,y,\zeta}\circ\mathsf{PT}_{u_\alpha\to\exp_{u_\alpha}\zeta}\right\|_{(k,2,\delta)\to(k-1,2,\delta)}\leq c\cdot\left\|\zeta\right\|_{k,2,\delta}
nodes.label: quadreducedtoPTcomp

nodes.name: Contraction property
nodes.statement: There exists $c'>0$ (depending on data which has been previously fixed) such that for sufficiently small $(\alpha,y)$: \begin{rlist} \item The map $\mathcal F_{\alpha,y}$ is defined for $\left\|\xi\right\|_{k,2,\delta}\leq c'$. \item For $\xi_1-\xi_2\in\operatorname{im} Q_{\alpha,y}$ and $\left\|\xi_1\right\|_{k,2,\delta},\left\|\xi_2\right\|_{k,2,\delta}\leq c'$, we have: \begin{equation} \left\|(\xi_1-\xi_2)-(Q_{\alpha,y}\mathcal F_{\alpha,y}\xi_1-Q_{\alpha,y}\mathcal F_{\alpha,y}\xi_2)\right\|_{k,2,\delta}\leq\frac 12\left\|\xi_1-\xi_2\right\|_{k,2,\delta} \end{equation} \end{rlist}
nodes.statement_short: On a small ball, xi -> xi - Q F xi is a 1/2-contraction along im Q_{alpha,y}.
assumptions: for sufficiently small $(\alpha,y)$
For $\xi_1-\xi_2\in\operatorname{im} Q_{\alpha,y}$ and $\left\|\xi_1\right\|_{k,2,\delta},\left\|\xi_2\right\|_{k,2,\delta}\leq c'$
conclusions: The map $\mathcal F_{\alpha,y}$ is defined for $\left\|\xi\right\|_{k,2,\delta}\leq c'$.
\left\|(\xi_1-\xi_2)-(Q_{\alpha,y}\mathcal F_{\alpha,y}\xi_1-Q_{\alpha,y}\mathcal F_{\alpha,y}\xi_2)\right\|_{k,2,\delta}\leq\frac 12\left\|\xi_1-\xi_2\right\|_{k,2,\delta}
nodes.label: contractionprop

nodes.name: Displayed equation in Section B.9
nodes.statement: \left\|(\xi_1-\xi_2)-(Q_{\alpha,y}\mathcal F_{\alpha,y}\xi_1-Q_{\alpha,y}\mathcal F_{\alpha,y}\xi_2)\right\|_{k,2,\delta}\leq\frac 12\left\|\xi_1-\xi_2\right\|_{k,2,\delta}

nodes.name: Proof
nodes.statement: The first assertion has been shown earlier. For the second, write: \begin{multline} \left\|(\xi_1-\xi_2)-(Q_{\alpha,y}\mathcal F_{\alpha,y}\xi_1-Q_{\alpha,y}\mathcal F_{\alpha,y}\xi_2)\right\|_{k,2,\delta}\\ =\left\|Q_{\alpha,y}D_{\alpha,y}(\xi_1-\xi_2)-(Q_{\alpha,y}\mathcal F_{\alpha,y}\xi_1-Q_{\alpha,y}\mathcal F_{\alpha,y}\xi_2)\right\|_{k,2,\delta}\\ \leq\left\|Q_{\alpha,y}\right\|\left\|D_{\alpha,y}(\xi_1-\xi_2)-(\mathcal F_{\alpha,y}\xi_1-\mathcal F_{\alpha,y}\xi_2)\right\|_{k-1,2,\delta}\\ \leq c\cdot\left\|Q_{\alpha,y}\right\|\left\|\xi_1-\xi_2\right\|_{k,2,\delta}(\left\|\xi_1\right\|_{k,2,\delta}+\left\|\xi_2\right\|_{k,2,\delta}) \end{multline} by Proposition \ref{quadestimate}. Since $\left\|Q_{\alpha,y}\right\|$ is uniformly bounded, this is enough.
nodes.statement_short: Write the difference as Q applied to the quadratic error and use the quadratic estimate with the bound on Q.

nodes.name: Displayed equation in Section B.9
nodes.statement: \left\|(\xi_1-\xi_2)-(Q_{\alpha,y}\mathcal F_{\alpha,y}\xi_1-Q_{\alpha,y}\mathcal F_{\alpha,y}\xi_2)\right\|_{k,2,\delta}\\ =\left\|Q_{\alpha,y}D_{\alpha,y}(\xi_1-\xi_2)-(Q_{\alpha,y}\mathcal F_{\alpha,y}\xi_1-Q_{\alpha,y}\mathcal F_{\alpha,y}\xi_2)\right\|_{k,2,\delta}\\ \leq\left\|Q_{\alpha,y}\right\|\left\|D_{\alpha,y}(\xi_1-\xi_2)-(\mathcal F_{\alpha,y}\xi_1-\mathcal F_{\alpha,y}\xi_2)\right\|_{k-1,2,\delta}\\ \leq c\cdot\left\|Q_{\alpha,y}\right\|\left\|\xi_1-\xi_2\right\|_{k,2,\delta}(\left\|\xi_1\right\|_{k,2,\delta}+\left\|\xi_2\right\|_{k,2,\delta})

nodes.name: Newton--Picard iteration
nodes.statement: There exists $c'>0$ (depending on data which has been previously fixed) so that for $(\alpha,y,\kappa\in K)$ sufficiently small, there exists a unique $\kappa_{\alpha,y}\in W^{k,2,\delta}(C_\alpha,u_\alpha^\ast TX)_D\oplus E$ satisfying: \begin{align} \kappa_{\alpha,y}&\in\kappa_\alpha+\operatorname{im} Q_{\alpha,y}\\ \left\|\kappa_{\alpha,y}\right\|_{k,2,\delta}&\leq c'\\ \mathcal F_{\alpha,y}\kappa_{\alpha,y}&=0 \end{align}
nodes.statement_short: For small (alpha,y,kappa) there is a unique small zero kappa_{alpha,y} of F_{alpha,y} in kappa_alpha + im Q_{alpha,y}.
assumptions: for $(\alpha,y,\kappa\in K)$ sufficiently small
conclusions: there exists a unique $\kappa_{\alpha,y}\in W^{k,2,\delta}(C_\alpha,u_\alpha^\ast TX)_D\oplus E$ satisfying:
nodes.label: newtoniteration

nodes.name: Displayed equation in Section B.9
nodes.statement: \kappa_{\alpha,y}&\in\kappa_\alpha+\operatorname{im} Q_{\alpha,y}\\ \left\|\kappa_{\alpha,y}\right\|_{k,2,\delta}&\leq c'\\ \mathcal F_{\alpha,y}\kappa_{\alpha,y}&=0

nodes.name: Proof
nodes.statement: In fact, we will show that $\kappa_{\alpha,y}$ is given explicitly as the limit of the Newton iteration: \begin{align} \xi_0&:=\kappa_\alpha\\ \xi_n&:=\xi_{n-1}-Q_{\alpha,y}\mathcal F_{\alpha,y}\xi_{n-1} \end{align} By Lemma \ref{contractionprop}, the map $\xi\mapsto\xi-Q_{\alpha,y}\mathcal F_{\alpha,y}\xi$ is a $\frac 12$-contraction mapping when restricted to: \begin{equation} \{\xi\in\kappa_\alpha+\operatorname{im} Q_{\alpha,y}:\left\|\xi\right\|_{k,2,\delta}\leq c'\} \end{equation} To finish the proof, it suffices to show that (for sufficiently small $(\alpha,y,\kappa)$) \eqref{domainofcontraction} is nonempty and is mapped to itself by $\xi\mapsto\xi-Q_{\alpha,y}\mathcal F_{\alpha,y}\xi$. We know that $\left\|\kappa_\alpha\right\|_{k,2,\delta}\to 0$ as $\kappa\to 0$ (uniformly in $(\alpha,y)$), so \eqref{domainofcontraction} is nonempty. By using Proposition \ref{quadestimate} with $(\xi_1,\xi_2)=(0,\kappa_\alpha)$ and Lemmas \ref{mappregluingissmall} and \ref{pregluingKestimate}, we conclude that: \begin{equation} \left\|\mathcal F_{\alpha,y}\kappa_\alpha\right\|_{k-1,2,\delta}\to 0 \end{equation} as $(\alpha,y,\kappa)\to 0$. Since the operator norm of $Q_{\alpha,y}$ is bounded uniformly as $(\alpha,y)\to 0$, we see that $\kappa_\alpha$ is almost fixed by $\xi\mapsto\xi-Q_{\alpha,y}\mathcal F_{\alpha,y}\xi$ as $(\alpha,y,\kappa)\to 0$. It then follows from the contraction property that $\xi\mapsto\xi-Q_{\alpha,y}\mathcal F_{\alpha,y}\xi$ maps \eqref{domainofcontraction} to itself.
nodes.statement_short: Contraction mapping principle for the Newton iteration xi -> xi - Q F xi on a ball in kappa_alpha + im Q; the pregluing estimates show the ball is nonempty and invariant.

nodes.name: Newton iteration
nodes.statement: \xi_0&:=\kappa_\alpha\\ \xi_n&:=\xi_{n-1}-Q_{\alpha,y}\mathcal F_{\alpha,y}\xi_{n-1}

nodes.name: Domain of contraction

nodes.name: Gluing map
nodes.statement: We define: \begin{align} u_{\alpha,y,\kappa}&:=\exp_{u_\alpha}\kappa_{\alpha,y}\\ e_{\alpha,y,\kappa}&:=e_0+\operatorname{proj}_E\kappa_{\alpha,y} \end{align} where $\kappa_{\alpha,y}$ is as in Proposition \ref{newtoniteration}, and we consider the map: \begin{align} \mathbb C^d\times\mathbb R^{\dim\overline{\mathcal M}^d}\times K&\to\overline{\mathcal M}(X)\\ (\alpha,y,\kappa)&\mapsto(\alpha,y,u_{\alpha,y,\kappa},e_{\alpha,y,\kappa}) \end{align} (with $\{x_i\}$ understood). It follows from the definition that \eqref{gluingmap} commutes with the projection from both sides to $\overline{\mathcal M}\times E/E'$.
nodes.statement_short: (alpha,y,kappa) maps to (alpha,y, exp_{u_alpha} kappa_{alpha,y}, e_0 + proj_E kappa_{alpha,y}), commuting with projection to M x E/E'.

nodes.statement: u_{\alpha,y,\kappa}&:=\exp_{u_\alpha}\kappa_{\alpha,y}\\ e_{\alpha,y,\kappa}&:=e_0+\operatorname{proj}_E\kappa_{\alpha,y}

nodes.name: Gluing lands in the regular locus
nodes.statement: The gluing map \eqref{gluingmap} maps sufficiently small $(\alpha,y,\kappa)$ to $\overline{\mathcal M}(X)^\mathrm{reg}$.
nodes.statement_short: Small gluing parameters map into the regular locus.
assumptions: sufficiently small $(\alpha,y,\kappa)$
conclusions: The gluing map \eqref{gluingmap} maps sufficiently small $(\alpha,y,\kappa)$ to $\overline{\mathcal M}(X)^\mathrm{reg}$.

nodes.name: Proof
nodes.statement: This is true since $Q_{\alpha,y}$ gives an approximate right inverse at $(u_{\alpha,y,\kappa},e_{\alpha,y,\kappa})$ (use \eqref{derivislip} with $\zeta=\kappa_{\alpha,y}$).
nodes.statement_short: Q_{alpha,y} remains an approximate right inverse at the glued point by the Lipschitz derivative estimate.

nodes.name: Preglued kernel K_alpha
nodes.statement: Let $K_\alpha\subseteq C^\infty(C_\alpha,u_\alpha^\ast TX)_D\oplus E$ denote the image of $\kappa\mapsto\kappa_\alpha$.

nodes.name: Argument for the splitting im Q + K_alpha
nodes.statement: It is clear by definition that $K\to K_\alpha$ is an isomorphism, and the respective $W^{k,2,\delta}$ norms are uniformly commensurable. It is also clear that the following commutes: \begin{equation} \begin{tikzcd}[column sep = tiny] K\ar{dr}[swap]{L_0}\ar{rr}{\kappa\mapsto\kappa_\alpha}&&K_\alpha\ar{dl}{L_\alpha}\\ &W \end{tikzcd} \end{equation} (all maps being isomorphisms). Since $\operatorname{im} Q_{\alpha,y}\subseteq\ker L_\alpha$, it follows in particular that $\operatorname{im} Q_{\alpha,y}\cap K_\alpha=0$. On the other hand, an index calculation shows that $\operatorname{ind} D_{\alpha,y}=\operatorname{ind} D_{0,0}$ (note that by Lemma \ref{fredholmandsamekernelcokernel}, it suffices to calculate their indices as operators $W^{k,2}\to W^{k-1,2}$ on $\tilde C_\alpha$ and $\tilde C_0$ respectively, and this is a standard calculation as in McDuff--Salamon \cite{mcduffsalamonJholsymp}). Both are surjective, and hence we have $\dim\operatorname{coker} Q_{\alpha,y}=\dim\ker D_{\alpha,y}=\dim\ker D_{0,0}=\dim K=\dim K_\alpha$.
nodes.statement_short: im Q meets K_alpha trivially (image in ker L_alpha), and an index count gives complementary dimensions.

nodes.name: Compatibility of L_0 and L_alpha on kernels
nodes.statement: \begin{tikzcd}[column sep = tiny] K\ar{dr}[swap]{L_0}\ar{rr}{\kappa\mapsto\kappa_\alpha}&&K_\alpha\ar{dl}{L_\alpha}\\ &W \end{tikzcd}
nodes.label: Lonkernelisgood

nodes.name: Splitting im Q_{alpha,y} + K_alpha
nodes.statement: It follows that $\operatorname{im} Q_{\alpha,y}=\ker L_\alpha$ and that: \begin{equation} \operatorname{im} Q_{\alpha,y}\oplus K_\alpha\xrightarrow\sim W^{k,2,\delta}(C_\alpha,u_\alpha^\ast TX)_D\oplus E \end{equation} is an isomorphism of Banach spaces.

nodes.name: Splitting im Q + K_alpha
nodes.statement: \operatorname{im} Q_{\alpha,y}\oplus K_\alpha\xrightarrow\sim W^{k,2,\delta}(C_\alpha,u_\alpha^\ast TX)_D\oplus E
nodes.label: QKtoall

nodes.name: Uniform commensurability of splitting norms
nodes.statement: We claim that in fact the two norms are uniformly commensurable as $(\alpha,y)\to 0$.

nodes.name: Proof of uniform commensurability
nodes.statement: The map written is clearly uniformly bounded, so we just need to show the same for its inverse. It suffices to show that the projection from the right hand side to $K_\alpha$ is uniformly bounded, but this is nothing other than $L_\alpha$ (clearly uniformly bounded) composed with the inverse of the isomorphism in \eqref{Lonkernelisgood} (also uniformly bounded).
nodes.statement_short: The projection to K_alpha is L_alpha followed by the inverse of a uniformly bounded isomorphism.

nodes.name: Injectivity of gluing
nodes.statement: The map \eqref{gluingmap} is injective in a neighborhood of zero.
nodes.statement_short: The gluing map is locally injective.
conclusions: The map \eqref{gluingmap} is injective in a neighborhood of zero.
nodes.label: gluingisinjective

nodes.name: Proof
nodes.statement: Suppose that: \begin{equation} (\alpha,y,u_{\alpha,y,\kappa},e_{\alpha,y,\kappa})=(\alpha',y',u_{\alpha',y',\kappa'},e_{\alpha',y',\kappa'}) \end{equation} We see immediately that $(\alpha,y)=(\alpha',y')$. Now we see that: \begin{align} \exp_{u_\alpha}\kappa_{\alpha,y}&=\exp_{u_\alpha}(\kappa')_{\alpha,y}\\ \operatorname{proj}_E\kappa_{\alpha,y}&=\operatorname{proj}_E(\kappa')_{\alpha,y} \end{align} Since the norms of $\kappa_{\alpha,y}$ and $\kappa_{\alpha,y}'$ go to zero as $(\alpha,y,\kappa,\kappa')\to 0$ (in $W^{k,2,\delta}$, and hence in $C^0$) and the injectivity radius of the exponential map is fixed, we see that $\kappa_{\alpha,y}=(\kappa')_{\alpha,y}$. It follows that $\kappa_\alpha-(\kappa')_\alpha\in\operatorname{im} Q_{\alpha,y}$, but since $K_\alpha\cap\operatorname{im} Q_{\alpha,y}=0$ we conclude $\kappa_\alpha=(\kappa')_\alpha$ and hence $\kappa=\kappa'$.
nodes.statement_short: Equal images force equal (alpha,y) and equal corrections; transversality of K_alpha and im Q then forces kappa = kappa'.

nodes.name: Displayed equation in Section B.10
nodes.statement: (\alpha,y,u_{\alpha,y,\kappa},e_{\alpha,y,\kappa})=(\alpha',y',u_{\alpha',y',\kappa'},e_{\alpha',y',\kappa'})

nodes.statement: \exp_{u_\alpha}\kappa_{\alpha,y}&=\exp_{u_\alpha}(\kappa')_{\alpha,y}\\ \operatorname{proj}_E\kappa_{\alpha,y}&=\operatorname{proj}_E(\kappa')_{\alpha,y}

nodes.name: Continuity of gluing
nodes.statement: The map \eqref{gluingmap} is continuous in a neighborhood of zero.
nodes.statement_short: The gluing map is continuous near zero.
conclusions: The map \eqref{gluingmap} is continuous in a neighborhood of zero.
nodes.label: continuityofgluing

nodes.name: A priori estimate on long pseudo-holomorphic necks
nodes.statement: For all $\mu<1$, there exists $\epsilon>0$ with the following property. Let $J$ be a smooth almost complex structure on $B^{2n}(1)\subseteq\mathbb R^{2n}$ satisfying $\left\|J-J_\mathrm{std}\right\|_{C^2}\leq\epsilon$ (measured with respect to $g_\mathrm{std}$). There exists $c_k<\infty$ depending only on $\left\|J\right\|_{C^k}$ with the following property. Let $u:[-R,R]\times S^1\to B^{2n}(1)$ be $J$-holomorphic. If: \begin{equation} \int_{\partial[-R,R]\times S^1}\Bigl|\frac{du}{dt}\Bigr|^2\,dt<\epsilon \end{equation} Then: \begin{equation} \left|(D^ku)(s,t)\right|\leq c_k\cdot e^{\mu\cdot(\left|s\right|-R)}\left(\int_{\partial[-R,R]\times S^1}\Bigl|\frac{du}{dt}\Bigr|^2\,dt\right)^{1/2} \end{equation} for $\left|s\right|\leq R-1$.
nodes.statement_short: Holomorphic cylinders with small boundary energy decay exponentially toward the middle in all C^k norms.
nodes.origin_citation: McDuff--Salamon, J-holomorphic curves and symplectic topology (well-known)

nodes.name: Proof
nodes.statement: First, apply Lemma \ref{energydecayexponential} to get an exponential decay bound on the $W^{1,2}$ norm of $u$ restricted to $[-r,r]\times S^1$. Second, apply Lemma \ref{energycontrolsWoneinfty} to conclude that the bound on the $W^{1,2}$ norm implies a similar bound on the $W^{1,\infty}$ norm. Finally, apply elliptic bootstrapping Lemma \ref{Woneinftycontrolsall} to conclude that the bound on the $W^{1,\infty}$ norm implies a similar bound on the $C^k$ norm for all $k<\infty$.
nodes.statement_short: Chain three lemmas: exponential decay of W^{1,2} norm, W^{1,2} controls W^{1,infinity}, and elliptic bootstrapping to C^k.

nodes.name: W^{1,2} norm decays exponentially
nodes.statement: For all $\mu<1$, there exists $\epsilon>0$ with the following property. Let $u:[-R,R]\times S^1\to B^{2n}(1)$ be $J$-holomorphic for an almost complex structure $J$ on $B^{2n}(1)\subseteq\mathbb R^{2n}$ satisfying $\left\|J-J_\mathrm{std}\right\|\leq\epsilon$ (measured with respect to $g_\mathrm{std}$). Then: \begin{equation*} \left(\int_{[-r,r]\times S^1}\biggl[\Bigl|\frac{du}{ds}\Bigr|^2+\Bigl|\frac{du}{dt}\Bigr|^2\biggr]\,ds\,dt\right)^{1/2}\leq c\cdot e^{\mu\cdot(r-R)}\left(\int_{\partial[-R,R]\times S^1}\Bigl|\frac{du}{dt}\Bigr|^2\,dt\right)^{1/2} \end{equation*} for $0\leq r\leq R$.
nodes.statement_short: On a long holomorphic cylinder the energy on [-r,r] decays like e^{mu(r-R)} relative to the boundary energy.
nodes.origin_citation: McDuff--Salamon, J-holomorphic curves and symplectic topology, Lemma 4.7.3
assumptions: For all $\mu<1$

conclusions: for $0\leq r\leq R$.

nodes.name: Proof
nodes.statement: This proof is essentially lifted from McDuff--Salamon \cite[p99, Lemma 4.7.3]{mcduffsalamonJholsymp}. Let $\lambda_\mathrm{std}:=\frac 12\sum_jx_j\,dy_j-y_j\,dx_j$. Note the identity: \begin{equation} \sum_jz_j\,d\bar z_j=\frac 12\sum_jd\left|z_j\right|^2-2i\lambda_\mathrm{std} \end{equation} Let $\gamma:S^1\to\mathbb R^{2n}$ be a smooth loop. Write the Fourier series $\gamma(t)=\sum_ka_ke^{ikt}\in\mathbb C^n$ where $a_k\in\mathbb C^n$. Now using \eqref{zdzbaridentity}, we see that: \begin{equation*} \int_{S^1}\gamma^\ast\lambda_\mathrm{std}=\frac i2\int_{S^1}\sum_j\gamma^\ast(z_j\,d\bar z_j)=\frac i2\int_{S^1}\sum_{k,\ell}a_k\bar a_\ell(-i\ell)e^{i(k-\ell)t}\,dt=\pi\sum_kk\left|a_k\right|^2 \end{equation*} We may also calculate: \begin{equation} \int_{S^1}\Bigl|\frac{d\gamma}{dt}\Bigr|^2\,dt=\int_{S^1}\sum_{k,\ell}a_k\bar a_\ell(ik)(-i\ell)e^{i(k-\ell)t}\,dt=2\pi\sum_kk^2\left|a_k\right|^2 \end{equation} Hence we conclude that: \begin{equation} \left|\int_{S^1}\gamma^\ast\lambda_\mathrm{std}\right|\leq\frac 12\int_{S^1}\Bigl|\frac{d\gamma}{dt}\Bigr|^2\,dt \end{equation} Let: \begin{equation} E(r):=\int_{[-r,r]\times S^1}\Bigl|\frac{du}{dt}\Bigr|^2\,ds\,dt\approx\int_{[-r,r]\times S^1}u^\ast\omega_\mathrm{std}=\int_{\partial[-r,r]\times S^1}u^\ast\lambda_\mathrm{std} \end{equation} ($\approx$ means equality up to a factor which can be made arbitrarily close to $1$ by taking $\epsilon>0$ sufficiently small). Applying \eqref{sympisoperimetric}, we conclude that: \begin{equation} E(r)\lesssim\frac 12\int_{\partial[-r,r]\times S^1}\Bigl|\frac{du}{dt}\Bigr|^2\,dt \end{equation} ($\lesssim$ means inequality up to a factor which can be made arbitrarily close to $1$ by taking $\epsilon>0$ sufficiently small). The right hand side above equals $\frac 12E'(r)$, so we have $E'(r)\gtrsim 2E(r)$, and hence $E'(r)\geq 2\mu E(r)$ (for $\epsilon>0$ sufficiently small), from which we conclude that $E(r)\leq e^{2\mu\cdot(r-R)}E(R)$. Using \eqref{boundonenergyfromboundary} to bound $E(R)$, we see that: \begin{equation} E(r)\lesssim e^{2\mu\cdot(r-R)}\frac 12\int_{\partial[-R,R]\times S^1}\Bigl|\frac{du}{dt}\Bigr|^2\,dt \end{equation} We have: \begin{equation} E(r)\approx\frac 12\int_{[-r,r]\times S^1}\biggl[\Bigl|\frac{du}{ds}\Bigr|^2+\Bigl|\frac{du}{dt}\Bigr|^2\biggr]\,ds\,dt \end{equation} Hence we conclude that: \begin{equation} \int_{[-r,r]\times S^1}\biggl[\Bigl|\frac{du}{ds}\Bigr|^2+\Bigl|\frac{du}{dt}\Bigr|^2\biggr]\,ds\,dt\lesssim e^{ 2\mu\cdot(r-R)}\int_{\partial[-R,R]\times S^1}\Bigl|\frac{du}{dt}\Bigr|^2\,dt \end{equation} which is the desired estimate.
nodes.statement_short: Isoperimetric inequality for loops via Fourier series gives the differential inequality E' >= 2 mu E, which integrates to exponential decay.

nodes.name: W^{1,2} controls W^{1,infinity}
nodes.statement: Let $J$ be an almost complex structure on $B^{2n}(1)\subseteq\mathbb R^{2n}$; there exist $\epsilon>0$ and $c<\infty$, depending only on $\left\|J\right\|_{C^2}$ (measured with respect to $g_\mathrm{std}$) with the following property. Let $u:[0,1]\times[0,1]\to B^{2n}(1)$ be $J$-holomorphic, and suppose that: \begin{equation} \int_{[0,1]^2}\biggl[\Bigl|\frac{du}{dx}\Bigr|^2+\Bigl|\frac{du}{dy}\Bigr|^2\biggr]\,dx\,dy<\epsilon \end{equation} Then we have: \begin{equation} \Bigl|\frac{du}{dx}({\textstyle\frac 12},{\textstyle\frac 12})\Bigr|+\Bigl|\frac{du}{dy}({\textstyle\frac 12},{\textstyle\frac 12})\Bigr|\leq c\cdot\left(\int_{[0,1]^2}\biggl[\Bigl|\frac{du}{dx}\Bigr|^2+\Bigl|\frac{du}{dy}\Bigr|^2\biggr]\,dx\,dy\right)^{1/2} \end{equation}
nodes.statement_short: For J-holomorphic maps from the square with small energy, the derivative at the center is bounded by the L^2 norm of the derivative.
nodes.origin_citation: McDuff--Salamon, J-holomorphic curves and symplectic topology, Lemma 4.3.1
assumptions: Let $u:[0,1]\times[0,1]\to B^{2n}(1)$ be $J$-holomorphic
\int_{[0,1]^2}\biggl[\Bigl|\frac{du}{dx}\Bigr|^2+\Bigl|\frac{du}{dy}\Bigr|^2\biggr]\,dx\,dy<\epsilon

nodes.name: Proof
nodes.statement: This proof is essentially lifted from McDuff--Salamon \cite[p80, Lemma 4.3.1]{mcduffsalamonJholsymp}. Let $w:=\frac 12u_x^2+\frac 12u_y^2$ (using the standard inner product $g_\mathrm{std}$), so $w:[0,1]^2\to\mathbb R_{\geq 0}$. Now we calculate: \begin{equation} w_{xx}+w_{yy}=\Bigl[u_{xx}^2+2u_{xy}^2+u_{yy}^2\Bigr]+\Bigl[u_x\cdot(u_{xxx}+u_{xyy})+u_y\cdot(u_{xxy}+u_{yyy})\Bigr] \end{equation} Now differentiating \eqref{formulaforDeltau} yields: \begin{align*} u_{xxx}+u_{xyy}=&\ddot J(u,u_x,u_y)\circ u_x+\dot J(u,u_{xy})\circ u_x+\dot J(u,u_y)\circ u_{xx}\\ &-\ddot J(u,u_x,u_x)\circ u_y-\dot J(u,u_{xx})\circ u_y-\dot J(u,u_x)\circ u_{xy}\\ u_{xxy}+u_{yyy}=&\ddot J(u,u_y,u_y)\circ u_x+\dot J(u,u_{yy})\circ u_x+\dot J(u,u_y)\circ u_{xy}\\ &-\ddot J(u,u_x,u_y)\circ u_y-\dot J(u,u_{xy})\circ u_y-\dot J(u,u_x)\circ u_{yy} \end{align*} Now we conclude that: \begin{align*} \bigl|u_x\cdot(u_{xxx}&+u_{xyy})+u_y\cdot(u_{xxy}+u_{yyy})\bigr|\\ &\leq 2\left\|J\right\|_{C^2}\cdot(\left|u_x\right|^3\left|u_y\right|+\left|u_x\right|\left|u_y\right|^3)\\ &\qquad+2\left\|J\right\|_{C^1}\cdot(\left|u_x\right|^2\left|u_{xy}\right|+\left|u_x\right|\left|u_y\right|\left|u_{xx}\right|+\left|u_y\right|^2\left|u_{xy}\right|+\left|u_x\right|\left|u_y\right|\left|u_{yy}\right|)\\ &\leq c\left\|J\right\|_{C^2}w^2+c\left\|J\right\|_{C^1}w\cdot(\left|u_{xx}\right|+\left|u_{xy}\right|+\left|u_{yy}\right|)\\ &\leq c\left\|J\right\|_{C^2}w^2+c\left\|J\right\|_{C^1}^2w^2+\frac 1{100}(u_{xx}^2+2u_{xy}^2+u_{yy}^2) \end{align*} Plugging this into \eqref{formulaforDeltaw}, we conclude that: \begin{equation} \Delta w=w_{xx}+w_{yy}\geq -c\cdot (\left\|J\right\|_{C^2}+\left\|J\right\|_{C^1}^2)w^2 \end{equation} Now we may apply a mean value inequality McDuff--Salamon \cite[p81, Lemma 4.3.2]{mcduffsalamonJholsymp} or Wehrheim \cite[p306, Theorem 1.1]{wehrheimmeanvalue} to see that there exist $\epsilon>0$ and $c<\infty$ such that if $\int_{[0,1]^2}w\,dx\,dy<\epsilon$, then $w(\frac 12,\frac 12)\leq c\cdot\int_{[0,1]^2}w\,dx\,dy$. Thus we are done.
nodes.statement_short: The energy density w satisfies Delta w >= -c w^2; a mean value inequality then bounds w at the center.

nodes.name: Laplacian of energy density
nodes.statement: w_{xx}+w_{yy}=\Bigl[u_{xx}^2+2u_{xy}^2+u_{yy}^2\Bigr]+\Bigl[u_x\cdot(u_{xxx}+u_{xyy})+u_y\cdot(u_{xxy}+u_{yyy})\Bigr]
nodes.label: formulaforDeltaw

nodes.name: W^{1,infinity} controls W^{k,p}
nodes.statement: Let $u:[0,1]\times[0,1]\to B^{2n}(1)$ be $J$-holomorphic for an almost complex structure $J$ on $B^{2n}(1)\subseteq\mathbb R^{2n}$. For all $k\geq 1$, there exists $c_k<\infty$ depending only on $\left\|J\right\|_{C^k}$ such that if: \begin{equation} \sup_{(x,y)\in[0,1]^2}\biggl[\Bigl|\frac{du}{dx}\Bigr|+\Bigl|\frac{du}{dy}\Bigr|\biggr]\leq 1 \end{equation} then: \begin{equation} \left|(D^ku)({\textstyle\frac 12},{\textstyle\frac 12})\right|\leq c_k\cdot\sup_{(x,y)\in[0,1]^2}\biggl[\Bigl|\frac{du}{dx}\Bigr|+\Bigl|\frac{du}{dy}\Bigr|\biggr] \end{equation}
nodes.statement_short: Elliptic bootstrapping: a C^1 bound on a J-holomorphic map from the square bounds all derivatives at the center.
nodes.origin_citation: McDuff--Salamon, J-holomorphic curves and symplectic topology, Section B.4 (elliptic bootstrapping)
assumptions: Let $u:[0,1]\times[0,1]\to B^{2n}(1)$ be $J$-holomorphic for an almost complex structure $J$ on $B^{2n}(1)\subseteq\mathbb R^{2n}$.
\sup_{(x,y)\in[0,1]^2}\biggl[\Bigl|\frac{du}{dx}\Bigr|+\Bigl|\frac{du}{dy}\Bigr|\biggr]\leq 1

nodes.name: Proof
nodes.statement: For more details see McDuff--Salamon \cite[p533, \S B.4]{mcduffsalamonJholsymp}. The $\bar\partial$-equation for $u$ may be written as: \begin{equation} u_y=J(u)\circ u_x \end{equation} Differentiating with respect to $x$ and to $y$, we conclude that: \begin{align} u_{xy}&=\dot J(u,u_x)\circ u_x+J(u)\circ u_{xx}\\ u_{xx}&=\dot J(u,u_y)\circ u_x+J(u)\circ u_{xy} \end{align} Combining these and using the fact that $\dot J$ and $J$ anticommute, we conclude that: \begin{equation} \Delta u=u_{xx}+u_{yy}=\dot J(u,u_y)\circ u_x-\dot J(u,u_x)\circ u_y \end{equation} Now a standard elliptic bootstrapping argument based on \eqref{formulaforDeltau} gives the desired result. By hypothesis, we have an $L^\infty$ bound in terms of $\left\|J\right\|_{C^1}$ on the right hand side of \eqref{formulaforDeltau}, which gives a $W^{2,p}$ bound ($2<p<\infty$) on $u$ in terms of $\left\|J\right\|_{C^1}$. Now we have a $W^{1,p}$ bound on the right hand side of \eqref{formulaforDeltau} in terms of $\left\|J\right\|_{C^2}$, which gives a $W^{3,p}$ bound on $u$ in terms of $\left\|J\right\|_{C^2}$. Iterating, we get a $W^{k,p}$ bound on $u$ in terms of $\left\|J\right\|_{C^{k-1}}$, which is enough. There is no need to worry about elliptic regularity estimates near the boundary since we can shrink the domain slightly after each iteration.
nodes.statement_short: Derive the semilinear Laplace equation for u and bootstrap W^{k,p} bounds by iterated elliptic estimates.

nodes.statement: u_y=J(u)\circ u_x
