nodes.statement: u_{xy}&=\dot J(u,u_x)\circ u_x+J(u)\circ u_{xx}\\ u_{xx}&=\dot J(u,u_y)\circ u_x+J(u)\circ u_{xy}

nodes.name: Laplacian of u formula
nodes.statement: \Delta u=u_{xx}+u_{yy}=\dot J(u,u_y)\circ u_x-\dot J(u,u_x)\circ u_y
nodes.label: formulaforDeltau

nodes.name: Surjectivity of gluing
nodes.statement: The restriction of \eqref{gluingmap} to any neighborhood of zero is surjective onto a neighborhood of $(0,0,u_0,e_0)\in\overline{\mathcal M}(X)$.
nodes.statement_short: Every point of M(X) near the basepoint is in the image of the gluing map restricted to any neighborhood of zero.
conclusions: The restriction of \eqref{gluingmap} to any neighborhood of zero is surjective onto a neighborhood of $(0,0,u_0,e_0)\in\overline{\mathcal M}(X)$.
nodes.label: gluingsurjective

nodes.name: Proof
nodes.statement: Let $(\alpha_i,y_i,u_i,\{x^i_j\},e_i)\in\overline{\mathcal M}(X)$ be a sequence converging to $(0,0,u_0,\{x^0_j\},e_0)$. We must show that for $i$ sufficiently large, $(\alpha_i,y_i,u_i,\{x^i_j\},e_i)$ is contained in the image of the map \eqref{gluingmap}. We may restrict to sequences rather than nets since the topology on $\overline{\mathcal M}(X)$ is first countable (recall the definition of the topology following \eqref{Mbarfirstdef}; it is even a metric topology). This is convenient when we apply Arzel\`a--Ascoli. Let us define $\xi_i\in C^\infty(C_{\alpha_i},u_{\alpha_i}^\ast TX)_D\oplus E$ by the property: \begin{align} u_i&=\exp_{u_{\alpha_i}}\xi_i\\ e_i&=e_0+\operatorname{proj}_E\xi_i \end{align} (and the exponential follows the shortest geodesic). Obviously $\operatorname{proj}_E\xi_i\to 0$ and $\left\|\xi_i\right\|_\infty\to 0$. Now we claim that $u_i\to u$ in the $C^\infty$ topology away from the nodes, or equivalently, that $\xi_i\to 0$ in the $C^\infty$ topology away from the nodes of $C_0$. To see this argue as follows. The thickened holomorphic curve equation from \eqref{modulispace} is equivalent to an honest holomorphic curve equation for the graph $u:C\to C\times X$ where the almost complex structure on $C\times X$ is defined in terms of $\lambda(e)$. Hence the Gromov--Schwarz Lemma (see \cite[p316, 1.3.A]{gromov} or \cite[p223, Corollary 4.1.4]{muller}) applies and we conclude that $\left\|du_i\right\|_\infty$ is uniformly bounded, on compact sets away from the nodes (equivalently, the same for $\left\|d\xi_i\right\|_\infty$). Now elliptic bootstrapping (as in the proof of Lemma \ref{Woneinftycontrolsall}) implies that all derivatives are bounded uniformly on compact sets away from the nodes. Using Arzel\`a--Ascoli and diagonalization, we conclude that there exists a subsequence of $u_i$ which is convergent in the $C^\infty$ topology away from the nodes. Since we know that $u_i\to u$ in the $C^0$ topology, the limit of this $C^\infty$ convergent subsequence must be $u$. This argument can be applied to any subsequence of $u_i$, so we conclude that every subsequence of $u_i$ has a subsequence which converges to $u$ in $C^\infty$ away from the nodes. It follows that in fact $u_i$ itself converges to $u$ in $C^\infty$ away from the nodes. In the ends/necks of $C_{\alpha_i}$, note that $u_i$ is genuinely $J$-holomorphic (the $\lambda$ term vanishes), so we may apply Proposition \ref{neckestimate} to conclude that $\left\|\xi_i\right\|_{k,2,\delta}\to 0$ (here using the fact that $\delta<1$). We should remark that to apply Proposition \ref{neckestimate}, we need to be able to choose some $M<\infty$ such that for any neck $[0,6S]\times S^2\subseteq C_{\alpha_i}$, the derivatives of $u_i$ restricted to $\partial[M,6S-M]\subseteq C_{\alpha_i}$ are bounded by $\delta$ (the constant in Proposition \ref{neckestimate}). Such an $M$ exists because of our earlier observation that $u_i\to u$ in $C^\infty$ on compact sets away from the nodes, and we can certainly choose a large $M$ such that the derivatives of $u$ over $\{M\}\times S^1\subseteq[0,\infty)\times S^1\subseteq C_0$ (any end) are arbitrarily small. Let us define $\kappa_i\in K$ by the property that $\xi_i\in(\kappa_i)_{\alpha_i}+\operatorname{im} Q_{\alpha_i,y_i}$. Now since $\left\|\xi_i\right\|_{k,2,\delta}\to 0$ and the norms on the left and right of \eqref{QKtoall} are uniformly commensurable, we see that $\kappa_i\to 0$. Now the uniqueness in Proposition \ref{newtoniteration} shows that $\xi_i=(\kappa_i)_{\alpha_i,y_i}$ for $i$ sufficiently large. Thus we are done.
nodes.statement_short: Write nearby curves as exp of corrections xi_i; Gromov-Schwarz, bootstrapping and Arzela-Ascoli give C^infinity convergence away from nodes, the neck estimate gives weighted convergence, and Newton uniqueness identifies xi_i as glued.

nodes.name: Corrections xi_i
nodes.statement: u_i&=\exp_{u_{\alpha_i}}\xi_i\\ e_i&=e_0+\operatorname{proj}_E\xi_i

nodes.name: Local homeomorphism criterion
nodes.statement: Let $X$ be a Hausdorff topological space and let $f:\mathbb R^n\to X$ be continuous. Suppose that: \begin{rlist} \item$f$ is injective. \item The restriction of $f$ to any neighborhood of zero is surjective onto a neighborhood of $f(0)$. \end{rlist} Then there is an open set $0\in U\subseteq\mathbb R^n$ such that $f(U)\subseteq X$ is open and $f:U\xrightarrow\sim f(U)$ is a homeomorphism.
nodes.statement_short: A continuous injective map from R^n to a Hausdorff space that is locally surjective near 0 is a homeomorphism onto an open set near 0.
assumptions: Let $X$ be a Hausdorff topological space and let $f:\mathbb R^n\to X$ be continuous.
$f$ is injective.
The restriction of $f$ to any neighborhood of zero is surjective onto a neighborhood of $f(0)$.
conclusions: Then there is an open set $0\in U\subseteq\mathbb R^n$ such that $f(U)\subseteq X$ is open and $f:U\xrightarrow\sim f(U)$ is a homeomorphism.
nodes.label: injectiveHdorffhomeo

nodes.name: Proof
nodes.statement: Let $B(1)\subseteq\mathbb R^n$ denote the closed unit ball and $B(1)^\circ$ its interior. We know that $f(B(1))$ is compact (since $f$ is continuous) and Hausdorff (since $X$ is Hausdorff). We know that $f:B(1)\to f(B(1))$ is bijective (since $f$ is injective), so it is in fact a homeomorphism. Now choose an open subset $V\subseteq X$ with $f(0)\in V\subseteq f(B(1)^\circ)$ (which exists by assumption). Set $U=f^{-1}(V)\cap B(1)^\circ$, which is clearly open. Now $f:U\to f(U)$ is a homeomorphism onto its image (since $U\subseteq B(1)$), and $f(U)=V$ is open.
nodes.statement_short: Compact-to-Hausdorff bijection on the closed ball is a homeomorphism; restrict to the preimage of an open set inside the image of the open ball.

nodes.name: Proof of Theorem \ref{mainresult}(\ref{openness}),(\ref{manifold}),(\ref{submersion})
nodes.statement: We have shown that the map $g:=$\eqref{gluingmap} is continuous, injective, and that its restriction to any neighborhood of zero is surjective onto a neighborhood of the image of zero. The target $\overline{\mathcal M}(X)$ is Hausdorff, and thus it follows from Lemma \ref{injectiveHdorffhomeo} that for some open neighborhood of zero $U\subseteq\mathbb C^d\times\mathbb R^{\dim\overline{\mathcal M}^d}\times K$, we have $g(U)$ is open and $g:U\xrightarrow\sim g(U)$ is a homeomorphism. Since $g$ respects the projection map from both sides to $\overline{\mathcal M}\times E/E'$, we obtain the desired conclusions (\ref{openness}), (\ref{manifold}), and (\ref{submersion}).
nodes.statement_short: The gluing map is continuous, injective and locally surjective into a Hausdorff space, hence a local homeomorphism compatible with the projection to M x E/E'.

nodes.name: Proof of Theorem B.1.1(iv) (gluing orientations)
nodes.statement: To show Theorem \ref{mainresult}(\ref{orientation}) (the statement about orientations), observe that since $\overline{\mathcal M}(X)^\mathrm{reg}\to\overline{\mathcal M}$ is a submersion, and $\overline{\mathcal M}$ is canonically oriented as a complex manifold, it follows that $\mathfrak o_{\overline{\mathcal M}(X)^\mathrm{reg}}$ is canonically identified with the orientation sheaf of the fibers of $\overline{\mathcal M}(X)^\mathrm{reg}\to\overline{\mathcal M}$. Now orienting a fiber is the same as orienting the kernel $K$. It is standard to see that $\mathfrak o_K=\mathfrak o_E\otimes\bigotimes_{i=1}^\ell\mathfrak o_{u(p_{n+i})^\ast N_{D/X}}^\vee$. This argument gives an identification $\mathfrak o_{\overline{\mathcal M}(X)^\mathrm{reg}}$ with $\mathfrak o_E\otimes\bigotimes_{i=1}^\ell\mathfrak o_{u(p_{n+i})^\ast N_{D/X}}^\vee$ at every point in $\overline{\mathcal M}(X)^\mathrm{reg}$. Via the gluing map, we get an identification of $\mathfrak o_{\overline{\mathcal M}(X)^\mathrm{reg}}$ with $\mathfrak o_E\otimes\bigotimes_{i=1}^\ell\mathfrak o_{u(p_{n+i})^\ast N_{D/X}}^\vee$ over a small neighborhood of every point in $\overline{\mathcal M}(X)^\mathrm{reg}$. It is probably straightforward to check that these identifications agree on overlaps (this is a concrete question about whether the projection map $K\to K_\alpha\to\ker D_{\alpha,y}$ is orientation preserving; a similar question is dealt with in Floer--Hofer \cite{floerhoferorientations}). This is the best way to prove the desired result, but we can actually get away with a less technical argument. Namely, it is easy to see that the identifications induced by points with smooth domain curve agree on overlaps (since then there is no gluing and we have a nice smooth Banach bundle picture). Since the nodal locus is codimension two inside $\overline{\mathcal M}(X)^\mathrm{reg}$ (this follows from the gluing map constructed previously), the identification $\mathfrak o_{\overline{\mathcal M}(X)^\mathrm{reg}}=\mathfrak o_E\otimes\bigotimes_{i=1}^\ell\mathfrak o_{u(p_{n+i})^\ast N_{D/X}}^\vee$ away from the nodal locus extends uniquely to all of $\overline{\mathcal M}(X)^\mathrm{reg}$.
nodes.statement_short: Orient fibers over M via the kernel K; identifications agree on the smooth-domain locus, which has codimension-two complement, so they extend uniquely.

nodes.statement: Fix a symplectic manifold $(M,\omega)$, an integer $n\geq 0$, and a simplex $\sigma\in J\!H_n(M)$, i.e.\ maps $H:\Delta^n\to C^\infty(M\times S^1)$ and $J:\Delta^n\to J(M)$ as in Definition \ref{JHdef}. Also fix $\gamma^-\in\mathcal P_{H(0)}$ and $\gamma^+\in\mathcal P_{H(n)}$.
nodes.name: Gluing setup data $(M,\omega)$, $\sigma$, $\gamma^\pm$
nodes.statement_short: Fix the symplectic manifold, a simplex $\sigma$ of Floer data $(H,J)$ and periodic orbits $\gamma^\pm$ at its ends.

nodes.statement: Thus let us fix a basepoint $(C_0,\ell_0,u_0,\{\phi^\beta_0\}_{\beta\in I},\{e^\beta_0\}_{\beta\in I})\in\overline{\mathcal M}(\sigma,\gamma^-,\gamma^+)^{\leq\mathfrak s}_I$ in the setup of either Proposition \ref{HFgluingneeded} or \ref{HFgluingSS}. This point consists (in particular) of the following data: \begin{rlist} \item $C_0$, a Riemann surface of genus zero with marked points $q^-,q^+\in C_0$. Note that $C_0$ may be written uniquely as ${\coprod_{i=1}^kC_0^{(i)}}/{\sim}$, where each $C_0^{(i)}$ is a nodal Riemann surface with marked points $q_{i-1},q_i$ (contained in the same irreducible component), the equivalence relation $\sim$ identifies $q_i\in C_0^{(i)}$ with $q_i\in C_0^{(i+1)}$, and $q^-=q_0$, $q^+=q_k$. We call any irreducible component containing some $q_i$ a \emph{main component}, and we call all other irreducible components \emph{bubble components}. The nodes other than $q_1,\ldots,q_{k-1}\in C_0$ will be called \emph{bubble nodes}. \item $\ell_0=\{\ell_0^i:\mathbb R\to\Delta^n\}_{1\leq i\leq k}$, where $\ell_0^i$ is a (possibly constant) Morse flow line (for the flow from Definition \ref{simplexflows}) from vertex $v_{i-1}$ to vertex $v_i$, for vertices $0=v_0\leq\cdots\leq v_k=n$. \item $A_0=\{A_0^i:C_0^{(i)}\setminus\{q_{i-1},q_i\}\to S^1\times\mathbb R\}_{1\leq i\leq k}$, where $A_0^i$ is holomorphic, sends $q_{i-1}$ (resp.\ $q_i$) to $-\infty$ (resp.\ $\infty$), and restricts to a biholomorphism on the main component of $C_0^{(i)}$. Recall that we always use $(t,s)\in S^1\times\mathbb R$ as coordinates, and that we equip $S^1\times\mathbb R$ (and any subset thereof) with the standard complex structure $z=e^{s+it}$. We may identify each main component of $C_0$ with $S^1\times\mathbb R$ via $A_0$, and thus we have coordinates $(t,s)$ on each such component. \item $u_0=\{u_0^i:C_0^{(i)}\setminus\{q_{i-1},q_i\}\to M\}_{1\leq i\leq k}$, where $u_0^i$ is a smooth map with finite energy, converging to $u_0^i(t,-\infty)=\gamma_{i-1}(t)$ and $u_0^i(t,\infty)=\gamma_i(t)$, for periodic orbits $\gamma_i\in\mathcal P_{H(v_i)}$ with $\gamma_0=\gamma^-$ and $\gamma_k=\gamma^+$. \item $e_0:=\bigoplus_{\beta\in I}e^\beta_0\in\bigoplus_{\beta\in I}E_\beta=E_I=:E$. \end{rlist} such that: \begin{equation} \Bigl(du_0+2d(\operatorname{proj}_{S^1}A_0)\otimes X_{H((\ell_0\times\operatorname{id}_{S^1})(A_0(\cdot)))}(u_0)+\sum_{\beta\in I}\lambda_\beta(e^\beta_0)(\phi^\beta_0(\cdot),u_0(\cdot))\Bigr)^{0,1}_{J(\ell_0(A_0(\cdot)))}=0 \end{equation}
nodes.name: Gluing basepoint $(C_0,\ell_0,A_0,u_0,e_0)$
nodes.statement_short: Fix a basepoint of the thickened Floer moduli space: broken curve $C_0$, Morse flow lines $\ell_0$, maps $A_0,u_0$ and $e_0\in E$ solving the perturbed Floer equation.

nodes.statement: We call any irreducible component containing some $q_i$ a \emph{main component}, and we call all other irreducible components \emph{bubble components}.
nodes.name: Main and bubble components
differentia: containing some $q_i$

nodes.statement: The nodes other than $q_1,\ldots,q_{k-1}\in C_0$ will be called \emph{bubble nodes}.
nodes.name: Bubble nodes
Perturbed Floer equation at the basepoint
nodes.statement: \Bigl(du_0+2d(\operatorname{proj}_{S^1}A_0)\otimes X_{H((\ell_0\times\operatorname{id}_{S^1})(A_0(\cdot)))}(u_0)+\sum_{\beta\in I}\lambda_\beta(e^\beta_0)(\phi^\beta_0(\cdot),u_0(\cdot))\Bigr)^{0,1}_{J(\ell_0(A_0(\cdot)))}=0
We immediately reindex these intersection points as $\{x_0^i\}_{1\leq i\leq r}$ (defining $r:=\sum_{\beta\in I}r_\beta$).
nodes.name: Reindexed intersection points $x_0^i$
nodes.section: C.1.1 Points $\{x^i_0\}_{1\leq i\leq r}$ and submanifolds $\{D_i\}_{1\leq i\leq r}\subseteq M\times S^1\times\Delta^n$

nodes.statement: Let $\tilde D_\beta:=(D_\beta\setminus\partial^\mathrm{ess} D_\beta)\times[0,\epsilon)^{\{1,\ldots,n\}\setminus\{i_0,\ldots,i_m\}}\subseteq M\times S^1\times\Delta^n$, and define $D_1,\ldots,D_r\subseteq M\times S^1\times\Delta^n$ as the reindexing of $\{\tilde D_\beta\}_{\beta\in I,1\leq i\leq r_\beta}$ corresponding to our earlier reindexing of $\{x_0^{\beta,i}\}_{\beta\in I,1\leq i\leq r_\beta}$ to $\{x_0^i\}_{1\leq i\leq r}$ (thus $D_1,\ldots,D_r$ contains $r_\beta$ copies of $\tilde D_\beta$).
nodes.name: Submanifolds $D_1,\ldots,D_r$
nodes.statement_short: Thicken each $D_\beta$ to $\tilde D_\beta$ in the normal directions of $\Delta^n$ and reindex them as $D_1,\dots,D_r$.
nodes.section: C.1.1 Points $\{x^i_0\}_{1\leq i\leq r}$ and submanifolds $\{D_i\}_{1\leq i\leq r}\subseteq M\times S^1\times\Delta^n$

nodes.statement: We claim that every unstable bubble component of $C_0$ has a point where $du_0$ is injective.
nodes.name: Unstable bubbles have injective points
assumptions: every unstable bubble component of $C_0$
conclusions: has a point where $du_0$ is injective
nodes.section: C.1.2 Points $\{p_i\}_{1\leq i\leq L},\{p_i'\}_{1\leq i\leq L'}\in C_0$ and submanifolds $D,H\subseteq M$

nodes.statement: Indeed, on any unstable bubble component which is not contained in $(C_0)_\beta$ for any $\beta\in I$, the map $u_0$ is a (nonconstant!) $J(\ell_0(A_0(\cdot)))$-holomorphic sphere in $M$, and thus has such a point of injectivity. Any unstable bubble component contained in $(C_0)_\beta$ for some $\beta\in I$ is stabilized by its intersections with the corresponding $D_\beta$. Since these intersections are transverse (and $A_0$ is constant on the bubble), it follows that $du_0$ has a point of injectivity on such bubble components as well. Hence the claim is valid.
nodes.name: Proof that unstable bubbles have injective points
nodes.statement_short: Case split: bubbles outside every $(C_0)_\beta$ are nonconstant holomorphic spheres; those inside are stabilized by transverse intersections with $D_\beta$.
nodes.section: C.1.2 Points $\{p_i\}_{1\leq i\leq L},\{p_i'\}_{1\leq i\leq L'}\in C_0$ and submanifolds $D,H\subseteq M$

nodes.statement: Let us now choose points $p_1,\ldots,p_L\in C_0$ (a minimal set of distinct non-nodal points stabilizing all bubble components of $C_0$) and a codimension two submanifold with boundary $D\subseteq M$ such that $u_0(p_i)\in D$ with transverse intersection for $1\leq i\leq L$.
nodes.name: Stabilizing points $p_i$ and divisor $D$
nodes.section: C.1.2 Points $\{p_i\}_{1\leq i\leq L},\{p_i'\}_{1\leq i\leq L'}\in C_0$ and submanifolds $D,H\subseteq M$

nodes.statement: We claim that every unstable main component of $C_0$ over which $\ell_0$ is constant has a point where $\frac\partial{\partial s}u_0$ is nonzero.
nodes.name: Unstable main components have $\partial_s u_0\neq 0$
nodes.section: C.1.2 Points $\{p_i\}_{1\leq i\leq L},\{p_i'\}_{1\leq i\leq L'}\in C_0$ and submanifolds $D,H\subseteq M$

nodes.statement: Indeed, this holds because such an unstable main component cannot be a trivial cylinder (otherwise the trajectory would be unstable).
nodes.name: Proof that unstable main components are not trivial cylinders
nodes.statement_short: Such a component cannot be a trivial cylinder, else the trajectory would be unstable.
nodes.section: C.1.2 Points $\{p_i\}_{1\leq i\leq L},\{p_i'\}_{1\leq i\leq L'}\in C_0$ and submanifolds $D,H\subseteq M$

nodes.statement: Let us now choose points $p_1',\ldots,p_{L'}'\in C_0$ (consisting of exactly one non-nodal point in every unstable main component over which $\ell_0$ is constant) and a codimension one submanifold with boundary $H\subseteq M$ such that $u_0(p_i')\in H$ with $\frac\partial{\partial s}u_0$ transverse to $H$ for $1\leq i\leq L'$.
nodes.name: Points $p_i'$ and hypersurface $H$
nodes.section: C.1.2 Points $\{p_i\}_{1\leq i\leq L},\{p_i'\}_{1\leq i\leq L'}\in C_0$ and submanifolds $D,H\subseteq M$

nodes.statement: We assume that $D$ and $H$ are disjoint: this can be achieved by first perturbing $D$ (and correspondingly $p_1,\ldots,p_L$) so that on each of the main components under consideration here, there exists a point where $\frac\partial{\partial s}u_0$ is nonzero and which is not mapped to $D$.
nodes.name: $D$ and $H$ disjoint
nodes.section: C.1.2 Points $\{p_i\}_{1\leq i\leq L},\{p_i'\}_{1\leq i\leq L'}\in C_0$ and submanifolds $D,H\subseteq M$

nodes.statement: A subset of the Riemann sphere $\mathbb C\cup\{\infty\}$ homeomorphic to $S^1$ is called a \emph{circle} iff its intersection with $\mathbb C$ is either a straight line or a circle (in the usual sense).
nodes.name: Circle in the Riemann sphere
nodes.genus: A subset of the Riemann sphere $\mathbb C\cup\{\infty\}$ homeomorphic to $S^1$
differentia: its intersection with $\mathbb C$ is either a straight line or a circle (in the usual sense)

nodes.statement: It is well-known that this notion is invariant under biholomorphisms of the Riemann sphere.
nodes.name: Circles are invariant under Möbius transformations
conclusions: this notion is invariant under biholomorphisms of the Riemann sphere

nodes.statement: For any Riemann surface $C$ biholomorphic to the Riemann sphere minus finitely many points, a subset of $C$ homeomorphic to $S^1$ is called a \emph{circle} iff its image under such a biholomorphism is a circle.
nodes.name: Circle in a punctured sphere
differentia: its image under such a biholomorphism is a circle

nodes.statement: On both sides of every bubble node of $C_0$, fix cylindrical ends: \begin{equation} S^1\times[0,\infty)\to C_0 \end{equation} which are \emph{circular}, in the sense that every (equivalently, some) cross section $S^1\times\{s\}$ is a circle (inside the corresponding irreducible component of $C_0$).
nodes.name: Circular cylindrical ends
Bubble ends
nodes.statement: S^1\times[0,\infty)\to C_0
nodes.label: bubbleends

nodes.statement: We will call the ends \eqref{bubbleends} the \emph{bubble ends}.
nodes.name: Bubble ends

nodes.statement: We also fix some large $N<\infty$, and we call the subsets $S^1\times[N,\infty)$ and $S^1\times(-\infty,-N]$ of the main components of $C_0$ the \emph{main ends} (which come in two types: \emph{positive} and \emph{negative}).
nodes.name: Main ends
nodes.genus: the subsets $S^1\times[N,\infty)$ and $S^1\times(-\infty,-N]$ of the main components of $C_0$

nodes.statement:
We now fix a smooth family of (necessarily integrable) almost complex structures $j_y$ on $C_0$ and a smooth family of $j_y$-holomorphic maps:  egin{equation} A_y^i:C^{(i)}_0\setminus\{q_{i-1},q_i\}	o S^1	imes\mathbb R \end{equation} parameterized by $y\in\mathbb R^\ast$ (for an integer $\ast\geq 0$ to be specified shortly), specializing to $(j_0,A_0)$ at $y=0$ (where $j_0$ denotes the given almost complex structure on $C_0$). We require that this family $(j_y,A_y)_{y\in\mathbb R^\ast}$ satisfy the following conditions. The family $j_y$ must be constant over the bubble ends, and $A_y$ (and hence $j_y$) must be constant over the main ends. The bubble ends \eqref{bubbleends} must also be circular with respect to every $j_y$. Now, for each stable bubble component of $C_0$ (say, with $
u\geq 3$ special points), the family $j_y$ induces a map $\mathbb R^\ast	o\mathcal M_{0,
u}$. For each main component of $C_0$ (say, with $
u\geq 0$ bubble nodes), the family $A_y$ induces a map $\mathbb R^\ast	o(S^1	imes\mathbb R)^
u$ (namely taking the images of the bubble nodes under $A_y$). We require that the resulting map:  egin{equation*} \mathbb R^\ast	o\prod_{ egin{smallmatrix}	ext{bubble components}\cr	ext{with $
u\geq 3$}\end{smallmatrix}}\mathcal M_{0,
u}	imes\prod_{ egin{smallmatrix}	ext{main components}\cr	ext{with $\ell_0$ non-constant}\end{smallmatrix}}(S^1	imes\mathbb R)^
u	imes\prod_{ egin{smallmatrix}	ext{main components}\cr	ext{with $\ell_0$ constant}\cr	ext{and $
u\geq 1$}\end{smallmatrix}}(S^1	imes\mathbb R)^
u\!/\mathbb R \end{equation*} be a diffeomorphism onto its image (in particular, this determines $\ast\in\mathbb Z_{\geq 0}$). We fix, once and for all, a family $(j_y,A_y)_{y\in\mathbb R^\ast}$ satisfying the above properties (such a family always exists).
nodes.name: Family $(j_y,A_y)_{y\in\mathbb R^\ast}$ of domain deformations
nodes.statement_short: Fix a smooth family $(j_y,A_y)$ of complex structures and holomorphic maps on $C_0$, constant on ends, giving a local chart of the moduli of the domain.

nodes.name: Family of maps $A_y^i$
nodes.statement: A_y^i:C^{(i)}_0\setminus\{q_{i-1},q_i\}\to S^1\times\mathbb R
nodes.label: Aymaps

nodes.statement: Given a set of gluing parameters\footnote{We only care about what happens for gluing parameters $\alpha$ in a neighborhood of zero, and many constructions will only make sense (and many statements will only be true) for sufficiently small gluing parameters $\alpha$, even though this assumption is not always explicitly stated. The same goes for the parameters $w$ (introduced below) and $y$.} $\alpha\in\mathbb C^d\times\mathbb R_{\geq 0}^{k-1}$ (where $d$ is the number of bubble nodes of $C_0$), we may glue $C_0$ to obtain a curve $C_\alpha$ as follows. At a bubble node with gluing parameter $\alpha=e^{-6S+i\theta}\in\mathbb C$, we truncate both bubble ends \eqref{bubbleends} from $S^1\times[0,\infty)$ to $S^1\times[0,6S]$, and we identify them via the map $s'=6S-s$ and $t'=\theta-t$ (if $\alpha=0$, then we do nothing). At each main node $q_i$ with gluing parameter $\alpha=e^{-6S}\in\mathbb R_{\geq 0}$, we truncate the main ends $S^1\times[N,\infty)\subseteq C_0^{(i)}$ and $S^1\times(-\infty,-N]\subseteq C_0^{(i+1)}$ incident at $q_i$ to $S^1\times[N,6S-N]$ and $S^1\times[-6S+N,-N]$, and we identify them via $s'=s-6S$ and $t'=t$ (if $\alpha=0$, then we do nothing). The curve $C_\alpha$ now has \emph{main ends} and \emph{bubble ends} (those where no gluing was performed), as well as \emph{bubble necks} $S^1\times[0,6S]$ and \emph{main necks} $S^1\times[N,6S-N]$.
nodes.name: Glued curve $C_\alpha$
nodes.statement_short: For gluing parameters $\alpha$, truncate and identify bubble ends and main ends of $C_0$ to obtain $C_\alpha$ with bubble/main necks.

nodes.statement: We perform a similar gluing operation to $\coprod_{i=1}^k\mathbb R$, and we denote the result by $(\coprod_{i=1}^k\mathbb R)_\alpha$. Namely, for the gluing parameter $\alpha=e^{-6S}\in\mathbb R_{\geq 0}$ associated to $q_i$, we truncate the $i$th copy of $\mathbb R$ to $(-\infty,6S]$, we truncate the $(i+1)$st copy of $\mathbb R$ to $[-6S,\infty)$, and we identify $[0,6S]$ in the $i$th copy with $[-6S,0]$ in the $(i+1)$st copy via $s'=s-6S$ (if $\alpha=0$, then we do nothing).
nodes.name: Glued line $(\coprod_{i=1}^k\mathbb R)_\alpha$

nodes.statement: The almost complex structure $j_y$ clearly descends to $C_\alpha$, since it is constant over the ends of $C_0$. Furthermore, the maps \eqref{Aymaps} induce $j_y$-holomorphic maps: \begin{equation} A_y:C_\alpha\setminus\{q_0,\ldots,q_k\}\to S^1\times\Bigl(\coprod_{i=1}^k\mathbb R\Bigr)_\alpha \end{equation} characterized uniquely by the property that they agree with \eqref{Aymaps} over the images of the truncated main components of $C_0$ (the existence of such a map $A_y$ follows from our assumption that the bubble ends \eqref{bubbleends} are circular with respect to every $j_y$). The points $p_1,\ldots,p_L,p_1',\ldots,p_{L'}'\in C_0$ clearly descend to points $p_1,\ldots,p_L,p_1',\ldots,p_{L'}'\in C_\alpha$, and there is a node $q_i\in C_\alpha$ whenever the corresponding gluing parameter is zero.
nodes.name: Induced maps $A_y$ on $C_\alpha$
nodes.statement_short: $j_y$, $A_y$ and the marked points descend to the glued curve $C_\alpha$, using circularity of the bubble ends.

nodes.name: Induced map $A_y$ on $C_\alpha$
nodes.statement: A_y:C_\alpha\setminus\{q_0,\ldots,q_k\}\to S^1\times\Bigl(\coprod_{i=1}^k\mathbb R\Bigr)_\alpha

Eventually, only a subset of $\mathbb C^d\times\mathbb R_{\geq 0}^{k-1}$ will be relevant for us, namely the subset $\mathbb C^d\times(\mathbb R_{\geq 0}^{k-1})^{\leq\mathfrak s}\subseteq\mathbb C^d\times\mathbb R_{\geq 0}^{k-1}$ cut out by the requirement that if the break in the trajectory at $(v_i,\gamma_i)$ is dictated by the stratum $\mathfrak s$, then the gluing parameter at $q_i$ is zero.
nodes.name: Stratum-compatible gluing parameters $(\mathbb R_{\geq 0}^{k-1})^{\leq\mathfrak s}$

nodes.statement: For every nonconstant $\ell_0^i$, choose a local hypersurface $H^i\subseteq\Delta^{[v_{i-1}\ldots v_i]}$ transverse to $\ell_0^i$ at $\ell_0^i(0)$.
nodes.name: Transverse hypersurfaces $H^i$

nodes.statement: For $w\in\prod_{i=1}^{k\prime}H^i$ (where $\prod_{i=1}^{k\prime}$ denotes the product over those $i$ for which $\ell_0^i$ is nonconstant), let $\ell_w:\coprod_{i=1}^k\mathbb R\to\Delta^n$ denote the unique trajectory satisfying $\prod_{i=1}^{k\prime}\ell_w^i(0)=w$ and broken at the same sequence of vertices $0=v_0\leq\cdots\leq v_k=n$. We let $0:=\prod_{i=1}^{k\prime}\ell_0^i(0)\in\prod_{i=1}^{k\prime}H^i$, so in this notation $\ell_w=\ell_0$ for $w=0$.
nodes.name: Trajectories $\ell_w$

nodes.statement: Now choose a neighborhood parameterization $\Delta^{[v_{i-1}\ldots v_i]}\times[0,\epsilon)^{\{1,\ldots,n\}\setminus\{v_{i-1},\ldots,v_i\}}\to\Delta^n$, and define a local hypersurface $\bar H^i:=H^i\times[0,\epsilon)^{\{1,\ldots,n\}\setminus\{v_{i-1},\ldots,v_i\}}\subseteq\Delta^n$ and a projection map $\bar H^i\to H^i$.
nodes.name: Extended hypersurfaces $\bar H^i$

nodes.statement: For $\alpha\in\mathbb R_{\geq 0}^{k-1}$, let $\ell_{\alpha,w}:(\coprod_{i=1}^k\mathbb R)_\alpha\to\Delta^n$ denote the trajectory characterized uniquely by the property that $\prod_{i=1}^{k\prime}\ell_{\alpha,w}(0_i)\in\prod_{i=1}^{k\prime}\bar H^i$ projects to $w\in\prod_{i=1}^{k\prime}H^i$, where $0_i\in(\coprod_{i=1}^k\mathbb R)_\alpha$ denotes the image of $0$ in the $i$th copy of $\mathbb R$. In this notation, $\ell_{\alpha,w}=\ell_0$ for $\alpha=0$ and $w=0$.
nodes.name: Glued trajectories $\ell_{\alpha,w}$

nodes.statement: The existence and uniqueness of $\ell_{\alpha,w}$ for $(\alpha,w)$ close to $(0,0)$ follows simply by explicitly integrating the Morse flow on $\Delta^n$ from Definition \ref{simplexflows}.
nodes.name: Existence and uniqueness of $\ell_{\alpha,w}$
conclusions: The existence and uniqueness of $\ell_{\alpha,w}$ for $(\alpha,w)$ close to $(0,0)$

nodes.statement: Eventually, only a subset of $\prod_{i=1}^{k\prime}H^i$ will be relevant for us, namely the subset $\prod_{i=1}^{k\prime}(H^i)^{\leq\mathfrak s}\subseteq\prod_{i=1}^{k\prime}H^i$, where $(H^i)^{\leq\mathfrak s}\subseteq H^i$ is the intersection of $H^i$ with $\Delta^{[i_0\ldots i_m]}\cap\Delta^{[v_{i-1}\ldots v_i]}=\Delta^{[i_0\ldots i_m]\cap[v_{i-1}\ldots v_i]}$, where $(\sigma|[i_0\ldots i_m],\gamma_a,\gamma_b)$ is the part of the stratum $\mathfrak s$ containing $\ell^i_0$.
nodes.name: Stratum-compatible parameters $(H^i)^{\leq\mathfrak s}$
Thickening linear maps $\lambda_\beta$
nodes.statement: \lambda_\beta:E_\beta\to C^\infty(\overline{\mathcal C}_{0,2+r_\beta}\times M,\Omega^{0,1}_{\overline{\mathcal C}_{0,2+r_\beta}/\overline{\mathcal M}_{0,2+r_\beta}}\otimes_\mathbb R TM)

We now repackage these $\lambda_\beta$ into a single linear map: \begin{equation} \lambda:E\to C^\infty(\mathbb C^d\times(\mathbb R_{\geq 0}^{k-1})^{\leq\mathfrak s}\times\mathbb R^\ast\times C_0^r\times C_0\times M,\Omega^1_{C_0}\otimes_\mathbb R TM) \end{equation} which vanishes over the ends of (the last factor of) $C_0$. We will actually only define $\lambda$ in a small neighborhood of $\{0\}\times\{0\}\times\{x_0^1\}\times\cdots\times\{x_0^r\}\times C_0\times M$, as this is the only part of the domain which will be relevant.
nodes.name: Repackaged linear map $\lambda$
Repackaged linear map $\lambda$
nodes.statement: \lambda:E\to C^\infty(\mathbb C^d\times(\mathbb R_{\geq 0}^{k-1})^{\leq\mathfrak s}\times\mathbb R^\ast\times C_0^r\times C_0\times M,\Omega^1_{C_0}\otimes_\mathbb R TM)

Suppose we are given $e\in E=\bigoplus_{\beta\in I}E_\beta$, $\alpha\in\mathbb C^d\times(\mathbb R_{\geq 0}^{k-1})^{\leq\mathfrak s}$, and $y\in\mathbb R^\ast$, along with points $x^1,\ldots,x^r\in C_0$, each in a small neighborhood of the corresponding $x_0^i$; let us define $\lambda(e)(\alpha,y,x^1,\ldots,x^r,\cdot,\cdot)$ as a section $C_0\times M\to\Omega^{0,1}_{C_0,j_y}\otimes_\mathbb R TM\subseteq\Omega^1_{C_0}\otimes_\mathbb R TM$. Consider the glued curve $C_\alpha$ equipped with the almost complex structure $j_y$ and the marked points $x^1,\ldots,x^r\in C_\alpha$ (descended from $C_0$). Since $\alpha\in\mathbb C^d\times(\mathbb R_{\geq 0}^{k-1})^{\leq\mathfrak s}$, there is a subcurve $(C_\alpha)_\beta\subseteq C_\alpha$ corresponding to any given $\beta\in I$. If we equip it with the $r_\beta$ marked points from $x^1,\ldots,x^r$ corresponding to $\beta$ (with respect to the reindexing from \S\ref{reindexingsec}), then this induces a unique map $\phi^\beta:(C_\alpha)_\beta\to\overline{\mathcal C}_{0,2+r_\beta}$ (isomorphism onto a fiber) which is close to the given map $\phi_0^\beta:(C_0)_\beta\to\overline{\mathcal C}_{0,2+r_\beta}$ (this assumes we are in the setting of Proposition \ref{HFgluingneeded}; in the setting of Proposition \ref{HFgluingSS}, we instead have a map $\phi^\beta:((C_\alpha)_\beta)^\mathrm{st}\to\overline{\mathcal C}_{0,2+r_\beta}$ close to the given map $\phi_0^\beta:((C_0)_\beta)^\mathrm{st}\to\overline{\mathcal C}_{0,2+r_\beta}$, where $(C_\alpha)_\beta\to((C_\alpha)_\beta)^\mathrm{st}$ contracts those components all of whose constituent components of $(C_0)_\beta$ were contracted by $(C_0)_\beta\to((C_0)_\beta)^\mathrm{st}$). Now the pullback of $\lambda_\beta(\operatorname{proj}_{E_\beta}e)$ under $\phi^\beta$ gives us a section $C_\alpha\times M\to\Omega^{0,1}_{C_\alpha,j_y}\otimes_\mathbb R TM$ (defined to be zero at those points not contained in $(C_\alpha)_\beta$). We may assume without loss of generality that the ends of $C_0$ were chosen small enough so that this section vanishes over the ends/necks of $C_\alpha$, and hence gives rise to a well-defined lift to a section $C_0\times M\to\Omega^{0,1}_{C_0,j_y}\otimes_\mathbb R TM$. We declare $\lambda(e)(\alpha,y,x^1,\ldots,x^r,\cdot,\cdot)$ to be the sum of these sections over all $\beta\in I$. This defines the function $\lambda$, which is indeed of class $C^\infty$ since the partially defined composition $C_0\to C_\alpha\to(C_\alpha)_\beta\to\overline{\mathcal C}_{0,2+r_\beta}$ depends smoothly on $\alpha,y,x^1,\ldots,x^r$.
nodes.name: Construction of $\lambda(e)(\alpha,y,x^1,\ldots,x^r,\cdot,\cdot)$
nodes.statement_short: Define $\lambda(e)$ by pulling back each $\lambda_\beta(\mathrm{proj}_{E_\beta}e)$ under the stabilization map $\phi^\beta$ of the glued subcurve and summing over $\beta$; it is smooth.

nodes.statement: Let $\overline{\mathcal M}(M)$ denote the moduli space of tuples $(\alpha,w,y,u,e,\{x^i\}_{1\leq i\leq r})$, where: \begin{rlist} \item$\alpha\in\mathbb C^d\times(\mathbb R_{\geq 0}^{k-1})^{\leq\mathfrak s}$. \item$w\in\prod_{i=1}^{k\prime}(H^i)^{\leq\mathfrak s}$. \item$y\in\mathbb R^\ast$. \item$u:C_\alpha\setminus\{q_0,\ldots,q_k\}\to M$ is smooth with finite energy, is asymptotic to $\gamma_i$ at $q_i\in C_\alpha$ (whenever the gluing parameter $\alpha$ at $q_i\in C_0$ is zero), and $u(p_i)\in D^\circ$ ($1\leq i\leq L$) and $u(p_i')\in H^\circ$ ($1\leq i\leq L'$). \item$e\in E$. \item$x^i\in C_\alpha$ (not nodes) satisfy $(\operatorname{id}_{M\times S^1}\times\ell_{\alpha,w})((u\times A_y)(x^i))\in D_i$ with transverse intersection ($1\leq i\leq r$). \item We require that: \begin{multline} \Bigl(du+2d(\operatorname{proj}_{S^1}A_y)\otimes X_{H((\ell_{\alpha,w}\times\operatorname{id}_{S^1})(A_y(\cdot)))}\\ +\lambda(e)(\alpha,y,x^1,\ldots,x^r,\cdot,u(\cdot))\Bigr)^{0,1}_{j_y,J(\ell_{\alpha,w}(A_y(\cdot)))}=0 \end{multline} \end{rlist}
nodes.name: Local gluing moduli space $\overline{\mathcal M}(M)$
nodes.genus: the moduli space of tuples $(\alpha,w,y,u,e,\{x^i\}_{1\leq i\leq r})$
nodes.statement_short: Tuples $(\alpha,w,y,u,e,x^i)$ of gluing/flow/domain parameters, a map $u$ on $C_\alpha$, $e\in E$ and marked points solving the perturbed Floer equation.
nodes.section: C.1.5 A new moduli space $\overline{\mathcal M}(M)$

nodes.name: Glued perturbed Floer equation
nodes.statement: \Bigl(du+2d(\operatorname{proj}_{S^1}A_y)\otimes X_{H((\ell_{\alpha,w}\times\operatorname{id}_{S^1})(A_y(\cdot)))}\\ +\lambda(e)(\alpha,y,x^1,\ldots,x^r,\cdot,u(\cdot))\Bigr)^{0,1}_{j_y,J(\ell_{\alpha,w}(A_y(\cdot)))}=0
nodes.section: C.1.5 A new moduli space $\overline{\mathcal M}(M)$
nodes.label: finalHFdelbareqn

nodes.statement: We equip $\overline{\mathcal M}(M)$ with the topology of uniform convergence. More precisely, let $\overline{\mathcal M}:=\mathbb C^d\times(\mathbb R_{\geq 0}^{k-1})^{\leq\mathfrak s}$, and let $\overline{\mathcal C}{}^\$\to\overline{\mathcal M}$ be the bundle whose fiber over $\alpha$ is $C_\alpha^\$$, obtained from $C_\alpha$ by replacing each $q_i$ ($0\leq i\leq k$) with a copy of $S^1$ (thus $u$ as above extends continuously to $C_\alpha^\$$ and equals $\gamma_i(t)$ on the $S^1$ over $q_i$ whenever the corresponding $\alpha$ is zero). We equip $\overline{\mathcal M}(M)$ with the obvious topology on $w\in\prod_{i=1}^{k\prime}(H^i)^{\leq\mathfrak s}$, $y\in\mathbb R^\ast$, $e\in E$, $\{x^i\}_{1\leq i\leq r}\in\overline{\mathcal C}{}^r$, and the Hausdorff topology on the graph of $u$ inside $\overline{\mathcal C}{}^\$\times M$.
nodes.name: Topology on $\overline{\mathcal M}(M)$
nodes.statement_short: Topology of uniform convergence on $\overline{\mathcal M}(M)$ via the bundle $\overline{\mathcal C}{}^\$\to\overline{\mathcal M}$ with circles replacing the ends.
nodes.section: C.1.5 A new moduli space $\overline{\mathcal M}(M)$

nodes.statement: Note that there is a distinguished basepoint $(0,0,0,u_0,e_0,\{x_0^i\}_{1\leq i\leq r})\in\overline{\mathcal M}(M)$. Furthermore, a neighborhood of this basepoint in $\overline{\mathcal M}(M)$ is canonically homeomorphic to a neighborhood of the given basepoint in $\overline{\mathcal M}(\sigma,\gamma^-,\gamma^+)_I^{\leq\mathfrak s}$ (as long as the given basepoint in $\overline{\mathcal M}(\sigma,\gamma^-,\gamma^+)_I^{\leq\mathfrak s}$ has trivial automorphism group).
nodes.name: $\overline{\mathcal M}(M)$ is a local model of the thickened moduli space
assumptions: (as long as the given basepoint in $\overline{\mathcal M}(\sigma,\gamma^-,\gamma^+)_I^{\leq\mathfrak s}$ has trivial automorphism group)
conclusions: a neighborhood of this basepoint in $\overline{\mathcal M}(M)$ is canonically homeomorphic to a neighborhood of the given basepoint in $\overline{\mathcal M}(\sigma,\gamma^-,\gamma^+)_I^{\leq\mathfrak s}$
nodes.statement_short: Near the basepoint, $\overline{\mathcal M}(M)$ is canonically homeomorphic to the thickened Floer moduli space.
nodes.section: C.1.5 A new moduli space $\overline{\mathcal M}(M)$

nodes.statement: Note that to justify this statement in the setting of Proposition \ref{HFgluingSS}, we must appeal to Lemma \ref{morseistransverse}.
nodes.name: Equivariant case needs Lemma 10.5.18
nodes.section: C.1.5 A new moduli space $\overline{\mathcal M}(M)$

nodes.statement: We now define a subset $\overline{\mathcal M}(M)^\mathrm{reg}\subseteq\overline{\mathcal M}(M)$, depending on a choice of subspace $E'\subseteq E$.
nodes.name: Subspace $E'\subseteq E$ for the regular locus

nodes.statement: Fix an integer $k\in\mathbb Z_{\geq 6}$ (not to be confused with the number $k$ of main components of $C_0$) and a small real number $\delta\in(0,1)$ (we will be precise about how small $\delta$ must be shortly). Let $W^{k,2,\delta}(C_\alpha,M)$ denote the smooth Banach manifold consisting of maps $u:C_\alpha\setminus\{q_0,\ldots,q_k\}\to M$ which are of locally of class $W^{k,2}$ such that for all positive main ends of $C_\alpha$ with corresponding node $q_i$, we have: \begin{equation} \int_{S^1\times[N',\infty)}\sum_{j=0}^k\left|D^j\bigl[\exp^{-1}_{\gamma_i(t)}u(t,s)\bigr]\right|^2e^{2s\delta}\;dt\,ds<\infty \end{equation} for sufficiently large $N'<\infty$ (along with the analogous condition over negative main ends); this definition is independent of the choice of metric and connection used in \eqref{deltaweightedend}.
nodes.name: Weighted Banach manifold $W^{k,2,\delta}(C_\alpha,M)$
nodes.statement_short: Maps on $C_\alpha$ locally $W^{k,2}$ with exponentially weighted ($e^{2s\delta}$) decay to the periodic orbits on the main ends.

nodes.name: Weighted decay condition on main ends (maps)
nodes.statement: \int_{S^1\times[N',\infty)}\sum_{j=0}^k\left|D^j\bigl[\exp^{-1}_{\gamma_i(t)}u(t,s)\bigr]\right|^2e^{2s\delta}\;dt\,ds<\infty
nodes.label: deltaweightedend

nodes.statement: Over $W^{k,2,\delta}(C_\alpha,M)$, we consider the smooth Banach bundle $\mathcal E$ whose fiber over $u:C_\alpha\to M$ is $W^{k-1,2,\delta}(\tilde C_\alpha,\Omega^{0,1}_{\tilde C_\alpha,j_y}\otimes_\mathbb C u^\ast TM_{J(\ell_{\alpha,w}(A_y(\cdot)))})$, namely the space of sections $\eta:\tilde C_\alpha\to\Omega^{0,1}_{\tilde C_\alpha,j_y}\otimes_\mathbb C u^\ast TM_{J(\ell_{\alpha,w}(A_y(\cdot)))}$ which are locally of class $W^{k-1,2}$ and which satisfy: \begin{equation} \int_{S^1\times[N',\infty)}\sum_{j=0}^{k-1}\Bigl|D^j\bigl[\mathsf{PT}_{u(t,s)\to\gamma_i(t)}\eta(t,s)\bigr]\Bigr|^2e^{2s\delta}\;dt\,ds<\infty \end{equation} over positive main ends (along with the analogous condition over negative main ends); this definition is independent of the choice of metric and connection used in \eqref{deltaweightedendII}.
nodes.name: Banach bundle $\mathcal E$
Weighted decay condition on main ends (sections)
nodes.statement: \int_{S^1\times[N',\infty)}\sum_{j=0}^{k-1}\Bigl|D^j\bigl[\mathsf{PT}_{u(t,s)\to\gamma_i(t)}\eta(t,s)\bigr]\Bigr|^2e^{2s\delta}\;dt\,ds<\infty
nodes.label: deltaweightedendII

nodes.statement: In particular, for $0\leq i\leq k$, there is a corresponding $\delta_i:=\delta_{H(v_i),J(v_i),\gamma_i}>0$. We fix $\delta\in(0,1)$ with $\delta<\delta_i$ for all $i$; thus $u_1\in W^{k,2,\delta}(C_\alpha,M)$.
nodes.name: Weights $\delta_i$ and $\delta$

nodes.statement: Now since $k\geq 6$, there are unique continuous functions: \begin{equation} x^i:W^{k,2,\delta}(C_\alpha,M)\to C_\alpha\quad(1\leq i\leq r) \end{equation} defined for $u$ in a neighborhood of $u_1\in W^{k,2,\delta}(C_\alpha,M)$, coinciding with the given $x^i_1\in C_\alpha$ at $u_1$, and which satisfy $(\operatorname{id}_{M\times S^1}\times\ell_{\alpha,y})((u\times A_y)(x^i(u)))\in D^i$ (the intersection is automatically transverse for $u$ close to $u_1$). Moreover, \eqref{intersectionsfunctionHF} are of class $C^{k-2}$ (see the discussion following \eqref{intersectionsfunction}).
nodes.name: Intersection functions $x^i$ on $W^{k,2,\delta}(C_\alpha,M)$
assumptions: $k\geq 6$
nodes.statement_short: For $k\ge6$ the marked points $x^i(u)$ (intersections with $D^i$) depend $C^{k-2}$ on $u$ near $u_1$.

nodes.name: Intersection point functions $x^i$
nodes.statement: x^i:W^{k,2,\delta}(C_\alpha,M)\to C_\alpha\quad(1\leq i\leq r)
nodes.label: intersectionsfunctionHF

nodes.statement: It follows that the left hand side of \eqref{finalHFdelbareqn} is a $C^{k-2}$ section of $\mathcal E$ over $W^{k,2,\delta}(C_\alpha,M)\times E$.
nodes.name: The Floer operator is a $C^{k-2}$ section of $\mathcal E$

nodes.statement: By results of Lockhart--McOwen \cite{lockhartmcowen}, this section is Fredholm for $\delta>0$ as above (note that over each end, the almost complex structure on $M$ is constant and $\omega$-compatible).
nodes.name: Fredholmness of the weighted Floer section
assumptions: for $\delta>0$ as above
conclusions: this section is Fredholm

nodes.statement: Let $W^{k,2,\delta}(C_\alpha,M)_{D,H}$ denote the subspace cut out by the requirements $u(p_i)\in D$ and $u(p_i')\in H$.
nodes.name: Constrained subspace $W^{k,2,\delta}(C_\alpha,M)_{D,H}$

nodes.statement: We say that the given point $(\alpha,w,y,u_1,e_1,\{x^i_1\}_{1\leq i\leq r})\in\overline{\mathcal M}(M)$ lies in $\overline{\mathcal M}(M)^\mathrm{reg}$ iff the section $(u,e)\mapsto\eqref{finalHFdelbareqn}\oplus e$ of $\mathcal E\oplus E/E'$ over $W^{k,2,\delta}(C_\alpha,M)_{D,H}\times E$ is transverse to the zero section at $(u_1,e_1)$ (it follows from elliptic regularity theory that this condition is independent of the choice of $k,\delta$ as above).
nodes.name: Regular locus $\overline{\mathcal M}(M)^\mathrm{reg}$
nodes.statement_short: A point is regular iff the linearized Floer section plus projection to $E/E'$ is transverse to zero there.

nodes.statement: Now suppose that we take $E':=E_{I'}$ for $I'\subseteq I$ and that the given basepoint in $\overline{\mathcal M}(\sigma,\gamma^-,\gamma^+)_I^{\leq\mathfrak s}$ was chosen inside the inverse image of $(\overline{\mathcal M}(\sigma,\gamma^-,\gamma^+)_{I'}^{\leq\mathfrak s})^\mathrm{reg}$. Then, the basepoint of $\overline{\mathcal M}(M)$ lies in $\overline{\mathcal M}(M)^\mathrm{reg}$ (this uses the fact that $L,L'$ were chosen to be minimal), and furthermore $\overline{\mathcal M}(M)^\mathrm{reg}\cap\operatorname{proj}_{E/E'}^{-1}(0)$ is contained inside the inverse image of $(\overline{\mathcal M}(\sigma,\gamma^-,\gamma^+)_{I'}^{\leq\mathfrak s})^\mathrm{reg}$.
nodes.name: Compatibility of regular loci
assumptions: we take $E':=E_{I'}$ for $I'\subseteq I$
conclusions: the basepoint of $\overline{\mathcal M}(M)$ lies in $\overline{\mathcal M}(M)^\mathrm{reg}$
nodes.statement_short: With $E'=E_{I'}$ and a basepoint over the $I'$-regular locus, the basepoint is regular and the regular zero set maps into the $I'$-regular locus.

nodes.statement: We henceforth assume that the basepoint in $\overline{\mathcal M}(M)$ lies in $\overline{\mathcal M}(M)^\mathrm{reg}$.
nodes.name: Basepoint is regular
nodes.section: C.2 Our goal: the gluing map

nodes.statement: The remainder of this appendix is devoted to the construction of a germ of a local chart: \begin{equation} \Bigl(\mathbb C^d\times(\mathbb R_{\geq 0}^{k-1})^{\leq\mathfrak s}\times\mathbb R^\ast\times\prod_{i=1}^{k\prime}(H^i)^{\leq\mathfrak s}\times K,(0,0,0,0)\Bigr)\to\Bigl(\overline{\mathcal M}(M),(0,0,0,u_0,e_0,\{x_0^i\}_{1\leq i\leq r})\Bigr) \end{equation} which respects the natural projection from both sides to $\mathbb C^d\times(\mathbb R_{\geq 0}^{k-1})^{\leq\mathfrak s}\times\mathbb R^\ast\times\prod_{i=1}^{k\prime}(H^i)^{\leq\mathfrak s}\times E/E'$ and whose image is contained in $\overline{\mathcal M}(M)^\mathrm{reg}$ ($K$ denotes the kernel of the linearization of \eqref{finalHFdelbareqn} at the distinguished basepoint of $\overline{\mathcal M}(M)$; see \eqref{definitionofkernel}).
nodes.name: Hamiltonian Floer gluing chart
nodes.statement_short: Main gluing result: a germ of a local chart from (gluing, domain, flow parameters) $\times K$ onto $\overline{\mathcal M}(M)^\mathrm{reg}$, compatible with projections.
nodes.section: C.2 Our goal: the gluing map

nodes.name: Gluing chart germ
nodes.statement: \Bigl(\mathbb C^d\times(\mathbb R_{\geq 0}^{k-1})^{\leq\mathfrak s}\times\mathbb R^\ast\times\prod_{i=1}^{k\prime}(H^i)^{\leq\mathfrak s}\times K,(0,0,0,0)\Bigr)\to\Bigl(\overline{\mathcal M}(M),(0,0,0,u_0,e_0,\{x_0^i\}_{1\leq i\leq r})\Bigr)
nodes.section: C.2 Our goal: the gluing map
nodes.label: HFgluinggoal

nodes.statement: Propositions \ref{HFgluingneeded} and \ref{HFgluingSS} follow from the existence of such a chart \eqref{HFgluinggoal} and our earlier observations relating $\overline{\mathcal M}(M)$ to $\overline{\mathcal M}(\sigma,\gamma^-,\gamma^+)_I^{\leq\mathfrak s}$.
nodes.name: Reduction of Propositions 10.3.10 and 10.6.21 to the gluing chart
nodes.statement_short: The local chart \eqref{HFgluinggoal} together with the identification of $\overline{\mathcal M}(M)$ with the thickened moduli space gives openness/submersion.
nodes.section: C.2 Our goal: the gluing map

nodes.statement: Let $\exp:TM\to M$ denote the exponential map of some Riemannian metric on $M$ for which $D$ and $H$ are totally geodesic (such a metric exists since $D$ and $H$ are disjoint).
nodes.name: Exponential map $\exp$

nodes.statement:
Let $
abla$ denote a smooth family of $J$-linear connections on $M$ parameterized by $\Delta^n$ which is constant near the vertices (for instance, we could take $
abla_XY:= rac 12(
abla^0_XY-J(
abla^0_X(JY)))$ for any fixed connection $
abla^0$).
nodes.name: $J$-linear connections $\nabla$

nodes.statement: Let $\mathsf{PT}_{x\to y}:T_xM\to T_yM$ denote parallel transport via $\nabla$ along the shortest geodesic between $x$ and $y$ (we will only use this notation when it may be assumed that $x$ and $y$ are very close in $M$); note that $\mathsf{PT}_{x\to y}$ is $J$-linear, and that $\mathsf{PT}_{x\to y}$ is a \emph{family} of maps parameterized by $\Delta^n$.
nodes.name: Parallel transport $\mathsf{PT}_{x\to y}$
Cutoff function $\chi$
nodes.statement: \chi(x)=\begin{cases}0&x\leq 0\cr 1&x\geq 1\end{cases}

nodes.name: Flattening
nodes.statement: For $\alpha\in\mathbb C^d\times\mathbb R_{\geq 0}^{k-1}$, we define the ``flattened'' map $u_{0|\alpha}:C_0\to M$ as follows. Away from the ends, $u_{0|\alpha}$ coincides with $u_0$. Over a bubble end $S^1\times[0,\infty)$, we define $u_{0|\alpha}$ as follows: \begin{equation} u_{0|\alpha}(t,s):=\begin{cases} u_0(t,s)&s\leq S-1\cr \exp_{u_0(n)}\left[\chi(S-s)\cdot\exp_{u_0(n)}^{-1}u_0(t,s)\right]&S-1\leq s\leq S\cr u_0(n)&S\leq s \end{cases} \end{equation} where $n\in C_0$ denotes the corresponding node. Over a positive main end $S^1\times[N,\infty)$, we define $u_{0|\alpha}$ as: \begin{equation} u_{0|\alpha}(t,s):=\begin{cases} u_0(t,s)&s\leq S-1\cr \exp_{\gamma(t)}\left[\chi(S-s)\cdot\exp_{\gamma(t)}^{-1}u_0(t,s)\right]&S-1\leq s\leq S\cr \gamma(t)&S\leq s \end{cases} \end{equation} where $\gamma(t)=u_0(t,\infty)$ denotes the corresponding periodic orbit; an analogous definition applies over the negative main ends.
nodes.statement_short: $u_{0|\alpha}$ cuts $u_0$ off to the nodal value / periodic orbit on the ends beyond $s=S$ using $\chi$ and $\exp$.

nodes.name: Flattening on bubble ends
nodes.statement: u_{0|\alpha}(t,s):=\begin{cases} u_0(t,s)&s\leq S-1\cr \exp_{u_0(n)}\left[\chi(S-s)\cdot\exp_{u_0(n)}^{-1}u_0(t,s)\right]&S-1\leq s\leq S\cr u_0(n)&S\leq s \end{cases}

nodes.name: Flattening on main ends
nodes.statement: u_{0|\alpha}(t,s):=\begin{cases} u_0(t,s)&s\leq S-1\cr \exp_{\gamma(t)}\left[\chi(S-s)\cdot\exp_{\gamma(t)}^{-1}u_0(t,s)\right]&S-1\leq s\leq S\cr \gamma(t)&S\leq s \end{cases}

nodes.name: Pregluing
nodes.statement: For $\alpha\in\mathbb C^d\times\mathbb R_{\geq 0}^{k-1}$, we define the ``preglued'' map $u_\alpha:C_\alpha\to M$ as follows. Away from the necks, $u_\alpha$ coincides with $u_0$. Over a bubble neck $S^1\times[0,6S]$, we define $u_\alpha$ as: \begin{equation} u_\alpha(t,s):=\begin{cases} u_0(t,s)&s\leq S-1\cr \exp_{u_0(n)}\left[\chi(S-s)\cdot\exp_{u_0(n)}^{-1}u_0(t,s)\right]&S-1\leq s\leq S\cr u_0(n)&S\leq s\leq 5S\cr \exp_{u_0(n)}\left[\chi(S-s')\cdot\exp_{u_0(n)}^{-1}u_0(t',s')\right]&5S\leq s\leq 5S+1\cr u_0(t',s')&5S+1\leq s \end{cases} \end{equation} and over a main neck $S^1\times[N,6S-N]$, we define $u_\alpha$ as: \begin{equation} u_\alpha(t,s):=\begin{cases} u_0(t,s)&s\leq S-1\cr \exp_{\gamma(t)}\left[\chi(S-s)\cdot\exp_{\gamma(t)}^{-1}u_0(t,s)\right]&S-1\leq s\leq S\cr \gamma(t)&S\leq s\leq 5S\cr \exp_{\gamma(t)}\left[\chi(S+s')\cdot\exp_{\gamma(t)}^{-1}u_0(t',s')\right]&5S\leq s\leq 5S+1\cr u_0(t',s')&5S+1\leq s \end{cases} \end{equation} ($u_\alpha$ should be thought of as the ``descent'' of $u_{0|\alpha}$ from $C_0$ to $C_\alpha$).
nodes.statement_short: $u_\alpha$ on $C_\alpha$ interpolates the two flattened ends across each bubble/main neck.

nodes.name: Pregluing on bubble necks
nodes.statement: u_\alpha(t,s):=\begin{cases} u_0(t,s)&s\leq S-1\cr \exp_{u_0(n)}\left[\chi(S-s)\cdot\exp_{u_0(n)}^{-1}u_0(t,s)\right]&S-1\leq s\leq S\cr u_0(n)&S\leq s\leq 5S\cr \exp_{u_0(n)}\left[\chi(S-s')\cdot\exp_{u_0(n)}^{-1}u_0(t',s')\right]&5S\leq s\leq 5S+1\cr u_0(t',s')&5S+1\leq s \end{cases}

nodes.name: Pregluing on main necks
nodes.statement: u_\alpha(t,s):=\begin{cases} u_0(t,s)&s\leq S-1\cr \exp_{\gamma(t)}\left[\chi(S-s)\cdot\exp_{\gamma(t)}^{-1}u_0(t,s)\right]&S-1\leq s\leq S\cr \gamma(t)&S\leq s\leq 5S\cr \exp_{\gamma(t)}\left[\chi(S+s')\cdot\exp_{\gamma(t)}^{-1}u_0(t',s')\right]&5S\leq s\leq 5S+1\cr u_0(t',s')&5S+1\leq s \end{cases}

nodes.name: Weighted Sobolev space $W^{k,2,\delta,\delta}(C_\alpha,u_\alpha^\ast TM)$
nodes.statement: We define the weighted Sobolev space $W^{k,2,\delta,\delta}(C_\alpha,u_\alpha^\ast TM)$ using the usual $(k,2)$-norm away from the ends/necks, and using the following weighted $(k,2)$-norms over the bubble ends/necks and main ends/necks respectively (we will write the contribution to the norm squared): \begin{align} \left|\xi(n)\right|^2+&\int_{S^1\times[0,\infty)}\biggl[\left|\xi(t,s)-\xi(n)\right|^2+\sum_{j=1}^k\left|D^j\xi(t,s)\right|^2\biggr]e^{2\delta s}\;dt\,ds\\ \biggl|\int_{S^1}\xi(t,3S)\,dt\biggr|^2+&\int_{S^1\times[0,6S]}\biggl[\Bigl|\xi(t,s)-\int_{S^1}\xi(t,3S)\,dt\Bigr|^2+\sum_{j=1}^k\left|D^j\xi(t,s)\right|^2\biggr]e^{2\delta\min(s,6S-s)}\;dt\,ds\\ &\int_{S^1\times[N,\infty)}\sum_{j=0}^k\left|D^j\xi(t,s)\right|^2e^{2\delta(s-N)}\;dt\,ds\\ &\int_{S^1\times[N,6S-N]}\sum_{j=0}^k\left|D^j\xi(t,s)\right|^2e^{2\delta\min(s-N,6S-N-s)}\;dt\,ds \end{align} These are to be interpreted as follows. For each bubble node $n\in C_0$, we fix, once and for all, a small trivialization of $TM$ in a neighborhood of $u_0(n)$; this allows us to view $\xi$ as a function (rather than a section) for the purposes of the integrals over the bubble ends/necks. For each $i=0,\ldots,k$, we fix, once and for all, a smooth family of trivializations of $TM$ near $\gamma_i(t)$ (parameterized by $t\in S^1$); this allows us to view $\xi$ as a section of $\gamma_i^\ast TM$ for the purposes of the integrals over the main ends/necks. We also fix, once and for all, a connection on each such bundle $\gamma_i^\ast TM$ over $S^1$. The derivatives in the integrals above are measured with respect to the standard metric on $S^1\times\mathbb R$. The case of negative main ends is completely analogous to that of positive main ends. By Sobolev embedding $W^{2,2}\hookrightarrow C^0$ in two dimensions, we get uniform bounds linear in $\left\|\xi\right\|_{k,2,\delta,\delta}$ on $\left|\xi(t,s)-\xi(n)\right|e^{\delta s}$ in the bubble ends, $\left|\xi(t,s)\right|e^{\delta s}$ in the main ends, and $\left|D^j\xi(t,s)\right|e^{\delta s}$ ($1\leq j\leq k-2$) in all ends (as well as similar estimates in the necks). We will occasionally use other very similar weighted Sobolev spaces (e.g.\ $W^{k,2,\delta,\delta}(C_0,u_{0|\alpha}^\ast TM)$), and we leave it to the reader to make the necessary adjustments to the definition (which is essentially identical to the above).
nodes.statement_short: $(k,2)$-norm with exponential weights over all ends and necks, measured relative to the nodal value / neck average on bubble ends/necks.
nodes.label: weightedonespace

nodes.name: Weighted norms on ends and necks
nodes.statement: \left|\xi(n)\right|^2+&\int_{S^1\times[0,\infty)}\biggl[\left|\xi(t,s)-\xi(n)\right|^2+\sum_{j=1}^k\left|D^j\xi(t,s)\right|^2\biggr]e^{2\delta s}\;dt\,ds\\ \biggl|\int_{S^1}\xi(t,3S)\,dt\biggr|^2+&\int_{S^1\times[0,6S]}\biggl[\Bigl|\xi(t,s)-\int_{S^1}\xi(t,3S)\,dt\Bigr|^2+\sum_{j=1}^k\left|D^j\xi(t,s)\right|^2\biggr]e^{2\delta\min(s,6S-s)}\;dt\,ds\\ &\int_{S^1\times[N,\infty)}\sum_{j=0}^k\left|D^j\xi(t,s)\right|^2e^{2\delta(s-N)}\;dt\,ds\\ &\int_{S^1\times[N,6S-N]}\sum_{j=0}^k\left|D^j\xi(t,s)\right|^2e^{2\delta\min(s-N,6S-N-s)}\;dt\,ds
nodes.label: endnormHFbubble

nodes.name: Independence of trivializations
nodes.statement: The particular choice of trivializations and connections in the definition above is not crucial: any other (fixed) choice would lead to a uniformly commensurable norm (this holds because $u_0$ satisfies the exponential decay estimates \eqref{uzerobubble}, \eqref{uzeromain}, and because $\delta<1$ and $\delta<\delta_i$).
nodes.statement_short: Other choices of trivializations/connections give uniformly commensurable norms, by exponential decay of $u_0$.

nodes.name: Weighted Sobolev space $W^{k-1,2,\delta,\delta}(\tilde C_\alpha,T^\ast\tilde C_\alpha\otimes u_\alpha^\ast TM)$
nodes.statement: We define the weighted Sobolev space $W^{k-1,2,\delta,\delta}(\tilde C_\alpha,T^\ast\tilde C_\alpha\otimes_\mathbb R u_\alpha^\ast TM)$ using the usual $(k-1,2)$-norm away from the ends/necks, and using the following weighted $(k-1,2)$-norms over the bubble ends/necks (we will write the contribution to the norm squared): \begin{align} \int_{S^1\times[0,\infty)}&\sum_{j=0}^{k-1}\left|D^j\eta(t,s)\right|^2e^{2\delta s}\;dt\,ds\\ \int_{S^1\times[0,6S]}&\sum_{j=0}^{k-1}\left|D^j\eta(t,s)\right|^2e^{2\delta\min(s,6S-s)}\;dt\,ds \end{align} (for the main ends/necks, simply make the obvious replacement of $[0,\infty)$ with $[N,\infty)$ and $e^{2\delta s}$ with $e^{2\delta(s-N)}$, etc.). These are to be interpreted as follows. We trivialize $T\tilde C_\alpha$ over any end/neck with the basis vectors $\frac\partial{\partial t},\frac\partial{\partial s}$. We trivialize $TM$ as in Definition \ref{weightedonespace}, and hence the section $\eta$ is simply a pair of functions $\eta=(\eta_1,\eta_2)$. By Sobolev embedding $W^{2,2}\hookrightarrow C^0$ in two dimensions, we get uniform exponential decay bounds on $\eta$ up to $k-3$ derivatives in any end/neck, linear in $\left\|\eta\right\|_{k-1,2,\delta,\delta}$. We are actually interested in certain closed subspaces of $W^{k-1,2,\delta,\delta}(\tilde C_\alpha,T^\ast\tilde C_\alpha\otimes_\mathbb R u_\alpha^\ast TM)$, e.g.\ $W^{k-1,2,\delta,\delta}(\tilde C_\alpha,\Omega^{0,1}_{\tilde C_\alpha,j}\otimes_\mathbb C u_\alpha^\ast TM_J)$ for certain almost complex structures $j,J$ on $C_\alpha,M$ respectively, which we equip with the restriction of the norm defined above. We will occasionally use other very similar weighted Sobolev spaces, and we leave it to the reader to make the necessary adjustments to the definition (which is essentially identical to the above).
nodes.statement_short: $(k-1,2)$-norm on one-forms with exponential weights over ends and necks.

nodes.name: Weighted norms for one-forms
nodes.statement: \int_{S^1\times[0,\infty)}&\sum_{j=0}^{k-1}\left|D^j\eta(t,s)\right|^2e^{2\delta s}\;dt\,ds\\ \int_{S^1\times[0,6S]}&\sum_{j=0}^{k-1}\left|D^j\eta(t,s)\right|^2e^{2\delta\min(s,6S-s)}\;dt\,ds

The Fredholm index and the kernel/cokernel of the relevant linearized operators are unchanged by the placement of weights in the bubble ends/necks (the argument from Lemma \ref{fredholmandsamekernelcokernel} applies without modification).
nodes.name: Weights at bubble ends do not change index or kernel/cokernel

nodes.statement: We consider the following partially defined function: \begin{equation*} \mathcal F_{\alpha,w,y}:C^\infty(C_\alpha,u_\alpha^\ast TM)_{D,H}\oplus E\to C^\infty(\tilde C_\alpha,\Omega^{0,1}_{\tilde C_\alpha,j_y}\otimes_\mathbb C u_\alpha^\ast TM_{J(\ell_{\alpha,w}(A_y(\cdot)))}) \end{equation*} \vspace{-0.2in} \begin{multline} \mathcal F_{\alpha,w,y}(\xi):=\mathsf{PT}_{\exp_{u_\alpha}\xi\to u_\alpha}^{\ell_{\alpha,w}(A_y(\cdot))}\Bigl(d\exp_{u_\alpha}\xi+2d(\operatorname{proj}_{S^1}A_y)\otimes X_{H((\ell_{\alpha,w}\times\operatorname{id}_{S^1})(A_y(\cdot)))}(\exp_{u_\alpha}\xi)\\ {}+\lambda(e_0+\operatorname{proj}_E\xi)(\alpha,y,x^1,\ldots,x^r,\cdot,(\exp_{u_\alpha}\xi)(\cdot))\Bigr)^{0,1}_{j_y,J(\ell_{\alpha,w}(A_y(\cdot)))} \end{multline} (recall that $\mathsf{PT}$ and $(\cdot)^{0,1}$ commute). This function $\mathcal F_{\alpha,w,y}$ is defined for $\xi$ in a $C^1$-neighborhood of zero; for these $\xi$ we define $x^i=x^i(\xi)$ as the unique intersection of $(\operatorname{id}_{M\times S^1}\times\ell_{\alpha,w})\circ(\exp_{u_\alpha}\xi\times A_y)$ with $D_i$ close to the image of $x^i_0\in C_0$ in $C_\alpha$ (note, however, that even $x^i(0)$ may not coincide exactly with the image of $x^i_0\in C_0$ in $C_\alpha$); as before, these functions $x^i$ are of class $C^{k-2}$. The subscript $_{D,H}$ indicates restriction to sections which are tangent to $D$ at $p_1,\ldots,p_L$ and tangent to $H$ at $p_1',\ldots,p_{L'}'$. Thus for $\xi$ contained in a $C^0$-neighborhood of zero, $\exp_{u_\alpha}\xi$ sends $p_1,\ldots,p_L$ to $D^\circ$ and sends $p_1',\ldots,p_{L'}'$ to $H^\circ$.
nodes.name: Based section $\mathcal F_{\alpha,w,y}$
nodes.statement_short: $\mathcal F_{\alpha,w,y}(\xi)$: parallel-transported perturbed Floer operator of $\exp_{u_\alpha}\xi$ with obstruction term $\lambda(e_0+\mathrm{proj}_E\xi)$.

abla^{\ell_{\alpha,w}(A_y(\cdot))}\xi+T_

abla_\xi^{\ell_{\alpha,w}(A_y(\cdot))}X_{H((\ell_{\alpha,w}	imes\operatorname{id}_{S^1})(A_y(\cdot)))}\ &\quad\quad+\sum_{i=1}^r rac{d[\lambda(e_0)]}{dx^i}(\alpha,y,x^1,\ldots,x^r,\cdot,u_\alpha(\cdot))(-\operatorname{proj}_{TC_\alpha}\xi(x^i))\ &\quad\quad+

nodes.statement: For $\kappa\in K\subseteq C^\infty(C_0,u_0^\ast TM)$, we define $\kappa_\alpha\in C^\infty(C_\alpha,u_\alpha^\ast TM)$ as follows. Away from the necks, $\kappa_\alpha$ coincides with $\kappa$. Over a bubble neck $S^1\times[0,6S]$, we define $\kappa_\alpha$ as: \begin{equation} \kappa_\alpha(t,s):=\begin{cases} \kappa(t,s)&s\leq S-1\cr \mathsf{PT}_{u_0(t,s)\to u_\alpha(t,s)}\left[\kappa(t,s)\right]&S-1\leq s\leq S\cr \mathsf{PT}_{u_0(t,s)\to u_\alpha(t,s)}\left[\kappa(t,s)\right]\cdot(1-\chi(s-S))+\chi(s-S)\cdot \kappa(n)&S\leq s\leq S+1\cr \kappa(n)&S+1\leq s\leq 5S-1\cr \mathsf{PT}_{u_0(t',s')\to u_\alpha(t',s')}\left[\kappa(t',s')\right]\cdot(1-\chi(s'-S))+\chi(s'-S)\cdot \kappa(n)&5S-1\leq s\leq 5S\cr \mathsf{PT}_{u_0(t',s')\to u_\alpha(t',s')}\left[\kappa(t',s')\right]&5S\leq s\leq 5S+1\cr \kappa(t',s')&5S+1\leq s \end{cases} \end{equation} and over a main neck $S^1\times[N,6S-N]$, we define $\kappa_\alpha$ as: \begin{equation} \kappa_\alpha(t,s):=\begin{cases} \kappa(t,s)&s\leq S-1\cr \mathsf{PT}_{u_0(t,s)\to u_\alpha(t,s)}\left[\kappa(t,s)\right]&S-1\leq s\leq S\cr \mathsf{PT}_{u_0(t,s)\to u_\alpha(t,s)}\left[\kappa(t,s)\right]\cdot(1-\chi(s-S))&S\leq s\leq S+1\cr 0&S+1\leq s\leq 5S-1\cr \mathsf{PT}_{u_0(t',s')\to u_\alpha(t',s')}\left[\kappa(t',s')\right]\cdot(1-\chi(-s'-S))&5S-1\leq s\leq 5S\cr \mathsf{PT}_{u_0(t',s')\to u_\alpha(t',s')}\left[\kappa(t',s')\right]&5S\leq s\leq 5S+1\cr \kappa(t',s')&5S+1\leq s \end{cases} \end{equation}

nodes.statement: Note that we have the following estimates on $u_0$ and $\kappa\in K$: \begin{align} \text{in bubble ends:}&&\left|D^j\exp_{u_0(n)}^{-1}u_0(t,s)\right|&\leq c_je^{-s}\\ \text{in bubble ends:}&&\left|D^j[\kappa(t,s)-\kappa(n)]\right|&\leq c_je^{-s}\left\|\kappa\right\|\\ \text{in main ends:}&&\left|D^j\exp_{\gamma_i(t)}^{-1}u_0(t,s)\right|&\leq c_je^{-\delta's}&&\forall\delta'<\delta_i\\ \text{in main ends:}&&\left|D^j\kappa(t,s)\right|&\leq c_je^{-\delta's}\left\|\kappa\right\|&&\forall\delta'<\delta_i \end{align}
nodes.name: Exponential decay of $u_0$ and $\kappa$ on the ends
nodes.statement_short: $u_0$ and kernel elements $\kappa$ decay like $e^{-s}$ on bubble ends and $e^{-\delta' s}$ ($\delta'<\delta_i$) on main ends.

nodes.name: Decay estimates for $u_0$ and $\kappa$
nodes.statement: \text{in bubble ends:}&&\left|D^j\exp_{u_0(n)}^{-1}u_0(t,s)\right|&\leq c_je^{-s}\\ \text{in bubble ends:}&&\left|D^j[\kappa(t,s)-\kappa(n)]\right|&\leq c_je^{-s}\left\|\kappa\right\|\\ \text{in main ends:}&&\left|D^j\exp_{\gamma_i(t)}^{-1}u_0(t,s)\right|&\leq c_je^{-\delta's}&&\forall\delta'<\delta_i\\ \text{in main ends:}&&\left|D^j\kappa(t,s)\right|&\leq c_je^{-\delta's}\left\|\kappa\right\|&&\forall\delta'<\delta_i
