nodes.statement: The estimates in the bubble ends hold simply because $u_0$ and $\kappa$ are smooth on $C_0\setminus\{q_0,\ldots,q_k\}$. The estimates in the main ends hold for $u_0$ by Proposition \ref{neckestimateHF} and for $\kappa$ since $K=\ker D_{0,0,0}$ remains the same for any choice of $k\geq 6$ and any collection of end weights $\delta$, each of which is less than the corresponding $\delta_i$.
nodes.name: Proof of the decay estimates
nodes.statement_short: Smoothness on bubble ends; Proposition \ref{neckestimateHF} and weight-independence of $K$ on main ends.

nodes.name: Estimate for map pregluing (Hamiltonian Floer)
nodes.statement: We have the following estimate on $\mathcal F_{\alpha,w,y}(0)$: \begin{multline} \biggl\|\Bigl(du_\alpha+2d(\operatorname{proj}_{S^1}A_y)\otimes X_{H((\ell_{\alpha,w}\times\operatorname{id}_{S^1})(A_y(\cdot)))}(u_\alpha)\\ {}+\lambda(e_0)(\alpha,y,x^1,\ldots,x^r,\cdot,u_\alpha(\cdot))\Bigr)^{0,1}_{j_y,J(\ell_{\alpha,w}(A_y(\cdot)))}\biggr\|_{k-1,2,\delta,\delta} \leq c\cdot\bigl(\left|\alpha\right|^\epsilon+\left|w\right|+\left|y\right|\bigr) \end{multline} uniformly over $(\alpha,w,y)$ in a neighborhood of zero, for $c<\infty$ and $\epsilon>0$ depending on data which has been previously fixed.
nodes.statement_short: $\|\mathcal F_{\alpha,w,y}(0)\|\le c(|\alpha|^\epsilon+|w|+|y|)$: the preglued map almost solves the equation.
conclusions: We have the following estimate on $\mathcal F_{\alpha,w,y}(0)$: \begin{multline}\label{mappregluingdelbar} \biggl\|\Bigl(du_\alpha+2d(\operatorname{proj}_{S^1}A_y)\otimes X_{H((\ell_{\alpha,w}\times\operatorname{id}_{S^1})(A_y(\cdot)))}(u_\alpha)\\ {}+\lambda(e_0)(\alpha,y,x^1,\ldots,x^r,\cdot,u_\alpha(\cdot))\Bigr)^{0,1}_{j_y,J(\ell_{\alpha,w}(A_y(\cdot)))}\biggr\|_{k-1,2,\delta,\delta} \leq c\cdot\bigl(\left|\alpha\right|^\epsilon+\left|w\right|+\left|y\right|\bigr) \end{multline} uniformly over $(\alpha,w,y)$ in a neighborhood of zero, for $c<\infty$ and $\epsilon>0$ depending on data which has been previously fixed.
nodes.label: mappregluingissmallHF

nodes.name: Map pregluing estimate
nodes.statement: \biggl\|\Bigl(du_\alpha+2d(\operatorname{proj}_{S^1}A_y)\otimes X_{H((\ell_{\alpha,w}\times\operatorname{id}_{S^1})(A_y(\cdot)))}(u_\alpha)\\ {}+\lambda(e_0)(\alpha,y,x^1,\ldots,x^r,\cdot,u_\alpha(\cdot))\Bigr)^{0,1}_{j_y,J(\ell_{\alpha,w}(A_y(\cdot)))}\biggr\|_{k-1,2,\delta,\delta} \leq c\cdot\bigl(\left|\alpha\right|^\epsilon+\left|w\right|+\left|y\right|\bigr)
nodes.label: mappregluingdelbar

nodes.name: Proof
nodes.statement: Recall that: \begin{equation} \Bigl(du_0+2d(\operatorname{proj}_{S^1}A_0)\otimes X_{H((\ell_{0,0}\times\operatorname{id}_{S^1})(A_0(\cdot)))}(u_0) +\lambda(e_0)(0,0,x_0^1,\ldots,x_0^r,\cdot,u_0(\cdot))\Bigr)^{0,1}_{j_0,J(\ell_{0,0}(A_0(\cdot)))}=0 \end{equation} We estimate $\mathcal F_{\alpha,w,y}(0)$ over the main ends/necks. Note that over this region, the $\lambda$ term vanishes, $j_y=j_0$, $J(\ell_{\alpha,w}(A_y(\cdot)))=J(\ell_{0,0}(A_0(\cdot)))$, and $H((\ell_{\alpha,w}\times\operatorname{id}_{S^1})(A_y(\cdot)))=H((\ell_{0,0}\times\operatorname{id}_{S^1})(A_0(\cdot)))$. Now due to \eqref{delbareqnforuzeroHF}, it follows that in this region, $\mathcal F_{\alpha,w,y}(0)$ is supported inside the subsets $S^1\times([S-1,S]\cup[5S,5S+1])$ of the main necks $S^1\times[N,6S-N]$. The contribution of such a region to the norm of $\mathcal F_{\alpha,w,y}(0)$ is bounded above by a constant times $\left|\alpha\right|^\epsilon$, as follows from the estimate \eqref{uzeromain} on the derivatives of $u_0$ and the fact that $\delta<\delta_i$. We estimate $\mathcal F_{\alpha,w,y}(0)$ away from the ends/necks. Note that $\ell_{\alpha,w}$ is close to $\ell_{0,0}$, in the sense that they differ over $\coprod_{i=1}^k[-N,N]$ (which may be viewed as a subset of $\coprod_{i=1}^k\mathbb R$ and of $(\coprod_{i=1}^k)_\alpha$) by a constant times $\left|\alpha\right|^\epsilon+\left|w\right|$ in $C^\ell$ for some fixed $\epsilon>0$ (depending on the flow on $\Delta^n$ from Definition \ref{simplexflows}) and any $\ell<\infty$. It follows that away from the ends/necks, the $C^\ell$ distance between $J(\ell_{\alpha,w}(A_y(\cdot)))$ on $C_\alpha$ and $J(\ell_{0,0}(A_0(\cdot)))$ on $C_0$ is bounded by a constant (depending on $\ell$) times $\left|\alpha\right|^\epsilon+\left|w\right|+\left|y\right|$, where we identify $C_0$ and $C_\alpha$ away from the ends/necks in the canonical way (any $\ell<\infty$). The same holds for $H((\ell_{\alpha,w}\times\operatorname{id}_{S^1})(A_y(\cdot)))$ and $H((\ell_{0,0}\times\operatorname{id}_{S^1})(A_0(\cdot)))$. It also follows that the distance between $x^i\in C_\alpha$ and (the image in $C_\alpha$ of) $x^i_0\in C_0$ is bounded by a constant times $|\alpha|^\epsilon+\left|w\right|$. Hence we conclude that away from the ends/necks, $\mathcal F_{\alpha,w,y}(0)$ differs from the left hand side of \eqref{delbareqnforuzeroHF} in $C^\ell$ by a constant times $\left|\alpha\right|^\epsilon+\left|w\right|+\left|y\right|$ for any $\ell<\infty$. It follows that the contribution of this region to the norm of $\mathcal F_{\alpha,w,y}(0)$ is bounded by a constant times $\left|\alpha\right|^\epsilon+\left|w\right|+\left|y\right|$. We estimate $\mathcal F_{\alpha,w,y}(0)$ over the bubble ends. The reasoning above applies as written to imply that $\mathcal F_{\alpha,w,y}(0)$ is bounded in $C^\ell$ (with respect to the usual metric on $\tilde C_\alpha$) by a constant times $\left|\alpha\right|^\epsilon+\left|w\right|+\left|y\right|$ for any $\ell<\infty$. Since $\delta<1$, the weighted Sobolev norm over the bubble ends is also bounded by a constant times $\left|\alpha\right|^\epsilon+\left|w\right|+\left|y\right|$. We estimate $\mathcal F_{\alpha,w,y}(0)$ over the bubble necks $S^1\times[0,6S]$. The argument for the bubble ends applies to show that the contribution outside $S^1\times[S-1,5S+1]$ is bounded by a constant times $\left|\alpha\right|^\epsilon+\left|w\right|+\left|y\right|$. Over $S^1\times([S-1,S]\cup[5S,5S+1])$, we bound the expression termwise: both $u_\alpha$ and $A_y$ are $O(e^{-s})$ in all derivatives, so the contribution of this region is bounded by $\left|\alpha\right|^\epsilon$. Over $S^1\times[S,5S]$, only the term involving $X_H$ is nonzero, and since $A_y=O(e^{-s})$ in all derivatives, its contribution to the norm is bounded by a constant times $\left|\alpha\right|^\epsilon$ since $\delta<1$.
nodes.statement_short: Region-by-region estimate of $\mathcal F_{\alpha,w,y}(0)$ (main ends/necks, interior, bubble ends, bubble necks) using the equation for $u_0$ and exponential decay.

nodes.name: Floer equation for $u_0$
nodes.statement: \Bigl(du_0+2d(\operatorname{proj}_{S^1}A_0)\otimes X_{H((\ell_{0,0}\times\operatorname{id}_{S^1})(A_0(\cdot)))}(u_0) +\lambda(e_0)(0,0,x_0^1,\ldots,x_0^r,\cdot,u_0(\cdot))\Bigr)^{0,1}_{j_0,J(\ell_{0,0}(A_0(\cdot)))}=0
nodes.label: delbareqnforuzeroHF

nodes.name: Estimate for kernel pregluing (Hamiltonian Floer)
nodes.statement: For all $\kappa\in K$, we have: \begin{equation} \left\|D_{\alpha,w,y}\kappa_\alpha\right\|_{k-1,2,\delta,\delta}\leq c\cdot\bigl(\left|\alpha\right|^\epsilon+\left|w\right|+\left|y\right|\bigr)\left\|\kappa\right\| \end{equation} uniformly over $(\alpha,w,y)$ in a neighborhood of zero, for $c<\infty$ and $\epsilon>0$ depending on data which has been previously fixed.
nodes.statement_short: $\|D_{\alpha,w,y}\kappa_\alpha\|\le c(|\alpha|^\epsilon+|w|+|y|)\|\kappa\|$ for preglued kernel elements.
assumptions: For all $\kappa\in K$
conclusions: \left\|D_{\alpha,w,y}\kappa_\alpha\right\|_{k-1,2,\delta,\delta}\leq c\cdot\bigl(\left|\alpha\right|^\epsilon+\left|w\right|+\left|y\right|\bigr)\left\|\kappa\right\|
nodes.label: pregluingKestimateHF

nodes.name: Kernel pregluing estimate
nodes.statement: \left\|D_{\alpha,w,y}\kappa_\alpha\right\|_{k-1,2,\delta,\delta}\leq c\cdot\bigl(\left|\alpha\right|^\epsilon+\left|w\right|+\left|y\right|\bigr)\left\|\kappa\right\|

nodes.name: Proof
nodes.statement: Recall that $D_{0,0,0}\kappa=0$; we will use this to estimate $D_{\alpha,w,y}\kappa_\alpha$ via the explicit expression for $D_{\alpha,w,y}$ from Lemma \ref{linearizedformulaHF}. We estimate $D_{\alpha,w,y}\kappa_\alpha$ over the main ends/necks. Over this region, the $\lambda$ terms vanish, and $J,H$ are the same for $(\alpha,w,y)$ as they are for $(0,0,0)$. Thus $D_{\alpha,w,y}\kappa_\alpha$ is supported inside $S^1\times([S-1,S+1]\cup[5S-1,5S+1])$ in the main necks, and vanishes in the main ends. From the exponential decay estimates \eqref{uzeromain}--\eqref{kappamain}, we obtain that the contribution to the norm of $D_{\alpha,w,y}\kappa_\alpha$ over the main ends/necks is bounded by a constant times $\left|\alpha\right|^\epsilon\left\|\kappa\right\|$. We estimate $D_{\alpha,w,y}\kappa_\alpha$ away from the ends/necks. As in the proof of Lemma \ref{mappregluingissmallHF}, the difference between $J,H$ for $(\alpha,w,y)$ and for $(0,0,0)$ is bounded in $C^\ell$ by a constant times $\left|\alpha\right|^\epsilon+\left|w\right|+\left|y\right|$ for any $\ell<\infty$; similarly for the distance between $x^i$ and $x^i_0$. It thus follows from the explicit form in Lemma \ref{linearizedformulaHF} that the contribution to the norm of $D_{\alpha,w,y}\kappa_\alpha$ over this region is bounded by a constant times $(\left|\alpha\right|^\epsilon+\left|w\right|+\left|y\right|)\left\|\kappa\right\|$. Over the bubble ends, the same reasoning applies, and we obtain the desired bound since $\delta<1$. We estimate $D_{\alpha,w,y}\kappa_\alpha$ over the bubble necks. Outside $S^1\times[S-1,5S+1]$, the reasoning for the bubble ends applies to show that the contribution is bounded as desired. Over $S^1\times([S-1,S+1]\cup[5S-1,5S+1])$, the exponential decay estimates on $u_0$ and $\kappa$, along with similar estimates on $A_y$, show that the contribution of this region is bounded by $\left|\alpha\right|^\epsilon\left\|\kappa\right\|$ for some $\epsilon>0$ since $\delta<1$. Over $S^1\times[S+1,5S-1]$, only the term involving $X_H$ is nonzero, and its contribution is bounded by a constant times $\left|\alpha\right|^\epsilon\left\|\kappa\right\|$ since $\delta<1$ and $A_y$ decays like $O(e^{-s})$ in all derivatives.
nodes.statement_short: Region-by-region estimate using $D_{0,0,0}\kappa=0$, the explicit formula for $D_{\alpha,w,y}$ and exponential decay.

nodes.name: Surjectivity of the linearized operator D_{0,0,0}
nodes.statement: D_{0,0,0}:W^{k,2,\delta,\delta}(C_0,u_0^\ast TM)_{D,H}\oplus E\to W^{k-1,2,\delta,\delta}(\tilde C_0,\Omega^{0,1}_{\tilde C_0,j_0}\otimes_\mathbb C u_0^\ast TM_{J(\ell_{0,0}(A_0(\cdot)))})
nodes.statement_short: The linearized operator $D_{0,0,0}$ at the glued-from curve, assumed surjective.

nodes.name: Right inverse Q_{0,0,0} (image in E')
nodes.statement: Q_{0,0,0}:W^{k-1,2,\delta,\delta}(\tilde C_0,\Omega^{0,1}_{\tilde C_0,j_0}\otimes_\mathbb C u_0^\ast TM_{J(\ell_{0,0}(A_0(\cdot)))})\to W^{k,2,\delta,\delta}(C_0,u_0^\ast TM)_{D,H}\oplus E'
nodes.label: Qzerozerozero

nodes.statement: Fix a collection of points $z_i\in C_0$ ($1\leq i\leq h$) not nodes and not contained in any of the ends, subspaces $V_i\subseteq T_{u_0(z_i)}M$, and a subspace $E''\subseteq E'$ so that the natural evaluation map: \begin{equation} L_0:K\xrightarrow\sim\biggl(\bigoplus_{i=1}^hT_{u_0(z_i)}M/V_i\biggr)\oplus E/E'' \end{equation} is an isomorphism (such choices exist since $K\twoheadrightarrow E/E'$ is surjective and we may shrink the ends without loss of generality).
nodes.name: Evaluation map L_0
nodes.statement_short: Choose points $z_i$, subspaces $V_i$ and $E''\subseteq E'$ so that evaluation $L_0$ identifies $K$ with $\bigoplus T_{u_0(z_i)}M/V_i\oplus E/E''$.

nodes.name: Evaluation isomorphism L_0 on K
nodes.statement: L_0:K\xrightarrow\sim\biggl(\bigoplus_{i=1}^hT_{u_0(z_i)}M/V_i\biggr)\oplus E/E''

Now we can consider the same evaluation map on the larger space: \begin{equation} L_0:W^{k,2,\delta,\delta}(C_0,u_0^\ast TM)_{D,H}\oplus E\to W:=\biggl(\bigoplus_{i=1}^hT_{u_0(z_i)}M/V_i\biggr)\oplus E/E'' \end{equation}
nodes.name: Target space W and extended evaluation map L_0
Evaluation map L_0 and target space W
nodes.statement: L_0:W^{k,2,\delta,\delta}(C_0,u_0^\ast TM)_{D,H}\oplus E\to W:=\biggl(\bigoplus_{i=1}^hT_{u_0(z_i)}M/V_i\biggr)\oplus E/E''
nodes.label: lineartofixinverseHF

nodes.statement: Since $L_0$ sends $K=\ker D_{0,0,0}$ isomorphically to $W$, it follows that the restriction of $D_{0,0,0}$ to $\ker L_0$ is an isomorphism of Banach spaces. Hence there is a unique right inverse: \begin{equation} Q_{0,0,0}:W^{k-1,2,\delta,\delta}(\tilde C_0,\Omega^{0,1}_{\tilde C_0,j_0}\otimes_\mathbb C u_0^\ast TM_{J(\ell_{0,0}(A_0(\cdot)))})\to W^{k,2,\delta,\delta}(C_0,u_0^\ast TM)_{D,H}\oplus E \end{equation} with image $\ker L_0$, and it is bounded. Since $E''\subseteq E'$, $\operatorname{im} Q_{0,0,0}=\ker L_0$ is in fact contained in the right hand side of \eqref{Qzerozerozero}. We fix once and for all this $Q_{0,0,0}$.
nodes.name: Right inverse Q_{0,0,0}
nodes.statement_short: $Q_{0,0,0}$ is the unique bounded right inverse of $D_{0,0,0}$ with image $\ker L_0$; its image lies in the $E'$-version.

nodes.name: Right inverse Q_{0,0,0}
nodes.statement: Q_{0,0,0}:W^{k-1,2,\delta,\delta}(\tilde C_0,\Omega^{0,1}_{\tilde C_0,j_0}\otimes_\mathbb C u_0^\ast TM_{J(\ell_{0,0}(A_0(\cdot)))})\to W^{k,2,\delta,\delta}(C_0,u_0^\ast TM)_{D,H}\oplus E

nodes.name: Approximate right inverse T_{alpha,w,y}
nodes.statement: We define a map: \begin{equation} T_{\alpha,w,y}:W^{k-1,2,\delta,\delta}(\tilde C_\alpha,\Omega^{0,1}_{\tilde C_\alpha,j_y}\otimes_\mathbb C u_\alpha^\ast TM_{J(\ell_{\alpha,w}(A_y(\cdot)))})\to W^{k,2,\delta,\delta}(C_\alpha,u_\alpha^\ast TM)_{D,H}\oplus E \end{equation} as the composition: \begin{equation} T_{\alpha,w,y}:={\operatorname{glue}}\circ\mathsf{PT}\circ Q_{0,0,0}\circ\mathsf{PT}\circ(\operatorname{id}^{1,0}_\ast\otimes\operatorname{id}^{1,0})^{-1}\circ\operatorname{break} \end{equation} of maps in the following diagram, to be defined below: \begin{equation} \begin{tikzcd} W^{k,2,\delta,\delta}(C_\alpha,u_\alpha^\ast TM)_{D,H}\oplus E\ar{r}{D_{\alpha,w,y}}&W^{k-1,2,\delta,\delta}(\tilde C_\alpha,\Omega^{0,1}_{\tilde C_\alpha,j_y}\otimes_\mathbb C u_\alpha^\ast TM_{J(\ell_{\alpha,w}(A_y(\cdot)))})\ar{d}{\mathrm{break}}\\ W^{k,2,\delta,\delta}(C_0,u_{0|\alpha}^\ast TM)_{D,H}\oplus E\ar{u}{\mathrm{glue}}\ar{r}{D_{0|\alpha,0,y}}&W^{k-1,2,\delta,\delta}(\tilde C_0,\Omega^{0,1}_{\tilde C_0,j_y}\otimes_\mathbb C u_{0|\alpha}^\ast TM_{J(\ell_{0,0}(A_y(\cdot)))})\\ W^{k,2,\delta,\delta}(C_0,u_{0|\alpha}^\ast TM)_{D,H}\oplus E\ar[equals]{u}\ar{r}{D_{0|\alpha,0,0}}&W^{k-1,2,\delta,\delta}(\tilde C_0,\Omega^{0,1}_{\tilde C_0,j_0}\otimes_\mathbb C u_{0|\alpha}^\ast TM_{J(\ell_{0,0}(A_0(\cdot)))})\ar[leftrightarrow]{d}{\mathsf{PT}}\ar[swap]{u}{{\operatorname{id}^{1,0}_\ast}\otimes{\operatorname{id}^{1,0}}}\\ W^{k,2,\delta,\delta}(C_0,u_0^\ast TM)_{D,H}\oplus E\ar[leftrightarrow]{u}{\mathsf{PT}}\ar[yshift=0.5ex]{r}{D_{0,0,0}}&\ar[yshift=-0.5ex]{l}{Q_{0,0,0}}W^{k-1,2,\delta,\delta}(\tilde C_0,\Omega^{0,1}_{\tilde C_0,j_0}\otimes_\mathbb C u_0^\ast TM_{J(\ell_{0,0}(A_0(\cdot)))}) \end{tikzcd} \end{equation} The top and bottom horizontal maps $D_{\alpha,w,y}$ and $D_{0,0,0}$ are the linearized operators defined earlier. The third horizontal map $D_{0|\alpha,0,0}$ is the linearized operator at the flattened map $u_{0|\alpha}$ (its definition is identical to that of $D_{0,0,0}$ except for using $u_{0|\alpha}$ in place of $u_0$). Similarly, the second horizontal map $D_{0|\alpha,0,y}$ is the linearized operator at the flattened map $u_{0|\alpha}$, using $(j_y,A_y)$ in place of $(j_0,A_0)$. The vertical maps $\mathsf{PT}$ are simply parallel transport $\mathsf{PT}^{\ell_{0,0}(A_0(\cdot))}$; this is valid since $\mathsf{PT}$ is $J$-linear. The vertical map $\operatorname{id}^{1,0}_\ast\otimes\operatorname{id}^{1,0}$ denotes the tensor product of $\operatorname{id}^{1,0}:TM_{J(a)}\to TM_{J(b)}$ (the $(1,0)$-component of the identity map) and $\operatorname{id}^{1,0}_\ast:\Omega^{0,1}_{C_0,j_0}\to\Omega^{0,1}_{C_0,j_y}$ (the map induced by $\operatorname{id}^{1,0}:(TC_0,j_0)\to(TC_0,j_y)$). We define the map: \begin{equation} W^{k,2,\delta,\delta}(C_0,u_{0|\alpha}^\ast TM)_{D,H}\xrightarrow{\mathrm{glue}}W^{k,2,\delta,\delta}(C_\alpha,u_\alpha^\ast TM)_{D,H} \end{equation} Let $\xi\in W^{k,2,\delta,\delta}(C_0,u_{0|\alpha}^\ast TM)_{D,H}$. Away from the necks of $C_\alpha$, $\operatorname{glue}(\xi)$ is simply $\xi$. In any particular bubble neck $S^1\times[0,6S]\subseteq C_\alpha$, we define: \begin{equation} \operatorname{glue}(\xi)(s,t):=\begin{cases} \xi(s,t)&s\leq 2S\cr \xi(n)+\chi(4S-s)\cdot[\xi(s,t)-\xi(n)]+\chi(4S-s')\cdot[\xi(s',t')-\xi(n)]&2S\leq s\leq 4S\cr \xi(s',t')&4S\leq s \end{cases} \end{equation} (noting the corresponding ends $(t,s)\in S^1\times[0,\infty)\subseteq C_0$ and $(t',s')\in S^1\times[0,\infty)\subseteq C_0$); this definition also applies over the main necks with the obvious adjustment (and no $\xi(n)$ terms). We define the map: \begin{equation} W^{k-1,2,\delta,\delta}(\tilde C_\alpha,\Omega^{0,1}_{\tilde C_\alpha,j_y}\otimes_\mathbb C u_\alpha^\ast TM_{J(\ell_{\alpha,w}(A_y(\cdot)))})\xrightarrow{\mathrm{break}}W^{k-1,2,\delta,\delta}(\tilde C_0,\Omega^{0,1}_{\tilde C_0,j_y}\otimes_\mathbb C u_{0|\alpha}^\ast TM_{J(\ell_{0,0}(A_y(\cdot)))}) \end{equation} as follows. Fix a smooth function $\bar\chi:\mathbb R\to[0,1]$ such that: \begin{equation} \bar\chi(x)=\begin{cases}1&x\leq-1\cr0&x\geq+1\end{cases}\qquad\bar\chi(x)+\bar\chi(-x)=1 \end{equation} Let $\eta\in W^{k-1,2,\delta,\delta}(\tilde C_\alpha,\Omega^{0,1}_{\tilde C_\alpha,j_y}\otimes_\mathbb C u_\alpha^\ast TM_{J(\ell_{\alpha,w}(A_y(\cdot)))})$. Away from the ends with $\alpha\ne 0$, $\operatorname{break}(\eta)$ is given by $(\operatorname{id}^{1,0})^{-1}(\eta)$, where $\operatorname{id}^{1,0}:TM_{J(\ell_{0,0}(A_y(\cdot)))}\to TM_{J(\ell_{\alpha,w}(A_y(\cdot)))}$ denotes the $(1,0)$-component of the identity map. In any particular bubble end $[0,\infty)\times S^1\subseteq C_0$ with $\alpha\ne 0$, we define: \begin{equation} \operatorname{break}(\eta)(t,s):=\begin{cases} (\operatorname{id}^{1,0})^{-1}(\eta(t,s))&s\leq 3S-1\cr \bar\chi(s-3S)\cdot(\operatorname{id}^{1,0})^{-1}(\eta(t,s))&3S-1\leq s\leq 3S+1\cr 0&3S+1\leq s \end{cases} \end{equation} (noting the corresponding neck $[0,6S]\times S^1\subseteq C_\alpha$); this definition also applies over the main ends, with the obvious adjustment for negative main ends.
nodes.statement_short: Defines $T_{\alpha,w,y}$ as glue∘PT∘$Q_{0,0,0}$∘PT∘(id$^{1,0}$)$^{-1}$∘break, with the cut-off maps glue and break on necks/ends.

nodes.name: Domain and codomain of T_{alpha,w,y}
nodes.statement: T_{\alpha,w,y}:W^{k-1,2,\delta,\delta}(\tilde C_\alpha,\Omega^{0,1}_{\tilde C_\alpha,j_y}\otimes_\mathbb C u_\alpha^\ast TM_{J(\ell_{\alpha,w}(A_y(\cdot)))})\to W^{k,2,\delta,\delta}(C_\alpha,u_\alpha^\ast TM)_{D,H}\oplus E

nodes.name: T_{alpha,w,y} as a composition
nodes.statement: T_{\alpha,w,y}:={\operatorname{glue}}\circ\mathsf{PT}\circ Q_{0,0,0}\circ\mathsf{PT}\circ(\operatorname{id}^{1,0}_\ast\otimes\operatorname{id}^{1,0})^{-1}\circ\operatorname{break}

nodes.name: Big inverse diagram (Hamiltonian Floer)
nodes.statement: \begin{tikzcd} W^{k,2,\delta,\delta}(C_\alpha,u_\alpha^\ast TM)_{D,H}\oplus E\ar{r}{D_{\alpha,w,y}}&W^{k-1,2,\delta,\delta}(\tilde C_\alpha,\Omega^{0,1}_{\tilde C_\alpha,j_y}\otimes_\mathbb C u_\alpha^\ast TM_{J(\ell_{\alpha,w}(A_y(\cdot)))})\ar{d}{\mathrm{break}}\\ W^{k,2,\delta,\delta}(C_0,u_{0|\alpha}^\ast TM)_{D,H}\oplus E\ar{u}{\mathrm{glue}}\ar{r}{D_{0|\alpha,0,y}}&W^{k-1,2,\delta,\delta}(\tilde C_0,\Omega^{0,1}_{\tilde C_0,j_y}\otimes_\mathbb C u_{0|\alpha}^\ast TM_{J(\ell_{0,0}(A_y(\cdot)))})\\ W^{k,2,\delta,\delta}(C_0,u_{0|\alpha}^\ast TM)_{D,H}\oplus E\ar[equals]{u}\ar{r}{D_{0|\alpha,0,0}}&W^{k-1,2,\delta,\delta}(\tilde C_0,\Omega^{0,1}_{\tilde C_0,j_0}\otimes_\mathbb C u_{0|\alpha}^\ast TM_{J(\ell_{0,0}(A_0(\cdot)))})\ar[leftrightarrow]{d}{\mathsf{PT}}\ar[swap]{u}{{\operatorname{id}^{1,0}_\ast}\otimes{\operatorname{id}^{1,0}}}\\ W^{k,2,\delta,\delta}(C_0,u_0^\ast TM)_{D,H}\oplus E\ar[leftrightarrow]{u}{\mathsf{PT}}\ar[yshift=0.5ex]{r}{D_{0,0,0}}&\ar[yshift=-0.5ex]{l}{Q_{0,0,0}}W^{k-1,2,\delta,\delta}(\tilde C_0,\Omega^{0,1}_{\tilde C_0,j_0}\otimes_\mathbb C u_0^\ast TM_{J(\ell_{0,0}(A_0(\cdot)))}) \end{tikzcd}
nodes.label: biginversediagramHF

nodes.name: Glue map on W^{k,2,delta,delta}
nodes.statement: W^{k,2,\delta,\delta}(C_0,u_{0|\alpha}^\ast TM)_{D,H}\xrightarrow{\mathrm{glue}}W^{k,2,\delta,\delta}(C_\alpha,u_\alpha^\ast TM)_{D,H}

nodes.name: Formula for glue on a bubble neck
nodes.statement: \operatorname{glue}(\xi)(s,t):=\begin{cases} \xi(s,t)&s\leq 2S\cr \xi(n)+\chi(4S-s)\cdot[\xi(s,t)-\xi(n)]+\chi(4S-s')\cdot[\xi(s',t')-\xi(n)]&2S\leq s\leq 4S\cr \xi(s',t')&4S\leq s \end{cases}

nodes.name: Break map on W^{k-1,2,delta,delta}
nodes.statement: W^{k-1,2,\delta,\delta}(\tilde C_\alpha,\Omega^{0,1}_{\tilde C_\alpha,j_y}\otimes_\mathbb C u_\alpha^\ast TM_{J(\ell_{\alpha,w}(A_y(\cdot)))})\xrightarrow{\mathrm{break}}W^{k-1,2,\delta,\delta}(\tilde C_0,\Omega^{0,1}_{\tilde C_0,j_y}\otimes_\mathbb C u_{0|\alpha}^\ast TM_{J(\ell_{0,0}(A_y(\cdot)))})

nodes.name: Cutoff function bar chi
nodes.statement: \bar\chi(x)=\begin{cases}1&x\leq-1\cr0&x\geq+1\end{cases}\qquad\bar\chi(x)+\bar\chi(-x)=1

nodes.name: Formula for break on a bubble end
nodes.statement: \operatorname{break}(\eta)(t,s):=\begin{cases} (\operatorname{id}^{1,0})^{-1}(\eta(t,s))&s\leq 3S-1\cr \bar\chi(s-3S)\cdot(\operatorname{id}^{1,0})^{-1}(\eta(t,s))&3S-1\leq s\leq 3S+1\cr 0&3S+1\leq s \end{cases}

Let us make the elementary observation that the definition of $L_0$ extends perfectly well to give an analogous bounded linear map: \begin{equation} L_\alpha:W^{k,2,\delta,\delta}(C_\alpha,u_\alpha^\ast TM)_{D,H}\oplus E\to W \end{equation}
nodes.name: Evaluation map L_alpha
Evaluation map L_alpha on preglued curve
nodes.statement: L_\alpha:W^{k,2,\delta,\delta}(C_\alpha,u_\alpha^\ast TM)_{D,H}\oplus E\to W
nodes.label: newLonpregluedHF

nodes.statement: Since $\operatorname{im} Q_{0,0,0}\subseteq\ker L_0$, it follows from the definition of $T_{\alpha,w,y}$ that $\operatorname{im} T_{\alpha,w,y}\subseteq\ker L_\alpha$ as well.
nodes.name: Image of T_{alpha,w,y} lies in ker L_alpha
assumptions: $\operatorname{im} Q_{0,0,0}\subseteq\ker L_0$
conclusions: $\operatorname{im} T_{\alpha,w,y}\subseteq\ker L_\alpha$

nodes.name: Approximation estimate, bottom square
nodes.statement: Let: \begin{equation} \begin{CD} X@>D>>Y\cr @AGAA@VVBV\cr X'@>D'>>Y' \end{CD} \end{equation} denote the bottom square in \eqref{biginversediagramHF}. Then for $\xi\in X'$ and $\eta\in Y$ with $D'\xi=B\eta$, we have: \begin{equation} \left\|DG\xi-\eta\right\|\leq c\cdot\left|\alpha\right|^\epsilon\left\|\xi\right\| \end{equation} uniformly over $(\alpha,w,y)$ in a neighborhood of zero, for $c<\infty$ and $\epsilon>0$ depending on data which has been previously fixed.
nodes.statement_short: The bottom (parallel transport) square of the inverse diagram commutes up to an error $c|\alpha|^\epsilon$.
assumptions: for $\xi\in X'$ and $\eta\in Y$ with $D'\xi=B\eta$
conclusions: \left\|DG\xi-\eta\right\|\leq c\cdot\left|\alpha\right|^\epsilon\left\|\xi\right\|
nodes.label: approxbottomHF

nodes.name: Bottom square of the inverse diagram
nodes.statement: \begin{CD} X@>D>>Y\cr @AGAA@VVBV\cr X'@>D'>>Y' \end{CD}

nodes.name: Bottom square estimate
nodes.statement: \left\|DG\xi-\eta\right\|\leq c\cdot\left|\alpha\right|^\epsilon\left\|\xi\right\|

nodes.name: Proof
nodes.statement: In simpler terms, we bound the operator norm of the difference between the two diagonal compositions: \begin{equation} \left\|\mathsf{PT}\circ D_{0,0,0}-D_{0|\alpha,0,0}\circ\mathsf{PT}\right\|\leq c\left|\alpha\right|^\epsilon \end{equation} (this trivially implies the claimed statement). To show \eqref{betterPTcommutingoperatornormboundHF}, observe that the two operators only differ over the $S^1\times[S-1,\infty)$ subset of each end. Now it follows from Lemma \ref{linearizedformulaHF} that the contribution to the operator norm over $S^1\times[S-1,\infty)$ is bounded by a constant times the $C^k$-distance between $u_0$ and $u_{0|\alpha}$ over $S^1\times[0,\infty)$. The estimates \eqref{uzerobubble}, \eqref{uzeromain} imply that this distance is bounded by a constant times $\left|\alpha\right|^\epsilon$ (to be precise, the bubble ends contribute $\left|\alpha\right|^{1/6-\rho}$ and each main end contributes $\left|\alpha\right|^{\delta_i/6-\rho}$ for any $\rho>0$).
nodes.statement_short: Reduce to an operator-norm bound on PT∘$D_{0,0,0}$ − $D_{0|\alpha,0,0}$∘PT; the operators differ only far out in the ends, where the explicit linearized formula and the exponential decay of $u_0$ give $|\alpha|^\epsilon$.

nodes.name: Parallel transport commutation estimate
nodes.statement: \left\|\mathsf{PT}\circ D_{0,0,0}-D_{0|\alpha,0,0}\circ\mathsf{PT}\right\|\leq c\left|\alpha\right|^\epsilon
nodes.label: betterPTcommutingoperatornormboundHF

nodes.name: Approximation estimate, middle square
nodes.statement: Let: \begin{equation} \begin{CD} X@>D>>Y\cr @AGAA@VVBV\cr X'@>D'>>Y' \end{CD} \end{equation} denote the middle square in \eqref{biginversediagramHF}. Then for $\xi\in X'$ and $\eta\in Y$ with $D'\xi=B\eta$, we have: \begin{equation} \left\|DG\xi-\eta\right\|\leq c\cdot\left|y\right|\left\|\xi\right\| \end{equation} uniformly over $(\alpha,w,y)$ in a neighborhood of zero, for $c<\infty$ and $\epsilon>0$ depending on data which has been previously fixed.
nodes.statement_short: The middle square (changing $(j_0,A_0)$ to $(j_y,A_y)$) commutes up to an error $c|y|$.
assumptions: for $\xi\in X'$ and $\eta\in Y$ with $D'\xi=B\eta$
conclusions: \left\|DG\xi-\eta\right\|\leq c\cdot\left|y\right|\left\|\xi\right\|
nodes.label: approxmiddleHF

nodes.name: Middle square of the inverse diagram
nodes.statement: \begin{CD} X@>D>>Y\cr @AGAA@VVBV\cr X'@>D'>>Y' \end{CD}

nodes.name: Middle square estimate
nodes.statement: \left\|DG\xi-\eta\right\|\leq c\cdot\left|y\right|\left\|\xi\right\|

nodes.name: Proof
nodes.statement: In simpler terms, we have $\left\|D_{0|\alpha,0,y}-(\operatorname{id}^{1,0}_\ast\otimes\operatorname{id}^{1,0})\circ D_{0|\alpha,0,0}\right\|\leq c\cdot\left|y\right|$, which trivially implies the claimed statement. To prove this, argue as follows. We are comparing two first-order differential operators. Appealing to their explicit form from Lemma \ref{linearizedformulaHF}, we see that their coefficients differ by a constant times $\left|y\right|$ in $C^\ell$ for any $\ell<\infty$ (measuring with respect to the cylindrical coordinates $S^1\times[0,\infty)$ in the ends). It follows that we have the desired estimate.
nodes.statement_short: Compare coefficients of the two first-order operators via the explicit linearized formula; they differ by $O(|y|)$.

nodes.name: Approximation estimate, top square
nodes.statement: Let: \begin{equation} \begin{CD} X@>D>>Y\cr @AGAA@VVBV\cr X'@>D'>>Y' \end{CD} \end{equation} denote the top square in \eqref{biginversediagramHF}. Then for $\xi\in X'$ and $\eta\in Y$ with $D'\xi=B\eta$, we have: \begin{equation} \left\|DG\xi-\eta\right\|\leq c\cdot\bigl(\left|\alpha\right|^\epsilon+\left|w\right|\bigr)\left\|\xi\right\| \end{equation} uniformly over $(\alpha,w,y)$ in a neighborhood of zero, for $c<\infty$ and $\epsilon>0$ depending on data which has been previously fixed.
nodes.statement_short: The top (gluing/breaking) square commutes up to an error $c(|\alpha|^\epsilon+|w|)$.
assumptions: for $\xi\in X'$ and $\eta\in Y$ with $D'\xi=B\eta$
conclusions: \left\|DG\xi-\eta\right\|\leq c\cdot\bigl(\left|\alpha\right|^\epsilon+\left|w\right|\bigr)\left\|\xi\right\|
nodes.label: approxtopHF

nodes.name: Top square of the inverse diagram
nodes.statement: \begin{CD} X@>D>>Y\cr @AGAA@VVBV\cr X'@>D'>>Y' \end{CD}

nodes.name: Top square estimate
nodes.statement: \left\|DG\xi-\eta\right\|\leq c\cdot\bigl(\left|\alpha\right|^\epsilon+\left|w\right|\bigr)\left\|\xi\right\|

nodes.name: Proof
nodes.statement: We consider the following diagram, which is a copy of the top square in \eqref{biginversediagramHF} with one extra vector space and some extra maps (to be defined below). \begin{equation} \begin{tikzcd}[row sep = tiny] {}&W^{k-1,2,\delta,\delta}(\tilde C_\alpha,\Omega^{0,1}_{\tilde C_\alpha,j_y}\otimes_\mathbb C u_\alpha^\ast TM_{J(\ell_{\alpha,w}(A_y(\cdot)))})\ar[shift left=0.5ex]{dd}{\mathrm{break}'}\ar[rounded corners,to path={(\tikztostart) -- ([xshift=2ex]\tikztostart.east) -- ([xshift=2ex]\tikztotarget.east) \tikztonodes -- (\tikztotarget)}]{dddd}{\mathrm{break}}\\ W^{k,2,\delta,\delta}(C_\alpha,u_\alpha^\ast TM)_{D,H}\oplus E\ar{ru}{D_{\alpha,w,y}}\\ {}&W^{k-1,2,\delta,\delta}(\tilde C_0,\Omega^{0,1}_{\tilde C_0,j_y}\otimes_\mathbb C u_{0|\alpha}^\ast TM_{J(\ell_{\alpha,w}(A_y(\cdot)))})\ar[shift right=-0.5ex]{uu}{\mathrm{glue}}\ar[shift left=0.5ex]{dd}{(\operatorname{id}^{1,0})^{-1}}\\ W^{k,2,\delta,\delta}(C_0,u_{0|\alpha}^\ast TM)_{D,H}\oplus E\ar{uu}{\mathrm{glue}}\ar{rd}{D_{0|\alpha,0,y}}\ar{ru}{D_{\alpha,w,y}}\\ {}&W^{k-1,2,\delta,\delta}(\tilde C_0,\Omega^{0,1}_{\tilde C_0,j_y}\otimes_\mathbb C u_{0|\alpha}^\ast TM_{J(\ell_{0,0}(A_y(\cdot)))})\ar[shift right=-0.5ex]{uu}{\operatorname{id}^{1,0}} \end{tikzcd} \end{equation} Since the almost complex structure $J(\ell_{\alpha,w}(A_y(\cdot)))$ is a function of a point in $C_\alpha$, we should remark immediately on what we mean by $W^{k-1,2,\delta,\delta}(\tilde C_0,\Omega^{0,1}_{\tilde C_0,j_y}\otimes_\mathbb C u_{0|\alpha}^\ast TM_{J(\ell_{\alpha,w}(A_y(\cdot)))})$. Away from the ends, the curve $C_0$ is identified canonically with $C_\alpha$, and this identification extends holomorphically to a (non-injective) map from $C_0$ to $C_\alpha$ defined outside the $S^1\times[4S,\infty)$ subsets of the ends. Thus there is a well-defined such $W^{k-1,2,\delta,\delta}$ space of sections on $C_0$ defined outside the $S^1\times[4S,\infty)$ subsets of the ends, valued in $\Omega^{0,1}_{\tilde C_0,j_y}\otimes_\mathbb C u_{0|\alpha}^\ast TM_{J(\ell_{\alpha,w}(A_y(\cdot)))}$. Now, for instance, the middle horizontal map $D_{\alpha,w,y}$ can be seen as giving a section in this $W^{k-1,2,\delta,\delta}$ space defined outside $S^1\times[4S,\infty)$. In the proof below, it is convenient to use this $W^{k-1,2,\delta,\delta}$ space of sections defined outside $S^1\times[4S,\infty)$, though we must be careful that the expressions we write are well-defined. Let us define the rest of the maps in \eqref{topdiagrambigger}. The vertical map $\operatorname{break}$ has been factored as $(\operatorname{id}^{1,0})^{-1}\circ\operatorname{break}'$ in the obvious way. Finally, let us define the map: \begin{equation} W^{k-1,2,\delta,\delta}(\tilde C_0,\Omega^{0,1}_{\tilde C_0,j_y}\otimes_\mathbb C u_{0|\alpha}^\ast TM_{J(\ell_{\alpha,w}(A_y(\cdot)))})\xrightarrow{\mathrm{glue}}W^{k-1,2,\delta,\delta}(\tilde C_\alpha,\Omega^{0,1}_{\tilde C_\alpha,j_y}\otimes_\mathbb C u_\alpha^\ast TM_{J(\ell_{\alpha,w}(A_y(\cdot)))}) \end{equation} Let $\eta\in W^{k-1,2,\delta,\delta}(\tilde C_0,\Omega^{0,1}_{\tilde C_0,j_y}\otimes_\mathbb C u_{0|\alpha}^\ast TM_{J(\ell_{\alpha,w}(A_y(\cdot)))})$. Away from the necks of $C_\alpha$, $\operatorname{glue}(\eta)$ is simply $\eta$. In any particular bubble neck $S^1\times[0,6S]\subseteq C_\alpha$, we define: \begin{equation} \operatorname{glue}(\eta)(t,s):=\begin{cases} \eta(t,s)&s\leq 2S\cr \chi(4S-s)\eta(t,s)+\chi(4S-s')\eta(t',s')&2S\leq s\leq 4S\cr \eta(t',s')&4S\leq s \end{cases} \end{equation} (this definition also applies over the main necks with the obvious adjustment). Note that $\operatorname{glue}\circ\operatorname{break}'$ is the identity map. Now suppose that $D_{0|\alpha,0,y}\xi=\operatorname{break}(\eta)$; we must show that: \begin{equation} \left\|D_{\alpha,w,y}(\operatorname{glue}(\xi))-\eta\right\|_{k-1,2,\delta,\delta}\leq c\cdot\bigl(\left|\alpha\right|^\epsilon+\left|w\right|\bigr)\left\|\xi\right\|_{k,2,\delta,\delta} \end{equation} Using the triangle inequality and the fact that $\eta=\operatorname{glue}(\operatorname{break}'(\eta))=\operatorname{glue}(\operatorname{id}^{1,0}(D_{0|\alpha,0,y}\xi))$, we conclude that $\left\|D_{\alpha,w,y}(\operatorname{glue}(\xi))-\eta\right\|$ is bounded above by: \begin{equation*} \left\|D_{\alpha,w,y}(\operatorname{glue}(\xi))-\operatorname{glue}(D_{\alpha,w,y}(\xi))\right\|+\left\|\operatorname{glue}\left[D_{\alpha,w,y}(\xi)-\operatorname{id}^{1,0}(D_{0|\alpha,0,y}(\xi))\right]\right\| \end{equation*} We now estimate each term separately. To estimate $\left\|D_{\alpha,w,y}(\operatorname{glue}(\xi))-\operatorname{glue}(D_{\alpha,w,y}(\xi))\right\|$, argue as follows. The difference is only nonzero over the regions $S^1\times([2S,2S+1]\cup[4S-1,4S])$ of each neck. Now the norm is bounded by $\left\|\xi\right\|e^{-2S\delta}$ (calculation left to the reader), where the factor of $e^{-2S\delta}$ comes as the ratio of the weight given to $S^1\times[4S-1,4S]$ inside a neck vs inside an end; this gives the desired bound since $\delta>0$. To estimate $\left\|\operatorname{glue}\left[D_{\alpha,w,y}(\xi)-\operatorname{id}^{1,0}(D_{0|\alpha,0,y}\xi)\right]\right\|$, argue as follows. This is bounded by a constant times the $(k-1,2,\delta,\delta)$-norm of $D_{\alpha,w,y}(\xi)-\operatorname{id}^{1,0}(D_{0|\alpha,0,y}\xi)$ over the complement of the subsets $S^1\times[4S,\infty)$ of the ends. Now this is bounded by $(\left|\alpha\right|^\epsilon+\left|w\right|)\left\|\xi\right\|_{k,2,\delta,\delta}$ using the reasoning from Lemma \ref{approxmiddleHF}.
nodes.statement_short: Enlarge the top square by factoring break through break' and a glue map on (0,1)-forms; split the error by the triangle inequality and bound the two terms by cut-off support and the middle-square reasoning.

nodes.name: Enlarged top square diagram
nodes.statement: \begin{tikzcd}[row sep = tiny] {}&W^{k-1,2,\delta,\delta}(\tilde C_\alpha,\Omega^{0,1}_{\tilde C_\alpha,j_y}\otimes_\mathbb C u_\alpha^\ast TM_{J(\ell_{\alpha,w}(A_y(\cdot)))})\ar[shift left=0.5ex]{dd}{\mathrm{break}'}\ar[rounded corners,to path={(\tikztostart) -- ([xshift=2ex]\tikztostart.east) -- ([xshift=2ex]\tikztotarget.east) \tikztonodes -- (\tikztotarget)}]{dddd}{\mathrm{break}}\\ W^{k,2,\delta,\delta}(C_\alpha,u_\alpha^\ast TM)_{D,H}\oplus E\ar{ru}{D_{\alpha,w,y}}\\ {}&W^{k-1,2,\delta,\delta}(\tilde C_0,\Omega^{0,1}_{\tilde C_0,j_y}\otimes_\mathbb C u_{0|\alpha}^\ast TM_{J(\ell_{\alpha,w}(A_y(\cdot)))})\ar[shift right=-0.5ex]{uu}{\mathrm{glue}}\ar[shift left=0.5ex]{dd}{(\operatorname{id}^{1,0})^{-1}}\\ W^{k,2,\delta,\delta}(C_0,u_{0|\alpha}^\ast TM)_{D,H}\oplus E\ar{uu}{\mathrm{glue}}\ar{rd}{D_{0|\alpha,0,y}}\ar{ru}{D_{\alpha,w,y}}\\ {}&W^{k-1,2,\delta,\delta}(\tilde C_0,\Omega^{0,1}_{\tilde C_0,j_y}\otimes_\mathbb C u_{0|\alpha}^\ast TM_{J(\ell_{0,0}(A_y(\cdot)))})\ar[shift right=-0.5ex]{uu}{\operatorname{id}^{1,0}} \end{tikzcd}
nodes.label: topdiagrambigger

nodes.name: Glue map on (0,1)-forms
nodes.statement: W^{k-1,2,\delta,\delta}(\tilde C_0,\Omega^{0,1}_{\tilde C_0,j_y}\otimes_\mathbb C u_{0|\alpha}^\ast TM_{J(\ell_{\alpha,w}(A_y(\cdot)))})\xrightarrow{\mathrm{glue}}W^{k-1,2,\delta,\delta}(\tilde C_\alpha,\Omega^{0,1}_{\tilde C_\alpha,j_y}\otimes_\mathbb C u_\alpha^\ast TM_{J(\ell_{\alpha,w}(A_y(\cdot)))})

nodes.name: Formula for glue on (0,1)-forms over a neck
nodes.statement: \operatorname{glue}(\eta)(t,s):=\begin{cases} \eta(t,s)&s\leq 2S\cr \chi(4S-s)\eta(t,s)+\chi(4S-s')\eta(t',s')&2S\leq s\leq 4S\cr \eta(t',s')&4S\leq s \end{cases}

nodes.name: Top square estimate to prove
nodes.statement: \left\|D_{\alpha,w,y}(\operatorname{glue}(\xi))-\eta\right\|_{k-1,2,\delta,\delta}\leq c\cdot\bigl(\left|\alpha\right|^\epsilon+\left|w\right|\bigr)\left\|\xi\right\|_{k,2,\delta,\delta}

nodes.name: Approximate right inverse T_{alpha,w,y}
nodes.statement: We have: \begin{align} \left\|T_{\alpha,w,y}\right\|&\leq c\\ \left\|D_{\alpha,w,y} T_{\alpha,w,y}-\mathbf 1\right\|&\to 0\\ \operatorname{im} T_{\alpha,w,y}&\subseteq\ker L_\alpha \end{align} as $(\alpha,w,y)\to 0$, for $c<\infty$ depending on data which has been previously fixed.
nodes.statement_short: $T_{\alpha,w,y}$ is uniformly bounded, is an approximate right inverse of $D_{\alpha,w,y}$ as $(\alpha,w,y)\to 0$, and has image in $\ker L_\alpha$.
assumptions: as $(\alpha,w,y)\to 0$, for $c<\infty$ depending on data which has been previously fixed
conclusions: \left\|T_{\alpha,w,y}\right\|&\leq c\\ \label{TapproxeqnHF}\left\|D_{\alpha,w,y} T_{\alpha,w,y}-\mathbf 1\right\|&\to 0\\ \operatorname{im} T_{\alpha,w,y}&\subseteq\ker L_\alpha
nodes.label: approxworksHF

nodes.name: Approximate right inverse estimate
nodes.statement: \left\|T_{\alpha,w,y}\right\|&\leq c\\ \left\|D_{\alpha,w,y} T_{\alpha,w,y}-\mathbf 1\right\|&\to 0\\ \operatorname{im} T_{\alpha,w,y}&\subseteq\ker L_\alpha
nodes.label: TapproxeqnHF

nodes.name: Proof
nodes.statement: It is easy to see that all the maps in \eqref{biginversediagramHF} are uniformly bounded. Hence $\left\|T_{\alpha,w,y}\right\|\leq c$ as $(\alpha,w,y)\to 0$. Now Lemma \ref{bootstrappingapprox} combined with Lemmas \ref{approxbottomHF}, \ref{approxmiddleHF}, \ref{approxtopHF} show that for $(\alpha,w,y)\to 0$, we have $\left\|D_{\alpha,w,y} T_{\alpha,w,y}-\mathbf 1\right\|\to 0$. We observed earlier that $\operatorname{im} T_{\alpha,w,y}\subseteq\ker L_\alpha$.
nodes.statement_short: Uniform boundedness of the diagram maps, plus the bootstrapping lemma applied to the three square estimates.

nodes.name: Right inverse Q_{alpha,w,y}
nodes.statement: We define a map: \begin{equation} Q_{\alpha,w,y}:W^{k-1,2,\delta,\delta}(\tilde C_\alpha,\Omega^{0,1}_{\tilde C_\alpha,j_y}\otimes_\mathbb C u_\alpha^\ast TM_{J(\ell_{\alpha,w}(A_y(\cdot)))})\to W^{k,2,\delta,\delta}(C_\alpha,u_\alpha^\ast TM)_{D,H}\oplus E \end{equation} as the sum: \begin{equation} Q_{\alpha,w,y}:=T_{\alpha,w,y}\sum_{k=0}^\infty(\mathbf 1-D_{\alpha,w,y}T_{\alpha,w,y})^k \end{equation}
nodes.statement_short: $Q_{\alpha,w,y}$ is the Neumann-series correction $T\sum_k(1-DT)^k$ of the approximate right inverse.

nodes.name: Domain and codomain of Q_{alpha,w,y}
nodes.statement: Q_{\alpha,w,y}:W^{k-1,2,\delta,\delta}(\tilde C_\alpha,\Omega^{0,1}_{\tilde C_\alpha,j_y}\otimes_\mathbb C u_\alpha^\ast TM_{J(\ell_{\alpha,w}(A_y(\cdot)))})\to W^{k,2,\delta,\delta}(C_\alpha,u_\alpha^\ast TM)_{D,H}\oplus E

nodes.name: Neumann series for Q_{alpha,w,y}
nodes.statement: Q_{\alpha,w,y}:=T_{\alpha,w,y}\sum_{k=0}^\infty(\mathbf 1-D_{\alpha,w,y}T_{\alpha,w,y})^k

nodes.name: Estimates for the right inverse Q_{alpha,w,y}
nodes.statement: We have: \begin{align} \left\|Q_{\alpha,w,y}\right\|&\leq c\\ D_{\alpha,w,y}Q_{\alpha,w,y}&=\mathbf 1\\ \operatorname{im} Q_{\alpha,w,y}&\subseteq\ker L_\alpha \end{align} uniformly over $(\alpha,w,y)$ in a neighborhood of zero, for $c<\infty$ depending on data which has been previously fixed.
nodes.statement_short: $Q_{\alpha,w,y}$ is a uniformly bounded right inverse of $D_{\alpha,w,y}$ with image in $\ker L_\alpha$.
assumptions: uniformly over $(\alpha,w,y)$ in a neighborhood of zero, for $c<\infty$ depending on data which has been previously fixed
conclusions: \left\|Q_{\alpha,w,y}\right\|&\leq c\\ D_{\alpha,w,y}Q_{\alpha,w,y}&=\mathbf 1\\ \operatorname{im} Q_{\alpha,w,y}&\subseteq\ker L_\alpha
nodes.label: QestimatesHF

nodes.name: Properties of Q_{alpha,w,y}
nodes.statement: \left\|Q_{\alpha,w,y}\right\|&\leq c\\ D_{\alpha,w,y}Q_{\alpha,w,y}&=\mathbf 1\\ \operatorname{im} Q_{\alpha,w,y}&\subseteq\ker L_\alpha

nodes.name: Proof
nodes.statement: Apply Lemma \ref{bootstrapinverse} and Proposition \ref{approxworksHF}.
nodes.statement_short: Apply the abstract inverse-bootstrapping lemma to the approximate right inverse.

nodes.name: Quadratic estimate
nodes.statement: There exist $c'>0$ and $c<\infty$ (depending on data which has been previously fixed) such that for $\left\|\xi_1\right\|_{k,2,\delta,\delta},\left\|\xi_2\right\|_{k,2,\delta,\delta}\leq c'$, we have: \begin{equation} \bigl\|D_{\alpha,w,y}(\xi_1-\xi_2)-(\mathcal F_{\alpha,w,y}\xi_1-\mathcal F_{\alpha,w,y}\xi_2)\bigr\|_{k-1,2,\delta,\delta}\leq c\cdot\left\|\xi_1-\xi_2\right\|_{k,2,\delta,\delta}(\left\|\xi_1\right\|_{k,2,\delta,\delta}+\left\|\xi_2\right\|_{k,2,\delta,\delta}) \end{equation} (and $\mathcal F_{\alpha,w,y}\xi_1$ and $\mathcal F_{\alpha,w,y}\xi_2$ are both defined), uniformly over $(\alpha,w,y)$ in a neighborhood of zero.
nodes.statement_short: The nonlinear section $\mathcal F_{\alpha,w,y}$ differs from its linearization by a quadratic error, uniformly near zero.
assumptions: for $\left\|\xi_1\right\|_{k,2,\delta,\delta},\left\|\xi_2\right\|_{k,2,\delta,\delta}\leq c'$
conclusions: \bigl\|D_{\alpha,w,y}(\xi_1-\xi_2)-(\mathcal F_{\alpha,w,y}\xi_1-\mathcal F_{\alpha,w,y}\xi_2)\bigr\|_{k-1,2,\delta,\delta}\leq c\cdot\left\|\xi_1-\xi_2\right\|_{k,2,\delta,\delta}(\left\|\xi_1\right\|_{k,2,\delta,\delta}+\left\|\xi_2\right\|_{k,2,\delta,\delta})
nodes.label: quadestimateHF

nodes.name: Quadratic estimate inequality
nodes.statement: \bigl\|D_{\alpha,w,y}(\xi_1-\xi_2)-(\mathcal F_{\alpha,w,y}\xi_1-\mathcal F_{\alpha,w,y}\xi_2)\bigr\|_{k-1,2,\delta,\delta}\leq c\cdot\left\|\xi_1-\xi_2\right\|_{k,2,\delta,\delta}(\left\|\xi_1\right\|_{k,2,\delta,\delta}+\left\|\xi_2\right\|_{k,2,\delta,\delta})
nodes.label: quadestgoalHF

nodes.name: Proof
nodes.statement: The proof is identical to the proof of Lemma \ref{quadestimate}, with the evident notational differences, $\mathcal F_{\alpha,w,y}$ for $\mathcal F_{\alpha,y}$, and Lemma \ref{linearizedformulaHF} for Lemma \ref{linearizedformula}. As with Lemma \ref{quadestimate}, we actually prove the stronger statement that: \begin{equation} \left\|\mathcal F_{\alpha,w,y}'(0,\xi)-\mathcal F_{\alpha,w,y}'(\zeta,\xi)\right\|_{k-1,2,\delta,\delta}\leq c\cdot\left\|\zeta\right\|_{k,2,\delta,\delta}\left\|\xi\right\|_{k,2,\delta,\delta} \end{equation}
nodes.statement_short: Same as the Gromov--Witten quadratic estimate with notational changes; in fact prove Lipschitz continuity of the derivative.

nodes.name: Lipschitz bound on the derivative of F_{alpha,w,y}
nodes.statement: \left\|\mathcal F_{\alpha,w,y}'(0,\xi)-\mathcal F_{\alpha,w,y}'(\zeta,\xi)\right\|_{k-1,2,\delta,\delta}\leq c\cdot\left\|\zeta\right\|_{k,2,\delta,\delta}\left\|\xi\right\|_{k,2,\delta,\delta}
nodes.label: derivislipHF

nodes.name: Contraction property
nodes.statement: There exists $c'>0$ (depending on data which has been previously fixed) such that for sufficiently small $(\alpha,w,y)$: \begin{rlist} \item The map $\mathcal F_{\alpha,w,y}$ is defined for $\left\|\xi\right\|_{k,2,\delta,\delta}\leq c'$. \item For $\xi_1-\xi_2\in\operatorname{im} Q_{\alpha,w,y}$ and $\left\|\xi_1\right\|_{k,2,\delta,\delta},\left\|\xi_2\right\|_{k,2,\delta,\delta}\leq c'$, we have: \begin{equation} \left\|(\xi_1-\xi_2)-(Q_{\alpha,w,y}\mathcal F_{\alpha,w,y}\xi_1-Q_{\alpha,w,y}\mathcal F_{\alpha,w,y}\xi_2)\right\|_{k,2,\delta,\delta}\leq\frac 12\left\|\xi_1-\xi_2\right\|_{k,2,\delta,\delta} \end{equation} \end{rlist}
nodes.statement_short: For small parameters, $\xi\mapsto\xi-Q\mathcal F\xi$ is a $\frac12$-contraction along $\operatorname{im}Q_{\alpha,w,y}$ on a fixed ball.
assumptions: for sufficiently small $(\alpha,w,y)$
conclusions: The map $\mathcal F_{\alpha,w,y}$ is defined for $\left\|\xi\right\|_{k,2,\delta,\delta}\leq c'$.
\left\|(\xi_1-\xi_2)-(Q_{\alpha,w,y}\mathcal F_{\alpha,w,y}\xi_1-Q_{\alpha,w,y}\mathcal F_{\alpha,w,y}\xi_2)\right\|_{k,2,\delta,\delta}\leq\frac 12\left\|\xi_1-\xi_2\right\|_{k,2,\delta,\delta}
nodes.label: contractionpropHF

nodes.name: Contraction inequality
nodes.statement: \left\|(\xi_1-\xi_2)-(Q_{\alpha,w,y}\mathcal F_{\alpha,w,y}\xi_1-Q_{\alpha,w,y}\mathcal F_{\alpha,w,y}\xi_2)\right\|_{k,2,\delta,\delta}\leq\frac 12\left\|\xi_1-\xi_2\right\|_{k,2,\delta,\delta}

nodes.name: Proof
nodes.statement: The proof is identical to the proof of Lemma \ref{contractionprop}, using Proposition \ref{quadestimateHF} in place of Proposition \ref{quadestimate}.
nodes.statement_short: Same as the Gromov--Witten contraction lemma, using the Floer quadratic estimate.

nodes.name: Newton--Picard iteration
nodes.statement: There exists $c'>0$ (depending on data which has been previously fixed) so that for $(\alpha,w,y,\kappa\in K)$ sufficiently small, there exists a unique $\kappa_{\alpha,w,y}\in W^{k,2,\delta,\delta}(C_\alpha,u_\alpha^\ast TM)_{D,H}\oplus E$ satisfying: \begin{align} \kappa_{\alpha,w,y}&\in\kappa_\alpha+\operatorname{im} Q_{\alpha,w,y}\\ \left\|\kappa_{\alpha,w,y}\right\|_{k,2,\delta,\delta}&\leq c'\\ \mathcal F_{\alpha,w,y}\kappa_{\alpha,w,y}&=0 \end{align}
nodes.statement_short: For small $(\alpha,w,y,\kappa)$ there is a unique zero $\kappa_{\alpha,w,y}$ of $\mathcal F_{\alpha,w,y}$ in $\kappa_\alpha+\operatorname{im}Q_{\alpha,w,y}$ of bounded norm.
assumptions: for $(\alpha,w,y,\kappa\in K)$ sufficiently small
conclusions: there exists a unique $\kappa_{\alpha,w,y}\in W^{k,2,\delta,\delta}(C_\alpha,u_\alpha^\ast TM)_{D,H}\oplus E$ satisfying: \begin{align} \kappa_{\alpha,w,y}&\in\kappa_\alpha+\operatorname{im} Q_{\alpha,w,y}\\ \left\|\kappa_{\alpha,w,y}\right\|_{k,2,\delta,\delta}&\leq c'\\ \mathcal F_{\alpha,w,y}\kappa_{\alpha,w,y}&=0
nodes.label: newtoniterationHF

nodes.name: Characterization of kappa_{alpha,w,y}
nodes.statement: \kappa_{\alpha,w,y}&\in\kappa_\alpha+\operatorname{im} Q_{\alpha,w,y}\\ \left\|\kappa_{\alpha,w,y}\right\|_{k,2,\delta,\delta}&\leq c'\\ \mathcal F_{\alpha,w,y}\kappa_{\alpha,w,y}&=0

nodes.name: Proof
nodes.statement: The proof is essentially identical to the proof of Proposition \ref{newtoniteration}; we write it out anyway. In fact, we will show that $\kappa_{\alpha,w,y}$ is given explicitly as the limit of the Newton iteration: \begin{align} \xi_0&:=\kappa_\alpha\\ \xi_n&:=\xi_{n-1}-Q_{\alpha,w,y}\mathcal F_{\alpha,w,y}\xi_{n-1} \end{align} By Lemma \ref{contractionpropHF}, the map $\xi\mapsto\xi-Q_{\alpha,w,y}\mathcal F_{\alpha,w,y}\xi$ is a $\frac 12$-contraction mapping when restricted to: \begin{equation} \{\xi\in\kappa_\alpha+\operatorname{im} Q_{\alpha,w,y}:\left\|\xi\right\|_{k,2,\delta,\delta}\leq c'\} \end{equation} To finish the proof, it suffices to show that (for sufficiently small $(\alpha,w,y,\kappa)$) \eqref{domainofcontractionHF} is nonempty and is mapped to itself by $\xi\mapsto\xi-Q_{\alpha,w,y}\mathcal F_{\alpha,w,y}\xi$. We know that $\left\|\kappa_\alpha\right\|_{k,2,\delta,\delta}\to 0$ as $\kappa\to 0$ (uniformly in $(\alpha,w,y)$), so \eqref{domainofcontractionHF} is nonempty. By using Proposition \ref{quadestimateHF} with $(\xi_1,\xi_2)=(0,\kappa_\alpha)$ and Lemmas \ref{mappregluingissmallHF} and \ref{pregluingKestimateHF}, we conclude that: \begin{equation} \left\|\mathcal F_{\alpha,w,y}\kappa_\alpha\right\|_{k-1,2,\delta,\delta}\to 0 \end{equation} as $(\alpha,w,y,\kappa)\to 0$. Since the operator norm of $Q_{\alpha,w,y}$ is bounded uniformly as $(\alpha,w,y)\to 0$, we see that $\kappa_\alpha$ is almost fixed by $\xi\mapsto\xi-Q_{\alpha,w,y}\mathcal F_{\alpha,w,y}\xi$ as $(\alpha,w,y,\kappa)\to 0$. It then follows from the contraction property that $\xi\mapsto\xi-Q_{\alpha,w,y}\mathcal F_{\alpha,w,y}\xi$ maps \eqref{domainofcontractionHF} to itself.
nodes.statement_short: Newton iteration as a contraction mapping: the contraction lemma plus smallness of $\mathcal F(\kappa_\alpha)$ show the ball is nonempty and mapped into itself.

nodes.name: Newton iteration
nodes.statement: \xi_0&:=\kappa_\alpha\\ \xi_n&:=\xi_{n-1}-Q_{\alpha,w,y}\mathcal F_{\alpha,w,y}\xi_{n-1}

nodes.name: Domain of the contraction
nodes.statement: \{\xi\in\kappa_\alpha+\operatorname{im} Q_{\alpha,w,y}:\left\|\xi\right\|_{k,2,\delta,\delta}\leq c'\}
nodes.label: domainofcontractionHF

nodes.name: Preglued kernel elements are almost holomorphic
nodes.statement: \left\|\mathcal F_{\alpha,w,y}\kappa_\alpha\right\|_{k-1,2,\delta,\delta}\to 0
nodes.label: kernelclosetoholomorphicHF

nodes.name: Gluing map (Hamiltonian Floer)
nodes.statement: We define: \begin{align} u_{\alpha,w,y,\kappa}&:=\exp_{u_\alpha}\kappa_{\alpha,w,y}\\ e_{\alpha,w,y,\kappa}&:=e_0+\operatorname{proj}_E\kappa_{\alpha,w,y} \end{align} where $\kappa_{\alpha,w,y}$ is as in Proposition \ref{newtoniterationHF}, and we consider the following \emph{gluing map}: \begin{align} \mathbb C^d\times(\mathbb R_{\geq 0}^{k-1})^{\leq\mathfrak s}\times\mathbb R^\ast\times\prod_{i=1}^{k\prime}(H^i)^{\leq\mathfrak s}\times K&\to\overline{\mathcal M}(M)\\ (\alpha,w,y,\kappa)&\mapsto(\alpha,w,y,u_{\alpha,w,y,\kappa},e_{\alpha,w,y,\kappa}) \end{align} ($\{x^i\}_{1\leq i\leq r}$ are determined uniquely by $\alpha,w,y,u_{\alpha,w,y,\kappa}$, so we omit them from the notation). It follows from the definition that the gluing map commutes with the projection from both sides to $\mathbb C^d\times(\mathbb R_{\geq 0}^{k-1})^{\leq\mathfrak s}\times\mathbb R^\ast\times\prod_{i=1}^{k\prime}(H^i)^{\leq\mathfrak s}\times E/E'$.
nodes.statement_short: Defines the gluing map $(\alpha,w,y,\kappa)\mapsto(\alpha,w,y,\exp_{u_\alpha}\kappa_{\alpha,w,y},e_0+\operatorname{proj}_E\kappa_{\alpha,w,y})$.

nodes.name: Glued map and obstruction element
nodes.statement: u_{\alpha,w,y,\kappa}&:=\exp_{u_\alpha}\kappa_{\alpha,w,y}\\ e_{\alpha,w,y,\kappa}&:=e_0+\operatorname{proj}_E\kappa_{\alpha,w,y}

nodes.name: Gluing map

nodes.name: Gluing map lands in the regular locus
nodes.statement: The gluing map \eqref{gluingmapHF} maps sufficiently small $(\alpha,w,y,\kappa)$ to $\overline{\mathcal M}(M)^\mathrm{reg}$.

nodes.statement: This is true since $Q_{\alpha,w,y}$ gives an approximate right inverse at $(u_{\alpha,w,y,\kappa},e_{\alpha,w,y,\kappa})$ (use \eqref{derivislipHF} with $\zeta=\kappa_{\alpha,w,y}$).

nodes.statement: Let $K_\alpha\subseteq C^\infty(C_\alpha,u_\alpha^\ast TM)_{D,H}\oplus E$ denote the image of $\kappa\mapsto\kappa_\alpha$.
nodes.name: Preglued kernel K_alpha

nodes.statement: It is clear by definition that $K\to K_\alpha$ is an isomorphism and that the respective $W^{k,2,\delta,\delta}$ norms are uniformly commensurable.
nodes.name: K to K_alpha is a uniformly bounded isomorphism
conclusions: $K\to K_\alpha$ is an isomorphism
the respective $W^{k,2,\delta,\delta}$ norms are uniformly commensurable

nodes.statement: It is also clear that the following commutes: \begin{equation} \begin{tikzcd}[column sep = tiny] K\ar{dr}[swap]{L_0}\ar{rr}{\kappa\mapsto\kappa_\alpha}&&K_\alpha\ar{dl}{L_\alpha}\\ &W \end{tikzcd} \end{equation} (all maps being isomorphisms).

nodes.statement: Since $\operatorname{im} Q_{\alpha,w,y}\subseteq\ker L_\alpha$, it follows in particular that $\operatorname{im} Q_{\alpha,w,y}\cap K_\alpha=0$. On the other hand, an index calculation shows that $\operatorname{ind} D_{\alpha,w,y}=\operatorname{ind} D_{0,0,0}$ (note that by the argument for Lemma \ref{fredholmandsamekernelcokernel}, it suffices to calculate their indices as operators $W^{k,2,\delta}\to W^{k-1,2,\delta}$, i.e.\ with no weights at the bubble nodes, on $\tilde C_\alpha$ and $\tilde C_0$ respectively; the calculation of such indices is originally due to Floer \cite{floersfhs,floerindex} and is by now standard). Both are surjective, and hence we have $\dim\operatorname{coker} Q_{\alpha,w,y}=\dim\ker D_{\alpha,w,y}=\dim\ker D_{0,0,0}=\dim K=\dim K_\alpha$.
nodes.name: Proof that im Q_{alpha,w,y} = ker L_alpha
nodes.statement_short: Dimension count: $\operatorname{im}Q\cap K_\alpha=0$ and equal Fredholm indices (Floer's index computation) give complementary dimensions.

nodes.statement: It follows that $\operatorname{im} Q_{\alpha,w,y}=\ker L_\alpha$ and that: \begin{equation} \operatorname{im} Q_{\alpha,w,y}\oplus K_\alpha\xrightarrow\sim W^{k,2,\delta,\delta}(C_\alpha,u_\alpha^\ast TX)_D\oplus E \end{equation} is an isomorphism of Banach spaces (an alternative justification for this is to use an argument similar to the proof of Propositions \ref{gluingsurjective}/\ref{gluingsurjectiveHF} to show that the natural projection $K_\alpha\xrightarrow{\kappa_\alpha\mapsto\kappa_\alpha-Q_{\alpha,w,y}D_{\alpha,w,y}\kappa_\alpha}\ker D_{\alpha,w,y}$ is surjective, and thus bijective).

conclusions: $\operatorname{im} Q_{\alpha,w,y}=\ker L_\alpha$
nodes.statement_short: $\operatorname{im}Q_{\alpha,w,y}=\ker L_\alpha$ and $\operatorname{im}Q_{\alpha,w,y}\oplus K_\alpha$ is the whole domain.

We claim that in fact the two norms are uniformly commensurable as $(\alpha,w,y)\to 0$.
nodes.name: Uniform commensurability of the splitting

nodes.statement: The map written is clearly uniformly bounded, so we just need to show the same for its inverse. It suffices to show that the projection from the right hand side to $K_\alpha$ is uniformly bounded, but this is nothing other than $L_\alpha$ (clearly uniformly bounded) composed with the inverse of the isomorphism in \eqref{LonkernelisgoodHF} (also uniformly bounded).
nodes.name: Proof of uniform commensurability
nodes.statement_short: The inverse is controlled by the projection to $K_\alpha$, which is $L_\alpha$ followed by the inverse of the commuting isomorphism.

nodes.name: Proof
nodes.statement:
The proof follows the same basic outline as the proof of Proposition ef{continuityofgluing}; some parts of the proof are identical, and we will omit these. The key ingredient is our precise control of the image of the right inverse $Q_{\alpha,w,y}$ (specifically, that $\operatorname{im} Q_{\alpha,w,y}=\ker L_\alpha$). Suppose $(\alpha_i,w_i,y_i,\kappa_i)	o(\alpha,w,y,\kappa)$ is a convergent net. ootnote{We could restrict to sequences rather than nets since $\mathbb C^d	imes(\mathbb R_{\geq 0}^{k-1})^{\leq\mathfrak s}	imes\mathbb R^\ast	imes\prod_{i=1}^{k\prime}(H^i)^{\leq\mathfrak s}	imes K$ is first countable. However, this would not make the argument any simpler.} We will show that:  egin{equation} (u_{\alpha_i,w_i,y_i,\kappa_i},e_{\alpha_i,w_i,y_i,\kappa_i})	o(u_{\alpha,w,y,\kappa},e_{\alpha,w,y,\kappa}) \end{equation} First, observe that the argument from the proof of Proposition ef{continuityofgluing} applies verbatim to give that in fact it suffices to show that:  egin{equation} (u_{\alpha_i,w_i,y_i,\kappa},e_{\alpha_i,w_i,y_i,\kappa})	o(u_{\alpha,w,y,\kappa},e_{\alpha,w,y,\kappa}) \end{equation} Now recall that by definition:  egin{align} u_{\alpha,w,y,\kappa}&=\exp_{u_\alpha}\kappa_{\alpha,w,y}&\kappa_{\alpha,w,y}&=\kappa_\alpha+\xi&	ext{for some }\xi&\in\operatorname{im} Q_{\alpha,w,y} \end{align} Now we define $\xi_{\alpha_i}\in W^{k,2,\delta,\delta}(C_{\alpha_i},u_{\alpha_i}^\ast TX)_D\oplus E$ by ``pregluing'' $\xi$ from $C_\alpha$ to $C_{\alpha_i}$ as follows. Note that we may assume without loss of generality that at the nodes where $\alpha
e 0$, we also have $\alpha_i
e 0$. Away from the ends/necks of $C_{\alpha_i}$, we set $\xi_{\alpha_i}=\xi$. Note that for every end of $C_{\alpha_i}$, there is a corresponding end of $C_\alpha$, so we may also simply set $\xi_{\alpha_i}=\xi$ over the ends of $C_{\alpha_i}$. Over the necks of $C_{\alpha_i}$ for which $\alpha=0$, we define $\xi_{\alpha_i}$ via \eqref{kernelpregluingformulaHFbubble}--\eqref{kernelpregluingformulaHFmain} (note that this is reasonable since $\xi$ satisfies the estimates \eqref{kappabubble}, \eqref{kappamain} as a consequence of Proposition ef{neckestimateHF}). Over the necks of $C_{\alpha_i}$ for which $\alpha
e 0$, we define $\xi_{\alpha_i}$ as:  egin{equation} \xi_{\alpha_i}(s,t):=\mathsf{PT}_{u_{\alpha}(t,f_i(s))	o u_{\alpha_i}(t,s)}[\xi(t,f_i(s)))] \end{equation} where $f_i:[0,6S_i]	o[0,6S]$ is smooth and satisfies:  egin{align} f_i(s):=& egin{cases} s&s\leq S-2\cr s-3S_i+3S&3S_i-2S+2\leq s\leq 3S_i+2S-2\cr s-6S_i+6S&6S_i-S+2\leq s\cr \end{cases}\ f_i([S-2,3S_i-2S+2])&\subseteq[S-2,S+2]\ f_i([3S_i+2S-2,6S_i-S+2])&\subseteq[5S-2,5S+2] \end{align} so that $f_i	o\operatorname{id}$ uniformly in all derivatives as $S_i	o S$. More informally, $f_i$ is smooth and matches up $[0,S-2],[S+2,5S-2],[5S+2,6S]\subseteq[0,6S]$ with corresponding intervals of the same length inside $[0,6S_i]$, symmetrically. Now at this point we appeal to the corresponding arguments from the proof of Proposition ef{continuityofgluing}, which apply as written (using the fact that $\operatorname{im} Q_{\alpha,w,y}=\ker L_\alpha$) and imply that it suffices to show that:  egin{equation} \left\|\mathcal F_{\alpha_i,w_i,y_i}(\kappa_{\alpha_i}+\xi_{\alpha_i})ight\|_{k-1,2,\delta,\delta}	o 0 \end{equation} Recall that $\mathcal F_{\alpha,w,y}(\kappa_\alpha+\xi)=0$; we will use this to estimate $\mathcal F_{\alpha_i,w_i,y_i}(\kappa_{\alpha_i}+\xi_{\alpha_i})$. Away from the ends/necks of $C_{\alpha_i}$, it is clear by definition that $\mathcal F_{\alpha_i,w_i,y_i}(\kappa_{\alpha_i}+\xi_{\alpha_i})	o\mathcal F_{\alpha,w,y}(\kappa_\alpha+\xi)$ uniformly in all derivatives. Thus the contribution to the norm of $\mathcal F_{\alpha_i,w_i,y_i}(\kappa_{\alpha_i}+\xi_{\alpha_i})$ over this region approaches zero. Over the necks of $C_{\alpha_i}$ which correspond to necks of $C_\alpha$, we again have uniform convergence in all derivatives, so the contribution of these regions approaches zero as well. We estimate the contribution over the ends of $C_{\alpha_i}$ (recall that these necessarily correspond to ends of $C_\alpha$). Over main ends, we have $\mathcal F_{\alpha_i,w_i,y_i}(\kappa_{\alpha_i}+\xi_{\alpha_i})=\mathcal F_{\alpha,w,y}(\kappa_\alpha+\xi)$. Now the convergence $\mathcal F_{\alpha_i,w_i,y_i}(\kappa_{\alpha_i}+\xi_{\alpha_i})	o\mathcal F_{\alpha,w,y}(\kappa_\alpha+\xi)$ uniformly in all derivatives is valid near the bubble nodes in the usual metric on $C_{\alpha_i}=C_\alpha$. It follows that we also have convergence in the relevant $\delta$-weighted Sobolev norm since $\delta<1$. Thus the contribution of this region to the norm approaches zero. Finally, let us estimate the contribution to the norm over the necks of $C_{\alpha_i}$ which correspond to ends of $C_\alpha$. We treat main necks and bubble necks separately. Over main necks, $\mathcal F_{\alpha_i,w_i,y_i}(\kappa_{\alpha_i}+\xi_{\alpha_i})$ is supported inside $S^1	imes([S-1,S+1],[5S-1,5S+1])$. The contribution of this region to its norm goes to zero, as follows using the exponential decrease on $\kappa$ and $\xi$ from Proposition ef{neckestimateHF} and the fact that $\delta<\delta_i$. Over bubble ends, $\mathcal F_{\alpha_i,w_i,y_i}(\kappa_{\alpha_i}+\xi_{\alpha_i})$ converges to $\mathcal F_{\alpha,w,y}(\kappa_\alpha+\xi)$ uniformly in all derivatives over the complement of $S^1	imes[S-1,5S+1]$ (measured with respect to the usual metric on $C_0$), and hence the contribution of this region to the weighted norm goes to zero since $\delta<1$. Over $S^1	imes([S-1,S+1]\cup[5S-1,5S+1])$, the smoothness of $\kappa$ and $\xi$ over $C_\alpha$ and the fact that $\delta<1$ shows that the contribution of this region to the norm goes to zero (since $S	o\infty$). Finally, over $S^1	imes[S+1,5S-1]$, both $u_{\alpha_i}$ and $\kappa_{\alpha_i}+\xi_{\alpha_i}$ are constant, so $\mathcal F_{\alpha_i,w_i,y_i}(\kappa_{\alpha_i}+\xi_{\alpha_i})$ is simply:  egin{equation*} \mathsf{PT}_{\exp_{u_0(n)}(\kappa(n)+\xi(n))	o u_0(n)}^{\ell_{\alpha_i,w_i}(A_{y_i}(\cdot))}\Bigl(2d(\operatorname{proj}_{S^1}A_{y_i})\otimes X_{H((\ell_{\alpha_i,w_i}	imes\operatorname{id}_{S^1})(A_{y_i}(\cdot)))}\Bigr)^{0,1}_{j,J(\ell_{\alpha_i,w_i}(A_{y_i}(\cdot)))} \end{equation*} The norm of this expression over $S^1	imes[S+1,5S-1]$ approaches zero since $A_{y_i}=O(e^{-s})$ in all derivatives and $\delta<1$.
nodes.statement_short: Follow the Gromov--Witten continuity proof: transport the correction $\xi$ to nearby parameters by a reparametrized pregluing and show $\mathcal F(\kappa_{\alpha_i}+\xi_{\alpha_i})\to 0$ region by region. The key input is $\operatorname{im}Q_{\alpha,w,y}=\ker L_\alpha$.

nodes.name: A priori estimate on decay of connecting cylinders
nodes.statement: Let $(M,\omega)$ be a symplectic manifold, $J$ an $\omega$-compatible almost complex structure on $M$, $H:M\times S^1\to\mathbb R$ a Hamiltonian, and $\gamma:S^1\to M$ a non-degenerate periodic orbit of $H$. We consider the (unbounded) asymptotic linearized operator: \begin{align} L^2(S^1,\gamma^\ast TM)&\to L^2(S^1,\gamma^\ast TM)\\ \xi&\mapsto J\mathcal L_{X_H}\xi \end{align} where $\mathcal L_{X_H}$ denotes the symplectic connection on $\gamma^\ast TM$ induced by $X_H$, and we use the standard inner product $g(\cdot,\cdot):=\omega(\cdot,J\cdot)$ on $\gamma^\ast TM$ for the inner product on $L^2(S^1,\gamma^\ast TM)$. This operator is self-adjoint; we denote by $\delta>0$ the smallest magnitude of any of its eigenvalues ($\delta$ is positive since the orbit is non-degenerate). We consider (partially defined) sections $\xi:S^1\times\mathbb R\to\gamma^\ast TM$ with $\left|\xi(t,s)\right|<\epsilon$ such that $u:=\exp_\gamma\xi:S^1\times\mathbb R\to M$ satisfies $(du+2dt\otimes X_H(u))^{0,1}_J=0$. Now for all $\mu<1$, there exists $\epsilon>0$ such that we have the following estimates. Suppose that $\xi$ as above is defined on $S^1\times[0,\infty)$. Then: \begin{equation} \left|D^k\xi\right|\leq c_k\cdot e^{-\mu\delta s}\left(\int_{S^1}\bigl|\xi(t,0)\bigr|^2\,dt\right)^{1/2}\qquad s\geq 1 \end{equation} for all $k\geq 0$. A symmetric statement holds for $u$ and $\xi$ defined over $S^1\times(-\infty,0]$. Suppose that $\xi$ as above is defined on $S^1\times[0,N]$. Then: \begin{equation*} \left|D^k\xi\right|\leq c_k\cdot\left[e^{-\mu\delta s}\left(\int_{S^1}\bigl|\xi(t,0)\bigr|^2\,dt\right)^{1/2}+e^{-\mu\delta(N-s)}\left(\int_{S^1}\bigl|\xi(t,N)\bigr|^2\,dt\right)^{1/2}\right]\qquad 1\leq s\leq N-1 \end{equation*} for all $k\geq 0$.
nodes.statement_short: Floer cylinders near a non-degenerate orbit decay exponentially at rate $\mu\delta$, $\delta$ the spectral gap of the asymptotic operator, with all derivatives controlled by $L^2$ boundary data.
nodes.origin_citation: Floer 1988 (pp801--802); Salamon, Lectures on Floer homology, Lemma 2.11
assumptions: Let $(M,\omega)$ be a symplectic manifold, $J$ an $\omega$-compatible almost complex structure on $M$, $H:M\times S^1\to\mathbb R$ a Hamiltonian, and $\gamma:S^1\to M$ a non-degenerate periodic orbit of $H$.

conclusions: \left|D^k\xi\right|\leq c_k\cdot e^{-\mu\delta s}\left(\int_{S^1}\bigl|\xi(t,0)\bigr|^2\,dt\right)^{1/2}\qquad s\geq 1
