nodes.name: Proof
nodes.statement: This proof is adapted from Salamon \cite[p170, Lemma 2.11]{salamonnotes}. We have by assumption that $\partial_su+J(u)(\partial_tu-X_H(u))=0$, where $u(t,s)=\exp_{\gamma(t)}\xi(t,s)$. Now we may rewrite this equation in exponential coordinates in terms of $\xi$ as follows. Denote by $\partial_t$ the connection $\mathcal L_{X_H}$ on $\gamma^\ast TM$, which is given by the Lie derivative with respect to $X_H$. Now the equation for $u$ is equivalent to: \begin{equation} \partial_s\xi+J\partial_t\xi+A(\xi)\partial_t\xi+Q(\xi)=0 \end{equation} for certain smooth (non-linear) bundle maps $A:\gamma^\ast TM\to\operatorname{End}(\gamma^\ast TM)$ and $Q:\gamma^\ast TM\to\gamma^\ast TM$. We have $A(0)=0$, $Q(0)=0$, and $Q'(0,\cdot)=0$ (we denote by $A'$ and $Q'$ their ``vertical'' derivatives). Now we let: \begin{equation} f(s):=\int_{S^1}\left|\xi(t,s)\right|^2dt=\left\|\xi\right\|_2^2 \end{equation} and we will show that $f''(s)\geq(1-o(1))4\delta^2f(s)$, where $o(1)$ denotes a quantity which can be made arbitrarily small by choosing $\epsilon>0$ sufficiently small. We have: \begin{equation} f''(s)=2\int_{S^1}\left|\partial_s\xi\right|^2dt+2\int_{S^1}\langle\xi,\partial_s\partial_s\xi\rangle\,dt=2\left\|\partial_s\xi\right\|_2^2+2\langle\xi,\partial_s\partial_s\xi\rangle \end{equation} and we will now prove estimates $\left\|\partial_s\xi\right\|_2^2\geq(1-o(1))\delta^2f(s)$ and $\langle\xi,\partial_s\partial_s\xi\rangle\geq(1-o(1))\delta^2f(s)$. Recall that $J\partial_t$ is self-adjoint and that $\left\|J\partial_t\xi\right\|_2\geq\delta\left\|\xi\right\|_2$. To bound $\left\|\partial_s\xi\right\|_2^2$, we write: \begin{align} \left\|\partial_s\xi\right\|_2&=\left\|J\partial_t\xi+A(\xi)\partial_t\xi+Q(\xi)\right\|_2\cr &\geq\left\|J\partial_t\xi\right\|_2-\left\|A(\xi)\partial_t\xi\right\|_2-\left\|Q(\xi)\right\|_2\cr &\geq\left\|J\partial_t\xi\right\|_2-\left\|A(\xi)\right\|_\infty\left\|\partial_t\xi\right\|_2-c\left\|\xi\right\|_\infty\left\|\xi\right\|_2\cr &=\left\|J\partial_t\xi\right\|_2-o(1)\left\|J\partial_t\xi\right\|_2-o(1)\left\|\xi\right\|_2\geq(1-o(1))\delta\left\|\xi\right\|_2 \end{align} and thus $\left\|\partial_s\xi\right\|_2^2\geq(1-o(1))\delta^2f(s)$. To bound $\langle\xi,\partial_s\partial_s\xi\rangle$, we write: \begin{align} \langle\xi,\partial_s\partial_s\xi\rangle&=-\langle\xi,\partial_s[J\partial_t\xi+A(\xi)\partial_t\xi+Q(\xi)]\rangle\cr &=-\langle J\partial_t\xi,\partial_s\xi\rangle-\langle\xi,A'(\xi,\partial_s\xi)\partial_t\xi\rangle-\langle\xi,A(\xi)\partial_t\partial_s\xi\rangle-\langle\xi,Q'(\xi,\partial_s\xi)\rangle \end{align} Now substituting in $\partial_s\xi=-J\partial_t\xi-A(\xi)\partial_t\xi-Q(\xi)$, we obtain the following: \begin{align} \langle\xi,\partial_s\partial_s\xi\rangle=\left\|J\partial_t\xi\right\|_2^2 &+\langle J\partial_t\xi,A(\xi)\partial_t\xi\rangle\cr &+\langle J\partial_t\xi,Q(\xi)\rangle\cr &+\langle\xi,A'(\xi,[J+A(\xi)]\partial_t\xi)\partial_t\xi\rangle\cr &+\langle\xi,A'(\xi,Q(\xi))\partial_t\xi\rangle\cr &+\langle\xi,A(\xi)\partial_t([J+A(\xi)]\partial_t\xi)\rangle\cr &+\langle\xi,A(\xi)\partial_t(Q(\xi))\rangle\cr &+\langle\xi,Q'(\xi,[J+A(\xi)]\partial_t\xi)\rangle\cr &+\langle\xi,Q'(\xi,Q(\xi))\rangle \end{align} The first term $\left\|J\partial_t\xi\right\|_2^2$ is the main term; let us estimate the remaining error terms. The first error term is bounded by $\left\|\xi\right\|_\infty\left\|J\partial_t\xi\right\|_2^2$, the second by $\left\|\xi\right\|_\infty\left\|\xi\right\|_2\left\|J\partial_t\xi\right\|_2$, the third by $\left\|\xi\right\|_\infty\left\|J\partial_t\xi\right\|_2^2$, the fourth by $\left\|\xi\right\|_\infty^2\left\|\xi\right\|_2\left\|J\partial_t\xi\right\|_2$, the fifth by $\left\|\xi\right\|_\infty\left\|J\partial_t\xi\right\|^2+\left\|\xi\right\|_\infty\left\|\xi\right\|_2\left\|J\partial_t\xi\right\|_2$ (integrate by parts to move the outermost $\partial_t$ onto $\xi$, $A(\xi)$, and $\langle\cdot,\cdot\rangle$), the sixth by $\left\|\xi\right\|_\infty^2\left\|\xi\right\|_2\left\|J\partial_t\xi\right\|_2$, the seventh by $\left\|\xi\right\|_\infty\left\|\xi\right\|_2\left\|J\partial_t\xi\right\|_2$, and the eighth by $\left\|\xi\right\|_\infty^2\left\|\xi\right\|_2^2$. All of these are $o(1)\left\|J\partial_t\xi\right\|_2^2$, so we conclude that $\langle\xi,\partial_s\partial_s\xi\rangle\geq(1-o(1))\delta^2f(s)$. Combining the above estimates, we obtain the desired inequality $f''(s)\geq(1-o(1))4\delta^2f(s)$. Now we have the following maximum principle for the differential inequality $g''(s)\geq r^2g(s)$. Namely, suppose that $g:[a,b]\to\mathbb R_{\geq 0}$ satisfies $g''(s)\geq r^2g(s)$ and that $G:[a,b]\to\mathbb R_{\geq 0}$ satisfies $G''(s)=r^2G(s)$; if $g\leq G$ at the endpoints $a,b$, then it follows that $g\leq G$ over the whole interval $[a,b]$ (one may easily derive a contradiction by assuming that, on the contrary, $g=G$ at $a_1,b_1$ and $g>G$ on $(a_1,b_1)$ for $a\leq a_1<b_1\leq b$). Specializing to the case at hand, we have: \begin{align*} f(s)&\leq e^{-(1-o(1))2\delta s}f(0)&&\text{in the case of }S^1\times[0,\infty)\\ f(s)&\leq e^{-(1-o(1))2\delta s}f(0)+e^{-(1-o(1))2\delta(N-s)}f(N)&&\text{in the case of }S^1\times[0,N] \end{align*} Now Lemma \ref{Ltwocontrolsinnbhd} below asserts that for a $J$-holomorphic curve $u_0$ and a sufficiently small perturbation thereof $u=\exp_{u_0}\xi$ which is also $J$-holomorphic, we have uniform bounds on all derivatives of $\xi$ (away from the boundary) in terms of the $L^2$-norm of $\xi$. Applying this where $u_0$ is the trivial cylinder over $\gamma(t)$, we conclude that our bounds on $f(s)$ imply the desired result.
nodes.statement_short: Following Salamon: write the Floer equation in exponential coordinates, prove the convexity inequality $f''\geq(1-o(1))4\delta^2 f$ for $f=\|\xi\|_2^2$, apply a maximum principle, and upgrade $L^2$ to $C^k$ bounds via the local elliptic lemma.

nodes.name: Floer equation in exponential coordinates
nodes.statement: \partial_s\xi+J\partial_t\xi+A(\xi)\partial_t\xi+Q(\xi)=0

nodes.name: L^2 energy function f(s)
nodes.statement: f(s):=\int_{S^1}\left|\xi(t,s)\right|^2dt=\left\|\xi\right\|_2^2

nodes.name: Second derivative of f
nodes.statement: f''(s)=2\int_{S^1}\left|\partial_s\xi\right|^2dt+2\int_{S^1}\langle\xi,\partial_s\partial_s\xi\rangle\,dt=2\left\|\partial_s\xi\right\|_2^2+2\langle\xi,\partial_s\partial_s\xi\rangle
nodes.label: fppexpr

nodes.name: Lower bound on the s-derivative
nodes.statement: \left\|\partial_s\xi\right\|_2&=\left\|J\partial_t\xi+A(\xi)\partial_t\xi+Q(\xi)\right\|_2\cr &\geq\left\|J\partial_t\xi\right\|_2-\left\|A(\xi)\partial_t\xi\right\|_2-\left\|Q(\xi)\right\|_2\cr &\geq\left\|J\partial_t\xi\right\|_2-\left\|A(\xi)\right\|_\infty\left\|\partial_t\xi\right\|_2-c\left\|\xi\right\|_\infty\left\|\xi\right\|_2\cr &=\left\|J\partial_t\xi\right\|_2-o(1)\left\|J\partial_t\xi\right\|_2-o(1)\left\|\xi\right\|_2\geq(1-o(1))\delta\left\|\xi\right\|_2

nodes.name: Expansion of the second s-derivative pairing
nodes.statement: \langle\xi,\partial_s\partial_s\xi\rangle&=-\langle\xi,\partial_s[J\partial_t\xi+A(\xi)\partial_t\xi+Q(\xi)]\rangle\cr &=-\langle J\partial_t\xi,\partial_s\xi\rangle-\langle\xi,A'(\xi,\partial_s\xi)\partial_t\xi\rangle-\langle\xi,A(\xi)\partial_t\partial_s\xi\rangle-\langle\xi,Q'(\xi,\partial_s\xi)\rangle

nodes.name: Substituted expansion of the pairing
nodes.statement: \langle\xi,\partial_s\partial_s\xi\rangle=\left\|J\partial_t\xi\right\|_2^2 &+\langle J\partial_t\xi,A(\xi)\partial_t\xi\rangle\cr &+\langle J\partial_t\xi,Q(\xi)\rangle\cr &+\langle\xi,A'(\xi,[J+A(\xi)]\partial_t\xi)\partial_t\xi\rangle\cr &+\langle\xi,A'(\xi,Q(\xi))\partial_t\xi\rangle\cr &+\langle\xi,A(\xi)\partial_t([J+A(\xi)]\partial_t\xi)\rangle\cr &+\langle\xi,A(\xi)\partial_t(Q(\xi))\rangle\cr &+\langle\xi,Q'(\xi,[J+A(\xi)]\partial_t\xi)\rangle\cr &+\langle\xi,Q'(\xi,Q(\xi))\rangle

nodes.name: L^2 norm controls derivatives of nearby holomorphic maps
nodes.statement: Let $u:[0,1]\times[0,1]\to B^{2n}(1)$ be $J$-holomorphic with respect to some smooth almost complex structure $J$ on the unit ball $B^{2n}(1)\subseteq\mathbb R^{2n}$. There exists $\epsilon>0$ (depending only on upper bounds on $\left\|J\right\|_{C^\ell}$ and $\left\|u\right\|_{C^\ell}$ for some absolute $\ell<\infty$) with the following property. Suppose that $\xi:[0,1]\times[0,1]\to\mathbb R^{2n}$ with $|\xi|<\epsilon$ pointwise is such that $u+\xi$ has image contained in $B^{2n}(1)$ and is $J$-holomorphic. Then: \begin{equation} \left|D^k\xi(0,0)\right|\leq c_k\biggl(\int_{[0,1]\times[0,1]}\left|\xi(x,y)\right|^2\,dx\,dy\biggr)^{1/2} \end{equation} for all $k<\infty$ for constants $c_k<\infty$ depending only on upper bounds on $\left\|J\right\|_{C^\ell}$ and $\left\|u\right\|_{C^\ell}$ for some $\ell=\ell(k)<\infty$.
nodes.statement_short: For a small $J$-holomorphic perturbation $u+\xi$ of a $J$-holomorphic disc, all derivatives of $\xi$ at an interior point are bounded by its $L^2$ norm.
assumptions: Let $u:[0,1]\times[0,1]\to B^{2n}(1)$ be $J$-holomorphic with respect to some smooth almost complex structure $J$ on the unit ball $B^{2n}(1)\subseteq\mathbb R^{2n}$.
Suppose that $\xi:[0,1]\times[0,1]\to\mathbb R^{2n}$ with $|\xi|<\epsilon$ pointwise is such that $u+\xi$ has image contained in $B^{2n}(1)$ and is $J$-holomorphic.
conclusions: \left|D^k\xi(0,0)\right|\leq c_k\biggl(\int_{[0,1]\times[0,1]}\left|\xi(x,y)\right|^2\,dx\,dy\biggr)^{1/2}
nodes.label: Ltwocontrolsinnbhd

nodes.name: Interior derivative bound by L^2 norm
nodes.statement: \left|D^k\xi(0,0)\right|\leq c_k\biggl(\int_{[0,1]\times[0,1]}\left|\xi(x,y)\right|^2\,dx\,dy\biggr)^{1/2}

nodes.name: Proof
nodes.statement: By assumption, we have: \begin{align} u_x+J(u)u_y&=0\\ (u+\xi)_x+J(u+\xi)(u+\xi)_y&=0 \end{align} which together imply that: \begin{equation} \xi_x+J(u+\xi)\xi_y=[J(u)-J(u+\xi)]u_y \end{equation} which we prefer to write as: \begin{equation} (\partial_x+B\partial_y)\xi=A(\xi) \end{equation} where $B:[0,1]^2\to\operatorname{End}(\mathbb R^{2n})$ denotes $J(u+\xi)$ and $A:[0,1]^2\times\mathbb R^{2n}\to\mathbb R^{2n}$ denotes $A(\xi)=[J(u)-J(u+\xi)]u_y$. By definition, we have $A(0)=0$ and: \begin{equation} \left|D^kA\right|\leq c_k \end{equation} for some $c_k<\infty$ depending only on upper bounds on $\left\|J\right\|_{C^\ell}$ and $\left\|u\right\|_{C^\ell}$ for some $\ell=\ell(k)<\infty$. By definition, we have $B^2=-1$; let us now argue that we also have: \begin{equation} \left|D^kB\right|\leq c_k \end{equation} for sufficiently small $\epsilon>0$ and $c_k<\infty$ as before. Indeed, for sufficiently small $\epsilon>0$, we may apply the Gromov--Schwarz lemma to $u+\xi$ and conclude that $|D\xi|\leq c<\infty$ depending only on upper bounds on $\left\|J\right\|_{C^\ell}$ and $\left\|u\right\|_{C^\ell}$ for some $\ell<\infty$. Now Lemma \ref{Woneinftycontrolsall} applied to $u+\xi$ gives $|D^k\xi|\leq c_k<\infty$, which implies the desired bound on the derivatives of $B$. Now we apply $(\partial_x-B\partial_y)$ to both sides of \eqref{ellipticforxi} to obtain: \begin{equation} \Delta\xi=(\partial_x-B\partial_y)A(\xi)-((\partial_x-B\partial_y)B)(\xi_y) \end{equation} For any smooth function $\phi:[0,1]^2\to\mathbb R_{\geq 0}$ supported in the interior of $[0,1]^2$, we thus have: \begin{equation*} \Delta(\phi\xi)=\xi\Delta\phi+2\phi_x\xi_x+2\phi_y\xi_y+\phi\cdot(\partial_x-B\partial_y)A(\xi)-\phi\cdot((\partial_x-B\partial_y)B)(\xi_y) \end{equation*} Now the desired result follows from the usual bootstrapping of the elliptic regularity estimates for the Laplacian on $\mathbb R^2$, namely $\left\|f\right\|_{H^{s+2}}\leq c_s\left\|f+\Delta f\right\|_{H^s}$ (the first step being the case $s=-1$). We may shrink the support of $\phi$ slightly at each step, so there is no need to worry about regularity near the boundary.
nodes.statement_short: Rewrite the difference of the two holomorphic equations as a first-order elliptic equation for $\xi$ with bounded coefficients (Gromov--Schwarz and a $W^{1,\infty}$ lemma), then bootstrap elliptic regularity for the Laplacian with cut-offs.

nodes.name: Holomorphic equations for u and u+xi
Equation for the difference xi
nodes.statement: \xi_x+J(u+\xi)\xi_y=[J(u)-J(u+\xi)]u_y

nodes.name: Elliptic equation for xi
nodes.statement: (\partial_x+B\partial_y)\xi=A(\xi)
nodes.label: ellipticforxi

nodes.name: Bound on A
nodes.statement: \left|D^kA\right|\leq c_k
nodes.label: boundonA

nodes.name: Bound on B
nodes.statement: \left|D^kB\right|\leq c_k
nodes.label: boundonB

nodes.name: Laplacian equation for xi
nodes.statement: \Delta\xi=(\partial_x-B\partial_y)A(\xi)-((\partial_x-B\partial_y)B)(\xi_y)

nodes.name: Surjectivity of gluing (Hamiltonian Floer)
nodes.statement: The restriction of the gluing map \eqref{gluingmapHF} to any neighborhood of zero is surjective onto a neighborhood of $(0,0,0,u_0,e_0,\{x^i_0\}_{1\leq i\leq r})\in\overline{\mathcal M}(M)$.
nodes.statement_short: The gluing map restricted to any neighborhood of zero covers a neighborhood of the base point in $\overline{\mathcal M}(M)$.
conclusions: The restriction of the gluing map \eqref{gluingmapHF} to any neighborhood of zero is surjective onto a neighborhood of $(0,0,0,u_0,e_0,\{x^i_0\}_{1\leq i\leq r})\in\overline{\mathcal M}(M)$.
nodes.label: gluingsurjectiveHF

nodes.name: Proof
nodes.statement: The proof is identical to the proof of Proposition \ref{gluingsurjective}, except for appealing to Proposition \ref{neckestimateHF} in addition to Proposition \ref{neckestimate} in the appropriate places.
nodes.statement_short: Identical to the Gromov--Witten surjectivity proof, using also the Floer cylinder decay estimate.

nodes.statement: We have shown that the map $g:=$\eqref{gluingmapHF} is continuous, injective, and that its restriction to any neighborhood of zero is surjective onto a neighborhood of the image of zero. The target $\overline{\mathcal M}(M)$ is Hausdorff, and thus it follows from Lemma \ref{injectiveHdorffhomeo} that for some open neighborhood of zero $U\subseteq\mathbb C^d\times(\mathbb R_{\geq 0}^{k-1})^{\leq\mathfrak s}\times\mathbb R^\ast\times\prod_{i=1}^{k\prime}(H^i)^{\leq\mathfrak s}\times K$, we have $g(U)$ is open and $g:U\xrightarrow\sim g(U)$ is a homeomorphism. Thus the gluing map \eqref{gluingmapHF} satisfies the properties desired for the map \eqref{HFgluinggoal}.
nodes.name: Conclusion of the proof of the Hamiltonian Floer gluing theorem
nodes.statement_short: Continuous, injective, locally surjective map into a Hausdorff space is a local homeomorphism; hence the gluing map is the desired chart.

nodes.name: Orientation line o_sigma
nodes.statement: \mathfrak o_\sigma:=\begin{cases}\bigotimes_{i=1}^{\dim\sigma-1}\mathfrak o_\mathbb R&\dim\sigma>0\cr\mathfrak o_\mathbb R^\vee&\dim\sigma=0\end{cases}
nodes.section: C.13.1 Orientations on spaces of flow lines on $\Delta^n$
nodes.statement_short: $\mathfrak o_\sigma$ is $\mathfrak o_\mathbb R^{\otimes(\dim\sigma-1)}$ for $\dim\sigma>0$ and $\mathfrak o_\mathbb R^\vee$ for $\dim\sigma=0$.

nodes.statement: Let us construct an identification between $\mathfrak o_\sigma$ and the orientation sheaf of the space of flow lines on $\sigma$ (from Definition \ref{simplexflows}) for $n=\dim\sigma>0$. Let $f:\mathbb R\to[0,1]$ be the unique solution to the initial value problem $f(0)=\frac 12$ and $f'(x)=\pi\sin(\pi f(x))$. Now every flow line $\ell:\mathbb R\to\Delta^n$ is of the form $\ell(t)=(f(t+a_1),\ldots,f(t+a_n))$ for some $a_1\leq\cdots\leq a_n$ which are unique up to the addition of an overall constant. Thus the space of flow lines is parameterized by $(b_1,\ldots,b_{n-1})\in[0,\infty)^{n-1}$, where $b_i=a_{i+1}-a_i$; moreover, this parameterization extends continuously to a homeomorphism between $[0,\infty]^{n-1}$ and the space of broken flow lines on $\Delta^n$. In these coordinates, $b_k=\infty$ iff the flow line is broken at vertex $k$, and $b_k=0$ iff the flow line factors through $\Delta^{[0\ldots\hat k\ldots n]}\subseteq\Delta^n$. Now the coordinates $b_1,\ldots,b_{n-1}$ determine an identification between $\mathfrak o_\sigma=\bigotimes_{i=1}^{n-1}\mathfrak o_\mathbb R$ and the orientation sheaf of the space of flow lines on $\sigma$, when $\dim\sigma>0$.
nodes.name: Identification of o_sigma with orientations of flow lines
nodes.definiendum: identification between $\mathfrak o_\sigma$ and the orientation sheaf of the space of flow lines on $\sigma$
nodes.statement_short: Parametrize flow lines on $\Delta^n$ by gaps $b_i=a_{i+1}-a_i\in[0,\infty]$; these coordinates orient the space of flow lines by $\mathfrak o_\mathbb R^{\otimes(n-1)}$.
nodes.section: C.13.1 Orientations on spaces of flow lines on $\Delta^n$

nodes.statement: For $\dim\sigma=0$, let us simply remark that tensoring with $\mathfrak o_\sigma=\mathfrak o_\mathbb R^\vee$ is the effect on orientation sheaves of quotienting by an $\mathbb R$-action, and it will follow from this fact that this is the correct definition of $\mathfrak o_\sigma$ when $\dim\sigma=0$ (morally speaking, we may think of the space of flow lines on $\sigma$ as the stacky quotient $\mathrm{pt}/\mathbb R$).
nodes.name: o_sigma for dim sigma = 0
nodes.statement_short: For a vertex, $\mathfrak o_\mathbb R^\vee$ accounts for quotienting by the $\mathbb R$-action (flow lines as $\mathrm{pt}/\mathbb R$).
nodes.section: C.13.1 Orientations on spaces of flow lines on $\Delta^n$

nodes.statement: Now let us observe that there are natural (odd) ``boundary'' maps: \begin{align} \mathfrak o_\sigma&\to\mathfrak o_{\sigma|[0\ldots k]}\otimes\mathfrak o_{\sigma|[k\ldots n]}\\ \mathfrak o_\sigma&\to\mathfrak o_{\sigma|[0\ldots\hat k\ldots n]} \end{align} induced by the geometric inclusions of boundary strata \eqref{Fproduct}--\eqref{Fface}. Specifically, the first map is induced by the inclusion of the space of pairs of flow lines on $\sigma|[0\ldots k]$ and $\sigma|[k\ldots n]$ into the space of flow lines on $\sigma$ ($0<k<n$), and the second by the inclusion of flow lines on $\sigma|[0\ldots\hat k\ldots n]$ into flow lines on $\sigma$ ($0<k<n$).
nodes.name: Boundary maps on o_sigma
nodes.statement_short: Odd maps $\mathfrak o_\sigma\to\mathfrak o_{\sigma|[0..k]}\otimes\mathfrak o_{\sigma|[k..n]}$ and $\mathfrak o_\sigma\to\mathfrak o_{\sigma|[0..\hat k..n]}$ induced by boundary strata inclusions.
nodes.section: C.13.1 Orientations on spaces of flow lines on $\Delta^n$

nodes.name: Boundary maps of o_sigma
nodes.statement: \mathfrak o_\sigma&\to\mathfrak o_{\sigma|[0\ldots k]}\otimes\mathfrak o_{\sigma|[k\ldots n]}\\ \mathfrak o_\sigma&\to\mathfrak o_{\sigma|[0\ldots\hat k\ldots n]}
nodes.section: C.13.1 Orientations on spaces of flow lines on $\Delta^n$
nodes.label: simplexflowproductor

nodes.statement: In fact, the first map \eqref{simplexflowproductor} admits the following alternative description, which shows that it is in fact defined for $0\leq k\leq n$. Let $\mathcal F^{(i)}(\sigma)$ denote the moduli space of stable broken Morse flow lines on a simplex $\sigma$ with $i$ ordered marked points appearing in order (this is defined in the expected way, allowing constant flow lines as long as they are stabilized by the presence of at least one marked point). Denote the orientation module of $\mathcal F^{(i)}(\sigma)$ by $\mathfrak o_\sigma^{(i)}$, and note that there is a natural isomorphism $\mathfrak o_\sigma^{(i)}=\mathfrak o_\sigma\otimes\mathfrak o_\mathbb R^{\otimes i}$ (even for $\dim\sigma=0$; this provides another justification of our definition of $\mathfrak o_\sigma$ in this case). Now there is a natural concatenation map $\mathcal F^{(i)}(\sigma|[0\ldots k])\times\mathcal F^{(j)}(\sigma|[k\ldots n])\to\mathcal F^{(i+j)}(\sigma)$ which is the inclusion of a codimension one boundary stratum, thus giving rise to a boundary map $\mathfrak o_\sigma^{(i+j)}\to\mathfrak o_{\sigma|[0\ldots k]}^{(i)}\otimes\mathfrak o_{\sigma|[k\ldots n]}^{(j)}$. After factoring out $\mathfrak o_\mathbb R^{\otimes(i+j)}$, this map coincides with \eqref{simplexflowproductor} for $0<k<n$, and thus may be used to define \eqref{simplexflowproductor} for $0\leq k\leq n$.
nodes.name: Product boundary map for 0 <= k <= n
nodes.statement_short: Using flow lines with marked points $\mathcal F^{(i)}(\sigma)$, the concatenation boundary map extends the product map to $0\leq k\leq n$.
nodes.section: C.13.1 Orientations on spaces of flow lines on $\Delta^n$

nodes.statement: Let $\mathcal F^{(i)}(\sigma)$ denote the moduli space of stable broken Morse flow lines on a simplex $\sigma$ with $i$ ordered marked points appearing in order (this is defined in the expected way, allowing constant flow lines as long as they are stabilized by the presence of at least one marked point).
nodes.name: Moduli space of broken flow lines with marked points

nodes.statement: Denote the orientation module of $\mathcal F^{(i)}(\sigma)$ by $\mathfrak o_\sigma^{(i)}$, and note that there is a natural isomorphism $\mathfrak o_\sigma^{(i)}=\mathfrak o_\sigma\otimes\mathfrak o_\mathbb R^{\otimes i}$ (even for $\dim\sigma=0$; this provides another justification of our definition of $\mathfrak o_\sigma$ in this case).

nodes.name: Sign convention for o_sigma boundary maps
nodes.statement: The standard orientation of $\mathbb R$ gives a standard generator $[\mathbb R]_1\otimes\cdots\otimes[\mathbb R]_{n-1}\in\mathfrak o_\sigma$ for $\dim\sigma>0$, and $[\mathbb R]^\vee\in\mathfrak o_\sigma$ for $\dim\sigma=0$, where $[\mathbb R]\cdot[\mathbb R]^\vee=1$ (i.e.\ $[\mathbb R]^\vee\in\mathfrak o_\mathbb R^\vee$ is the ``right dual'' of $[\mathbb R]\in\mathfrak o_\mathbb R$). Using these generators to trivialize $\mathfrak o_\sigma$ determines a sign convention in which \eqref{simplexflowproductor} is given by $(-1)^{k+1}$ and \eqref{simplexflowfaceor} is given by $(-1)^k$.
nodes.section: C.13.1 Orientations on spaces of flow lines on $\Delta^n$
nodes.statement_short: Trivializing $\mathfrak o_\sigma$ by standard generators, the product and face boundary maps are $(-1)^{k+1}$ and $(-1)^k$.

nodes.statement: Fix two Hamiltonians $H_0,H_1:M\times S^1\to\mathbb R$ and two non-degenerate periodic orbits $p,q:S^1\to M$ of $H_0,H_1$ respectively. Now for any path of $\omega$-compatible almost complex structures $J:\mathbb R\to J(M)$ (constant near $s=\pm\infty$), any path of Hamiltonians $H:M\times S^1\times\mathbb R\to\mathbb R$ (constant near $s=\pm\infty$) with $H(s=-\infty)=H_0$ and $H(s=\infty)=H_1$, and any map $u:S^1\times\mathbb R\to M$ in $W^{k,2,\delta}(S^1\times\mathbb R,M)$ (converging to $q$ at $-\infty$ and to $p$ at $\infty$), there is a natural linearized operator: \begin{equation} D_\text{Floer}:W^{k,2,\delta}(S^1\times\mathbb R,u^\ast TM)\to W^{k-1,2,\delta}(S^1\times\mathbb R,\Omega^{0,1}_{S^1\times\mathbb R}\otimes_\mathbb C u^\ast TM_J) \end{equation} (we assume that $\delta>0$ is less than the smallest positive eigenvalues of the asymptotic linearized operators).
nodes.name: Floer linearized operator D_Floer
nodes.statement_short: For paths $J,H$ and a map $u$ from $q$ to $p$, the linearized Floer operator between weighted Sobolev spaces.
nodes.section: C.13.2 Orientations of linearized operators of Floer equations

nodes.name: Floer linearized operator D_Floer
nodes.statement: D_\text{Floer}:W^{k,2,\delta}(S^1\times\mathbb R,u^\ast TM)\to W^{k-1,2,\delta}(S^1\times\mathbb R,\Omega^{0,1}_{S^1\times\mathbb R}\otimes_\mathbb C u^\ast TM_J)
nodes.section: C.13.2 Orientations of linearized operators of Floer equations
nodes.label: Dfloer

nodes.statement:
Let us agree to define this linearized operator using the $\mathbb R$-family of $J$-linear connections on $TM$ given by $
abla_XY:= rac 12(
abla^0_XY-J(
abla^0_X(JY)))$, where $
abla^0$ denotes the Levi-Civita connection of the metric associated to the compatible pair $(\omega,J)$.
nodes.name: J-linear connection convention for D_Floer
nodes.section: C.13.2 Orientations of linearized operators of Floer equations

nodes.statement: The results of Floer--Hofer \cite{floerhoferorientations} (see the remark after Theorem 2) imply that the Fredholm orientation line of $D_\text{Floer}$ is a trivial bundle over the space of paths $H$, $J$, and maps $u$.
nodes.name: Triviality of the Floer orientation line (Floer--Hofer)
nodes.origin_citation: Floer--Hofer, Coherent orientations for periodic orbit problems
conclusions: the Fredholm orientation line of $D_\text{Floer}$ is a trivial bundle over the space of paths $H$, $J$, and maps $u$
nodes.section: C.13.2 Orientations of linearized operators of Floer equations

nodes.statement: Thus if we fix $p$, $q$, and a homotopy class of maps $u$, there is a well-defined orientation line $\mathfrak o_{p,q}$, canonically isomorphic to $\mathfrak o_{D_\text{Floer}}$ for any choice of $H$, $J$, and $u$.
nodes.name: Orientation line o_{p,q}
nodes.section: C.13.2 Orientations of linearized operators of Floer equations

nodes.statement: Floer--Hofer \cite[Theorem 10]{floerhoferorientations} also construct natural associative (even) isomorphisms: \begin{equation} \mathfrak o_{p,q}\otimes\mathfrak o_{q,r}\to\mathfrak o_{p,r} \end{equation} by a certain kernel gluing procedure.
nodes.name: Floer--Hofer gluing of orientation lines
nodes.statement_short: Natural associative even isomorphisms $\mathfrak o_{p,q}\otimes\mathfrak o_{q,r}\to\mathfrak o_{p,r}$ via kernel gluing.
nodes.section: C.13.2 Orientations of linearized operators of Floer equations

nodes.name: Floer--Hofer gluing isomorphism of orientation lines
nodes.statement: \mathfrak o_{p,q}\otimes\mathfrak o_{q,r}\to\mathfrak o_{p,r}
nodes.section: C.13.2 Orientations of linearized operators of Floer equations
nodes.label: floerhoferoogluing

nodes.statement: We refer the reader to \cite{floerhoferorientations} for the details of this construction. Suffice it to say here that, after adding a finite-dimensional piece to the domains of each of two linearized operators \eqref{Dfloer} (from $p$ to $q$ and from $q$ to $r$ respectively) so that they become surjective with kernels $K_1$ and $K_2$, there is a natural kernel pregluing map from $K_1\oplus K_2$ to the domain of certain glued operator (from $p$ to $r$); the $L^2$-orthogonal projection onto the kernel $K_3$ of the glued operator gives an isomorphism $K_1\oplus K_2\xrightarrow\sim K_3$, and this induces the map \eqref{floerhoferoogluing}, which may be shown to be independent of the choices used to define it.
nodes.name: Sketch of the Floer--Hofer kernel gluing
nodes.statement_short: Stabilize both operators to be surjective, preglue kernels, and $L^2$-project onto the glued kernel to get $K_1\oplus K_2\cong K_3$.
nodes.section: C.13.2 Orientations of linearized operators of Floer equations

nodes.statement: The coherent trivializations of $\mathfrak o_{p,q}$ resulting from the maps \eqref{floerhoferoogluing} are known to coincide with the usual coherent orientations of Morse theory, when restricted to $S^1$-invariant Hamiltonians and their $S^1$-invariant Floer trajectories, see e.g.\ Floer \cite{floersfhs}.
nodes.name: Floer--Hofer orientations agree with Morse orientations
nodes.origin_citation: Floer, Symplectic fixed points and holomorphic spheres
nodes.section: C.13.2 Orientations of linearized operators of Floer equations

nodes.name: Coherent orientations on Hamiltonian Floer moduli spaces
nodes.statement: The orientation sheaf (in the sense of Definition \ref{IAorientationsheaf}) of every moduli space $\overline{\mathcal M}(\sigma,p,q)$ can be canonically identified with $\mathfrak o_\sigma\otimes\mathfrak o_{p,q}$. Moreover, under these identifications, the boundary maps on orientation sheaves induced (as in \eqref{sesofO}) by the structure maps: \begin{align} \overline{\mathcal M}(\sigma|[0\ldots k],p,q)\times\overline{\mathcal M}(\sigma|[k\ldots n],q,r)&\to\partial\overline{\mathcal M}(\sigma,p,r)\\ \overline{\mathcal M}(\sigma|[0\ldots\hat k\ldots n],p,q)&\to\partial\overline{\mathcal M}(\sigma,p,q) \end{align} coincide with the maps: \begin{align} \mathfrak o_\sigma\otimes\mathfrak o_{p,r}&\to\mathfrak o_{\sigma|[0\ldots k]}\otimes\mathfrak o_{p,q}\otimes\mathfrak o_{\sigma|[k\ldots n]}\otimes\mathfrak o_{q,r}\\ \mathfrak o_\sigma\otimes\mathfrak o_{p,q}&\to\mathfrak o_{\sigma|[0\ldots\hat k\ldots n]}\otimes\mathfrak o_{p,q} \end{align} induced by \eqref{simplexflowproductor}--\eqref{simplexflowfaceor} and \eqref{floerhoferoogluing}.
nodes.section: C.13.3 Orientations on thickened moduli spaces $\overline{\mathcal M}(\sigma,p,q)_I^\mathrm{reg}$
nodes.statement_short: Orientation sheaves of $\overline{\mathcal M}(\sigma,p,q)$ are canonically $\mathfrak o_\sigma\otimes\mathfrak o_{p,q}$, and boundary maps match the simplex boundary maps tensored with the Floer--Hofer gluing maps.
conclusions: The orientation sheaf (in the sense of Definition \ref{IAorientationsheaf}) of every moduli space $\overline{\mathcal M}(\sigma,p,q)$ can be canonically identified with $\mathfrak o_\sigma\otimes\mathfrak o_{p,q}$.

Moreover, under these identifications, the boundary maps on orientation sheaves induced (as in \eqref{sesofO}) by the structure maps: \begin{align} \label{hforproduct}\overline{\mathcal M}(\sigma|[0\ldots k],p,q)\times\overline{\mathcal M}(\sigma|[k\ldots n],q,r)&\to\partial\overline{\mathcal M}(\sigma,p,r)\\ \label{hforface}\overline{\mathcal M}(\sigma|[0\ldots\hat k\ldots n],p,q)&\to\partial\overline{\mathcal M}(\sigma,p,q) \end{align} coincide with the maps: \begin{align} \label{hforproductor}\mathfrak o_\sigma\otimes\mathfrak o_{p,r}&\to\mathfrak o_{\sigma|[0\ldots k]}\otimes\mathfrak o_{p,q}\otimes\mathfrak o_{\sigma|[k\ldots n]}\otimes\mathfrak o_{q,r}\\ \label{hforfaceor}\mathfrak o_\sigma\otimes\mathfrak o_{p,q}&\to\mathfrak o_{\sigma|[0\ldots\hat k\ldots n]}\otimes\mathfrak o_{p,q} \end{align} induced by \eqref{simplexflowproductor}--\eqref{simplexflowfaceor} and \eqref{floerhoferoogluing}.
nodes.label: gluingHForientations

nodes.name: Proof of Proposition \ref{gluingHForientations}
nodes.statement: To identify the orientation sheaf of $\overline{\mathcal M}(\sigma,p,q)$ with $\mathfrak o_\sigma\otimes\mathfrak o_{p,q}$, it suffices to identify the orientation sheaf of every $\overline{\mathcal M}(\sigma,p,q)_I^\mathrm{reg}$ with $\mathfrak o_{E_I}\otimes\mathfrak o_\sigma\otimes\mathfrak o_{p,q}$ in a compatible way (for all finite subsets $I\subseteq\mathcal A(\sigma,p,q)^{\geq\mathfrak s^\mathrm{top}}$). Moreover, it suffices to make this identification over the open subset $\overline{\mathcal M}(\sigma,p,q)_I^{\mathrm{reg}\circ}\subseteq\overline{\mathcal M}(\sigma,p,q)_I^\mathrm{reg}$ where the domain curve is smooth (it then automatically extends uniquely to all of $\overline{\mathcal M}(\sigma,p,q)_I^\mathrm{reg}$, by virtue of the local topological description of $\overline{\mathcal M}(\sigma,p,q)_I^\mathrm{reg}$ given by the gluing map); we may also check compatibility with the inclusions $I\subseteq J$ over $\overline{\mathcal M}(\sigma,p,q)_I^{\mathrm{reg}\circ}$. Now the kernel $\tilde K=\ker D$ of the linearization \eqref{linearizedstd} forms a vector bundle over $\overline{\mathcal M}(\sigma,p,q)_I^{\mathrm{reg}\circ}$, and the orientation sheaf of $\overline{\mathcal M}(\sigma,p,q)_I^{\mathrm{reg}\circ}$ is isomorphic to $\mathfrak o_\sigma\otimes\mathfrak o_{\tilde K}$ (to see this, one must distinguish the two cases $\dim\sigma>0$ and $\dim\sigma=0$). Now we have $\mathfrak o_{\tilde K}=\mathfrak o_D=\mathfrak o_{D_\text{hol}}=\mathfrak o_{E_I}\otimes\mathfrak o_{p,q}$; this defines a fiberwise isomorphism of $\mathfrak o_{\tilde K}$ with $\mathfrak o_{E_I}\otimes\mathfrak o_{p,q}$, and since the operators $D$ and $D_\text{hol}$ vary nicely over the base $\overline{\mathcal M}(\sigma,p,q)_I^{\mathrm{reg}\circ}$, it is easy to see that this is in fact an isomorphism of sheaves. Thus we have the desired identification. Now let us show that the boundary map induced by \eqref{hforface} coincides with the tautological map \eqref{hforfaceor} (this just amounts to chasing definitions). Let $\mathfrak s\in\mathcal S_{\overline{\mathcal M}}(\sigma,p,q)$ denote the stratum $(\sigma|[0\ldots\hat k\ldots n],p,q)$ (i.e.\ the stratum consisting of trajectories over $\sigma$ which factor through $\sigma|[0\ldots\hat k\ldots n]$). Now on the space $\overline{\mathcal M}(\sigma|[0\ldots\hat k\ldots n],p,q)=\overline{\mathcal M}(\sigma,p,q)^{\leq\mathfrak s}$, we have three implicit atlases: \begin{equation} \mathcal A(\sigma|[0\ldots\hat k\ldots n],p,q)^{\geq\mathfrak s^\mathrm{top}}\subseteq\mathcal A(\sigma,p,q)^{\geq\mathfrak s}\supseteq\mathcal A(\sigma,p,q)^{\geq\mathfrak s^\mathrm{top}} \end{equation} (note that the two occurences of $\mathfrak s^\mathrm{top}$ refer to the top elements of two different strata posets); in fact (the index set of) the middle atlas is the disjoint union of (the index sets of) the atlases on the right and on the left. The reasoning used above to identify the orientation sheaf of $\overline{\mathcal M}(\sigma|[0\ldots\hat k\ldots n],p,q)=\overline{\mathcal M}(\sigma,p,q)^{\leq\mathfrak s}$ under the leftmost implicit atlas applies equally well for all three atlases (and, in particular, the resulting identifications coincide). Hence, for the purpose of identifying the boundary map on orientation sheaves, it suffices to consider the single atlas $\mathcal A(\sigma,p,q)^{\geq\mathfrak s^\mathrm{top}}$ on $\overline{\mathcal M}(\sigma,p,q)$ and the inclusion of the boundary stratum $\overline{\mathcal M}(\sigma,p,q)^{\leq\mathfrak s}\hookrightarrow\overline{\mathcal M}(\sigma,p,q)$. Now it suffices to check that the desired compatibility holds for the inclusion $(\overline{\mathcal M}(\sigma,p,q)^{\leq\mathfrak s}_I)^{\mathrm{reg}\circ}\hookrightarrow\overline{\mathcal M}(\sigma,p,q)_I^{\mathrm{reg}\circ}$ (for all finite subsets $I\subseteq\mathcal A(\sigma,p,q)^{\geq\mathfrak s^\mathrm{top}}$), and this follows by definition. Now let us show that the boundary map induced by \eqref{hforproduct} coincides with the tautological map \eqref{hforproductor}. First, we chase definitions as above. Let $\mathfrak s\in\mathcal S_{\overline{\mathcal M}}(\sigma,p,r)$ denote the stratum $(\sigma|[0\ldots k],p,q)$--$(\sigma|[k\ldots n],q,r)$ (i.e.\ the stratum consisting of Floer trajectories over $\sigma$ which are broken at vertex $k$ and periodic orbit $q\in\mathcal P_{H(k)}$). Now on the space $\overline{\mathcal M}(\sigma|[0\ldots k],p,q)\times\overline{\mathcal M}(\sigma|[k\ldots n],q,r)=\overline{\mathcal M}(\sigma,p,r)^{\leq\mathfrak s}$, we have three implicit atlases: \begin{equation*} \mathcal A(\sigma|[0\ldots k],p,q)^{\geq\mathfrak s^\mathrm{top}}\sqcup\mathcal A(\sigma|[k\ldots n],q,r)^{\geq\mathfrak s^\mathrm{top}}\subseteq\mathcal A(\sigma,p,r)^{\geq\mathfrak s}\supseteq\mathcal A(\sigma,p,r)^{\geq\mathfrak s^\mathrm{top}} \end{equation*} and in fact (the index set of) the middle atlas is the disjoint union of (the index sets of) the atlases on the right and on the left. The reasoning used above to identify the orientation sheaves of $\overline{\mathcal M}(\sigma|[0\ldots k],p,q)$ and $\overline{\mathcal M}(\sigma|[k\ldots n],q,r)$ applies equally well to identify the orientation sheaf of their product $\overline{\mathcal M}(\sigma|[0\ldots k],p,q)\times\overline{\mathcal M}(\sigma|[k\ldots n],q,r)=\overline{\mathcal M}(\sigma,p,r)^{\leq\mathfrak s}$ under all three atlases above (the fact that the thickening datums in the latter two atlases do not treat the portions of the trajectories from $p$ to $q$ and from $q$ to $r$ ``independently'' does not cause any problems). Hence for the purposes of identifying the boundary map on orientation sheaves, it suffices to consider the single atlas $\mathcal A(\sigma,p,r)^{\geq\mathfrak s^\mathrm{top}}$ on $\overline{\mathcal M}(\sigma,p,r)$ and the inclusion of the boundary stratum $\overline{\mathcal M}(\sigma,p,r)^{\leq\mathfrak s}\hookrightarrow\overline{\mathcal M}(\sigma,p,r)$. As before, it suffices to check that the desired compatibility holds for the inclusion $(\overline{\mathcal M}(\sigma,p,r)^{\leq\mathfrak s}_I)^\mathrm{reg}\hookrightarrow\overline{\mathcal M}(\sigma,p,r)_I^\mathrm{reg}$ (for all finite subsets $I\subseteq\mathcal A(\sigma,p,r)^{\geq\mathfrak s^\mathrm{top}}$), and moreover, this may be checked on the locus where the domain curve is smooth except for the required node over $k$ asymptotic to $q\in\mathcal P_{H(k)}$. It will be convenient to assume that $0<k<n$, so let us first deduce the case of general $0\leq k\leq n$ from the case $0<k<n$. Fix $\sigma$ and $0\leq k\leq n=\dim\sigma$. We consider the degenerate simplex $\sigma'\to\sigma$ given by ``doubling vertex $0$'' if $k=0$ and ``doubling vertex $n$'' if $k=n$ (i.e.\ if $0=k<n$, we consider $\Delta^{n+1}\to\Delta^n$ given by superimposing the first two vertices of $\Delta^{n+1}$, if $0<k=n$, we consider $\Delta^{n+1}\to\Delta^n$ given by superimposing the last two vertices of $\Delta^{n+1}$, and if $0=k=n$ we consider $\Delta^2\to\Delta^0$); let $k'=1$ if $k=0$ and let $k'=n'-1$ if $k=n$, where $n'=\dim\sigma'$, and note that $0<k'<n'$. Now there is a natural map $\mathcal A(\sigma,p,q)^{\geq\mathfrak s^\mathrm{top}}\to\mathcal A(\sigma',p,q)^{\geq\mathfrak s^\mathrm{top}}$ given by pulling back along $\sigma'\to\sigma$, and $\sigma'\to\sigma$ maps flow lines to flow lines (for the flow from Definition \ref{simplexflows}). Hence, given any point $x\in\overline{\mathcal M}(\sigma,p,r)_I^\mathrm{reg}$ with a single node over $k$ asymptotic to $q\in\mathcal P_{H(k)}$, we may lift it (canonically, up to translating the part(s) of the trajectory over $0=k$ and/or over $k=n$) to a point $x'\in\overline{\mathcal M}(\sigma',p,r)_I^\mathrm{reg}$ with a single node over $k'$ asymptotic to $q\in\mathcal P_{H'(k')}=\mathcal P_{H(k)}$. Moreover, there is a germ of homeomorphism $\overline{\mathcal M}(\sigma',p,r)_I^\mathrm{reg}=\overline{\mathcal M}(\sigma,p,r)_I^\mathrm{reg}\times\mathbb R^{\mathbf 1(k=0)+\mathbf 1(k=n)}$ between neighborhoods of $x'$ and $x\times 0$. Now the desired compatibility of orientations for $(\overline{\mathcal M}(\sigma,p,r)_I^{\leq\mathfrak s})^\mathrm{reg}\hookrightarrow\overline{\mathcal M}(\sigma,p,r)_I^\mathrm{reg}$ follows from the compatibility for $(\overline{\mathcal M}(\sigma',p,r)_I^{\leq\mathfrak s'})^\mathrm{reg}\hookrightarrow\overline{\mathcal M}(\sigma',p,r)_I^\mathrm{reg}$ (which has from $0<k'<n'$). Hence we may assume without loss of generality that $0<k<n$. Now we have come to the heart of the matter, where we will need to analyze the gluing map. To review: we have identified the orientation sheaf of $\overline{\mathcal M}(\sigma,p,r)_I^\mathrm{reg}$ with $\mathfrak o_{E_I}\otimes\mathfrak o_\sigma\otimes\mathfrak o_{p,r}$, and we have identified the orientation sheaf of $(\overline{\mathcal M}(\sigma,p,r)^{\leq\mathfrak s}_I)^\mathrm{reg}$ with $\mathfrak o_{E_I}\otimes\mathfrak o_{\sigma|[0\ldots k]}\otimes\mathfrak o_{p,q}\otimes\mathfrak o_{\sigma|[k\ldots n]}\otimes\mathfrak o_{q,r}$ (recall that $\mathfrak s$ denotes the stratum consisting of trajectories broken at vertex $k$ and periodic orbit $q\in\mathcal P_{H(k)}$). We must show that the boundary map on orientation sheaves induced by the inclusion $(\overline{\mathcal M}(\sigma,p,r)^{\leq\mathfrak s}_I)^\mathrm{reg}\hookrightarrow\overline{\mathcal M}(\sigma,p,r)_I^\mathrm{reg}$ is the expected map \eqref{hforproductor}, and it suffices to check this over the locus where the domain curve is smooth except for the required node over $k$ asymptotic to $q\in\mathcal P_{H(k)}$. We may further assume that $0<k<n$. We consider the gluing setup for $\overline{\mathcal M}(\sigma,p,r)_I^\mathrm{reg}$ at a point in $(\overline{\mathcal M}(\sigma,p,r)^{\leq\mathfrak s}_I)^\mathrm{reg}$ where $C_0$ is smooth except for the required node over vertex $k$ asymptotic to $q\in\mathcal P_{H(k)}$. In other words, $C_0\setminus\{q_0,q_1,q_2\}=S^1\times\mathbb R\sqcup S^1\times\mathbb R$, and $u_0:S^1\times\mathbb R\sqcup S^1\times\mathbb R\to M$ is a trajectory from $p$ to $q$ and from $q$ to $r$. From \S\ref{choosingDH}, we take $L=L'=0$ (i.e.\ no points $p_i$ or $p_i'$), and we may take $D=H=\varnothing$. From \S\ref{gluingandvaryingjAl}, there is one gluing parameter $\alpha\in\mathbb R_{\geq 0}$, there is no nontrivial variation in $(j_0,A_0)$ (i.e.\ $y\in\mathbb R^\ast=\mathbb R^0$), and there is some variation in $\ell_0$ parameterized by $w\in\prod_{i=1}^{2\prime}H^i$. As usual, we denote by $K\subseteq W^{k,2,\delta}(C_0,u_0^\ast TM)$ the kernel of the linearized operator (we shall omit the subscript $D,H$ since $L=L'=0$). Now the gluing construction gives rise to a gluing map: \begin{align} K\times\mathbb R_{\geq 0}\times\prod_{i=1}^{2\prime}H^i&\to\overline{\mathcal M}(\sigma,p,r)_I^\mathrm{reg}\\ (\kappa,\alpha,w)&\mapsto(u_{\alpha,w,y,\kappa},e_{\alpha,w,y,\kappa}) \end{align} ($y=0$). Now if we restrict to $\alpha=0$, this map realizes the identification of the orientation sheaf of $(\overline{\mathcal M}(\sigma,p,r)^{\leq\mathfrak s}_I)^\mathrm{reg}$ with $\mathfrak o_K\otimes\mathfrak o_{\sigma|[0\ldots k]}\otimes\mathfrak o_{\sigma|[k\ldots n]}$. Thus it suffices to show that for fixed (sufficiently small) $\alpha>0$ and fixed $w=0$, the gluing map is differentiable in the $K$ direction, and that its derivative (a map from $K$ to the kernel of the linearized operator at the glued map $u_{\alpha,w,y,\kappa}$) agrees (on orientation lines) with the Floer--Hofer map \eqref{floerhoferoogluing} (recall that $\mathfrak o_K$ is identified with $\mathfrak o_{E_I}\otimes\mathfrak o_{p,q}\otimes\mathfrak o_{q,r}$ and that the orientation line of the kernel at the glued map is identified with $\mathfrak o_{E_I}\otimes\mathfrak o_{p,r}$). For fixed $(\alpha,w,y)$, the gluing map is given by: \begin{equation} K\xrightarrow{\kappa\mapsto\kappa_\alpha}K_\alpha\xrightarrow{\kappa_\alpha\mapsto\kappa_{\alpha,w,y}}\mathcal F_{\alpha,w,y}^{-1}(0) \end{equation} The second map is defined \emph{a priori} by a Newton iteration, however a more natural description \emph{a posteriori} is that $\{\kappa_{\alpha,w,y}\}=\{\kappa_\alpha+\operatorname{im} Q_{\alpha,w,y}\}\pitchfork\mathcal F_{\alpha,w,y}^{-1}(0)$ is the unique (necessarily transverse) intersection in a $(k,2,\delta,\delta)$-neighborhood of zero of fixed size. Note that in this neighborhood of fixed size, $\mathcal F_{\alpha,w,y}^{-1}(0)$ is a (highly differentiable) submanifold, since $\mathcal F_{\alpha,w,y}$ is highly differentiable and $D_{\kappa_{\alpha,w,y}}\mathcal F_{\alpha,w,y}$ is surjective as observed in the proof of Lemma \ref{mapsstufftoregHF}. From this description of the second map, it is clearly differentiable. Thus the derivative of the restricted gluing map \eqref{restrictedgluingmap} at a given $\kappa$ is given by: \begin{equation} T_\kappa K\xrightarrow{\dot\kappa\mapsto\dot\kappa_\alpha}T_{\kappa_\alpha}K_\alpha\xrightarrow{\operatorname{proj}_{Q_{\alpha,w,y}}}T_{\kappa_{\alpha,w,y}}\mathcal F_{\alpha,w,y}^{-1}(0)=\ker D_{\kappa_{\alpha,w,y}}\mathcal F_{\alpha,w,y} \end{equation} The second map is ``projection with respect to $Q_{\alpha,w,y}$'', i.e.\ the map induced by identifying both the domain and codomain with $W^{k,2,\delta,\delta}(C_\alpha,u_\alpha^\ast TM)/\operatorname{im} Q_{\alpha,w,y}$. It suffices to study the derivative at $\kappa=0$, namely the first line of the following commuting diagram: \begin{equation} \begin{tikzcd}[column sep = small] T_0K\ar{rr}{\dot\kappa\mapsto\dot\kappa_\alpha}&&T_0K_\alpha\ar{rr}{\operatorname{proj}_{Q_{\alpha,w,y}}}\ar{dr}[swap]{\operatorname{proj}_{Q_{\alpha,w,y}}}&&\ker D_{(0)_{\alpha,w,y}}\mathcal F_{\alpha,w,y}\ar{dl}{\operatorname{proj}_{Q_{\alpha,w,y}}}\\ &&&\ker D_{\alpha,w,y} \end{tikzcd} \end{equation} The rightmost diagonal map is orientation preserving (i.e.\ it commutes with the identification of the orientation lines of the domain and codomain with $\mathfrak o_{E_I}\otimes\mathfrak o_{p,r}$), because $\operatorname{proj}_{Q_{\alpha,w,y}}$ gives a local trivialization of the bundle $\ker D\mathcal F_{\alpha,w,y}$ with respect to which the orientation is constant by definition. Now the leftmost diagonal map is just $\dot\kappa_\alpha\mapsto\dot\kappa_\alpha-Q_{\alpha,w,y}D_{\alpha,w,y}\dot\kappa_\alpha$. Hence it suffices to show that the following composition (note that we have changed notation from $\dot\kappa$ back to $\kappa$): \begin{equation} \ker D_{0,0,0}=K\xrightarrow{\kappa\mapsto\kappa_\alpha}K_\alpha\xrightarrow{\kappa_\alpha\mapsto\kappa_\alpha-Q_{\alpha,w,y}D_{\alpha,w,y}\kappa_\alpha}\ker D_{\alpha,w,y} \end{equation} acts as \eqref{floerhoferoogluing} on orientations (with respect to the previously defined isomorphisms $\mathfrak o_K=\mathfrak o_{E_I}\otimes\mathfrak o_{p,q}\otimes\mathfrak o_{q,r}$ and $\mathfrak o_{\ker D_{\alpha,w,y}}=\mathfrak o_{E_I}\otimes\mathfrak o_{p,r}$). We analyze \eqref{concretestufftocheckorientations} as follows. For convenience, we may as well assume that $w=0$, and recall that necessarily $y=0$. Now let us consider the following diagram: \begin{equation} \begin{tikzcd} K_{\alpha,0,0}\ar[hook,yshift=-0.5ex]{r}\ar[leftarrow,yshift=0.5ex]{r}{\operatorname{proj}_{T_{\alpha,0,0}}}&W^{k,2,\delta,\delta}(C_\alpha,u_\alpha^\ast TM)\oplus E_I\ar{r}{D_{\alpha,0,0}}&W^{k-1,2,\delta,\delta}(\tilde C_\alpha,\Omega^{0,1}_{\tilde C_\alpha,j_0}\otimes_\mathbb C u_\alpha^\ast TM_{J(\ell_{\alpha,0}(A_0(\cdot)))})\ar{d}{\mathrm{break}}\\ K_{0|\alpha,0,0}\ar[hook,yshift=-0.5ex]{r}\ar[leftarrow,yshift=0.5ex]{r}{\operatorname{proj}_{T_{0|\alpha,0,0}}}&W^{k,2,\delta,\delta}(C_0,u_{0|\alpha}^\ast TM)\oplus E_I\ar{u}{\mathrm{glue}}\ar{r}{D_{0|\alpha,0,0}}&W^{k-1,2,\delta,\delta}(\tilde C_0,\Omega^{0,1}_{\tilde C_0,j_0}\otimes_\mathbb C u_{0|\alpha}^\ast TM_{J(\ell_{0,0}(A_0(\cdot)))})\ar[leftrightarrow]{d}{\mathsf{PT}}\\ K_{0,0,0}\ar[hook,yshift=0.5ex]{r}\ar[leftarrow,yshift=-0.5ex]{r}[swap]{\operatorname{proj}_{Q_{0,0,0}}}\ar{ru}{\kappa\mapsto\kappa_{0|\alpha}}&W^{k,2,\delta,\delta}(C_0,u_0^\ast TM)\oplus E_I\ar[leftrightarrow]{u}{\mathsf{PT}}\ar[yshift=0.5ex]{r}{D_{0,0,0}}&\ar[yshift=-0.5ex]{l}{Q_{0,0,0}}W^{k-1,2,\delta,\delta}(\tilde C_0,\Omega^{0,1}_{\tilde C_0,j_0}\otimes_\mathbb C u_0^\ast TM_{J(\ell_{0,0}(A_0(\cdot)))}) \end{tikzcd} \end{equation} The right half is just a copy of \eqref{biginversediagramHF} (with the middle square collapsed since $y=0$). The left half consists of the inclusions of the kernels of the operators on the right half, as well as the projection maps associated to the images of the (approximate) right inverses $Q_{0,0,0}$, $T_{0|\alpha,0,0}:=\mathsf{PT}\circ Q_{0,0,0}\circ\mathsf{PT}$, and $T_{\alpha,0,0}=\mathrm{glue}\circ\mathsf{PT}\circ Q_{0,0,0}\circ\mathsf{PT}\circ\mathrm{break}$ (recall that $\operatorname{im} T_{\alpha,0,0}=\operatorname{im} Q_{\alpha,0,0}$). The diagonal map $\kappa\mapsto\kappa_{0|\alpha}$ is defined by cutting off as in Definition \ref{kernelpregluingHF}; thus $\kappa_\alpha=\mathrm{glue}(\kappa_{0|\alpha})$. Now the map \eqref{concretestufftocheckorientations} which we would like to analyze may be written as the composition $\kappa\mapsto\operatorname{proj}_{T_{\alpha,0,0}}(\mathrm{glue}(\kappa_{0|\alpha}))$ from \eqref{orientationsinversediagram}. Now, we know that $\|D_{0|\alpha,0,0}\kappa_{0|\alpha}\|_{k-1,2,\delta,\delta}=\|D_{\alpha,0,0}\kappa_\alpha\|_{k-1,2,\delta,\delta}$, which is small by Lemma \ref{pregluingKestimateHF}. It follows that the map we would like to analyze is well-approximated (as $\alpha\to 0$) by the map $\kappa\mapsto\operatorname{proj}_{T_{\alpha,0,0}}(\mathrm{glue}(\operatorname{proj}_{T_{0|\alpha,0,0}}\kappa_{0|\alpha}))$. In particular, since we are only interested in its action on orientations, it suffices to consider the latter map $\kappa\mapsto\operatorname{proj}_{T_{\alpha,0,0}}(\mathrm{glue}(\operatorname{proj}_{T_{0|\alpha,0,0}}\kappa_{0|\alpha}))$. Now we claim that the map $K_{0,0,0}\to K_{0|\alpha,0,0}$ given by $\kappa\mapsto\operatorname{proj}_{T_{0|\alpha,0,0}}\kappa_{0|\alpha}$ preserves orientation (the orientation lines of the domain and codomain are both identified with $\mathfrak o_{E_I}\otimes\mathfrak o_{p,q}\otimes\mathfrak o_{q,r}$). To see this, simply observe the map (as well as its domain and codomain and their orientations) vary continuously over $\alpha\in[0,\epsilon)$, and that the statement is true for $\alpha=0$ because then the map is the identity map. Hence we have reduced the problem to showing that the map: \begin{equation} W^{k,2,\delta,\delta}(C_0,u_{0|\alpha}^\ast TM)\supseteq K_{0|\alpha,0,0}\xrightarrow{\mathrm{glue}}W^{k,2,\delta,\delta}(C_\alpha,u_\alpha^\ast TM)\oplus E_I\xrightarrow{\operatorname{proj}_{T_{\alpha,0,0}}}K_{\alpha,0,0} \end{equation} acts by \eqref{floerhoferoogluing}. To analyze the map ${\operatorname{proj}_{T_{\alpha,0,0}}}\circ{\mathrm{glue}}:K_{0|\alpha,0,0}\to K_{\alpha,0,0}$, argue as follows. For any finite-dimensional vector space $F$ and a map $\Lambda:F\to W^{k-1,2,\delta,\delta}(\tilde C_0,\Omega^{0,1}_{\tilde C_0,j_0}\otimes_\mathbb C u_0^\ast TM_{J(\ell_{0,0}(A_0(\cdot)))})$ supported away from the ends, we may consider the following modified version of \eqref{orientationsinversediagram}: \begin{equation} \begin{tikzcd} K_{\alpha,0,0}^{\Lambda,t}\ar[hook,yshift=-0.5ex]{r}\ar[leftarrow,yshift=0.5ex]{r}{\operatorname{proj}_{T_{\alpha,0,0}^{\Lambda,t}}}&F\oplus W^{k,2,\delta,\delta}(C_\alpha,u_\alpha^\ast TM)\oplus E_I\ar{r}{\Lambda\oplus D_{\alpha,0,0}^t}&W^{k-1,2,\delta,\delta}(\tilde C_\alpha,\Omega^{0,1}_{\tilde C_\alpha,j_0}\otimes_\mathbb C u_\alpha^\ast TM_{J(\ell_{\alpha,0}(A_0(\cdot)))})\ar{d}{\mathrm{break}}\\ K_{0|\alpha,0,0}^{\Lambda,t}\ar[hook,yshift=-0.5ex]{r}\ar[leftarrow,yshift=0.5ex]{r}{\operatorname{proj}_{T_{0|\alpha,0,0}^{\Lambda,t}}}&F\oplus W^{k,2,\delta,\delta}(C_0,u_{0|\alpha}^\ast TM)\oplus E_I\ar{u}{\operatorname{id}\oplus\mathrm{glue}}\ar{r}{\Lambda\oplus D_{0|\alpha,0,0}^t}&W^{k-1,2,\delta,\delta}(\tilde C_0,\Omega^{0,1}_{\tilde C_0,j_0}\otimes_\mathbb C u_{0|\alpha}^\ast TM_{J(\ell_{0,0}(A_0(\cdot)))})\ar[leftrightarrow]{d}{\mathsf{PT}}\\ K_{0,0,0}^{\Lambda,t}\ar[hook,yshift=0.5ex]{r}\ar[leftarrow,yshift=-0.5ex]{r}[swap]{\operatorname{proj}_{Q_{0,0,0}^{\Lambda,t}}}\ar{ru}{\kappa\mapsto\kappa_{0|\alpha}}&F\oplus W^{k,2,\delta,\delta}(C_0,u_0^\ast TM)\oplus E_I\ar[leftrightarrow]{u}{\operatorname{id}\oplus\mathsf{PT}}\ar[yshift=0.5ex]{r}{\Lambda\oplus D_{0,0,0}^t}&\ar[yshift=-0.5ex]{l}{Q_{0,0,0}^{\Lambda,t}}W^{k-1,2,\delta,\delta}(\tilde C_0,\Omega^{0,1}_{\tilde C_0,j_0}\otimes_\mathbb C u_0^\ast TM_{J(\ell_{0,0}(A_0(\cdot)))}) \end{tikzcd} \end{equation} Here $t\in[0,1]$ indicates that the terms \eqref{firstLterm}--\eqref{lastLterm} carry a factor of $t$. The estimates from Lemmas \ref{approxbottomHF} and \ref{approxtopHF} apply to this modified diagram as well. Thus as long as we fix a bounded right inverse $Q_{0,0,0}^{\Lambda,t}$ of $D_{0,0,0}^{\Lambda,t}$, the rest of the diagram makes sense (and, in particular, $T_{0|\alpha,0,0}^{\Lambda,t}$ and $T_{\alpha,0,0}^{\Lambda,t}$ are approximate right inverses) for sufficiently small $\alpha>0$. Furthermore, in any family of $(\Lambda,t,Q^{\Lambda,t})$, the kernels $K_{0,0,0}$, $K_{0|\alpha,0,0}$, $K_{\alpha,0,0}$ form vector bundles, and the identifications of their orientation lines with $\mathfrak o_F\otimes\mathfrak o_{p,q}\otimes\mathfrak o_{q,r}\otimes\mathfrak o_{E_I}$ and $\mathfrak o_F\otimes\mathfrak o_{p,r}\otimes\mathfrak o_{E_I}$ (respectively) vary continuously. Now the map: \begin{equation} K_{0|\alpha,0,0}^{\Lambda,t}\xrightarrow{{\operatorname{proj}_{T_{\alpha,0,0}^{\Lambda,t}}}\circ{\mathrm{glue}}}K_{\alpha,0,0}^{\Lambda,t} \end{equation} is exactly the map we wish to analyze when $F=0$, $\Lambda=0$, $t=1$, and $Q_{0,0,0}^{\Lambda,t}=0\oplus Q_{0,0,0}$. More generally, if we allow $F$ nonzero (but still $\Lambda=0$), this map is simply our desired map plus the identity map on $F$. Since the space of acceptable maps $\Lambda$ is contractible, it suffices to show that \eqref{KmapLt} has the desired action on orientations for any single pair $(F,\Lambda)$, $t=1$, and $Q_{0,0,0}^{\Lambda,t}=0\oplus Q_{0,0,0}$. Now by compactness of $[0,1]$, there exists a pair $(F,\Lambda)$ so that $\Lambda\oplus D_{0,0,0}^t$ is surjective for all $t\in[0,1]$. Fix such a pair $(F,\Lambda)$, and also fix a continuously varying family of bounded right inverses $Q_{0,0,0}^{\Lambda,t}$ with $Q_{0,0,0}^{\Lambda,1}=0\oplus Q_{0,0,0}$. Since the kernels form a bundle over the base $[0,1]$ and their orientations vary continuously, it suffices to analyze \eqref{KmapLt} for this $(F,\Lambda)$, $t=0$, and this $Q_{0,0,0}^{\Lambda,0}$. Now the Floer--Hofer map \eqref{floerhoferoogluing} is \emph{defined} (see \cite[Proposition 9]{floerhoferorientations}) by the property that it is induced by a certain map $K_{0|\alpha,0,0}^{\Lambda,0}\to K_{\alpha,0,0}^{\Lambda,0}$ closely related to \eqref{KmapLt}; clearly it suffices to show that the difference between the Floer--Hofer map and \eqref{KmapLt} is very small. Consider the map: \begin{equation} K_{0|\alpha,0,0}^{\Lambda,t}\xrightarrow{{\operatorname{proj}_{L^2}}\circ{\mathrm{glue}}}K_{\alpha,0,0}^{\Lambda,t} \end{equation} in the setting of the above choices of $(F,\Lambda)$, $t=0$, and $Q_{0,0,0}^{\Lambda,t}$, where instead of projecting off of $\operatorname{im} T_{\alpha,0,0}^{\Lambda,0}$, we use the $L^2$-orthogonal projection. The difference between \eqref{KmapLtLtwo} and \eqref{KmapLt} is exactly ${\operatorname{proj}_{L^2}}\circ Q^{\Lambda,0}_{\alpha,0,0}\circ(\Lambda\oplus D^0_{\alpha,0,0})\circ{\mathrm{glue}}$, which has small norm by the estimate in Lemma \ref{approxtopHF}. Thus it suffices to compare \eqref{KmapLtLtwo} to the Floer--Hofer map. Now the Floer--Hofer map is given by: \begin{equation} K_{0|\alpha,0,0}^{\Lambda,0}\xrightarrow{{\operatorname{proj}_{L^2}}\circ{\mathrm{glue}'}}K_{\alpha,0,0}^{\Lambda,0} \end{equation} for a certain map $\mathrm{glue}'$ (see \cite[Proposition 9]{floerhoferorientations}). However, the norm of the difference $\mathrm{glue}-\mathrm{glue}'$ is very small due to the exponential decay of elements of the kernel (here, we may use the explicit description of $K_{0|\alpha,0,0}$ as the image of $\kappa\mapsto\kappa_{0|\alpha}-Q_{0|\alpha,0,0}D_{0|\alpha,0,0}\kappa_{0|\alpha}$). Thus we are done.
nodes.section: C.13.3 Orientations on thickened moduli spaces $\overline{\mathcal M}(\sigma,p,q)_I^\mathrm{reg}$
nodes.statement_short: Identify orientation sheaves via kernels of linearized operators, reduce boundary compatibility to a single atlas and the case $0<k<n$, then show the derivative of the gluing map in the kernel direction agrees with the Floer--Hofer kernel gluing map. Key step: deform via a stabilization $(F,\Lambda)$ and a homotopy in $t$, and compare projections using the top-square estimate and exponential decay.
