nodes.statement: In this case, the implicit atlas $A=\{\alpha\}$ consists of a topological manifold $X_\alpha$, a function $s_\alpha:X_\alpha\to E_\alpha$, and an identification $X=s_\alpha^{-1}(0)$. This atlas being $S^1$-equivariant means that $X_\alpha$ is equipped with an $S^1$-action for which $s_\alpha$ is $S^1$-invariant and which induces the given action on $X$.
nodes.name: Single-chart equivariant setup
nodes.statement_short: Describe the S^1-equivariant single chart.

nodes.statement: The desired statement follows from the following diagram, as we explain below: \begin{equation*} \begin{CD} \check H^d(X/S^1)@=H_{\dim E_\alpha-1}^{S^1}(X_\alpha,X_\alpha\setminus X)@>(s_\alpha)_\ast>>H_{\dim E_\alpha-1}^{S^1}(E_\alpha,E_\alpha\setminus 0)\cr @V\pi^\ast VV@VV\pi^!V@VV\pi^!V\cr \check H^d(X)@=H_{\dim E_\alpha}(X_\alpha,X_\alpha\setminus X)@>(s_\alpha)_\ast>>H_{\dim E_\alpha}(E_\alpha,E_\alpha\setminus 0)@>[E_\alpha]\mapsto 1>>\mathbb Z \end{CD} \end{equation*} The map $\pi^\ast$ is pullback under $\pi:X\to X/S^1$. The maps $\pi^!$ are the maps from the Gysin long exact sequence for an $S^1$-space: \begin{equation} \cdots\xrightarrow{\cap e}H_{\bullet-1}^{S^1}(Z)\xrightarrow{\pi^!}H_\bullet(Z)\xrightarrow{\pi_\ast}H_\bullet^{S^1}(Z)\xrightarrow{\cap e}H_{\bullet-2}^{S^1}(Z)\xrightarrow{\pi^!}\cdots \end{equation} The two leftmost horizontal identifications are a form of Poincar\'e duality (which can be proven, along with the commutativity of the square, with homotopy $\mathcal K$-sheaves as in \S\ref{homotopysheavesintrosec}); it is at this step where we use the fact that $S^1$ acts freely on $X$.
nodes.name: Comparison diagram via Gysin maps
nodes.statement_short: Set up the commutative diagram of equivariant Poincare duality and Gysin maps.

nodes.statement: Now $[X]^\mathrm{vir}$ is by definition the composition of the bottom row. Hence $\pi_\ast[X]^\mathrm{vir}$ is the map from the upper left corner to the bottom right. On the other hand, the rightmost vertical map $\pi^!:H_{\dim E_\alpha-1}^{S^1}(E_\alpha,E_\alpha\setminus 0)\to H_{\dim E_\alpha}(E_\alpha,E_\alpha\setminus 0)$ vanishes since $S^1$ acts trivially on $E_\alpha$. It follows that $\pi_\ast[X]^\mathrm{vir}=0$ as desired.
nodes.name: Gysin map vanishes on E
nodes.statement_short: Conclude since the Gysin map on (E,E minus 0) vanishes for the trivial action.

nodes.name: Homotopy sheaf property
nodes.statement: Applying Lemmas \ref{singularchainshomotopyKsheaf} and \ref{associatedgradedhomotopysheaf}, we see that $C^\bullet_\mathrm{vir}(-;A)_{IJ}$ and $C^\bullet_\mathrm{vir}(-\operatorname{rel}\partial;A)_{IJ}$ are both homotopy $\mathcal K$-sheaves.
nodes.statement_short: Apply general lemmas to see the partial complexes are homotopy $\mathcal K$-sheaves.

nodes.name: $X_{I,J,A}$ is a manifold with boundary
nodes.statement: Now let us calculate $H^\bullet_\mathrm{vir}(K;A)_{IJ}$ and $H^\bullet_\mathrm{vir}(K\operatorname{rel}\partial;A)_{IJ}$. It follows from the submersion axiom that $X_{I,J,A}$ is a topological manifold of dimension $\operatorname{vdim}_AX+\dim E_A+\#I$ with boundary (not necessarily second countable or paracompact).\footnote{In fact, it carries a natural structure of a manifold with corners, which for the present purpose is mostly irrelevant.} The boundary $\partial(X_{I,J,A})$ is a (not necessarily disjoint) union of two pieces, namely the locus where $x\in\partial X_J^\mathrm{reg}$ (which is precisely $(\partial X)_{I,J,A}$) and the locus where $t_\alpha=0$ for some $\alpha\in I$. It is easy to see that the first piece $(\partial X)_{I,J,A}\subseteq\partial(X_{I,J,A})$ is a closed tamely embedded codimension zero submanifold with boundary.
nodes.statement_short: By the submersion axiom $X_{I,J,A}$ is a topological manifold whose boundary has two pieces.

nodes.name: Poincar\'e--Lefschetz duality
nodes.statement: Hence we may apply Poincar\'e--Lefschetz duality in the form of Lemma \ref{poincareduality} to see that: \begin{align} H^\bullet_\mathrm{vir}(K\operatorname{rel}\partial;A)_{IJ}&=\check H_c^{\bullet+\#I}(\psi_{\varnothing J}^{-1}(K\cap V_I\cap V_J)\times\mathbb R_{>0}^I,\mathfrak o_\mathbb R^{\otimes I}\otimes\mathfrak o_{E_J}^\vee\otimes\mathfrak o_{X_J^\mathrm{reg}\operatorname{rel}\partial})^{\Gamma_A}\\ H^\bullet_\mathrm{vir}(K;A)_{IJ}&=\check H_c^{\bullet+\#I}(\psi_{\varnothing J}^{-1}(K\cap V_I\cap V_J)\times\mathbb R_{>0}^I,\mathfrak o_\mathbb R^{\otimes I}\otimes\mathfrak o_{E_J}^\vee\otimes\mathfrak o_{X_J^\mathrm{reg}})^{\Gamma_A} \end{align} (the orientation sheaf of $X_{I,J,A}$ is given by $\mathfrak o_{X_J^\mathrm{reg}}\otimes\mathfrak o_{E_A}\otimes\mathfrak o_{E_J}^\vee\otimes\mathfrak o_\mathbb R^{\otimes I}$).
nodes.statement_short: Apply Poincar\'e--Lefschetz duality to express the cohomology as compactly supported \v Cech cohomology.

nodes.name: K\"unneth formula
nodes.statement: Now we apply the K\"unneth formula to conclude that: \begin{align} H^\bullet_\mathrm{vir}(K\operatorname{rel}\partial;A)_{IJ}&=\check H^\bullet_c(\psi_{\varnothing J}^{-1}(K\cap V_I\cap V_J),\mathfrak o_{E_J}^\vee\otimes\mathfrak o_{X_J^\mathrm{reg}\operatorname{rel}\partial})^{\Gamma_A}\\ H^\bullet_\mathrm{vir}(K;A)_{IJ}&=\check H^\bullet_c(\psi_{\varnothing J}^{-1}(K\cap V_I\cap V_J),\mathfrak o_{E_J}^\vee\otimes\mathfrak o_{X_J^\mathrm{reg}})^{\Gamma_A} \end{align}
nodes.statement_short: Remove the $\mathbb R_{>0}^I$ factor by the K\"unneth formula.

nodes.name: Use local orientability
nodes.statement: Since $X$ is locally orientable, we have $\mathfrak o_{X_J^\mathrm{reg}}\otimes\mathfrak o_{E_J}^\vee=\psi_{\varnothing J}^\ast\mathfrak o_X$, so we can write: \begin{align} H^\bullet_\mathrm{vir}(K\operatorname{rel}\partial;A)_{IJ}&=\check H^\bullet_c(\psi_{\varnothing J}^{-1}(K\cap V_I\cap V_J),\psi_{\varnothing J}^\ast\mathfrak o_{X\operatorname{rel}\partial})^{\Gamma_A}\\ H^\bullet_\mathrm{vir}(K;A)_{IJ}&=\check H^\bullet_c(\psi_{\varnothing J}^{-1}(K\cap V_I\cap V_J),\psi_{\varnothing J}^\ast\mathfrak o_X)^{\Gamma_A} \end{align}
nodes.statement_short: Rewrite the coefficients as the pullback of $\mathfrak o_X$.

nodes.name: Quotient by finite group
nodes.statement: Now $\Gamma_A$ acts through the projection $\Gamma_A\to\Gamma_J$, and $\psi_{\varnothing J}:\psi_{\varnothing J}^{-1}(K\cap V_I\cap V_J)\to K\cap V_I\cap V_J$ is exactly the quotient by $\Gamma_J$. Hence by Lemma \ref{cechcohomologyfinitequotient} we get isomorphisms: \begin{align} H^\bullet_\mathrm{vir}(K\operatorname{rel}\partial;A)_{IJ}&=\check H^\bullet_c(K\cap V_I\cap V_J,\mathfrak o_{X\operatorname{rel}\partial})\\ H^\bullet_\mathrm{vir}(K;A)_{IJ}&=\check H^\bullet_c(K\cap V_I\cap V_J,\mathfrak o_X) \end{align}
nodes.statement_short: Pass to the quotient by $\Gamma_J$ using \v Cech cohomology of finite quotients.

nodes.name: Extension by zero
nodes.statement: Now use Lemma \ref{cptcechembeddingproperty} to write this as: \begin{align} H^\bullet_\mathrm{vir}(K\operatorname{rel}\partial;A)_{IJ}&=\check H^\bullet(K,j_!j^\ast\mathfrak o_{X\operatorname{rel}\partial})\\ H^\bullet_\mathrm{vir}(K;A)_{IJ}&=\check H^\bullet(K,j_!j^\ast\mathfrak o_X) \end{align}
nodes.statement_short: Rewrite compactly supported cohomology as cohomology of $j_!j^\ast\mathfrak o_X$.

nodes.name: Conclude purity
nodes.statement: Thus $C^\bullet_\mathrm{vir}(-;A)_{IJ}$ and $C^\bullet_\mathrm{vir}(-\operatorname{rel}\partial;A)_{IJ}$ are both pure, and we manifestly have the desired isomorphisms \eqref{EisoI}--\eqref{EisoII}.
nodes.statement_short: Conclude purity and the isomorphisms.

nodes.name: Reduce to gluing lemma
nodes.statement: This is a special case of Lemma \ref{gluingcechsimple}; we just need to make sure all of the hypotheses are satisfied.
nodes.statement_short: Reduce to the gluing lemma for pure homotopy $\mathcal K$-sheaves.

nodes.name: The open cover $V_I$
nodes.statement: The open cover in question is $V_I:=\psi_{\varnothing I}((s_I|X_I^\mathrm{reg})^{-1}(0))$; it follows from the axioms of an implicit atlas that $V_I\cap V_K\subseteq V_J$ for $I\subseteq J\subseteq K$ and $V_I\cap V_{I'}\subseteq V_{I\cup I'}$ for all $I,I'$.
nodes.statement_short: Introduce the cover $V_I$ and verify its intersection properties from the atlas axioms.

nodes.name: Compatibility on stalks
nodes.statement: Now we just need to check that the system of isomorphisms from Lemma \ref{CSTpure} are compatible with the maps of the homotopy diagram. These being maps of sheaves, it suffices to check compatibility locally (on stalks) and thus is a straightforward calculation (this is where the extra normalization factor of $(\#\Gamma_{J\setminus J'})^{-1}$ in Definition \ref{Ccomplexdef} is important).
nodes.statement_short: Check compatibility of the isomorphisms with the homotopy diagram on stalks.

nodes.name: Reduce to sheaf diagram
nodes.statement: By the definition of the vertical identifications, the commutativity of the first two squares of \eqref{compatibilityoflesdiagram} reduces to the commutativity of the diagram of sheaves: \begin{equation} \begin{tikzcd} H^0_\mathrm{vir}(-\operatorname{rel}\partial;A)\ar{r}{\eqref{sesofF}}\ar[equal]{d}{\text{Prop \ref{Cpure}}}&H^0_\mathrm{vir}(-;A)\ar{r}{\eqref{sesofF}}\ar[equal]{d}{\text{Prop \ref{Cpure}}}&H^0_\mathrm{vir}(-;A)\ar[equal]{d}{\text{Prop \ref{Cpure}}}\\ \mathfrak o_{X\operatorname{rel}\partial}\ar{r}{\eqref{sesofO}}&\mathfrak o_X\ar{r}{\eqref{sesofO}}&i_\ast\mathfrak o_{\partial X} \end{tikzcd} \end{equation} It suffices to check commutativity on stalks, and to do this, we can work with the complexes on the right in Lemma \ref{localdescofISO}, for which the commutativity is clear.
nodes.statement_short: Reduce the first two squares to a diagram of sheaves checked on stalks via local models.
nodes.section: 4.4 Long exact sequence for the pair \texorpdfstring{$(X,\partial X)$}{(X,dX)}

nodes.name: Auxiliary diagram
nodes.statement: In fact, the commutativity of the last square of \eqref{compatibilityoflesdiagram} is also a consequence of the commutativity of \eqref{sheafcommutativity}. To see this, consider the following diagram: \begin{equation*} \begin{tikzcd}[column sep = small] H^\bullet_\mathrm{vir}(\partial X;A)\ar[equal]{d}{\text{Prop \ref{cechcohomologypurehomotopysheaf}}}&\ar{l}[swap]{\sim}H^\bullet[C^{\bullet+1}_\mathrm{vir}(X\operatorname{rel}\partial;A)\to C^\bullet_\mathrm{vir}(X;A)]\ar{r}\ar[equal]{d}{\text{Prop \ref{cechcohomologypurehomotopysheaf}}}&H^{\bullet+1}_\mathrm{vir}(X\operatorname{rel}\partial;A)\ar[equal]{d}{\text{Prop \ref{cechcohomologypurehomotopysheaf}}}\\ \check H^\bullet(\partial X;H^0_\mathrm{vir}(-;A))\ar{d}{\sim}&\ar{l}[swap]{\sim}\check H^\bullet(X;[H^0_\mathrm{vir}(-\operatorname{rel}\partial;A)[1]\to H^0_\mathrm{vir}(-;A)])\ar{r}\ar{d}{\sim}&\check H^{\bullet+1}(X,H^0_\mathrm{vir}(-\operatorname{rel}\partial;A))\ar{d}{\sim}\\ \check H^\bullet(\partial X;\mathfrak o_{\partial X})&\ar{l}[swap]{\sim}\check H^\bullet(X;[\mathfrak o_{X\operatorname{rel}\partial}[1]\to\mathfrak o_X])\ar{r}&\check H^{\bullet+1}(X,\mathfrak o_{X\operatorname{rel}\partial}) \end{tikzcd} \end{equation*}
nodes.statement_short: Introduce an auxiliary diagram with mapping cones for the last square.
nodes.section: 4.4 Long exact sequence for the pair \texorpdfstring{$(X,\partial X)$}{(X,dX)}

nodes.name: Check the squares
nodes.statement: The middle vertical arrow is defined because of the commutativity of the left square in \eqref{sheafcommutativity}. The top left horizontal arrow is a quasi-isomorphism, and thus every left horizontal arrow is a quasi-isomorphism. The bottom left square is commutative because of the commutativity of the right square in \eqref{sheafcommutativity}; the other squares are trivially commutative.
nodes.statement_short: Each square of the auxiliary diagram commutes by \eqref{sheafcommutativity}.
nodes.section: 4.4 Long exact sequence for the pair \texorpdfstring{$(X,\partial X)$}{(X,dX)}

nodes.name: Conclude
nodes.statement: Reversing the left horizontal arrows, we see that the outermost square commutes, and this is exactly the last square in \eqref{compatibilityoflesdiagram}.
nodes.statement_short: Reversing quasi-isomorphisms gives the last square.
nodes.section: 4.4 Long exact sequence for the pair \texorpdfstring{$(X,\partial X)$}{(X,dX)}

nodes.name: Reduce to finite atlas
nodes.statement: We may assume that $A$ is finite. Certainly there is a map $C^\bullet_\mathrm{vir}(X\operatorname{rel}\partial;A')\to C^\bullet_\mathrm{vir}(X\operatorname{rel}\partial;A)$ which respects the map \eqref{Fpushforward}.
nodes.statement_short: Assume $A$ finite; chains push forward compatibly with $s_\ast$.

nodes.name: Reduce to sheaf diagram and check locally
nodes.statement: Hence it suffices to show that the following diagram commutes: \begin{equation} \begin{tikzcd} H^\bullet_\mathrm{vir}(X\operatorname{rel}\partial;A')\ar{d}\ar[equal]{r}{\text{Thm \ref{Fsheaffundamentaliso}}}&\check H^\bullet(X;\mathfrak o_{X\operatorname{rel}\partial})\ar[equal]{d}\\ H^\bullet_\mathrm{vir}(X\operatorname{rel}\partial;A)\ar[equal]{r}{\text{Thm \ref{Fsheaffundamentaliso}}}&\check H^\bullet(X;\mathfrak o_{X\operatorname{rel}\partial}) \end{tikzcd} \end{equation} where the left vertical arrow is induced by the obvious pushforward on chains. By definition of the isomorphisms above, it suffices to check commutativity of the corresponding diagram of sheaves with $\bullet=0$. This can be checked locally, where it is clear.
nodes.statement_short: Reduce to commutativity of a square of isomorphisms, then to degree-zero sheaves, checked locally.

nodes.name: Splitting over disjoint union
nodes.statement: We may assume that $A$ is finite. There is a natural isomorphism: \begin{equation} C^\bullet_\mathrm{vir}(X\sqcup Y\operatorname{rel}\partial;A)=C^\bullet_\mathrm{vir}(X\operatorname{rel}\partial;A)\oplus C^\bullet_\mathrm{vir}(Y\operatorname{rel}\partial;A) \end{equation} compatible with the map to $C_{-\bullet}(E;A)$.
nodes.statement_short: Assume $A$ finite; virtual cochains split over $X\sqcup Y$.

nodes.name: Reduce to sheaf square
nodes.statement: Thus it suffices to show that the following square of isomorphisms commutes: \begin{equation} \begin{tikzcd} H^\bullet_\mathrm{vir}(X\sqcup Y\operatorname{rel}\partial;A)\ar[equal]{d}\ar[equal]{r}{\text{Thm \ref{Fsheaffundamentaliso}}}&\check H^\bullet(X\sqcup Y;\mathfrak o_{X\sqcup Y\operatorname{rel}\partial})\ar[equal]{d}\\ H^\bullet_\mathrm{vir}(X\operatorname{rel}\partial;A)\oplus H^\bullet_\mathrm{vir}(Y\operatorname{rel}\partial;A)\ar[equal]{r}{\text{Thm \ref{Fsheaffundamentaliso}}}&\check H^\bullet(X;\mathfrak o_{X\operatorname{rel}\partial})\oplus\check H^\bullet(Y;\mathfrak o_{Y\operatorname{rel}\partial}) \end{tikzcd} \end{equation} By definition of the horizontal maps, it suffices to check the commutativity of the corresponding diagram of sheaves on $X\sqcup Y$, which is clear.
nodes.statement_short: Reduce to a square of sheaves, which commutes.

nodes.name: Connecting map commutes with $s_\ast$
nodes.statement: We may assume that $A$ is finite. The map $C^\bullet_\mathrm{vir}(\partial X;A)\to C^{\bullet+1}_\mathrm{vir}(X\operatorname{rel}\partial;A)$ in \eqref{sesofF} commutes with the maps from both of these groups to $C_{d-\bullet}(E;A)$.
nodes.statement_short: Assume $A$ finite; the connecting map commutes with the maps to $C(E;A)$.

nodes.name: Apply compatibility of long exact sequences
nodes.statement: Hence the result follows from the commutativity of the last square in Proposition \ref{compatibilityoflongexactsequence}.
nodes.statement_short: Conclude from Proposition 4.4.17.

nodes.name: Empty subatlas
nodes.statement: We may replace $A$ with the finite subatlas $\varnothing\subseteq A$. Now in this case, we have: \begin{equation} C^\bullet_\mathrm{vir}(K\operatorname{rel}\partial;\varnothing)=C^\bullet_\mathrm{vir}(K\operatorname{rel}\partial;\varnothing)_{\varnothing\varnothing}=C_{d-\bullet}(X_{\varnothing,\varnothing,\varnothing},X_{\varnothing,\varnothing,\varnothing}\setminus X_{\varnothing,\varnothing,\varnothing}^K)=C_{d-\bullet}(X,X\setminus K) \end{equation}
nodes.statement_short: Use the empty subatlas, where virtual cochains are relative chains.

nodes.name: Identify with Poincar\'e duality
nodes.statement: It follows that the identification $\check H^\bullet(X;\mathfrak o_{X\operatorname{rel}\partial})=H^\bullet_\mathrm{vir}(X\operatorname{rel}\partial;\varnothing)=H_{d-\bullet}(X)$ is simply the usual Poincar\'e duality isomorphism, and the map $H_{-\bullet}(X)\to H_{-\bullet}(E;\varnothing)\to R$ is the usual augmentation on $H_0$.
nodes.statement_short: The identification is Poincar\'e duality and $s_\ast$ is augmentation.

nodes.name: Conclude
nodes.statement: Hence the composition $\check H^\bullet(X;\mathfrak o_{X\operatorname{rel}\partial})\to R$ is pairing against the usual fundamental class of $X$.
nodes.statement_short: The functional is pairing with $[X]$.

nodes.name: Choose a transverse deformation
nodes.statement: The statement about orientation sheaves is a straightforward calculation which we omit. Choose some smooth family of sections $\tilde s:B\times[0,1]\to E$ with $\tilde s^{-1}(0)$ compact, so that $\tilde s(\cdot,0)=s$ and $s_1:=\tilde s(\cdot,1)$ is transverse to the zero section.
nodes.statement_short: Omit the orientation calculation; choose a family of sections from $s$ to a transverse $s_1$.

nodes.name: Atlases on the cobordism
nodes.statement: Now $B\times[0,1]$ is a smooth manifold with boundary, so let $\tilde A$ be the implicit atlas on $\tilde X:=\tilde s^{-1}(0)$ from Definition \ref{IAonvectorbundlezeroset}. Similarly, let $A'$ be the implicit atlas on $X':=(s')^{-1}(0)$.
nodes.statement_short: Introduce the implicit atlases $\tilde A$ on $\tilde X$ and $A'$ on $X'$.

nodes.name: Compare atlases via subatlas
nodes.statement: Now we have two implicit atlases on $X$, namely $A$ and (the restriction to the boundary of) $\tilde A$. On the other hand, we can exhibit $A$ as a subatlas of $\tilde A$ by the map on thickening datums sending $V_\alpha$ to $V_\alpha\times[0,1]$ and $\lambda_\alpha$ to its obvious extension. Hence they induce the same virtual fundamental class (Lemma \ref{sameassubatlas}), so we may just write $[X]^\mathrm{vir}$ (dropping the subscript indicating which atlas we use). The same reasoning applies to $X'$.
nodes.statement_short: $A$ is a subatlas of the restriction of $\tilde A$, so both give the same class.

nodes.name: Cobordism invariance
nodes.statement: Now $\partial\tilde X=X\sqcup X'$, so we have $[X]^\mathrm{vir}=[X']^\mathrm{vir}$ as homology classes on $\tilde X$ (Lemmas \ref{disjointunionfc} and \ref{cobordismworks}). Hence we have: \begin{equation} [X]^\mathrm{vir}=[X']^\mathrm{vir} \end{equation} as elements of $H^{\dim B-\dim E}(B;\mathfrak o_B\otimes\mathfrak o_E^\vee)^\vee$.
nodes.statement_short: By additivity and cobordism invariance $[X]^\mathrm{vir}=[X']^\mathrm{vir}$.

nodes.name: Transverse case
nodes.statement: We know $X'=(X')^\mathrm{reg}$ (it is cut out transversally), so $X'$ is a closed smooth manifold and $[X']^\mathrm{vir}=[X']$ (Lemma \ref{fclasstransverse}). But now $[X']=e_c(E,s)\cap[B]$ by elementary Poincar\'e duality.
nodes.statement_short: In the transverse case the virtual class is the fundamental class, equal to $e_c(E,s)\cap[B]$.

nodes.name: Part (i)
nodes.statement: Since $\mathfrak s\prec\mathfrak t$, we have $M^\mathfrak s\subseteq M^{<\mathfrak t}=\partial M^{\leq\mathfrak t}$, giving (\ref{inbdry}).
nodes.statement_short: Part (i) from the definition of cell-like.

nodes.name: Invariance of domain
nodes.statement: Recall Brouwer's ``invariance of domain'', which implies that if a subset $X\subseteq\mathbb R^n$ is (in the subspace topology) locally homeomorphic to $\mathbb R^m$, then $m\leq n$, with equality iff $X$ is open. This immediately gives (\ref{toplessdim}), (\ref{topopen}).
nodes.statement_short: Recall invariance of domain, giving parts (ii) and (iii).

nodes.name: Part (iv)
nodes.statement: We prove (\ref{bdrystratumstruct}). Fix $p\in M^\mathfrak s$. A neighborhood of $p$ is covered by strata $\succ\mathfrak s$, so since $M^\mathfrak s\subseteq M$ is not open, there exists a stratum $\mathfrak t\succ\mathfrak s$. Now $M^\mathfrak s\subseteq\partial M^{\leq\mathfrak t}$ is open by (\ref{topopen}) (applied to $M^{<\mathfrak t}\to\mathcal S^{<\mathfrak t}$). A doubling argument (and invariance of domain) near $p\in\partial M$ shows that $M^s\cup M^\mathfrak t$ contains a neighborhood of $p$. Since we have exhausted a neighborhood of $p\in M^\mathfrak s$, it follows using (\ref{inbdry}) that there is no other stratum $\succ\mathfrak s$.
nodes.statement_short: Boundary codimension-one strata: doubling and invariance of domain show exactly one adjacent top stratum.

nodes.name: Part (v)
nodes.statement: We prove (\ref{intstratumstruct}). Fix $p\in M^\mathfrak s$. A neighborhood of $p$ is covered by strata $\succ\mathfrak s$, so since $M^\mathfrak s\subseteq M$ is not open, there exists a stratum $\mathfrak t\succ\mathfrak s$. Now $M^\mathfrak s\subseteq\partial M^{\leq\mathfrak t}$ is open by (\ref{topopen}), as is $M^\mathfrak t\subseteq M$. This gives a collar on one side of $M^\mathfrak s\subseteq M$. This still does not fill out a neighborhood of $p$, so there exists $\mathfrak t'\ne\mathfrak t$ with $\mathfrak t'\succ\mathfrak s$, giving a collar on the other side of $M^\mathfrak s\subseteq M$. Now by invariance of domain, we have thus exhausted a neighborhood of $p\in M^\mathfrak s$ inside $M$, and hence it follows using (\ref{inbdry}) that there are no more strata $\succ\mathfrak s$ other than $\mathfrak t,\mathfrak t'$.
nodes.statement_short: Interior codimension-one strata: collars on both sides from exactly two adjacent strata.

nodes.name: Reduce to stalks
nodes.statement: To see that \eqref{stratchainstousual} is a quasi-isomorphism, observe that it is the map on global sections of a corresponding map of complexes of $\mathcal K$-presheaves $C_\bullet(M,M\setminus K;\mathcal S)\to C_\bullet(M,M\setminus K)$ on the one-point compactification $M_+$ of $M$. Both are homotopy $\mathcal K$-sheaves by Lemma \ref{singularchainshomotopyKsheaf}. Thus by Corollary \ref{homotopysheafcheckqionstalks}, it suffices to show that the map $C_\bullet(M,M\setminus p;\mathcal S)\to C_\bullet(M,M\setminus p)$ is a quasi-isomorphism for every $p\in M$.
nodes.statement_short: Sheafify over $M_+$ and reduce to stalks.

nodes.name: Local homology is $\mathbb Z$
nodes.statement: This holds by the following local argument. Note that $H_\bullet(M,M\setminus p;\mathcal S)$ is isomorphic to $\mathbb Z$ (to see this, consider the filtration by $\dim\mathfrak s$), so it suffices to construct a cycle in $C_\bullet(M,M\setminus p;\mathcal S)$ representing a generator of $\mathbb Z$ and show that its image in $H_\bullet(M,M\setminus p)=\mathbb Z$ is a generator.
nodes.statement_short: Local stratified homology is $\mathbb Z$; it suffices to map a generator to a generator.

nodes.name: Construct generating cycle
nodes.statement: Such a cycle may be constructed by induction on $\mathcal S$ (starting from the stratum containing $p$ and going up), and its image in $H_\bullet(M,M\setminus p)$ generates since its degree at $p$ coincides with its degree at any nearby point in an open stratum, which is one by construction. A similar argument appears in Barraud--Cornea \cite[p670, Lemma 2.2]{barraudcornea}.
nodes.statement_short: Build the cycle inductively up the strata; its degree is one by comparison with an open stratum.

nodes.name: Homotopy sheaf by filtration
nodes.statement: Filter $C^\bullet_\mathrm{vir}(-,\mathcal S;A)$ by $\dim\mathfrak s$; the associated graded of this filtration is the direct sum of $C^\bullet_\mathrm{vir}(-\cap X^{\leq\mathfrak s}\operatorname{rel}\partial;A)$. Each these is a homotopy $\mathcal K$-sheaf on $X$ (pushforward from $X^{\leq\mathfrak s}$ to $X$ preserves homotopy $\mathcal K$-sheaves by Definition \ref{pushforwardofHsheavesworks}), and hence $C^\bullet_\mathrm{vir}(-,\mathcal S;A)$ is also a homotopy $\mathcal K$-sheaf (Lemma \ref{associatedgradedhomotopysheaf}).
nodes.statement_short: Filtering by stratum dimension shows the stratified complex is a homotopy $\mathcal K$-sheaf.

nodes.name: Check on stalks
nodes.statement: Now the map \eqref{stratifiedtounstratifiedpushforward} is a map of homotopy $\mathcal K$-sheaves, so to check that it is a quasi-isomorphism, it suffices to check it is a quasi-isomorphism on stalks (Corollary \ref{homotopysheafcheckqionstalks}). For this, we may use the argument from Example \ref{stratifiedchainsremark} (adapted to the case with boundary) along with Lemma \ref{localdescofISO}. Moreover, this local construction also gives us the desired commutativity of the diagram of sheaves on $X$.
nodes.statement_short: Check quasi-isomorphism on stalks via the local argument of Example 6.2.9.

nodes.name: Product decomposition and cube
nodes.statement: Write $\mathfrak s_0$ in the form \eqref{SdataA}--\eqref{SdataB}. Then we have: \begin{equation} \mathcal S_\mathcal W(\sigma,p,q)^{\leq\mathfrak s_0}=\mathcal S_\mathcal W(\sigma|[j_{a_0}\ldots j_{a_1}],p_0,p_1)\times\cdots\times\mathcal S_\mathcal W(\sigma|[j_{a_{m-1}}\ldots j_{a_m}],p_{m-1},p_m) \end{equation} Now we consider the $m$-cubical diagram: \begin{equation} \bigotimes_{i=1}^m\left[\operatornamewithlimits{colim}_{\mathfrak s\in\partial\mathcal S_\mathcal W(\sigma|[j_{a_{i-1}}\ldots j_{a_i}],p_{i-1},p_i)}\mathcal W_\bullet(\sigma|[j_{a_{i-1}}\ldots j_{a_i}],p_{i-1},p_i,\mathfrak s)\rightarrowtail\mathcal W_\bullet(\sigma|[j_{a_{i-1}}\ldots j_{a_i}],p_{i-1},p_i)\right] \end{equation}
nodes.statement_short: Decompose the strata below $\mathfrak s_0$ as a product and form the $m$-cube of boundary maps.

nodes.name: Reduce to cubical cofibrations
nodes.statement: Now \eqref{generalizedboundaryinjective} is simply the map to the maximal vertex of the $m$-cube from the colimit over the $m$-cube minus the maximal vertex. This is a cofibration for any cubical diagram of the form $\bigotimes_{i=1}^m[A_i\rightarrowtail B_i]$ where each $A_i\rightarrowtail B_i$ is a cofibration.
nodes.statement_short: The map is the cube's colimit-to-top map, a cofibration for tensor cubes of cofibrations.

nodes.name: Split and compute cokernel
nodes.statement: To see this, write $B_i=A_i\oplus P_i$ where $P_i$ is projective, and then the map is obviously injective with cokernel $\bigotimes_{i=1}^mP_i$. A tensor product of projective modules is projective, as can be seen using either the tensor-hom adjunction or the fact that a module is projective iff it is a direct summand of a free module.
nodes.statement_short: Split each cofibration; the cokernel is a tensor product of projectives, hence projective.

nodes.name: Set up induction on $\#\mathcal T$
nodes.statement: Let us abbreviate $A_\mathfrak s:=\mathcal W_\bullet(\sigma,p,q,\mathfrak s)$. We proceed by induction on the cardinality of $\mathcal T$, the case $\mathcal T=\varnothing$ being clear. Using the fact that a composition of cofibrations is again a cofibration, it suffices to consider the case $(\mathcal S,\mathcal T)=(\mathcal S\setminus\mathfrak s_0,\mathcal S)$ where $\mathfrak s_0\in\mathcal S$ is a maximal element.
nodes.statement_short: Induct on $\#\mathcal T$ and reduce to adding one maximal element $\mathfrak s_0$.

nodes.name: Pushout of cofibrations
nodes.statement: Now $\operatornamewithlimits{colim}_{\mathfrak s\in\mathcal S}A_\mathfrak s$ is the colimit of the following diagram: \begin{equation} \begin{tikzcd}[row sep = tiny] &A_{\mathfrak s_0}\\ \smash{\displaystyle\operatornamewithlimits{colim}_{\begin{smallmatrix}\mathfrak s\in\mathcal S\cr\mathfrak s\prec\mathfrak s_0\end{smallmatrix}}}A_\mathfrak s\ar[tail]{ur}\ar[tail]{rd}\\ &\displaystyle\operatornamewithlimits{colim}_{\mathfrak s\in\mathcal S\setminus\mathfrak s_0}A_\mathfrak s \end{tikzcd} \end{equation} where the top arrow is a cofibration by Lemma \ref{cofibrantinjectivelemma} and the bottom arrow is a cofibration by the induction hypothesis.
nodes.statement_short: Express the colimit as a pushout whose arrows are cofibrations by Lemma 7.4.22 and induction.

nodes.name: Conclude cofibration
nodes.statement: It follows that $\operatornamewithlimits{colim}_{\mathfrak s\in\mathcal S\setminus\mathfrak s_0}A_\mathfrak s\to\operatornamewithlimits{colim}_{\mathfrak s\in\mathcal S}A_\mathfrak s$ is injective, with cokernel isomorphic to the cokernel of the top map above. Hence it is a cofibration as needed.
nodes.statement_short: The pushed-out map is injective with cofibrant cokernel.

nodes.name: Reduce to two factors
nodes.statement: Since the tensor product of projective modules is projective, we may use induction to reduce to the case $k=2$.
nodes.statement_short: Induct on the number of factors, reducing to $k=2$.

nodes.name: Apply K\"unneth
nodes.statement: Thus, we have two cofibrant complexes $A_\bullet$ and $B_\bullet$ with $H_iA_\bullet=H_iB_\bullet=0$ for $i<0$ and we would like to conclude that $H_i(A_\bullet\otimes B_\bullet)=0$ for $i<0$. This follows from the K\"unneth theorem, specifically in the form of \cite[p301, Theorem 9.16]{osborne} or \cite[p679, Theorem 10.81]{rotman} (both of which apply because $\operatorname{Tor}^i_\mathbb Z(\cdot,\cdot)=0$ for $i>1$).\footnote{If we were assuming $A_\bullet$ and $B_\bullet$ to be bounded below, then we could apply the K\"unneth spectral sequence $\bigoplus_{i+j=q}\operatorname{Tor}_p(H_iA_\bullet,H_jB_\bullet)\Rightarrow H_{p+q}(A_\bullet\otimes B_\bullet)$ (see \cite[p686, Theorem 10.90]{rotman}) to reach the desired conclusion without any assumptions on the ground ring.}
nodes.statement_short: Apply the K\"unneth theorem over $\mathbb Z$ to two connective cofibrant complexes.

nodes.name: Vanishing in negative degrees
nodes.statement: Let us abbreviate $A_\mathfrak s:=\mathcal W_\bullet(\sigma,p,q,\mathfrak s)$. Since $A_\mathfrak s$ is a tensor product of various $\mathcal W_\bullet(\sigma',p',q')$, it follows (using Lemma \ref{tensorproductvanishing}) that $H_iA_\mathfrak s$ for $i<0$, so the left hand side of \eqref{tocolimitsurjective} vanishes for $i<0$. Hence it remains just to show that \eqref{tocolimitsurjective} is surjective for $i\leq 0$.
nodes.statement_short: Lemma 7.4.25 gives vanishing of the left side for $i<0$; reduce to surjectivity.

nodes.name: Induction on $\#\mathcal S$
nodes.statement: We proceed by induction on the cardinality of $\mathcal S$, the case $\mathcal S=\varnothing$ being clear. Let $\mathfrak s_0\in\mathcal S$ be any maximal element. Now $\operatornamewithlimits{colim}_{\mathfrak s\in\mathcal S}A_\mathfrak s$ is the colimit of \eqref{colimitdiagrambuildup}; it follows that we have the following exact sequence: \begin{equation} 0\to\operatornamewithlimits{colim}_{\begin{smallmatrix}\mathfrak s\in\mathcal S\cr\mathfrak s\prec\mathfrak s_0\end{smallmatrix}}A_\mathfrak s\to A_{\mathfrak s_0}\oplus\operatornamewithlimits{colim}_{\mathfrak s\in\mathcal S\setminus\mathfrak s_0}A_\mathfrak s\to\operatornamewithlimits{colim}_{\mathfrak s\in\mathcal S}A_\mathfrak s\to 0 \end{equation}
nodes.statement_short: Induct on $\#\mathcal S$; adding a maximal element yields a short exact sequence of colimits.

nodes.name: Long exact sequence
nodes.statement: By the induction hypothesis, it suffices to show that the second map above is surjective on $H_i$ for $i\leq 0$. By the long exact sequence induced by \eqref{colimitSEScofibrant}, it suffices to show that $H_i\operatornamewithlimits{colim}_{\begin{smallmatrix}\mathfrak s\in\mathcal S\cr\mathfrak s\prec\mathfrak s_0\end{smallmatrix}}A_\mathfrak s=0$ for $i<0$. Now this follows from the induction hypothesis.
nodes.statement_short: Via the long exact sequence, reduce to vanishing of $H_{<0}$ of the smaller colimit, given by induction.

nodes.name: Universal coefficients
nodes.statement: By Lemma \ref{universalcoefficient}, we have: \begin{align} H^0\operatorname{Hom}(A_\bullet,\mathbb Z)&\xrightarrow\sim\operatorname{Hom}(H_0A_\bullet,\mathbb Z)\\ H^0\operatorname{Hom}(\tilde A_\bullet,\mathbb Z)&\twoheadrightarrow\operatorname{Hom}(H_0\tilde A_\bullet,\mathbb Z) \end{align}
nodes.statement_short: Universal coefficients give an isomorphism for $A$ and a surjection for $\tilde A$ in degree $0$.

nodes.name: Choose cocycle $\tilde f$
nodes.statement: Let $f:A_0\to\mathbb Z$ denote the vertical map in the first diagram. Using the surjectivity of \eqref{tildesurj}, there exists a cocycle $\tilde f:\tilde A_0\to\mathbb Z$ giving the desired map on homology.
nodes.statement_short: Pick a cocycle $\tilde f$ on $\tilde A$ realizing the given map on homology.

nodes.name: Difference is a coboundary
nodes.statement: Denote by $i:A_\bullet\rightarrowtail\tilde A_\bullet$ the inclusion. Now by the commutativity of the second diagram, the difference $f-\tilde fi$ acts as zero on $H_0A_\bullet$. Since \eqref{notildeiso} is an isomorphism, this difference is thus a coboundary $\delta g$ for some $g:A_{-1}\to\mathbb Z$.
nodes.statement_short: The difference $f-\tilde fi$ vanishes on $H_0$, hence is a coboundary $\delta g$.

nodes.name: Extend and correct
nodes.statement: Now extend $g$ to $\tilde g:\tilde A_{-1}\to\mathbb Z$ (using the fact that $A_{-1}\rightarrowtail\tilde A_{-1}$ splits) and let the dotted arrow be $\tilde f+\delta\tilde g$.
nodes.statement_short: Extend $g$ via the splitting and take $\tilde f+\delta\tilde g$.

nodes.name: Reformulate as extension problem
nodes.statement: It is equivalent to show that given any $f:\Delta^n\to Z_\bullet$ along with data (\ref{subatlaschoice})--(\ref{augmentationschoice}) over $\partial\Delta^n$, the data can be extended over $\Delta^n$. For ease of notation, let us rename $(f^\ast\mathcal X,f^\ast\mathcal A,f^\ast\omega)$ as $(\mathcal X,\mathcal A,\omega)$.
nodes.statement_short: Equivalent to extending the data over $\partial\Delta^n$ to $\Delta^n$.
nodes.section: 7.5 Resolution \texorpdfstring{$\tilde Z_\bullet\to Z_\bullet$}{tilde Z to Z}

nodes.name: Well-founded induction on triples
nodes.statement: We construct (\ref{subatlaschoice})--(\ref{augmentationschoice}) via $H$-equivariant induction on the set of triples $(\sigma,p,q)$, equipped with the partial order $\preceq_\mathcal X$ in which $(\sigma',p',q')\preceq_\mathcal X(\sigma,p,q)$ iff $(\sigma',p',q')$ appears as a ``factor'' of some element of $\mathcal S_\mathcal X(\sigma,p,q)$. This partial order is \emph{well-founded} (i.e.\ there is no strictly decreasing infinite sequence) since each $\mathcal S_\mathcal X(\sigma,p,q)$ is finite, and thus it is valid for induction. The induction works $H$-equivariantly since the action of $H$ on $\mathcal P$ is free, and $(\sigma,p,q)$ and $(\sigma,hp,hq)$ are always incomparable for $h\in H$ (so we may henceforth ignore the action of $H$). The inductive step is as follows.
nodes.statement_short: Construct the data by $H$-equivariant induction on the well-founded order on triples.
nodes.section: 7.5 Resolution \texorpdfstring{$\tilde Z_\bullet\to Z_\bullet$}{tilde Z to Z}

nodes.name: Choose subatlas and fundamental cycles
nodes.statement: \textbf{Choosing $\mathcal B(\sigma,p,q)$.}\ We must choose a finite $\bar\mathcal B(\sigma,p,q)\subseteq\bar\mathcal A(\sigma,p,q)$ so that the corresponding subatlas of $\mathcal A(\sigma,p,q)^{\geq\mathfrak s^\mathrm{top}}=\bar\mathcal A(\sigma,p,q)$ on $\mathcal X(\sigma,p,q)$ satisfies the covering axiom (and thus is an implicit atlas). This is possible by compactness. \textbf{Choosing $[E_\alpha]$.}\ Trivial.
nodes.statement_short: Choose a finite covering subatlas by compactness; fundamental cycles are trivial to choose.
nodes.section: 7.5 Resolution \texorpdfstring{$\tilde Z_\bullet\to Z_\bullet$}{tilde Z to Z}

nodes.name: Choose the augmentation $[[E]]$
nodes.statement: \textbf{Choosing $[[E]]_{\sigma,p,q}:QC_\bullet(E;\mathcal B)^+_\mathbb Z(\sigma,p,q)\to\mathbb Z$.}\ We need to construct $[[E]]_{\sigma,p,q}$ fitting into the following diagram: \begin{equation} \begin{tikzcd}[column sep = huge] \smash{\displaystyle\operatornamewithlimits{colim}_{\mathfrak s\in\partial\mathcal S_\mathcal X(\sigma,p,q)}}QC_\bullet(E;\mathcal B)^+_\mathbb Z(\sigma,p,q,\mathfrak s)\ar[tail]{r}{\text{product/face}}\ar{d}[swap]{[[E]]}&QC_\bullet(E;\mathcal B)^+_\mathbb Z(\sigma,p,q)\ar[dashed]{dl}{?\exists\,[[E]]_{\sigma,p,q}}\\ \mathbb Z\\ H_\bullet\smash{\displaystyle\operatornamewithlimits{colim}_{\mathfrak s\in\partial\mathcal S_\mathcal X(\sigma,p,q)}}QC_\bullet(E;\mathcal B)^+_\mathbb Z(\sigma,p,q,\mathfrak s)\ar{r}{\text{product/face}}\ar{d}[swap]{[[E]]}&H_\bullet QC_\bullet(E;\mathcal B)^+_\mathbb Z(\sigma,p,q)\ar{dl}{[E]\mapsto 1}\\ \mathbb Z \end{tikzcd} \end{equation} Since $QC_\bullet(E;\mathcal B)^+_\mathbb Z$ is cofibrant, it follows that the top horizontal map is a cofibration between cofibrant complexes (this uses Lemma \ref{cofibranthaslotsofcofibrations}). Now Lemma \ref{Hzeroofcofibrantcolimit} tells us that the direct sum of $H_0QC_\bullet(E;\mathcal B)^+_\mathbb Z(\sigma,p,q,\mathfrak s)$ surjects onto $H_0$ on the left, and this makes it easy to check that the second diagram commutes. Lemma \ref{Hzeroofcofibrantcolimit} also tells us that $H_{-1}$ on the left vanishes. Hence we may apply Lemma \ref{cocycleextendinglemma} to conclude the existence of a suitable $[[E]]_{\sigma,p,q}$.
nodes.statement_short: Extend $[[E]]$ along a cofibration using Lemmas 7.4.23, 7.4.26 and 7.4.30.
nodes.section: 7.5 Resolution \texorpdfstring{$\tilde Z_\bullet\to Z_\bullet$}{tilde Z to Z}

nodes.name: Choose $\lambda$ (key step)
nodes.statement: \textbf{Choosing $\lambda_{\sigma,p,q}$ (the key step).}\ According to Lemma \ref{mappingconechoiceboundary}, we may choose a $\lambda_{\sigma,p,q}$ with the required property iff the homology class of $\mu_{\sigma,p,q}\in H^\bullet_\mathrm{vir}(\partial\mathcal X;\mathcal B)^+(\sigma,p,q)$ coincides with $d\omega(\sigma,p,q)\in\check H^0(\partial\mathcal X(\sigma,p,q);\mathfrak o_{\partial\mathcal X(\sigma,p,q)})$. Let us now prove this desired statement $[\mu_{\sigma,p,q}]=d\omega(\sigma,p,q)$. Let us fix $\mathfrak r_0\in\partial\mathcal S_\mathcal X(\sigma,p,q)$ and verify equality over $\mathcal X(\sigma,p,q)^{\mathfrak r_0}$ (this is clearly enough). We consider the following diagram: \begin{align} \mu_{\sigma,p,q}\in&&&C_\mathrm{vir}^\bullet(\partial\mathcal X;\mathcal B)^+(\sigma,p,q)\\ &&&\qquad\uparrow\cr \bigoplus_{\mathfrak r\in\partial\mathcal S_\mathcal X(\sigma,p,q)}\mu_{\sigma,p,q,\mathfrak r}\in&&\bigoplus_{\mathfrak r\in\partial\mathcal S_\mathcal X(\sigma,p,q)}\operatornamewithlimits{hocolim}_{\mathfrak s\prec\mathfrak t\in\mathcal S_\mathcal X(\sigma,p,q)^{\leq\mathfrak r}}&C_\mathrm{vir}^\bullet(\mathcal X(\sigma,p,q)^{\leq\mathfrak s}\operatorname{rel}\partial;\mathcal B(\sigma,p,q)^{\geq\mathfrak t})\\ &&&\qquad\downarrow\cr \bigoplus_{\mathfrak r\in\partial\mathcal S_\mathcal X(\sigma,p,q)^{\leq\mathfrak r_0}}\mu_{\sigma,p,q,\mathfrak r}\in&&\bigoplus_{\mathfrak r\in\partial\mathcal S_\mathcal X(\sigma,p,q)^{\leq\mathfrak r_0}}\operatornamewithlimits{hocolim}_{\mathfrak s\prec\mathfrak t\in\mathcal S_\mathcal X(\sigma,p,q)^{\leq\mathfrak r}}&C_\mathrm{vir}^\bullet(\mathcal X(\sigma,p,q)^{\leq\mathfrak s}\operatorname{rel}\partial;\mathcal B(\sigma,p,q)^{\geq\mathfrak t})\\ &&&\qquad\uparrow\cr \mu_{\sigma,p,q,\mathfrak r_0}\in&&\operatornamewithlimits{hocolim}_{\mathfrak s\prec\mathfrak t\in\mathcal S_\mathcal X(\sigma,p,q)^{\leq\mathfrak r_0}}&C_\mathrm{vir}^\bullet(\mathcal X(\sigma,p,q)^{\leq\mathfrak s}\operatorname{rel}\partial;\mathcal B(\sigma,p,q)^{\geq\mathfrak t}) \end{align} The differentials in \eqref{muallstrat}--\eqref{musomestrat} are given by the sum over $\operatorname{codim}(\mathfrak r\preceq\mathfrak r')=1$ of the obvious pushforward maps (plus the internal differentials of each $\operatornamewithlimits{hocolim}$). The first vertical map is the sum over $\operatorname{codim}\mathfrak r=0$ (i.e.\ over maximal elements of $\partial\mathcal S_\mathcal X(\sigma,p,q)$); clearly this is a chain map. The remaining vertical maps are clear. The easiest way to keep track of signs in the present discussion is to use the orientation lines associated to elements of $\mathcal S_\mathcal X(\sigma,p,q)$, as in Definition \ref{stratifiedvirtualdef}, though we will supress them from the notation. Note that there is a natural diagram of complexes of $\mathcal K$-presheaves on $\partial\mathcal X(\sigma,p,q)$ whose diagram of global sections is \eqref{mucareabout}--\eqref{muonestratum}. We will see below that these complexes of $\mathcal K$-presheaves are in fact pure homotopy $\mathcal K$-sheaves and that the induced diagram of sheaves (obtained by taking $H^0$) is given by the tautological maps: \begin{equation} \mathfrak o_{\partial\mathcal X(\sigma,p,q)}\leftarrow\mathfrak o_{\partial\mathcal X(\sigma,p,q)}\to\mathfrak o_{\mathcal X(\sigma,p,q)^{\leq\mathfrak r_0}}\leftarrow\mathfrak o_{\mathcal X(\sigma,p,q)^{\leq\mathfrak r_0}\operatorname{rel}\partial} \end{equation} First, though, let us argue that this claim implies the desired result. The cycle $\mu_{\sigma,p,q}\in\eqref{mucareabout}$ lifts to a cycle $\bigoplus_{\mathfrak r\in\partial\mathcal S_\mathcal X(\sigma,p,q)}\mu_{\sigma,p,q,\mathfrak r}\in\eqref{muallstrat}$, where $\mu_{\sigma,p,q,\mathfrak r}$ is obtained by applying the product/face maps to the tensor product of the various $\lambda$'s corresponding to the factors on the left hand side of \eqref{Wtotalcomposition} corresponding to $\mathfrak r$ (this is a cycle by \eqref{lambdamaster}). Obviously $\bigoplus_{\mathfrak r\in\partial\mathcal S_\mathcal X(\sigma,p,q)}\mu_{\sigma,p,q,\mathfrak r}\in\eqref{muallstrat}$ maps to $\bigoplus_{\mathfrak r\in\partial\mathcal S_\mathcal X(\sigma,p,q)^{\leq\mathfrak r_0}}\mu_{\sigma,p,q,\mathfrak r}\in\eqref{musomestrat}$. On sections over $K\subseteq\mathcal X(\sigma,p,q)^{\mathfrak r_0}$, the last vertical map is an isomorphism, and (the restriction to $K$ of) $\bigoplus_{\mathfrak r\in\partial\mathcal S_\mathcal X(\sigma,p,q)^{\leq\mathfrak r_0}}\mu_{\sigma,p,q,\mathfrak r}\in\eqref{musomestrat}$ lifts to (the restriction to $K$ of) $\mu_{\sigma,p,q,\mathfrak r_0}\in\eqref{muonestratum}$. Finally, observe that over any $K\subseteq\mathcal X(\sigma,p,q)^{\mathfrak r_0}$, the homology class of $\mu_{\sigma,p,q,\mathfrak r_0}\in\eqref{muonestratum}$ coincides with the restriction of $d\omega(\sigma,p,q)$ to the $\mathfrak r_0$ stratum (this follows from the induction hypothesis, using the fact that the orientations are coherent and the observation at the end of Definition \ref{productatlasF}). Clearly this implies that $\mu_{\sigma,p,q}$ coincides with $d\omega(\sigma,p,q)$ in homology over $\mathcal X(\sigma,p,q)^{\mathfrak r_0}$. Thus it remains only to show that \eqref{mucareabout}--\eqref{muonestratum} are pure homotopy $\mathcal K$-sheaves and that the induced maps on $H^0$ coincide with the tautological maps on orientation sheaves \eqref{orientationdiagramforHFbdry}. Note that by Proposition \ref{stratifiedispurehomotopysheaf}, the following closely related diagram satisfies all of the desired properties (i.e.\ is a diagram of pure homotopy $\mathcal K$-sheaves inducing \eqref{orientationdiagramforHFbdry} on $H^0$): \begin{align} &C_\mathrm{vir}^\bullet(\partial\mathcal X(\sigma,p,q);\mathcal B(\sigma,p,q)^{\geq\mathfrak s^\mathrm{top}})\\ &\qquad\uparrow\cr \bigoplus_{\mathfrak r\in\partial\mathcal S_\mathcal X(\sigma,p,q)}&C_\mathrm{vir}^\bullet(\mathcal X(\sigma,p,q)^{\leq\mathfrak r}\operatorname{rel}\partial;\mathcal B(\sigma,p,q)^{\geq\mathfrak s^\mathrm{top}})\\ &\qquad\downarrow\cr \bigoplus_{\mathfrak r\in\partial\mathcal S_\mathcal X(\sigma,p,q)^{\leq\mathfrak r_0}}&C_\mathrm{vir}^\bullet(\mathcal X(\sigma,p,q)^{\leq\mathfrak r}\operatorname{rel}\partial;\mathcal B(\sigma,p,q)^{\geq\mathfrak s^\mathrm{top}})\\ &\qquad\uparrow\cr &C_\mathrm{vir}^\bullet(\mathcal X(\sigma,p,q)^{\leq\mathfrak r_0}\operatorname{rel}\partial;\mathcal B(\sigma,p,q)^{\geq\mathfrak s^\mathrm{top}}) \end{align} Hence it is enough to relate this diagram to \eqref{mucareabout}--\eqref{muonestratum} via quasi-isomorphisms. The diagram obtained from \eqref{mucareabout}--\eqref{muonestratum} by replacing every occurence of $\mathcal B(\sigma,p,q)^{\geq\mathfrak t}$ with $\mathcal B(\sigma,p,q)^{\geq\mathfrak s^\mathrm{top}}$ maps quasi-isomorphically to \eqref{mucareabout}--\eqref{muonestratum} (by pairing with the fixed fundamental cycles), and it also maps quasi-isomorphically to the diagram above (use the obvious pushforwards on the $p=0$ level of the homotopy colimits, and zero for $p>0$), thus giving the desired result.
nodes.statement_short: Show $[\mu_{\sigma,p,q}]=d\omega(\sigma,p,q)$ so that $\lambda$ can be chosen.
