nodes.statement: Now since $u_0$ is smooth, it and all its derivatives decay exponentially in any cylindrical end $[0,\infty)\times S^1$ (since every end is holomorphically conjugate to the map $[0,\infty)\times S^1\to D^2$ given by $z=e^{-s-it}$). Precisely, we have the following pointwise bound over $[S-1,S]$: \begin{equation} \left|D^ju_0(s,t)\right|\leq c_je^{-S} \end{equation} (derivatives with respect to $s$ and $t$).
nodes.statement_short: Derivatives of u_0 are O(e^{-S}) on [S-1,S].

nodes.name: Weighted bound
nodes.statement: It follows from the definition of $u_\alpha$ that the same bound holds for $u_\alpha$. Thus the contribution of $[S-1,S]$ to the norm of $\bar\partial_yu_\alpha$ is bounded by a constant times $e^{S\delta}e^{-S}$.
nodes.statement_short: Same bound for u_alpha; weight gives e^{S delta} e^{-S}.

nodes.name: Away from necks
nodes.statement: Away from the ends/necks, the norm is bounded by $c\cdot\left|y\right|\left\|\kappa\right\|$. In the ends, the expression is zero. In the necks, argue as follows.
nodes.statement_short: Bound by |y| ||kappa|| away from necks; zero in ends.

nodes.name: Neck estimate
nodes.statement: The expression is only nonzero over $[S-1,S+1]\cup[5S-1,5S+1]$; by symmetry we may just work over $[S-1,S+1]$. Then since $u_0$ and $\kappa$ are smooth, we have (by the same reasoning used to justify \eqref{uzeroexponentialdecay}) the following pointwise bound over $[S-1,S+1]$: \begin{equation} \left|D^j\kappa_\alpha(s,t)\right|\leq c_je^{-S}\left\|\kappa\right\| \end{equation} (derivatives with respect to $s$ and $t$, in local coordinates \eqref{localPTcoords}). Thus the overall contribution of $[S-1,S+1]$ to the total norm of the expression is bounded by a constant times $e^{S\delta}e^{-S}\left\|\kappa\right\|$.
nodes.statement_short: Exponential decay of kappa gives the weighted bound.

nodes.name: Reduce to operator norm bound
nodes.statement: In simpler terms, we bound the operator norm of the difference between the two diagonal compositions: \begin{equation} \left\|\mathsf{PT}\circ D_{0,y}-D_{0|\alpha,y}\circ\mathsf{PT}\right\|\leq c\cdot\sum_{i=1}^de^{-S_i} \end{equation} (this trivially implies the claimed statement).
nodes.statement_short: Suffices to bound ||PT D_{0,y} - D_{0|alpha,y} PT||.

nodes.name: Use exponential decay
nodes.statement: To show \eqref{betterPTcommutingoperatornormbound}, observe that the two operators only differ over the $[S-1,\infty)$ subset of each end $[0,\infty)\times S^1\subseteq C_0$. Using estimates \eqref{uzeroexponentialdecay} arising from the fact that $u_0$ is smooth, we obtain the desired bound.
nodes.statement_short: Operators differ only on [S-1,infty) where u_0 decays.

nodes.name: Localize error
nodes.statement: The difference $DG\xi-\eta$ is only nonzero in the necks over $s\in[2S,2S+1]$ and $s\in[4S-1,4S]$. By symmetry, we may just do the bound over $s\in[4S-1,4S]$.
nodes.statement_short: Error supported on cutoff intervals; by symmetry treat [4S-1,4S].

nodes.name: Weight ratio
nodes.statement: Over this region, one calculates that the norm of the difference is bounded as claimed. The factor of $e^{-2\delta S}$ comes as the ratio between the $e^{2\delta S}$ weight given to $[4S-1,4S]\times S^1\subseteq[0,6S]\times S^1\subseteq C_\alpha$ and the $e^{4\delta S}$ weight given to $[4S-1,4S]\times S^1\subseteq[0,\infty)\times S^1\subseteq C_0$.
nodes.statement_short: The factor e^{-2 delta S} is the ratio of the weights.

nodes.name: Base case and bottom square estimate
nodes.statement: We work by induction on $n$. The case $n=1$ is clear: $\epsilon(1,c,\delta)=\infty$. Now assume $n\geq 2$. Let us also assume without loss of generality that $c\geq 1$. Applying \eqref{keytocheckforARI} to $i=n$ and $\xi=Q_nB_{n-1}\eta$, we see that: \begin{equation} \left\|D_{n-1}G_{n-1}Q_nB_{n-1}-\mathbf 1_{Y_{n-1}}\right\|\leq\epsilon\cdot\left\|Q_n\right\|\left\|B_{n-1}\right\|\leq\epsilon c^2 \end{equation}
nodes.statement_short: Base case n=1 is trivial; for n>=2 apply the hypothesis with i=n to Q_n B_{n-1} eta.

nodes.name: Construct Q_{n-1}
nodes.statement: Let us require that $\epsilon\leq\frac 12c^{-2}$, so the above bound is $\leq\frac 12$. Then by Lemma \ref{bootstrapinverse} applied to $T=G_{n-1}Q_nB_{n-1}$, we see that there exists $Q_{n-1}$ with $D_{n-1}Q_{n-1}=\mathbf 1_{Y_{n-1}}$ and: \begin{equation} \left\|Q_{n-1}\right\|\leq 2c^3\qquad\left\|Q_{n-1}-G_{n-1}Q_nB_{n-1}\right\|\leq 2\epsilon c^5 \end{equation}
nodes.statement_short: Neumann series lemma gives a right inverse Q_{n-1} near G Q_n B.

nodes.name: Compare compositions
nodes.statement: Now we see that: \begin{multline} \left\|D_1G_1\cdots G_{n-2}G_{n-1}Q_nB_{n-1}B_{n-2}\cdots B_1-D_1G_1\cdots G_{n-2}Q_{n-1}B_{n-2}\cdots B_1\right\|\\ \leq c^{2n-3}\left\|G_{n-1}Q_nB_{n-1}-Q_{n-1}\right\|\leq 2\epsilon c^{2n+2} \end{multline}
nodes.statement_short: Replacing G Q_n B by Q_{n-1} changes the composition by O(epsilon).

nodes.name: Apply induction hypothesis
nodes.statement: Let us require that $\epsilon\leq\frac 14\delta c^{-2n-2}$, so the above bound is $\leq\frac 12\delta$. Let us also require that $\epsilon\leq\epsilon(n-1,2c^3,\frac 12\delta)$ (which exists by the induction hypothesis), so that: \begin{equation} \left\|D_1G_1\cdots G_{n-2}Q_{n-1}B_{n-2}\cdots B_1-\mathbf 1_{Y_1}\right\|\leq\frac 12\delta \end{equation}
nodes.statement_short: Shorter chain with Q_{n-1} gives error delta/2.

nodes.name: Combine
nodes.statement: Combining \eqref{approxclosetogiven} and \eqref{inductionbound}, we get the desired bound \eqref{approxbootstrappingworks}.
nodes.statement_short: Triangle inequality.

nodes.name: Bound and approximate inverse
nodes.statement: It is easy to see that all the maps in \eqref{biginversediagram} are uniformly bounded. Hence $\left\|T_{\alpha,y}\right\|\leq c$ as $(\alpha,y)\to 0$. Now Lemma \ref{bootstrappingapprox} combined with Lemmas \ref{approxbottom}, \ref{approxmiddle}, \ref{approxtop} show that for $(\alpha,y)\to 0$, we have $\left\|D_{\alpha,y} T_{\alpha,y}-\mathbf 1\right\|\to 0$.
nodes.statement_short: Uniform bounds and Lemma B.7.17 with Lemmas B.7.13-15.

nodes.name: Image condition
nodes.statement: We observed earlier that $\operatorname{im} T_{\alpha,y}\subseteq\ker L_\alpha$.
nodes.statement_short: Recall im T in ker L_alpha.

nodes.name: Reference and domain
nodes.statement: This is similar to McDuff--Salamon \cite[p68, Proposition 3.5.3]{mcduffsalamonJholsymp}. We have already remarked that $\mathcal F_{\alpha,y}\xi$ is defined for $\left\|\xi\right\|_{k,2,\delta}\leq c'$.
nodes.statement_short: Similar to McDuff-Salamon Prop. 3.5.3; F is defined on a ball.

nodes.name: Reduce to Lipschitz derivative
nodes.statement: Let $\mathcal F_{\alpha,y}'(\zeta,\xi)$ denote the derivative of $\mathcal F_{\alpha,y}$ at $\zeta$ applied to $\xi$. So, for instance, $D_{\alpha,y}(\xi):=\mathcal F_{\alpha,y}'(0,\xi)$. It suffices to show that: \begin{equation} \left\|\mathcal F_{\alpha,y}'(0,\xi)-\mathcal F_{\alpha,y}'(\zeta,\xi)\right\|_{k-1,2,\delta}\leq c\cdot\left\|\zeta\right\|_{k,2,\delta}\left\|\xi\right\|_{k,2,\delta} \end{equation} for $\left\|\zeta\right\|_{k,2,\delta}\leq c'$ uniformly as $(\alpha,y)\to 0$ (one recovers \eqref{quadestgoal} by integrating $\int_{\xi_1}^{\xi_2}\mathcal F_{\alpha,y}'(0,d\zeta)-\mathcal F_{\alpha,y}'(\zeta,d\zeta)$).
nodes.statement_short: Suffices to bound F'(0,xi) - F'(zeta,xi).

nodes.name: Sections based at exp(zeta)
nodes.statement: For $\zeta\in W^{k,2,\delta}(C_\alpha,u_\alpha^\ast TX)_D\oplus E$, let: \begin{equation} \mathcal F_{\alpha,y,\zeta}:W^{k,2,\delta}(C_\alpha,(\exp_{u_\alpha}\zeta)^\ast TX)_D\oplus E\to W^{k-1,2,\delta}(\tilde C_\alpha,\Omega^{0,1}_{\tilde C_\alpha,j_y}\otimes_\mathbb C(\exp_{u_\alpha}\zeta)^\ast TX) \end{equation} denote the $\bar\partial$-section based at $\exp_{u_\alpha}\zeta:C_\alpha\to X$ and $e_0+\operatorname{proj}_E\zeta$ (so, for example, $\mathcal F_{\alpha,y}:=\mathcal F_{\alpha,y,0}$). Let: \begin{equation} D_{\alpha,y,\zeta}:W^{k,2,\delta}(C_\alpha,(\exp_{u_\alpha}\zeta)^\ast TX)_D\oplus E\to W^{k-1,2,\delta}(\tilde C_\alpha,\Omega^{0,1}_{\tilde C_\alpha,j_y}\otimes_\mathbb C(\exp_{u_\alpha}\zeta)^\ast TX) \end{equation} denote the derivative of $\mathcal F_{\alpha,y,\zeta}$ at zero. Of course, $D_{\alpha,y,\zeta}$ may be calculated as in Lemma \ref{linearizedformula}, and the result is the same (i.e.\ we just substitute $(\exp_{u_\alpha}\zeta,e_0+\operatorname{proj}_E\zeta)$ in place of $(u_\alpha,e_0)$).
nodes.statement_short: Define F_{alpha,y,zeta} and its linearization D_{alpha,y,zeta}.

nodes.name: Change of base point
nodes.statement: Now the first step in proving \eqref{derivislip} is to express $\mathcal F_{\alpha,y}'(\zeta,\xi)$ in terms of $D_{\alpha,y,\zeta}$. To do this, we observe that: \begin{equation} \mathcal F_{\alpha,y}(a)=\left[\mathsf{PT}_{\exp_{u_\alpha}a\to u_\alpha}\circ\mathsf{PT}_{\exp_{u_\alpha}\zeta\to\exp_{u_\alpha}a}\right]\left[\mathcal F_{\alpha,y,\zeta}\Bigl((\exp_{\exp_{u_\alpha}\zeta}^{-1}\exp_{u_\alpha}a)\oplus(\operatorname{proj}_Ea-\operatorname{proj}_E\zeta)\Bigr)\right] \end{equation} We now differentiate with respect to $a$ and evaluate at $a=\zeta$ and $\dot a=\xi$. We find: \begin{multline} \mathcal F_{\alpha,y}'(\zeta,\xi)=\Biggl[\frac d{da}\biggr|_{\begin{smallmatrix}a=\zeta\cr\dot a=\xi\end{smallmatrix}}\Bigl(\mathsf{PT}_{\exp_{u_\alpha}a\to u_\alpha}\circ\mathsf{PT}_{\exp_{u_\alpha}\zeta\to\exp_{u_\alpha}a}\Bigr)\Biggr]\bigl(\mathcal F_{\alpha,y,\zeta}(0)\bigr)\\ +\mathsf{PT}_{\exp_{u_\alpha}\zeta\to u_\alpha}\Biggl[D_{\alpha,y,\zeta}\Biggl(\frac d{da}\biggr|_{\begin{smallmatrix}a=\zeta\cr\dot a=\xi\end{smallmatrix}}\Bigl(\exp_{\exp_{u_\alpha}\zeta}^{-1}\exp_{u_\alpha}a\Bigr)\oplus\operatorname{proj}_E\xi\Biggr)\Biggr] \end{multline}
nodes.statement_short: Express F'(zeta,xi) in terms of D_{alpha,y,zeta}.

nodes.name: First term is quadratic
nodes.statement: We rewrite the first term: \begin{equation} \Biggl[\frac d{da}\biggr|_{\begin{smallmatrix}a=\zeta\cr\dot a=\xi\end{smallmatrix}}\Bigl(\mathsf{PT}_{\exp_{u_\alpha}a\to u_\alpha}\circ\mathsf{PT}_{\exp_{u_\alpha}\zeta\to\exp_{u_\alpha}a}\Bigr)\Biggr]\mathsf{PT}_{u_\alpha\to\exp_{u_\alpha}\zeta}\bigl(\mathcal F_{\alpha,y}(\zeta)\bigr) \end{equation} We know that $\left\|\mathcal F_{\alpha,y}(\zeta)\right\|_{k-1,2,\delta}$ is bounded uniformly for $(\alpha,y)\to 0$ and $\left\|\zeta\right\|_{k,2,\delta}\leq c'$ (Lemma \ref{mappregluingissmall} implies that $\left\|\mathcal F_{\alpha,y}(0)\right\|_{k-1,2,\delta}$ is bounded as $(\alpha,y)\to 0$, and from this one may derive a bound on $\left\|\mathcal F_{\alpha,y}(\zeta)\right\|_{k-1,2,\delta}$ in terms of $\left\|\zeta\right\|_{k,2,\delta}$). The operator $[\frac d{da}(\mathsf{PT}\circ\mathsf{PT})]\mathsf{PT}$ in front is of the form $H(\zeta,\xi)$ for a smooth (non-linear) bundle map $H:TX\oplus TX\to\operatorname{End}(TX)$ (defined in a neighborhood of $\zeta=\xi=0$). Since $H$ satisfies $H(0,\cdot)=H(\cdot,0)=0$, it follows that $\left\|H(\zeta,\xi)\right\|_{k,2,\delta}$ is bounded by $c\cdot\left\|\zeta\right\|_{k,2,\delta}\left\|\xi\right\|_{k,2,\delta}$ for $\left\|\zeta\right\|_{k,2,\delta},\left\|\xi\right\|_{k,2,\delta}\leq c'$. Hence the $\left\|\cdot\right\|_{k-1,2,\delta}$-norm of the first term in \eqref{changebasisderivative} is bounded by $c\cdot\left\|\zeta\right\|_{k,2,\delta}\left\|\xi\right\|_{k,2,\delta}$, so for the purposes of proving \eqref{derivislip} it may be ignored.
nodes.statement_short: Bundle map vanishing on axes gives bound c||zeta|| ||xi||.

nodes.name: Second term error
nodes.statement: The second term in \eqref{changebasisderivative} is approximated by $\mathsf{PT}_{\exp_{u_\alpha}\zeta\to u_\alpha}\left[D_{\alpha,y,\zeta}\left(\mathsf{PT}_{u_\alpha\to\exp_{u_\alpha}\zeta}\xi\right)\right]$ with error: \begin{equation} \mathsf{PT}_{\exp_{u_\alpha}\zeta\to u_\alpha}\Biggl[D_{\alpha,y,\zeta}\Biggl(\biggl[\mathsf{PT}_{u_\alpha\to\exp_{u_\alpha}\zeta}\xi-\frac d{da}\biggr|_{\begin{smallmatrix}a=\zeta\cr\dot a=\xi\end{smallmatrix}}\Bigl(\exp_{\exp_{u_\alpha}\zeta}^{-1}\exp_{u_\alpha}a\Bigr)\biggr]\oplus 0\Biggr)\Biggr] \end{equation} which we may write as: \begin{equation} \mathsf{PT}_{\exp_{u_\alpha}\zeta\to u_\alpha}\Biggl[D_{\alpha,y,\zeta}\Biggl(\mathsf{PT}_{u_\alpha\to\exp_{u_\alpha}\zeta}\biggl[\xi-\mathsf{PT}_{\exp_{u_\alpha}\zeta\to u_\alpha}\frac d{da}\biggr|_{\begin{smallmatrix}a=\zeta\cr\dot a=\xi\end{smallmatrix}}\Bigl(\exp_{\exp_{u_\alpha}\zeta}^{-1}\exp_{u_\alpha}a\Bigr)\biggr]\oplus 0\Biggr)\Biggr] \end{equation} Now the $\left\|\cdot\right\|_{(k-1,2,\delta)\to(k-1,2,\delta)}$ norm of the outer $\mathsf{PT}$ is bounded uniformly for $(\alpha,y)\to 0$ and $\left\|\zeta\right\|_{k,2,\delta}\leq c'$, as is the $\left\|\cdot\right\|_{(k,2,\delta)\to(k-1,2,\delta)}$ norm of $D_{\alpha,y,\zeta}$ and the $\left\|\cdot\right\|_{(k,2,\delta)\to(k,2,\delta)}$ norm of the following $\mathsf{PT}$. The difference $\xi-\mathsf{PT}\frac d{da}()$ is of the form $H(\zeta,\xi)$ for a smooth (non-linear) bundle map $H:TX\oplus TX\to TX$ (defined in a neighborhood of $\zeta=\xi=0$). Since $H$ satisfies $H(0,\cdot)=H(\cdot,0)=0$, it follows that $\left\|H(\zeta,\xi)\right\|_{k,2,\delta}$ is bounded by $c\cdot\left\|\zeta\right\|_{k,2,\delta}\left\|\xi\right\|_{k,2,\delta}$ for $\left\|\zeta\right\|_{k,2,\delta},\left\|\xi\right\|_{k,2,\delta}\leq c'$. Hence the error \eqref{errorexpression} has $\left\|\cdot\right\|_{k-1,2,\delta}$ bounded by
nodes.statement_short: The error in replacing the derivative of exp^{-1} by PT is quadratic.

nodes.name: Term-by-term comparison
nodes.statement: Thus we have reduced the estimate \eqref{derivislip} to proving: \begin{equation} \left\|D_{\alpha,y}-\mathsf{PT}_{\exp_{u_\alpha}\zeta\to u}\circ D_{\alpha,y,\zeta}\circ\mathsf{PT}_{u_\alpha\to\exp_{u_\alpha}\zeta}\right\|_{(k,2,\delta)\to(k-1,2,\delta)}\leq c\cdot\left\|\zeta\right\|_{k,2,\delta} \end{equation} We calculated $D_{\alpha,y}$ in Lemma \ref{linearizedformula}, and $D_{\alpha,y,\zeta}$ may be expressed in exactly the same way (specifically, it is obtained by taking the expression for $D_{\alpha,y}$ and replacing every occurence of $u_\alpha$ with $\exp_{u_\alpha}\zeta$ and $e_0$ by $e_0+\operatorname{proj}_E\zeta$). Now we compare term by term to prove \eqref{quadreducedtoPTcomp}. We omit the details of this calculation.
nodes.statement_short: Reduced to comparing D_{alpha,y} with transported D_{alpha,y,zeta}; details omitted.

nodes.name: First assertion
nodes.statement: The first assertion has been shown earlier.
nodes.statement_short: Already shown.

nodes.name: Contraction estimate
nodes.statement: For the second, write: \begin{multline} \left\|(\xi_1-\xi_2)-(Q_{\alpha,y}\mathcal F_{\alpha,y}\xi_1-Q_{\alpha,y}\mathcal F_{\alpha,y}\xi_2)\right\|_{k,2,\delta}\\ =\left\|Q_{\alpha,y}D_{\alpha,y}(\xi_1-\xi_2)-(Q_{\alpha,y}\mathcal F_{\alpha,y}\xi_1-Q_{\alpha,y}\mathcal F_{\alpha,y}\xi_2)\right\|_{k,2,\delta}\\ \leq\left\|Q_{\alpha,y}\right\|\left\|D_{\alpha,y}(\xi_1-\xi_2)-(\mathcal F_{\alpha,y}\xi_1-\mathcal F_{\alpha,y}\xi_2)\right\|_{k-1,2,\delta}\\ \leq c\cdot\left\|Q_{\alpha,y}\right\|\left\|\xi_1-\xi_2\right\|_{k,2,\delta}(\left\|\xi_1\right\|_{k,2,\delta}+\left\|\xi_2\right\|_{k,2,\delta}) \end{multline} by Proposition \ref{quadestimate}. Since $\left\|Q_{\alpha,y}\right\|$ is uniformly bounded, this is enough.
nodes.statement_short: Use D Q = 1 and the quadratic estimate.

nodes.name: Newton iteration
nodes.statement: In fact, we will show that $\kappa_{\alpha,y}$ is given explicitly as the limit of the Newton iteration: \begin{align} \xi_0&:=\kappa_\alpha\\ \xi_n&:=\xi_{n-1}-Q_{\alpha,y}\mathcal F_{\alpha,y}\xi_{n-1} \end{align}
nodes.statement_short: Define the iteration starting at kappa_alpha.

nodes.name: Contraction
nodes.statement: By Lemma \ref{contractionprop}, the map $\xi\mapsto\xi-Q_{\alpha,y}\mathcal F_{\alpha,y}\xi$ is a $\frac 12$-contraction mapping when restricted to: \begin{equation} \{\xi\in\kappa_\alpha+\operatorname{im} Q_{\alpha,y}:\left\|\xi\right\|_{k,2,\delta}\leq c'\} \end{equation}
nodes.statement_short: The iteration map is a 1/2-contraction on the domain.

nodes.name: Reduce to invariance
nodes.statement: To finish the proof, it suffices to show that (for sufficiently small $(\alpha,y,\kappa)$) \eqref{domainofcontraction} is nonempty and is mapped to itself by $\xi\mapsto\xi-Q_{\alpha,y}\mathcal F_{\alpha,y}\xi$.
nodes.statement_short: Suffices: domain nonempty and invariant.

nodes.name: Nonempty
nodes.statement: We know that $\left\|\kappa_\alpha\right\|_{k,2,\delta}\to 0$ as $\kappa\to 0$ (uniformly in $(\alpha,y)$), so \eqref{domainofcontraction} is nonempty.
nodes.statement_short: kappa_alpha is small.

nodes.name: Invariance
nodes.statement: By using Proposition \ref{quadestimate} with $(\xi_1,\xi_2)=(0,\kappa_\alpha)$ and Lemmas \ref{mappregluingissmall} and \ref{pregluingKestimate}, we conclude that: \begin{equation} \left\|\mathcal F_{\alpha,y}\kappa_\alpha\right\|_{k-1,2,\delta}\to 0 \end{equation} as $(\alpha,y,\kappa)\to 0$. Since the operator norm of $Q_{\alpha,y}$ is bounded uniformly as $(\alpha,y)\to 0$, we see that $\kappa_\alpha$ is almost fixed by $\xi\mapsto\xi-Q_{\alpha,y}\mathcal F_{\alpha,y}\xi$ as $(\alpha,y,\kappa)\to 0$. It then follows from the contraction property that $\xi\mapsto\xi-Q_{\alpha,y}\mathcal F_{\alpha,y}\xi$ maps \eqref{domainofcontraction} to itself.
nodes.statement_short: kappa_alpha is almost holomorphic, hence almost fixed; contraction gives invariance.

nodes.name: K_alpha and L_alpha
nodes.statement: It is clear by definition that $K\to K_\alpha$ is an isomorphism, and the respective $W^{k,2,\delta}$ norms are uniformly commensurable. It is also clear that the following commutes: \begin{equation} \begin{tikzcd}[column sep = tiny] K\ar{dr}[swap]{L_0}\ar{rr}{\kappa\mapsto\kappa_\alpha}&&K_\alpha\ar{dl}{L_\alpha}\\ &W \end{tikzcd} \end{equation} (all maps being isomorphisms).
nodes.statement_short: K is isomorphic to K_alpha, compatibly with L_0 and L_alpha.

nodes.name: Trivial intersection
nodes.statement: Since $\operatorname{im} Q_{\alpha,y}\subseteq\ker L_\alpha$, it follows in particular that $\operatorname{im} Q_{\alpha,y}\cap K_\alpha=0$.
nodes.statement_short: im Q in ker L_alpha meets K_alpha trivially.

nodes.name: Index count
nodes.statement: On the other hand, an index calculation shows that $\operatorname{ind} D_{\alpha,y}=\operatorname{ind} D_{0,0}$ (note that by Lemma \ref{fredholmandsamekernelcokernel}, it suffices to calculate their indices as operators $W^{k,2}\to W^{k-1,2}$ on $\tilde C_\alpha$ and $\tilde C_0$ respectively, and this is a standard calculation as in McDuff--Salamon \cite{mcduffsalamonJholsymp}). Both are surjective, and hence we have $\dim\operatorname{coker} Q_{\alpha,y}=\dim\ker D_{\alpha,y}=\dim\ker D_{0,0}=\dim K=\dim K_\alpha$.
nodes.statement_short: Index is preserved, so codim im Q = dim K_alpha.

nodes.name: Equal images
nodes.statement: Suppose that: \begin{equation} (\alpha,y,u_{\alpha,y,\kappa},e_{\alpha,y,\kappa})=(\alpha',y',u_{\alpha',y',\kappa'},e_{\alpha',y',\kappa'}) \end{equation} We see immediately that $(\alpha,y)=(\alpha',y')$.
nodes.statement_short: Assume equal images; then (alpha,y) agree.

nodes.name: Equal corrections
nodes.statement: Now we see that: \begin{align} \exp_{u_\alpha}\kappa_{\alpha,y}&=\exp_{u_\alpha}(\kappa')_{\alpha,y}\\ \operatorname{proj}_E\kappa_{\alpha,y}&=\operatorname{proj}_E(\kappa')_{\alpha,y} \end{align} Since the norms of $\kappa_{\alpha,y}$ and $\kappa_{\alpha,y}'$ go to zero as $(\alpha,y,\kappa,\kappa')\to 0$ (in $W^{k,2,\delta}$, and hence in $C^0$) and the injectivity radius of the exponential map is fixed, we see that $\kappa_{\alpha,y}=(\kappa')_{\alpha,y}$.
nodes.statement_short: Small norms and injectivity radius give equal kappa_{alpha,y}.

nodes.name: Conclude
nodes.statement: It follows that $\kappa_\alpha-(\kappa')_\alpha\in\operatorname{im} Q_{\alpha,y}$, but since $K_\alpha\cap\operatorname{im} Q_{\alpha,y}=0$ we conclude $\kappa_\alpha=(\kappa')_\alpha$ and hence $\kappa=\kappa'$.
nodes.statement_short: K_alpha meets im Q trivially.

nodes.name: Key ingredient
nodes.statement: The key ingredient in this proof is our precise control of the image of the right inverse $Q_{\alpha,y}$ (specifically, that $\operatorname{im} Q_{\alpha,y}=\ker L_\alpha$).
nodes.statement_short: Uses im Q = ker L_alpha.

nodes.name: Convergent net
nodes.statement: Suppose $(\alpha_i,y_i,\kappa_i)\to(\alpha,y,\kappa)$ is a convergent net.\footnote{We could restrict to sequences rather than nets since $\mathbb C^d\times\mathbb R^{\dim\overline{\mathcal M}^d}\times K$ is first countable. However, this would not make the argument any simpler.} We will show that: \begin{equation} (u_{\alpha_i,y_i,\kappa_i},e_{\alpha_i,y_i,\kappa_i})\to(u_{\alpha,y,\kappa},e_{\alpha,y,\kappa}) \end{equation}
nodes.statement_short: Take a convergent net; show convergence of glued maps.

nodes.name: Claim: varying kappa
nodes.statement: First, we claim that $\left\|(\kappa_i)_{\alpha_i,y_i}-\kappa_{\alpha_i,y_i}\right\|_\infty\to 0$. In fact, we will show the stronger statement that $\left\|(\kappa_i)_{\alpha_i,y_i}-\kappa_{\alpha_i,y_i}\right\|_{k,2,\delta}\to 0$. Since the Newton iteration converges uniformly, it suffices to show that $\bigl\|(\kappa_i)_{\alpha_i,y_i}^{n}-\kappa_{\alpha_i,y_i}^{n}\bigr\|_{k,2,\delta}\to 0$ for all $n\geq 0$, where $\kappa_{\alpha,y}^{n}$ denotes the $n$th step of the Newton iteration converging to $\kappa_{\alpha,y}$. It is easy to verify this for $n=0$: \begin{equation} \left\|(\kappa_i)_{\alpha_i,y_i}^{0}-\kappa_{\alpha_i,y_i}^{0}\right\|_{k,2,\delta}=\left\|(\kappa_i-\kappa)_{\alpha_i}\right\|_{k,2,\delta}\to 0 \end{equation} The inductive step follows from the fact that $Q_{\alpha_i,y_i}$ is uniformly bounded and $\mathcal F_{\alpha_i,y_i}$ is uniformly Lipschitz (e.g.\ as a consequence of Proposition \ref{quadestimate}).
nodes.statement_short: Corrections depend continuously on kappa uniformly in (alpha,y).

nodes.name: Reduce to Newton steps
nodes.statement: In fact, we will show the stronger statement that $\left\|(\kappa_i)_{\alpha_i,y_i}-\kappa_{\alpha_i,y_i}\right\|_{k,2,\delta}\to 0$. Since the Newton iteration converges uniformly, it suffices to show that $\bigl\|(\kappa_i)_{\alpha_i,y_i}^{n}-\kappa_{\alpha_i,y_i}^{n}\bigr\|_{k,2,\delta}\to 0$ for all $n\geq 0$, where $\kappa_{\alpha,y}^{n}$ denotes the $n$th step of the Newton iteration converging to $\kappa_{\alpha,y}$.
nodes.statement_short: Suffices to compare each Newton step.

nodes.name: Induction over Newton steps
nodes.statement: It is easy to verify this for $n=0$: \begin{equation} \left\|(\kappa_i)_{\alpha_i,y_i}^{0}-\kappa_{\alpha_i,y_i}^{0}\right\|_{k,2,\delta}=\left\|(\kappa_i-\kappa)_{\alpha_i}\right\|_{k,2,\delta}\to 0 \end{equation} The inductive step follows from the fact that $Q_{\alpha_i,y_i}$ is uniformly bounded and $\mathcal F_{\alpha_i,y_i}$ is uniformly Lipschitz (e.g.\ as a consequence of Proposition \ref{quadestimate}).
nodes.statement_short: True for n=0; inductive step by uniform bounds.

nodes.name: Fix kappa
nodes.statement: Now from the claim, we see that it suffices to show that: \begin{equation} (u_{\alpha_i,y_i,\kappa},e_{\alpha_i,y_i,\kappa})\to(u_{\alpha,y,\kappa},e_{\alpha,y,\kappa}) \end{equation}
nodes.statement_short: Suffices to vary only (alpha,y).

nodes.name: Recall decomposition
nodes.statement: Recall that by definition: \begin{align} u_{\alpha,y,\kappa}&=\exp_{u_\alpha}\kappa_{\alpha,y}&\kappa_{\alpha,y}&=\kappa_\alpha+\xi&\text{for some }\xi&\in\operatorname{im} Q_{\alpha,y}\\ u_{\alpha_i,y_i,\kappa}&=\exp_{u_{\alpha_i}}\kappa_{\alpha_i,y_i}&\kappa_{\alpha_i,y_i}&=\kappa_{\alpha_i}+\xi_i&\text{for some }\xi_i&\in\operatorname{im} Q_{\alpha_i,y_i} \end{align}
nodes.statement_short: kappa_{alpha,y} = kappa_alpha + xi with xi in im Q.

nodes.name: Transplant xi
nodes.statement:
Now we define $\xi_{\alpha_i}\in W^{k,2,\delta}(C_{\alpha_i},u_{\alpha_i}^\ast TX)_D\oplus E$ by ``pregluing'' $\xi$ from $C_\alpha$ to $C_{\alpha_i}$ as follows. Note that we may assume without loss of generality that at the nodes where $\alpha
e 0$, we also have $\alpha_i
e 0$. Away from the ends/necks of $C_{\alpha_i}$, we set $\xi_{\alpha_i}=\xi$. Over the ends of $C_{\alpha_i}$, note there is a corresponding end of $C_\alpha$, so we may also simply set $\xi_{\alpha_i}=\xi$ over the ends of $C_{\alpha_i}$. Over the necks of $C_{\alpha_i}$ for which $\alpha=0$, we define $\xi_{\alpha_i}$ via \eqref{kernelpregluingformula} (note that this is reasonable since $\xi$ is smooth on $C_{\alpha}$). Over the necks of $C_{\alpha_i}$ for which $\alpha
e 0$ we define $\xi_{\alpha_i}$ as:  egin{equation} \xi_{\alpha_i}(s,t):=\mathsf{PT}_{u_{\alpha}(f_i(s),t)	o u_{\alpha_i}(s,t)}[\xi(f_i(s),t))] \end{equation} where $f_i:[0,6S_i]	o[0,6S]$ is defined as follows:  egin{align} f_i(s):=& egin{cases} s&s\leq S-2\cr s-3S_i+3S&3S_i-2S+2\leq s\leq 3S_i+2S-2\cr s-6S_i+6S&6S_i-S+2\leq s\cr \end{cases}\ f_i([S-2,3S_i-2S+2])&\subseteq[S-2,S+2]\ f_i([3S_i+2S-2,6S_i-S+2])&\subseteq[5S-2,5S+2] \end{align} and is smooth with absolutely bounded derivatives of all orders. More informally, $f_i$ is smooth and matches up $[0,S-2],[S+2,5S-2],[5S+2,6S]\subseteq[0,6S]$ with corresponding intervals of the same length inside $[0,6S_i]$, symmetrically.
nodes.statement_short: Preglue xi from C_alpha to C_{alpha_i} using a reparametrization f_i of the necks.

nodes.name: Reduce to correction comparison
nodes.statement: Now the $C^0$-distance between: \begin{align} u_{\alpha,y,\kappa}=\exp_{u_\alpha}(\kappa_\alpha+\xi)&:C_\alpha\to X\quad\text{and}\cr \exp_{u_{\alpha_i}}(\kappa_{\alpha_i}+\xi_{\alpha_i})&:C_{\alpha_i}\to X \end{align} goes to zero (this is easy to see from \eqref{kernelpregluingformula} and \eqref{xitoIpregluingforcontinuous}). Hence it suffices to show that $\left\|\xi_i-\xi_{\alpha_i}\right\|_\infty\to 0$. In fact, we will prove the stronger statement that: \begin{equation} \left\|\xi_i-\xi_{\alpha_i}\right\|_{k,2,\delta}\to 0 \end{equation}
nodes.statement_short: Suffices to show xi_i - xi_{alpha_i} tends to zero.

nodes.name: Claim: transplanted correction small
nodes.statement: First, we claim that we may assume that: \begin{equation} \limsup_i\left\|\xi_{\alpha_i}\right\|_{k,2,\delta} \end{equation} is arbitrarily small by taking $(\alpha,y,\kappa)$ sufficiently close to zero. We know $\|F_{\alpha,y}\kappa_\alpha\|_{k-1,2,\delta}\to 0$ as $(\alpha,y,\kappa)\to 0$ by \eqref{kernelclosetoholomorphic}. Now since the Newton iteration is uniformly convergent and $Q_{\alpha,y}$ is uniformly bounded, it follows that $\left\|\xi\right\|_{k,2,\delta}\to 0$ as $(\alpha,y,\kappa)\to 0$. We may easily bound $\|\xi_{\alpha_i}\|_{k,2,\delta}$ in terms of $\|\xi\|_{k,2,\delta}$ and the desired claim follows.
nodes.statement_short: limsup ||xi_{alpha_i}|| can be made small.

nodes.name: Almost holomorphic
nodes.statement: We know $\|F_{\alpha,y}\kappa_\alpha\|_{k-1,2,\delta}\to 0$ as $(\alpha,y,\kappa)\to 0$ by \eqref{kernelclosetoholomorphic}.
nodes.statement_short: Recall F kappa_alpha tends to zero.

nodes.name: Bound xi
nodes.statement: Now since the Newton iteration is uniformly convergent and $Q_{\alpha,y}$ is uniformly bounded, it follows that $\left\|\xi\right\|_{k,2,\delta}\to 0$ as $(\alpha,y,\kappa)\to 0$. We may easily bound $\|\xi_{\alpha_i}\|_{k,2,\delta}$ in terms of $\|\xi\|_{k,2,\delta}$ and the desired claim follows.
nodes.statement_short: Hence xi is small, so is xi_{alpha_i}.

nodes.name: Reduce to almost holomorphic
nodes.statement: Now since the $\limsup$ \eqref{pregluedisntbig} can be assumed to be arbitrarily small, we may, in particular, assume that for sufficiently large $i$, $\|\kappa_{\alpha_i}+\xi_{\alpha_i}\|_{k,2,\delta}\leq c'$ for the constant $c'>0$ from Proposition \ref{contractionprop} for which \eqref{domainofcontraction} is a domain of contraction. By construction, the fact that $\xi\in\operatorname{im} Q_{\alpha,y}=\ker L_\alpha$ implies that $\xi_{\alpha_i}\in\ker L_{\alpha_i}=\operatorname{im} Q_{\alpha_i,y_i}$. Hence $\kappa_{\alpha_i}+\xi_{\alpha_i}$ lies in the domain of contraction \eqref{domainofcontraction} for $(\alpha_i,y_i,\kappa)$ where the Newton iteration applies. By definition, we have $\mathcal F_{\alpha_i,y_i}(\kappa_{\alpha_i}+\xi_i)=0$ and $\kappa_{\alpha_i}+\xi_i$ is in the same domain of contraction. Since the Newton iteration is a $\frac 12$-contraction on this domain and $Q_{\alpha_i,y_i}$ is uniformly bounded, to show \eqref{correctedgetsbetter}, it suffices to show that: \begin{equation} \left\|\mathcal F_{\alpha_i,y_i}(\kappa_{\alpha_i}+\xi_{\alpha_i})\right\|_{k-1,2,\delta}\to 0 \end{equation}
nodes.statement_short: Transplant lies in the domain of contraction; suffices F(kappa_{alpha_i}+xi_{alpha_i}) -> 0.

nodes.name: Away from necks
nodes.statement: To prove \eqref{pregluedcorrectionalmosthol}, first recall that $\mathcal F_{\alpha,y}(\kappa_\alpha+\xi)=0$. Away from the ends/necks of $C_{\alpha_i}$, the expression $\mathcal F_{\alpha_i,y_i}(\kappa_{\alpha_i}+\xi_{\alpha_i})$ differs from $\mathcal F_{\alpha,y}(\kappa_\alpha+\xi)=0$ only in terms of the complex structure $j_{y_i}$ in place of $j_y$. Clearly this difference goes to zero as $y_i\to y$.
nodes.statement_short: Away from necks only the complex structure changes.

nodes.name: In ends
nodes.statement: Over the ends of $C_{\alpha_i}$, the expression $\mathcal F_{\alpha_i,y_i}(\kappa_{\alpha_i}+\xi_{\alpha_i})$ coincides with $\mathcal F_{\alpha,y}(\kappa_\alpha+\xi)=0$.
nodes.statement_short: Zero in the ends.

nodes.name: In necks
nodes.statement: Over the necks of $C_{\alpha_i}$, we bound $\mathcal F_{\alpha_i,y_i}(\kappa_{\alpha_i}+\xi_{\alpha_i})$ as follows. Fix a neck $[0,6S_i]\subseteq C_{\alpha_i}$. If $\alpha\ne 0$ for this neck, then the desired estimate follows easily from the definition of $\xi_{\alpha_i}$, $\kappa_{\alpha_i}$, and $u_{\alpha_i}$, and the fact that $\mathcal F_{\alpha,y}(\kappa_\alpha+\xi)=0$. If $\alpha=0$ for this neck, then we argue as follows. The expression $\mathcal F_{\alpha_i,y_i}(\kappa_{\alpha_i}+\xi_{\alpha_i})$ is only nonzero over $[S_i-1,S_i+1]\cup[5S_i-1,5S_i+1]$; by symmetry we may just bound it over $[S_i-1,S_i+1]$. As in the proof of Lemma \ref{mappregluingissmall}, we win because of the weights: the expression in question has derivatives bounded by $e^{-S}$ and is weighted by $e^{\delta S}$.
nodes.statement_short: Exponential decay beats the weights, as in the map pregluing estimate.

nodes.name: Energy decay
nodes.statement: First, apply Lemma \ref{energydecayexponential} to get an exponential decay bound on the $W^{1,2}$ norm of $u$ restricted to $[-r,r]\times S^1$.
nodes.statement_short: Exponential decay of W^{1,2} norm.

nodes.name: Pointwise bound
nodes.statement: Second, apply Lemma \ref{energycontrolsWoneinfty} to conclude that the bound on the $W^{1,2}$ norm implies a similar bound on the $W^{1,\infty}$ norm.
nodes.statement_short: W^{1,2} controls W^{1,infinity}.

nodes.name: Higher derivatives
nodes.statement: Finally, apply elliptic bootstrapping Lemma \ref{Woneinftycontrolsall} to conclude that the bound on the $W^{1,\infty}$ norm implies a similar bound on the $C^k$ norm for all $k<\infty$.
nodes.statement_short: Elliptic bootstrapping.

nodes.name: Source
nodes.statement: This proof is essentially lifted from McDuff--Salamon \cite[p99, Lemma 4.7.3]{mcduffsalamonJholsymp}.
nodes.statement_short: Following McDuff-Salamon Lemma 4.7.3.

nodes.name: Liouville form
nodes.statement: Let $\lambda_\mathrm{std}:=\frac 12\sum_jx_j\,dy_j-y_j\,dx_j$. Note the identity: \begin{equation} \sum_jz_j\,d\bar z_j=\frac 12\sum_jd\left|z_j\right|^2-2i\lambda_\mathrm{std} \end{equation}
nodes.statement_short: Define lambda_std and note the identity.

nodes.name: Isoperimetric inequality
nodes.statement: Let $\gamma:S^1\to\mathbb R^{2n}$ be a smooth loop. Write the Fourier series $\gamma(t)=\sum_ka_ke^{ikt}\in\mathbb C^n$ where $a_k\in\mathbb C^n$. Now using \eqref{zdzbaridentity}, we see that: \begin{equation*} \int_{S^1}\gamma^\ast\lambda_\mathrm{std}=\frac i2\int_{S^1}\sum_j\gamma^\ast(z_j\,d\bar z_j)=\frac i2\int_{S^1}\sum_{k,\ell}a_k\bar a_\ell(-i\ell)e^{i(k-\ell)t}\,dt=\pi\sum_kk\left|a_k\right|^2 \end{equation*} We may also calculate: \begin{equation} \int_{S^1}\Bigl|\frac{d\gamma}{dt}\Bigr|^2\,dt=\int_{S^1}\sum_{k,\ell}a_k\bar a_\ell(ik)(-i\ell)e^{i(k-\ell)t}\,dt=2\pi\sum_kk^2\left|a_k\right|^2 \end{equation} Hence we conclude that: \begin{equation} \left|\int_{S^1}\gamma^\ast\lambda_\mathrm{std}\right|\leq\frac 12\int_{S^1}\Bigl|\frac{d\gamma}{dt}\Bigr|^2\,dt \end{equation}
nodes.statement_short: Fourier series give the symplectic isoperimetric inequality.

nodes.name: Differential inequality
nodes.statement: Let: \begin{equation} E(r):=\int_{[-r,r]\times S^1}\Bigl|\frac{du}{dt}\Bigr|^2\,ds\,dt\approx\int_{[-r,r]\times S^1}u^\ast\omega_\mathrm{std}=\int_{\partial[-r,r]\times S^1}u^\ast\lambda_\mathrm{std} \end{equation} ($\approx$ means equality up to a factor which can be made arbitrarily close to $1$ by taking $\epsilon>0$ sufficiently small). Applying \eqref{sympisoperimetric}, we conclude that: \begin{equation} E(r)\lesssim\frac 12\int_{\partial[-r,r]\times S^1}\Bigl|\frac{du}{dt}\Bigr|^2\,dt \end{equation} ($\lesssim$ means inequality up to a factor which can be made arbitrarily close to $1$ by taking $\epsilon>0$ sufficiently small). The right hand side above equals $\frac 12E'(r)$, so we have $E'(r)\gtrsim 2E(r)$, and hence $E'(r)\geq 2\mu E(r)$ (for $\epsilon>0$ sufficiently small), from which we conclude that $E(r)\leq e^{2\mu\cdot(r-R)}E(R)$. Using \eqref{boundonenergyfromboundary} to bound $E(R)$, we see that: \begin{equation} E(r)\lesssim e^{2\mu\cdot(r-R)}\frac 12\int_{\partial[-R,R]\times S^1}\Bigl|\frac{du}{dt}\Bigr|^2\,dt \end{equation}
nodes.statement_short: E' >= 2 mu E, so E decays exponentially.

nodes.name: Conclude
nodes.statement: We have: \begin{equation} E(r)\approx\frac 12\int_{[-r,r]\times S^1}\biggl[\Bigl|\frac{du}{ds}\Bigr|^2+\Bigl|\frac{du}{dt}\Bigr|^2\biggr]\,ds\,dt \end{equation} Hence we conclude that: \begin{equation} \int_{[-r,r]\times S^1}\biggl[\Bigl|\frac{du}{ds}\Bigr|^2+\Bigl|\frac{du}{dt}\Bigr|^2\biggr]\,ds\,dt\lesssim e^{ 2\mu\cdot(r-R)}\int_{\partial[-R,R]\times S^1}\Bigl|\frac{du}{dt}\Bigr|^2\,dt \end{equation} which is the desired estimate.
nodes.statement_short: Relate E to the W^{1,2} norm.

nodes.name: Source
nodes.statement: This proof is essentially lifted from McDuff--Salamon \cite[p80, Lemma 4.3.1]{mcduffsalamonJholsymp}.
nodes.statement_short: Following McDuff-Salamon Lemma 4.3.1.

nodes.name: Energy density
nodes.statement: Let $w:=\frac 12u_x^2+\frac 12u_y^2$ (using the standard inner product $g_\mathrm{std}$), so $w:[0,1]^2\to\mathbb R_{\geq 0}$. Now we calculate: \begin{equation} w_{xx}+w_{yy}=\Bigl[u_{xx}^2+2u_{xy}^2+u_{yy}^2\Bigr]+\Bigl[u_x\cdot(u_{xxx}+u_{xyy})+u_y\cdot(u_{xxy}+u_{yyy})\Bigr] \end{equation}
nodes.statement_short: Define w and compute its Laplacian.

nodes.name: Bound third derivatives
nodes.statement: Now differentiating \eqref{formulaforDeltau} yields: \begin{align*} u_{xxx}+u_{xyy}=&\ddot J(u,u_x,u_y)\circ u_x+\dot J(u,u_{xy})\circ u_x+\dot J(u,u_y)\circ u_{xx}\\ &-\ddot J(u,u_x,u_x)\circ u_y-\dot J(u,u_{xx})\circ u_y-\dot J(u,u_x)\circ u_{xy}\\ u_{xxy}+u_{yyy}=&\ddot J(u,u_y,u_y)\circ u_x+\dot J(u,u_{yy})\circ u_x+\dot J(u,u_y)\circ u_{xy}\\ &-\ddot J(u,u_x,u_y)\circ u_y-\dot J(u,u_{xy})\circ u_y-\dot J(u,u_x)\circ u_{yy} \end{align*} Now we conclude that: \begin{align*} \bigl|u_x\cdot(u_{xxx}&+u_{xyy})+u_y\cdot(u_{xxy}+u_{yyy})\bigr|\\ &\leq 2\left\|J\right\|_{C^2}\cdot(\left|u_x\right|^3\left|u_y\right|+\left|u_x\right|\left|u_y\right|^3)\\ &\qquad+2\left\|J\right\|_{C^1}\cdot(\left|u_x\right|^2\left|u_{xy}\right|+\left|u_x\right|\left|u_y\right|\left|u_{xx}\right|+\left|u_y\right|^2\left|u_{xy}\right|+\left|u_x\right|\left|u_y\right|\left|u_{yy}\right|)\\ &\leq c\left\|J\right\|_{C^2}w^2+c\left\|J\right\|_{C^1}w\cdot(\left|u_{xx}\right|+\left|u_{xy}\right|+\left|u_{yy}\right|)\\ &\leq c\left\|J\right\|_{C^2}w^2+c\left\|J\right\|_{C^1}^2w^2+\frac 1{100}(u_{xx}^2+2u_{xy}^2+u_{yy}^2) \end{align*}
nodes.statement_short: Differentiate the Laplace equation for u and bound the cross terms.

nodes.name: Differential inequality
nodes.statement: Plugging this into \eqref{formulaforDeltaw}, we conclude that: \begin{equation} \Delta w=w_{xx}+w_{yy}\geq -c\cdot (\left\|J\right\|_{C^2}+\left\|J\right\|_{C^1}^2)w^2 \end{equation}
nodes.statement_short: Delta w >= -c w^2.

nodes.name: Mean value inequality
nodes.statement: Now we may apply a mean value inequality McDuff--Salamon \cite[p81, Lemma 4.3.2]{mcduffsalamonJholsymp} or Wehrheim \cite[p306, Theorem 1.1]{wehrheimmeanvalue} to see that there exist $\epsilon>0$ and $c<\infty$ such that if $\int_{[0,1]^2}w\,dx\,dy<\epsilon$, then $w(\frac 12,\frac 12)\leq c\cdot\int_{[0,1]^2}w\,dx\,dy$. Thus we are done.
nodes.statement_short: Apply the mean value inequality (McDuff-Salamon, Wehrheim).

nodes.name: Reference
nodes.statement: For more details see McDuff--Salamon \cite[p533, \S B.4]{mcduffsalamonJholsymp}.
nodes.statement_short: See McDuff-Salamon B.4.

nodes.name: Laplace equation for u
nodes.statement: The $\bar\partial$-equation for $u$ may be written as: \begin{equation} u_y=J(u)\circ u_x \end{equation} Differentiating with respect to $x$ and to $y$, we conclude that: \begin{align} u_{xy}&=\dot J(u,u_x)\circ u_x+J(u)\circ u_{xx}\\ u_{xx}&=\dot J(u,u_y)\circ u_x+J(u)\circ u_{xy} \end{align} Combining these and using the fact that $\dot J$ and $J$ anticommute, we conclude that: \begin{equation} \Delta u=u_{xx}+u_{yy}=\dot J(u,u_y)\circ u_x-\dot J(u,u_x)\circ u_y \end{equation}
nodes.statement_short: Differentiate the CR equation to get Delta u in terms of first derivatives.

nodes.name: Bootstrap
nodes.statement: Now a standard elliptic bootstrapping argument based on \eqref{formulaforDeltau} gives the desired result. By hypothesis, we have an $L^\infty$ bound in terms of $\left\|J\right\|_{C^1}$ on the right hand side of \eqref{formulaforDeltau}, which gives a $W^{2,p}$ bound ($2<p<\infty$) on $u$ in terms of $\left\|J\right\|_{C^1}$. Now we have a $W^{1,p}$ bound on the right hand side of \eqref{formulaforDeltau} in terms of $\left\|J\right\|_{C^2}$, which gives a $W^{3,p}$ bound on $u$ in terms of $\left\|J\right\|_{C^2}$. Iterating, we get a $W^{k,p}$ bound on $u$ in terms of $\left\|J\right\|_{C^{k-1}}$, which is enough. There is no need to worry about elliptic regularity estimates near the boundary since we can shrink the domain slightly after each iteration.
nodes.statement_short: Iterate interior elliptic estimates to get W^{k,p} bounds.

nodes.name: Sequence near basepoint
nodes.statement: Let $(\alpha_i,y_i,u_i,\{x^i_j\},e_i)\in\overline{\mathcal M}(X)$ be a sequence converging to $(0,0,u_0,\{x^0_j\},e_0)$. We must show that for $i$ sufficiently large, $(\alpha_i,y_i,u_i,\{x^i_j\},e_i)$ is contained in the image of the map \eqref{gluingmap}. We may restrict to sequences rather than nets since the topology on $\overline{\mathcal M}(X)$ is first countable (recall the definition of the topology following \eqref{Mbarfirstdef}; it is even a metric topology). This is convenient when we apply Arzel\`a--Ascoli.
nodes.statement_short: Take a convergent sequence; must show it lies in the image.

nodes.name: Corrections xi_i
nodes.statement: Let us define $\xi_i\in C^\infty(C_{\alpha_i},u_{\alpha_i}^\ast TX)_D\oplus E$ by the property: \begin{align} u_i&=\exp_{u_{\alpha_i}}\xi_i\\ e_i&=e_0+\operatorname{proj}_E\xi_i \end{align} (and the exponential follows the shortest geodesic). Obviously $\operatorname{proj}_E\xi_i\to 0$ and $\left\|\xi_i\right\|_\infty\to 0$.
nodes.statement_short: Write u_i = exp(xi_i); xi_i tends to zero in C^0.

nodes.name: Claim: smooth convergence away from nodes
nodes.statement: Now we claim that $u_i\to u$ in the $C^\infty$ topology away from the nodes, or equivalently, that $\xi_i\to 0$ in the $C^\infty$ topology away from the nodes of $C_0$. To see this argue as follows. The thickened holomorphic curve equation from \eqref{modulispace} is equivalent to an honest holomorphic curve equation for the graph $u:C\to C\times X$ where the almost complex structure on $C\times X$ is defined in terms of $\lambda(e)$. Hence the Gromov--Schwarz Lemma (see \cite[p316, 1.3.A]{gromov} or \cite[p223, Corollary 4.1.4]{muller}) applies and we conclude that $\left\|du_i\right\|_\infty$ is uniformly bounded, on compact sets away from the nodes (equivalently, the same for $\left\|d\xi_i\right\|_\infty$). Now elliptic bootstrapping (as in the proof of Lemma \ref{Woneinftycontrolsall}) implies that all derivatives are bounded uniformly on compact sets away from the nodes. Using Arzel\`a--Ascoli and diagonalization, we conclude that there exists a subsequence of $u_i$ which is convergent in the $C^\infty$ topology away from the nodes. Since we know that $u_i\to u$ in the $C^0$ topology, the limit of this $C^\infty$ convergent subsequence must be $u$. This argument can be applied to any subsequence of $u_i$, so we conclude that every subsequence of $u_i$ has a subsequence which converges to $u$ in $C^\infty$ away from the nodes.
nodes.statement_short: u_i converges to u in C^infinity away from nodes.

nodes.name: Gromov-Schwarz
nodes.statement: To see this argue as follows. The thickened holomorphic curve equation from \eqref{modulispace} is equivalent to an honest holomorphic curve equation for the graph $u:C\to C\times X$ where the almost complex structure on $C\times X$ is defined in terms of $\lambda(e)$. Hence the Gromov--Schwarz Lemma (see \cite[p316, 1.3.A]{gromov} or \cite[p223, Corollary 4.1.4]{muller}) applies and we conclude that $\left\|du_i\right\|_\infty$ is uniformly bounded, on compact sets away from the nodes (equivalently, the same for $\left\|d\xi_i\right\|_\infty$).
nodes.statement_short: Graph trick and Gromov-Schwarz give uniform derivative bounds.

nodes.name: Bootstrapping and Arzela-Ascoli
nodes.statement: Now elliptic bootstrapping (as in the proof of Lemma \ref{Woneinftycontrolsall}) implies that all derivatives are bounded uniformly on compact sets away from the nodes. Using Arzel\`a--Ascoli and diagonalization, we conclude that there exists a subsequence of $u_i$ which is convergent in the $C^\infty$ topology away from the nodes. Since we know that $u_i\to u$ in the $C^0$ topology, the limit of this $C^\infty$ convergent subsequence must be $u$.
nodes.statement_short: Bounds on all derivatives give a C^infinity convergent subsequence with limit u.

nodes.name: Subsequence argument
nodes.statement: This argument can be applied to any subsequence of $u_i$, so we conclude that every subsequence of $u_i$ has a subsequence which converges to $u$ in $C^\infty$ away from the nodes.
nodes.statement_short: Every subsequence has a further convergent subsequence.

nodes.name: Neck estimate
nodes.statement: In the ends/necks of $C_{\alpha_i}$, note that $u_i$ is genuinely $J$-holomorphic (the $\lambda$ term vanishes), so we may apply Proposition \ref{neckestimate} to conclude that $\left\|\xi_i\right\|_{k,2,\delta}\to 0$ (here using the fact that $\delta<1$). We should remark that to apply Proposition \ref{neckestimate}, we need to be able to choose some $M<\infty$ such that for any neck $[0,6S]\times S^2\subseteq C_{\alpha_i}$, the derivatives of $u_i$ restricted to $\partial[M,6S-M]\subseteq C_{\alpha_i}$ are bounded by $\delta$ (the constant in Proposition \ref{neckestimate}). Such an $M$ exists because of our earlier observation that $u_i\to u$ in $C^\infty$ on compact sets away from the nodes, and we can certainly choose a large $M$ such that the derivatives of $u$ over $\{M\}\times S^1\subseteq[0,\infty)\times S^1\subseteq C_0$ (any end) are arbitrarily small.
nodes.statement_short: Apply the a priori neck estimate to get weighted convergence of xi_i.

nodes.name: Identify with glued solution
nodes.statement: Let us define $\kappa_i\in K$ by the property that $\xi_i\in(\kappa_i)_{\alpha_i}+\operatorname{im} Q_{\alpha_i,y_i}$. Now since $\left\|\xi_i\right\|_{k,2,\delta}\to 0$ and the norms on the left and right of \eqref{QKtoall} are uniformly commensurable, we see that $\kappa_i\to 0$. Now the uniqueness in Proposition \ref{newtoniteration} shows that $\xi_i=(\kappa_i)_{\alpha_i,y_i}$ for $i$ sufficiently large. Thus we are done.
nodes.statement_short: Decompose xi_i; kappa_i -> 0 and Newton uniqueness shows xi_i is the glued correction.

nodes.name: Compact ball
nodes.statement: Let $B(1)\subseteq\mathbb R^n$ denote the closed unit ball and $B(1)^\circ$ its interior. We know that $f(B(1))$ is compact (since $f$ is continuous) and Hausdorff (since $X$ is Hausdorff). We know that $f:B(1)\to f(B(1))$ is bijective (since $f$ is injective), so it is in fact a homeomorphism.
nodes.statement_short: f restricted to the closed ball is a homeomorphism onto its image.

nodes.name: Choose U
nodes.statement: Now choose an open subset $V\subseteq X$ with $f(0)\in V\subseteq f(B(1)^\circ)$ (which exists by assumption). Set $U=f^{-1}(V)\cap B(1)^\circ$, which is clearly open. Now $f:U\to f(U)$ is a homeomorphism onto its image (since $U\subseteq B(1)$), and $f(U)=V$ is open.
nodes.statement_short: U = f^{-1}(V) in the open ball works.

nodes.name: Collect properties
nodes.statement: We have shown that the map $g:=$\eqref{gluingmap} is continuous, injective, and that its restriction to any neighborhood of zero is surjective onto a neighborhood of the image of zero.
nodes.statement_short: Gluing map is continuous, injective, locally surjective.

nodes.name: Local homeomorphism
nodes.statement: The target $\overline{\mathcal M}(X)$ is Hausdorff, and thus it follows from Lemma \ref{injectiveHdorffhomeo} that for some open neighborhood of zero $U\subseteq\mathbb C^d\times\mathbb R^{\dim\overline{\mathcal M}^d}\times K$, we have $g(U)$ is open and $g:U\xrightarrow\sim g(U)$ is a homeomorphism.
nodes.statement_short: Apply Lemma B.12.33.

nodes.name: Conclude parts (i)-(iii)
nodes.statement: Since $g$ respects the projection map from both sides to $\overline{\mathcal M}\times E/E'$, we obtain the desired conclusions (\ref{openness}), (\ref{manifold}), and (\ref{submersion}).
nodes.statement_short: Compatibility with the projection gives openness, manifold and submersion.

nodes.name: Orient via the kernel
nodes.statement: To show Theorem \ref{mainresult}(\ref{orientation}) (the statement about orientations), observe that since $\overline{\mathcal M}(X)^\mathrm{reg}\to\overline{\mathcal M}$ is a submersion, and $\overline{\mathcal M}$ is canonically oriented as a complex manifold, it follows that $\mathfrak o_{\overline{\mathcal M}(X)^\mathrm{reg}}$ is canonically identified with the orientation sheaf of the fibers of $\overline{\mathcal M}(X)^\mathrm{reg}\to\overline{\mathcal M}$. Now orienting a fiber is the same as orienting the kernel $K$. It is standard to see that $\mathfrak o_K=\mathfrak o_E\otimes\bigotimes_{i=1}^\ell\mathfrak o_{u(p_{n+i})^\ast N_{D/X}}^\vee$.
nodes.statement_short: Orientation of M(X)^reg reduces to orienting K, which is standard.

nodes.name: Local identifications
nodes.statement: This argument gives an identification $\mathfrak o_{\overline{\mathcal M}(X)^\mathrm{reg}}$ with $\mathfrak o_E\otimes\bigotimes_{i=1}^\ell\mathfrak o_{u(p_{n+i})^\ast N_{D/X}}^\vee$ at every point in $\overline{\mathcal M}(X)^\mathrm{reg}$. Via the gluing map, we get an identification of $\mathfrak o_{\overline{\mathcal M}(X)^\mathrm{reg}}$ with $\mathfrak o_E\otimes\bigotimes_{i=1}^\ell\mathfrak o_{u(p_{n+i})^\ast N_{D/X}}^\vee$ over a small neighborhood of every point in $\overline{\mathcal M}(X)^\mathrm{reg}$. It is probably straightforward to check that these identifications agree on overlaps (this is a concrete question about whether the projection map $K\to K_\alpha\to\ker D_{\alpha,y}$ is orientation preserving; a similar question is dealt with in Floer--Hofer \cite{floerhoferorientations}).
nodes.statement_short: Gluing gives local identifications; compatibility on overlaps is plausible.

nodes.name: Codimension two argument
nodes.statement: This is the best way to prove the desired result, but we can actually get away with a less technical argument. Namely, it is easy to see that the identifications induced by points with smooth domain curve agree on overlaps (since then there is no gluing and we have a nice smooth Banach bundle picture). Since the nodal locus is codimension two inside $\overline{\mathcal M}(X)^\mathrm{reg}$ (this follows from the gluing map constructed previously), the identification $\mathfrak o_{\overline{\mathcal M}(X)^\mathrm{reg}}=\mathfrak o_E\otimes\bigotimes_{i=1}^\ell\mathfrak o_{u(p_{n+i})^\ast N_{D/X}}^\vee$ away from the nodal locus extends uniquely to all of $\overline{\mathcal M}(X)^\mathrm{reg}$.
nodes.statement_short: Identifications agree on the smooth locus, whose complement has codimension two.

nodes.name: Recall the equation for $u_0$
nodes.statement: Recall that: \begin{equation} \Bigl(du_0+2d(\operatorname{proj}_{S^1}A_0)\otimes X_{H((\ell_{0,0}\times\operatorname{id}_{S^1})(A_0(\cdot)))}(u_0) +\lambda(e_0)(0,0,x_0^1,\ldots,x_0^r,\cdot,u_0(\cdot))\Bigr)^{0,1}_{j_0,J(\ell_{0,0}(A_0(\cdot)))}=0 \end{equation}
nodes.statement_short: Recall that $u_0$ solves the perturbed Floer equation \eqref{delbareqnforuzeroHF}.

nodes.name: Main ends/necks
nodes.statement: We estimate $\mathcal F_{\alpha,w,y}(0)$ over the main ends/necks. Note that over this region, the $\lambda$ term vanishes, $j_y=j_0$, $J(\ell_{\alpha,w}(A_y(\cdot)))=J(\ell_{0,0}(A_0(\cdot)))$, and $H((\ell_{\alpha,w}\times\operatorname{id}_{S^1})(A_y(\cdot)))=H((\ell_{0,0}\times\operatorname{id}_{S^1})(A_0(\cdot)))$. Now due to \eqref{delbareqnforuzeroHF}, it follows that in this region, $\mathcal F_{\alpha,w,y}(0)$ is supported inside the subsets $S^1\times([S-1,S]\cup[5S,5S+1])$ of the main necks $S^1\times[N,6S-N]$. The contribution of such a region to the norm of $\mathcal F_{\alpha,w,y}(0)$ is bounded above by a constant times $\left|\alpha\right|^\epsilon$, as follows from the estimate \eqref{uzeromain} on the derivatives of $u_0$ and the fact that $\delta<\delta_i$.
nodes.statement_short: On main ends/necks the error is supported near $s\in[S-1,S]\cup[5S,5S+1]$ and is $O(|\alpha|^\epsilon)$.

nodes.name: Away from ends/necks
nodes.statement: We estimate $\mathcal F_{\alpha,w,y}(0)$ away from the ends/necks. Note that $\ell_{\alpha,w}$ is close to $\ell_{0,0}$, in the sense that they differ over $\coprod_{i=1}^k[-N,N]$ (which may be viewed as a subset of $\coprod_{i=1}^k\mathbb R$ and of $(\coprod_{i=1}^k)_\alpha$) by a constant times $\left|\alpha\right|^\epsilon+\left|w\right|$ in $C^\ell$ for some fixed $\epsilon>0$ (depending on the flow on $\Delta^n$ from Definition \ref{simplexflows}) and any $\ell<\infty$. It follows that away from the ends/necks, the $C^\ell$ distance between $J(\ell_{\alpha,w}(A_y(\cdot)))$ on $C_\alpha$ and $J(\ell_{0,0}(A_0(\cdot)))$ on $C_0$ is bounded by a constant (depending on $\ell$) times $\left|\alpha\right|^\epsilon+\left|w\right|+\left|y\right|$, where we identify $C_0$ and $C_\alpha$ away from the ends/necks in the canonical way (any $\ell<\infty$). The same holds for $H((\ell_{\alpha,w}\times\operatorname{id}_{S^1})(A_y(\cdot)))$ and $H((\ell_{0,0}\times\operatorname{id}_{S^1})(A_0(\cdot)))$. It also follows that the distance between $x^i\in C_\alpha$ and (the image in $C_\alpha$ of) $x^i_0\in C_0$ is bounded by a constant times $|\alpha|^\epsilon+\left|w\right|$. Hence we conclude that away from the ends/necks, $\mathcal F_{\alpha,w,y}(0)$ differs from the left hand side of \eqref{delbareqnforuzeroHF} in $C^\ell$ by a constant times $\left|\alpha\right|^\epsilon+\left|w\right|+\left|y\right|$ for any $\ell<\infty$. It follows that the contribution of this region to the norm of $\mathcal F_{\alpha,w,y}(0)$ is bounded by a constant times $\left|\alpha\right|^\epsilon+\left|w\right|+\left|y\right|$.
nodes.statement_short: Away from ends/necks, $J$, $H$ and $x^i$ move by $O(|\alpha|^\epsilon+|w|+|y|)$, giving that bound.

nodes.name: Bubble ends
nodes.statement: We estimate $\mathcal F_{\alpha,w,y}(0)$ over the bubble ends. The reasoning above applies as written to imply that $\mathcal F_{\alpha,w,y}(0)$ is bounded in $C^\ell$ (with respect to the usual metric on $\tilde C_\alpha$) by a constant times $\left|\alpha\right|^\epsilon+\left|w\right|+\left|y\right|$ for any $\ell<\infty$. Since $\delta<1$, the weighted Sobolev norm over the bubble ends is also bounded by a constant times $\left|\alpha\right|^\epsilon+\left|w\right|+\left|y\right|$.
nodes.statement_short: Same $C^\ell$ bound on bubble ends; $\delta<1$ controls the weight.

nodes.name: Bubble necks
nodes.statement: We estimate $\mathcal F_{\alpha,w,y}(0)$ over the bubble necks $S^1\times[0,6S]$. The argument for the bubble ends applies to show that the contribution outside $S^1\times[S-1,5S+1]$ is bounded by a constant times $\left|\alpha\right|^\epsilon+\left|w\right|+\left|y\right|$. Over $S^1\times([S-1,S]\cup[5S,5S+1])$, we bound the expression termwise: both $u_\alpha$ and $A_y$ are $O(e^{-s})$ in all derivatives, so the contribution of this region is bounded by $\left|\alpha\right|^\epsilon$. Over $S^1\times[S,5S]$, only the term involving $X_H$ is nonzero, and since $A_y=O(e^{-s})$ in all derivatives, its contribution to the norm is bounded by a constant times $\left|\alpha\right|^\epsilon$ since $\delta<1$.
nodes.statement_short: On bubble necks: cutoff regions are $O(|\alpha|^\epsilon)$ by decay, and on $[S,5S]$ only the $X_H$ term survives, also $O(|\alpha|^\epsilon)$.

nodes.name: Strategy
nodes.statement: Recall that $D_{0,0,0}\kappa=0$; we will use this to estimate $D_{\alpha,w,y}\kappa_\alpha$ via the explicit expression for $D_{\alpha,w,y}$ from Lemma \ref{linearizedformulaHF}.
nodes.statement_short: Compare $D_{\alpha,w,y}\kappa_\alpha$ with $D_{0,0,0}\kappa=0$ via the explicit formula.

nodes.name: Main ends/necks
nodes.statement: We estimate $D_{\alpha,w,y}\kappa_\alpha$ over the main ends/necks. Over this region, the $\lambda$ terms vanish, and $J,H$ are the same for $(\alpha,w,y)$ as they are for $(0,0,0)$. Thus $D_{\alpha,w,y}\kappa_\alpha$ is supported inside $S^1\times([S-1,S+1]\cup[5S-1,5S+1])$ in the main necks, and vanishes in the main ends. From the exponential decay estimates \eqref{uzeromain}--\eqref{kappamain}, we obtain that the contribution to the norm of $D_{\alpha,w,y}\kappa_\alpha$ over the main ends/necks is bounded by a constant times $\left|\alpha\right|^\epsilon\left\|\kappa\right\|$.
nodes.statement_short: Supported near the cutoff regions; exponential decay gives $O(|\alpha|^\epsilon\|\kappa\|)$.

nodes.name: Away from ends/necks
nodes.statement: We estimate $D_{\alpha,w,y}\kappa_\alpha$ away from the ends/necks. As in the proof of Lemma \ref{mappregluingissmallHF}, the difference between $J,H$ for $(\alpha,w,y)$ and for $(0,0,0)$ is bounded in $C^\ell$ by a constant times $\left|\alpha\right|^\epsilon+\left|w\right|+\left|y\right|$ for any $\ell<\infty$; similarly for the distance between $x^i$ and $x^i_0$. It thus follows from the explicit form in Lemma \ref{linearizedformulaHF} that the contribution to the norm of $D_{\alpha,w,y}\kappa_\alpha$ over this region is bounded by a constant times $(\left|\alpha\right|^\epsilon+\left|w\right|+\left|y\right|)\left\|\kappa\right\|$.
nodes.statement_short: Perturbation of $J,H,x^i$ and the explicit formula bound the interior contribution.

nodes.name: Bubble ends
nodes.statement: Over the bubble ends, the same reasoning applies, and we obtain the desired bound since $\delta<1$.
nodes.statement_short: Bubble ends handled as the interior, using $\delta<1$.

nodes.name: Bubble necks
nodes.statement: We estimate $D_{\alpha,w,y}\kappa_\alpha$ over the bubble necks. Outside $S^1\times[S-1,5S+1]$, the reasoning for the bubble ends applies to show that the contribution is bounded as desired. Over $S^1\times([S-1,S+1]\cup[5S-1,5S+1])$, the exponential decay estimates on $u_0$ and $\kappa$, along with similar estimates on $A_y$, show that the contribution of this region is bounded by $\left|\alpha\right|^\epsilon\left\|\kappa\right\|$ for some $\epsilon>0$ since $\delta<1$. Over $S^1\times[S+1,5S-1]$, only the term involving $X_H$ is nonzero, and its contribution is bounded by a constant times $\left|\alpha\right|^\epsilon\left\|\kappa\right\|$ since $\delta<1$ and $A_y$ decays like $O(e^{-s})$ in all derivatives.
nodes.statement_short: Bubble necks: decay estimates on $u_0,\kappa,A_y$ give $O(|\alpha|^\epsilon\|\kappa\|)$.

nodes.name: Reduce to operator-norm bound
nodes.statement: In simpler terms, we bound the operator norm of the difference between the two diagonal compositions: \begin{equation} \left\|\mathsf{PT}\circ D_{0,0,0}-D_{0|\alpha,0,0}\circ\mathsf{PT}\right\|\leq c\left|\alpha\right|^\epsilon \end{equation} (this trivially implies the claimed statement).
nodes.statement_short: Reduce to bounding PT∘$D_{0,0,0}$ − $D_{0|\alpha,0,0}$∘PT in operator norm.

nodes.name: Localize the difference
nodes.statement: To show \eqref{betterPTcommutingoperatornormboundHF}, observe that the two operators only differ over the $S^1\times[S-1,\infty)$ subset of each end.
nodes.statement_short: The two operators differ only over $S^1\times[S-1,\infty)$ in each end.

nodes.name: Bound by C^k distance
nodes.statement: Now it follows from Lemma \ref{linearizedformulaHF} that the contribution to the operator norm over $S^1\times[S-1,\infty)$ is bounded by a constant times the $C^k$-distance between $u_0$ and $u_{0|\alpha}$ over $S^1\times[0,\infty)$.
nodes.statement_short: The linearized formula bounds the difference by the $C^k$-distance of $u_0$ and $u_{0|\alpha}$.

nodes.name: Decay estimates give |alpha|^epsilon
nodes.statement: The estimates \eqref{uzerobubble}, \eqref{uzeromain} imply that this distance is bounded by a constant times $\left|\alpha\right|^\epsilon$ (to be precise, the bubble ends contribute $\left|\alpha\right|^{1/6-\rho}$ and each main end contributes $\left|\alpha\right|^{\delta_i/6-\rho}$ for any $\rho>0$).
nodes.statement_short: Exponential decay of $u_0$ bounds that distance by $|\alpha|^\epsilon$.

nodes.name: Reduce to operator bound
nodes.statement: In simpler terms, we have $\left\|D_{0|\alpha,0,y}-(\operatorname{id}^{1,0}_\ast\otimes\operatorname{id}^{1,0})\circ D_{0|\alpha,0,0}\right\|\leq c\cdot\left|y\right|$, which trivially implies the claimed statement. To prove this, argue as follows.
nodes.statement_short: Reduce to $\|D_{0|\alpha,0,y}-(\mathrm{id}^{1,0}_*\otimes\mathrm{id}^{1,0})D_{0|\alpha,0,0}\|\leq c|y|$.

nodes.name: Compare coefficients
nodes.statement: We are comparing two first-order differential operators. Appealing to their explicit form from Lemma \ref{linearizedformulaHF}, we see that their coefficients differ by a constant times $\left|y\right|$ in $C^\ell$ for any $\ell<\infty$ (measuring with respect to the cylindrical coordinates $S^1\times[0,\infty)$ in the ends). It follows that we have the desired estimate.
nodes.statement_short: Coefficients from the linearized formula differ by $O(|y|)$ in $C^\ell$.

nodes.name: Enlarged top square
nodes.statement: We consider the following diagram, which is a copy of the top square in \eqref{biginversediagramHF} with one extra vector space and some extra maps (to be defined below). \begin{equation} \begin{tikzcd}[row sep = tiny] {}&W^{k-1,2,\delta,\delta}(\tilde C_\alpha,\Omega^{0,1}_{\tilde C_\alpha,j_y}\otimes_\mathbb C u_\alpha^\ast TM_{J(\ell_{\alpha,w}(A_y(\cdot)))})\ar[shift left=0.5ex]{dd}{\mathrm{break}'}\ar[rounded corners,to path={(\tikztostart) -- ([xshift=2ex]\tikztostart.east) -- ([xshift=2ex]\tikztotarget.east) \tikztonodes -- (\tikztotarget)}]{dddd}{\mathrm{break}}\\ W^{k,2,\delta,\delta}(C_\alpha,u_\alpha^\ast TM)_{D,H}\oplus E\ar{ru}{D_{\alpha,w,y}}\\ {}&W^{k-1,2,\delta,\delta}(\tilde C_0,\Omega^{0,1}_{\tilde C_0,j_y}\otimes_\mathbb C u_{0|\alpha}^\ast TM_{J(\ell_{\alpha,w}(A_y(\cdot)))})\ar[shift right=-0.5ex]{uu}{\mathrm{glue}}\ar[shift left=0.5ex]{dd}{(\operatorname{id}^{1,0})^{-1}}\\ W^{k,2,\delta,\delta}(C_0,u_{0|\alpha}^\ast TM)_{D,H}\oplus E\ar{uu}{\mathrm{glue}}\ar{rd}{D_{0|\alpha,0,y}}\ar{ru}{D_{\alpha,w,y}}\\ {}&W^{k-1,2,\delta,\delta}(\tilde C_0,\Omega^{0,1}_{\tilde C_0,j_y}\otimes_\mathbb C u_{0|\alpha}^\ast TM_{J(\ell_{0,0}(A_y(\cdot)))})\ar[shift right=-0.5ex]{uu}{\operatorname{id}^{1,0}} \end{tikzcd} \end{equation}
nodes.statement_short: Introduce an enlarged version of the top square with extra maps.

nodes.name: Meaning of the intermediate Sobolev space
nodes.statement: Since the almost complex structure $J(\ell_{\alpha,w}(A_y(\cdot)))$ is a function of a point in $C_\alpha$, we should remark immediately on what we mean by $W^{k-1,2,\delta,\delta}(\tilde C_0,\Omega^{0,1}_{\tilde C_0,j_y}\otimes_\mathbb C u_{0|\alpha}^\ast TM_{J(\ell_{\alpha,w}(A_y(\cdot)))})$. Away from the ends, the curve $C_0$ is identified canonically with $C_\alpha$, and this identification extends holomorphically to a (non-injective) map from $C_0$ to $C_\alpha$ defined outside the $S^1\times[4S,\infty)$ subsets of the ends. Thus there is a well-defined such $W^{k-1,2,\delta,\delta}$ space of sections on $C_0$ defined outside the $S^1\times[4S,\infty)$ subsets of the ends, valued in $\Omega^{0,1}_{\tilde C_0,j_y}\otimes_\mathbb C u_{0|\alpha}^\ast TM_{J(\ell_{\alpha,w}(A_y(\cdot)))}$. Now, for instance, the middle horizontal map $D_{\alpha,w,y}$ can be seen as giving a section in this $W^{k-1,2,\delta,\delta}$ space defined outside $S^1\times[4S,\infty)$. In the proof below, it is convenient to use this $W^{k-1,2,\delta,\delta}$ space of sections defined outside $S^1\times[4S,\infty)$, though we must be careful that the expressions we write are well-defined.
nodes.statement_short: Explain the $W^{k-1,2,\delta,\delta}$ space on $C_0$ defined outside $S^1\times[4S,\infty)$.

nodes.name: Define break' and glue on forms
nodes.statement: Let us define the rest of the maps in \eqref{topdiagrambigger}. The vertical map $\operatorname{break}$ has been factored as $(\operatorname{id}^{1,0})^{-1}\circ\operatorname{break}'$ in the obvious way. Finally, let us define the map: \begin{equation} W^{k-1,2,\delta,\delta}(\tilde C_0,\Omega^{0,1}_{\tilde C_0,j_y}\otimes_\mathbb C u_{0|\alpha}^\ast TM_{J(\ell_{\alpha,w}(A_y(\cdot)))})\xrightarrow{\mathrm{glue}}W^{k-1,2,\delta,\delta}(\tilde C_\alpha,\Omega^{0,1}_{\tilde C_\alpha,j_y}\otimes_\mathbb C u_\alpha^\ast TM_{J(\ell_{\alpha,w}(A_y(\cdot)))}) \end{equation} Let $\eta\in W^{k-1,2,\delta,\delta}(\tilde C_0,\Omega^{0,1}_{\tilde C_0,j_y}\otimes_\mathbb C u_{0|\alpha}^\ast TM_{J(\ell_{\alpha,w}(A_y(\cdot)))})$. Away from the necks of $C_\alpha$, $\operatorname{glue}(\eta)$ is simply $\eta$. In any particular bubble neck $S^1\times[0,6S]\subseteq C_\alpha$, we define: \begin{equation} \operatorname{glue}(\eta)(t,s):=\begin{cases} \eta(t,s)&s\leq 2S\cr \chi(4S-s)\eta(t,s)+\chi(4S-s')\eta(t',s')&2S\leq s\leq 4S\cr \eta(t',s')&4S\leq s \end{cases} \end{equation} (this definition also applies over the main necks with the obvious adjustment). Note that $\operatorname{glue}\circ\operatorname{break}'$ is the identity map.
nodes.statement_short: Factor break as $(\mathrm{id}^{1,0})^{-1}\circ$break' and define glue on (0,1)-forms; glue∘break' = id.

nodes.name: Triangle inequality split
nodes.statement: Now suppose that $D_{0|\alpha,0,y}\xi=\operatorname{break}(\eta)$; we must show that: \begin{equation} \left\|D_{\alpha,w,y}(\operatorname{glue}(\xi))-\eta\right\|_{k-1,2,\delta,\delta}\leq c\cdot\bigl(\left|\alpha\right|^\epsilon+\left|w\right|\bigr)\left\|\xi\right\|_{k,2,\delta,\delta} \end{equation} Using the triangle inequality and the fact that $\eta=\operatorname{glue}(\operatorname{break}'(\eta))=\operatorname{glue}(\operatorname{id}^{1,0}(D_{0|\alpha,0,y}\xi))$, we conclude that $\left\|D_{\alpha,w,y}(\operatorname{glue}(\xi))-\eta\right\|$ is bounded above by: \begin{equation*} \left\|D_{\alpha,w,y}(\operatorname{glue}(\xi))-\operatorname{glue}(D_{\alpha,w,y}(\xi))\right\|+\left\|\operatorname{glue}\left[D_{\alpha,w,y}(\xi)-\operatorname{id}^{1,0}(D_{0|\alpha,0,y}(\xi))\right]\right\| \end{equation*} We now estimate each term separately.
nodes.statement_short: Split the error into a commutator term and a difference-of-operators term.

nodes.name: Commutator term
nodes.statement: To estimate $\left\|D_{\alpha,w,y}(\operatorname{glue}(\xi))-\operatorname{glue}(D_{\alpha,w,y}(\xi))\right\|$, argue as follows. The difference is only nonzero over the regions $S^1\times([2S,2S+1]\cup[4S-1,4S])$ of each neck. Now the norm is bounded by $\left\|\xi\right\|e^{-2S\delta}$ (calculation left to the reader), where the factor of $e^{-2S\delta}$ comes as the ratio of the weight given to $S^1\times[4S-1,4S]$ inside a neck vs inside an end; this gives the desired bound since $\delta>0$.
nodes.statement_short: The commutator is supported on cut-off regions and is bounded by $e^{-2S\delta}\|\xi\|$.

nodes.name: Difference-of-operators term
nodes.statement: To estimate $\left\|\operatorname{glue}\left[D_{\alpha,w,y}(\xi)-\operatorname{id}^{1,0}(D_{0|\alpha,0,y}\xi)\right]\right\|$, argue as follows. This is bounded by a constant times the $(k-1,2,\delta,\delta)$-norm of $D_{\alpha,w,y}(\xi)-\operatorname{id}^{1,0}(D_{0|\alpha,0,y}\xi)$ over the complement of the subsets $S^1\times[4S,\infty)$ of the ends. Now this is bounded by $(\left|\alpha\right|^\epsilon+\left|w\right|)\left\|\xi\right\|_{k,2,\delta,\delta}$ using the reasoning from Lemma \ref{approxmiddleHF}.
nodes.statement_short: Bound the second term by $(|\alpha|^\epsilon+|w|)\|\xi\|$ as in the middle-square lemma.

nodes.name: Uniform bound on T
nodes.statement: It is easy to see that all the maps in \eqref{biginversediagramHF} are uniformly bounded. Hence $\left\|T_{\alpha,w,y}\right\|\leq c$ as $(\alpha,w,y)\to 0$.
nodes.statement_short: All maps in the diagram are uniformly bounded, so $\|T\|\leq c$.

nodes.name: Approximate inverse property
nodes.statement: Now Lemma \ref{bootstrappingapprox} combined with Lemmas \ref{approxbottomHF}, \ref{approxmiddleHF}, \ref{approxtopHF} show that for $(\alpha,w,y)\to 0$, we have $\left\|D_{\alpha,w,y} T_{\alpha,w,y}-\mathbf 1\right\|\to 0$.
nodes.statement_short: Bootstrapping lemma with the three square estimates gives $\|DT-1\|\to 0$.

nodes.name: Image condition
nodes.statement: We observed earlier that $\operatorname{im} T_{\alpha,w,y}\subseteq\ker L_\alpha$.
nodes.statement_short: Recall the earlier observation $\operatorname{im}T\subseteq\ker L_\alpha$.

nodes.name: Same as Gromov--Witten case
nodes.statement: The proof is essentially identical to the proof of Proposition \ref{newtoniteration}; we write it out anyway.
nodes.statement_short: Note the proof parallels the Gromov--Witten Newton iteration.

nodes.name: Newton iteration
nodes.statement: In fact, we will show that $\kappa_{\alpha,w,y}$ is given explicitly as the limit of the Newton iteration: \begin{align} \xi_0&:=\kappa_\alpha\\ \xi_n&:=\xi_{n-1}-Q_{\alpha,w,y}\mathcal F_{\alpha,w,y}\xi_{n-1} \end{align}
nodes.statement_short: Define the Newton iteration $\xi_n$ starting from $\kappa_\alpha$.

nodes.name: Contraction on the domain
nodes.statement: By Lemma \ref{contractionpropHF}, the map $\xi\mapsto\xi-Q_{\alpha,w,y}\mathcal F_{\alpha,w,y}\xi$ is a $\frac 12$-contraction mapping when restricted to: \begin{equation} \{\xi\in\kappa_\alpha+\operatorname{im} Q_{\alpha,w,y}:\left\|\xi\right\|_{k,2,\delta,\delta}\leq c'\} \end{equation}
nodes.statement_short: The iteration map is a $\frac12$-contraction on the affine ball.

nodes.name: Reduce to self-mapping
nodes.statement: To finish the proof, it suffices to show that (for sufficiently small $(\alpha,w,y,\kappa)$) \eqref{domainofcontractionHF} is nonempty and is mapped to itself by $\xi\mapsto\xi-Q_{\alpha,w,y}\mathcal F_{\alpha,w,y}\xi$.
nodes.statement_short: It suffices that the ball is nonempty and mapped into itself.

nodes.name: Ball nonempty; kappa_alpha almost holomorphic
nodes.statement: We know that $\left\|\kappa_\alpha\right\|_{k,2,\delta,\delta}\to 0$ as $\kappa\to 0$ (uniformly in $(\alpha,w,y)$), so \eqref{domainofcontractionHF} is nonempty. By using Proposition \ref{quadestimateHF} with $(\xi_1,\xi_2)=(0,\kappa_\alpha)$ and Lemmas \ref{mappregluingissmallHF} and \ref{pregluingKestimateHF}, we conclude that: \begin{equation} \left\|\mathcal F_{\alpha,w,y}\kappa_\alpha\right\|_{k-1,2,\delta,\delta}\to 0 \end{equation} as $(\alpha,w,y,\kappa)\to 0$.
nodes.statement_short: Nonemptiness, and $\|\mathcal F(\kappa_\alpha)\|\to 0$ from the quadratic estimate and pregluing estimates.

nodes.name: Self-mapping by contraction
nodes.statement: Since the operator norm of $Q_{\alpha,w,y}$ is bounded uniformly as $(\alpha,w,y)\to 0$, we see that $\kappa_\alpha$ is almost fixed by $\xi\mapsto\xi-Q_{\alpha,w,y}\mathcal F_{\alpha,w,y}\xi$ as $(\alpha,w,y,\kappa)\to 0$. It then follows from the contraction property that $\xi\mapsto\xi-Q_{\alpha,w,y}\mathcal F_{\alpha,w,y}\xi$ maps \eqref{domainofcontractionHF} to itself.
nodes.statement_short: $\kappa_\alpha$ is almost fixed, so the contraction maps the ball into itself.

nodes.name: Outline
nodes.statement: The proof follows the same basic outline as the proof of Proposition \ref{continuityofgluing}; some parts of the proof are identical, and we will omit these. The key ingredient is our precise control of the image of the right inverse $Q_{\alpha,w,y}$ (specifically, that $\operatorname{im} Q_{\alpha,w,y}=\ker L_\alpha$).
nodes.statement_short: Follow the Gromov--Witten proof; key input $\operatorname{im}Q=\ker L_\alpha$.

nodes.name: Convergent net
nodes.statement: Suppose $(\alpha_i,w_i,y_i,\kappa_i)\to(\alpha,w,y,\kappa)$ is a convergent net.\footnote{We could restrict to sequences rather than nets since $\mathbb C^d\times(\mathbb R_{\geq 0}^{k-1})^{\leq\mathfrak s}\times\mathbb R^\ast\times\prod_{i=1}^{k\prime}(H^i)^{\leq\mathfrak s}\times K$ is first countable. However, this would not make the argument any simpler.} We will show that: \begin{equation} (u_{\alpha_i,w_i,y_i,\kappa_i},e_{\alpha_i,w_i,y_i,\kappa_i})\to(u_{\alpha,w,y,\kappa},e_{\alpha,w,y,\kappa}) \end{equation}
nodes.statement_short: Take a convergent net of parameters; aim to show convergence of glued maps.

nodes.name: Reduce to fixed kappa
nodes.statement: First, observe that the argument from the proof of Proposition \ref{continuityofgluing} applies verbatim to give that in fact it suffices to show that: \begin{equation} (u_{\alpha_i,w_i,y_i,\kappa},e_{\alpha_i,w_i,y_i,\kappa})\to(u_{\alpha,w,y,\kappa},e_{\alpha,w,y,\kappa}) \end{equation} Now recall that by definition: \begin{align} u_{\alpha,w,y,\kappa}&=\exp_{u_\alpha}\kappa_{\alpha,w,y}&\kappa_{\alpha,w,y}&=\kappa_\alpha+\xi&\text{for some }\xi&\in\operatorname{im} Q_{\alpha,w,y} \end{align}
nodes.statement_short: Reduce to fixed $\kappa$ and recall $\kappa_{\alpha,w,y}=\kappa_\alpha+\xi$ with $\xi\in\operatorname{im}Q$.

nodes.name: Transport the correction xi
nodes.statement:
Now we define $\xi_{\alpha_i}\in W^{k,2,\delta,\delta}(C_{\alpha_i},u_{\alpha_i}^\ast TX)_D\oplus E$ by ``pregluing'' $\xi$ from $C_\alpha$ to $C_{\alpha_i}$ as follows. Note that we may assume without loss of generality that at the nodes where $\alpha
e 0$, we also have $\alpha_i
e 0$. Away from the ends/necks of $C_{\alpha_i}$, we set $\xi_{\alpha_i}=\xi$. Note that for every end of $C_{\alpha_i}$, there is a corresponding end of $C_\alpha$, so we may also simply set $\xi_{\alpha_i}=\xi$ over the ends of $C_{\alpha_i}$. Over the necks of $C_{\alpha_i}$ for which $\alpha=0$, we define $\xi_{\alpha_i}$ via \eqref{kernelpregluingformulaHFbubble}--\eqref{kernelpregluingformulaHFmain} (note that this is reasonable since $\xi$ satisfies the estimates \eqref{kappabubble}, \eqref{kappamain} as a consequence of Proposition ef{neckestimateHF}). Over the necks of $C_{\alpha_i}$ for which $\alpha
e 0$, we define $\xi_{\alpha_i}$ as:  egin{equation} \xi_{\alpha_i}(s,t):=\mathsf{PT}_{u_{\alpha}(t,f_i(s))	o u_{\alpha_i}(t,s)}[\xi(t,f_i(s)))] \end{equation} where $f_i:[0,6S_i]	o[0,6S]$ is smooth and satisfies:  egin{align} f_i(s):=& egin{cases} s&s\leq S-2\cr s-3S_i+3S&3S_i-2S+2\leq s\leq 3S_i+2S-2\cr s-6S_i+6S&6S_i-S+2\leq s\cr \end{cases}\ f_i([S-2,3S_i-2S+2])&\subseteq[S-2,S+2]\ f_i([3S_i+2S-2,6S_i-S+2])&\subseteq[5S-2,5S+2] \end{align} so that $f_i	o\operatorname{id}$ uniformly in all derivatives as $S_i	o S$. More informally, $f_i$ is smooth and matches up $[0,S-2],[S+2,5S-2],[5S+2,6S]\subseteq[0,6S]$ with corresponding intervals of the same length inside $[0,6S_i]$, symmetrically.
nodes.statement_short: Define $\xi_{\alpha_i}$ by pregluing $\xi$ to $C_{\alpha_i}$, using a reparametrization $f_i$ on persisting necks.

nodes.name: Reduce to almost-holomorphicity
nodes.statement: Now at this point we appeal to the corresponding arguments from the proof of Proposition \ref{continuityofgluing}, which apply as written (using the fact that $\operatorname{im} Q_{\alpha,w,y}=\ker L_\alpha$) and imply that it suffices to show that: \begin{equation} \left\|\mathcal F_{\alpha_i,w_i,y_i}(\kappa_{\alpha_i}+\xi_{\alpha_i})\right\|_{k-1,2,\delta,\delta}\to 0 \end{equation} Recall that $\mathcal F_{\alpha,w,y}(\kappa_\alpha+\xi)=0$; we will use this to estimate $\mathcal F_{\alpha_i,w_i,y_i}(\kappa_{\alpha_i}+\xi_{\alpha_i})$.
nodes.statement_short: By the Gromov--Witten argument it suffices that $\mathcal F(\kappa_{\alpha_i}+\xi_{\alpha_i})\to 0$.

nodes.name: Away from ends and necks
nodes.statement: Away from the ends/necks of $C_{\alpha_i}$, it is clear by definition that $\mathcal F_{\alpha_i,w_i,y_i}(\kappa_{\alpha_i}+\xi_{\alpha_i})\to\mathcal F_{\alpha,w,y}(\kappa_\alpha+\xi)$ uniformly in all derivatives. Thus the contribution to the norm of $\mathcal F_{\alpha_i,w_i,y_i}(\kappa_{\alpha_i}+\xi_{\alpha_i})$ over this region approaches zero.
nodes.statement_short: Uniform convergence away from ends/necks.

nodes.name: Necks corresponding to necks
nodes.statement: Over the necks of $C_{\alpha_i}$ which correspond to necks of $C_\alpha$, we again have uniform convergence in all derivatives, so the contribution of these regions approaches zero as well.
nodes.statement_short: Uniform convergence over persisting necks.

nodes.name: Ends
nodes.statement: We estimate the contribution over the ends of $C_{\alpha_i}$ (recall that these necessarily correspond to ends of $C_\alpha$). Over main ends, we have $\mathcal F_{\alpha_i,w_i,y_i}(\kappa_{\alpha_i}+\xi_{\alpha_i})=\mathcal F_{\alpha,w,y}(\kappa_\alpha+\xi)$. Now the convergence $\mathcal F_{\alpha_i,w_i,y_i}(\kappa_{\alpha_i}+\xi_{\alpha_i})\to\mathcal F_{\alpha,w,y}(\kappa_\alpha+\xi)$ uniformly in all derivatives is valid near the bubble nodes in the usual metric on $C_{\alpha_i}=C_\alpha$. It follows that we also have convergence in the relevant $\delta$-weighted Sobolev norm since $\delta<1$. Thus the contribution of this region to the norm approaches zero.
nodes.statement_short: Convergence in the weighted norm over ends since $\delta<1$.

nodes.name: New necks
nodes.statement: Finally, let us estimate the contribution to the norm over the necks of $C_{\alpha_i}$ which correspond to ends of $C_\alpha$. We treat main necks and bubble necks separately. Over main necks, $\mathcal F_{\alpha_i,w_i,y_i}(\kappa_{\alpha_i}+\xi_{\alpha_i})$ is supported inside $S^1\times([S-1,S+1],[5S-1,5S+1])$. The contribution of this region to its norm goes to zero, as follows using the exponential decrease on $\kappa$ and $\xi$ from Proposition \ref{neckestimateHF} and the fact that $\delta<\delta_i$. Over bubble ends, $\mathcal F_{\alpha_i,w_i,y_i}(\kappa_{\alpha_i}+\xi_{\alpha_i})$ converges to $\mathcal F_{\alpha,w,y}(\kappa_\alpha+\xi)$ uniformly in all derivatives over the complement of $S^1\times[S-1,5S+1]$ (measured with respect to the usual metric on $C_0$), and hence the contribution of this region to the weighted norm goes to zero since $\delta<1$. Over $S^1\times([S-1,S+1]\cup[5S-1,5S+1])$, the smoothness of $\kappa$ and $\xi$ over $C_\alpha$ and the fact that $\delta<1$ shows that the contribution of this region to the norm goes to zero (since $S\to\infty$). Finally, over $S^1\times[S+1,5S-1]$, both $u_{\alpha_i}$ and $\kappa_{\alpha_i}+\xi_{\alpha_i}$ are constant, so $\mathcal F_{\alpha_i,w_i,y_i}(\kappa_{\alpha_i}+\xi_{\alpha_i})$ is simply: \begin{equation*} \mathsf{PT}_{\exp_{u_0(n)}(\kappa(n)+\xi(n))\to u_0(n)}^{\ell_{\alpha_i,w_i}(A_{y_i}(\cdot))}\Bigl(2d(\operatorname{proj}_{S^1}A_{y_i})\otimes X_{H((\ell_{\alpha_i,w_i}\times\operatorname{id}_{S^1})(A_{y_i}(\cdot)))}\Bigr)^{0,1}_{j,J(\ell_{\alpha_i,w_i}(A_{y_i}(\cdot)))} \end{equation*} The norm of this expression over $S^1\times[S+1,5S-1]$ approaches zero since $A_{y_i}=O(e^{-s})$ in all derivatives and $\delta<1$.
nodes.statement_short: Over newly formed necks use exponential decay from the cylinder estimate and decay of $A_y$.

nodes.name: Source of the argument
nodes.statement: This proof is adapted from Salamon \cite[p170, Lemma 2.11]{salamonnotes}.
nodes.statement_short: Cite Salamon's lecture notes.

nodes.name: Floer equation in exponential coordinates
nodes.statement: We have by assumption that $\partial_su+J(u)(\partial_tu-X_H(u))=0$, where $u(t,s)=\exp_{\gamma(t)}\xi(t,s)$. Now we may rewrite this equation in exponential coordinates in terms of $\xi$ as follows. Denote by $\partial_t$ the connection $\mathcal L_{X_H}$ on $\gamma^\ast TM$, which is given by the Lie derivative with respect to $X_H$. Now the equation for $u$ is equivalent to: \begin{equation} \partial_s\xi+J\partial_t\xi+A(\xi)\partial_t\xi+Q(\xi)=0 \end{equation} for certain smooth (non-linear) bundle maps $A:\gamma^\ast TM\to\operatorname{End}(\gamma^\ast TM)$ and $Q:\gamma^\ast TM\to\gamma^\ast TM$. We have $A(0)=0$, $Q(0)=0$, and $Q'(0,\cdot)=0$ (we denote by $A'$ and $Q'$ their ``vertical'' derivatives).
nodes.statement_short: Rewrite Floer's equation as $\partial_s\xi+J\partial_t\xi+A(\xi)\partial_t\xi+Q(\xi)=0$.

nodes.name: Energy function and goal
nodes.statement: Now we let: \begin{equation} f(s):=\int_{S^1}\left|\xi(t,s)\right|^2dt=\left\|\xi\right\|_2^2 \end{equation} and we will show that $f''(s)\geq(1-o(1))4\delta^2f(s)$, where $o(1)$ denotes a quantity which can be made arbitrarily small by choosing $\epsilon>0$ sufficiently small. We have: \begin{equation} f''(s)=2\int_{S^1}\left|\partial_s\xi\right|^2dt+2\int_{S^1}\langle\xi,\partial_s\partial_s\xi\rangle\,dt=2\left\|\partial_s\xi\right\|_2^2+2\langle\xi,\partial_s\partial_s\xi\rangle \end{equation} and we will now prove estimates $\left\|\partial_s\xi\right\|_2^2\geq(1-o(1))\delta^2f(s)$ and $\langle\xi,\partial_s\partial_s\xi\rangle\geq(1-o(1))\delta^2f(s)$. Recall that $J\partial_t$ is self-adjoint and that $\left\|J\partial_t\xi\right\|_2\geq\delta\left\|\xi\right\|_2$.
nodes.statement_short: Set $f(s)=\|\xi\|_2^2$; aim for $f''\geq(1-o(1))4\delta^2 f$ via two estimates.

nodes.name: Bound on ||d_s xi||
