nodes.statement: To bound $\left\|\partial_s\xi\right\|_2^2$, we write: \begin{align} \left\|\partial_s\xi\right\|_2&=\left\|J\partial_t\xi+A(\xi)\partial_t\xi+Q(\xi)\right\|_2\cr &\geq\left\|J\partial_t\xi\right\|_2-\left\|A(\xi)\partial_t\xi\right\|_2-\left\|Q(\xi)\right\|_2\cr &\geq\left\|J\partial_t\xi\right\|_2-\left\|A(\xi)\right\|_\infty\left\|\partial_t\xi\right\|_2-c\left\|\xi\right\|_\infty\left\|\xi\right\|_2\cr &=\left\|J\partial_t\xi\right\|_2-o(1)\left\|J\partial_t\xi\right\|_2-o(1)\left\|\xi\right\|_2\geq(1-o(1))\delta\left\|\xi\right\|_2 \end{align} and thus $\left\|\partial_s\xi\right\|_2^2\geq(1-o(1))\delta^2f(s)$.
nodes.statement_short: Spectral gap gives $\|\partial_s\xi\|_2^2\geq(1-o(1))\delta^2 f$.

nodes.name: Bound on <xi, d_s^2 xi>
nodes.statement: To bound $\langle\xi,\partial_s\partial_s\xi\rangle$, we write: \begin{align} \langle\xi,\partial_s\partial_s\xi\rangle&=-\langle\xi,\partial_s[J\partial_t\xi+A(\xi)\partial_t\xi+Q(\xi)]\rangle\cr &=-\langle J\partial_t\xi,\partial_s\xi\rangle-\langle\xi,A'(\xi,\partial_s\xi)\partial_t\xi\rangle-\langle\xi,A(\xi)\partial_t\partial_s\xi\rangle-\langle\xi,Q'(\xi,\partial_s\xi)\rangle \end{align} Now substituting in $\partial_s\xi=-J\partial_t\xi-A(\xi)\partial_t\xi-Q(\xi)$, we obtain the following: \begin{align} \langle\xi,\partial_s\partial_s\xi\rangle=\left\|J\partial_t\xi\right\|_2^2 &+\langle J\partial_t\xi,A(\xi)\partial_t\xi\rangle\cr &+\langle J\partial_t\xi,Q(\xi)\rangle\cr &+\langle\xi,A'(\xi,[J+A(\xi)]\partial_t\xi)\partial_t\xi\rangle\cr &+\langle\xi,A'(\xi,Q(\xi))\partial_t\xi\rangle\cr &+\langle\xi,A(\xi)\partial_t([J+A(\xi)]\partial_t\xi)\rangle\cr &+\langle\xi,A(\xi)\partial_t(Q(\xi))\rangle\cr &+\langle\xi,Q'(\xi,[J+A(\xi)]\partial_t\xi)\rangle\cr &+\langle\xi,Q'(\xi,Q(\xi))\rangle \end{align} The first term $\left\|J\partial_t\xi\right\|_2^2$ is the main term; let us estimate the remaining error terms. The first error term is bounded by $\left\|\xi\right\|_\infty\left\|J\partial_t\xi\right\|_2^2$, the second by $\left\|\xi\right\|_\infty\left\|\xi\right\|_2\left\|J\partial_t\xi\right\|_2$, the third by $\left\|\xi\right\|_\infty\left\|J\partial_t\xi\right\|_2^2$, the fourth by $\left\|\xi\right\|_\infty^2\left\|\xi\right\|_2\left\|J\partial_t\xi\right\|_2$, the fifth by $\left\|\xi\right\|_\infty\left\|J\partial_t\xi\right\|^2+\left\|\xi\right\|_\infty\left\|\xi\right\|_2\left\|J\partial_t\xi\right\|_2$ (integrate by parts to move the outermost $\partial_t$ onto $\xi$, $A(\xi)$, and $\langle\cdot,\cdot\rangle$), the sixth by $\left\|\xi\right\|_\infty^2\left\|\xi\right\|_2\left\|J\partial_t\xi\right\|_2$, the seventh by $\left\|\xi\right\|_\infty\left\|\xi\right\|_2\left\|J\partial_t\xi\right\|_2$, and the eighth by $\left\|\xi\right\|_\infty^2\left\|\xi\right\|_2^2$. All of these are $o(1)\left\|J\partial_t\xi\right\|_2^2$, so we conclude that $\langle\xi,\partial_s\partial_s\xi\rangle\geq(1-o(1))\delta^2f(s)$. Combining the above estimates, we obtain the desired inequality $f''(s)\geq(1-o(1))4\delta^2f(s)$.
nodes.statement_short: Expand, substitute the equation, and bound eight error terms; conclude the convexity inequality.

nodes.name: Maximum principle
nodes.statement: Now we have the following maximum principle for the differential inequality $g''(s)\geq r^2g(s)$. Namely, suppose that $g:[a,b]\to\mathbb R_{\geq 0}$ satisfies $g''(s)\geq r^2g(s)$ and that $G:[a,b]\to\mathbb R_{\geq 0}$ satisfies $G''(s)=r^2G(s)$; if $g\leq G$ at the endpoints $a,b$, then it follows that $g\leq G$ over the whole interval $[a,b]$ (one may easily derive a contradiction by assuming that, on the contrary, $g=G$ at $a_1,b_1$ and $g>G$ on $(a_1,b_1)$ for $a\leq a_1<b_1\leq b$). Specializing to the case at hand, we have: \begin{align*} f(s)&\leq e^{-(1-o(1))2\delta s}f(0)&&\text{in the case of }S^1\times[0,\infty)\\ f(s)&\leq e^{-(1-o(1))2\delta s}f(0)+e^{-(1-o(1))2\delta(N-s)}f(N)&&\text{in the case of }S^1\times[0,N] \end{align*}
nodes.statement_short: A maximum principle for $g''\geq r^2 g$ gives exponential decay of $f$.

nodes.name: Upgrade L^2 to C^k bounds
nodes.statement: Now Lemma \ref{Ltwocontrolsinnbhd} below asserts that for a $J$-holomorphic curve $u_0$ and a sufficiently small perturbation thereof $u=\exp_{u_0}\xi$ which is also $J$-holomorphic, we have uniform bounds on all derivatives of $\xi$ (away from the boundary) in terms of the $L^2$-norm of $\xi$. Applying this where $u_0$ is the trivial cylinder over $\gamma(t)$, we conclude that our bounds on $f(s)$ imply the desired result.
nodes.statement_short: Local elliptic lemma turns $L^2$ decay into decay of all derivatives.

nodes.name: Elliptic equation for xi
nodes.statement: By assumption, we have: \begin{align} u_x+J(u)u_y&=0\\ (u+\xi)_x+J(u+\xi)(u+\xi)_y&=0 \end{align} which together imply that: \begin{equation} \xi_x+J(u+\xi)\xi_y=[J(u)-J(u+\xi)]u_y \end{equation} which we prefer to write as: \begin{equation} (\partial_x+B\partial_y)\xi=A(\xi) \end{equation} where $B:[0,1]^2\to\operatorname{End}(\mathbb R^{2n})$ denotes $J(u+\xi)$ and $A:[0,1]^2\times\mathbb R^{2n}\to\mathbb R^{2n}$ denotes $A(\xi)=[J(u)-J(u+\xi)]u_y$.
nodes.statement_short: Subtract the two holomorphic equations to get $(\partial_x+B\partial_y)\xi=A(\xi)$.

nodes.name: Bounds on A
nodes.statement: By definition, we have $A(0)=0$ and: \begin{equation} \left|D^kA\right|\leq c_k \end{equation} for some $c_k<\infty$ depending only on upper bounds on $\left\|J\right\|_{C^\ell}$ and $\left\|u\right\|_{C^\ell}$ for some $\ell=\ell(k)<\infty$.
nodes.statement_short: Derivatives of $A$ are bounded.

nodes.name: Bounds on B
nodes.statement: By definition, we have $B^2=-1$; let us now argue that we also have: \begin{equation} \left|D^kB\right|\leq c_k \end{equation} for sufficiently small $\epsilon>0$ and $c_k<\infty$ as before. Indeed, for sufficiently small $\epsilon>0$, we may apply the Gromov--Schwarz lemma to $u+\xi$ and conclude that $|D\xi|\leq c<\infty$ depending only on upper bounds on $\left\|J\right\|_{C^\ell}$ and $\left\|u\right\|_{C^\ell}$ for some $\ell<\infty$. Now Lemma \ref{Woneinftycontrolsall} applied to $u+\xi$ gives $|D^k\xi|\leq c_k<\infty$, which implies the desired bound on the derivatives of $B$.
nodes.statement_short: Gromov--Schwarz and a $W^{1,\infty}$-to-$C^k$ lemma bound derivatives of $B$.

nodes.name: Laplacian equation with cut-off
nodes.statement: Now we apply $(\partial_x-B\partial_y)$ to both sides of \eqref{ellipticforxi} to obtain: \begin{equation} \Delta\xi=(\partial_x-B\partial_y)A(\xi)-((\partial_x-B\partial_y)B)(\xi_y) \end{equation} For any smooth function $\phi:[0,1]^2\to\mathbb R_{\geq 0}$ supported in the interior of $[0,1]^2$, we thus have: \begin{equation*} \Delta(\phi\xi)=\xi\Delta\phi+2\phi_x\xi_x+2\phi_y\xi_y+\phi\cdot(\partial_x-B\partial_y)A(\xi)-\phi\cdot((\partial_x-B\partial_y)B)(\xi_y) \end{equation*}
nodes.statement_short: Apply $\partial_x-B\partial_y$ to get a Laplace equation and multiply by a cut-off $\phi$.

nodes.name: Elliptic bootstrapping
nodes.statement: Now the desired result follows from the usual bootstrapping of the elliptic regularity estimates for the Laplacian on $\mathbb R^2$, namely $\left\|f\right\|_{H^{s+2}}\leq c_s\left\|f+\Delta f\right\|_{H^s}$ (the first step being the case $s=-1$). We may shrink the support of $\phi$ slightly at each step, so there is no need to worry about regularity near the boundary.
nodes.statement_short: Bootstrap elliptic estimates for the Laplacian, shrinking the cut-off at each step.

nodes.name: Reduce to smooth-domain locus
nodes.statement: To identify the orientation sheaf of $\overline{\mathcal M}(\sigma,p,q)$ with $\mathfrak o_\sigma\otimes\mathfrak o_{p,q}$, it suffices to identify the orientation sheaf of every $\overline{\mathcal M}(\sigma,p,q)_I^\mathrm{reg}$ with $\mathfrak o_{E_I}\otimes\mathfrak o_\sigma\otimes\mathfrak o_{p,q}$ in a compatible way (for all finite subsets $I\subseteq\mathcal A(\sigma,p,q)^{\geq\mathfrak s^\mathrm{top}}$). Moreover, it suffices to make this identification over the open subset $\overline{\mathcal M}(\sigma,p,q)_I^{\mathrm{reg}\circ}\subseteq\overline{\mathcal M}(\sigma,p,q)_I^\mathrm{reg}$ where the domain curve is smooth (it then automatically extends uniquely to all of $\overline{\mathcal M}(\sigma,p,q)_I^\mathrm{reg}$, by virtue of the local topological description of $\overline{\mathcal M}(\sigma,p,q)_I^\mathrm{reg}$ given by the gluing map); we may also check compatibility with the inclusions $I\subseteq J$ over $\overline{\mathcal M}(\sigma,p,q)_I^{\mathrm{reg}\circ}$.
nodes.statement_short: It suffices to identify orientation sheaves of thickened regular loci compatibly, over the locus of smooth domains.
nodes.section: C.13.3 Orientations on thickened moduli spaces $\overline{\mathcal M}(\sigma,p,q)_I^\mathrm{reg}$

nodes.name: Orientation via kernels
nodes.statement: Now the kernel $\tilde K=\ker D$ of the linearization \eqref{linearizedstd} forms a vector bundle over $\overline{\mathcal M}(\sigma,p,q)_I^{\mathrm{reg}\circ}$, and the orientation sheaf of $\overline{\mathcal M}(\sigma,p,q)_I^{\mathrm{reg}\circ}$ is isomorphic to $\mathfrak o_\sigma\otimes\mathfrak o_{\tilde K}$ (to see this, one must distinguish the two cases $\dim\sigma>0$ and $\dim\sigma=0$). Now we have $\mathfrak o_{\tilde K}=\mathfrak o_D=\mathfrak o_{D_\text{hol}}=\mathfrak o_{E_I}\otimes\mathfrak o_{p,q}$; this defines a fiberwise isomorphism of $\mathfrak o_{\tilde K}$ with $\mathfrak o_{E_I}\otimes\mathfrak o_{p,q}$, and since the operators $D$ and $D_\text{hol}$ vary nicely over the base $\overline{\mathcal M}(\sigma,p,q)_I^{\mathrm{reg}\circ}$, it is easy to see that this is in fact an isomorphism of sheaves. Thus we have the desired identification.
nodes.statement_short: Orientation sheaf $\cong\mathfrak o_\sigma\otimes\mathfrak o_{\tilde K}$ and $\mathfrak o_{\tilde K}=\mathfrak o_D=\mathfrak o_{D_\mathrm{hol}}=\mathfrak o_{E_I}\otimes\mathfrak o_{p,q}$.
nodes.section: C.13.3 Orientations on thickened moduli spaces $\overline{\mathcal M}(\sigma,p,q)_I^\mathrm{reg}$

nodes.name: Face boundary map
nodes.statement: Now let us show that the boundary map induced by \eqref{hforface} coincides with the tautological map \eqref{hforfaceor} (this just amounts to chasing definitions). Let $\mathfrak s\in\mathcal S_{\overline{\mathcal M}}(\sigma,p,q)$ denote the stratum $(\sigma|[0\ldots\hat k\ldots n],p,q)$ (i.e.\ the stratum consisting of trajectories over $\sigma$ which factor through $\sigma|[0\ldots\hat k\ldots n]$). Now on the space $\overline{\mathcal M}(\sigma|[0\ldots\hat k\ldots n],p,q)=\overline{\mathcal M}(\sigma,p,q)^{\leq\mathfrak s}$, we have three implicit atlases: \begin{equation} \mathcal A(\sigma|[0\ldots\hat k\ldots n],p,q)^{\geq\mathfrak s^\mathrm{top}}\subseteq\mathcal A(\sigma,p,q)^{\geq\mathfrak s}\supseteq\mathcal A(\sigma,p,q)^{\geq\mathfrak s^\mathrm{top}} \end{equation} (note that the two occurences of $\mathfrak s^\mathrm{top}$ refer to the top elements of two different strata posets); in fact (the index set of) the middle atlas is the disjoint union of (the index sets of) the atlases on the right and on the left. The reasoning used above to identify the orientation sheaf of $\overline{\mathcal M}(\sigma|[0\ldots\hat k\ldots n],p,q)=\overline{\mathcal M}(\sigma,p,q)^{\leq\mathfrak s}$ under the leftmost implicit atlas applies equally well for all three atlases (and, in particular, the resulting identifications coincide). Hence, for the purpose of identifying the boundary map on orientation sheaves, it suffices to consider the single atlas $\mathcal A(\sigma,p,q)^{\geq\mathfrak s^\mathrm{top}}$ on $\overline{\mathcal M}(\sigma,p,q)$ and the inclusion of the boundary stratum $\overline{\mathcal M}(\sigma,p,q)^{\leq\mathfrak s}\hookrightarrow\overline{\mathcal M}(\sigma,p,q)$. Now it suffices to check that the desired compatibility holds for the inclusion $(\overline{\mathcal M}(\sigma,p,q)^{\leq\mathfrak s}_I)^{\mathrm{reg}\circ}\hookrightarrow\overline{\mathcal M}(\sigma,p,q)_I^{\mathrm{reg}\circ}$ (for all finite subsets $I\subseteq\mathcal A(\sigma,p,q)^{\geq\mathfrak s^\mathrm{top}}$), and this follows by definition.
nodes.statement_short: Show compatibility with face boundary maps by chasing definitions.
nodes.section: C.13.3 Orientations on thickened moduli spaces $\overline{\mathcal M}(\sigma,p,q)_I^\mathrm{reg}$

nodes.name: Face stratum and three atlases
nodes.statement: Now let us show that the boundary map induced by \eqref{hforface} coincides with the tautological map \eqref{hforfaceor} (this just amounts to chasing definitions). Let $\mathfrak s\in\mathcal S_{\overline{\mathcal M}}(\sigma,p,q)$ denote the stratum $(\sigma|[0\ldots\hat k\ldots n],p,q)$ (i.e.\ the stratum consisting of trajectories over $\sigma$ which factor through $\sigma|[0\ldots\hat k\ldots n]$). Now on the space $\overline{\mathcal M}(\sigma|[0\ldots\hat k\ldots n],p,q)=\overline{\mathcal M}(\sigma,p,q)^{\leq\mathfrak s}$, we have three implicit atlases: \begin{equation} \mathcal A(\sigma|[0\ldots\hat k\ldots n],p,q)^{\geq\mathfrak s^\mathrm{top}}\subseteq\mathcal A(\sigma,p,q)^{\geq\mathfrak s}\supseteq\mathcal A(\sigma,p,q)^{\geq\mathfrak s^\mathrm{top}} \end{equation} (note that the two occurences of $\mathfrak s^\mathrm{top}$ refer to the top elements of two different strata posets); in fact (the index set of) the middle atlas is the disjoint union of (the index sets of) the atlases on the right and on the left.
nodes.statement_short: Introduce the face stratum and the three implicit atlases on it.
nodes.section: C.13.3 Orientations on thickened moduli spaces $\overline{\mathcal M}(\sigma,p,q)_I^\mathrm{reg}$

nodes.name: Reduce to a single atlas
nodes.statement: The reasoning used above to identify the orientation sheaf of $\overline{\mathcal M}(\sigma|[0\ldots\hat k\ldots n],p,q)=\overline{\mathcal M}(\sigma,p,q)^{\leq\mathfrak s}$ under the leftmost implicit atlas applies equally well for all three atlases (and, in particular, the resulting identifications coincide). Hence, for the purpose of identifying the boundary map on orientation sheaves, it suffices to consider the single atlas $\mathcal A(\sigma,p,q)^{\geq\mathfrak s^\mathrm{top}}$ on $\overline{\mathcal M}(\sigma,p,q)$ and the inclusion of the boundary stratum $\overline{\mathcal M}(\sigma,p,q)^{\leq\mathfrak s}\hookrightarrow\overline{\mathcal M}(\sigma,p,q)$.
nodes.statement_short: Identifications agree for all three atlases, so use the single top atlas.
nodes.section: C.13.3 Orientations on thickened moduli spaces $\overline{\mathcal M}(\sigma,p,q)_I^\mathrm{reg}$

nodes.name: Check on thickened loci
nodes.statement: Now it suffices to check that the desired compatibility holds for the inclusion $(\overline{\mathcal M}(\sigma,p,q)^{\leq\mathfrak s}_I)^{\mathrm{reg}\circ}\hookrightarrow\overline{\mathcal M}(\sigma,p,q)_I^{\mathrm{reg}\circ}$ (for all finite subsets $I\subseteq\mathcal A(\sigma,p,q)^{\geq\mathfrak s^\mathrm{top}}$), and this follows by definition.
nodes.statement_short: Compatibility on thickened regular loci holds by definition.
nodes.section: C.13.3 Orientations on thickened moduli spaces $\overline{\mathcal M}(\sigma,p,q)_I^\mathrm{reg}$

nodes.name: Product boundary map: reduction
nodes.statement: Now let us show that the boundary map induced by \eqref{hforproduct} coincides with the tautological map \eqref{hforproductor}. First, we chase definitions as above. Let $\mathfrak s\in\mathcal S_{\overline{\mathcal M}}(\sigma,p,r)$ denote the stratum $(\sigma|[0\ldots k],p,q)$--$(\sigma|[k\ldots n],q,r)$ (i.e.\ the stratum consisting of Floer trajectories over $\sigma$ which are broken at vertex $k$ and periodic orbit $q\in\mathcal P_{H(k)}$). Now on the space $\overline{\mathcal M}(\sigma|[0\ldots k],p,q)\times\overline{\mathcal M}(\sigma|[k\ldots n],q,r)=\overline{\mathcal M}(\sigma,p,r)^{\leq\mathfrak s}$, we have three implicit atlases: \begin{equation*} \mathcal A(\sigma|[0\ldots k],p,q)^{\geq\mathfrak s^\mathrm{top}}\sqcup\mathcal A(\sigma|[k\ldots n],q,r)^{\geq\mathfrak s^\mathrm{top}}\subseteq\mathcal A(\sigma,p,r)^{\geq\mathfrak s}\supseteq\mathcal A(\sigma,p,r)^{\geq\mathfrak s^\mathrm{top}} \end{equation*} and in fact (the index set of) the middle atlas is the disjoint union of (the index sets of) the atlases on the right and on the left. The reasoning used above to identify the orientation sheaves of $\overline{\mathcal M}(\sigma|[0\ldots k],p,q)$ and $\overline{\mathcal M}(\sigma|[k\ldots n],q,r)$ applies equally well to identify the orientation sheaf of their product $\overline{\mathcal M}(\sigma|[0\ldots k],p,q)\times\overline{\mathcal M}(\sigma|[k\ldots n],q,r)=\overline{\mathcal M}(\sigma,p,r)^{\leq\mathfrak s}$ under all three atlases above (the fact that the thickening datums in the latter two atlases do not treat the portions of the trajectories from $p$ to $q$ and from $q$ to $r$ ``independently'' does not cause any problems). Hence for the purposes of identifying the boundary map on orientation sheaves, it suffices to consider the single atlas $\mathcal A(\sigma,p,r)^{\geq\mathfrak s^\mathrm{top}}$ on $\overline{\mathcal M}(\sigma,p,r)$ and the inclusion of the boundary stratum $\overline{\mathcal M}(\sigma,p,r)^{\leq\mathfrak s}\hookrightarrow\overline{\mathcal M}(\sigma,p,r)$. As before, it suffices to check that the desired compatibility holds for the inclusion $(\overline{\mathcal M}(\sigma,p,r)^{\leq\mathfrak s}_I)^\mathrm{reg}\hookrightarrow\overline{\mathcal M}(\sigma,p,r)_I^\mathrm{reg}$ (for all finite subsets $I\subseteq\mathcal A(\sigma,p,r)^{\geq\mathfrak s^\mathrm{top}}$), and moreover, this may be checked on the locus where the domain curve is smooth except for the required node over $k$ asymptotic to $q\in\mathcal P_{H(k)}$.
nodes.statement_short: Reduce compatibility with product boundary maps to the single top atlas near once-broken trajectories.
nodes.section: C.13.3 Orientations on thickened moduli spaces $\overline{\mathcal M}(\sigma,p,q)_I^\mathrm{reg}$

nodes.name: Breaking stratum and three atlases
nodes.statement: Now let us show that the boundary map induced by \eqref{hforproduct} coincides with the tautological map \eqref{hforproductor}. First, we chase definitions as above. Let $\mathfrak s\in\mathcal S_{\overline{\mathcal M}}(\sigma,p,r)$ denote the stratum $(\sigma|[0\ldots k],p,q)$--$(\sigma|[k\ldots n],q,r)$ (i.e.\ the stratum consisting of Floer trajectories over $\sigma$ which are broken at vertex $k$ and periodic orbit $q\in\mathcal P_{H(k)}$). Now on the space $\overline{\mathcal M}(\sigma|[0\ldots k],p,q)\times\overline{\mathcal M}(\sigma|[k\ldots n],q,r)=\overline{\mathcal M}(\sigma,p,r)^{\leq\mathfrak s}$, we have three implicit atlases: \begin{equation*} \mathcal A(\sigma|[0\ldots k],p,q)^{\geq\mathfrak s^\mathrm{top}}\sqcup\mathcal A(\sigma|[k\ldots n],q,r)^{\geq\mathfrak s^\mathrm{top}}\subseteq\mathcal A(\sigma,p,r)^{\geq\mathfrak s}\supseteq\mathcal A(\sigma,p,r)^{\geq\mathfrak s^\mathrm{top}} \end{equation*} and in fact (the index set of) the middle atlas is the disjoint union of (the index sets of) the atlases on the right and on the left.
nodes.statement_short: Introduce the stratum of trajectories broken at vertex $k$ and the three atlases on it.
nodes.section: C.13.3 Orientations on thickened moduli spaces $\overline{\mathcal M}(\sigma,p,q)_I^\mathrm{reg}$

nodes.name: Reduce to a single atlas
nodes.statement: The reasoning used above to identify the orientation sheaves of $\overline{\mathcal M}(\sigma|[0\ldots k],p,q)$ and $\overline{\mathcal M}(\sigma|[k\ldots n],q,r)$ applies equally well to identify the orientation sheaf of their product $\overline{\mathcal M}(\sigma|[0\ldots k],p,q)\times\overline{\mathcal M}(\sigma|[k\ldots n],q,r)=\overline{\mathcal M}(\sigma,p,r)^{\leq\mathfrak s}$ under all three atlases above (the fact that the thickening datums in the latter two atlases do not treat the portions of the trajectories from $p$ to $q$ and from $q$ to $r$ ``independently'' does not cause any problems). Hence for the purposes of identifying the boundary map on orientation sheaves, it suffices to consider the single atlas $\mathcal A(\sigma,p,r)^{\geq\mathfrak s^\mathrm{top}}$ on $\overline{\mathcal M}(\sigma,p,r)$ and the inclusion of the boundary stratum $\overline{\mathcal M}(\sigma,p,r)^{\leq\mathfrak s}\hookrightarrow\overline{\mathcal M}(\sigma,p,r)$.
nodes.statement_short: The product identifications agree for all three atlases; use the top atlas.
nodes.section: C.13.3 Orientations on thickened moduli spaces $\overline{\mathcal M}(\sigma,p,q)_I^\mathrm{reg}$

nodes.name: Localize near once-broken trajectories
nodes.statement: As before, it suffices to check that the desired compatibility holds for the inclusion $(\overline{\mathcal M}(\sigma,p,r)^{\leq\mathfrak s}_I)^\mathrm{reg}\hookrightarrow\overline{\mathcal M}(\sigma,p,r)_I^\mathrm{reg}$ (for all finite subsets $I\subseteq\mathcal A(\sigma,p,r)^{\geq\mathfrak s^\mathrm{top}}$), and moreover, this may be checked on the locus where the domain curve is smooth except for the required node over $k$ asymptotic to $q\in\mathcal P_{H(k)}$.
nodes.statement_short: Check on thickened regular loci near trajectories with a single node over $k$.
nodes.section: C.13.3 Orientations on thickened moduli spaces $\overline{\mathcal M}(\sigma,p,q)_I^\mathrm{reg}$

nodes.name: Reduce to 0<k<n
nodes.statement: It will be convenient to assume that $0<k<n$, so let us first deduce the case of general $0\leq k\leq n$ from the case $0<k<n$. Fix $\sigma$ and $0\leq k\leq n=\dim\sigma$. We consider the degenerate simplex $\sigma'\to\sigma$ given by ``doubling vertex $0$'' if $k=0$ and ``doubling vertex $n$'' if $k=n$ (i.e.\ if $0=k<n$, we consider $\Delta^{n+1}\to\Delta^n$ given by superimposing the first two vertices of $\Delta^{n+1}$, if $0<k=n$, we consider $\Delta^{n+1}\to\Delta^n$ given by superimposing the last two vertices of $\Delta^{n+1}$, and if $0=k=n$ we consider $\Delta^2\to\Delta^0$); let $k'=1$ if $k=0$ and let $k'=n'-1$ if $k=n$, where $n'=\dim\sigma'$, and note that $0<k'<n'$. Now there is a natural map $\mathcal A(\sigma,p,q)^{\geq\mathfrak s^\mathrm{top}}\to\mathcal A(\sigma',p,q)^{\geq\mathfrak s^\mathrm{top}}$ given by pulling back along $\sigma'\to\sigma$, and $\sigma'\to\sigma$ maps flow lines to flow lines (for the flow from Definition \ref{simplexflows}). Hence, given any point $x\in\overline{\mathcal M}(\sigma,p,r)_I^\mathrm{reg}$ with a single node over $k$ asymptotic to $q\in\mathcal P_{H(k)}$, we may lift it (canonically, up to translating the part(s) of the trajectory over $0=k$ and/or over $k=n$) to a point $x'\in\overline{\mathcal M}(\sigma',p,r)_I^\mathrm{reg}$ with a single node over $k'$ asymptotic to $q\in\mathcal P_{H'(k')}=\mathcal P_{H(k)}$. Moreover, there is a germ of homeomorphism $\overline{\mathcal M}(\sigma',p,r)_I^\mathrm{reg}=\overline{\mathcal M}(\sigma,p,r)_I^\mathrm{reg}\times\mathbb R^{\mathbf 1(k=0)+\mathbf 1(k=n)}$ between neighborhoods of $x'$ and $x\times 0$. Now the desired compatibility of orientations for $(\overline{\mathcal M}(\sigma,p,r)_I^{\leq\mathfrak s})^\mathrm{reg}\hookrightarrow\overline{\mathcal M}(\sigma,p,r)_I^\mathrm{reg}$ follows from the compatibility for $(\overline{\mathcal M}(\sigma',p,r)_I^{\leq\mathfrak s'})^\mathrm{reg}\hookrightarrow\overline{\mathcal M}(\sigma',p,r)_I^\mathrm{reg}$ (which has from $0<k'<n'$). Hence we may assume without loss of generality that $0<k<n$.
nodes.statement_short: Handle $k=0$ or $k=n$ by pulling back along a degenerate simplex doubling a vertex.
nodes.section: C.13.3 Orientations on thickened moduli spaces $\overline{\mathcal M}(\sigma,p,q)_I^\mathrm{reg}$

nodes.name: Recap of the remaining goal
nodes.statement: Now we have come to the heart of the matter, where we will need to analyze the gluing map. To review: we have identified the orientation sheaf of $\overline{\mathcal M}(\sigma,p,r)_I^\mathrm{reg}$ with $\mathfrak o_{E_I}\otimes\mathfrak o_\sigma\otimes\mathfrak o_{p,r}$, and we have identified the orientation sheaf of $(\overline{\mathcal M}(\sigma,p,r)^{\leq\mathfrak s}_I)^\mathrm{reg}$ with $\mathfrak o_{E_I}\otimes\mathfrak o_{\sigma|[0\ldots k]}\otimes\mathfrak o_{p,q}\otimes\mathfrak o_{\sigma|[k\ldots n]}\otimes\mathfrak o_{q,r}$ (recall that $\mathfrak s$ denotes the stratum consisting of trajectories broken at vertex $k$ and periodic orbit $q\in\mathcal P_{H(k)}$). We must show that the boundary map on orientation sheaves induced by the inclusion $(\overline{\mathcal M}(\sigma,p,r)^{\leq\mathfrak s}_I)^\mathrm{reg}\hookrightarrow\overline{\mathcal M}(\sigma,p,r)_I^\mathrm{reg}$ is the expected map \eqref{hforproductor}, and it suffices to check this over the locus where the domain curve is smooth except for the required node over $k$ asymptotic to $q\in\mathcal P_{H(k)}$. We may further assume that $0<k<n$.
nodes.statement_short: Recap: show the boundary map is the expected map near once-broken trajectories.
nodes.section: C.13.3 Orientations on thickened moduli spaces $\overline{\mathcal M}(\sigma,p,q)_I^\mathrm{reg}$

nodes.name: Gluing setup near a broken trajectory
nodes.statement: We consider the gluing setup for $\overline{\mathcal M}(\sigma,p,r)_I^\mathrm{reg}$ at a point in $(\overline{\mathcal M}(\sigma,p,r)^{\leq\mathfrak s}_I)^\mathrm{reg}$ where $C_0$ is smooth except for the required node over vertex $k$ asymptotic to $q\in\mathcal P_{H(k)}$. In other words, $C_0\setminus\{q_0,q_1,q_2\}=S^1\times\mathbb R\sqcup S^1\times\mathbb R$, and $u_0:S^1\times\mathbb R\sqcup S^1\times\mathbb R\to M$ is a trajectory from $p$ to $q$ and from $q$ to $r$. From \S\ref{choosingDH}, we take $L=L'=0$ (i.e.\ no points $p_i$ or $p_i'$), and we may take $D=H=\varnothing$. From \S\ref{gluingandvaryingjAl}, there is one gluing parameter $\alpha\in\mathbb R_{\geq 0}$, there is no nontrivial variation in $(j_0,A_0)$ (i.e.\ $y\in\mathbb R^\ast=\mathbb R^0$), and there is some variation in $\ell_0$ parameterized by $w\in\prod_{i=1}^{2\prime}H^i$. As usual, we denote by $K\subseteq W^{k,2,\delta}(C_0,u_0^\ast TM)$ the kernel of the linearized operator (we shall omit the subscript $D,H$ since $L=L'=0$). Now the gluing construction gives rise to a gluing map: \begin{align} K\times\mathbb R_{\geq 0}\times\prod_{i=1}^{2\prime}H^i&\to\overline{\mathcal M}(\sigma,p,r)_I^\mathrm{reg}\\ (\kappa,\alpha,w)&\mapsto(u_{\alpha,w,y,\kappa},e_{\alpha,w,y,\kappa}) \end{align} ($y=0$).
nodes.statement_short: Set up the gluing map with one gluing parameter $\alpha$ near the broken trajectory.
nodes.section: C.13.3 Orientations on thickened moduli spaces $\overline{\mathcal M}(\sigma,p,q)_I^\mathrm{reg}$

nodes.name: Reduce to derivative of gluing
nodes.statement: Now if we restrict to $\alpha=0$, this map realizes the identification of the orientation sheaf of $(\overline{\mathcal M}(\sigma,p,r)^{\leq\mathfrak s}_I)^\mathrm{reg}$ with $\mathfrak o_K\otimes\mathfrak o_{\sigma|[0\ldots k]}\otimes\mathfrak o_{\sigma|[k\ldots n]}$. Thus it suffices to show that for fixed (sufficiently small) $\alpha>0$ and fixed $w=0$, the gluing map is differentiable in the $K$ direction, and that its derivative (a map from $K$ to the kernel of the linearized operator at the glued map $u_{\alpha,w,y,\kappa}$) agrees (on orientation lines) with the Floer--Hofer map \eqref{floerhoferoogluing} (recall that $\mathfrak o_K$ is identified with $\mathfrak o_{E_I}\otimes\mathfrak o_{p,q}\otimes\mathfrak o_{q,r}$ and that the orientation line of the kernel at the glued map is identified with $\mathfrak o_{E_I}\otimes\mathfrak o_{p,r}$).
nodes.statement_short: Suffices: the derivative of the gluing map in the $K$ direction matches the Floer--Hofer map.
nodes.section: C.13.3 Orientations on thickened moduli spaces $\overline{\mathcal M}(\sigma,p,q)_I^\mathrm{reg}$

nodes.name: Differentiability of the gluing map
nodes.statement: For fixed $(\alpha,w,y)$, the gluing map is given by: \begin{equation} K\xrightarrow{\kappa\mapsto\kappa_\alpha}K_\alpha\xrightarrow{\kappa_\alpha\mapsto\kappa_{\alpha,w,y}}\mathcal F_{\alpha,w,y}^{-1}(0) \end{equation} The second map is defined \emph{a priori} by a Newton iteration, however a more natural description \emph{a posteriori} is that $\{\kappa_{\alpha,w,y}\}=\{\kappa_\alpha+\operatorname{im} Q_{\alpha,w,y}\}\pitchfork\mathcal F_{\alpha,w,y}^{-1}(0)$ is the unique (necessarily transverse) intersection in a $(k,2,\delta,\delta)$-neighborhood of zero of fixed size. Note that in this neighborhood of fixed size, $\mathcal F_{\alpha,w,y}^{-1}(0)$ is a (highly differentiable) submanifold, since $\mathcal F_{\alpha,w,y}$ is highly differentiable and $D_{\kappa_{\alpha,w,y}}\mathcal F_{\alpha,w,y}$ is surjective as observed in the proof of Lemma \ref{mapsstufftoregHF}. From this description of the second map, it is clearly differentiable.
nodes.statement_short: Describe $\kappa_{\alpha,w,y}$ as a transverse intersection, so the gluing map is differentiable.
nodes.section: C.13.3 Orientations on thickened moduli spaces $\overline{\mathcal M}(\sigma,p,q)_I^\mathrm{reg}$

nodes.name: Formula for the derivative
nodes.statement: Thus the derivative of the restricted gluing map \eqref{restrictedgluingmap} at a given $\kappa$ is given by: \begin{equation} T_\kappa K\xrightarrow{\dot\kappa\mapsto\dot\kappa_\alpha}T_{\kappa_\alpha}K_\alpha\xrightarrow{\operatorname{proj}_{Q_{\alpha,w,y}}}T_{\kappa_{\alpha,w,y}}\mathcal F_{\alpha,w,y}^{-1}(0)=\ker D_{\kappa_{\alpha,w,y}}\mathcal F_{\alpha,w,y} \end{equation} The second map is ``projection with respect to $Q_{\alpha,w,y}$'', i.e.\ the map induced by identifying both the domain and codomain with $W^{k,2,\delta,\delta}(C_\alpha,u_\alpha^\ast TM)/\operatorname{im} Q_{\alpha,w,y}$.
nodes.statement_short: The derivative is pregluing followed by projection with respect to $Q_{\alpha,w,y}$.
nodes.section: C.13.3 Orientations on thickened moduli spaces $\overline{\mathcal M}(\sigma,p,q)_I^\mathrm{reg}$

nodes.name: Derivative at kappa=0
nodes.statement: It suffices to study the derivative at $\kappa=0$, namely the first line of the following commuting diagram: \begin{equation} \begin{tikzcd}[column sep = small] T_0K\ar{rr}{\dot\kappa\mapsto\dot\kappa_\alpha}&&T_0K_\alpha\ar{rr}{\operatorname{proj}_{Q_{\alpha,w,y}}}\ar{dr}[swap]{\operatorname{proj}_{Q_{\alpha,w,y}}}&&\ker D_{(0)_{\alpha,w,y}}\mathcal F_{\alpha,w,y}\ar{dl}{\operatorname{proj}_{Q_{\alpha,w,y}}}\\ &&&\ker D_{\alpha,w,y} \end{tikzcd} \end{equation} The rightmost diagonal map is orientation preserving (i.e.\ it commutes with the identification of the orientation lines of the domain and codomain with $\mathfrak o_{E_I}\otimes\mathfrak o_{p,r}$), because $\operatorname{proj}_{Q_{\alpha,w,y}}$ gives a local trivialization of the bundle $\ker D\mathcal F_{\alpha,w,y}$ with respect to which the orientation is constant by definition.
nodes.statement_short: Study the derivative at zero; the right diagonal projection preserves orientation.
nodes.section: C.13.3 Orientations on thickened moduli spaces $\overline{\mathcal M}(\sigma,p,q)_I^\mathrm{reg}$

nodes.name: Reduce to explicit composition
nodes.statement: Now the leftmost diagonal map is just $\dot\kappa_\alpha\mapsto\dot\kappa_\alpha-Q_{\alpha,w,y}D_{\alpha,w,y}\dot\kappa_\alpha$. Hence it suffices to show that the following composition (note that we have changed notation from $\dot\kappa$ back to $\kappa$): \begin{equation} \ker D_{0,0,0}=K\xrightarrow{\kappa\mapsto\kappa_\alpha}K_\alpha\xrightarrow{\kappa_\alpha\mapsto\kappa_\alpha-Q_{\alpha,w,y}D_{\alpha,w,y}\kappa_\alpha}\ker D_{\alpha,w,y} \end{equation} acts as \eqref{floerhoferoogluing} on orientations (with respect to the previously defined isomorphisms $\mathfrak o_K=\mathfrak o_{E_I}\otimes\mathfrak o_{p,q}\otimes\mathfrak o_{q,r}$ and $\mathfrak o_{\ker D_{\alpha,w,y}}=\mathfrak o_{E_I}\otimes\mathfrak o_{p,r}$).
nodes.statement_short: Suffices: the composition $\kappa\mapsto\kappa_\alpha-QD\kappa_\alpha$ acts as the Floer--Hofer map on orientations.
nodes.section: C.13.3 Orientations on thickened moduli spaces $\overline{\mathcal M}(\sigma,p,q)_I^\mathrm{reg}$

nodes.name: Orientation inverse diagram
nodes.statement: We analyze \eqref{concretestufftocheckorientations} as follows. For convenience, we may as well assume that $w=0$, and recall that necessarily $y=0$. Now let us consider the following diagram: \begin{equation} \begin{tikzcd} K_{\alpha,0,0}\ar[hook,yshift=-0.5ex]{r}\ar[leftarrow,yshift=0.5ex]{r}{\operatorname{proj}_{T_{\alpha,0,0}}}&W^{k,2,\delta,\delta}(C_\alpha,u_\alpha^\ast TM)\oplus E_I\ar{r}{D_{\alpha,0,0}}&W^{k-1,2,\delta,\delta}(\tilde C_\alpha,\Omega^{0,1}_{\tilde C_\alpha,j_0}\otimes_\mathbb C u_\alpha^\ast TM_{J(\ell_{\alpha,0}(A_0(\cdot)))})\ar{d}{\mathrm{break}}\\ K_{0|\alpha,0,0}\ar[hook,yshift=-0.5ex]{r}\ar[leftarrow,yshift=0.5ex]{r}{\operatorname{proj}_{T_{0|\alpha,0,0}}}&W^{k,2,\delta,\delta}(C_0,u_{0|\alpha}^\ast TM)\oplus E_I\ar{u}{\mathrm{glue}}\ar{r}{D_{0|\alpha,0,0}}&W^{k-1,2,\delta,\delta}(\tilde C_0,\Omega^{0,1}_{\tilde C_0,j_0}\otimes_\mathbb C u_{0|\alpha}^\ast TM_{J(\ell_{0,0}(A_0(\cdot)))})\ar[leftrightarrow]{d}{\mathsf{PT}}\\ K_{0,0,0}\ar[hook,yshift=0.5ex]{r}\ar[leftarrow,yshift=-0.5ex]{r}[swap]{\operatorname{proj}_{Q_{0,0,0}}}\ar{ru}{\kappa\mapsto\kappa_{0|\alpha}}&W^{k,2,\delta,\delta}(C_0,u_0^\ast TM)\oplus E_I\ar[leftrightarrow]{u}{\mathsf{PT}}\ar[yshift=0.5ex]{r}{D_{0,0,0}}&\ar[yshift=-0.5ex]{l}{Q_{0,0,0}}W^{k-1,2,\delta,\delta}(\tilde C_0,\Omega^{0,1}_{\tilde C_0,j_0}\otimes_\mathbb C u_0^\ast TM_{J(\ell_{0,0}(A_0(\cdot)))}) \end{tikzcd} \end{equation} The right half is just a copy of \eqref{biginversediagramHF} (with the middle square collapsed since $y=0$). The left half consists of the inclusions of the kernels of the operators on the right half, as well as the projection maps associated to the images of the (approximate) right inverses $Q_{0,0,0}$, $T_{0|\alpha,0,0}:=\mathsf{PT}\circ Q_{0,0,0}\circ\mathsf{PT}$, and $T_{\alpha,0,0}=\mathrm{glue}\circ\mathsf{PT}\circ Q_{0,0,0}\circ\mathsf{PT}\circ\mathrm{break}$ (recall that $\operatorname{im} T_{\alpha,0,0}=\operatorname{im} Q_{\alpha,0,0}$). The diagonal map $\kappa\mapsto\kappa_{0|\alpha}$ is defined by cutting off as in Definition \ref{kernelpregluingHF}; thus $\kappa_\alpha=\mathrm{glue}(\kappa_{0|\alpha})$.
nodes.statement_short: Introduce the diagram of kernels and (approximate) right-inverse projections.
nodes.section: C.13.3 Orientations on thickened moduli spaces $\overline{\mathcal M}(\sigma,p,q)_I^\mathrm{reg}$

nodes.name: Approximate by projected pregluing
nodes.statement: Now the map \eqref{concretestufftocheckorientations} which we would like to analyze may be written as the composition $\kappa\mapsto\operatorname{proj}_{T_{\alpha,0,0}}(\mathrm{glue}(\kappa_{0|\alpha}))$ from \eqref{orientationsinversediagram}. Now, we know that $\|D_{0|\alpha,0,0}\kappa_{0|\alpha}\|_{k-1,2,\delta,\delta}=\|D_{\alpha,0,0}\kappa_\alpha\|_{k-1,2,\delta,\delta}$, which is small by Lemma \ref{pregluingKestimateHF}. It follows that the map we would like to analyze is well-approximated (as $\alpha\to 0$) by the map $\kappa\mapsto\operatorname{proj}_{T_{\alpha,0,0}}(\mathrm{glue}(\operatorname{proj}_{T_{0|\alpha,0,0}}\kappa_{0|\alpha}))$.
nodes.statement_short: By the kernel pregluing estimate, replace the map by one projecting first onto $K_{0|\alpha,0,0}$.
nodes.section: C.13.3 Orientations on thickened moduli spaces $\overline{\mathcal M}(\sigma,p,q)_I^\mathrm{reg}$

nodes.name: First projection preserves orientation
nodes.statement: Now we claim that the map $K_{0,0,0}\to K_{0|\alpha,0,0}$ given by $\kappa\mapsto\operatorname{proj}_{T_{0|\alpha,0,0}}\kappa_{0|\alpha}$ preserves orientation (the orientation lines of the domain and codomain are both identified with $\mathfrak o_{E_I}\otimes\mathfrak o_{p,q}\otimes\mathfrak o_{q,r}$). To see this, simply observe the map (as well as its domain and codomain and their orientations) vary continuously over $\alpha\in[0,\epsilon)$, and that the statement is true for $\alpha=0$ because then the map is the identity map.
nodes.statement_short: The map $K_{0,0,0}\to K_{0|\alpha,0,0}$ preserves orientation by continuity from $\alpha=0$.
nodes.section: C.13.3 Orientations on thickened moduli spaces $\overline{\mathcal M}(\sigma,p,q)_I^\mathrm{reg}$

nodes.name: Reduced problem
nodes.statement: Hence we have reduced the problem to showing that the map: \begin{equation} W^{k,2,\delta,\delta}(C_0,u_{0|\alpha}^\ast TM)\supseteq K_{0|\alpha,0,0}\xrightarrow{\mathrm{glue}}W^{k,2,\delta,\delta}(C_\alpha,u_\alpha^\ast TM)\oplus E_I\xrightarrow{\operatorname{proj}_{T_{\alpha,0,0}}}K_{\alpha,0,0} \end{equation} acts by \eqref{floerhoferoogluing}.
nodes.statement_short: Reduce to the map proj$_T$∘glue: $K_{0|\alpha,0,0}\to K_{\alpha,0,0}$.
nodes.section: C.13.3 Orientations on thickened moduli spaces $\overline{\mathcal M}(\sigma,p,q)_I^\mathrm{reg}$

nodes.name: Stabilized family of diagrams
nodes.statement: To analyze the map ${\operatorname{proj}_{T_{\alpha,0,0}}}\circ{\mathrm{glue}}:K_{0|\alpha,0,0}\to K_{\alpha,0,0}$, argue as follows. For any finite-dimensional vector space $F$ and a map $\Lambda:F\to W^{k-1,2,\delta,\delta}(\tilde C_0,\Omega^{0,1}_{\tilde C_0,j_0}\otimes_\mathbb C u_0^\ast TM_{J(\ell_{0,0}(A_0(\cdot)))})$ supported away from the ends, we may consider the following modified version of \eqref{orientationsinversediagram}: \begin{equation} \begin{tikzcd} K_{\alpha,0,0}^{\Lambda,t}\ar[hook,yshift=-0.5ex]{r}\ar[leftarrow,yshift=0.5ex]{r}{\operatorname{proj}_{T_{\alpha,0,0}^{\Lambda,t}}}&F\oplus W^{k,2,\delta,\delta}(C_\alpha,u_\alpha^\ast TM)\oplus E_I\ar{r}{\Lambda\oplus D_{\alpha,0,0}^t}&W^{k-1,2,\delta,\delta}(\tilde C_\alpha,\Omega^{0,1}_{\tilde C_\alpha,j_0}\otimes_\mathbb C u_\alpha^\ast TM_{J(\ell_{\alpha,0}(A_0(\cdot)))})\ar{d}{\mathrm{break}}\\ K_{0|\alpha,0,0}^{\Lambda,t}\ar[hook,yshift=-0.5ex]{r}\ar[leftarrow,yshift=0.5ex]{r}{\operatorname{proj}_{T_{0|\alpha,0,0}^{\Lambda,t}}}&F\oplus W^{k,2,\delta,\delta}(C_0,u_{0|\alpha}^\ast TM)\oplus E_I\ar{u}{\operatorname{id}\oplus\mathrm{glue}}\ar{r}{\Lambda\oplus D_{0|\alpha,0,0}^t}&W^{k-1,2,\delta,\delta}(\tilde C_0,\Omega^{0,1}_{\tilde C_0,j_0}\otimes_\mathbb C u_{0|\alpha}^\ast TM_{J(\ell_{0,0}(A_0(\cdot)))})\ar[leftrightarrow]{d}{\mathsf{PT}}\\ K_{0,0,0}^{\Lambda,t}\ar[hook,yshift=0.5ex]{r}\ar[leftarrow,yshift=-0.5ex]{r}[swap]{\operatorname{proj}_{Q_{0,0,0}^{\Lambda,t}}}\ar{ru}{\kappa\mapsto\kappa_{0|\alpha}}&F\oplus W^{k,2,\delta,\delta}(C_0,u_0^\ast TM)\oplus E_I\ar[leftrightarrow]{u}{\operatorname{id}\oplus\mathsf{PT}}\ar[yshift=0.5ex]{r}{\Lambda\oplus D_{0,0,0}^t}&\ar[yshift=-0.5ex]{l}{Q_{0,0,0}^{\Lambda,t}}W^{k-1,2,\delta,\delta}(\tilde C_0,\Omega^{0,1}_{\tilde C_0,j_0}\otimes_\mathbb C u_0^\ast TM_{J(\ell_{0,0}(A_0(\cdot)))}) \end{tikzcd} \end{equation} Here $t\in[0,1]$ indicates that the terms \eqref{firstLterm}--\eqref{lastLterm} carry a factor of $t$. The estimates from Lemmas \ref{approxbottomHF} and \ref{approxtopHF} apply to this modified diagram as well. Thus as long as we fix a bounded right inverse $Q_{0,0,0}^{\Lambda,t}$ of $D_{0,0,0}^{\Lambda,t}$, the rest of the diagram makes sense (and, in particular, $T_{0|\alpha,0,0}^{\Lambda,t}$ and $T_{\alpha,0,0}^{\Lambda,t}$ are approximate right inverses) for sufficiently small $\alpha>0$. Furthermore, in any family of $(\Lambda,t,Q^{\Lambda,t})$, the kernels $K_{0,0,0}$, $K_{0|\alpha,0,0}$, $K_{\alpha,0,0}$ form vector bundles, and the identifications of their orientation lines with $\mathfrak o_F\otimes\mathfrak o_{p,q}\otimes\mathfrak o_{q,r}\otimes\mathfrak o_{E_I}$ and $\mathfrak o_F\otimes\mathfrak o_{p,r}\otimes\mathfrak o_{E_I}$ (respectively) vary continuously.
nodes.statement_short: Introduce stabilizations $(F,\Lambda)$ and a parameter $t$ scaling the thickening terms; kernels form bundles.
nodes.section: C.13.3 Orientations on thickened moduli spaces $\overline{\mathcal M}(\sigma,p,q)_I^\mathrm{reg}$

nodes.name: Reduce to a single stabilization
nodes.statement: Now the map: \begin{equation} K_{0|\alpha,0,0}^{\Lambda,t}\xrightarrow{{\operatorname{proj}_{T_{\alpha,0,0}^{\Lambda,t}}}\circ{\mathrm{glue}}}K_{\alpha,0,0}^{\Lambda,t} \end{equation} is exactly the map we wish to analyze when $F=0$, $\Lambda=0$, $t=1$, and $Q_{0,0,0}^{\Lambda,t}=0\oplus Q_{0,0,0}$.
nodes.statement_short: Contractibility of the space of $\Lambda$ lets us use one pair $(F,\Lambda)$.
nodes.section: C.13.3 Orientations on thickened moduli spaces $\overline{\mathcal M}(\sigma,p,q)_I^\mathrm{reg}$

nodes.name: Deform to t=0
nodes.statement: Now by compactness of $[0,1]$, there exists a pair $(F,\Lambda)$ so that $\Lambda\oplus D_{0,0,0}^t$ is surjective for all $t\in[0,1]$. Fix such a pair $(F,\Lambda)$, and also fix a continuously varying family of bounded right inverses $Q_{0,0,0}^{\Lambda,t}$ with $Q_{0,0,0}^{\Lambda,1}=0\oplus Q_{0,0,0}$. Since the kernels form a bundle over the base $[0,1]$ and their orientations vary continuously, it suffices to analyze \eqref{KmapLt} for this $(F,\Lambda)$, $t=0$, and this $Q_{0,0,0}^{\Lambda,0}$.
nodes.statement_short: Choose $(F,\Lambda)$ surjective for all $t$ and deform to $t=0$.
nodes.section: C.13.3 Orientations on thickened moduli spaces $\overline{\mathcal M}(\sigma,p,q)_I^\mathrm{reg}$

nodes.name: Compare with L^2 projection
nodes.statement: Now the Floer--Hofer map \eqref{floerhoferoogluing} is \emph{defined} (see \cite[Proposition 9]{floerhoferorientations}) by the property that it is induced by a certain map $K_{0|\alpha,0,0}^{\Lambda,0}\to K_{\alpha,0,0}^{\Lambda,0}$ closely related to \eqref{KmapLt}; clearly it suffices to show that the difference between the Floer--Hofer map and \eqref{KmapLt} is very small. Consider the map: \begin{equation} K_{0|\alpha,0,0}^{\Lambda,t}\xrightarrow{{\operatorname{proj}_{L^2}}\circ{\mathrm{glue}}}K_{\alpha,0,0}^{\Lambda,t} \end{equation} in the setting of the above choices of $(F,\Lambda)$, $t=0$, and $Q_{0,0,0}^{\Lambda,t}$, where instead of projecting off of $\operatorname{im} T_{\alpha,0,0}^{\Lambda,0}$, we use the $L^2$-orthogonal projection. The difference between \eqref{KmapLtLtwo} and \eqref{KmapLt} is exactly ${\operatorname{proj}_{L^2}}\circ Q^{\Lambda,0}_{\alpha,0,0}\circ(\Lambda\oplus D^0_{\alpha,0,0})\circ{\mathrm{glue}}$, which has small norm by the estimate in Lemma \ref{approxtopHF}. Thus it suffices to compare \eqref{KmapLtLtwo} to the Floer--Hofer map.
nodes.statement_short: Replacing the projection by $L^2$-projection changes the map by a small amount (top-square estimate).
nodes.section: C.13.3 Orientations on thickened moduli spaces $\overline{\mathcal M}(\sigma,p,q)_I^\mathrm{reg}$

nodes.name: Compare with Floer--Hofer map
nodes.statement: Now the Floer--Hofer map is given by: \begin{equation} K_{0|\alpha,0,0}^{\Lambda,0}\xrightarrow{{\operatorname{proj}_{L^2}}\circ{\mathrm{glue}'}}K_{\alpha,0,0}^{\Lambda,0} \end{equation} for a certain map $\mathrm{glue}'$ (see \cite[Proposition 9]{floerhoferorientations}). However, the norm of the difference $\mathrm{glue}-\mathrm{glue}'$ is very small due to the exponential decay of elements of the kernel (here, we may use the explicit description of $K_{0|\alpha,0,0}$ as the image of $\kappa\mapsto\kappa_{0|\alpha}-Q_{0|\alpha,0,0}D_{0|\alpha,0,0}\kappa_{0|\alpha}$). Thus we are done.
nodes.statement_short: Floer--Hofer use $L^2$-projection after a slightly different glue'; exponential decay makes the difference small.
nodes.section: C.13.3 Orientations on thickened moduli spaces $\overline{\mathcal M}(\sigma,p,q)_I^\mathrm{reg}$
